verdict.rationale: Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (and has Invited Speaker as a subclass), while Student non speaker in iasted is explicitly a delegate who does NOT speak/present. These are disjoint concepts.

Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic in edas representing a subject area for papers, while Transport vehicle is a subclass of Item in iasted representing physical vehicles (car, taxi, etc.). They are completely unrelated concepts.

In edas, Conference represents an academic conference event (with dates, topics, papers). In ekaw, Organisation represents an organisational body (with children like Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) that organises events. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assignment action), while write relates a Person to an Item (authoring action). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'reviewes' links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they review.

maxPapers limits the number of papers a Program Committee Member can handle, while minChoice specifies a minimum choice value for Social/Working events. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a subclass of Person (inherited from the ontology structure), representing people involved in a conference. In ekaw, 'Person' is the top-level class for all people. Thus, Conference Member in cmt is more specific than (subsumed by) Person in ekaw.

Regular in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while Regular Paper in ekaw is a subclass of Paper (a document). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and are unrelated.
Country (edas) represents a nation, while Location (ekaw) is a more general concept for any place where an event can be held. A country is a type of location, so Country is subsumed by Location.
heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location, while Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property linking a Sponsor to a string. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, and semantics.

Working event is a type of conference event (e.g., workshop, tutorial), while Communications Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

Organisation in ekaw is an organizational entity (with children like Academic Institution, Organising Agency), while Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. These are entirely different concepts.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.
Review in cmt is a document (the actual review of a paper), while Call For Reviews in edas is a type of call soliciting reviews. They are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, Paper is a full conference contribution (a regular paper) and Abstract is a separate component of it. In Ontology B, Abstract is a sibling of Paper under Document, representing abstracts for invited talks or tutorials. They denote different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered details), while Property B links a Topic to a Conference part. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Person is a class representing human beings, while City is a class representing geographical locations. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

has_title is a datatype property linking events to their string titles, while go_through is an object property linking Items to Activities. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Both properties link a reviewer (Reviewer in cmt, Possible Reviewer in ekaw) to a Paper they are assigned to review. Despite the slight difference in domain class naming, they express the same reviewer-to-paper assignment relation in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property linking programme brochures/websites to events, while Property B is a datatype property linking a conference to its start date/time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'authorOf' denotes the authorship relation between a Person and a Document, while 'send' denotes the act of sending/submission between a Person and an Item. Although both share domain Person and a document-like range, they represent different relations (authorship vs. submission action). They are related but not equivalent.
Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee-of relation), while Property B links a Person to an Organization (employment relation). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a banquet event within a conference context. They share the same parent (Social event/Social Event), similar sibling structures (Trip/Conference Trip), and identical intended instances.

Class A 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself, while class B 'Conference fees' represents the monetary fees associated with a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of 'Author', representing authors who are not reviewers. In sigkdd, 'Author' is the general class for all authors (with children like 'Author of paper'). The cmt 'Author Not Reviewer' is strictly more specific than the sigkdd 'Author', so it is subsumed by it.
'has workshops' relates a Conference volume to its Workshop parts, while 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place and Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (has a review) goes from Reviewed contribution to Review, while Property B (reviewOfPaper) goes from Review to Paper. They have opposite directions and different domains/ranges; they are inverses of each other, not equivalent.

hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a phone number string, while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A (co-writePaper) goes from Co-author to Paper, while property B (writtenBy) goes from Contribution (Paper) to Author. They are inverses of each other (A is 'writes', B is 'is written by'), and per the instructions a property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are related as they describe the same authorship relationship in opposite directions.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a broad class under Person with children including Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, and Program Committee Member. In confOf, 'Member PC' specifically denotes a program committee member/reviewer (as indicated by its comment 'Reviewer' and properties like 'reviewes'). Thus, confOf's Member_PC corresponds to cmt's Program Committee Member, which is a child of Conference Member. Therefore, Conference Member subsumes Member PC.
writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. The domains, ranges, and semantic roles are entirely different.
'has gender' captures a person's gender while 'Name' captures a person's name. These are entirely different attributes of a Person and are not semantically related.
hasVAT is a datatype property linking events to a VAT string value, while heldIn is an object property linking events to a Location. They represent entirely different concepts and are unrelated.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while expertOn links a PC Member to a Topic. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while City is a geographic location. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the concept of a Conference in the conference-organisation domain. Ontology A's Conference has properties like name and children like Conference volume, while Ontology B's (sigkdd) Conference has properties like city, start/end dates, name, and organizer. Despite different property sets, both denote the same real-world concept of a conference event.

Contribution co author in Ontology A is a specific role (a co-author of a contribution) under Regular author, while Author in Ontology B is a general class for all authors of papers. Every Contribution co author is an Author, but not every Author is a co-author (some may be first/sole authors). Thus A is subsumed by B.

Activity after conference is a temporal activity/event occurring after the conference, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories (Activity vs Place) and are unrelated.

Property A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value for camera-ready paper submission, while Property B is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating early registration. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Acceptance in cmt is a type of Decision (an outcome), while Deadline for notification of acceptance in iasted is a type of Deadline (a point in time). They are fundamentally different concepts and thus unrelated.

Early Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered early, while Organizing Committee member is a person involved in organizing the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

The property 'provided By' in edas links a Sponsorship to an Organization (the sponsor), while 'give' in iasted links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent fees associated with a conference. 'Conference fees' in Ontology A and 'Fee' in Ontology B (with children Registration fee and Sponzor fee) denote the same concept of monetary charges in the conference domain.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documents/artefacts related to a conference (calls for papers, reviews, contributions, etc.), whereas Conference in Ontology B (edas) refers to the conference event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Proceedings is a document/volume class (a publication), while Organizator is a person role class involved in organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent an 'Abstract' in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is a subtype of Extended abstract (a kind of contribution), while in Ontology B it is a Document sibling to Paper and Review. Despite differing taxonomic placements, both denote the same concept: the abstract text/summary associated with a conference submission. The properties in A (has an abstract, is the 1th part of) confirm it serves as the abstract component of papers/posters/presentations, aligning with B's Abstract class.

memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference, while City_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (city name). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Steering committee and Organizing Committee are distinct types of committees in conference organization. In Ontology A, Steering committee and Organizing committee are siblings under Committee, indicating they are different concepts. Ontology B's Organizing Committee corresponds to Ontology A's Organizing committee, not its Steering committee. They are related as sibling committee types but not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings. They are unrelated.

Acceptance in cmt is a decision outcome (subclass of Decision), while Renting in iasted is an activity before the conference (e.g., renting equipment or venue). They are completely different concepts.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference registrant who paid late), while Sponzorship is a subclass of Money (financial sponsorship). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Workshop is an academic sub-event or part of a conference (sibling of Track and Tutorial), while a Meal Break is a non-academic break event during a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Home Page' captures a person's website URL. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they represent entirely different attributes.

Property A links a Conference to its members (people), while property B links a Conference volume to its tutorials (events/program parts). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.
Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging, while Student lecturer is a person role (a student who lectures). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

confOf:Contribution is a general class for any submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper), while ekaw:Assigned_Paper is a specific subclass of Submitted Paper that has been assigned to reviewers. Contribution strictly subsumes Assigned Paper.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class for people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Workshop Chair (B) is a specific organizational role. While a workshop chair could be considered a contributor in a loose sense, B is much more specific than A, so A subsumes B at best, but they are not equivalent.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (the head of the PC), while Workshop Chair in ekaw is specifically the chair of a workshop. These are distinct roles; ekaw has its own 'PC Chair' class which would be the true equivalent of confOf's 'Chair PC'. They are related as both are chair roles within a conference but not equivalent.
writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (the act of writing a review), while invited_by relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding on papers to review), while hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. These are entirely different concepts and relations in the conference domain.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to structural components of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while OC Member in Ontology B refers to a person who is a member of the Organizing Committee. These are entirely different concepts.

'organised By' relates an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'occupy' relates a Person to a physical location (Building, City, State). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers, while Registration fee is a monetary fee for conference registration. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Cheque is a payment document (financial instrument) in the iasted ontology, while Paper is an academic submission in the sigkdd ontology. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

The property 'added By' in cmt links a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them, while 'has a committee chair' in Conference links a Committee to its Chair. These relate entirely different domain/range classes and express different semantics (addition action vs. leadership role), so they are unrelated.
The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Author), ranges (Conference vs Paper), and semantics (running assignment tools vs submitting a paper). They are unrelated.

Property A links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (a specific governance role for a conference edition), while Property B links an Organisation or Person to an Event (a general organising relation). Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly; they are not equivalent.

Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume (membership/part-of relation), while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (giving/presenting relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Invited speaker (Conference) is a conference contributor specifically invited to speak. Lecturer (iasted) is a subclass of Speaker/Author with children like Student lecturer and Worker lecturer, and siblings including Plenary lecture speaker and Tutorial speaker. While both involve giving talks at a conference, 'Lecturer' in iasted is broader (includes non-invited speakers like student lecturers) and does not specifically denote an invited role. They overlap but are not equivalent.
Worker non speaker is a delegate who does not speak (a non-speaker worker), while Speaker is a person who gives presentations. These are disjoint concepts in the conference domain.

A Session Chair (edas) is responsible for chairing a specific session during the conference, whereas an OC Chair (ekaw) is the chair of the Organizing Committee. These are distinct roles in conference organization; the equivalent of OC Chair in edas would be Conference Chair.

Property A is an object property linking Item to Person ('is used by'), while Property B is a datatype property linking Person to a string (name). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the physical venue/building where a conference takes place. In edas, ConferenceVenuePlace is a subclass of Place with siblings like AccommodationPlace and DiningPlace. In iasted, Conference_building is a subclass of Building (which is under Place) with siblings like Conference_hotel and Conference_restaurant. Despite slight naming differences (venue place vs building), they denote the same concept in the conference domain: the location where conference sessions are held.

Conference building in iasted is a physical place/building where the conference takes place, while Conference in sigkdd is the event itself with properties like start date, end date, and name. A building and an event are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference Chair is the main chairperson of a conference (a leadership role), while Listener is a delegate who attends but does not present. These are entirely different roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

A 'Double hotel room' is a specific type of room within a hotel, while 'Hotel' is the building/establishment itself. They are related (a double hotel room is part of a hotel) but not equivalent; Hotel is more general and represents a different level of granularity.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the overall chair of a conference, while Demo Chair (ekaw) is specifically responsible for the demo track/session. They are both chair roles but not equivalent; they are related as different types of conference chairs.
Security Topic is a subject area for papers in the edas ontology, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass) in the iasted ontology. They are completely unrelated concepts.

OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) in ekaw and General Chair in sigkdd both denote the person who chairs/leads the organizing committee of a conference. In the conference domain these are synonymous roles.
hasReview links a Paper to its Review, while presentation links a Speaker to a Document. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Property A relates a Chair to a Committee (committee chair role), while Property B relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation). They involve entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Company (confOf) is a commercial organization under Organization, while Academic Institution (ekaw) is an academic body under Organisation. They are siblings in their respective hierarchies (both have University as sibling/child), but a Company is not an Academic Institution and vice versa. They overlap conceptually as types of organizations but are not equivalent.
Conference in ekaw is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while Conference hotel in iasted is a physical building/place where attendees may stay. They are entirely different concepts.
Research Institute is an organization (a type of academic institution), while Review is a document (an evaluation of a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Registration form' is a document (subclass of Form) used to collect registration information, while 'Registration Non Member' is a type of registration fee (subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (document vs. monetary fee) and are unrelated.

Reviewed contribution is a class representing a paper/submission that has been reviewed (a document), while Reviewer is a class representing a person who performs reviews. They are fundamentally different concepts (artefact vs. person) and thus unrelated.

Review Rating in edas represents the rating or score assigned to a paper (e.g., Accept, Reject), while Review in iasted represents the review document itself. They are related concepts in the reviewing process but not equivalent.

Both properties express the location of a conference-related entity, but they differ significantly: A is a datatype property (range string) on Conference volume, while B is an object property (range Place) on Conference Event. They are related in purpose but not equivalent due to different domains, ranges, and property types.

Property A links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (how the paper is presented), while Property B links a Speaker to a Document (what the speaker presents). They have completely different domains and ranges and express different relationships.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Microelectronics Topic is a subject area (a subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to reviewers/chairs who review it, while 'is visited by' relates physical locations (Building, City, State) to a Person who visits them. These are entirely different relations in both domain and semantics.

Conference participant is a Person who attends the conference, while Social Event is a type of non-academic event (e.g., reception, excursion). They belong to entirely different categories (people vs. events) and are unrelated.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a score or evaluation). Decisions and ratings are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are not equivalent.

Location in ekaw represents a physical place where events are held, while Money in iasted represents financial concepts (fees, sponsorships, etc.). These are entirely different domain concepts with no semantic overlap.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper), meaning 'reviews'. Property B (hasReview) links a Paper to a Review object. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.
Departure is a post-conference activity/event, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. Author book proceedings included (B) is a very specific subclass of Author. Since B's instances are a subset of A's intended instances (authors who contribute to the conference), A subsumes B.

In edas, Author is a Person who writes papers and has a child class Presenter. In sigkdd, Speaker is a Person who gives presentations and has Author as a child class. Thus, edas:Author aligns more closely with sigkdd:Author (child of Speaker), while sigkdd:Speaker aligns more with edas:Presenter (child of Author). They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent; they are related.
Committee member is a person role in a conference committee, while Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (location), while organisedBy relates an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a Paper to a person who reviews it. However, cmt:readByReviewer has range strictly Reviewer, while edas:isReviewedBy has a broader range including Conference Chair, Session Chair, and TPC Member. Additionally, 'read by' implies the act of reading whereas 'reviewed by' implies completing a review. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.
Property A links a conference volume to its steering committee, while property B links a document to its speaker/presenter. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Accpet If Room Rating is a type of review rating (a classification outcome for a paper), while Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Paid applicant is a person who has paid to attend/register for a conference, while Travel Grant is a type of sponsorship/funding. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a complete academic paper submission, while Registration form is an administrative document for conference registration. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a paper), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a type of deadline (a point in time). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting paper submissions, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while Accepting manuscript is an administrative activity related to paper acceptance. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used to communicate information, while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a specific subject area/topic for papers. They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent an Author in the conference domain—someone who writes/submits papers or gives talks. Despite differing hierarchical placements (cmt places Author under Conference Member; iasted places it under Speaker > Delegate), their intended instances coincide: persons authoring contributions to a conference.
Both classes represent social events at a conference (e.g., receptions, excursions/trips, banquets/meals). They share the same intended instances and similar children, making them equivalent.
Registration form is a document/form used for registering, while Hotel is a physical place for accommodation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking an Item to a Time indicating temporal ordering. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (has an email) has domain Person and represents a person's email address, while property B (contact Email) has domain Contribution and represents the contact email for a paper/submission. Different domains and different intended meanings make them unrelated.

Both classes represent a Reviewer in the conference domain: a person who reviews papers. Despite differences in parent hierarchy (Conference Member vs Person) and associated properties, their intended instances coincide as people performing the reviewer role.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing the first author of a contribution (a person role), while Proceedings is a class representing a published volume of conference papers (a document). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Workshop is an academic working event (a session for presenting and discussing research), while Free Time Break is a non-academic break event during a conference. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a type of Scientific Event (with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial), whereas Speaker in sigkdd is a type of Person (with children Author, Invited Speaker). They are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. person) and are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Conference airport is a physical place/building. They share only the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

A Welcome Talk is a specific ceremonial talk at the opening of a conference, while a Plenary lecture is a lecture delivered to all attendees in a plenary session. Both are types of conference talks/lectures but serve different purposes and are not equivalent. They are related as sibling-like concepts under the broader category of conference presentations.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (subclass of Chairman) responsible for chairing the conference, while IASTED non member in iasted is a type of delegate who is not a member of IASTED. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent scheduled occurrences at a conference. confOf:Event has children like Administrative event, Social event, and Working event, while iasted:Activity has children like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference. Both have temporal properties (ends on/starts on vs is dated on/is held after/is held before). In the conference domain, Event and Activity are standard synonyms denoting the same concept.

locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while is_dated_on is a datatype property linking an Activity to a dateTime value. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, 'Member' is a subclass of Participant with siblings Regular and Student, indicating it refers to a general conference member/attendee (likely a confTool role). In ekaw, 'OC Member' specifically denotes an Organising Committee member, which is a distinct organisational role. While both are types of conference participants, they represent different concepts: one is a general attendee/member, the other is a committee member. They overlap in that both are participants but are not equivalent.
Property A links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, while Property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Paper in cmt refers to a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Record of attendance in iasted is an administrative document tracking who attended. They are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

AcademiaOrganization in edas refers to academic institutions (universities, research centers) as a type of organization, while OrganisingAgency in ekaw refers to the entity responsible for organizing the conference. These are conceptually different roles; an academic institution could serve as an organising agency but they are not equivalent concepts. They are related as both are types of organizations in the conference domain.
Acceptance is a type of decision regarding a paper submission, while Banquet is a social event at a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a research topic/subject area, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Active Paper in edas is a Paper that has been submitted and is under review (has Rating), which is a specific state of a Submission. Submission in iasted is the general class for submitted documents (with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript). Thus Active Paper is subsumed by Submission.

Program Committee Member (cmt) and Conference Chair (edas) are distinct roles in conference organization. A PC member reviews papers as part of the program committee, while a Conference Chair is the overall chair of the conference. In edas, the equivalent of Program Committee Member would be TPC Member, not Conference Chair.

A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Measurements) while B is a type of presentation event (Contributed Talk). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Both properties link a Person to some artefact (Document/Item). 'authorOf' specifically denotes authorship of a document, while 'prepare' is more general (preparing an item, which could be a paper, presentation, etc.). They overlap in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent.

Conference in Ontology A represents the overall conference event/organization, while Conference days in Ontology B is a subclass of Time representing the temporal duration (days) of a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'paperInVolume' relates a paper to a volume/proceedings. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Tip (a gratuity, subclass of Money) and Registration fee (a conference registration charge, subclass of Fee) are entirely different financial concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'name' is a datatype property for the name of a Conference or Person (range: string), while property B 'hasEndDateTime' is a datatype property for the end date/time of a Conference Event (range: dateTime). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while relatedToEvent relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers, while Neutral Review is a type of Review document. They are entirely different concepts (agent vs. artefact).

Topic in confOf represents a subject area or research topic (used as range of dealsWith, expertOn, hasTopic), while Event in ekaw represents an occurrence such as a scientific or social event. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper, while Transparency in iasted is a type of document (likely overhead slides or presentation transparencies). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Accommodation Place is a type of location for lodging, while Shuttle bus is a type of transport vehicle. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Chairman in cmt is a general class for chair roles (Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, Associated Chair), while PC Member in ekaw specifically denotes a member of the program committee. Although ekaw's PC Chair is a child of PC Member and cmt's Program Committee Chair is a child of Chairman, the two classes themselves are not equivalent: one represents chairs broadly, the other represents PC members. They overlap via their respective PC Chair subclasses but are not equivalent overall.

Both classes represent persons who serve on conference committees. In Ontology A, 'Committee member' has children Chair and Co-chair and is linked to Committee via membership properties. In Ontology B (sigkdd), 'Organizator' has children including Organizing Committee member, Program Committee member, General Chair, and Program Chair. Despite the different labels, their intended instances (people organizing/serving on conference committees) coincide, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

Both properties express a start date/time, but they differ in domain: confOf's 'starts on' applies to any Event (conferences, sessions, etc.), while edas's 'startDate' applies specifically to Conference. Since Conference is a kind of Event in the conference domain, the edas property is more specific. They are related but not equivalent.
'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is sent by' relates an Item to a Person (sender). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Ontology A's Paper is a general class for regular conference contributions (papers), while Ontology B's Accepted Paper is a specific subclass of Paper that has been evaluated and accepted. Therefore, A's Paper subsumes B's Accepted Paper.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'set Max Papers' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while 'organised By' relates an Event to its organiser (Organisation or Person). They share no domain, range, or meaning.

A Paper Abstract is a summary of a paper, while a Camera Ready Paper is the final version of an accepted paper ready for publication. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with different intended instances.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (event organization). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'topicCoveredBy' links a Research Topic to Events or Papers, while 'design' links ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. They are unrelated.
The 'email' property represents an email address of a Person, while 'has Home Page' represents a URL/webpage of a Person. These are distinct contact/identification attributes and not equivalent.

Conference announcement is a type of document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Conference activity is an event or action occurring at the conference (e.g., lecture, coffee break, registration). They belong to entirely different categories in the domain.

Banquet in confOf is a specific type of Social event, while Social program in iasted is a broader category that includes Dinner banquet as a child class. Therefore, Banquet is subsumed by Social program.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Event is an occurrence such as a scientific or social event. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Reviewer and TPC Member are sibling classes under Person, meaning they are distinct roles. In ekaw, PC_Member is a subclass of Possible_Reviewer and serves as the primary reviewing role (with children like PC Chair, Session Chair). Thus edas:Reviewer aligns more closely with ekaw:Possible_Reviewer, while edas:TPC Member aligns with ekaw:PC_Member. The two classes overlap in function (both can review papers) but are not equivalent.

The property 'detailsEnteredBy' in cmt links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'relatesTo' in edas links a Document to various entities (events, conferences, persons). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignedByReviewer links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (an assignment relationship between people), while isReviewHistoryOf links a Personal Review History document to a Reviewer. These relate entirely different domain concepts and serve different purposes.

In Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a direct subclass of Person with children Chair and Co-chair, representing someone who serves on a committee. In ekaw, 'Possible Reviewer' is a superclass of 'PC Member' (Program Committee Member). While both relate to people involved in reviewing/committee work, they are not equivalent: Committee member denotes actual membership, whereas Possible Reviewer denotes anyone eligible to review (a broader pool that includes but is not limited to PC members). They overlap conceptually but are not the same class.
PC Member is a program committee member (a reviewer/organizer role), while Author is someone who writes a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference is an event (one edition of a conference). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.
Microelectronics Topic is a subject area for papers in edas, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass) in iasted. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Entity A ('Contribution 1th author') is a specific subclass of 'Regular author' representing the first/primary author of a contribution. Entity B ('Author') in confOf is a general class for any author who writes contributions. Since every first author is an author but not every author is a first author, A is subsumed by B.

Working event is a type of conference event (e.g., workshop, tutorial), while Non speaker is a type of delegate/attendee who does not present. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (likely to finalize/end the review process), while reviewes relates a PC Member to a Contribution (the paper being reviewed). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

In Ontology A, Paper is a general class for regular conference contributions. In Ontology B (edas), RatedPapers is a highly specific subclass of Paper (via Active Paper) representing only those papers that have already been rated. Therefore, edas:RatedPapers is strictly subsumed by Conference:Paper.
hasBiography relates a Person to their biographical text, while Name relates a Person to their name. These are distinct attributes with different intended meanings.

Property A 'is given by' links Presentation -> Active conference participant (inverse direction: the presenter gives the presentation). Property B 'give' links Person -> Activity, Item (forward direction: the person gives the activity/item). They express inverse directions of a similar giving relationship in the conference domain, so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A (relatedToEvent) links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event in edas, while property B (technicallyOrganisedBy) is a sub-property of organisedBy in ekaw linking something to its technical organiser. These properties have entirely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

In ekaw, Abstract is a specific subclass of Document (a summary of a paper/talk). In iasted, Document is a broad class encompassing forms, letters, submissions, etc. They are at different levels of specificity and denote different concepts; the ekaw Abstract is not equivalent to the general iasted Document.

'is Initiated By' links a Call (for papers) to the person who initiated it (e.g., Conference Chair), while 'is given by' links an Activity or Item to the Person who presents/gives it. These describe different relationships in the conference domain: initiating a call vs. presenting/delivering an activity.
Tutorial in ontology A is a conference event/part (a session type), while Tutorial Chair in ontology B is a person role (someone who chairs tutorials). These are fundamentally different concepts.

The property 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of printing mailing manifests, while 'follows' relates one Administrative event to another to indicate temporal or sequential ordering. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Workshop is a type of Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), representing a full workshop event. In ekaw, Poster Session is a type of Session dedicated to poster presentations, and Workshop Session is a separate sibling class. These denote different kinds of conference activities and are not equivalent.
Property A captures the last name (surname) of a Person, while Property B captures the first name (given name). These are distinct attributes and not equivalent.

Property A is an object property linking a Topic to a Conference part, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to its name (a string). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

has_short_title is a datatype property linking events to a string (a short title), while hasStartDateTime links conference events to a dateTime value. They represent entirely different concepts (title vs. start time) with different ranges.

Cd proceening (CD proceedings) is a type of publication containing conference papers, while Review is an evaluation document of a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Program Committee' is a specific committee type. In sigkdd, 'Committee' is a general class with 'Program Committee' as one of its children (alongside Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee). Therefore, cmt's Program Committee is subsumed by sigkdd's more general Committee class.

In cmt, Chairman is a general class with children including Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair. In confOf, Chair PC specifically denotes the Program Committee Chair. Therefore, cmt:Chairman subsumes confOf:Chair_PC, as the latter corresponds to only one of the former's subclasses.

Property A 'name' applies to Conference and Person entities (giving their names), while property B 'hasTitle' applies to Contribution (paper) entities (giving their titles). They have different domains and denote different concepts (name vs title), so they are unrelated.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while 'organises' in ekaw relates organisations or persons to events they organise. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to the Conference Event it is part of. These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A ('has a location') denotes the physical or virtual location of a conference volume, while property B ('has Name') denotes the full name of a conference. They capture entirely different attributes (location vs. name) and are therefore unrelated.
hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic, while presentation links a Speaker to a Document. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while notification_until links an Author to a Deadline for author notification. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while Property B links a Document to events, conferences, sessions, or persons. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

A Flyer is a promotional document for the conference, while an Author information form is an administrative form used to collect author details. They serve entirely different purposes and are unrelated.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while CAD Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Written contribution in Conference ontology includes children like 'Regular contribution' and 'Submitted contribution', which are written papers, but its siblings include 'Poster' and 'Presentation', suggesting it covers all written textual contributions to a conference. In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is specifically a paper (with siblings like Poster Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). Written contribution is broader than Conference Paper because it may encompass other written artefacts beyond just papers, while Conference Paper is strictly a paper submitted/presented at a conference. Thus Written contribution subsumes Conference Paper.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Camera Ready event is an administrative event/deadline in the conference process. They are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person (inverse usage), while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). They share no domain or range overlap and describe unrelated relations.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property on Call providing submission instructions text, while Name is a datatype property on Person providing a person's name. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

Presenter in edas is a subclass of Author (someone who presents their own paper), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Speaker with Author as a sibling, meaning it refers to a keynote or invited talk presenter rather than a paper author. They overlap in that both present at a conference, but they are not equivalent concepts.

Important dates (A) is a container class grouping multiple deadline dates for a conference volume (abstract submission, full paper submission, camera ready, acceptance announcement, start/end dates). Deadline (B) represents a single deadline point in time, with subclasses for specific deadlines (camera ready, notification, submissions, etc.). A subsumes B conceptually since Important dates aggregates multiple Deadlines, but they are not strictly equivalent as one is a collection and the other is an individual deadline.

Conference Venue Place in edas refers to the location where the conference is held (a type of Place), while Sponsor company house in iasted refers to the building/house of a sponsoring company. These are conceptually distinct types of places with no overlap in intended instances.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class encompassing all roles involved in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members). Active conference participant in Conference ontology specifically denotes participants who give presentations, excluding passive participants. They overlap but are not equivalent; Conference Member is broader and includes non-presenting roles like reviewers.

Workshop in Ontology A is a conference part (similar to Workshop Session in ekaw's siblings), while Demo Session in ekaw is a distinct type of session for demonstrations. They are different concepts; note that ekaw has 'Workshop Session' as a sibling of 'Demo Session', confirming they are not equivalent.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Applications) while B is an organizational committee. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Document refers to conference-related textual artefacts (papers, reviews, flyers, etc.). In iasted, Payment document is a financial instrument (bank transfer, cheque) under a different Document hierarchy. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Programme is a Document representing a conference schedule/programme, while Speaker is a Person who presents at the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
In confOf, 'Working event' is a superclass of Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop. In edas, 'Conference' is a specific type of event. Therefore, confOf's Working event subsumes edas's Conference.

Conference Event in edas is a broad class encompassing both academic and non-academic events at a conference. Conference Trip in ekaw is a specific type of Social Event (which itself would be a kind of non-academic event). Therefore, Conference Event subsumes Conference Trip.

Paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a registrant who has paid), while Payment document is a subclass of Document (a financial instrument like a cheque or bank transfer). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history (a record of an individual's publications), while Review in sigkdd is a document that evaluates a paper. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' and 'Conference contributor', representing an author who submits a regular paper/contribution. In Ontology B (iasted), 'Lecturer' is a subclass of 'Author' under 'Speaker' > 'Delegate', representing someone who gives a lecture/presentation at the conference. While both involve authors in a conference context, they capture different roles: one is about contributing a regular paper, the other about delivering a lecture. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Program Committee Member (cmt) and TPC Member (edas) both denote a member of the Technical Program Committee. TPC stands for Technical Program Committee, so these are synonymous concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for human individuals in their respective conference ontologies. In Ontology A, Person has children like Committee member, Conference participant, Reviewer, etc. In Ontology B (iasted), Person has children like Delegate and Sponsor. Despite different subclass structures reflecting each ontology's modeling choices, both represent the same general concept of a person involved in a conference context.

Reviewer (A) is a subclass of Speaker/Delegate who reviews papers, while Author (B) is a subclass of Speaker who writes and submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different intended instances.

Both properties express an organizing relationship for conference-related entities, but they differ significantly in domain and range. 'has an organizing committee' links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (a specific committee entity), while 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

A 'Short paper' in confOf is a type of Contribution (a full but brief research paper), while an 'Abstract' in ekaw is a summary document associated with a Paper via presentation properties. They represent different kinds of artefacts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.
Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, while Session Chair (B) is a specific role under Conference Participant in ekaw. Thus A subsumes B.

Accepted contribution and Rejected Paper are disjoint concepts: one represents a paper that was accepted after review, the other a paper that was rejected. They are siblings in their respective hierarchies (Accepted vs Rejected) and do not denote the same concept.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation responsible for publishing proceedings, while Organizing Committee is a Committee responsible for organizing the conference. They have different parents (Organisation vs Committee), different roles, and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.
Positive Review is a subclass of Review representing a favorable evaluation of a paper, while Abstract is a summary document of a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Document in edas refers to written artefacts (papers, reviews, slides), while Sponzor in sigkdd refers to financial supporters/sponsors of the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any person who authored a paper (subclass of Person). Student lecturer in iasted is a very specific subclass of Lecturer (which is under Speaker > Author > Delegate > Conference building > Building > Place), denoting a student who lectures. These are conceptually distinct: one is a broad author role, the other is a highly specific lecturing role with a student status. They do not denote the same concept.
Property A gives the last name of a Person, while property B gives the full name of a Conference. Different domains and different semantics; they are unrelated.

Lecturer in iasted is a general speaker/author role with subtypes Student lecturer and Worker lecturer. Author of paper student in sigkdd specifically denotes a student author. They overlap (Student lecturer is similar to Author of paper student) but Lecturer as a whole is broader and not equivalent to the student-specific class.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Class A 'Conference' represents the overall academic conference event/organization, while class B 'Conference Dinner' is a specific meal event (a social sub-event) that may occur during a conference. They denote entirely different concepts in the domain.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (a late-paying conference applicant), while Entity B is a subclass of Money/Fee (a member registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote fundamentally different concepts.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (street address), while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Author Not Reviewer (cmt) denotes an author who is not also a reviewer, while Contribution co author (Conference) denotes a co-author of a contribution. Both are subclasses of Author in their respective ontologies, but they capture different facets (reviewer status vs. authorship order/role). They overlap as both are authors but are not equivalent.
Author is a person who writes or submits papers, while Conference Session is an event/session at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Session in edas is an event/time slot during a conference, while Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (subclass of Document). These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different meanings, domains, and ranges. 'acceptsHardcopySubmissions' is a boolean property on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted, while 'has_a_volume' is an integer property on Conference proceedings indicating the volume number.

Both classes represent a room within a venue where conference sessions or meetings take place. 'Meeting Room Place' in edas and 'Session room' in iasted are both subclasses of 'Place' and serve the same purpose in the conference domain, making them equivalent.
Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (committee-of relation), while Property B links a Person to a Conference (membership relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

AccommodationPlace is a general class for places providing accommodation, while Single hotel room is a very specific type of hotel room. AccommodationPlace subsumes Single hotel room since a single hotel room is a kind of accommodation place.

An 'Extended abstract' is a type of regular conference contribution (a short paper/abstract submitted for review), while a 'Published Paper' in edas is a paper that has reached the published state. They differ both in document type (abstract vs full paper) and in lifecycle stage (contribution type vs publication status), so they are unrelated.

Decision (cmt) represents the outcome/verdict of a review process (Acceptance or Rejection), while Reviewed contribution (Conference) represents the paper/artefact that has been reviewed and can be accepted or rejected. They are closely related in the domain (a decision is made about a reviewed contribution) but denote fundamentally different concepts: one is an abstract verdict, the other is a document.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (part of reviewer assignment), while Property B links a Contribution (paper) to a Topic (subject area). They have different domains, ranges, and semantic purposes.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Platinum Supporter is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Both properties have the same domain (Author) and range (Paper), representing the act of an author submitting a paper. They are semantically equivalent.
Taxi is a transport vehicle class, while Listener is a person role at a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Time is a temporal concept. They are completely unrelated.

In edas, Programme is a specific type of Document representing a conference schedule/programme. In iasted, Document is a broad superclass covering many administrative and submission-related items (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). The edas Programme does not correspond to the general iasted Document class; they differ significantly in scope and intended instances.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document, while Company is a type of organization. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while obtain links an Author to an Award. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A links a conference volume to its organizing committee (a group), while property B links a conference to an individual person who is a member. They have different domains and ranges and express fundamentally different relationships.

Property A ('has the last name') is a datatype property on Person for surnames, while Property B ('has Title') is a datatype property on Contribution (paper) for titles. They have different domains and denote entirely different concepts.

enterConferenceDetails relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action), while hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (a subject-matter association). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

OC Member in ekaw refers to an Organizing Committee member of a conference, while IASTED member in iasted refers to a member of the IASTED organization attending as a delegate. These are conceptually different roles: one is a conference organizing role, the other is an organizational membership status.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the overall chair of the conference, while PC Chair (ekaw) is specifically the Program Committee Chair. In cmt, Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair are distinct siblings under Chairman. These are related but not equivalent roles.

Both properties link an event (or paper) to a topic/research topic it addresses. 'has Topic' in confOf and 'covers Topic' in ekaw serve the same semantic role: relating a conference entity to its subject matter. The domains (Working event vs Event/Paper) and ranges (Topic vs Research Topic) are closely aligned in the conference domain.
Sponsorship is a financial support concept (with cost and provider properties), while Person represents human individuals. They are entirely unrelated classes in the conference domain.

External Reviewer in cmt is explicitly someone who reviews on behalf of a reviewer but is NOT themselves a program committee member/reviewer. Member PC in confOf is a program committee member who reviews contributions. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

Trip (confOf) and Conference Banquet (ekaw) are both social events at a conference, but they denote different specific activities. Trip corresponds to 'Conference Trip' in ekaw (a sibling of Conference Banquet), not to Conference Banquet itself. They are related as sibling concepts under the same parent category.
has an email refers to a person's email address, while has First Name refers to a person's given name. These are distinct attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

hasStartDateTime specifically denotes the start date/time of a Conference Event, while is_dated_on is a more general property indicating when an Activity is dated. They overlap in relating event-like entities to dateTime values but differ in specificity (start vs. general date), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A links a Track workshop chair (person) to a Conference part they chaired, while Property B links an Activity/Item to the Person who gives it. The domains and ranges are reversed in direction and differ in specificity; these properties describe different relations.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Card is a physical item (e.g., credit card). They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasMenu links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu, while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Call For Reviews is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting reviews), while Review is a Document (the actual review artefact). They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Acceptance in cmt is a type of Decision (the outcome of accepting a paper), while Receiving manuscript in iasted is an Activity (the act of receiving a submission). These are fundamentally different concepts; the iasted equivalent of Acceptance would be 'Accepting manuscript'.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), while property B 'reviewWrittenBy' links a Review to the Possible Reviewer (the person who wrote it). They share the same domain (Review) but have entirely different ranges and semantics; they are unrelated.

Call For Reviews is a type of Call (an invitation to submit reviews), while Negative Review is a type of Review (a document expressing a negative evaluation). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (providing sponsorship), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level (e.g., high, medium, low), while property B links a paper to an actual Review object. The ranges (Review expertise vs Review) and the semantics are entirely different.

Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in a conference, while State in iasted is a geographical or administrative region (with children like Conference state, Presenter state being sub-regions or status locations). They are entirely different concepts.

Chair in Ontology A is a committee chair (subclass of Committee member), while Scholar in Ontology B is a person who studies at a university (a price category). These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Working event is a type of conference event (e.g., workshop, tutorial), while Cryptography Topic is a specific subject topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, PaperAbstract is a subclass of Paper (a specific version/format of a paper), while in ekaw, Abstract is a sibling of Paper under Document and represents an abstract document that can be for papers, invited talks, or tutorials. They overlap conceptually as both represent abstracts, but their hierarchical placement and intended instances differ significantly.

Property A (assignedTo) links a Paper to a Reviewer, indicating an assignment relationship. Property B (reviews) links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, indicating which paper a review evaluates. They have different domains (Paper vs Review), different ranges (Reviewer vs Reviewed contribution), and express fundamentally different relations in the conference domain.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Conference Paper in ekaw is a type of document/paper submitted to a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Conference in Ontology B is a subclass of Event/Working event (the conference itself). These are entirely different concepts.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline (a subclass of Deadline). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subtype of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version'). In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a subtype of Paper representing a full paper submitted/presented at a conference (sibling of 'Camera Ready Paper', 'Demo Paper', etc.). These denote fundamentally different concepts: one is an abstract document component, the other is a complete conference paper.
Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Author is a person who writes and submits papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered details), while Property B links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where it was submitted). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Renting is an activity performed before a conference (subclass of Activity before conference). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a person/role who chairs the program committee, while Program Committee (sigkdd) is the committee itself (a group). They are related but not equivalent; one is a chair of the other.

'rejected By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (rejection action), while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events (temporal parallelism). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Passive conference participant is a subclass of Person (a role for attendees who do not actively present), while Conference Banquet is a subclass of Event (a social activity). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and are unrelated.

Property A ('done till') represents the end date of a Deadline, while Property B ('Start of conference') represents the start date of a Conference. They have different domains (Deadline vs Conference), different semantics (end vs start), and apply to different concepts, making them unrelated.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and sibling to 'Conference Chair', suggesting it refers to an Associate/Co-Chair role rather than the top General Chair. In sigkdd, 'General Chair' is the primary organizer (under Organizator), with 'Program Chair' as a separate sibling. These are distinct organizational roles that overlap in the broader concept of conference chairs but are not equivalent.

hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members, while parallel_with links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A gives the title of a Paper, while property B gives the last name of a Person. They have different domains and completely different semantics.

A Workshop Paper is a specific type of academic paper presented at a workshop, while a Mailing list is a communication tool or document used for distributing information. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Accpet If Room Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a classification/decision outcome), whereas Review in sigkdd is a subclass of Document (the actual review document). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a rating category, the other is a document type.
Conference Member is a person participating in a conference, while Fee is a monetary charge. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent social activities at a conference. confOf's 'Social event' has children Banquet, Reception, Trip; iasted's 'Social program' has child Dinner banquet and sibling Coctail reception. They cover the same concept of non-academic social gatherings during a conference.

'writtenBy' links a Document to its author (Person), while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to the person who presents it (Speaker). Writing and presenting are distinct roles in the conference domain; an author is not necessarily the presenter and vice versa. They share the same domain (Document) but have different semantics, so they are related but not equivalent.
hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Workshop Session is a specific subclass of Session (alongside Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.). In iasted, Session is a broader class under Lecture. The ekaw Workshop Session is a more specific type of the iasted Session, so ekaw's Workshop Session is subsumed by iasted's Session.
University in confOf is a subclass of Organization, while Organisation in ekaw is the general class (with Academic Institution as a child). Thus University is subsumed by Organisation.

Both properties link a scholarly artefact (Paper in cmt, Working event in confOf) to its subject/topic classification (Subject Area vs Topic). The concepts 'Subject Area' and 'Topic' are synonymous in the conference domain, but the domains differ slightly: Paper is more specific than Working event (which also includes non-paper events). Thus they are closely related but not strictly equivalent.
hasPostalCode relates Contact Information to a postal code string, while Name relates Person to a name string. They have different domains and represent entirely different concepts.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level Working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference. In ekaw, Poster Session is a specific type of Session within a scientific event. These are distinct concepts: one is the whole conference, the other is a particular session format.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has applied and registered for a conference (with children like Paid applicant), while an 'Organizator' is a person involved in organizing the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair). These are distinct roles with no overlap.

'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'updatedVersionOf' relates a Document to another Document as a versioning link. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties express where an event takes place, but they differ fundamentally in modeling: confOf:location is a datatype property with range string, while ekaw:heldIn is an object property with range Location (a class). They capture the same real-world relation but are not equivalent due to different ranges and property kinds.

Conference in edas represents the academic event itself, while Conference restaurant in iasted is a physical building/place (subclass of Building) where meals might be served during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is an event (a scheduled activity for participant registration), while Entity B is a document/form used during registration. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Document) and are not equivalent.

Country (confOf) represents a nation, while Location (ekaw) is a general place where events are held. A country is a type of location, so Country is subsumed by Location, but they are not equivalent since Location can also be cities, venues, etc.

'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of Person representing an attendee who does not actively present, while 'Conference state' is a subclass of State representing a status or condition related to the conference. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while OC Member is a person role (Organizing Committee member). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Track is a conference part (like a session track), while Tax is a type of Money. They are completely unrelated concepts.

PC Member in ekaw is a specific role (member of the program committee), while Organizator in sigkdd is a broader class encompassing all organizing roles including General Chair, Webmaster, and Program Committee member. PC Member overlaps with one child of Organizator but is not equivalent to the whole class.
Chairman is a person role (a type of Person who chairs something), while Break Event is a type of non-academic conference event (e.g., coffee break). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper Full Version (cmt) refers to the complete version of a paper as opposed to an abstract, while Demo Paper (ekaw) refers to a specific category/type of paper (a demonstration). They are both subclasses of Paper but represent different classification dimensions and are not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference for entering review criteria, while 'has Reviewer' links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer to assign reviewers.

Chairman in cmt refers to a leadership/organizational role (Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, etc.), while Conference contributor in the Conference ontology refers to people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants). These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

Conference www is a web document/URL resource (subclass of Conference document), while Conference days is a temporal concept (subclass of Time). They represent entirely different aspects of a conference and are unrelated.

In confOf, Workshop is a top-level Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), representing an entire workshop event. In ekaw, Regular Session is a type of Session (a sub-event within a conference), and Workshop Session is actually a sibling of Regular Session. Thus, these two classes represent different concepts at different granularities and are not equivalent.

Both properties express authorship/writing, but A is specifically for reviews (domain: Review, range: Possible Reviewer) while B is a general writing property (domain: Item, range: Person). They overlap in intent but differ significantly in specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Rejection is a decision outcome regarding a paper submission, while Banquet is a social event at a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

The properties have different domains (Sponsorship vs Money) and different ranges (Organization vs Person). 'providedBy' links a sponsorship to the sponsoring organization, while 'is paid by' links money to a person who pays it. These are conceptually distinct relations in the conference domain.

Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Card (with child Credit card) refers to a payment or identification card. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while locationOf relates a Location to an Event (venue). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'searched by' relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
