Despite different property vocabularies, both denote the same general concept of a person involved in a conference.

Both classes represent commercial/industry organizations within their respective ontologies. confOf's 'Company' (sibling of University under Organization) and edas's 'Industry Organization' (sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO under Organization) denote the same concept: a business or industry entity involved in the conference domain.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a person/role (subclass of Reviewer), while Review in ekaw is a document (subclass of Document). They represent fundamentally different concepts (a reviewer vs. the review they write) and are unrelated.

In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a specific subclass of Chairman (alongside Conference Chair and Associated Chair), denoting the chair of the program committee. In Conference, Co-chair is a sibling of Chair under Committee member, typically referring to a co-chair of the overall conference. These are related leadership roles but not equivalent: one is specifically the PC chair, the other is a general co-chair.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a general class for regular conference contributions (a sibling of Extended abstract). In Ontology B, 'Assigned Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Submitted Paper', which itself is a subclass of 'Paper'. Thus, the general 'Paper' in A subsumes the more specific 'Assigned Paper' in B.

Submission event is an administrative event (activity) for submitting contributions, while Organizing Committee is a committee (group of people). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Conference Banquet is a social event. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and represents people who interact with the system (Administrators, Authors, Reviewers). In sigkdd, Person is the top-level class for all people (Listeners, Organizators, Speakers). The cmt User class is more specific than the sigkdd Person class, so User is subsumed by Person.

A Workshop is a working event (like a conference or tutorial) typically involving multiple sessions and participants, while an Invited Talk is an individual presentation given by a speaker. They are distinct types of events in the conference domain with different intended instances.

Accommodation Place refers to lodging (e.g., hotel rooms), while Session room refers to a room where conference sessions are held. These are distinct types of places with different intended instances.
Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document), while Author of paper student is a subclass of Author (a person). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper submission, while Van is a type of transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Invited speaker is a conference contributor who presents at the event, while Webmaster is an organizer responsible for web infrastructure. They are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.

Reviewed contribution in Ontology A is a paper/submission that has been reviewed (a subclass of Submitted contribution), whereas Review in Ontology B is the review document itself. These are distinct concepts: one is the thing being reviewed, the other is the review artefact.

A 'Single hotel room' is a specific type of room within a hotel, while 'Hotel' is the building/establishment itself. They are related (a single hotel room is located in a hotel) but not equivalent, nor is one a subclass of the other.

Conference document refers to written artefacts (papers, reviews, announcements), while Activity refers to events or actions (before/after conference activities). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Both classes represent a place where conference participants dine. 'Dining Place' in edas and 'Conference restaurant' in iasted refer to the same concept in the conference domain.

Both properties capture the abstract of a contribution/paper, but they differ fundamentally in modeling: A is an object property linking to an Abstract class instance, while B is a datatype property linking to a string literal. They are related (same conceptual role) but not equivalent.

Conference Session in ekaw is a type of scientific event (a session within a conference), while Conference days in iasted is a temporal concept representing the days on which a conference takes place. They belong to different conceptual categories (event vs. time) and are unrelated.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Cheque is a payment document. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and share no semantic overlap.

'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership), while 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (authorship/signature). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

hasFirstName captures a person's first name (a name component), while hasBiography captures biographical information about a person. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they represent entirely different attributes.
Decision represents the outcome of a paper review (acceptance/rejection), while Country represents a geographical nation. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (academic affiliation), while 'is visited by' relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (physical visitation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume (membership/part-of relation), while Property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal parallelism). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reception (confOf) and Conference Trip (ekaw) are both subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different kinds of social events. In confOf, Reception is a sibling of Trip, while in ekaw, Conference Trip is a sibling of Conference Banquet. They share the same parent concept (Social Event) but are not equivalent to each other.
Entity A is a student registration fee while Entity B is a non-member registration fee. They are distinct sibling concepts under Registration fee in their respective ontologies.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and a sibling of 'Program Committee Chair', indicating it is a distinct role (likely an Associate/Co-Chair of the conference). In ekaw, 'PC Chair' is the Program Committee Chair. These are different specific chair roles within a conference organization, so they are related but not equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is an announcement document inviting people to participate in a conference, while 'Conference Proceedings' is a published volume of accepted papers. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a type of conference contribution (oral talk), with Invited talk as a child. In Ontology B, 'Power Point presentation' is a specific format/medium of delivering a presentation (a child of Presentation). They are related in the conference domain but not equivalent: one denotes the act/type of presenting, the other a specific slide-based delivery method.

Property A links a conference contribution to a conference volume (submission relation), while property B links a conference to a person (membership relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-of hierarchy), while Property B relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (parallel scheduling). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'follows' expresses a temporal/sequential ordering between Administrative events, while property B 'inverse of part Of 7' is an inverse meronymic (part-whole) relation with range Event. They model fundamentally different relationships.
heldIn relates an Event to a Location (spatial), while is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal). They have different ranges and express fundamentally different relations.

In Ontology A, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person with child 'Registeered applicant', indicating someone who applies/registers for the conference. In Ontology B, 'Participant' is also a subclass of Person (with children Regular, Student) and has an 'early Registration' property, suggesting it refers to registered attendees. However, Ontology B separately defines Author, Chair PC, Member PC, etc. as siblings of Participant, while Ontology A places Committee member, Conference contributor, Reviewer as siblings of Conference applicant. An 'applicant' is not necessarily yet a 'participant' (they must be accepted/registered first), so they overlap but are not strictly equivalent.

Preference in cmt represents a reviewer's topic or paper preference (e.g., bidding), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw represents a person who can serve as a reviewer. These are entirely different concepts.

Student is a subclass of Person representing an academic role, while Bronze Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor representing a funding tier. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
partOfEvent relates an Event to a containing Event (mereological), while award relates something to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area/topic within a conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Entity A 'Committee' is a class representing an organizational body (with subclasses like Organizing committee, Program committee), while Entity B 'Organizing Committee member' is a class representing a person who is a member of the organizing committee. One is a group/committee, the other is a person/role; they are fundamentally different concepts.

Reception in confOf is a social event (like a welcome party) occurring as part of the conference. Activity before conference in iasted refers to pre-conference administrative or preparatory tasks (accepting manuscripts, renting, etc.). These are entirely different concepts.

Assigned Paper in ekaw is a paper that has been submitted and then assigned (e.g., to reviewers), making it a specific stage after submission. Submission in iasted is a general class for any submitted document (with children like Final manuscript, Initial manuscript). They overlap conceptually as both relate to submitted papers/documents, but Assigned Paper is more specific (post-assignment) while Submission is broader (any submitted item). Thus they are related but not equivalent.

attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (attendance), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Banquet and Reception are both subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different specific types of social events (a formal meal vs. a welcome gathering). They are siblings/related concepts, not equivalent.
Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Hotel presenter is a type of delegate (a person). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while City is a geographical location. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Presenter is a Person (a conference participant who presents), while Introduction of speaker is an Activity (the act of introducing a speaker). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself, with properties like date, logo URL, and accepting submissions. In ontology B (Conference), 'Conference participant' is a subclass of Person representing someone who participates in the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Participant is a person attending the conference, while Renting is an activity performed before the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

'written By' relates a Document to its author (Person), while 'is visited by' relates a location (Building, City, State) to a visitor (Person). These are entirely different relations with different domains and semantics.

Both properties express the relationship between a location/place and an event/activity in the conference domain. However, they are inverses of each other: 'locationOf' has domain Location and range Event, while 'is held in' has domain Activity and range Place. Since inverse properties are not equivalent, they are related.

In cmt, Conference Member is a subclass of Person (which is not shown but implied by the path 'Person > Conference Member'). In edas, Person is the top-level class for people. The children of cmt's Conference Member (Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, Program Committee Member) align with children of edas's Person (Author, Conference Chair, Reviewer, TPC Member). Thus, cmt:ConferenceMember corresponds to edas:Person, meaning cmt:ConferenceMember is subsumed by edas:Person.

In edas, Paper is a submitted scholarly document (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper), while Review is a separate sibling class representing the evaluation of a paper. In iasted, Review is also an evaluation document, and Submission is the sibling that corresponds to edas:Paper. Thus edas:Paper and iasted:Review are entirely different concepts.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is paid with' relates Money to an Item (payment). These are entirely different relations in both domain/range and semantics.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, with children Active and Passive conference participant. Student (B) is a specific type of Participant (a role-based subclass). Thus, Conference participant subsumes Student, as every Student is a conference participant but not vice versa.

Active conference participant in Ontology A refers to someone who gives presentations (e.g., speakers, authors), while Conference Chair in Ontology B is an organizational role responsible for initiating calls and managing reviews. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and no subsumption relationship.

An Organizational Meeting in edas is an academic event for organizational purposes (e.g., committee meetings), while an Industrial Session in ekaw is a conference session dedicated to industry-related presentations. They serve different purposes and have different positions in their respective hierarchies.
Property A links 'Important dates' to a 'Conference volume', while property B links a 'Conference Event' to a 'Programme'. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

In cmt, Paper is a Document (a written submission with authors, reviews, decisions). In iasted, Research is an Activity before conference (with children Modelling and Simulating), representing the act of conducting research, not a document artefact. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Topic in confOf refers to a subject area or theme of a paper/event, while Time in iasted refers to temporal concepts (days, deadlines). They are completely unrelated.
Presenter is a person role (subclass of Conference Participant), while 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a document type (subclass of Document). They are entirely different concepts.

Administrative event is a type of event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B 'technicallyOrganisedBy' relates an event or entity to its technical organizer. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference city is a geographical location (a type of City). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers (subclass of Person/Conference Member), while Poster in Conference is a type of conference contribution/document. They represent entirely different concepts (a role vs. an artefact) and are unrelated.
Invited Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (someone who gives a talk), while Non speaker is explicitly someone who does not speak/present. These are disjoint concepts.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them, while write links a Person to an Item they authored. These are entirely different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference, while 'has a publisher' relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. They are unrelated.

Property A 'has a name' is a general naming property with domain including Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc., while property B 'Name of conference' is specifically scoped to Conference. Thus B is more specific and is subsumed by A.

A 'Mailing list' is a distribution list document used for communication, while an 'Abstract' is a summary of a paper. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

Rejected contribution is a document/artefact (a paper that was rejected), while Accepting manuscript is an activity/event (the process of accepting a manuscript). They differ in both kind (document vs. activity) and semantics (rejected vs. accepting), so they are unrelated.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (sibling to Paper Presentation, Talk Event). In ekaw, Conference Session is a broader class whose sibling is Workshop Session. Thus edas:Workshop corresponds more closely to ekaw:Workshop_Session, while ekaw:Conference_Session is more general. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

Rejected contribution is a specific outcome (rejected) of a reviewed submission, while Evaluated Paper is the general class of papers that have been evaluated, which includes both Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper as children. Thus Rejected contribution roughly corresponds to ekaw's Rejected Paper, not to the broader Evaluated Paper. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the deadline by which authors are notified of paper acceptance. 'Deadline for notification of acceptance' (iasted) and 'Deadline Author notification' (sigkdd) denote the same concept in the conference domain, both being subclasses of Deadline with matching semantics.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer, while design links ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Meta Review is a type of review document (a written evaluation), while Textual Review Question is a type of question used in the review form. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and are unrelated.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submitting a paper). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a broad class encompassing Extended abstracts and Papers (full papers) that are written contributions to a conference. In Ontology B, 'Submitted Paper' specifically denotes a paper that has been submitted (and is a subclass of Paper). While both relate to standard scholarly submissions, Regular contribution is broader (includes extended abstracts) and does not necessarily imply the submission status that Submitted Paper does. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

Property A relates an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details), while Property B relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (mereological relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Mobile Computing Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In confOf, 'Conference' is a type of Working event (sibling to Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference as an event. In edas, 'Conference Session' is a sub-part or session within a conference. A whole conference and a session within a conference are distinct concepts, so they are unrelated.
The properties have completely different domains and ranges (Conference->Administrator vs Author->Contribution) and describe unrelated actions (entering review criteria vs writing a contribution).
The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'forEvent' links a Call to an Academic Event.

A Conference Session is a time-bound event or meeting slot within a conference, whereas Conference Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume) containing the published papers. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for anyone participating in a conference, with children Active and Passive participants. Session chair (B) is a specific role of a delegate who chairs a session. A Session chair is a kind of Conference participant, so A subsumes B, but they are not equivalent.
Invited speaker is a person who gives a talk at a conference, while Research Institute is an academic organization. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

In ontology A, 'Program Committee' is a specific committee type. In ontology B, 'Committee' is a general class with 'Program committee' as one of its children (alongside Organizing and Steering committees). Therefore, A's Program Committee is subsumed by B's more general Committee class.

Both classes are named Document and serve as the top-level class for conference-related written artefacts. They share key children (Paper, Review) and are linked to Person via authorship/interest properties. Although ekaw's Document has additional subclasses (Flyer, Programme Brochure, etc.), the core intended instances—papers and reviews submitted or produced in a conference context—coincide, making them equivalent in the reference alignment.
hasSubjectArea links a paper to its subject area/topic, while has_an_abstract links a paper to its abstract content. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and purposes.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item they prepare. They are unrelated.
heldIn relates an Event to a Location (spatial), while is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (temporal). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties share the name 'obtain' and relate a person-like entity to something they receive. However, in iasted the range is the very general 'Item' (domain Person), while in sigkdd the range is specifically 'Award' (domain Author). Since Award is a specific kind of Item and Author a specific kind of Person, the sigkdd property is more specific. They are related but not strictly equivalent; one could argue subsumes, but given the different ontological contexts and granularity, 'related' is the safest alignment verdict.

memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference, while End_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime. They describe entirely different relations.
Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee (membership/role), while Property B relates an Event to a Location (venue). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and semantics (finalizing paper assignments vs issuing proceedings). They are unrelated.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding process), while reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment). These are conceptually distinct relations in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference website to its URL string, while Property B is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference announcement is a type of document (e.g., call for papers), while Single Level Conference is a type of conference event structure. They are entirely different concepts.
Lecture is a conference activity (event), while Speaker is a person role. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (indicating who added the member), while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (indicating who holds/organizes the conference). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Both properties link a Paper to its Author with identical domain and range, expressing the same authorship relation using synonymous phrasing ('has Author' vs 'is Written By').

Administrator in confOf is a general administrative role (e.g., system or conference admin), while PC Chair in ekaw is specifically the chair of the Program Committee. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and intended instances.

Property A is an object property (Person -> Item) representing sending an item, while Property B is a datatype property (Person -> string) representing an email address. They differ in type, range, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference Member to a Conference (individual membership), while Property B links a Conference volume to an Organizing committee (committee assignment). These relate different domain and range classes and express fundamentally different relationships.

Property A links a conference contribution to the conference volume it was submitted to, while property B links a speaker to a document they present. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

hasCostCurrency specifies the currency of a sponsorship cost (domain: Sponsorship, range: string), while has_amount_of specifies a numeric monetary amount (domain: Money, range: int). Currency and amount are distinct concepts; these properties relate different things with different domains and ranges.

Organization in edas refers to institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorships, while Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. These are entirely different concepts.

Chair in Ontology A is a committee chair (with Co-chair as sibling), while Program Committee member in Ontology B is a general member of the program committee (with Program Chair and General Chair as siblings). A Chair is a more specific leadership role than a generic committee member. They are related but not equivalent; if anything, Chair would subsume Program Committee member since chairs are also members, but given the different hierarchies they are best classified as related.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI string representing its website URL, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location instance representing the physical venue. They differ in type (datatype vs object), range (anyURI vs Location), and intended meaning (web address vs physical location).
Accepted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been accepted), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for finalizing paper assignments, while write relates a Person to an Item for authoring. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to a topic it addresses. However, ekaw's coversTopic has domain Event or Paper (broader than confOf's Contribution which is just papers), and the range differs slightly (Research Topic vs Topic). They overlap significantly for the Paper->Topic case but are not strictly equivalent due to the broader domain in ekaw.

Both classes represent a Workshop as a type of event within the conference domain. In confOf it is under 'Working event' and in ekaw under 'Scientific Event', but both serve the same purpose: a workshop held as part of a conference. Their sibling classes (Conference, Tutorial/Session) confirm they occupy the same conceptual role.

Personal History in edas is a class representing an individual's historical record (with children like Personal Publication History and Personal Review History), whereas Review in sigkdd is a document type (sibling of Paper and Abstract) representing a review of a submission. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Building is a physical place/structure. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Early paid applicant is a subclass of Person representing a conference registrant who paid early, while Published Paper is a subclass of Document representing a paper that has been published. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Both classes are named 'Review', share the same parent class 'Document', and appear in the conference domain context. They represent the same concept: a review document of a paper.

Session Chair in ekaw is a role responsible for chairing a session (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). One day presenter in iasted is a delegate who presents for one day. These are distinct roles; notably, iasted has its own 'Session chair' class as a sibling of 'One day presenter', confirming they are different concepts.
Review is a document evaluating a paper, while Departure tax is a type of monetary tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., signing a document), while property B 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Track in Conference refers to a thematic track within a conference (e.g., parallel sessions), while Tip in iasted refers to a gratuity (a type of Money). These are completely unrelated concepts.

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positiveInteger (maximum number of choices), while organisedBy is an object property linking events to their organizing Organisation or Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Record of attendance is a Document (an artefact tracking who attended), while Author is a Person (someone who writes and submits papers). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Chairman is a general class with children including Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair. In sigkdd, Program Chair is a specific role (child of Organizator) alongside General Chair. Thus, cmt:Chairman subsumes sigkdd:Program_Chair since Program Chair is one type of Chairman.

In edas, 'Conference Dinner' is a child of 'Meal Event', making Meal Event a broader class covering all meal-related events (including Break Event siblings). In iasted, 'Dinner banquet' is a specific type of social program event corresponding to a dinner/banquet. Therefore, 'Dinner banquet' is more specific than and subsumed by 'Meal Event'.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (an artefact-to-artefact relation), while property B 'reviewerOfPaper' links a Possible Reviewer (a person) to a Paper. The domains and ranges are fundamentally different kinds of entities, so these properties are unrelated.

Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (the event they chair), while Property B links a Call to the person who initiated it (a chair or TPC member). The domains, ranges, and directions are entirely different; they describe unrelated relations.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (member -> conference), while hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person (event -> attendee). They are roughly inverse in direction and differ in domain/range specificity, so they are related but not equivalent.

External Reviewer in cmt is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another reviewer, while Author in iasted is a speaker who authored a work. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a temporal deadline by which papers must be submitted. They are conceptually distinct entities in the conference domain—one is a document, the other is a date/deadline.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Speaker is a person who presents. They are entirely different concepts.

The properties have opposite directions and different semantics: 'hasRelatedPaper' links an Author to a Paper, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (inverse direction). They are not equivalent.

Conference in cmt represents the conference event/organization itself, while Conference hotel in iasted is a physical building (subclass of Place > Building) where attendees may stay. These are entirely different concepts.

acceptedBy links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (indicating it has a review). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Track is a type of scientific event. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (abstract for a tutorial) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewed contribution is a specific type of conference document (a paper that has been reviewed), while Activity in iasted is a broad class representing events or actions (with children like Conference activity, Activity before/after conference). They denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

cmt:writePaper links an Author to a Paper, while ekaw:authorOf links a Person to a Document. In the conference domain, Author corresponds to Person (as author) and Paper is a kind of Document. The two properties express the same authorship relation but with slightly different domain/range specificity (Paper vs Document), making them related rather than strictly equivalent.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g., sub-events), while is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'name' applies to both Conference and Person and likely represents a full name or general name string. Property B 'hasSurname' applies only to Person and specifically denotes the family/last name. They overlap for persons but differ in scope (domain) and specificity (full name vs surname), so they are related but not equivalent.
readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reviewing context), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation context). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Hotel fee is a monetary charge for accommodation. They belong to entirely different categories and are not semantically related.

Property A is a specific datatype property for the abstract submission deadline within 'Important dates', while Property B is a general date property for an 'Activity'. They differ in domain (Important dates vs Activity), specificity (abstract submission date vs generic date), and intended use, making them unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of conference part (often involving tutorials or research presentations), while an Industrial Session is a specific type of conference session focused on industry topics. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with different parents and purposes.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Tutorial is a type of scientific event/presentation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents their paper). In iasted, Hotel_presenter is a subclass of Delegate (a conference attendee staying at the hotel) and is a sibling of Speaker and One day presenter. The iasted 'Hotel presenter' appears to denote a delegate associated with a hotel rather than someone presenting a paper, so it is not equivalent to edas Presenter. They are loosely related as both involve people at a conference.

Workshop is a type of working event (a meeting/session), while Cd proceening is a type of publication (a CD containing proceedings). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Closing Talk is a specific ceremonial talk at the end of a conference, while Invited Talk is a presentation by an invited speaker. Both are types of talks/presentations at academic events, so they are related (siblings under a common 'talk' concept), but they denote different kinds of talks and are not equivalent.
Event in ekaw refers to conference activities (scientific or social events), while Time zone in iasted refers to a geographical time region. These are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A refers to the camera-ready paper submission date with domain 'Important dates', while Property B refers to the general paper submission deadline with domain 'Conference'. They represent different deadlines (camera-ready vs. initial paper) and have different domains, so they are not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'topicCoveredBy' links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper, while 'designed_by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD. They are unrelated.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while OC Chair is a person role (Organizing Committee Chair). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Paper in ekaw is a type of document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Conference building in iasted is a physical place/building where the conference takes place. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to submitted artefacts (papers, posters, talks as documents), while Academic Event in edas refers to scheduled conference events (meetings, presentations, workshops). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a document/submission, the other is an event/activity.

Personal Review History represents a reviewer's history of reviews in edas, while Research Topic represents a subject area covered by papers or events in ekaw. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

hasFirstName specifically denotes the first/given name of a person, while Name is more general and could represent a full name. Thus hasFirstName is subsumed by Name, but they are not strictly equivalent.

In cmt, Review is a general class for all reviews (with child Meta Review). In ekaw, Neutral Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Positive and Negative Review). Thus, the cmt Review class subsumes the ekaw Neutral Review class.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (preference relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Antennas Topic is a subject area classification (a topic), while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

confOf 'Chair PC' denotes the chair of the program committee (a leadership role), while ekaw 'PC Member' denotes a general member of the program committee. In ekaw, 'PC Chair' is a subclass of 'PC Member', confirming that the chair role is distinct from and more specific than a regular member. Thus confOf's Chair PC corresponds to ekaw's PC Chair, not to the broader PC Member class. They are related but not equivalent.
detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Late Registered Participant is a person (a type of conference participant). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

paperID is a datatype property assigning a numeric identifier to a paper, while paperPresentedAs is an object property linking a paper to its presentation format. They are entirely different concepts.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization (with sibling University). In edas, Organization is the top-level class with children like Academia Organization and Industry Organization. Thus confOf:Company is strictly more specific than edas:Organization, making it subsumed by edas:Organization.

Both classes represent the academic/working portion of a conference as opposed to social or administrative events. confOf's 'Working event' (children: Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) and edas's 'Academic Event' (children: Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop) serve the same role in their respective ontologies, partitioning conference events into scholarly vs. non-scholarly categories.
hasDecision links a Paper to its acceptance/rejection Decision, while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a website), while Author is a person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the role of a person who authors or writes papers in the conference domain. cmt's Author is defined by properties like writePaper and submitPaper, while ekaw's Paper_Author serves the same purpose as a Person subclass. They denote the same concept.
Paper Full Version is a type of academic document (a complete paper), while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier for the conference. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Review' and share the same parent class 'Document' within their respective conference ontologies. They both represent the concept of a review document in the conference domain.
Trip is a social event (an organized excursion), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent or related in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a 'Review expertise' entity to an unspecified value (likely a level of expertise), while Property B is an object property linking an 'Active Paper' to a 'Review Rating'. They have different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker indicating who presents it. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review in Ontology A is a document (subclass of Conference document) representing the written evaluation of a paper. Conference Chair in Ontology B is a person role (subclass of Person) who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
A Review Form is a template or form used for conducting reviews, while a Paper is a submitted academic document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering of sending), while property B relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Trip day is a subclass of Time representing days allocated for travel, while Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline representing the due date for submitting papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference contribution refers to academic submissions (papers, posters, talks) while Tax refers to a financial charge under Money. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Review in Ontology A is a document that reviews a contribution (child of Conference document), while Contribution in Ontology B represents the submitted work itself (Paper, Poster, Short paper). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Dining Place refers to a location for eating meals, while Hotel room refers to accommodation/lodging. They are distinct types of places with different intended instances and purposes in the conference domain.
Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) while Presentation is a conference activity (subclass of Activity). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Contribution 1th author in Ontology A is a specific role (first/primary author of a contribution), while Author in Ontology B is a general class for all authors. Every first author is an author, but not every author is a first author, so A is subsumed by B.

Property A ('is designed for') relates activities/money/time to activities/persons (indicating purpose or target), while property B ('designed by') relates deadlines to an organization (ACM SIGKDD) indicating the creator. They have different directions, domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'addedBy' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while 'providedBy' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (that provides it). They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt refers to any person participating in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members), while Delegate in iasted refers specifically to a registered attendee of the conference. They overlap as both are persons involved in the conference, but they are not equivalent: Conference Member includes roles like Reviewer and Author that are not necessarily Delegates, and Delegate is more about attendance/registration.

Both properties link a Paper to an author-type entity, but 'has Co author' specifically targets co-authors (a subset of authors), while 'is Written By' targets any Author. They overlap in meaning but are not strictly equivalent; 'has Co author' is more specific.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'has Updated Version' relates a Document to an updated version of itself. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendance), while prepare relates a Person to an Item (preparation). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Personal History in edas is a class representing an individual's historical record (with children Personal Publication History and Personal Review History), whereas Review in ekaw is a document that evaluates a paper. These are entirely different concepts.

Web Site in ekaw is a type of document representing a website (used to list events), while Paper in sigkdd is a scholarly paper submitted by an author. These are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

In edas, TalkEvent is a specific kind of AcademicEvent (with children ClosingTalk, WelcomeTalk and sibling PaperPresentation), representing an individual talk. In ekaw, ScientificEvent is a broad category encompassing Conference, Session, Track, Workshop, and IndividualPresentation. While both relate to the scientific/academic program of a conference, their scopes differ significantly: ekaw's ScientificEvent is much broader (including entire conferences and sessions), whereas edas's TalkEvent is narrower (a single talk). They overlap in intent but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an acceptance announcement date, while Property B is an object property linking programme brochures or web sites to events. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Non Academic Event in edas refers to social/break/meal events at a conference, while Conference in ekaw refers to the entire scientific event (one edition of a conference). These are completely different concepts.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered details, while 'parallel_with' links two Administrative events that occur simultaneously. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a specific role (member of a committee, with children Chair and Co-chair), distinct from its sibling 'Conference participant'. In Ontology B, 'Conference Participant' is a broad class covering anyone participating in the conference (including presenters, registered participants, chairs, etc.). These are not equivalent; Committee member is a much narrower concept than Conference Participant.
Conference announcement is a type of document (e.g., call for papers), while Reception is a social event at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference in Ontology A represents the conference event/organization itself (with children like Conference volume and properties like has a name), while Place in edas represents a physical location or venue (with children like Accommodation Place, Dining Place). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference document refers to documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, announcements), while City refers to a geographical location. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Author), ranges (Conference vs Contribution), and semantics (running paper assignment tools vs writing contributions). They are unrelated.

Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's topic or paper preference for assignment purposes, while ReviewForm in edas is a document/template used to structure the review process. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organization in edas represents an institutional entity (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorship, while Money in iasted represents a financial concept (fees, tips, taxes). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Entity A is a research topic related to computer networks measurements, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Entity A is a Review (an evaluation of a paper), while Entity B is a Paper (the submitted contribution). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain. Note that edas also has its own 'Review' class as a sibling of Paper, confirming they are different.

Rejection in cmt is a type of Decision (the outcome), while Receiving manuscript in iasted is an Activity before conference (a process step). They are conceptually different kinds of entities. The closer match to Rejection would be Refusing manuscript in iasted, but even that is an activity rather than a decision object. Thus they are only loosely related within the paper-handling workflow.

In cmt, Review is a general class for all reviews (with child Meta Review). In ekaw, Positive Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Negative and Neutral Review). Therefore, the general Review in cmt subsumes the more specific Positive Review in ekaw.
'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks, while 'has City' relates an Organization or Person to a City. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference participant refers to someone attending or taking part in the conference (with children Active/Passive participant), while Sponsor refers to a person providing financial support. These are distinct roles with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

In iasted, Form is a type of administrative document (registration forms, hotel forms, etc.), while in sigkdd, Paper is a scholarly submission. They are distinct concepts under Document and are unrelated.

In Ontology A, 'Review' is a subclass of 'Conference document', representing the written review artefact (linked via properties to reviewed contributions). In Ontology B, 'Reviewing event' is a subclass of 'Administrative event', representing the reviewing procedure or phase in the conference timeline. One is a document/artefact and the other is an event/process, so they are unrelated.
Meta Reviewer is a specialized type of reviewer who evaluates papers and other reviews, while Author is a person who writes contributions. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Property A (date) has domain Conference and represents the date of a conference, while property B (is_a_starting_date) has domain Important dates and represents the starting date of an important date/deadline. They have different domains and different intended meanings, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in the conference (with children like Author, Reviewer), while Track in Conference ontology is a sub-event or thematic division of a conference (sibling of Tutorial, Workshop). These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, Chairman is a general class with children including Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair. In sigkdd, General Chair is a specific role (the main conference chair) alongside Program Chair as a sibling. Therefore, cmt:Chairman subsumes sigkdd:General_Chair.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Performance Topic in edas is a type of Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In confOf, Workshop is a top-level Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial). In ekaw, Conference Session is a type of Session, and Workshop Session is one of its siblings. Thus, confOf:Workshop corresponds more closely to ekaw:Workshop_Session rather than ekaw:Conference_Session. They are related as both pertain to conference scheduling units but are not equivalent.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'writtenBy' links a Contribution to its Author (inverse direction: paper -> author), while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they present. The domains, ranges, and directions differ significantly; these are not equivalent properties.

Organization in confOf represents institutions like companies and universities that employ people, while Place in sigkdd represents physical locations like conference halls, hotels, and offices where people can stay. These are fundamentally different concepts (organization vs. location).

Property A links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while Property B links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who gives the presentation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Deadline for notification of acceptance refers to when authors are informed of paper acceptance decisions, while Deadline Abstract Submission refers to the deadline for submitting abstracts. These are distinct events in the conference workflow and not equivalent.

Meta Review is a summary review written by a meta-reviewer based on other reviews, while Negative Review is a review with a negative recommendation. Both are subclasses of Review but represent different classification dimensions (role/purpose vs. sentiment), so they are related but not equivalent.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who performed the assignment), while hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their PersonalReviewHistory. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

In edas, Conference Event is a high-level concept with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event, representing the conference as a whole or its major event types. In iasted, Conference activity (child of Activity) represents specific scheduled activities within a conference such as lectures, coffee breaks, registration, and cocktail receptions. Thus, edas Conference Event is more general and subsumes iasted Conference activity.

'Information for participants' is a conference document providing logistical or instructional information to attendees, while 'Cd proceening' (CD proceedings) is a specific publication medium containing the papers of a conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Decision in cmt represents the outcome of a paper review (acceptance/rejection), while Call in edas represents an invitation to submit papers or reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Document is a broad class encompassing papers, reviews, abstracts, flyers, etc. In iasted, Form is a specific subclass of Document (Item > Document > Form) covering registration forms and author information forms. Thus ekaw:Document subsumes iasted:Form.

CAD Topic is a subject area (a subclass of Topic) related to Computer-Aided Design, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (subclass of Abstract). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent a Workshop as a type of academic/working event within a conference context. Despite different sibling structures and parent labels (Working event vs Academic Event), the intended instances coincide: workshops held as part of a conference.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Performance Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-of relation), while Property B relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A is a datatype property (remark) on Contribution with string range, while B is an object property (obtain) on Person with Item range. They differ in kind, domain, range, and semantics.

Person in iasted is a general class (with children Delegate, Sponsor), while Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (with siblings Listener, Organizator). Thus, the iasted Person subsumes the sigkdd Speaker.

Property A (isReviewedBy) links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while Property B (write) links a Person to an Item they authored. These represent entirely different relations (reviewing vs. writing) with different domains and ranges.

The property 'remark' has domain Contribution (a paper/submission) and represents a comment or note, while 'Name' has domain Person and represents a person's name. They have different domains, ranges of application, and semantics.

Review in cmt is a peer-review document written by a reviewer for a paper, while Publication in iasted refers to published proceedings (books, CDs). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Break Event is a type of non-academic conference event (e.g., coffee break), while Speaker is a person who presents at the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Conference is the main conference event/organisation entity. In ekaw, Conference is a sibling of Individual Presentation under Scientific Event, meaning Individual Presentation refers to a single talk/presentation slot, not the conference itself. These are entirely different concepts.
Co chair is a person role (committee member), while Location is a place where events are held. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker). Two Level Conference in Ontology B is a subclass of Conference representing a type of conference event. These are fundamentally different concepts (a person role vs. a conference type) and are unrelated.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Positive Review is a type of document/review. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a short paper/abstract), while Active Paper in edas denotes a paper that is currently under review or active in the submission process (a status-based subclass of Paper). They represent different concepts: one is a document format/type, the other is a workflow state.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History document. These properties have completely different meanings, domains, and ranges.

In edas, Conference is the main conference event with properties like paper due dates and country. In iasted, Activity is a broader concept that includes 'Conference activity' as a child, along with pre- and post-conference activities. Thus, edas:Conference roughly corresponds to iasted's 'Conference activity' subclass, making Activity more general. They overlap but are not equivalent.

In Ontology A, 'Active conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference contributor' and 'Conference participant', specifically denoting participants who give presentations (with siblings like Passive conference participant). In ekaw, 'Conference Participant' is the general class for all participants (including chairs, registered participants, etc.). Thus, the more specific 'Active conference participant' from A is subsumed by the broader 'Conference Participant' in B.
Meta Review is a document (a type of review), while Reviewer is a person/role who performs reviews. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (presentation/delivery). Different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

has_title is a datatype property linking events to their string titles, while hasEvent is an object property linking events to other events. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference (metadata about what they can/want to review), while Property B links a PC Member to a Contribution they actually review. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'held In' relates an Event to a Location, while 'searched by' relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to the conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Conference days is a subclass of Time representing temporal duration of the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Rejected contribution (A) is a document/artefact class representing a paper that was rejected, while Receiving manuscript (B) is an activity/event class representing the act of receiving a manuscript. They belong to different ontological categories (document vs. activity). The related concept in B would be 'Refusing manuscript' as a sibling activity, but even then one is a thing and the other is a process. They are only loosely related through the rejection/refusal theme.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while is_paid_by links Money to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution, while Deadline Abstract Submission is a type of deadline. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference fees refers to the monetary charges for attending a conference, while Conference Proceedings refers to a published document containing the papers presented at the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

'has title' is a datatype property for the name/title of social or working events, while 'City of conference' specifies the city where a conference is held. They describe entirely different attributes and have different domains.

Property A (technicallyOrganises) relates an Organisation to something it organises technically, while Property B (presentationed_by) relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Contribution 1th author is a role for paper authors, while Single hotel room is an accommodation type. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Early paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a registrant who paid early), while Accepting manuscript is a subclass of Activity (the process of accepting manuscripts). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

cmt:writtenBy links a Review to its Reviewer (inverse direction of writing), while iasted:write links a Person to an Item (forward direction of writing). They are related as they both concern authorship/writing in the conference domain, but they differ in direction (one is effectively the inverse) and in specificity (Review->Reviewer vs Person->Item), so they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Document is a class for written artefacts (papers, reviews, abstracts, etc.). In iasted, Item is a much broader physical/logistical entity class whose children include audiovisual equipment, transport vehicles, cards, and documents. They do not denote the same concept; if anything, iasted's Document would be a subclass of ekaw's Document, but Item is far too general to be equivalent or directly subsuming in the conference-document sense.

In edas, Break Event and Social Event are sibling subclasses of Non Academic Event, meaning they are disjoint concepts (breaks vs. social gatherings). In ekaw, Social Event is a direct subclass of Event covering banquets and trips. Since edas explicitly distinguishes breaks from social events, the two 'Social Event' classes do not denote the same concept; they merely overlap as types of non-academic conference activities.
A Conference hall is a venue for conference sessions, while a Hotel is an accommodation facility. Both are subclasses of Place but represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Paper is a scholarly submission with authors, reviews, and decisions, while Mailing list is a communication document. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

Sponsorship in edas is an abstract concept representing financial support (with cost amount/currency and provided by an Organization), while Sponsor in iasted is a subclass of Person (an individual who sponsors). They are related in the sponsorship domain but denote fundamentally different things: one is a funding arrangement, the other is a person.
Property A links a conference volume to its organizing committee, while property B links administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme, while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Accommodation Place in edas refers to lodging for conference attendees (sibling of Conference Venue Place, Dining Place), while Sponsor company house in iasted refers to the building/house of a sponsoring company. These are conceptually distinct types of places with no overlap.

TPC Member in edas is a specific role (Technical Program Committee member) under Person, while Conference Participant in ekaw is a broader class encompassing many roles (OC Member, PC Chair, Session Chair, Presenter, etc.). A TPC Member is a type of conference participant, so TPC Member is subsumed by Conference Participant.

'writtenBy' links a Document to its author (Person), while 'is given by' links an Activity or Item to the presenter/giver (Person). These are different relations with different domains and semantics in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a conference in the academic domain. EKAW's comment 'One edition of a conference' and EDAS's properties (dates, country, name, topics) confirm they denote the same concept: a specific instance/edition of an academic conference.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting people to participate, while 'Deadline hotel reservation' is a temporal deadline for reserving a hotel. They belong to entirely different categories (document vs. time/deadline) and are unrelated.
Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (committee-of relation), while Property B links a Conference to a Person (membership relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Company in confOf is a commercial organization (sibling of University), while Government Organization in edas is a public-sector entity. They are disjoint subclasses of Organization with different intended instances.

Both are subclasses of Person representing administrative or support staff in a conference context. However, 'Administrator' (confOf) is a general administrative role, while 'Agency Staff Member' (ekaw) specifically refers to staff from an external agency. They overlap in function but are not strictly equivalent; they are related as similar support-staff roles.

A Workshop is a sub-event of a conference focused on interactive sessions, while a Plenary lecture is a specific type of lecture given to all attendees. They are distinct types of conference activities with different intended instances.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Programme Brochure in ekaw is a document listing conference events. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.
Property A links an organizing committee to a conference volume, while Property B links a building/city/state to a person. They describe entirely different relationships in the domain.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Value added tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

A 'Published Paper' is an individual paper that has been published (a subclass of Paper in edas), while a 'Book proceeding' is the entire proceedings volume (a subclass of Publication in iasted). A published paper may appear within a book proceeding, but they are distinct concepts: one is a single contribution, the other is the collection/container. They are related but not equivalent.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference (domain: Reviewer, range: Review expertise/Review preference). Property B is the inverse of 'hasReviewHistory', linking a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain: Personal Review History, range: Reviewer). They relate different concepts in different directions and are not equivalent.

hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Regular contribution in Conference is a broad category of contributions (including papers, extended abstracts) that are not invited talks or posters. Assigned Paper in ekaw is a specific lifecycle stage of a paper that has been submitted and then assigned to reviewers. These represent different concepts: one is a type/category of contribution, the other is a processing state of a paper.
Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area for conference papers, while Transport vehicle is a physical means of transportation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Session in iasted is a subclass of Lecture/Activity representing a conference event. These are entirely different concepts.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring), while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Topic in confOf refers to a subject area or theme of a paper/event, while Place in iasted refers to a physical location (building, room, etc.). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Program Committee to its individual members (Program Committee -> Program Committee Member), while Property B links a Conference volume to its Program Committee as a whole (Conference volume -> Program committee). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while Radio Communications Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person representing attendees, while Break Event is a subclass of Conference Event representing non-academic schedule items like coffee breaks. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A (readByMeta-Reviewer) has domain Paper and range Meta Reviewer, linking a paper to the meta-reviewer who reads it. Property B (reviewes) has domain Member PC and range Contribution, linking a PC member to the paper they review. The domains and ranges are reversed in direction (A: Paper->Person, B: Person->Paper), and the roles differ (meta reviewer vs. PC member reviewer). They are not equivalent, nor inverses of each other in a matching sense, so they are unrelated.

'has parts' is a mereological relation linking a conference volume to its constituent parts, while 'holded by' links a conference to its organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are semantically unrelated properties with different domains and ranges.

Both classes represent the same concept of an organization/organisation in the conference domain. The spelling difference (Organization vs Organisation) is merely British vs American English. Both have children that are types of organizations (Company/University vs Academic Institution/Organising Agency/Proceedings Publisher), and both participate in properties relating to people, events, or locations typical of organizational entities.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision (an act/outcome), while Rejected contribution in Conference is a type of document/contribution that has been rejected. They are closely related (a Rejection decision applies to a contribution making it a Rejected contribution) but they denote different kinds of entities: one is a decision event, the other is a document.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the process/activity of submitting contributions), while B 'Deadline Abstract Submission' is a deadline (a specific point in time by which abstracts must be submitted). They are related concepts in the submission workflow but belong to different categories (event vs. deadline) and are not equivalent.

Scholar in confOf is a subclass of Person (a role for someone who studies at a university), while Author attendee cd registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Money/Registration fee (a financial concept). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (with siblings Regular and Student), representing a general conference participant/member. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a subclass of Organizator, representing someone who helps organize the conference. These are distinct roles: one is an attendee-level membership, the other is an organizing role. They overlap in that both are people involved in the conference, but they are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Presenter is a superclass of Invited Speaker and a sibling of Session Chair, meaning it denotes someone who presents content. In iasted, Session chair is a role for managing/leading a session, with Speaker as a separate sibling class. These are distinct roles (presenting vs. chairing), though both are types of conference participants, so they are related but not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges. 'has Review History' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, while 'has Review' links a Paper to a Review. They describe different relationships in the conference domain.
Program Committee in cmt is a committee/group entity, while Scholar in confOf is a type of Person (a price category for attendees). They are entirely different concepts.

'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. The domains, ranges, and directions differ entirely; they describe different relationships in the conference domain.

Both properties share the same name and range (Country), but their domains differ significantly: confOf's hasCountry applies to Organization and Person, while edas's hasCountry applies to Conference. Since they relate different kinds of entities to a country, they are not equivalent but semantically related.

Entity A is 'Organizing committee' while Entity B is 'Program Committee'. These are distinct types of committees within a conference organization, as evidenced by the fact that sigkdd (Ontology B) lists both 'Organizing Committee' and 'Program Committee' as siblings.
