They are related as sibling concepts under Committee but not equivalent.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while go_through links an Item to an Activity (a process or event). These properties have different semantics, domains, and ranges, and are unrelated.

Author in edas is a Person who writes papers, while Author information form in iasted is a Document/Form used to collect author details. They are entirely different concepts (a person vs. a document).
The properties have completely different domains (Person vs Sponsorship) and semantics (first name vs cost currency). They are unrelated.

Paper Author is a person who writes papers (subclass of Person), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor (subclass of Sponzor). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person (a specific role). In Ontology B, 'Person' is the top-level class for all people. Thus, Committee member is subsumed by Person.

The 'abstract' property describes the abstract text of a Contribution (paper), while 'Currency' describes the currency of a Registration fee. They have completely different domains and semantic meanings.

registrationDueOn is a specific property linking Conference to a dateTime for registration deadlines, while done_till is a general property linking Deadline to a date indicating when any deadline occurs. They differ in domain (Conference vs Deadline), range (dateTime vs date), and specificity (registration-specific vs generic deadline).

Banquet and Excursion are both subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different specific types of social events (a formal dinner vs. a trip/outing). They are siblings under the same parent concept, hence related but not equivalent.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events indicating they occur simultaneously, while 'give' relates a person to an activity or item they provide. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (title) applies to Paper and gives its full title, while property B (has short title) applies to Social event/Working event and gives a shortened title. Different domains and different semantics (full vs short title), so they are unrelated.

Short paper in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), while Rejected Paper in ekaw is a paper classified by its review outcome (rejected vs accepted). These are orthogonal classifications and denote entirely different concepts.
Tutorial in ekaw is a type of scientific event/presentation, while Computer in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts.

Reviewed contribution (A) is a paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Review (B) is the review document itself. They are distinct but related concepts: A is the domain/range of properties involving B.

Written contribution in Conference refers to papers/submissions contributed to a conference (including submitted and regular contributions), while Publication in iasted refers to published proceedings (book proceedings, CD proceedings). They overlap conceptually as both relate to written/published conference materials, but they are not equivalent: one is about the contribution act/artefact before or during the conference, the other is about the formal publication output.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting submissions, while Main office is a physical place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a reviewed contribution (paper) to its review, while property B links a reviewer to their personal review history. They have completely different domains and ranges and express different relationships.

Academic Institution in ekaw is an Organisation (e.g., University, Research Institute), while Building in iasted is a physical Place/structure. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (parent of Invited Speaker), while IASTED member in iasted is a membership status of a delegate within the IASTED organization. These are conceptually distinct: one describes a role at the conference, the other an organizational affiliation.

Both are subclasses of Author in their respective ontologies, but they denote different specializations: 'Co author' (cmt) is any co-author of a paper, while 'Author book proceedings included' (iasted) is specifically an author whose work appears in the book proceedings. They overlap but are not equivalent.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while need links a Person to an Item (a requirement). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

minChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positiveInteger (minimum number of choices), while Start_of_conference links a Conference to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'email' property represents an email address, while 'hasSurname' represents a person's last name. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they denote entirely different attributes.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Book proceeding is a type of publication. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (a session or meeting), while Worker lecturer in iasted is a type of person (a lecturer who is also a worker). These are entirely different concepts.

In confOf, 'Short paper' and 'Poster' are sibling subclasses of Contribution, meaning they are distinct types. In ekaw, 'Poster Paper' is a subclass of Paper. A short paper (brief research paper) is conceptually different from a poster paper (paper accompanying a poster presentation). Therefore, these two classes denote different concepts and are unrelated.
Paper Full Version is a type of academic document (a complete paper), while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a conference document to its author (Person), while property B links a Person to a Conference Event they attend. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A refers to the date of acceptance announcement (domain: Important dates), while Property B refers to the submission deadline (domain: Call). These are distinct events in the conference lifecycle with different domains and meanings.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (paper), while property B 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. They have completely different domains and ranges and represent distinct relationships in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Registration deadline is a temporal deadline for conference registration. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.
Member PC in confOf is a Person (a reviewer), while Review in ekaw is a Document (the written review itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Both properties link a Paper to a topic/subject area (Subject Area vs Research Topic are equivalent concepts). However, 'coversTopic' in ekaw has a broader domain (Event or Paper) while 'hasSubjectArea' in cmt is restricted to Paper. They overlap significantly on the Paper-to-Topic relation but are not strictly equivalent due to the domain difference.

topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to Events or Papers that cover it, while write relates a Person to an Item they authored. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

reviewsPerPaper is an integer datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while has_a_name is a string datatype property providing a name for various entities. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
'Information for participants' is a type of conference document, while 'Trip day' is a type of time/date. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Presenter city is a geographic location (city). They are completely unrelated concepts.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the conference system (authors, reviewers, administrators). Research in iasted is a subclass of Activity before conference representing research tasks like modelling and simulating. These are entirely different concepts.

TalkEvent in edas represents a talk (with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk), while Demo_Session in ekaw is a session dedicated to demonstrations. These are distinct types of conference events with different intended instances.

Reject Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a classification/score assigned to a review), while Negative Review in ekaw is a subclass of Review (the actual review document with negative sentiment). They are conceptually distinct types (rating vs. document) but semantically related as both represent the negative/rejection aspect of the review process.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference). In sigkdd, Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount/fee category). One denotes a type of person, the other a type of fee; they are unrelated concepts.
Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while Review is a type of Document (an evaluation of a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Poster Paper is a specific type of full paper (a sibling of Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.), while Abstract is a short summary document distinct from a Paper in the sigkdd ontology. They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of 'Person'. In Ontology B, 'Person' is the general class for people. Therefore, 'Committee member' from A is subsumed by 'Person' from B, as every committee member is a person but not every person is a committee member.
Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity (event), while Organizator is a type of Person who organizes the conference. They are completely different concepts.

Regular in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while Registration SIGKDD Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote fundamentally different concepts.

hasCity is an object property linking Organization/Person to a City class, while City_of_conference is a datatype property linking Conference to a string. They differ in domain, range type (object vs datatype), and the kind of entity they describe the city for.

Conference Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a type of Chairman) responsible for chairing the conference. Delegate in iasted is a general term for any conference attendee/participant, with children including speakers, listeners, and session chairs. A Conference Chair is not equivalent to a Delegate; they represent different concepts (a specific role vs. a general participant).

Student is a type of conference participant (person), while Platinum Supporter is a type of sponsor (organization). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.

In confOf, Author is a Person who writes a Contribution. In sigkdd, Speaker is a broader class (parent of Author and Invited Speaker) representing anyone who gives a presentation. Since sigkdd's Speaker subsumes its own Author class, confOf's Author is more specific than sigkdd's Speaker but they overlap in the conference domain (authors often present their papers). They are related but not equivalent.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (PC), while OC Chair in ekaw refers to the Organizing Committee Chair. These are distinct roles within conference organization (program vs. organizing committee), so they are related but not equivalent.

'partOf' is a general mereological (part-whole) relation with unspecified domain/range, while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., signing a document). They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of 'Author', representing specifically a co-author of a paper. In sigkdd, 'Author' is the general class for all authors (with children like 'Author of paper'). Therefore, cmt's Co author is subsumed by sigkdd's Author.

The 'name' property in cmt provides a name for a Conference or Person, while the 'abstract' property in confOf provides an abstract text for a Contribution. These are entirely different concepts with different domains and semantics.

Poster Session in ekaw is a specific type of Session (a sibling of Conference Session, Demo Session, etc.), while Session in iasted is a more general concept under Lecture/Conference activity. Therefore, the iasted Session subsumes the ekaw Poster Session.

Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (indicating committee membership of a conference), while Property B links an Event to an Organisation or Person (indicating who organised the event). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while Property B is an object property linking an Item to an Activity or Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume (an organizational/structural relation), while Property B links an Event to another Event (a mereological part-of relation between events). Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Both properties link a person/author to a paper/item they are associated with writing. However, 'has Related Paper' is broader (any related paper) while 'write' specifically denotes authorship. They overlap but are not strictly equivalent.
Committee member is a person role in a conference committee, while Meeting Room Place is a physical location for meetings. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A (is_paid_for) has domain Money and range Activity/Item, expressing what money pays for. Property B (pay) has domain Person and range Registration_fee, expressing who pays a fee. The domains, ranges, and directions differ fundamentally, so they are unrelated.

Publisher in Ontology A is a general class representing an entity that issues conference proceedings. ACM SIGKDD in Ontology B is a specific organization that holds conferences and designs deadlines. They represent different concepts with different roles in the domain.
In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document, while in sigkdd, Document is the parent class that includes Paper, Abstract, and Review as children. Thus, cmt:Paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Document.

Both classes represent the concept of a sponsor fee/payment in the conference domain. Despite being placed under different parent classes (Money vs Fee) due to differing ontology design choices, their intended instances coincide: money paid by or associated with sponsors.
Reception is a social event (like a cocktail reception), while Presentation is an academic activity involving presenting work. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who performed the assignment), while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible_Reviewer (who is assigned to review it). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantic meanings.
Call for paper is a type of conference document (an invitation to submit papers), while Security Topic is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They are entirely different concepts.

Working event is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Antennas Topic is a specific research Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology.

Entity A is a class representing a person who authors a paper, while Entity B is a class representing a specific type of registration fee (money). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Review Rating is a class representing the rating/score given to a paper (e.g., accept, reject), while Possible Reviewer is a class representing a person who can review papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference city in iasted is a type of City (a location). They represent fundamentally different concepts.
University is an organization where scholars study, while Meal Menu is a document describing food options for a meal event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
'is made from' relates Item to Item (derivation/composition), while 'obtain' relates Author to Award (receiving an award). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers specifically to submitted works (papers, posters, presentations, talks) and is a subclass of Conference document. Document in edas is a much broader class that includes not only papers and reviews but also meal menus, programmes, and slide sets. They overlap on the concept of papers/contributions but are not equivalent; they are related.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award/honor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

A 'Plenary lecture speaker' is a specific type of invited speaker who delivers a plenary lecture, while 'Invited Speaker' in sigkdd is a more general category that could include keynote speakers, plenary speakers, and other invited presenters. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; Invited Speaker subsumes Plenary lecture speaker.
has First Name captures a person's given name, while E mail captures their email address. These are distinct attributes of a Person and not equivalent.

Review in iasted represents a review document (a type of Document), while Paper in sigkdd represents a submitted paper. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; notably, sigkdd itself has a separate Review class as a sibling of Paper.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Powerline Transmission Topic is a specific conference topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
Paper in cmt is a submitted document (child of Document), while Call For Reviews in edas is an announcement/call (child of Call). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A gives the issue date of a conference document, while property B gives the start date/time of a conference event. They have different domains (Conference document vs Conference), different ranges (date vs dateTime), and entirely different semantics.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite the unusual parentage including Person/TPC Member), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a type of person who speaks at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In confOf, 'Assistant' is a sibling of Volunteer and Administrator, likely referring to a student/research assistant or helper role at the conference. In ekaw, 'Agency Staff Member' refers to personnel from an external agency (e.g., travel or staffing agency). These denote different roles in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person representing an individual participant (author, reviewer, chair, etc.), while Committee in the Conference ontology is an organizational body (e.g., organizing committee, program committee) that has members. One is a person role, the other is a group/organization, so they are unrelated.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author submits paper), while writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (document is written by person). They differ in both direction and semantics: one describes a submission action, the other authorship. Even though their domains/ranges overlap conceptually (Author~Person, Paper~Document), the properties themselves are not equivalent nor inverses in a strict alignment sense.

Property A links a Paper Presentation to its corresponding Accepted Paper, while property B links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes in the conference domain.
Ontology A's 'Topic' is a general class for conference topics, while Ontology B's 'Medicine Topic' is a specific subclass of 'Topic'. Therefore, A's Topic subsumes B's Medicine Topic.

Submitted contribution is a document/paper artefact (subclass of Conference document), while Author is a person who writes papers. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Pending Paper in edas refers to a paper's review status (awaiting decision), while Regular Paper in ekaw refers to a paper's submission track/type (as opposed to demo, poster, industrial). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.

defaultChoice is a datatype property mapping events to a positiveInteger (likely a selection or preference indicator), while hasEndDateTime maps conference events to a dateTime representing the end time. They have different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Both classes represent a member of the Program Committee (PC Member). In cmt, Program Committee Member is a Conference Member/Person with PC-related properties; in ekaw, PC Member is a Possible Reviewer/Person with PC Chair as a child. Despite different parent hierarchies, their intended instances coincide: people serving on the program committee.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Fee is a monetary charge. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing the start date. They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain, range, and semantic meaning.

cmt:Person is a general class for all people in the conference domain (with children like Chairman, Reviewer, etc.), while edas:TPC Member is a specific subclass of edas:Person representing Technical Program Committee members. Thus cmt:Person subsumes edas:TPC Member.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference Dinner is a social event (a type of Meal Event). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties express a start date, but they differ in domain (Important dates vs Event) and range (date vs string). They capture overlapping semantics (a starting date for something in the conference domain) but are not strictly equivalent due to different domains.

A Call (e.g., Call for Papers) is an announcement inviting submissions, while a Deadline is a temporal constraint by which something must be done. They are related because a Call typically has a submission deadline, but they are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

Accepted contribution is a document/artefact (a subclass of Conference contribution) representing a paper that has been accepted. Receiving manuscript is an activity/event (subclass of Activity before conference) representing the process of receiving a manuscript. They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. activity) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Conference Session in edas represents a temporal/organizational session of a conference, while Place in iasted represents a physical location. These are fundamentally different concepts with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Both properties express a writing/authorship relation, but they differ significantly in specificity. 'reviewWrittenBy' has domain Review and range Possible Reviewer (a specific type of person), while 'write' has domain Person and range Item (very general). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent; 'write' is more general.

TextualReviewQuestion in edas is a type of review question (a form field or criterion used during reviewing), whereas Review in sigkdd is a document representing the actual review written by a reviewer. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a question template, the other is a completed review document.
attendeeAt relates a Person to a Conference Event (attendance), while hold relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference (organizing/hosting). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Presenter is a person (a conference participant who presents). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.
Workshop is a conference event/part (subclass of Conference part), while Speaker is a person role (subclass of Person). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Conference is the main academic event (the conference itself) with properties like paper deadlines and topics. In ekaw, Conference Trip is a Social Event (subclass of Event > Social Event), representing an excursion or trip associated with the conference, similar to a Conference Banquet. These are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Steering committee, while property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Tip (a gratuity under Money) and Sponzor fee (a sponsorship fee under Fee) are distinct financial concepts in the conference domain with different meanings and hierarchical placements.

Break Event in edas refers to pauses/breaks during a conference (coffee break, meal break, free time), while Registration in iasted refers to the act of registering for the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions (a call/announcement), while 'Rated Papers' in edas refers to papers that have already been submitted and received ratings. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subtype of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), whereas Published Paper in edas is a subtype of Paper representing a paper that has been published. These denote entirely different concepts within the paper lifecycle/structure.

Presentation in Ontology A is a specific type of conference contribution (oral talk), while Item in iasted is a very broad physical/logical object class with children like Audiovisual equipment, Card, Transport vehicle, etc. They denote entirely different concepts.

Student lecturer in iasted is a person role (a lecturer who is a student), while Registration Student in sigkdd is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (person vs. fee) and are unrelated.

Regular contribution in ontology A is a type of conference document/submission (with children Extended abstract and Paper), while Regular Session in ontology B is a type of event/session. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain (artefacts vs. scheduled events) and are unrelated.
'technicallyOrganisedBy' relates an event to its technical organizer, while 'awarded_by' relates an Award to the entity granting it. These are semantically distinct relations in different contexts.
Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer), while Review in iasted is a document (the review artefact itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Conference Member is a person participating in a conference (subclass of Person), while Tutorial is an educational session that is part of a conference (subclass of Conference part). They are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their email string, while Property B is an object property linking an Item to a Person who uses it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Event in confOf refers to conference occurrences (administrative, social, working events) with start/end times, while Document in sigkdd refers to written artefacts (abstracts, papers, reviews) submitted by speakers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Tutorial is a conference part (an academic session), while Meal Menu is a document describing food options for a meal event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference participant (A) is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference (active and passive). Organizing Committee member (B) is a specific role within the organizing structure. Every organizing committee member is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is an organizing committee member. Thus A subsumes B.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Reviewing results event is an administrative event in the conference schedule. They are entirely different concepts.

The property 'title' gives the name of a Paper, while 'starts on' gives the start date/time of an Event. They have different domains, ranges (semantically), and meanings; they are completely unrelated.

Early Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered early (child of Conference Participant), while Program Committee member is an organizer serving on the program committee (child of Organizator). These are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.

'has Co author' links a Paper to a Co-author (a contributing author), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting it). These are distinct roles in the conference domain: co-authorship vs. presentation.

In EKAW, 'Research Topic' is a subject area or theme that papers and events cover (a conceptual topic). In IASTED, 'Research' is an activity performed before the conference, with children like Modelling and Simulating (a process/action). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Multi-author Volume in ekaw refers to a compiled publication such as proceedings containing multiple papers, while Form in iasted refers to administrative documents like registration or author information forms. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (the chair of a conference), while Talk Event is a type of event (a talk given at a conference). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties represent a start date/time, but they have different domains: 'Important dates' (a deadline/schedule entity) in ontology A versus 'Conference Event' (an actual event) in ontology B. They are semantically related as both capture starting temporal information, but are not equivalent due to the domain mismatch.

hasPhone relates a Person to their phone number string, while hasLastName relates a Person to their last name string. These are entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range types.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class for anyone involved in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members). Speaker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate specifically for those who present, with children Author and Reviewer. While they overlap significantly (both cover authors and reviewers), Conference Member also includes non-speaking roles like chairs and general PC members, and Speaker excludes non-speaking delegates like Listeners. They are related but not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property giving the date of a Conference, while Property B is an object property linking Important dates to a Conference volume. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

In edas, ConferenceEvent is a full event entity with location, programme, attendees, and start/end times. In iasted, Conference_days is a subclass of Time representing the temporal duration (days) of a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event, the other is a time period.

Camera Ready event in confOf is an administrative event (a process/activity), while Registation deadline in iasted is a temporal deadline for registration. They refer to entirely different concepts (camera-ready vs registration) and different kinds of entities (event vs deadline).
rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper they reject, while write relates a Person to an Item they author. These are entirely different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference Session in edas refers to a temporal event (a session of presentations), while Session room in iasted is a subclass of Place referring to the physical location where a session takes place. They are distinct concepts (event vs. venue) and thus unrelated.
Poster is a type of conference contribution (a document/artefact), while Author is a person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while belongsToEvent relates a Programme to a Conference Event. The domains, ranges, and semantic meanings are entirely different.
Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers, while Value added tax is a type of tax under Money. They are completely unrelated concepts.

A Volunteer in confOf is a general helper role under Person, while an Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a specific organizer role under Organizator. Volunteers are not necessarily organizing committee members and vice versa; they represent distinct roles in conference organization.

Property A (abstract) relates a Contribution to its abstract text string, while property B (hasPostalCode) relates Contact Information to a postal code string. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.
confOf:Contribution is a superclass that includes Paper, Poster, and Short paper as children. edas:Paper corresponds specifically to the Paper subclass. Therefore Contribution subsumes Paper.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (a full workshop). In ekaw, Regular Session is a type of Session within a conference, and Workshop Session is listed as a sibling of Regular Session, indicating they are distinct concepts. A workshop and a regular session are different kinds of events in the conference domain.

A Tutorial is a specific type of educational/instructional session at a conference, while a PowerPoint presentation refers to a presentation delivered using PowerPoint slides (a medium/format). They are conceptually distinct: one describes the nature of the event (instructional), the other describes the delivery format. They do not denote the same concept.

Poster Session is a type of scientific event/session where posters are presented, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education), while authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference contributor (A) is a person who contributes content to the conference (children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, Regular author). Attendee (B) in edas is a person who attends the conference. These are overlapping but distinct roles: contributors typically attend, and attendees may or may not contribute. They share the parent Person but have different intended instance sets, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Introduction of speaker in iasted is a specific activity that takes place during a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who finalized paper assignments, while 'relatedToEvent' links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event. They are unrelated.
One property captures a person's last name while the other captures their email address; they represent entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range.

Workshop is a type of academic event (a session or meeting), while Plenary lecture speaker is a role/person who gives a plenary talk. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

'heldIn' specifically links an Event to a Location (venue), while 'is_connected_with' is a very general property linking Activity or Person to Item or Place. The latter is far broader and not semantically equivalent to the specific venue-location relation of 'heldIn'.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Simulating is a type of research activity before a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's past publications (a type of personal history), while Initial manuscript is the first version of a paper submitted to a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (presentation/authorship). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the role of a person who reviews papers in a conference context. edas:Reviewer is a direct subclass of Person with properties for reviewing papers and having review history. ekaw:Possible_Reviewer is also a subclass of Person with properties linking to papers (reviewerOfPaper) and reviews (reviewWrittenBy). Despite the 'Possible' qualifier in ekaw's name, both serve as the reviewer role class in their respective ontologies, making them equivalent in the conference domain alignment.

organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while Name_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string name. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference participant is a Person who attends or contributes to a conference, while Scientific Event is an Event (such as a conference, workshop, or session). They belong to entirely different categories in the domain.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Money is a financial amount/currency class (with children like Fee, Tax, Tip), while Sponzor is a sponsor entity/person/organization class (with children like Gold Supporter, Exhibitor). They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Chair PC in confOf is a program committee chair (a role under Person), while Author in iasted is someone who authored a paper (under Speaker/Delegate). These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document indicating a conflict of interest, while 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item indicating acquisition. These are semantically completely different relations.
Signal Processing Topic is a research topic classification in edas, while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They are entirely different concepts.
Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's publications (under Personal History), while Sponzorship is a financial concept (under Money). They are entirely unrelated.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document. In iasted, Review is also a subclass of Document (Item > Document > Review). Therefore, cmt:Review is subsumed by iasted:Document, as the latter is a more general class that includes reviews among many other document types.

edas:hasMember links a Conference to a Person (membership), while ekaw:partOf is a general mereological part-whole relation with unspecified domain/range. They are not equivalent; at best they are loosely related since being a member could be modeled as being part of a conference in some ontologies, but the semantics and directionality differ.

Rejected Paper is a document (a paper that was evaluated and rejected), while Receiving manuscript is an activity/event (the act of receiving a manuscript). They belong to fundamentally different categories (artefact vs. process) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Conference in edas is an event (with dates, members, topics), while Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document/publication (subclass of Proceedings > Multi author Volume > Document). They are fundamentally different concepts.
A 'Call for paper' is a conference document soliciting submissions, while a 'Workshop' is an academic event within a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Committee in Ontology A refers to conference committees (organizing, program, steering) with chairs and members. Organisation in ekaw refers to institutions like academic institutions, organising agencies, and publishers. These are conceptually distinct entities in the conference domain.
Author is a Person who writes contributions, while Multi-author Volume is a Document (e.g., proceedings). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Tutorial in confOf is a type of working event (an academic session), while Computer in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, while Property B links a Review to a Paper. They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a specific chair role (a type of Chairman) in cmt, while Early Registered Participant is a registration-timing category of conference participant in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts with no hierarchical or semantic overlap.

Property A is a datatype property for the starting date of important dates (domain: Important dates, range: date), while Property B is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating early registration status. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Banquet is a specific type of social event (a meal/gathering), while Non Academic Event in edas is a broader class that includes Social Event, Meal Event, and Break Event as children. Therefore Banquet is subsumed by Non Academic Event.

Both classes represent the role of a Session Chair at a conference. Despite differing parent hierarchies (ekaw places it under Conference Participant and PC Member; iasted under Delegate), the intended instances are the same: persons who chair a session.

Both classes represent the Program Committee in a conference context. In cmt it is a top-level class with members; in sigkdd it is a subclass of Committee alongside Organizing Committee and Best Paper Awards Committee. The intended instances (the group responsible for reviewing and selecting papers) coincide.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a web page/URL resource), while Session room is a physical place where sessions are held. They are entirely different concepts.
Car is a transport vehicle (subclass of Item), while Listener is a person attending the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Abstract in ekaw is a type of Document (the text summary of a paper), while Deadline Abstract Submission in sigkdd is a type of Deadline (a temporal milestone for submitting abstracts). They are entirely different concepts.

hasCountry is an object property linking a Conference to a Country entity, while Name_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string representing its name. They capture entirely different information.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates administrative events to each other in a temporal/sequential order, while 'organised By' in ekaw relates an event to its organizing entity (Organisation or Person). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (general membership), while Property B links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (inverse of having a steering committee). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Conference Event in edas represents an event or activity occurring at a conference (with start/end times, programmes, attendees), while Place in sigkdd represents a physical location (hotel, conference hall). These are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting participation), while B 'Registration of participants event' is an administrative event (the act/process of registering). They differ in kind (document vs. event) and purpose, so they are unrelated.

confOf:Event is a general class with children including Administrative event, Social event, and Working event. edas:SocialEvent is specifically a social/non-academic event. Thus confOf:Event subsumes edas:SocialEvent.

Property A links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract (presentation -> paper), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (document -> speaker). They have different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.
'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (mereological), while 'need' relates a Person to an Item (requirement). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class for people who contribute to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). General Chair (B) is a specific organizational role. While a General Chair could be considered a contributor in a loose sense, they are not equivalent; A is strictly more general than B.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (despite odd multiple inheritance with Person/TPC Member), representing a type of conference organization. Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Organization in edas refers to external entities like academia, government, industry, and NGOs that provide sponsorship. Committee in sigkdd refers to internal conference organizing bodies (program committee, organizing committee). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee, but A is specifically for 'Author attendee cd' (author with CD registration) while B is for 'Student'. They represent different categories of registrants and thus overlap only as sibling registration fee types.

Accepted Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper representing papers that have been accepted for presentation. Document in iasted is a broad superclass encompassing many types of documents (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). They are at very different levels of specificity and do not denote the same concept.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'send' relates a Person to an Item (sending/submission). These are entirely different relations with different semantics and ranges.
Social event is a type of conference event (e.g., banquet, reception), while Fee is a monetary charge. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Audiovisual equipment refers to physical hardware like projectors and computers. These are entirely different concepts.
hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating, while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Accept Rating is a type of review rating. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

hasStreet is a datatype property for street addresses (domain: Contact Information, range: string), while has_amount_of is a datatype property for monetary amounts (domain: Money, range: int). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

forEvent links a Call to an Academic Event (indicating which event a call is for), while partOfEvent links an Event to another Event (indicating mereological parthood). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links an Abstract to the document it is part of (Paper, Poster, Presentation), while Property B links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

cmt:Review is the general class for all reviews, while ekaw:Negative_Review is a specific subclass of Review (a review with a negative recommendation). Therefore cmt:Review subsumes ekaw:Negative_Review.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of 'Author', representing specifically a co-author of a paper. In iasted, 'Author' is the general class for authors (with children like book proceedings author, lecturer, etc.). Therefore, cmt's Co author is strictly more specific than iasted's Author, making it subsumed_by.
heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location, while has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an integer. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, and semantics.
A Conference Chair is the person who chairs/organizes the conference, while a Plenary lecture speaker is someone who delivers a plenary talk. These are entirely different roles in a conference.
LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

The property 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. These relate entirely different domain concepts and serve completely different purposes in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing information to attendees, while 'Silver Supporter' is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class encompassing anyone with a role in the conference (authors, chairs, reviewers, PC members). Presenter in ekaw is a specific type of Conference Participant who presents (with child Invited Speaker). These are not equivalent; Conference Member is much broader and includes non-presenting roles like reviewers and chairs.

Free Time Break in edas is a specific type of break event (non-academic), while Conference activity in iasted is a broad class encompassing lectures, presentations, registrations, social programs, and breaks. Free Time Break is subsumed by Conference activity.

A Program committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the technical program of a conference, whereas an Academic Institution (in ekaw) is an organization such as a university or research institute. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Paper is a document/submission class in cmt, while Communication Theory Topic is a specific subject area/topic class in edas. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Presentation in edas is a conference event (the act of presenting a paper), linked to an Accepted Paper via relatedToPaper. Paper in sigkdd is a document/artefact submitted by an author. They are related (a presentation presents a paper) but not equivalent concepts.

'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members (membership), while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (organizing/holding an event). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a type of conference contribution (e.g., a talk or poster presentation) given by a participant. In Ontology B, Document is a broad administrative/paperwork category (Item > Document) with children like Form, Payment document, Visa, etc. These are conceptually distinct; Presentation is not a Document in the iasted sense.

Presenter in edas is a general class for anyone who presents (typically papers) at a conference, while Tutorial speaker in iasted is specifically someone who gives a tutorial. A tutorial speaker is a kind of presenter, but Presenter is broader and not limited to tutorials. They overlap but are not equivalent.

The 'email' property represents an email address while the 'Name' property represents a person's name. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture entirely different attributes of a person.

An 'Extended abstract' is a specific short type of regular contribution (a sibling of Paper in Ontology A), whereas 'Submitted Paper' in ekaw refers to any paper that has been submitted to the conference regardless of its type. They represent different concepts: one is a document format/length category, the other is a lifecycle status.
Viza (visa) is a travel document for conference attendance, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are completely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

In ekaw, Event represents a conference happening (scientific or social event) with properties like heldIn and organisedBy. In iasted, State is a geographical/administrative region (a type of Place alongside Building and City) used for location purposes. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A relates a conference part to a conference volume (part-of relation for proceedings), while Property B relates a place to a conference event (location relation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Simulating is a type of research activity before a conference, while Organizing Committee member is a person role involved in organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Presenter house is a type of building (physical place). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Social event is a type of conference event (e.g., banquet, reception), while Building is a physical place/structure. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a specific administrative document used to introduce a session chair, while a 'Paper' in sigkdd is a scholarly submission authored by researchers. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while sign relates a Person to an Item (signing). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (authorship), while reviewerOfPaper links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (reviewing). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while designed_by links a Deadline to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Ontology A's Paper is a general class for regular conference contributions (papers), while Ontology B's Rejected_Paper is a highly specific subclass of Paper representing only those papers that have been evaluated and rejected. Therefore, Rejected_Paper is subsumed by Paper.

'starts on' denotes the start date of an Event, while 'done till' denotes the deadline (end date) of a Deadline. They differ in both semantics (start vs. end) and domain (Event vs. Deadline), making them unrelated.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (sibling to Paper Presentation, Talk Event). In ekaw, Session is a broader Scientific Event that has Workshop Session as a child, and Workshop as a sibling. Thus edas:Workshop roughly corresponds to ekaw:Workshop or ekaw:Workshop Session, not to the more general ekaw:Session. They overlap but are not equivalent.

startDate is a dateTime property indicating when a conference begins, while Name_of_conference is a string property for the conference's name. They describe entirely different attributes of a Conference.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference event/organization. They are entirely different concepts.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted contribution (with authors, decisions, subject areas), while Review in Conference represents an evaluation of a contribution. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Travel Grant is a type of Sponsorship (a funding mechanism), while Invited Speaker is a type of Person/Presenter (a conference role). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, 'Member PC' is explicitly commented as 'Reviewer' and has properties for reviewing contributions and expertise on topics, making it a Program Committee member. In sigkdd, 'Organizing Committee member' is a sibling of 'Program Committee member' under 'Organizator', meaning it refers to the organizing/logistics committee, not the program/reviewing committee. These are distinct roles in conference organization.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Fee is a monetary charge. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
'done till' is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a date, while 'Price' links a Registration fee to an int. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location (spatial), while is_dated_on is a datatype property linking an Activity to a dateTime (temporal). They relate different kinds of things in entirely different dimensions.
Workshop is a type of scientific event, while Program Committee is a type of committee. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Fee is a monetary concept. They are completely unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In ekaw, Poster Paper is a specific subtype of Paper. Therefore, the general Paper class in cmt subsumes the more specific Poster Paper class in ekaw.

Property A ('is paid with') links Money to Item (the instrument used for payment), while Property B ('payed by') links Registration fee to Person (the agent who pays). They have different domains, ranges, and semantic directions (instrument vs. payer), so they are unrelated.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the overall conference gathering), while Presentation in iasted is a specific activity that takes place within a conference (e.g., giving a talk). They are at different levels of granularity and denote different concepts.

In cmt, Paper is a full document with children including 'Paper Abstract' and 'Paper Full Version'. In sigkdd, Abstract and Paper are siblings under Document, meaning Abstract is a distinct, shorter artefact. Thus cmt:Paper (the full paper) and sigkdd:Abstract (just the abstract) are not equivalent; they are related as parts of the same submission process but denote different concepts.

'attendeeAt' relates a Person to a Conference Event (attending), while 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (preparing something). These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and ranges.

markConflictOfInterest indicates a conflict between a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) and a Paper, preventing assignment. reviewerOfPaper links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they review or could review. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and directions of intent.

minChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (minimum number of choices), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.

Property A relates a PC member to a contribution (paper) they review, while property B relates money to a building where payment occurs. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers (with children like Co-author). Active conference participant in Conference is a broader class that includes anyone actively participating (giving presentations), with Regular author as a sibling. Author is more specific and focused on paper writing, while Active conference participant covers presenters more broadly. They overlap but are not equivalent; Author is related to Regular author (a sibling of B), making A and B merely related.
Short paper is a type of academic contribution (a brief research paper), while Bank transfer is a payment method/document. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
AuthorNotReviewer is a subclass of Author representing authors who are not reviewers, while Reviewer represents people who review papers. These are disjoint concepts in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Place is a physical location (hotel, conference hall). They are completely unrelated concepts.
Session Chair in edas is a Person role (someone who chairs a session), while Regular Session in ekaw is an Event (a type of session). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A (cmt:date) is a general date property with domain Conference, while Property B (Conference:is_a_full_paper_submission_date) is a specific deadline property for full paper submissions with domain Important dates. They differ in both specificity and domain, making them unrelated.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract (a document part), while property B links a document to the speaker who presents it. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.
'has an ISBN' is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an ISBN string, while 'ends on' links an Event to a date string. They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

Speaker_lecture in iasted is a type of conference activity (a session/lecture), while Organizator in sigkdd is a type of Person who organizes the conference. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. person) and are unrelated.
Conference hall in iasted is a physical place/venue (subclass of Place), while Conference in sigkdd is an event with temporal properties (start/end dates). They are fundamentally different concepts.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), representing the overall conference event. In iasted, Speaker lecture is a specific session-level activity within a conference. These are conceptually distinct: one is the overarching event, the other is a small sub-activity within it.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (an applicant who paid late), while Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Money/Fee (a type of registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent different concepts.

In edas, relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a specific event). In ekaw, partOfEvent links an Event to another Event (mereological part-whole between events). While both connect entities to events in the conference domain, their domains and ranges differ significantly: one relates a document/artefact to an event, the other relates an event to a super-event. They are semantically related but not equivalent.
'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (who adjusted the bid), while 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author (who wrote it). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Introduction in iasted is a type of conference activity (event), while Speaker in sigkdd is a type of Person. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities and are unrelated.

'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document, while 'writtenBy' has domain Document and range Person. They are inverse properties relating the same kinds of entities in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (a person role), while property B links an administrative event to another administrative event that runs in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite oddly having Person and TPC Member as parents), while PC Chair in ekaw is a person role (Program Committee Chair). These are entirely different concepts.

University (confOf) is a specific type of academic institution, while Academia Organization (edas) is a broader class encompassing all academic organizations (universities, research institutes, etc.). Thus University is subsumed by Academia Organization.

Organisation in ekaw represents an organizational body (with children like Academic Institution, Organising Agency), while Conference in sigkdd represents a specific conference event. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
logoURL is a datatype property linking Conference to a URI for a logo, while hasFirstName links Person to a string for their first name. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (event/organization), while Author in iasted is a person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Performance Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Talk Event in edas is a type of conference event (an activity/scheduled session), while Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (a written abstract). They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. document) and are not equivalent or hierarchically related.
Property A links a Topic to a Review preference, while Property B links a Person to a Place/Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Acceptance in cmt is a Decision (an act/outcome of deciding), while Accepted contribution in Conference is the document/contribution that has been accepted. They are closely related (the decision applies to the contribution) but belong to different ontological categories (decision vs. document), so they are not equivalent.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a Person who may review papers, while Review in sigkdd is a Document (the written review itself). They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. artefact) and thus unrelated.

Reviewer in iasted is a person (a subclass of Speaker/Delegate) who performs reviews, while Review in sigkdd is a document (subclass of Document) that is the output of a review process. They represent fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. artefact) and are unrelated.

Associated Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person) in cmt, while Organizing Committee is a committee/group entity (subclass of Committee) in sigkdd. A chair may be part of an organizing committee, but the concepts are fundamentally different kinds (person vs. group), making them unrelated.
Lecture is a conference activity (event), while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Property A links a conference contribution to the conference volume it was submitted at, while property B links a document to the speaker who presents it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (assignment of reviews), while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (giving something). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (date), while 'go through' is an object property linking an Item to an Activity. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a short paper/abstract), while Rated Papers refers to papers that have received reviews/ratings. These are conceptually distinct classes with no meaningful overlap.

Both properties link conference-related entities to topics (Topic / Research Topic). However, A's domain is 'Conference part' (tracks, workshops, tutorials) while B's domain includes 'Event' and 'Paper'. Since papers covering a topic is semantically different from a track/workshop having a topic, they are related but not equivalent.

assignedByReviewer links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (a delegation/assignment relation), while give links a Person to an Activity or Item (a general action). Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Break Event in edas is a non-academic event (coffee breaks, meal breaks), while Scientific Event in ekaw covers academic activities (sessions, workshops, presentations). They are disjoint concepts within the conference domain.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (an action of submission), while has_authors relates a Conference document to a Person (a compositional/authorship relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers; Registration fee is a monetary charge for attending a conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Talk Event is a conference event where talks are given (e.g., welcome talk, closing talk), while Modelling is a pre-conference research activity. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Free Time Break is a type of break event (non-academic) during a conference, while a Conference Banquet is a social event (a formal meal/gathering). They are distinct types of non-academic/social events with different intended instances.
One is a datatype property linking Person to a string (email), the other is an object property linking Person to an Item (obtain). They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

Review preference is a class representing a reviewer's topic preference or expertise level for reviewing submissions, while ACM SIGKDD represents the organizing body/conference series entity. They are completely unrelated concepts.

assignedTo (Paper -> Reviewer) and isReviewing (Reviewer -> Paper) are inverse properties: they relate the same domain concepts but in opposite directions. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person specifically invited to present at the conference, while a 'One day presenter' in IASTED is a delegate who presents for only one day (likely tied to a single-day registration). These are distinct roles: one describes invitation status, the other describes attendance/presentation duration. They overlap as both are types of speakers/presenters but are not equivalent.

CAD Topic is a subject area (topic) in the conference domain, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Meeting Room Place' is a subclass of 'Place', making it a specific type of place (a room for meetings). In sigkdd, 'Place' is the general class with children like Conference hall, Hotel, and Main office. Therefore, edas:MeetingRoomPlace is subsumed by sigkdd:Place.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission process). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Committee member' is a person serving on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair), while an 'Agency Staff Member' in ekaw refers to staff of an external agency (e.g., funding or travel agency). They are distinct roles under Person with no semantic overlap.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a registrant who paid late), while Pending Paper is a subclass of Document/Paper (a paper awaiting decision). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Organization is a class representing an organizational entity (e.g., institution, company), while Activity before conference represents temporal activities or tasks occurring prior to the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts in the domain.
Property A is a datatype property linking a Conference to a date, while Property B is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document soliciting submissions, while a 'Paper Presentation' is an academic event where an accepted paper is presented. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Break Event in edas refers to non-academic breaks (coffee, meals, free time), while Technic activity in iasted is a sibling of Coffee break and Lecture, referring to technical/hands-on activities. They denote different concepts with no subsumption relationship.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) and Conference Chair (edas) are distinct roles in conference organization. In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member, with siblings including Conference Chair, showing they are separate concepts. In edas, Conference Chair is a direct subclass of Person responsible for initiating calls. These are related as both are leadership roles but not equivalent.

In confOf, Contribution represents a scholarly submission (paper, poster, short paper) with properties like abstract, title, and author. In iasted, Activity represents an event or scheduled happening (conference activity, before/after conference) with properties like time, place, and being given by a person. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Conference volume to a string representing its location. Property B is an object property linking a Place to an Item it is equipped with. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain semantics, range semantics, and intended meaning.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property linking a Call to a string of submission instructions, while submit_until is an object property linking a Document to a Deadline. They differ in domain, range, property type, and semantic meaning.

In confOf, 'Social event' is a specific type of event (e.g., banquet, reception, trip) occurring within a conference. In edas, 'Conference' represents the overall academic conference itself. These are distinct concepts at different levels of granularity and purpose.

Rejection in cmt is a type of Decision (the outcome of rejecting a paper), while Accpet If Room Rating in edas is a type of Review Rating (a reviewer's score suggesting acceptance if space permits). They belong to different hierarchies and represent fundamentally different concepts.

Trip city is a subclass of City representing a city visited during a trip, while Hotel is a subclass of Place representing an accommodation venue. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic (a subject area for papers), while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named Reviewer, share the same parent (Person), and represent the role of a person who reviews papers in a conference context. Their properties align: both involve reviewing papers or having review-related attributes.

acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (the act of accepting a paper), while hasReview relates a Paper to a Review (linking a paper to its review). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review a particular topic or submission (with properties like degree, belongs to reviewers, has a topic). Review in Ontology B is a Document subclass representing the actual written review artefact. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, representing the end date/time of a conference. The edas comment explicitly states 'Conference End Date and Time', matching sigkdd's 'End of conference'.

confOf:Event is a broad class encompassing administrative, social, and working events at a conference. edas:TalkEvent is a specific kind of academic event (with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk) nested under Conference Event > Academic Event. Therefore, confOf:Event subsumes edas:TalkEvent.

Paper Abstract is a specific part/summary of a paper (subclass of Paper in cmt), while Slide Set is a collection of presentation slides (subclass of Document in edas). They represent entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Conference state is a subclass of State representing a status or condition in the iasted ontology. They are entirely different concepts.

confOf:Person is a general class for all people involved in the conference (with children including Author, Participant, Administrator, etc.), while edas:Author is specifically a subclass of edas:Person representing only authors. Thus confOf:Person subsumes edas:Author.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Review is a document (an evaluation of a paper). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
expertOn relates a PC member to a topic of expertise, while hasMember relates a conference to a person who is a member. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Publisher is an entity that issues conference proceedings, while Country is a geographical/political entity associated with organizations and persons. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
