The property 'email' captures an email address while 'has Phone' captures a phone number. Although both are datatype properties from Person to string, they represent entirely different contact information and are not equivalent.
Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range string, representing the name of a conference. The edas comment 'Conference Full Name' confirms they denote the same relation.

Passive conference participant is a type of person who attends a conference without an active role (e.g., listener), while Two Level Conference is a type of conference event structure in edas. They belong to entirely different categories (person vs. conference) and are unrelated.

Student in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person role), while Registration Student in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount/fee type). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote different concepts.

Sponzorship in iasted is the general class for all sponsorships (parent: Money), while Silver Supporter in sigkdd is a specific tier/level of sponsorship (child of Sponzor). The general class subsumes the specific one.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject area/topic. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Published Paper in edas denotes a paper that has been published (a lifecycle status), while Demo Paper in ekaw denotes a specific type/track of paper (a demonstration). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.
isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while pay relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Property A relates a Place to an Item (equipment), while Property B relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Acceptance is a type of Decision regarding paper acceptance, while Sponzorship is a type of Money related to financial sponsorship. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a Social Event (an activity/excursion), while Trip day in iasted is a subclass of Time (a temporal designation for when trips occur). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. time) and are not equivalent.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference hall in iasted is a type of Place (a physical location). They represent fundamentally different concepts.

Participant in confOf represents a person attending the conference (with children like Member, Regular, Student), while Sponsor in iasted represents an entity or person providing financial support. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State (likely representing a status or condition), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a subclass of Place (a physical venue). They share only the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

'has gender' is a datatype property on Person indicating gender, while 'written By' is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while obtain relates a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Free Time Break is a type of conference event (a break in the schedule), while Registration Non Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent the same concept of a University as an academic organization/institution within the conference domain. Despite slightly different parent class names (Organization vs Organisation > Academic Institution), their intended instances coincide.

minChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (minimum number of choices), while done_till links a Deadline to a date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasRelatedDocument links events/conferences/sessions/persons to documents, while presentationed_by links documents to speakers. They have different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Camera ready contribution is a post-acceptance stage (after review and acceptance, the final formatted version), while Accepted Paper in edas is any paper that has been accepted (siblings include Active Paper, Pending Paper, etc., suggesting it covers all accepted papers regardless of camera-ready status). Camera ready contribution is more specific than Accepted Paper, but since edas lacks a distinct CameraReady class, they are related rather than strictly subsumed in a reference alignment.

'is Reviewing' relates reviewing roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper they review, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item they author. Reviewing and writing/authoring are distinct activities in the conference domain.
has_a_name is a datatype property linking entities to their name string, while speak_in is an object property linking a Person to a Place and Time. They are completely unrelated.

startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference (initiating the bidding phase), while invited_by relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who extended the invitation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper in edas refers to a scientific paper/contribution submitted to a conference, while Viza (Visa) in iasted refers to a travel visa document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'accept Paper' relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance action), while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
coversTopic relates a Paper or Event to a Research Topic, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for anyone participating in a conference, with children Active and Passive participants. Conference Hiker (B) is a very specific subclass of Delegate in the iasted ontology, likely referring to someone attending a hike/excursion during the conference. B is much more specific than A; they overlap but are not equivalent. 'related' best captures this partial overlap without clear subsumption given the different hierarchies.

Talk Event in edas is a type of academic event with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, and sibling Paper Presentation. Presentation in iasted has siblings including Lecture and Introduction, and children like Power Point presentation and Video presentation (which are formats/media rather than event types). While both relate to presenting/talking at a conference, their taxonomic structures differ significantly: edas's Talk Event is an event slot, whereas iasted's Presentation seems more focused on the medium/format. They overlap conceptually but are not strictly equivalent.

The 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while 'has Cost Currency' relates a Sponsorship to its currency (string). They have completely different domains and semantic meanings.

'has important dates' links a conference volume to its important dates (deadlines, key dates), while 'has Programme' links a conference event to its programme (schedule of sessions). These are conceptually distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur simultaneously. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ekaw, Student is a direct subclass of Person and can include student authors or participants. In iasted, Worker non speaker is a specific type of delegate who is a worker (non-student) and not a speaker. The iasted ontology has a separate 'Student non speaker' sibling class. These concepts overlap in the broader sense of conference attendees but are not equivalent; they are only related.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for human participants in their respective conference ontologies. Although their children differ (reflecting different modeling granularity), both represent the same concept: people involved in a conference.

Paper Full Version is a type of academic document (a full paper), while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Deadline for notification of acceptance refers to when authors are informed of paper acceptance decisions, while Deadline Paper Submission refers to the deadline for submitting papers. These are distinct types of deadlines in the conference domain.

Reviewer in edas is a person who reviews papers, while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives presentations. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different functions and properties.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. Authors and reviewers are distinct roles in the conference domain, so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

OperatingTopicsystems is a subclass of Topic (a subject area for papers), while Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee (a group of people organizing the conference). They are entirely different concepts.

Departure tax is a type of government tax (under Money > Tax), while Registration fee is a conference registration cost (under Fee). They are conceptually distinct types of monetary charges in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Talk Event' is a specific type of academic event (with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk), while in ekaw, 'Conference' represents an entire conference edition (a top-level scientific event containing sessions, tracks, workshops, etc.). These are conceptually distinct: one is a single talk within a conference, the other is the whole conference itself.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict), while 'is used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money. They share no conceptual overlap.
Person represents a human individual involved in the conference, while Sponsorship represents financial support or grants. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsorship provision). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

reviewerOfPaper links a reviewer to a paper they review, while presentationed_by links a document to the speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations involving different roles and directions.

hasFirstName is specifically the first name of a Person, while Name in sigkdd is a general full name property for Person. First name is a part of (or more specific than) a full name, so hasFirstName is subsumed by Name.
'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'write' links a Person to an Item they authored. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

paperDueOn is a specific deadline property for paper submissions on a Conference, while is_dated_on is a general date property for an Activity. They differ in domain (Conference vs Activity) and specificity (deadline vs general date), so they are unrelated.
Property A links a conference document to its authors (Person), while property B links a Person to an Item they need. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a Social Event (an activity/excursion), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a Building (a physical place). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. location) and are not equivalent.
Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee (membership/leadership role), while Property B relates an Item to a Person (signing). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'date' captures a temporal value (date) for a Conference, while property B 'has a name' captures a textual identifier (string) for various entities including Conference. They represent fundamentally different attributes (time vs. name) with different ranges and are unrelated.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Registration fee is a monetary amount charged for registration. They are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is a committee (a group/organizational body), while Entity B is a member of an organizing committee (a person). They represent fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class (child of Person) encompassing Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Speaker in Ontology B is narrower, being a subclass of Delegate with children Author and Reviewer. Since Conference contributor includes non-speaker roles like Regular author (who may not present) and Active conference participant, it is strictly more general than Speaker, hence subsumes.
manuscriptDueOn refers to the deadline for submitting manuscripts/papers, while Start_of_conference refers to when the conference event begins. These are entirely different temporal concepts.
Signal Processing Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while property B (reviews) links a Review to the paper it evaluates (Reviewed contribution). They share the same domain but have entirely different ranges and semantics.

Property A links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment/delegation relation), while property B links a PC Member to a Contribution (a reviewing relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a conference part to its track/workshop/tutorial chair (a role assignment), while property B links chairs or TPC members to a Call they initiate. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'presentationOfPaper' relates an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. These have completely different domains and ranges and describe different relationships in the conference domain.
Property A links papers/posters/presentations to their abstracts, while property B links authors to the contributions they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while Property B links a Conference part to Conference volumes (publications). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

markConflictOfInterest links people (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) to a Paper to flag a conflict of interest, while notification_until links an Author to a Deadline for author notification. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a Speaker at a conference who presents documents/papers. They share similar children (Author) and siblings (Listener), and both are subclasses of a person/delegate attending the conference. The intended instances coincide.

Entity A is a Review (an evaluation of a paper), while Entity B is a Paper (the submitted contribution itself). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; notably, ontology B (ekaw) has its own separate 'Review' class as a sibling of 'Paper'.

isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (organization). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor in Ontology A refers to people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants), while Volunteer in Ontology B refers to a person offering unpaid help/assistance. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.
Individual Presentation in ekaw is a type of scientific event (e.g., talk, tutorial), while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts (days, deadlines). They are completely unrelated.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event where review results are made available to authors, while Call For Manuscripts is a call soliciting manuscript submissions. They belong to different hierarchies (Event vs Call) and represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes contributions, while Conference Session is an event/session at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a type of Chairman (organizational leadership role) in cmt, while One day presenter is a type of Delegate who presents for one day in iasted. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

endReview is an object property linking a Program Committee Chair to a Review (an action to end the review process), while ends_on is a datatype property linking an Event to a string date. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Conference in confOf is a working event (a gathering/meeting), while Book proceeding in iasted is a type of publication. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'initiates' in edas relates conference chairs/TPC members to a Call (for papers), while 'presentationed by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker. These describe entirely different relationships between different kinds of entities.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a string-valued property of Call describing submission instructions, while done_till is a date-valued property of Deadline indicating when the deadline expires. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award given to a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Workshop is a type of academic event, while Tutorial speaker is a person/role who gives a tutorial. They are completely different concepts (event vs. person) and share no meaningful relation.

Workshop is an academic event (a type of session at a conference), while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor (an entity that exhibits/sponsors). They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links review expertise or preference to a reviewer, while property B links personal review history to a reviewer. The domains (Review expertise/preference vs Personal Review History) represent different concepts, so these properties are not equivalent.

Conference contributor (A) is a person who contributes to the conference (authors, speakers), while IASTED member (B) is a specific membership status of a delegate in the IASTED organization. They overlap conceptually as both are roles held by people involved in a conference, but they are not equivalent: one denotes contribution type, the other organizational membership.
Accept Rating is a type of review rating (evaluation outcome) in edas, while Abstract is a type of document (textual summary) in sigkdd. They are entirely different concepts.

The two properties describe entirely different aspects: 'accepts Hardcopy Submissions' is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted, while 'has an ISBN' is a string property on Conference proceedings providing the ISBN identifier. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Performance Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

'has tracks' relates a conference volume to its tracks (a part-whole relationship), while 'is held in' relates an activity to a place and time (a location/temporal relationship). These are entirely different relations.

In iasted, Registration is a Conference activity (an event/action), with Delegate as a child. In sigkdd, Registration Student is a type of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to fundamentally different categories (activity vs. fee) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Conference Session in ekaw is a specific type of scientific event occurring during the conference (e.g., demo session, poster session), while Activity before conference in iasted refers to preparatory activities that take place before the conference (e.g., receiving manuscripts, renting). These are entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Web Site in ekaw represents a website document that lists events and is published by an organisation. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

In Ontology A, Abstract is a very specific subclass of Extended abstract (under Regular contribution), representing the abstract part of papers/posters/presentations. In Ontology B, Tutorial Abstract is a subclass of Abstract specifically for tutorials. These denote different kinds of abstracts in the conference domain and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

In cmt, Conference Member is a general class for any person involved in the conference, with Conference Chair as one of its children. In edas, Conference Chair is a specific role (a direct child of Person). Therefore, cmt:Conference Member subsumes edas:Conference Chair.

In ontology A (iasted), Money is a general class with Fee as one of its children (alongside Sponzorship, Tax, Tip). In ontology B (sigkdd), Fee is the top-level monetary concept. Therefore, Money in iasted is more general than and subsumes Fee in sigkdd.
Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (event/session), while Property B links a PC Member to a Topic (subject area). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A links a review preference to a topic or submitted contribution, while property B links a reviewer to their personal review history. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Sponsor company house is a type of building (physical place). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a short summary of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), while Initial manuscipt in iasted refers to the first submitted version of a full manuscript (sibling of Final manuscript). These are conceptually distinct: one is an abstract/summary document type, the other is a submission stage/version of a manuscript.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URL (anyURI), while startDate links a Conference to its start date/time (dateTime). They represent entirely different attributes of a conference.

Conference Trip is a social event involving an excursion/trip, while Coffee break is a short refreshment break during the conference. They are distinct types of conference activities with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Both classes represent the same conference role: a Session Chair. Despite different parent hierarchies (Person in edas vs Delegate in iasted), their intended instances coincide as persons chairing sessions at a conference.

Rejection in cmt is a type of Decision (the outcome of rejecting a paper), while Accepting manuscript in iasted is an Activity before conference (the process of accepting a manuscript). They represent opposite concepts (rejection vs acceptance) and different categories (decision vs activity), so they are unrelated.

'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., signing a document or form), while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are distinct actions with different ranges and semantics in the conference domain.
AcademiaOrganization is a type of organization (academic institution), while Modelling is a research activity. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (who reads the paper), while property B links a PC Member to a Topic (their area of expertise). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paid applicant (A) is a general class for applicants who have paid, with children Early paid applicant and Late paid applicant. Early Registered Participant (B) specifically denotes participants who registered early. B corresponds more closely to A's child 'Early paid applicant' rather than to 'Paid applicant' itself. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent; they are related.
The property 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while 'is given to' links an Item to a Person (recipient). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different meanings and domains: 'has an ISBN' assigns an ISBN string to Conference proceedings, while 'has Submission Instructions' assigns submission instruction text to a Call. They are unrelated.

Property A links Money to Building (where payment occurs), while Property B links Person to Registration fee (what is being paid). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference context.

Poster is a type of academic contribution (a presentation format), while Gold Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Company is an organization (business entity), while Car is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

Invited talk (A) and Contributed Talk (B) are distinct types of conference presentations. In ontology B, Invited Talk is a sibling of Contributed Talk, confirming they are different concepts. They are related as both are forms of oral presentations/talks at a conference, but not equivalent.

The property 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating rejection), while 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings (indicating publication). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) for reviewing purposes, while property B (obtain) links an Author to an Award. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

In the conference domain, 'submit Paper' (Author -> Paper) and 'write' (Person -> Item) are closely related: authors write papers and then submit them. However, writing and submitting are distinct actions (one can write without submitting, and submission is a specific event). The domains (Author vs Person) and ranges (Paper vs Item) also differ in specificity. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person invited to speak at a conference (often a keynote or special session), while a 'Tutorial speaker' specifically gives tutorials. Both are types of speakers at conferences and thus overlap/are related, but they are not equivalent concepts.

'is submitted at' links a conference contribution to a conference volume (submission relation), while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item (preparation/authoring relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while hasReview is an object property linking a Paper to a Review object. They relate entirely different concepts and have different property types.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference website to its URL string, while Property B is an object property linking a Person to an Item they obtain. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Call For Papers is a type of Call (an announcement inviting submissions), while Conference Paper is a type of Paper (a submitted document). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) responsible for chairing, while Registration Non Member is a type of registration fee (subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote completely different concepts.
assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who assigned them), while reviewes links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper they review). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Conference' denotes the event itself (with child 'Conference volume'), whereas in Ontology B, 'Conference Proceedings' is a document/publication (subclass of Proceedings). These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. its published proceedings.

Topic in confOf represents a subject area or research theme (used for paper topics and PC member expertise), while Conference Session in edas represents an event/session within a conference program. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a subclass of 'Conference contribution', while in Ontology B, Contribution is the top-level class for submitted works (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper). Thus, Presentation in A corresponds to a specific type of Contribution in B, meaning A's Presentation is subsumed by B's Contribution.
Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Lecturer is a type of person/role (someone who gives lectures). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a member of the Technical Program Committee (TPC/PC). confOf's 'Member PC' has comment 'Reviewer' and reviews contributions; edas's 'TPC Member' is also involved in reviewing papers. Both are subclasses of Person and serve the same role in conference organization.
hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while has_amount_of links Money to an integer amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Meeting Room Place in edas is a physical location (a place). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to another Document (a newer version), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Conference announcement' is a general document announcing the conference (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while an 'Invitation letter' is a specific personal letter inviting someone to attend or participate. They are distinct types of documents with different intended instances.

Attendee (edas) is a general class for anyone attending the conference, while Paper Author (ekaw) specifically denotes an author of a paper. In ekaw, Conference Participant is the closer equivalent to Attendee. A Paper Author may be an Attendee but the two classes are not equivalent; they overlap.

Talk Event is a type of academic event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk), while Committee is an organizational body (e.g., program committee, organizing committee). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a broader class that has 'Paper', 'Extended abstract', etc. as children. In Ontology B, 'Regular Paper' is specifically a type of paper (a regular-length research paper). Thus, Regular contribution subsumes Regular Paper, as it includes papers but also extended abstracts and potentially other regular written contributions.

hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Presenter in edas is a subclass of Author (a Person who presents a paper), while Presenter state in iasted is a subclass of State (a status/state related to a presenter). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a role/person, the other is a state/status.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a specific subclass of 'Paper' (sibling to 'Paper Abstract'), representing the complete version of a paper. In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (with children like Submitted Paper, Camera Ready Paper, etc.). Therefore, cmt's 'Paper Full Version' is subsumed by ekaw's more general 'Paper' class.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation). These are different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Venue Place in edas is the place where the conference sessions are held (a sibling of Dining Place and Accommodation Place). Conference restaurant in iasted is a place for dining at the conference. These are distinct concepts (venue vs. restaurant) but both are conference-related places, so they are related rather than equivalent or completely unrelated.

Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while Single Level Conference in edas is a specific kind of Conference organized without sub-conferences. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.
hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while hasReview links a Paper to its Review. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the head/chair of the conference, while Organizing Committee member (sigkdd) is a general member of the organizing committee. In sigkdd, General Chair and Program Chair are siblings of Organizing Committee member, indicating that the chair role is distinct from a regular committee member. Thus these classes denote different roles.

Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (with child Invited Speaker), while Organizator in sigkdd is an organizer role (with children like General Chair, Program Chair). These are distinct roles: presenting vs organizing. Note that sigkdd's 'Speaker' sibling would be the equivalent of Presenter, not Organizator.

In cmt, Author is a Person/Conference Member who writes and submits papers. In Conference ontology, Regular_author is classified under Conference_contribution (a document/artefact), not as a person, despite its label suggesting otherwise. The ontological modeling differs fundamentally (person vs contribution/document), so they are not equivalent but related in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself (with properties like accepts hardcopy submissions, has conference member, etc.). In iasted, 'Activity' is a broad superclass of various activities including 'Activity before conference', 'Activity after conference', and 'Conference activity'. Thus 'Activity' is far more general than 'Conference' and does not denote the same concept; they are unrelated in terms of direct alignment.

'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an action of entering details), while 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (a temporal or sequential ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (email address), while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have different types, domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Chair in cmt is the main chairperson of a conference (subclass of Chairman), while IASTED member in iasted is a type of delegate who is a member of the IASTED organization. These are entirely different roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Ontology B's 'Member PC' has the rdfs:comment 'Reviewer' and its properties (expert On -> Topic, reviewes -> Contribution) confirm it represents a reviewer role. Ontology A's 'Reviewer' is also a Person who reviews papers. Despite different labels, their intended instances coincide in the conference domain.
hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have different types, ranges, and semantics.

Trip in confOf is a specific type of Social event (sibling of Banquet, Reception), while Activity after conference in iasted is a broader category that includes tours and departures. A Trip could be an activity after the conference, but they are not equivalent; they overlap conceptually as post-conference excursions.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while updatedVersionOf links a Document to another Document (versioning relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (the act of reading), while reviews relates a Review to a Reviewed contribution (linking the review artefact to what it evaluates). Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding on papers), while invites_co-reviewers relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers). Different domains of action and different ranges; they are unrelated.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code), while is_dated_on links an Activity to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Venue Place in edas refers to the location where the conference sessions take place (a sibling of Accommodation Place and Dining Place). Presenter house in iasted refers to accommodation/lodging for presenters (a sibling of Conference hotel and Conference building). These denote different concepts: one is a venue for events, the other is lodging.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Scientific Event is a type of event (e.g., conference, workshop). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents (with Invited Speaker as a child), while Lecturer in iasted is a subtype of Speaker/Author who gives lectures. Both denote persons who deliver talks at a conference, but their hierarchies differ: Presenter includes non-author presenters and is broader than just lecturing, whereas Lecturer is specifically an author giving a lecture. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent.
Registration in iasted is a conference activity (event), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person role. They are entirely different concepts.

Medicine Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area, while Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Two Level Conference is a type of conference in edas, while Webmaster is an organizer role in sigkdd. They are entirely different concepts.

Camera Ready event is an administrative deadline/event for submitting final paper versions, while Workshop is an academic session at a conference. They belong to different branches (Administrative vs Academic) and denote entirely different concepts.
PC Chair is the chair of the Program Committee, while Webmaster is responsible for web/technical aspects. These are distinct organizational roles with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Property A ('has a date of issue') refers to the issuance/publication date of a Conference document, while Property B ('has End Date Time') refers to the end time of a Conference Event. They have different domains (document vs event), different ranges (date vs dateTime), and capture entirely different temporal concepts.

Property A links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (assignment relationship), while Property B links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while relatesTo links a Document to various entities (events, conferences, sessions, persons). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while 'give' links a person to an activity or item they give. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

An Organizing committee is a specific committee responsible for organizing a conference, while an NGO (Non-Governmental Organization) is a type of organization in the edas ontology. These are conceptually distinct entities with no meaningful overlap in the conference domain.

defaultChoice is a datatype property mapping events to a positiveInteger (a default selection count), while organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. They differ in type, domain semantics, and range entirely.

In ekaw, Abstract is a subclass of Document and a sibling of Paper, representing a summary document (e.g., for invited talks or tutorials). In sigkdd, Paper is a subclass of Document representing the full submitted paper. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; an abstract is not equivalent to a paper.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Conference_www in the Conference ontology represents a conference website/URL document. These are entirely different concepts.

confOf 'Social event' is a specific type of event (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while ekaw 'Event' is the top-level class for all events (with children Scientific Event and Social Event). Thus confOf Social_event is subsumed by ekaw Event.

Conference contributor (A) is a subclass of Person whose children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author—people who contribute content or participation to the conference. Science Worker (B) in confOf is also a subclass of Person, with siblings like Administrator, Assistant, Author, Chair PC, etc., suggesting it groups academic/scientific roles. However, B's label 'Science Worker' implies a professional researcher/academic, while A's 'Conference contributor' is broader (including invited speakers and active participants who may not be science workers). They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; hence 'related'.
Workshop is a type of event (a working session), while Conference Hiker is a type of delegate/person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (review assignment), while Property B links a document to a speaker (presentation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enableVirtualMeeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference, while 'is_given_by' relates a Presentation to an Active conference participant. They are unrelated.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (academic gathering), while Presenter city in iasted is a type of City where a presenter is located. These are entirely different concepts.
Tutorial is a type of individual presentation/event at a conference, while Simulating is a pre-conference research activity. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a complete version of a submitted paper (a subclass of Paper), while Conference announcement is an administrative document announcing conference details (a subclass of Conference document). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'name' denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while property B 'has a location' denotes the location of a Conference volume. These are semantically distinct properties with different meanings and domains.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (a late-paying applicant), while Entity B is a subclass of Money/Registration fee (a specific type of fee). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote fundamentally different concepts.

Property A ('technically Organises') relates an Organisation to something it organises (e.g., a technical event), while Property B ('is occupied by') relates a physical location (Building, City, State) to a Person who occupies it. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Presenter in edas is a subclass of Author (someone who presents their own paper). One day presenter in iasted is a subclass of Delegate with siblings like Speaker and Non speaker, suggesting it refers to someone presenting for only one day of the conference. They overlap conceptually (both present) but differ in scope and hierarchy, so they are related rather than equivalent.

An Organizational Meeting is an administrative/organizational event within a conference, while a Tutorial is an educational lecture session. They are distinct types of conference activities with different purposes and intended instances.

hasCountry links an Organization or Person to their Country of origin/affiliation, while can_stay_in links a Person to a Place they can stay in (e.g., accommodation). These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (a general membership relation), while Property B links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (a specific role assignment). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for a tutorial), while Tip is a type of money/gratuity. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship), while property B 'holded by' relates a Conference to an organization (ACM SIGKDD). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper (author -> paper), while is_writen_by relates an Item to a Person (paper -> author). They are inverses of each other in direction, not equivalent properties.

writtenBy (Contribution -> Author) and authorOf (Person -> Document) are inverse properties: writtenBy links a paper to its author, while authorOf links an author to a paper. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as inverses in the same domain.

A Co-chair is a committee leadership role (co-chairing the organizing/program committee), while a Session chair presides over an individual session at the conference. Both are chair-like roles but operate at different levels of the conference organization, so they are related but not equivalent.

Short paper is a type of academic contribution (document), while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties express a deadline date/time, but hasSubmissionDeadline is specifically for submission deadlines (domain: Call), while done_till is a generic deadline property (domain: Deadline). They overlap in meaning but are not strictly equivalent due to differing specificity and domains.

Review in cmt is a document that evaluates a paper (written by a reviewer), while Evaluated Paper in ekaw is a paper that has undergone evaluation. They are distinct concepts: one is the review artefact, the other is the paper being reviewed.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes the complete version of a paper (as opposed to an abstract), while Conference Paper in ekaw denotes a paper submitted to/published at a conference (as opposed to workshop, demo, etc.). They overlap conceptually—a full version is typically what becomes a conference paper—but they classify papers along different axes (completeness vs. venue type), so they are related rather than equivalent.
Workshop Chair is a person who chairs a workshop session, while Webmaster is a person responsible for the conference website. These are distinct organizational roles with no semantic overlap.

Conference Venue Place in edas refers to the location where the conference is held (with siblings like Meeting Room Place, Dining Place), while Hotel in sigkdd refers to accommodation. Both are subclasses of Place but serve different purposes; they overlap only in that a hotel can sometimes host a conference, making them related but not equivalent.

In the conference domain, 'Submitted Paper' (ekaw) and 'Submission' (iasted) both denote a paper/manuscript that has been submitted to the conference. The iasted children 'Initial manuscipt' and 'Final manuscript' confirm that Submission refers to a submitted paper rather than the act of submission. Thus their intended instances coincide.
Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer), while Review in sigkdd is a document (the review artefact itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
The 'email' property captures a person's email address (string), while 'has gender' captures a person's gender. These are entirely different attributes of a Person and are unrelated.

Property A ('has a date of issue') refers to the issuance date of a conference document, while Property B ('end Date') refers to the end date and time of a conference event. They have different domains (Conference document vs Conference), different ranges (date vs dateTime), and entirely different semantics.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Regular author in Ontology A is a person/role (a contributor to the conference), while Contributed Talk in Ontology B is an event (a type of presentation). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

The properties have opposite directions: 'has authors' goes from Conference document to Person, while 'prepare' goes from Person to Item. Even if Item corresponds to a conference document, the domain and range are swapped, so they are not equivalent (a property and its inverse are not equivalent).

Pending Paper is a status of a paper (Document > Paper), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Author is a person who writes papers in the conference domain, while State is a geographical or administrative region (with children like Conference state, Presenter state). These are entirely different concepts.

readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer (reviewing relation), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). These are entirely different relations involving different roles and activities in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Dining Place is a physical location for meals. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of Working event), while Student lecturer in iasted is a person/role (a subclass of Lecturer). They are entirely different concepts.

Track is a scientific event (a thematic track within a conference), while Program Committee is a committee responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reception in confOf is a social event (subclass of Event), while Dining Place in edas is a physical location (subclass of Place). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. place) and are unrelated.

Conference in ontology A represents the overall conference event (with children like Conference volume), while Conference Session in edas represents a specific session within a conference. These are distinct concepts at different granularities; a session is part of a conference, not equivalent to it.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution), while ekaw:Evaluated_Paper is a much more specific subclass representing only those papers that have already been assigned and evaluated. Therefore, confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Evaluated_Paper.

Industrial Session in EKAW is a type of Conference Session focused on industry-related presentations, while Speaker lecture in IASTED is a type of session centered on a speaker giving a lecture. They represent different kinds of conference events with no direct equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Property A is a datatype property linking conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while Property B is an object property linking a paper to its presentation format. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution, alongside Poster and Short paper). iasted:Final_manuscript is specifically the final version of a submitted manuscript (as opposed to Initial manuscipt). While both refer to paper-like documents in the conference domain, Final manuscript is a more specific stage/version of a paper, so they are related but not strictly equivalent.

Paper in Conference ontology is a general class for conference papers (a type of regular contribution), while Pending Paper in edas is a specific status subclass of Paper (papers awaiting a decision). They are not equivalent; the edas Paper class would be closer to an equivalent match. They are related as both concern conference papers.

Both classes are named 'Conference' and represent the same core concept in the conference-organisation domain: the academic conference event itself. Ontology A (cmt) models it with administrative properties (dates, submissions, members), while Ontology B models it with a name property and a child class 'Conference volume'. Despite different levels of detail, their intended instances coincide.
'Conference fees' refers to the monetary charges for attending a conference, while 'Conference' in edas refers to the event itself. These are distinct concepts.
Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference, while Property B links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite odd parentage), while IASTED non member in iasted is a type of delegate/person who is not an IASTED member. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Organizer' is a general class for anyone involved in organizing the conference. In Ontology B (sigkdd), 'Organizing Committee member' is a specific subclass of 'Organizator', with siblings like General Chair, Program Chair, etc. Thus, the general 'Organizer' class subsumes the more specific 'Organizing Committee member' class.

Property A (assignedTo) links a Paper to a Reviewer for the purpose of review assignment. Property B (is_given_by) links an Activity or Item to a Person who presents or provides it. These describe fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain with different domains and ranges.
The property 'title' gives the title of a Paper, while 'has City' gives the city in Contact Information. They have completely different domains and semantics.

The property 'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise, while 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is oddly placed under 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact class) while also being a 'Conference contributor'. In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Paper Author' is clearly a subclass of 'Person' representing someone who authored a paper. Both refer to the concept of an author of a conference paper, but their ontological modeling differs significantly (A conflates contribution and contributor). They are related/overlapping rather than strictly equivalent.

A Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (e.g., tutorial, workshop track), while a Program Committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the program. They are entirely different concepts.

Associated Chair is a role under Chairman (a person managing the conference), while Regular author is a type of conference contribution/author. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Administrative event in confOf covers submission, reviewing, registration, etc., while Social Event in ekaw covers banquets and trips. They are disjoint sibling concepts under Event in their respective ontologies.

In edas, Meal Event is a general class for meal-related events with Conference Dinner as a child. In ekaw, Conference Banquet is a specific event (a banquet). A banquet is a type of meal event, so Conference Banquet would be subsumed by Meal Event, but they are not equivalent since Meal Event is broader and includes other meals beyond banquets.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person representing conference system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In confOf, Scholar is a subclass of Person representing an academic/scholar with a 'study At' property and comment about price category. These are different concepts: one is a system role grouping, the other is an academic status/registration category. They overlap (both can include authors) but are not equivalent.
Conference Banquet is a social event at a conference, while Sponzorship is a financial concept (subclass of Money). They are entirely unrelated.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (subclass of Person), while Conference building in iasted is a physical Place (subclass of Building). They are entirely different concepts.

In edas, 'Published Paper' is a subclass of Document/Paper representing a paper artefact that has been published. In iasted, 'Accepting manuscript' is a subclass of Activity (specifically 'Activity before conference'), representing the action/process of accepting a manuscript. One is a document state, the other is an activity; they are fundamentally different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.

confOf:Member is a general conference participant (subclass of Participant, with siblings Regular and Student), while ekaw:SC_Member is a specific Steering Committee member (subclass of PC Member). They are not equivalent; they only loosely overlap as roles a person can hold at a conference.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Wireless Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (parent of Invited Speaker), while Non speaker in iasted is explicitly a delegate who does not speak/present. These are disjoint concepts.
In cmt, Paper is a Document (the written submission), while in edas, Paper Presentation is a Conference Event (the act of presenting the paper). They are related but not equivalent.
A Reviewer evaluates papers, while an Invited Speaker presents at the conference. These are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.

'Activity before conference' is a class representing pre-conference activities (e.g., accepting/receiving manuscripts), while 'Author' is a class representing a person who writes and submits papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Trip city is a type of city/location. They are completely unrelated concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is oddly placed under 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact class) while also being a 'Conference contributor', mixing the person and their contribution. In Ontology B, 'Author of paper' is clearly a Person > Speaker > Author subclass representing someone who authored a paper. They overlap in referring to paper authors but differ structurally: A conflates author with contribution, while B cleanly models the person role. Hence 'related' rather than equivalent.

'is Initiated By' links a Call to the person who initiated it (e.g., Conference Chair), while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person who signed it. These are different relations with different domains and semantics.

In confOf, Participant is a general class for anyone attending the conference (children: Member, Regular, Student), while Author is a separate sibling class. In edas, Author is a specific role (someone who wrote a paper) and Attendee is a separate sibling. Thus confOf:Participant is more general than edas:Author and subsumes it.
hasSurname captures a person's family name, while hasBiography captures biographical information. These are semantically distinct datatype properties despite sharing the same domain and range.

Property A relates an Author to a Paper they wrote (authorship), while Property B relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation it is the first part of (mereological/part-of relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both properties link an event/activity to the person or organization responsible for it. However, 'organised By' (ekaw) has domain Event and range Organisation or Person, while 'is given by' (iasted) has domain Activity/Item and range only Person. They overlap in meaning but differ in scope (organisation vs person-only, event vs activity/item), so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Wireless Communications Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Review is a conference document used to evaluate contributions, while Departure tax is a type of monetary tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Social event in confOf refers to non-academic social gatherings (banquets, receptions, trips), while Talk Event in edas refers to academic talks (closing talk, welcome talk). These are disjoint types of conference events.

Both classes represent the concept of a Conference in the conference-organisation domain. In confOf it is a subclass of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), while in sigkdd it has properties like start/end dates, city, and name. Despite different modeling details, their intended instances coincide: they both denote the conference event itself.

Property A ('parallel with') relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur in parallel. Property B ('related To Paper') links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Working event in confOf is a type of event (conference, tutorial, workshop), while Conference building in iasted is a physical place/building where a conference takes place. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Meta Review is a type of review document summarizing other reviews, while Personal History is information about a person's background (publications, review history). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Organization is a general class with children Company and University, while edas:IndustryOrganization is a specific subclass of edas:Organization representing only industry-type organizations. Thus confOf:Organization subsumes edas:IndustryOrganization.

A is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person (range: string), while B is an object property linking a Document to its author (Person). They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics entirely.

scientificallyOrganisedBy relates an event to an Academic Institution (a sub-property of organisedBy), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has authors' links a document to its author(s) (domain: Conference document, range: Person), while 'submit' links an author to a paper (domain: Author, range: Paper). They are roughly inverse relations involving the same domain concepts but with reversed direction and slightly different semantics (authorship vs. submission action), so they are related but not equivalent.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Track is a subdivision of a conference (like a tutorial or workshop). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper in Ontology A is a regular conference contribution (a scholarly paper), while Flyer in Ontology B is a promotional document published by an organisation. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'held In' relates an event to a location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference and Workshop are distinct types of events. In both ontologies they appear as siblings (confOf: siblings Tutorial, Workshop under Working event; ekaw: siblings Conference, Individual Presentation, etc. under Scientific Event). They are related as co-hyponyms but not equivalent.

Entity A is a type of conference document (the final camera-ready paper), while Entity B is a deadline (a point in time) for submitting the camera-ready manuscript. They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the deadline for submitting papers to a conference. 'Submissions deadline' in iasted and 'Deadline Paper Submission' in sigkdd share the same parent (Deadline) and denote the same concept.

Review in cmt is a document (the written review text), while Review Rating in edas is an evaluation score/rating assigned to a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a textual artifact, the other is a rating value.

Property A ('is paid in') links Money to a Building (indicating the location where payment occurs), while Property B ('payed by') links Registration fee to a Person (indicating the agent who pays). The domains, ranges, and semantic meanings are entirely different.

Contribution_1th-author is a specific role (first author of a contribution), while edas:Author is the general class for any author of a paper. Every first author is an author, but not every author is a first author, so A is subsumed by B.

'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer for the purpose of review assignment, while 'is_sent_by' links an Item to a Person indicating who sent it. These represent fundamentally different relations in the conference domain.

writtenBy relates a Review to its author (Reviewer), while invited_by relates a Reviewer to the person who invited them (also a Reviewer). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

has the last name is a datatype property on Person for surnames, while has Postal Code is a datatype property on Contact Information for postal codes. They have different domains and represent entirely different concepts.

Meal Menu is a document describing food options for a meal event, while Review is an evaluation of a submission. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest with a paper), while 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (indicating employment). These are semantically distinct properties with different ranges and meanings.

Conference Banquet is a formal social dining event, while Coffee break is a short refreshment pause during the conference. Both are conference-related activities/events but denote distinctly different concepts.

In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' is a specific subtype of 'Paper', while in sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for papers (a direct child of Document). Therefore, ekaw's Regular Paper is subsumed by sigkdd's Paper, as Regular Paper is a more specific concept.

Property A links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (person-to-group membership). Property B links a Program committee to a Conference volume (group-to-event association). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent, inverse, or subproperties of each other.

Both properties relate a topic to conference-related entities (A: Topic -> Conference part; B: Research Topic -> Event, Paper). They share the same semantic direction and similar domain concepts, but their ranges differ in scope ('Conference part' vs 'Event, Paper'), so they are related rather than strictly equivalent.

Computer Networks Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific leadership role heading the conference, subclass of Chairman. Member PC (confOf) is a program committee member/reviewer. These are distinct roles in conference organization; confOf has a separate 'Chair PC' class for the PC chair role, and neither corresponds to the overall Conference Chair.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is a specific subclass of conference contributors (alongside Invited speaker, etc.), representing authors who are not invited. In Ontology B (edas), 'Author' is a general class under Person with no such restriction. Therefore, Regular author is subsumed by the more general Author class in edas.
In edas, NGO is a subclass of Organization (path: Organization > NGO). In the Conference ontology, Organization is the general class. Therefore, Organization subsumes NGO.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area (subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.
Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while Conference Paper is a type of Paper (a submitted document). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event), while Listener in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.

University is an organization type where scholars study, while Numerical Review Question is a type of review question expecting a numerical answer. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee in their respective ontologies, but they refer to different categories: A is specifically for author attendees who have a CD registration, while B is for non-member registrations. They overlap conceptually as registration fee types but are not equivalent.

The 'abstract' property relates a Contribution to its textual abstract (string), while 'has amount of' relates Money to an integer amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria, while 'isReviewing' links reviewing roles (e.g., Reviewer) to a Paper they are reviewing. They are unrelated.

Conference Chair (the overall chair of a conference) and Session Chair (the chair of an individual session) are distinct roles in the conference domain. They are related as both are chairing roles held by persons, but they are not equivalent.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'search' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponsor. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'paperInVolume' relates a paper to a proceedings volume, while 'write' relates a person to an item they authored. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing information to attendees, while 'Gold Supporter' is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper for the purpose of rejection, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker for the purpose of presentation. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Invitation letter is a document used for visa or attendance purposes. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper they are associated with, while hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to its updated version. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Bank transfer is a payment document (financial instrument), while Abstract is a scholarly document summarizing a paper. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A is a research topic related to optical computer networks, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Property A (isLocationOf) links a Place to a Conference Event it hosts, while Property B (is_situated_in) links spatial entities (Building, City, Place) to broader spatial containers (State, etc.). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
The 'name' property captures the name of a Conference or Person, while 'hasPhone' captures a phone number for a Person. These are entirely different attributes with different semantics.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while technicallyOrganises relates an Organisation to something it organizes. These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Active Paper in edas refers to a paper that is currently under review (has a rating), representing a lifecycle status. Industrial Paper in ekaw refers to a paper submitted to an industrial track, representing a category/type of paper. These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered details), while 'has a track workshop tutorial topic' links a Conference part to a Topic. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Chair PC in confOf is the Program Committee Chair (head of the program committee), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a general member of the organizing committee. These are distinct roles: one leads the program committee, the other serves on the organizing committee. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.
Country and City are distinct geographic concepts. A country is a nation/state while a city is an urban settlement within a country or state. They do not denote the same concept.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a paper they authored). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

paperAssignmentToolsRunBy links a Conference to an Administrator (who runs paper assignment tools), while hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Abstract is a subclass of Paper (a document/artefact), while Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
'submitPaper' specifically relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while 'obtain' is a generic property relating a Person to an Item (acquisition). The semantics are entirely different.

writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author (Contribution -> Author), while prepare relates a Person to an Item (Person -> Item). The domains and ranges are reversed in direction: writtenBy goes from the artifact to the creator, whereas prepare goes from the creator to the artifact. They are not equivalent; they would be closer to inverses, but even then the domain/range classes differ (Contribution vs Item, Author vs Person).

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered review criteria, while 'isReviewedBy' links a Paper to the person(s) who reviewed it. They are unrelated.

A Programme Brochure is a document listing conference events/sessions, while an Author information form is a form for collecting author details. They are entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.
Published Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been published), while Renting is an activity performed before a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'is Written By' links a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person (signing). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.
Co author in cmt is a person role (a type of Author), while Poster in Conference is a type of conference contribution/document. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference Event in edas represents scheduled events/activities at a conference (with start/end times, locations, attendees), while Organisation in ekaw represents organizational bodies such as academic institutions, publishers, and organising agencies. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of a conference), while Industry Organization is a type of organization. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country (geographic location), while organises links an Organisation or Person to an Event (organizing activity). The ranges and semantics are entirely different.
partOfEvent relates an Event to a containing Event (mereological), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (agentive). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Contribution 1th author' in Conference is a specific role (first author of a contribution), while 'Author' in iasted is a general class for any author. The first-author class is strictly more specific than the general Author class, so it is subsumed by it.

'Information for participants' is a broad category of conference documents intended for attendees, while 'Hotel registration form' is a very specific type of form used for hotel booking. They are related in that a hotel registration form could be considered part of the information provided to participants, but they are not equivalent nor in a direct subsumption relationship given their different ontological contexts.

Property A links a Program Committee to a Conference Volume (committee membership/role), while Property B links a Conference Event to a Programme (event schedule). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
