PC Member in ekaw is a program committee member (a reviewer role), while Speaker in iasted is someone who presents at the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

Paper in cmt is a submitted document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while Call For Manuscripts in edas is a type of Call (an invitation to submit). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A Conference Chair is the person who chairs/leads a conference, while a Sponsor is a person or entity that provides financial support. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Property A links a conference contribution to a conference volume (submission relation), while property B links a person to an activity or item (giving/presenting relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee (an organizational body), while Property B links a Conference to a Person (an individual member). The domains and ranges differ fundamentally: one targets a group/committee structure, the other targets individual persons. They are not equivalent.

'organised By' is an object property linking an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'City of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a city name string. They describe entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Document is a broad class encompassing Paper, Review, Programme, Meal Menu, and Slide Set. In iasted, Form is a subclass of Document specifically for administrative forms (registration, hotel, author info). The edas Document class is strictly more general than the iasted Form class, so it subsumes it.

Pending Paper is a status of a paper (a Document subclass), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers (a Deadline subclass). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

confOf:Contribution represents submitted scholarly works (Paper, Poster, Short paper) authored by Authors and reviewed by PC Members. sigkdd:Document is a broader class that includes not only Paper but also Abstract and Review, and is linked to Speakers and Deadlines rather than authors/reviewers. They overlap via the shared Paper subclass but are not equivalent; Contribution does not strictly subsume Document (which includes Review) nor is it subsumed by it.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information), while Closing Talk is a specific type of talk event at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a general class for people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.), while Student in confOf is a specific type of participant (a student attendee). They represent different concepts with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Subject Area in cmt refers to a topic or research area of a paper, while Location in ekaw refers to a physical place where an event is held. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has gender' is a datatype property on Person describing gender, while 'is needed for' is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and purposes.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who finalized paper assignments, while 'parallel_with' links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They are unrelated.
Both properties relate a location/place to an event/conference event in the same direction. 'Place' and 'Location' are synonymous, as are 'Conference Event' and 'Event' in this domain context.

'has authors' links a conference document to its author(s), while 'is needed for' links an item to a person who needs it. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and directions.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documentary artefacts (papers, reviews, calls for papers, announcements), while Event in ekaw refers to occurrences/activities (scientific events, social events). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name (string), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

has a URL links a conference website to a URL string, while has Email links contact information or a person to an email string. They have different domains and represent different kinds of contact details (URL vs email), so they are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'adjustedBy' links a Bid to a Reviewer (indicating who adjusted the bid), while 'hasReviewHistory' links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. They are unrelated.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Invited Speaker is a person/role (a type of presenter). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Program Committee' is a group of people (committee members) who review papers. In edas, 'Programme' is a Document (subclass of Document, sibling of Paper and Review) that represents the schedule or programme of conference events. These are entirely different concepts.

A Co-chair (co-chair of a committee) and a Session Chair (person chairing a specific session at a conference) are distinct roles in the conference domain. They have different parents, siblings, and properties, and their intended instances do not coincide.
'was a committee of' links a Committee to a Conference volume, while 'write' links a Person to an Item (authorship). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference hall and Main office are distinct types of places within a conference venue. A conference hall is where sessions/talks occur, while a main office is an administrative space. They are siblings in ontology A and both appear as separate concepts across the two ontologies, so they are not equivalent.

Property A is an object property linking activities/money/time to activities/persons, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Person to a string name. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Viza is a document (visa). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Author is a general class for anyone who writes a contribution (paper). sigkdd:Author_of_paper is a more specific subclass under Author and Speaker, representing specifically an author of a paper (as opposed to 'Author of paper student'). Thus confOf:Author subsumes sigkdd:Author_of_paper.
Member PC in confOf is a person (reviewer) who reviews contributions, while Week Reject Rating in edas is a type of review rating. They are entirely different concepts.

topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (indicating topic coverage), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking 'Important dates' to a date value specifically for full paper submissions. Property B is an object property linking a 'Document' to a 'Deadline'. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain (Important dates vs Document), range (date vs Deadline), and specificity (full paper submission vs general document submission).

In confOf, 'Conference' is a Working event (the main academic conference itself), whereas in ekaw, 'Conference Banquet' is a Social Event (a banquet held during the conference). These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a scholarly document), while Card in iasted is a physical item (with child Credit card). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference Chair is a leadership/organizational role (chairman of the conference), while Invited speaker is a contributor who gives a talk. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

PaperAbstract in cmt represents the abstract portion of a paper (a structural part of the document), while ActivePaper in edas represents a paper that is currently active/under review (a lifecycle status). These are conceptually distinct and unrelated.

Rejected contribution is a class of documents (a paper that was rejected), while Reviewing event is an administrative event/procedure for reviewing contributions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Positive_Review in ekaw is a specific subclass of Review (a review with a positive recommendation), whereas Review in iasted is the general class for all reviews. Thus, Positive_Review is subsumed by Review.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is equipped by' relates a Place to an Item (equipment). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
hasSurname refers to a person's family name, while Nation refers to a person's country/nationality. These are distinct attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Review Question' in edas is a specific question or criterion used within a review form (with subtypes Numerical and Textual), whereas 'Review' in iasted is the complete review document itself (a subclass of Document). They are related as part-to-whole but not equivalent.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (a late-paying conference applicant), while Entity B is a subclass of Fee (a student registration fee category). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent different concepts (person vs. fee type).

In iasted, 'Deadline hotel reservation' is a specific subclass of 'Deadline', while in sigkdd, 'Deadline' is the general class. The iasted concept is strictly more specific (a particular type of deadline), so it is subsumed by the sigkdd Deadline class.

Both properties link a Conference to its members. In cmt the range is Conference Member (a role class), while in edas the range is Person. Since Conference Member instances are persons participating in the conference, these properties express the same relation in the conference domain.
writeReview links a Reviewer to a Review (who wrote the review), while reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper (what paper the review is about). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both are datatype properties that specify the start date/time of an event. 'Event' in confOf and 'Conference Event' in edas refer to the same concept in this domain, and string vs dateTime are minor range differences for the same semantic purpose.

confOf's 'Member PC' has the comment 'Reviewer' and properties for reviewing contributions and having expertise on topics. iasted's 'Reviewer' represents the same role in the conference domain. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide.
Workshop Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while Car is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Conference proceedings is a published volume of papers, while Topic is a subject area or theme. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time (a temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Value added tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference Member in cmt refers to people who are part of the conference organization (chairs, authors, reviewers, PC members), while Conference applicant in the Conference ontology refers to someone applying/submitting to attend or participate. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'provided By' relates a Sponsorship to an Organization. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

Entity A is 'Paper' (a scholarly contribution/submission), while Entity B is 'Review' (an evaluation document). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; a paper is what gets reviewed, not the review itself.

Programme in edas is a schedule/programme document for a conference event, while Review in iasted is an evaluation document of a submission. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

'Information for participants' in Conference is a specific type of conference document providing information to attendees. 'Document' in iasted is a broad class encompassing many types of documents (forms, letters, submissions, reviews, etc.). The iasted Document class is much more general and includes items that are not participant information, so they are related but not equivalent; Document subsumes the concept.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for a person who studies at a university (a student attendee), with no connection to authoring papers. In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications. These represent distinct roles in the conference domain: a student/learner vs. a paper submitter. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

'expert On' relates a PC member to a topic they have expertise in, while 'obtain' relates a person to an item they acquire. These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (a type of Chairman and Conference Member), whereas Worker non speaker in iasted is a non-speaking delegate/worker at the conference building. These are conceptually distinct roles with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while Abstract is a type of Document (a submitted artefact). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and are unrelated.
Tutorial is a type of scientific event/presentation in ekaw, while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor in sigkdd. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (an organizational body), while Property B links a Conference to a Person (an individual member). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documents/artefacts related to a conference (papers, reviews, calls, announcements), while Event in Ontology B refers to scheduled occurrences during the conference (administrative, social, working events). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Operating Topicsystems is a conference topic (subject area) in edas, while Simulating is a research activity before a conference in iasted. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

confOf:Conference is a general conference event class (child of Working event). edas:TwoLevelConference is a specific subtype of Conference (a conference with two levels, e.g., main conference and workshops). Therefore confOf:Conference subsumes edas:TwoLevelConference.

Pending Paper in edas refers to a paper awaiting a decision (a status), while Demo Paper in ekaw refers to a specific type/track of paper (a demonstration). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Welcome address is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject area/topic for papers, while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Review in ontology A is a document (subclass of Conference document), while Possible Reviewer in ontology B is a person (subclass of Person) who may write reviews. They are fundamentally different concepts: one is an artefact, the other is an agent.

In Ontology A, 'Organizing committee' is a specific type of Committee responsible for organizing a conference volume. In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Organisation' is a broad class representing organizations/institutions (with children like Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher). These are conceptually different: one is a committee role within a conference structure, the other is an organizational entity. They are unrelated.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who runs paper assignment tools, while Property B links a Conference contribution to the Conference volume it is submitted at. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference contribution refers to submitted works (papers, posters, talks), while Building refers to a physical structure/venue. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In edas, Excursion is a specific type of Social Event (sibling of Reception). In iasted, Social program is the general category for social activities (parent of Dinner banquet, sibling of Coctail reception). Thus, Excursion is a kind of Social program, making A subsumed by B.
One is a datatype property linking Person to a string (email), the other is an object property linking Person to Document (authorOf). They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

Rejected Paper (edas) denotes a paper that has been reviewed and rejected, while Submitted Paper (ekaw) denotes a paper that has been submitted (and may or may not be accepted/rejected yet). They represent different stages/outcomes in the paper lifecycle. Both are subclasses of Paper, so they are related but not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class covering anyone with a role in the conference (authors, chairs, reviewers, PC members). Speaker in sigkdd is specifically someone who gives a presentation. These are conceptually different roles; a speaker may or may not be considered a 'conference member' in the cmt sense, and most conference members (e.g., reviewers) are not speakers. They are unrelated.
hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place, while is_equipped_by links a Place to an Item. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Medicine Topic is a subject area classification (a topic), while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer, while 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization.

Both classes represent the chair/chairman role in a conference organization context. In cmt, Chairman is a subclass of Person with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair. In Conference, Chair is a subclass of Committee member (which is under Person) with properties linking it to committees. Despite slightly different parent hierarchies, they denote the same concept: a person serving as a chair in a conference.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the event it organizes), while Property B links an Academic Institution to something it scientifically organizes. The domains are entirely different (committee vs institution) and the relations describe different roles in conference organization.

A 'Welcome Talk' is a specific type of talk event that opens a conference, while 'Introduction of speaker' is an activity where a speaker is introduced to the audience. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with different intended instances.

A Plenary lecture speaker is a type of author/speaker who delivers a plenary talk, while a Program Chair is an organizer responsible for the conference program. These are distinct roles in a conference.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite an unusual parent path including Person/TPC Member), while Sponsor in iasted is a person who sponsors the event. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Student in the conference domain. In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (which is under Person), and in ekaw, Student is directly under Person with Conference Participant as a sibling. Despite slight structural differences in the hierarchy, both denote the same concept: a student attending or participating in a conference.

Rejection in cmt is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of rejecting a paper), while Accept Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a reviewer's positive rating). They belong to different conceptual hierarchies and represent opposite sentiments; they are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person and represents someone who serves on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair). In Ontology B, 'IASTED member' is a subclass of Delegate (which is under Place > Building > Conference building) and its siblings include 'Technical commitee' and 'Session chair', suggesting it refers to a member of the IASTED organization attending as a delegate rather than specifically a committee member. The two concepts overlap in the broader sense of people involved in the conference but are not equivalent.
Short paper is a type of contribution/submission, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Introduction is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment of a paper to review), while Property B links a Submitted contribution or Topic to a Review preference (assignment of a review reference/preference). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a street name string, while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and types.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a specific leadership role), while Property B links a Conference to any Person who is a member. They differ in domain (Committee vs Conference), range (Chair vs Person), and semantics (leadership role vs general membership).

Call in edas represents a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts associated with an academic event, while Abstract in ekaw is a type of Document representing the abstract of a paper or presentation. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Submitted contribution is a class of documents (papers) that have been submitted to a conference, while Possible Reviewer is a class of persons who may review papers. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a general class for anyone involved in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.) under Person. Conference Hiker in iasted is a very specific subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building, likely referring to someone participating in a hiking excursion. These are conceptually unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'hardcopy Mailing Manifests Printed By' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings. They are unrelated.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while speak_in relates a Person to a Place and Time (presentation/speaking action). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Topic in confOf represents a subject area or theme that contributions deal with and PC members are experts on. Conference in sigkdd represents the conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Camera ready contribution' is a document/artefact (a subclass of Accepted contribution). In Ontology B, 'Camera Ready event' is an administrative event/deadline (a subclass of Administrative event, sibling to Submission event, etc.). They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a paper version, the other is a deadline or process event.

Worker non speaker (iasted) refers to a conference worker who is not presenting, while Organizator (sigkdd) refers to organizing roles such as chairs and committee members. Both represent people involved in running the conference rather than speaking, so they overlap conceptually, but Organizator includes high-level roles (General Chair, Program Chair) that are not necessarily 'workers' or 'non-speakers', and Worker non speaker could include support staff not considered organizers. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Rejection is a decision outcome (subclass of Decision) indicating a paper was not accepted, while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Call to submission instructions (a string), while Property B is an object property linking an Author to a Paper they submit. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A represents an email address of a Person, while Property B represents the name of a Person. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture entirely different attributes and are therefore unrelated.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its Reviewer, while property B (isWrittenBy) links a Paper to its Author. The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Free Time Break is a type of non-academic event (a scheduled break during the conference). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Trip is a social event (an excursion during a conference), while Slide Set is a document (presentation slides). They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent a paper/contribution that has been reviewed and rejected. The paths show parallel hierarchies (Document > Paper/Contribution > Submitted > Reviewed/Evaluated > Rejected), and siblings match (Accepted contribution / Accepted Paper). In the conference domain, 'contribution' and 'paper' are used synonymously here.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and serve unrelated purposes: 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, while 'is given to' links an Item to a Person.

Property A (isReviewedBy) links a Paper to the people who review it (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while Property B (reviewOfPaper) links a Review document to the Paper it reviews. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics: one connects papers to reviewers, the other connects review artefacts to papers. They are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Rejected Paper is a document (a paper that was not accepted), while Receiving manuscript is an activity/event (the act of receiving a manuscript). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

A Sponsor is a person or entity providing financial support for the conference, while a Program Chair is an organizer responsible for the technical program. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Week Reject Rating is a subclass of Review Rating (a classification/score given to a paper), while Accepting manuscript is an Activity before conference (an action/process). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They represent entirely different relations.

Both classes represent the concept of a City in the conference domain. Although iasted's City has more detailed properties and specialized subclasses (Conference city, Presenter city, etc.), the core intended instances are the same: cities relevant to conferences.

siteURL has domain Conference and range anyURI, while hasHomePage has domain Person and range string. They relate completely different entities (a conference's website vs a person's homepage) and are therefore unrelated.

Both properties express a location relationship, but A is a datatype property mapping a Conference volume to a string, while B is an object property linking physical entities (Building, City, Place) to other physical entities (State, etc.). They differ in type, domain, and range, so they are only related, not equivalent.

Associated Chair is a type of Chairman (organizational role), while Author book proceedings included is a subtype of Author (contributor role). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference part to a Conference volume (mereological/containment), while Property B links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (subject matter). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (an organizational role), while Property B links a document to a speaker (a presentation role). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a type of academic contribution (document), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documents/artefacts related to a conference (papers, reviews, calls, etc.), while Conference in Ontology B is a type of working event (the conference itself). These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and is a sibling of 'Program Committee Chair', indicating it is a distinct role (e.g., an associate/vice chair). In confOf, 'Chair PC' refers to the Program Committee Chair. These are different specific roles within conference organization, so they are related but not equivalent.

NGO is a subclass of Organization in edas, while Sponsor is a subclass of Person in iasted. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and represent fundamentally different concepts (an organization type vs. a person role), so they are unrelated.

In confOf, Regular is a subtype of Participant (alongside Student and Member), representing a regular (non-student) attendee. In edas, Attendee is the general class for all people attending the conference. Thus, confOf:Regular is subsumed by edas:Attendee, as every regular participant is an attendee but not every attendee is necessarily a regular participant (some may be students).
Rejection is a decision outcome regarding a paper submission, while Shuttle bus is a type of transport vehicle. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Programme in edas is a document describing the schedule of conference events. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author (the person who wrote it), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (the person who presents it). Writing and presenting are distinct roles in the conference domain, so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.
Entity A is the general class 'Topic', while Entity B is a specific subclass 'Microelectronics Topic' in edas (whose parent is also 'Topic'). Therefore A subsumes B.

Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, contributions, reviews, announcements, etc. Form in Ontology B (iasted) is a narrow subclass of Document specifically for administrative forms (registration form, hotel registration form, author information form). Their intended instances do not coincide; they are largely disjoint concepts within the conference domain.
writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while hasReview links a Paper to its Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Important dates is a class representing deadlines and key dates for a conference, while Accepted Paper is a class representing a paper that has been accepted. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasEmail and hasLastName are both datatype properties on Person with string range, but they capture entirely different attributes (email address vs. last name). They are unrelated.

'Invited speaker' in Conference is a specific role for someone invited to give a talk at the conference. 'Science Worker' in confOf is a broad category (likely encompassing researchers, scholars, etc.) that serves as a parent class for many roles including Author, Chair PC, Scholar, etc. They are not equivalent; 'Science Worker' is far more general and does not specifically denote an invited speaker.

setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a specific subclass of 'Chairman', distinct from its sibling 'Associated Chair'. In Conference, 'Co chair' is a committee member role with sibling 'Chair'. A conference chair (main chair) and a co-chair are different roles; they overlap as leadership positions but are not equivalent. The main 'Chair' in ontology B would be the closer match to 'Conference Chair' in ontology A.

confOf:Contribution represents submitted scholarly works (Paper, Poster, Short paper) and is the range of 'writes' by Author. ekaw:Document is a much broader class encompassing not only papers but also Reviews, Flyers, Programme Brochures, Web Sites, etc. While they overlap on Paper, Document is significantly more general and includes non-contribution artefacts, so they are related but not equivalent.

Both classes represent the Program Committee Chair role in a conference. 'Chair PC' in confOf and 'PC Chair' in ekaw are synonymous labels for the same concept, both being subclasses of Person/Conference Participant with related PC roles as siblings.

'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (indicating who added the member), while 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (indicating conference membership). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference Session is a type of scientific event (a scheduled session at a conference), while Hotel room is a type of place (accommodation). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (sibling to Paper Presentation, Talk Event). In ekaw, Demo Session is a type of Session under Scientific Event, and Workshop Session is a separate sibling. A workshop and a demo session are distinct types of conference events, though they are related as both being scientific/academic event sub-types.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting), while submit_until relates a Document to a Deadline (a temporal constraint). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Topic is a subject area of the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

has_title is a datatype property linking events to their title (string), while hasStartDateTime links conference events to their start date/time (dateTime). They represent entirely different attributes.
Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper, while Viza in iasted represents a visa document needed for travel to the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A 'Paper' is a general class for conference papers (a type of regular contribution), while Entity B 'Rejected Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper in edas representing only those papers that have been rejected. They are not equivalent; Rejected Paper is more specific than Paper. Since the parent 'Paper' in edas is not provided to establish a direct subsumption link, they are best classified as related.

AcademicEvent in edas is specifically the academic portion of a conference (paper presentations, talks, workshops), while Conference_activity in iasted encompasses all activities during a conference including social events (cocktail reception, coffee break, welcome address). They overlap significantly but neither strictly subsumes the other; they are related concepts covering different scopes of conference happenings.
Tutorial is a type of working event in a conference, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts.

'Information for participants' is a specific type of conference document providing details to attendees, while 'Mailing list' is a distribution mechanism or list of contacts. They represent different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it, while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person who signs it (e.g., an author signing a document). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants), while OC Chair in ekaw is a specific organizing committee role. These are conceptually distinct and neither subsumes the other.

Place represents a physical location (with children like Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place), while Time represents temporal concepts (with children like Conference days, Deadline). These are fundamentally different dimensions and are unrelated.

Industrial Session in ekaw is a specific type of Conference Session, while Session in iasted is a general session class (child of Lecture). The general Session subsumes the more specific Industrial Session.

Both properties express a start date/time, but 'starts on' applies to any Event (domain: Event) while 'Start of conference' applies specifically to Conference (domain: Conference). Since Conference is a kind of Event in the domain, they overlap semantically but are not equivalent due to different domains and ranges (string vs dateTime).

'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (organizational/logistical subdivisions of the event), while 'has Topic' relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject matter). These are fundamentally different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

paperID is a datatype property assigning a numeric identifier to a paper, while remark is a string-valued property for comments/notes on a contribution. They serve entirely different purposes and have different ranges.

Conference Member in cmt refers to participants with organizational roles (chairs, authors, reviewers, PC members), while Paid applicant in the Conference ontology refers to a registered attendee who has paid their fee. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a broad class covering all people participating in the conference (chairs, authors, presenters, registered participants, etc.). Non speaker in iasted is a specific subclass of Delegate that excludes speakers/presenters. Thus Conference Participant strictly subsumes Non speaker.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific type of Chairman (a committee role), while Conference contributor in the Conference ontology is a broad class for people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants). These are conceptually distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

Both properties capture the notion of a city, but they differ significantly: confOf's hasCity is an object property linking Organization/Person to a City class, while edas's hasCity is a datatype property linking ContactInformation to a string. They are related in meaning but not equivalent due to different domains, ranges, and property types.
Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in a conference (subclass of Person), while Conference in the Conference ontology is the event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is a class representing a person who participates in a conference (subclass of Person), while Entity B represents the conference event itself (subclass of Scientific Event). They are entirely different concepts.

Conference applicant in Ontology A refers to a person applying/registering for the conference (with child Registeered applicant), while Tutorial Chair in ekaw is a specific organizational role responsible for tutorials. These are entirely different concepts.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical info to attendees, while 'Computer Networks Measurements Topic' is a specific research topic within computer networks. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic paper (Document), while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Review expertise in Ontology A represents a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill regarding a topic, while Paper in Ontology B represents a submitted document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Committee member is a person serving on a conference committee (with roles like Chair), while a Sponsor is a person or entity providing financial support. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class of persons who contribute to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Technical commitee in Ontology B is a specific role under Delegate, akin to a committee member. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking an Item to an Activity or Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

hasAuthor links Paper to Author (document -> person), while contributes links Person to Conference document (person -> document). They are inverses of each other in direction and have different domain/range types, so they are not equivalent but related.
'writtenBy' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship), while 'referencedIn' indicates that something is cited/referenced in another work. These are semantically distinct relations.

In cmt, User is a superclass of Administrator (as well as Author and Reviewer), representing any person with a system account. In confOf, Administrator is a specific role under Person. Therefore, cmt:User subsumes confOf:Administrator.

The two properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges. 'printHardcopyMailingManifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference for printing manifests, while 'relatedToPaper' relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, while 'notification until' links an Author to a Deadline Author notification. They are unrelated.

Both are classes named Document in the conference domain, but their scopes differ significantly. In cmt, Document is narrowly defined with only Paper and Review as children (core academic artefacts). In iasted, Document is much broader, including administrative items like Invitation letter, Payment document, Viza, Mailing list, etc., under a general Item class. They overlap (both include Review) but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related.
TPC Member is a person role involved in reviewing papers, while Registration fee is a monetary charge for conference registration. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the invitation to submit papers (a call/announcement), whereas an 'Active Paper' in edas is a submitted paper that is currently under review. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'OC Member' in ekaw stands for Organizing Committee Member, which is exactly what 'Organizing Committee member' denotes in sigkdd. Both are subclasses of Person representing members of the organizing committee.

Author in cmt is a person who writes and submits papers, while Submitted contribution in Conference is a document (a submitted paper/contribution). They represent entirely different concepts (person vs. document) and are unrelated.

readPaper (domain: Reviewer, range: Paper) and isReviewedBy (domain: Paper, range: Reviewer/Chair/etc.) are inverse properties relating reviewers to papers in opposite directions. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as they describe the same reviewer-paper relationship from opposite perspectives.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (a role for someone applying to attend), while Registration is a subclass of Conference activity (an event/process). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote fundamentally different concepts.
'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Street' captures a street address. These are entirely different attributes despite both being datatype properties with string range.

In cmt, Document is a superclass of both Paper and Review, making it a general document concept. In Conference, Review is a specific subclass of 'Conference document'. Therefore, cmt:Document subsumes Conference:Review.

Demo Chair (responsible for demo sessions) and Program Chair (responsible for the overall program) are distinct roles in conference organization. They are related as both are chair/organizer positions but not equivalent.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Steering committee, while Property B links a PC Member to a Topic of expertise. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who assigned them), while Property B links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preferences. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while occupy relates a Person to a location (Building, City, State). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Social_event is a general class for social events (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip), while edas:Reception is a specific type of social event. Thus confOf:Social_event subsumes edas:Reception.

In cmt, Author is a general class for anyone who writes/submits a paper (child of Conference Member). In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Speaker, which is a subclass of Author—meaning Lecturer is a specific kind of author who gives lectures. Thus, cmt:Author is more general and subsumes iasted:Lecturer.

Conference fees refers to monetary charges for attending a conference, while Conference Session refers to a scheduled event or meeting within a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history record (metadata about an author's past publications), whereas Paper in ekaw is the actual scholarly document submitted to a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Simulating is a research activity before a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Company (confOf) is a general commercial organization under Organization, while Proceedings Publisher (ekaw) is a specific role of an organization that publishes conference proceedings. A company could act as a proceedings publisher, but the two classes are not equivalent; they overlap in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Camera ready contribution is a type of accepted paper/document. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference in edas represents the academic event/organization itself, while Conference airport in iasted is a physical building (a type of Place > Building) used as an airport for conference attendees. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Pending Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper awaiting a decision), whereas Paper in ekaw is the general class for all papers. Thus, Pending Paper is subsumed by ekaw's Paper.

Talk Event in edas refers to a presentation or speech occurring during the conference (e.g., Welcome Talk, Closing Talk), while Activity before conference in iasted refers to pre-conference administrative or preparatory tasks (e.g., Accepting manuscript, Renting). These are entirely different concepts with no overlap.
A Tutorial is a type of conference session/event, while an Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reception is a social event (like a welcome gathering), while Full day tour is an excursion/tour activity after the conference. Both are post-conference or social activities but denote distinctly different types of events; they share a common ancestor concept (social/after-conference activity) but are not equivalent.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while design relates ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Proceedings in ekaw is a document/volume class (a publication), while Author cd proceedings included in iasted is a person/role class (an author whose work is included in CD proceedings). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Published Paper is a paper that has been published, while Invitation letter is a document used to invite someone (e.g., for visa purposes). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Registration SIGKDD Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while maxChoice is a datatype property on Social/Working events indicating maximum choices. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop is a type of academic event (a session at a conference), while Student lecturer is a type of person/role (a student who lectures). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a document soliciting paper submissions, while a 'Record of attendance' documents who attended the conference. These are entirely different types of conference documents with no semantic overlap.
Meeting Room Place is a physical location (a room for meetings), while Hotel registration form is a document/form used for hotel registration. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference document in Ontology A represents documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, calls, etc.), while Contact Information in edas represents address/phone/email details of a person or organization. These are entirely different concepts.
Organizer is a role or entity that organizes a conference, while Currency refers to a monetary unit. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Written contribution in Conference refers specifically to authored scholarly contributions (papers, posters) submitted to a conference. Document in iasted is much broader, encompassing forms, invitation letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. They overlap (e.g., Submission could be a written contribution), but neither subsumes the other cleanly, so they are related.

Both classes represent a Paper in the conference domain. In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document with children like Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version, and properties linking it to authors, reviewers, and decisions. In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution with siblings Poster and Short paper. Despite different parent class names (Document vs Contribution), both denote the same concept: a paper submitted to a conference.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person (a type of attendee/role), while Registration SIGMOD Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a type of fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent different concepts.
Property A assigns an ISBN string to conference proceedings, while property B assigns a deadline date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'name' applies to Conference and Person entities, while property B 'has_title' applies to Social event and Working event entities. They have completely different domains and serve different purposes in the conference domain; one names people/conferences, the other titles events.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Author representing someone who co-writes a paper (with property 'co write Paper'). In ekaw, 'Paper Author' represents an author of a paper directly under Person. While both denote people who author papers, 'Co author' in cmt specifically emphasizes the co-authorship role and is a specialization of Author, whereas 'Paper Author' in ekaw is the general class for paper authors. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; 'related' best captures their partial semantic overlap.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the overall conference event/organization (with properties like accepts Hardcopy Submissions, has Conference Member, logo URL). In ekaw, 'Conference Session' is a sub-event within a conference (a specific session such as an Industrial Session), subclass of Session < Scientific Event < Event. These are fundamentally different concepts: the whole conference vs. a session within it.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop) representing the entire conference. In edas, Welcome Talk is a specific type of talk event occurring within a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Volunteer (a person who volunteers) and PC Chair (the chair of the program committee) are entirely different roles in a conference organization.

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positiveInteger (maximum number of choices), while End_of_conference links a Conference to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a person participating in or attending a conference. 'Conference participant' in Ontology A (with children Active/Passive) and 'Attendee' in edas both sit directly under Person and serve the same role of denoting someone who takes part in the conference. In the OAEI Conference track reference alignments, these are typically treated as equivalent.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for human individuals in their respective conference ontologies. In confOf, children include Author, Participant, Administrator, etc.; in iasted, children include Delegate, Sponsor. Both represent the same general concept of a person involved in a conference.

'is connected with' in iasted is a broad property linking Activity or Person to Item or Place, while 'can stay in' in sigkdd specifically links Person to Place for accommodation. They overlap on the Person-to-Place dimension but are not equivalent since 'is connected with' has a much broader domain and range.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation that publishes proceedings, while Author cd proceedings included is a person (Author) whose work appears in CD proceedings. They are entirely different concepts.

Short paper in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), whereas Pending Paper in edas is a status-based subclass of Paper indicating the paper's review state. They represent orthogonal dimensions (format vs. status) and are not equivalent.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while TPC Member in edas is a Technical Program Committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls. These are distinct roles in conference organization, though they may overlap (a person can be both). They are related but not equivalent.
Topic represents a subject area of a paper or conference, while Award represents a prize given to authors/papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasEvent relates an Event to another Event in ekaw, while need relates a Person to an Item in iasted. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Invited talk' is a type of Conference contribution (a document/artefact) and also a Presentation. In Ontology B, 'Talk Event' is a type of Conference Event (a scheduled session), with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk. While both relate to talks at a conference, one models the contribution/document aspect and the other models the event/scheduling aspect. They overlap in domain but are not equivalent.

Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume (indicating committee membership/role), while Property B links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference (indicating who holds/organizes it). These relate entirely different domain and range concepts with different semantics.

In confOf, 'Chair PC' (Program Committee Chair) is a direct subclass of Person with no separate Program Chair sibling, suggesting it covers the program chair role. In sigkdd, 'General Chair' is a distinct sibling of 'Program Chair' under Organizator, meaning it refers specifically to the overall conference chair. These are different roles in conference organization, so they are related but not equivalent.

In edas, Paper is a subclass of Document, while in ekaw, Document is the superclass that includes Paper as one of its children (along with Abstract, Flyer, Review, etc.). Therefore, edas:Paper is subsumed by ekaw:Document; they are not equivalent since ekaw:Document is strictly more general.
hasRelatedDocument links events or persons to documents, while partOfEvent links an event to a parent event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

maxPapers is a datatype property on Program Committee Member indicating the maximum number of papers they can handle (range int), while abstract is a datatype property on Contribution holding the paper's abstract text (range string). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (indicating reviewer topic preferences), while Property B links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (indicating the rating a paper received). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Reviewer is a Conference Member who has been assigned to review papers (a committed role). In ekaw, Possible_Reviewer is a broader class of persons who could potentially review (its child is PC Member). Thus cmt:Reviewer denotes someone actively reviewing, while ekaw:Possible_Reviewer denotes a candidate pool; they overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A is specifically the date of acceptance announcement (domain: Important dates), while Property B is a generic Date property for any Deadline. They overlap in that both represent dates associated with conference scheduling, but A is much more specific than B, so they are related rather than equivalent.

hasPostalCode refers to a postal/zip code (a geographic address component), while E-mail refers to an electronic mail address. These are entirely different contact attributes despite both being datatype properties with string ranges.
Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Activity in iasted represents events or tasks (e.g., conference activities). These are entirely different concepts.

paperPresentedAs links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (describing the format of presentation), while give links a Person to an Activity or Item (describing who delivers something). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reviewed contribution is a paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Review Rating is the rating or score assigned to a paper during review. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties named 'hasEmail' with domain Person (edas also includes Contact Information) and range string, serving the same purpose of associating an email address with a person in the conference domain.

Student is a type of conference participant (person attending as a student), while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier under Sponzor. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Contribution is a general class for submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper), while iasted:Submission specifically refers to manuscript submissions (Final manuscript, Initial manuscipt) and is a subclass of Document. Contribution subsumes Submission because it also includes non-manuscript contributions like posters.

Rejected contribution is a submitted paper/contribution that was not accepted, while Review is the evaluation document written by a reviewer. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

One is a datatype property on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted; the other is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution), while ekaw:Camera_Ready_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing the final camera-ready version. Thus confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Camera_Ready_Paper.

In Ontology A, 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference participant', which itself is a subclass of 'Person'. In Ontology B (confOf), 'Participant' is a direct subclass of 'Person' and serves as the general class for all attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student). The confOf 'Participant' corresponds to the broader 'Conference participant' in Ontology A, not specifically to the 'Passive conference participant' subclass. Therefore, Passive conference participant is subsumed by Participant.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Written contribution in Conference is a broad class encompassing all written contributions (with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution). Final manuscript in iasted is a specific type of submission representing the final version of a paper. Thus, Written contribution subsumes Final manuscript, as every final manuscript is a written contribution but not vice versa.
Non speaker in iasted is a delegate who does not present (child of Delegate, sibling of Speaker), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a type of Speaker who presents. These are disjoint concepts.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while defaultChoice is a datatype property on events (Social event, Working event) with a completely different meaning. They are unrelated.

Both classes represent a person who participates in a conference. They share the same parent (Person) and have analogous children representing different types of participants (active/passive vs regular/student). The confOf comment 'confTool' confirms it refers to conference management system participants, matching the Conference ontology's intent.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property (Conference -> int) indicating the number of reviews per paper configured for a conference, while reviewerOfPaper is an object property (Possible Reviewer -> Paper) linking a reviewer to a paper they review. They have different types, domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference is an event/organization entity (with children like Conference volume), while Speaker is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A ('is given by') links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it (Presentation -> Participant). Property B ('presentation') links a Speaker to a Document (Speaker -> Document). The domains and ranges are reversed in role (participant vs presentation) and point to different kinds of entities. They are not equivalent, nor inverses with matching types, so they are unrelated.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), while property B 'reviewes' links a Member PC (a person) to a Contribution (the paper they review). The domains are entirely different (Review vs. Person), so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.
dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic, while obtain relates a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Conference is an event/organization. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a general Conference Member to a Conference, while Property B links a specific Steering committee to a Conference volume. The domains differ significantly (general member vs. steering committee), so these properties are not equivalent and do not subsume each other.

Entity A is a class for informational documents provided to conference participants (a type of Conference document), while Entity B is a specific research topic in computer networks management (a type of Topic). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In Ontology A, Poster is a type of Conference contribution (a document/artefact), whereas in Ontology B, Paper Presentation is a type of Academic Event (an event where a paper is presented). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event) and refer to different things (poster vs. paper presentation).

Session Chair in ekaw is a role for chairing sessions (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building, likely referring to someone hiking/touring at the conference venue. These are entirely different concepts; note that iasted has its own separate 'Session chair' class as a sibling of Conference Hiker.

Entity A 'Conference' denotes the conference event/organization itself, while Entity B 'Conference Paper' denotes a paper submitted to or presented at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents (with child Invited Speaker). In iasted, Delegate is a general conference attendee (with children including Listener, Non speaker, and Speaker). Since Delegate includes non-presenting attendees while Presenter specifically denotes someone who presents, they overlap but are not equivalent; Delegate is more general.

Security Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (abstract for a tutorial) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'write' links a Person to an Item they authored. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Mobile Computing Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while 'volumeContainsPaper' links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Social Event is a type of conference event (e.g., excursion, reception), while Speaker is a type of person who presents at the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference participant in Ontology A refers to people attending or participating in the conference, while Agency Staff Member in Ontology B refers to staff from an external agency (e.g., funding or travel agency). These are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.

'Conference fees' in Ontology A refers to the monetary charges for attending a conference, whereas 'Conference' in Ontology B refers to the event itself (a subtype of Working event). These are entirely different concepts.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'send' relates a Person to an Item (something they send). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Co-chair in Ontology A is a general committee co-chair (sibling of Chair), while PC Chair in Ontology B is specifically the Program Committee chair. They are related leadership roles but not equivalent; PC Chair is more specific to the program committee.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (despite also inheriting from Person/TPC Member, likely an ontology modeling artifact), while Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person representing a student role. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has the last name' is a datatype property for a person's surname (domain: Person), while 'has VAT' refers to value added tax for events (domain: Social event, Working event). They are completely unrelated.
A Conference Paper is a scholarly paper submitted to a conference, while a Mailing list is a distribution list for communications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Accepted contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted after review, while Reject Rating is a class representing a rating value indicating rejection. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejection action), while has_a_publisher relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic, while Property B links a Working event to a Topic. They have different domains (Review preference vs Working event) and different ranges, so they are unrelated properties.

'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership), while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (providing/delivering something). These are semantically unrelated properties.

The properties describe entirely different relations: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who runs paper assignment tools, while 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Talk Event is a type of academic conference event (e.g., closing or welcome talk), while Platinum Supporter is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property specifying the ending date of important dates, while Property B is an object property indicating that an item is sent after a certain time. They have different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property representing an abstract submission date (domain: Important dates, range: date), while Property B represents the abstract text of a contribution (domain: Contribution, range: string). They model entirely different concepts.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they review. Property B (isReviewHistoryOf) links a Personal Review History document to a Reviewer. The domains and ranges are entirely different kinds of entities, so these properties are unrelated.

In EKAW, 'Accepted Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been evaluated and accepted). In SIGKDD, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers. Therefore, EKAW's Accepted Paper is subsumed by SIGKDD's Paper.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history (a record of an individual's publications), while Review in iasted is a document representing a review of a submission. These are entirely different concepts.
Paper Author is a person who authored a paper, while Author attendee book registration fee is a type of monetary fee for conference registration. They are completely different concepts.

Associated Chair in cmt is a type of Chairman (organizing role), while Late Registered Participant in ekaw is a type of Conference Participant based on registration timing. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used to communicate information, while Computer Networks Management Topic is a subject area/topic within the computer networks domain. They are entirely different concepts.
A Workshop is an academic working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), while a Coffee Break is a non-academic break event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reception and Excursion are both subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different specific types of social events (a reception/party vs. a trip/excursion). They are siblings in edas and analogous siblings in confOf, so they are related but not equivalent.
The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings: 'has a committee chair' links a Committee to a Chair, while 'held In' links an Event to a Location.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Main office is a place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

The property 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a contribution (paper) they review, while 'is sent before' relates an item to a time point indicating temporal ordering. These are completely different relations in both domain/range and semantics.
'has authors' links a document to its author (document -> person), while 'write' links a person to an item they wrote (person -> item). They are inverse properties of each other, not equivalent.
Workshop is a type of working event (a meeting/session), while Proceedings is a multi-author document/volume. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (writes) has domain Author and range Contribution, linking an author to their paper. Property B (is sent by) has domain Item and range Person, linking an item to the person who sent it. The directions are reversed (A: Person->Document, B: Document->Person), and the semantics differ (authorship vs. sending). They are not equivalent nor inverses in a strict sense.

startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference for initiating reviewer bidding, while write relates a Person to an Item for authoring. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

In Ontology A, 'Conference' is the event itself (with a child 'Conference volume'), whereas in Ontology B, 'Proceedings' is a document/publication (Multi author Volume > Proceedings). They are related because proceedings are produced by a conference, but they denote different concepts (event vs. publication).

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the entire conference event with properties like date, logo URL, and accepting submissions. In the Conference ontology, 'Conference part' represents a sub-component of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop) that is part of a conference volume. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the whole event, the other is a constituent part.
Conference is a type of working event (an organized gathering), while Hotel is a type of place (accommodation). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Subject Area refers to a topic or field of study that a paper falls under, while Country refers to a geographical nation associated with a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'title' has domain Paper and represents the title of a paper. Property B 'has a name' has domains Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic and represents the name of those entities. The domains are completely disjoint (Paper vs. conference-related entities), so these properties relate different kinds of things and are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference represents the main conference event/organization entity with properties like accepting submissions and having members. In ekaw, Conference Trip is a specific social event (a trip/excursion) that occurs during or around a conference, subclass of Social Event. These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'eventOnList' links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed. They are unrelated.

Test Only Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (abstract for a tutorial) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
'coversTopic' relates a Paper or Event to a Research Topic, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (document). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document soliciting paper submissions, while an 'Organizational Meeting' is a type of academic event/meeting. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties differ in both direction and domain/range. 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event that it comes after (A follows B means A is after B). 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time, indicating the activity occurs before that time. The domains, ranges, and temporal directions are incompatible.

Conference Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a type of Chairman), while Conference contributor in the Conference ontology is a broad category for people who contribute content (authors, speakers). These are conceptually distinct roles with no subsumption relationship.
