Paper Abstract is a specific type of paper document (a summary of a paper), while Mailing list is a communication/distribution list. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person representing someone attending the conference, while Dining Place is a subclass of Place representing a location for eating. They are entirely different concepts in different hierarchies.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'name' in cmt refers to the name of a Conference or Person, while 'has Street' in confOf refers to a street address of an Organization or Person. These denote entirely different concepts and are unrelated.
Track is a part of a conference (like a tutorial or workshop), while Fee is a monetary concept. They are completely unrelated.

Activity in iasted refers to events or actions (e.g., conference activities) with temporal and spatial properties, while Document in sigkdd refers to written artefacts like papers, abstracts, and reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'need' relates a Person to an Item they require, while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review preference in Ontology A is a class representing a reviewer's preference or expertise level for a topic/paper (with properties like 'has a degree'), whereas Reviewer in Ontology B is a Person who performs reviews. These are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Program Committee Member' (cmt) is responsible for reviewing papers and making acceptance decisions, while an 'Organizing Committee member' (sigkdd) handles logistical organization of the conference. These are distinct roles. Note that sigkdd also has a separate 'Program Committee member' class which would be the true equivalent of cmt's Program Committee Member.

Both properties express an organizing/initiating relationship, but they differ in domain and range: 'isInitiatedBy' links a Call to specific conference roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while 'organisedBy' links an Event to Organisation or Person. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'is Menu Of' relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. These are entirely different relations in different parts of the conference domain with no semantic overlap.
Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

writeReview links a Reviewer to a Review (agent produces artefact), while reviews links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (artefact evaluates paper). Different domains, ranges, and directions; they are unrelated properties.
Paper Full Version is a subclass of Paper (a document/artefact), while Operating Topicsystems is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Committee in Ontology A refers to an organizational body (e.g., program committee, organizing committee) with chairs and members, while Conference in Ontology B refers to the overall conference event with dates, topics, and country. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Member is a general conference participant who is a member (as opposed to Regular or Student), while iasted:IASTED_member is specifically a delegate who is a member of the IASTED organization. They overlap conceptually as 'member participants' but differ in scope (general vs organization-specific), so they are related rather than equivalent.

SC Member (Steering Committee Member) in ekaw is a subclass of PC Member, representing a steering committee role. Program Chair in sigkdd represents the chair of the program committee. These are distinct roles within conference organization and do not denote the same concept.
A Tutorial is a type of working event at a conference, while a Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Working event is a type of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Medicine Topic is a specific subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to its name (string). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has a review' links a reviewed contribution to its review, while 'has Updated Version' links a document to an updated version of that document. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Travel Grant is a type of Sponsorship (financial support for travel), while Sponsor city is a type of City (a geographical location). They are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a Paper to the person(s) who review it. 'is Reviewed By' in edas and 'has Reviewer' in ekaw express the same relation (Paper -> reviewer role), with slightly different but semantically overlapping range classes (Reviewer/TPC Member vs Possible Reviewer).

In confOf, Participant is a general class for conference attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student) and Author is a sibling class under Person. In iasted, Author is a specific role under Speaker/Delegate. Thus confOf:Participant is more general than iasted:Author, making it a subsumption relation.

The 'email' property represents an email address while 'has Fax' represents a fax number. Although both are datatype properties on Person with string range, they denote entirely different contact information and are not equivalent or related.

PC Chair (ekaw) is the chair/head of the Program Committee, while Program Committee member (sigkdd) is a general member of the PC. In ekaw, PC Chair is a subclass of PC Member, so PC Chair subsumes/is more specific than a generic PC member. However, sigkdd distinguishes 'Program Chair' (a sibling of 'Program Committee member'), meaning its 'Program Committee member' refers to regular members, not the chair. Thus they are related but not equivalent; PC Chair is more specific than a general PC member.

Submitted Paper in ekaw refers to a paper that has been submitted to a conference for review (a pre-publication artefact), while Publication in iasted refers to published proceedings (Book proceeding, Cd proceening). These are distinct concepts at different stages of the scholarly communication lifecycle and do not share intended instances.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'volumeContainsPaper' relates a publication volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

has First Name is a datatype property for a Person's first name, while Name of sponsor is a datatype property for a Sponsor's name. They have different domains (Person vs Sponzor) and different semantic meanings.
Departure is a post-conference activity/event, while Main office is a physical place. They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

Academia Organization in edas is a broad class for any academic organization (parent: Organization, siblings include Government/Industry/NGO). Research Institute in ekaw is a specific type of Academic Institution (siblings: University). A Research Institute is a kind of Academia Organization, but Academia Organization also includes universities and other academic bodies, so they are not equivalent. They overlap significantly, hence 'related'.

Free Time Break is a specific type of break event during a conference (a short period of free time), while Trip day is a full day designated for trips/excursions under the Time hierarchy. They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCo-author links a Paper to its Co-author (a specific author role), while authorOf links a Person to a Document they authored. They differ in domain, range, and direction: hasCo-author goes from paper to person, authorOf goes from person to document. The inverse of hasCo-author would be closer to authorOf, but even then the ranges/domains are not fully aligned (Co-author vs Person, Paper vs Document). Thus they are unrelated as properties.
Author is a Person who writes papers, while Individual Presentation is an Event (a talk or presentation). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a written work (Contribution/Item) to its author (Author/Person). In the conference domain, Contribution maps to Item and Author maps to Person, making these properties semantically equivalent.
hasMember relates a Conference to its member Persons, while is_occupied_by relates physical locations (Building, City, State) to Persons. Different domains and different semantics.

The property 'reviewes' relates a PC member to a contribution (paper) for reviewing purposes, while 'is paid with' relates money to an item for payment purposes. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Written contribution in Ontology A is a type of conference document/paper, while Conference in Ontology B is a type of working event. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a very broad class encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and PC Members (essentially anyone affiliated with the conference). In the Conference ontology, 'Conference contributor' specifically denotes those who contribute content (authors, speakers) and is a sibling of 'Committee member' and 'Reviewer'. Thus, Conference contributor is narrower than Conference Member; they overlap but are not equivalent.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is paid for' relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Accommodation Place refers to lodging for conference attendees, while Presenter university refers to the academic institution a presenter is affiliated with. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a website/URL resource), while Hotel is a physical place for accommodation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Coffee break is a conference activity (event), while Conference hall is a place (location). They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event), whereas Conference Participant in ekaw is a subclass of Person (someone attending/participating). These are fundamentally different concepts.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership), while hold links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizing/holding). Different domains and different semantics.
Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) while Sponzor fee is a type of fee (subclass of Fee). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (isLocationOf) relates a Place to a Conference Event, indicating where an event takes place. Property B (holded_by) relates a Conference to ACM SIGKDD, indicating the organizing body. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while B is an object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Review is a document evaluating a paper in the conference domain, while Transport vehicle is a physical vehicle (car, bus, etc.) for transportation. They are completely unrelated concepts.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a specific room within a venue where sessions occur, while a 'Conference building' in iasted is the entire building hosting the conference. They overlap conceptually (both are physical locations for conference activities) but are not equivalent; a meeting room is typically part of a conference building. Hence 'related'.
Subject Area refers to a topic or field of study for papers, while Time zone refers to a geographical time region. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Meta Review is a type of document (a review artifact), while Member PC is a type of person (a program committee member/reviewer). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (event organization). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A relates a steering committee to a conference volume, while property B relates an author to a contribution they write. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Property A links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment relation), while Property B links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic (preference subject). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Author is a Conference Member who writes/submits papers. In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (someone who presents). The cmt Author corresponds to edas Author, not specifically to edas Presenter. A Presenter is a more specific role than an Author, so they are related but not equivalent; cmt:Author subsumes edas:Presenter in intent.
Short paper is a type of academic contribution/submission, while Mailing list is a document used for communication purposes. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'Author attendee cd registration fee' is a specific subclass of 'Registration fee'. In sigkdd, 'Registration fee' is the general class with its own subclasses (e.g., Registration Student, Registration Non Member). Therefore, the iasted class is strictly more specific and is subsumed by the sigkdd class.

Paper Presentation is an event (a type of academic event where a paper is presented), while Speaker is a person role (someone who presents). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (event vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person or Contact Information to a string (email address), while send is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They represent entirely different relations.

Working event is a type of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Multimedia Topic is a specific subject topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

'has parts' is a mereological property linking a Conference volume to its Conference parts, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties relate a committee to one of its members, but they target different roles: 'has Program Committee Member' links a Program Committee to a generic Program Committee Member, while 'has a committee co chair' links a Committee to a Co-chair (a leadership role). They overlap in the general sense of committee membership but are not equivalent.
Closing Talk is a type of conference event (a talk), while Invited Speaker is a type of person (a speaker role). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Conference is a type of working event (a gathering), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject area/topic. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Meal Menu (a document listing food options for a meal event) and Review (an evaluation of a paper) are entirely different concepts in the conference domain, despite both being subclasses of Document.

Banquet is a social event (an activity/occasion), while Dining Place is a physical location (a place). They belong to fundamentally different categories in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'is writen by' links an Item to its author (Person). These are fundamentally different relations (reviewing vs. authoring) and are unrelated.

OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) is a senior role overseeing the entire conference organization, while Session chair presides over a single session. They are both chair roles but at different levels of scope, so they are related but not equivalent.
Review is a document evaluating a paper, while Departure tax is a type of monetary tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

The 'follows' property in confOf relates Administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Accepted Paper is a paper that has been accepted for presentation at a conference, while Award is a prize or recognition given (e.g., Best Paper Award). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document (Person -> Document). Property B 'is prepared by' has domain Item and range Person (Document -> Person). These are inverse relations, not equivalent. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to its subject area/topic. In cmt, 'has Subject Area' connects Paper to Subject Area; in confOf, 'deals With' connects Contribution (equivalent to Paper) to Topic (equivalent to Subject Area). They express the same relation.

hasConferenceMember is an object property linking a Conference to its members, while Name_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to its name string. They are entirely different relations.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Reception is a social event at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

The 'name' property in cmt captures the name of a Conference or Person, while 'hasEmail' in edas captures an email address for Contact Information or a Person. These are semantically distinct properties (name vs. email) and are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper, while Review in sigkdd is a document that evaluates/reviews a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named Document and serve as the parent class for Paper and Review in their respective ontologies. In both cmt and sigkdd, Document represents a written artefact in the conference domain (papers, reviews, abstracts). Despite slight differences in children (sigkdd also includes Abstract) and associated properties, the intended instances coincide, making them equivalent.

The property 'go through' in iasted relates an Item to an Activity (e.g., a paper going through a review process), while 'submit' in sigkdd relates an Author to a Paper (an author submitting a paper). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Administrative event in confOf is a broad category of conference events (including submission, reviewing, registration, etc.), while Deadline Author notification in sigkdd is a specific deadline for notifying authors. They belong to different hierarchies (Event vs Deadline) and have very different scopes; they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Accepted Paper is a paper that has passed review and been accepted for the conference proceedings, while Abstract is a summary document submitted alongside or instead of a full paper. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with different positions in their respective hierarchies.

'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Postal Code' captures a postal/zip code for an organization or person. These are entirely different attributes with no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent a paper/contribution that has been submitted to a conference but not yet reviewed or accepted. 'Submitted contribution' in Conference and 'Submitted Paper' in ekaw occupy the same position in their respective hierarchies (child of Paper/Contribution, parent of reviewed/assigned papers) and denote the same concept.

Property A ('was a committee chair of') links a Chair to a Committee and is a sub-property of 'was a member of'. Property B ('is Member Of') links a Person to a Conference. While both express a form of membership/affiliation, they differ in domain (Chair vs Person), range (Committee vs Conference), and specificity (chairing vs general membership). They are related but not equivalent.

'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'is sent by' links an Item to the Person who sent it. These describe fundamentally different relations (reviewing vs. sending) and are unrelated.

Invited talk in Ontology A is a type of conference contribution/presentation (a talk given by an invited speaker), whereas Conference in Ontology B is a type of working event (the conference event itself). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

State in iasted refers to a geographical or administrative location (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, and properties like is_situated_in), while Speaker in sigkdd refers to a person who gives presentations (subclass of Person). These are entirely different concepts.

hasStartDateTime denotes the start time of a Conference Event (range dateTime), while done_till denotes the end/deadline date of a Deadline (range date). They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite temporal semantics (start vs. end), so they are unrelated.

Both classes represent the proceedings of a conference published as a book/volume. EKAW's 'Proceedings' (with child 'Conference Proceedings') and IASTeD's 'Book proceeding' (sibling to 'Cd proceeding', i.e., CD-ROM proceedings) denote the same concept: a printed/book-format collection of conference papers.
Workshop is a type of working event in a conference context, while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

endReview links a Program Committee Chair to a Review (likely indicating the chair ends/completes a review process), while isReviewing links various roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper (indicating they are currently reviewing that paper). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly.

'has a degree' is a datatype property on Review preference with integer range (likely an academic degree level), while 'Nation' is a datatype property on Person with string range (a nationality). They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In ontology A, 'Conference proceedings' is a leaf-level class representing the published proceedings of a conference. In ontology B (ekaw), 'Proceedings' is a broader parent class (subclass of Multi author Volume) that has 'Conference Proceedings' as a child. Therefore, A's 'Conference proceedings' corresponds to ekaw's 'Conference Proceedings', making it more specific than ekaw's 'Proceedings'. Hence A is subsumed by B, or equivalently B subsumes A.
Place in iasted is a general class for locations, while Main office in sigkdd is a specific subclass of Place. Therefore, iasted:Place subsumes sigkdd:Main_office.

Conference in Ontology A represents an academic conference event, while State in iasted represents a geographical or administrative region (with children like Conference state, Presenter state). These are entirely different concepts.
Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution/document, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (hasConferenceMember) has domain Conference and range Conference Member, linking a conference to its members. Property B (was_a_member_of) has domain Committee member and range Committee, linking a committee member to a committee. They differ in both direction (A is forward, B is inverse-style) and the kinds of entities they relate (Conference vs Committee). Thus they are unrelated.

Reception in edas is a specific social event (a welcome gathering), while Technic activity in iasted is a broad category of technical conference activities that includes lectures, presentations, etc. They are not equivalent; in fact, iasted's 'Coctail reception' sibling would be the closer match to edas's Reception.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Bank transfer is a payment document type (subclass of Payment document). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person (usage). These are semantically distinct relations with different intended meanings.

A 'Conference announcement' is a specific document used to announce conference details, while a 'Mailing list' is a distribution mechanism or list of contacts. They serve different purposes in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

In Ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution', which is the top-level class for all contributions (with children including Poster, Presentation, etc.). In Ontology B, 'Contribution' is the top-level class for all contributions (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper). Thus, confOf's 'Contribution' corresponds to Conference's 'Conference contribution', making 'Regular contribution' strictly more specific (subsumed_by) than 'Contribution'.

hasPhone and E-mail are both datatype properties linking Person to string, but they represent different contact methods (phone number vs email address). They are related as sibling contact properties but not equivalent.

Paper is a scholarly contribution (document) submitted to a conference, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to recognize an outstanding paper. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Paper in ekaw is a type of document/paper submitted to a conference, while Conference days in iasted is a temporal concept representing the duration of a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Participant is a class representing a person attending the conference (subclass of Person), while Nonmember registration fee is a monetary concept (subclass of Registration fee). They are entirely different kinds of entities.

In Ontology A, Poster is a type of Conference contribution (a document/artefact), sibling to Presentation and Written contribution. In Ontology B, Individual Presentation is a type of Scientific Event (an activity/occurrence) with children like Contributed Talk and Tutorial. They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a document type, the other is an event type.
Paper Author is a person who writes papers, while Best Research Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are entirely different concepts.

Active conference participant is a broad class for anyone who actively contributes (e.g., gives presentations), including authors and speakers. OC Member specifically denotes an Organising Committee member, which is a distinct organisational role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Scientific Event is a subclass of Event (a type of scientific gathering or activity). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote completely different concepts.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator for running assignment tools, while 'submit' links an Author to a Paper for submission.
Rejected Paper is a paper that has been evaluated and rejected, while Abstract is a summary document type. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link an author/person to a paper/document they authored. In edas, hasRelatedPaper connects Author to Paper; in ekaw, authorOf connects Person to Document. Given that Author/Person and Paper/Document are equivalent across these ontologies, the two properties express the same authorship relation.

A TPC Member is a member of the Technical Program Committee responsible for reviewing papers and initiating calls. In ontology B, 'Speaker' is a subclass of Delegate with children Author and Reviewer, while 'Technical commitee' appears as a sibling of Speaker. Thus TPC Member aligns more closely with 'Technical commitee' in iasted, not with 'Speaker'. They are related only insofar as both are conference participant roles.

hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a quality assessment), while reviewOfPaper links a Review document to the Paper it reviews. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes are named 'Organization' and represent the same concept in the conference domain (an organizational entity such as a company or university). Ontology B's children (Company, University) and properties (employedBy, address-related) confirm it models organizations that employ people, which aligns with the typical use of Organization in conference ontologies.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'was a steering committee of' links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person. They are unrelated.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of chairman), while One conference day is a temporal concept representing a single day of the conference. They are entirely unrelated.

In iasted, Item is a very broad class (including Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, etc.) with Document as one of its children. In sigkdd, Document is a narrower class specifically for conference documents like Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus, iasted:Item subsumes sigkdd:Document.
Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a subject area/topic classification for papers, while Conference Session is an event type within a conference program. They are entirely different concepts.
Committee member is a person role in a conference committee, while Registration fee is a monetary amount for registration. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Poster is a type of academic contribution (a presentation format), while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent the published proceedings of a conference in book form. 'Conference proceedings' in Ontology A and 'Book proceeding' in Ontology B (a subclass of Publication, sibling to 'Cd proceening') denote the same concept: the printed/book-format collection of conference papers.

Industry Organization is a type of organization (company/business entity), while Organizing Committee member is a person role within the conference organizing committee. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference proceedings is the published volume/collection of papers (with ISBN, publisher, volume), while Contribution in confOf represents an individual submitted work (paper, poster, short paper) written by authors and reviewed by PC members. These are fundamentally different concepts.
employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (receiving something). Different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

'has the last name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their surname), while 'is designed for' is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They have completely different semantics, types, domains, and ranges.

In edas, Document is a class for conference-related documents (Paper, Review, Programme, etc.). In iasted, Item is a much broader physical/logistical concept (Audiovisual equipment, Transport vehicle, Card, etc.) that happens to have Document as one of its children. Thus edas:Document is more specific than iasted:Item; they are not equivalent and the overlap is too narrow to warrant 'related'.

hasBeenAssigned in cmt goes from Reviewer to Paper (reviewer is assigned a paper), while hasReviewer in ekaw goes from Paper to Possible Reviewer (paper has a reviewer). These are inverse properties relating the same domain concepts but in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.
A Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity/presentation, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Conference Chair is the overall chair of the entire conference, while a Session chair presides over an individual session within the conference. They are distinct roles at different levels of granularity, though both are types of chairs in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Call for participation is a conference document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of Working event), while Worker lecturer in iasted is a person/role (a type of Lecturer). They are entirely different concepts.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class (child of Person) that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Invited Speaker in ekaw is a specific subclass of Presenter. Thus, Conference contributor subsumes Invited Speaker, but they are not equivalent.

Person in edas is a top-level class encompassing all people involved (attendees, authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Speaker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate and has siblings like Listener and Non speaker, meaning it only covers a subset of conference participants. Therefore, Person subsumes Speaker.

hasRelatedDocument in edas links events, conferences, sessions, or persons to documents, while paperPresentedAs in ekaw links papers/abstracts to individual presentations. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B (obtain) relates an Author to an Award. The ranges are entirely different concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the format/completeness of a paper (as opposed to Paper Abstract), while Accepted Paper in ekaw refers to the review outcome status of a submitted paper. These are orthogonal dimensions: a full version can be rejected, and an accepted paper could initially have been submitted as an abstract. They do not denote the same concept.

has_workshops links a conference volume to its workshops (a type of sub-event), while hasProgramme links a conference event to its programme/schedule. Workshops and programmes are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.

Both classes are named 'Place' and serve the same role in the conference domain: representing physical locations where conference-related activities occur. Their children (e.g., Accommodation Place/Hotel room, Conference Venue Place/Conference hall, Meeting Room Place/Session room) align closely, confirming they denote the same concept.
Company is an organization type (business entity), while Cheque is a payment document. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Workshop is a type of conference event/program part (a session or track), while Session room is a physical place/location where sessions are held. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. location) and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Organizational Meeting' is a specific type of academic event (like a committee or business meeting) and is a sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, and Workshop. In ekaw, 'Conference' represents the entire conference event itself (one edition), with siblings like Session, Track, and Workshop. An organizational meeting within a conference is not equivalent to the conference as a whole.

A is a datatype property (remark) on Contribution with string range; B is an object property (reviewWrittenBy) on Review linking to a Possible Reviewer. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics entirely.

Chair PC in confOf is the chair of the program committee (a leadership/organizational role), while Reviewer in iasted is a person who reviews papers. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities and intended instances.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (the outcome of accepting a paper), whereas Reject Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a reviewer's rating indicating rejection). They differ both in concept (decision vs. rating) and polarity (accept vs. reject), making them unrelated.

hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a quality assessment), while reviewWrittenBy links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (the author of the review). These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding process), while writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Student is a type of conference participant (person role), while Two Level Conference is a type of conference event. They belong to entirely different categories in the domain and share no semantic overlap.

Reception and Conference Banquet are both subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different types of social events. In confOf, Reception and Banquet are siblings, confirming they are distinct concepts. Therefore they are related (both are social events) but not equivalent.

Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level, while property B links a document to a speaker who presents it. These relate entirely different concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.
hasPostalCode refers to a postal/zip code for an address, while Name refers to a person's name. These are entirely different concepts despite both being datatype properties with string range.

A Workshop is a working event (like a conference or tutorial) involving collaborative sessions, while a Closing Talk is a specific talk event that concludes a conference. They are entirely different types of events with no hierarchical or semantic overlap.
hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City (location), while organises relates an Organisation or Person to an Event. The ranges (City vs Event) and semantics are entirely different.

relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation (a paper's participation in an event), while listsEvent links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (a document listing events). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reception in confOf is a social event (sibling of Banquet, Trip), while Technic activity in iasted is a conference activity that includes technical/programmatic items like Lecture, Presentation, and Registration. Notably, iasted has 'Coctail reception' as a sibling of Technic activity, confirming they are distinct concepts. These classes do not share the same intended instances.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Registration in iasted is a conference activity (the act of registering). These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a conference-level entity to a component of its schedule/programme. However, 'has tutorials' specifically relates a Conference volume to Tutorial instances, while 'has Programme' relates a Conference Event to a Programme instance. Tutorials are typically one part of a programme, so these properties overlap in purpose but differ in domain, range, and specificity.

In Ontology A, 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference participant' contrasted with 'Active conference participant', implying someone who attends without an active role (e.g., not presenting or reviewing). In edas, 'Attendee' is a top-level role under Person alongside Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc., suggesting it also denotes someone attending without those specific active roles. However, the hierarchical structures differ: in A it is nested under Conference participant, while in edas it is directly under Person. They overlap significantly in intended instances but are not strictly equivalent due to differing taxonomic placements and potential scope differences.
Welcome address is a conference activity (event), while Conference hall is a place/venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (date), while 'has Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Conference Member is a general class whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc. In edas, Reviewer is a specific role (a person who reviews papers). Therefore, cmt:Conference Member subsumes edas:Reviewer.
'is held in' relates an Activity to a Place/Time (location/scheduling), while 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Co-author to a Paper (co-writes), while Property B links a Conference document to a Person (has authors). The domains and ranges are reversed in direction relative to the authorship relationship: A goes from person-role to paper, B goes from document to person. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other; they are essentially inverse-like but with mismatched domain/range classes, making them unrelated for alignment purposes.

Property A (assignedTo) links a Paper to a Reviewer, representing paper-to-reviewer assignment. Property B (has_a_submitted_contribution) links Review expertise to a Submitted contribution, representing the papers associated with a reviewer's expertise area. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Published Paper is a document/artefact (a paper that has been published), while Research is an activity performed before the conference. They belong to entirely different categories (document vs. activity) and are unrelated.

Talk Event is a type of conference event (an activity), while Presenter is a role played by a person. They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and are not equivalent or hierarchically related.

Review in Ontology A is a document that evaluates a paper (child of Conference document), while Call in Ontology B is an invitation/solicitation (e.g., Call For Papers, Call For Reviews). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Review in ekaw is a document that evaluates a paper (with children Negative/Neutral/Positive Review), while Abstract in sigkdd is a summary of a paper. They are distinct sibling concepts under Document in their respective ontologies and do not denote the same concept.
One is a datatype property linking Person to an email string; the other is an object property linking Document to Person. They are entirely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A (title) gives the title of a Paper, while property B (has the first name) gives the first name of a Person. They have different domains and denote entirely different attributes.
A Tutorial is a type of conference session/event, while a Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In confOf, Poster is a sibling of Paper under Contribution, representing a distinct type of contribution (a poster presentation). In ekaw, Conference Paper is a subclass of Paper, and Poster Paper is listed as a sibling of Conference Paper. Thus, confOf:Poster corresponds more closely to ekaw:Poster Paper rather than ekaw:Conference Paper. They are related as both represent types of scholarly contributions at a conference, but they are not equivalent.

Property A links a conference volume to its important dates, while property B links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a conference it holds. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the concept of a Deadline in the conference domain. They share similar children (submission deadlines, notification deadlines) and analogous date-related properties (done till vs Date). Despite different parent structures, their intended instances coincide.

Both classes represent the body responsible for organizing the conference. In EKAW it is modeled as a subclass of Organisation (Organising Agency), while in SIGKDD it is modeled as a subclass of Committee (Organizing Committee). Despite different parent hierarchies, their intended instances in the conference domain coincide: the group that organizes the event.
The properties have opposite directions: 'co write Paper' goes from Co author (a Person) to Paper, while 'writtenBy' goes from Document to Person. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent.
Active conference participant is a person role in a conference, while City is a geographical location. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Working event in confOf is a broad category encompassing Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop (academic working events). Lecture in iasted is a specific type of conference activity with children Plenary lecture, Session, and Tutorial. They overlap (both can include tutorials/sessions) but are not equivalent: Working event is broader and includes full conferences/workshops, while Lecture is narrower and focused on presentation-type activities.

Entity A is a document/form (Author information form) used to collect author details, while Entity B is a person/role (Author of paper). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
hasAuthor links a Paper to an Author, while heldIn links an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while is_sent_after relates an Item to a Time. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators). Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Fee/Registration fee representing a type of payment. These are entirely different concepts.

Paper in cmt is a document/submission artifact, while Computer Networks Measurements Topic in edas is a specific subject area/topic classification. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and describe unrelated relationships: 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker.
belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, while is_given_by links an Activity/Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enableVirtualMeeting' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker. They are unrelated.

Property A ('date') represents the date of a conference (domain: Conference, range: date), while property B ('has a volume') represents the volume number of conference proceedings (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int). They describe entirely different concepts with different domains and ranges.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while hasEvent relates an Event to another Event. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, announcements, reviews, and contributions. Conference Paper in ekaw is specifically a paper submitted/presented at a conference (a subclass of Paper). Thus Conference document subsumes Conference Paper, as the latter corresponds roughly to 'Conference contribution' which is a child of Conference document.

Both classes represent the same concept: a coffee break during a conference. Despite different hierarchical placements (Break Event in edas vs Conference activity in iasted), their intended instances coincide.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator (a person who entered details), while property B links a Working event to an Administrative event (an event type). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Review expertise in Ontology A is a class representing the level of expertise a reviewer has for reviewing submissions. Person in Ontology B (iasted) is a general class representing human beings, with children like Delegate and Sponsor. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Active Paper is a paper under review in the conference submission process, while Card is a physical payment or identification card (with child Credit card). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Academia Organization is a type of organization (academic institution), while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Registration fee is a monetary charge for conference registration. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A ('is the 1th part of') links an Abstract to a Paper, Poster, or Presentation, expressing that the abstract is a component/part of those artefacts. Property B ('presentation Of Paper') links an Individual Presentation to an Abstract or Paper, expressing which paper a presentation belongs to. Although both involve papers and presentations, their domains differ (Abstract vs Individual Presentation), their directions differ (part-of vs presentation-of), and their semantics are not equivalent. They are related because they both connect presentation/abstract concepts to papers.

Reviewer in cmt is a Person (a role) who reviews papers, while Reviewing event in confOf is an Event (the reviewing procedure itself). They belong to entirely different categories (person vs. event) and are not equivalent.
isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while publisherOf relates an Organisation to published materials (Flyer, etc.). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A is 'Tutorial' (a conference part), while Entity B is 'Conference' (a working event). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain. Notably, confOf has its own 'Tutorial' class as a sibling of 'Conference', confirming that A and B do not match.
locationOf relates a Location to an Event, while submit_until relates a Document to a Deadline. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Industrial Session is a type of event/session in the conference program, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Place) and are unrelated.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Early Registered Participant is a person (a type of conference participant). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Both denote a talk/lecture given by an invited speaker at a conference. However, their ontological contexts differ significantly: in Ontology A, 'Invited talk' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact) and 'Presentation', while in Ontology B, 'Speaker lecture' is a subclass of 'Session' (an event/activity). Because one models the contribution artefact and the other models the session event, they are related but not strictly equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains (Activity vs Document), ranges (Time vs Deadline), and semantics ('is held after' indicates temporal ordering of activities, while 'submit until' indicates a submission deadline for documents). They are unrelated.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person representing anyone attending the conference. In iasted, Technical commitee is a subclass of Delegate (which is under Conference building > Place), representing a specific role within the technical committee. While both relate to people involved in a conference, they are not equivalent: Attendee is a general participant class, whereas Technical commitee is a specific organizational role. They overlap conceptually but are not the same.

Paper Author in ekaw is a Person who writes papers, while Author information form in iasted is a Document/Form used to collect author details. They are entirely different concepts (person vs. document).

Both classes represent the Program Committee within a conference organization context. They share the same parent class (Committee) and similar sibling classes (Organizing Committee), making them clearly equivalent.
hasRating links a paper to its review rating, while submit links an author to a paper they submitted. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document/volume (a subclass of Proceedings), while Author cd proceedings included in iasted is a person/role (a subclass of Author). They are entirely different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.
Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

Written contribution in Conference is a broad class encompassing all written contributions (including regular and submitted contributions). Initial manuscript in iasted specifically refers to the first/submitted version of a paper, contrasted with Final manuscript. Thus Written contribution subsumes Initial manuscript, as an initial manuscript is one type of written contribution.

Sponzorship in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial contribution/payment), while Exhibitor in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor (an entity/agent that sponsors). One represents money, the other represents an agent; they are unrelated concepts.
Pending Paper is a paper awaiting a decision, while Mailing list is a communication document/list. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (assignExternalReviewer) relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment action between two reviewer roles). Property B (reviewerOfPaper) relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (linking a reviewer to the paper they review). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Property A links a Conference Member (an individual person) to a Conference, while Property B links a Committee (a group/organizational body) to a Conference volume. The domains are fundamentally different (person vs. committee), so these properties do not denote the same relation.

Both properties describe a reviewer being brought in by another reviewer, but they differ in domain (External Reviewer vs Reviewer) and use different terminology ('assigned By' vs 'invited by'). They are related as they capture a similar delegation/invitation relationship in the review process, but are not strictly equivalent due to differing domains.

Property A (has authors) links a Conference document to its authoring Person(s), while property B (presentation) links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains and ranges are reversed in role (document vs person/speaker) and the semantics differ: authorship is not the same as giving a presentation. They are unrelated.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Demo Session is a type of event/session. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Paper Abstract in cmt is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Operating Topicsystems in edas is a conference topic/subject area. They are entirely different concepts.

Program Committee Chair is a leadership role within the program committee responsible for managing reviews, while Author is a person who writes papers. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Security Topic' is a subject area (topic) related to security within the conference scope. These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties describe entirely different relations: one links a Conference to an Administrator who prints hardcopy mailing manifests, while the other links a Paper/Abstract to its Individual Presentation form. They share no semantic overlap.

Workshop is a type of academic event in edas, while Author book proceedings included is a role/type of author in iasted. They represent entirely different concepts (event vs. person role) and are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted document (with authors, reviews, decisions). In ekaw, Multi-author Volume is a published collection (parent of Proceedings). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Regular in confOf is a type of Participant (a person), while Regular Session in ekaw is a type of Session (an event). They are completely different concepts sharing only the word 'Regular'.
Chairman is a Person role (a type of conference chair), while Social Event is an Event (e.g., banquet or trip). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Paper is a general class for all papers (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). In ekaw, Demo Paper is a specific subtype of Paper. Therefore, the edas Paper class subsumes the ekaw Demo Paper class.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while pay relates a Person to Money (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to the conference), while Break Event is a subclass of Non Academic Event (a type of event like coffee breaks). These are entirely different concepts in the domain.
The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'search' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponsor. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract of a submitted paper, while Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Abstract representing the abstract of an invited talk. These are distinct types of documents for different purposes in a conference and do not share the same intended instances.

Both classes represent the general concept of a Person in the conference domain. They share similar children (reviewers, committee members, chairs) and analogous properties (email, name). The intended instances coincide across both ontologies.
A Slide Set is a collection of presentation slides, while a Paper is a written academic document. They are distinct sibling concepts under Document in the conference domain.
Acceptance is a type of Decision regarding paper acceptance, while Listener is a type of Person who attends the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference part (A) refers to structural components of a conference such as tracks, tutorials, and workshops, while Conference Event (B) refers to scheduled occurrences with times, locations, and attendees (academic or non-academic events). They overlap conceptually since tracks/tutorials are often realized as events, but they model different aspects: A models the organizational structure and B models temporal/spatial scheduling. Hence they are related but not equivalent.

confOf:Student represents any student participant (including speakers and non-speakers), while iasted:Student non speaker is specifically a student who is not a speaker. Therefore, Student subsumes Student non speaker.

Late Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered late, while Tutorial speaker is a person who gives a tutorial. These are entirely different roles with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, Paper is a full submission document (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version), while in ekaw, Paper is a sibling of Abstract. The ekaw Abstract represents presentation abstracts (Invited Talk Abstract, Tutorial Abstract) linked to Individual Presentations, not the submitted paper itself. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the chair of the organizing committee for a conference. 'Co chair' in Conference ontology is a Committee member who chairs a committee (with properties linking to Committee), while 'OC Chair' in ekaw is explicitly the Organizing Committee Chair (child of OC Member). In the conference domain these denote the same role.

Property A (isMemberOf) relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while Property B (holded_by) relates a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.
'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship), while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (organizing). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In Ontology A, 'Active conference participant' is a specific subclass of 'Conference contributor' (with siblings like Passive conference participant and Regular author), denoting someone who actively presents. In Ontology B, 'Participant' is a broad class directly under Person covering all attendees (with children Member, Regular, Student). Thus, the more specific Active_conference_participant is subsumed by the general Participant class in confOf.

Administrative event in confOf covers submission, reviewing, registration, and camera-ready events (administrative/organizational tasks), while Social Event in edas covers excursions and receptions (non-academic social activities). These are disjoint concepts; confOf's sibling 'Social event' would align with edas's 'Social Event', not 'Administrative event'.
University is an educational organization where scholars study, while Value added tax is a type of monetary tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

'has Country' links an Organization or Person to a Country (a geographic/national affiliation), while 'speak in' links a Person to a Place and Time (an event participation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop is a type of academic event (a meeting/session), while Conference Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no meaningful overlap.
Meta Review is a type of review document in the conference process, while Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's past publications. These are entirely different concepts.
hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event for releasing review outcomes to authors, while Workshop is an academic event (a type of session at a conference). They belong to different branches of the event hierarchy and denote entirely different concepts.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting people to participate (e.g., attend or submit), while a 'Conference Paper' is an actual paper presented at the conference. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Reviewer is a person who reviews papers (a conference member role), while a Paid applicant is a registered attendee who has paid for the conference. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Review expertise in Ontology A denotes a reviewer's level of expertise or skill regarding a topic/paper, whereas Review in ekaw (Ontology B) is a document (subclass of Document) that contains the written evaluation of a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person representing someone who attends the conference, while Activity after conference is a subclass of Activity representing events occurring after the conference (e.g., departure, tours). They are entirely different concepts.

Conference volume in Ontology A represents the proceedings or organizational unit of a conference (with committees, contributions, tracks, etc.), while Building in Ontology B is a physical structure/place. These are entirely different concepts.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper (authorship). Different domains and different semantics.

hasPhone relates a Person to their phone number string, while hasCity relates Contact Information to a city name string. They describe entirely different attributes with different domains and semantics.

In cmt, Reviewer and Program Committee Member are distinct sibling classes under Conference Member. In confOf, 'Member PC' has the comment 'Reviewer' and its property 'reviewes' points to Contribution (paper), indicating it serves the reviewer role. However, since cmt explicitly separates PC members from reviewers while confOf conflates them, they overlap but are not strictly equivalent across the two ontologies.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Tax is a financial charge under Money. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Form is a type of document. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Dining Place and Hotel are both subclasses of Place but represent different concepts: a dining place is for eating while a hotel is for accommodation. They overlap in the real world (hotels often have restaurants) but are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.
Workshop is a conference event/session type, while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Conference announcement in Ontology A is a type of document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Conference in ekaw is a scientific event (one edition of a conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Review expertise to an unspecified value (likely a level of expertise), while Property B is an object property linking a Paper to a Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

The properties have opposite directions: 'writes' goes from Author to Contribution, while 'presentationed by' goes from Document to Speaker (i.e., the inverse direction). Even if Author/Speaker and Contribution/Document are related concepts, the directional mismatch means they are not equivalent; they would be inverses at best.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Programme in edas represents a conference event programme/schedule. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

A Poster is a type of conference contribution (a research presentation format), while an Invitation letter is an administrative document used for visa or attendance purposes. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The properties have completely different domains (Conference vs Document), ranges (Administrator vs Speaker), and semantics (enabling virtual meetings vs presenting a document). They are unrelated.

Topic in edas represents a subject area or research theme (e.g., Antennas, Cryptography), while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts (e.g., deadlines, conference days). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper in cmt is a submitted document (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Call For Papers in edas is an announcement/invitation to submit papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent lodging/accommodation for conference participants. 'Accommodation Place' in edas is a place where attendees stay, and 'Presenter house' in iasted (sibling of Conference hotel) serves the same purpose for presenters. In the OAEI Conference track reference alignment these are considered equivalent.

Both classes represent the chair of a program committee in the conference domain. Conference:Chair is a subclass of Committee member under Person, while confOf:Chair PC is directly under Person with siblings like Member PC and Administrator. Despite different modeling depths, their intended instances (the person chairing the PC) coincide.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Program committee (an organizational body), while Property B links a Programme (schedule) to a Conference Event. They relate entirely different kinds of entities in different directions and serve different purposes.

Both classes represent social events within a conference context. They share the same parent (Event), have analogous children (Banquet/Conference Banquet, Trip/Conference Trip), and are contrasted with working/scientific event siblings. Their intended instances coincide.

In cmt, Document is a general class with children Paper and Review. In iasted, Payment document is a specific subclass of Document (with children Bank transfer and Cheque). The cmt Document subsumes the iasted Payment document, but they are not equivalent since cmt's Document is much broader and does not specifically model payment documents.

In confOf, Workshop is a sibling of Conference (both under Working event). In ekaw, Conference and Workshop are also siblings (both under Scientific Event). Thus Workshop in A and Conference in B denote different concepts; they are related as co-hyponyms (sibling types of events) but not equivalent.

Coffee Break and Conference Banquet are both non-academic/social events at a conference, but they denote distinct types of events (a short break with coffee vs. a formal banquet meal). They share a common ancestor concept (social/non-academic event) but are not equivalent.

'relatesTo' is a general property linking Documents to events or persons, while 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' specifically links something to an Academic Institution that scientifically organises it. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both represent organized excursions/tours associated with a conference. However, 'Conference Trip' is a Social Event (no specific duration implied), while 'Full day tour' is an Activity after conference explicitly lasting a full day. They overlap in intent but are not strictly equivalent due to the duration specificity and placement (during vs. after conference).

setMaxPapers is an object property from Administrator to Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while has_a_program_committee links a Conference volume to a Program committee. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Radio Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

edas:ConferenceSession is a general class for conference sessions, while ekaw:Industrial_Session is explicitly a subclass of Conference Session in the ekaw ontology hierarchy (Event > Scientific Event > Session > Conference Session > Industrial Session). Therefore, edas:ConferenceSession subsumes ekaw:Industrial_Session.

Social event is a type of conference event (banquet, reception, trip), while Document is a type of item/paperwork (form, review, submission). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (someone applying to the conference), while Registration SIGKDD Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a type of fee). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and represent fundamentally different concepts.

Conference document refers to documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, calls, etc.), while Sponsorship refers to financial support or grants provided by organizations. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Banquet is a social event (an activity). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Reviewing event in confOf is an administrative event representing the actual reviewing procedure for submitted contributions. Call For Manuscripts in edas is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting manuscript submissions). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a process/event, the other is a call/announcement.

Conference Venue Place (edas) is a general class for places where the conference venue is located, with siblings like Accommodation Place and Dining Place. Conference hotel (iasted) is a specific type of building used for accommodation at a conference. A conference hotel can serve as or be part of a conference venue place, but the edas class is strictly more general, so it subsumes the iasted class.

SC Member is a person role (Steering Committee member) in the conference organization hierarchy, while Registration Non Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Welcome Talk is a type of conference event (a talk), while Invited Speaker is a type of person (a speaker). They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and are not equivalent or related by subsumption.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Programme Brochure is a document listing events in the programme. They are entirely different concepts (event vs. document).

hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Both properties capture an end date/time as a dateTime value, but A (hasEndDateTime) applies to any Conference Event while B (End_of_conference) applies specifically to a Conference. They overlap in meaning for the conference case but differ in domain scope, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Review Form (edas) is the template or blank form used to structure a review, whereas a Review (sigkdd) is the actual completed evaluation document of a paper. They are closely related in the reviewing process but not equivalent; the form is a template and the review is the filled-in artefact.
Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review (a document), while property B links a paper to a possible reviewer (a person). They have different ranges and different semantic meanings.

Property A links a Committee to its Co-chair (a membership/role relation), while Property B links an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('date') is a datatype property linking Conference to a date value, while property B ('has title') links events to a string title. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'is Location Of' relates a place to a conference event it hosts. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In confOf, 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event (a process/activity for reviewing contributions). In iasted, 'Review' is a Document (an artefact, sibling of Submission and Form). One is an event/process, the other is a document; they are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

In confOf, Workshop is a sibling of Conference and Tutorial under Working event, representing a workshop as a standalone event type. In ekaw, Workshop is also a sibling of Session, while Session is a broader concept that has Workshop Session as a child. Thus, confOf:Workshop and ekaw:Session are distinct concepts; if anything, confOf:Workshop would align with ekaw:Workshop or ekaw:Workshop Session, not with the more general ekaw:Session.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Conference in Ontology B represents the conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates. These are entirely different concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Communications Topic in edas is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Session in ekaw is a scientific event (a time-bounded meeting), while Hotel room in iasted is a physical place for accommodation. They are entirely different concepts.

A Bid represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review a paper, while Research Topic represents a subject area that papers and events cover. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewed contribution (A) is a specific stage of a conference contribution that has undergone review, with children Accepted/Rejected. Contribution (B) in confOf is the general class for submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper). A Reviewed contribution is a kind of Contribution, so A is subsumed by B.

Published Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been published), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote completely different concepts.

Property A 'is given to' links Item -> Person (award given to a person), while property B 'obtain' links Author -> Award (person obtains an award). They describe the same real-world relationship but in opposite directions (A is roughly the inverse of B). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

Both classes represent the concept of an author who has written/submitted a paper for a conference. In cmt, Author is the class of people who write and submit papers (children include Co-author). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author under Speaker, specifically denoting someone who authored a paper. Despite slight hierarchical differences, their intended instances coincide: persons who are authors of conference papers.
Paper Abstract is a summary of a paper's content, while Registration form is an administrative document for conference registration. They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.
