In ontology B (Conference), 'Paper' is the full regular contribution, which *has an abstract* as a separate related entity. Thus, cmt's Paper Abstract is a more specific concept subsumed by Conference's Paper.

confOf:Participant is a general class for all conference participants (with children Member, Regular, Student), while ekaw:PC_Member is a specific role (a member of the programme committee). Participant subsumes PC Member since a PC member is a type of participant, but they are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the concept of a conference in the conference-organisation domain. Ontology A's Conference is a top-level class with children like 'Conference volume', while Ontology B's Conference is explicitly defined as 'One edition of a conference' under Scientific Event. Despite different positions in their respective hierarchies, they denote the same real-world concept and would be aligned as equivalent in a reference alignment.
hasDecision links a Paper to its acceptance/rejection Decision, while hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
A is a datatype property linking Contribution to a string (abstract text), while B is an object property linking Person to Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In iasted, Submission is a subclass of Document representing specifically submitted manuscripts (with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript). In sigkdd, Document is a broader class encompassing Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus, iasted:Submission is more specific than sigkdd:Document, making it subsumed_by the latter.

A 'Program committee' is a group of people (a committee) responsible for reviewing papers, while an 'Administrative event' in confOf is a type of event or activity (e.g., submission, reviewing process). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (group vs. event) and are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Program Committee Member' is a specific type of committee member (for the program committee). In Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a general class for members of any committee, with children Chair and Co-chair. Thus, cmt's Program Committee Member is subsumed by Conference's more general Committee member.

Co chair in Conference is a committee leadership role (subclass of Committee member), while Scholar in confOf is a price/registration category for attendees who study at a university. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Acceptance in cmt is a positive decision (child of Decision, sibling of Rejection), while Refusing manuscript in iasted is a negative activity (sibling of Accepting manuscript). They are conceptually opposite outcomes; the true equivalent of Acceptance would be 'Accepting manuscript' in iasted. They are related as they both pertain to the paper decision process but are not equivalent.
confOf's Topic is the general class for all conference topics, while edas's MicroelectronicsTopic is a specific subclass of Topic. Therefore, confOf:Topic subsumes edas:MicroelectronicsTopic.

'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'is occupied by' links physical locations (Building, City, State) to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'locationOf' relates a Location to an Event, while 'searched_by' relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publication relationship), while property B 'has Topic' relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject matter relationship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. These are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a website/URL resource), while University is an academic institution/organisation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Submissions deadline' refers to the deadline for submitting papers, while B 'Deadline Author notification' refers to the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection. These are distinct events in the conference timeline. A's sibling 'Deadline for notification of acceptance' would be equivalent to B, but A itself is not.
Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Audiovisual equipment is a type of physical item/equipment. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.) with properties like title, abstract, and authors. ReviewRating in edas represents the rating given to a paper during review (accept, reject, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (which is under Person), representing a general conference member/attendee. In ekaw, Conference Participant is directly under Person and serves as the broad superclass for all participant roles (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.). Thus confOf's Member is subsumed by ekaw's Conference Participant.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (a person role), while property B links a programme brochure or web site to an event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Person in Ontology A is a general class for all people involved in the conference (including reviewers, committee members, participants, etc.). Author in Ontology B is explicitly a subclass of Person, representing only those who write papers. Therefore, Person subsumes Author.

Company in confOf is a type of Organization (business entity), while Computer Networks Enterprise Topic in edas is a specific research topic related to enterprise computer networks. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference in cmt represents a conference event/organization, while Time in iasted is a temporal concept (with children like Deadline, Conference days). These are entirely different concepts.
Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper (child of Decision), while Company is a type of organization. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, Workshop is a structural part of a conference (sibling of Track and Tutorial). In Ontology B (ekaw), Workshop is a sibling of Session under Scientific Event, while Session is a broader concept whose children include Workshop Session. Thus, Workshop in A does not correspond to Session in B; they are distinct concepts.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference Member' is a broad class with children including Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, etc. In ontology B (Conference), 'Reviewer' is a specific role under Person. Therefore, Conference Member subsumes Reviewer, as every reviewer in cmt is a conference member but not vice versa.

Property A gives the first name of a Person, while property B gives the full name of a Conference. They have different domains (Person vs Conference) and different semantics (first name vs full name), so they are unrelated.
hasReview links a Paper to its Review, while write links a Person to an Item they authored. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Review is a general class for all reviews. In ekaw, Neutral_Review is a specific subclass of Review (alongside Positive_Review and Negative_Review). Therefore, the edas Review subsumes the ekaw Neutral_Review.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'CAD Topic' is a specific subject area (Computer-Aided Design) under the Topic class. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Break Event in edas is a specific type of non-academic event (with children like Coffee Break, Meal Break), while Event in ekaw is the top-level class for all events (including Scientific Event and Social Event). Therefore, Break Event is strictly subsumed by the more general Event class.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing the first author of a conference contribution (a person role), while Conference in confOf is a type of working event. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while 'hasReview' links a Paper to a Review. They are unrelated.

confOf:Contribution is a general class for any submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper), while edas:RatedPapers is a very specific subclass of Paper that has already been rated/reviewed. Contribution strictly subsumes RatedPapers since all rated papers are contributions, but not all contributions are rated papers.

One conference day is a temporal concept (a single day of the conference), while Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational group responsible for selecting best papers. They are entirely unrelated.

Property A relates a Person to a Conference document (contribution), while property B relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (occupation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, 'Government Organization' is a type of Organization (e.g., a government agency). In iasted, 'Sponsor state' is a subclass of State, representing the geopolitical state/country of a sponsor. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an organizational entity type, the other is a country/state associated with a sponsorship role.
Conference Chair is a person role (the chair of a conference), while Technic activity is a type of conference event/activity. They are entirely different concepts.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person (a type of attendee/role). In sigkdd, Registration Student is a subclass of Registration fee (a type of fee/payment category). They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and are not equivalent.

Organisation in ekaw refers to an institutional entity (e.g., academic institution, publisher) that organises events, while Activity in iasted refers to scheduled events or tasks (e.g., conference activity). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both classes represent a Person in the conference domain. They share similar children (e.g., Chairman/Conference Chair, Reviewer, Program Committee Member/TPC Member) and properties (email, name). Their intended instances coincide as people involved in conferences.

Both are datatype properties mapping to string for naming purposes. However, A's domain includes both Conference and Person, while B's domain is only Person. Therefore B (Name) is strictly more specific than A (name), meaning A subsumes B, or equivalently B is subsumed_by A.
Contribution co author is a role class for a co-author of a conference contribution, while Two Level Conference is a type of conference event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A relates an Activity to a Time (indicating temporal ordering of events), while Property B relates an Author to a Deadline for author notification. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations: 'employed By' links a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is paid by' links Money to a Person (payment). They are unrelated.

Conference Session in ekaw is a type of event/session during the conference (e.g., demo session, poster session), while Research in iasted is an activity performed before the conference (with children like Modelling and Simulating). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is a research topic (Computer Networks Management) while B is an event type (Conference Session). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

'has a name' is a general name property for organizations and topics (Conference, Publisher, etc.), while 'has First Name' is specifically the first name of a Person. They differ in domain specificity and intended use.

Conference in Ontology A represents the main academic conference event (with proceedings, topics, etc.), while Conference Banquet in ekaw is a specific social event (a banquet) that may occur during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Program Committee member who reviews papers. confOf's 'Member PC' has comment 'Reviewer' and property 'reviewes', while ekaw's 'PC Member' is a subclass of 'Possible Reviewer'. Despite slight differences in hierarchy (ekaw places various chairs under PC Member), the intended instances are the same concept.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an ending date value, while Property B is an object property linking an event to a location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their biography), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have different ranges (string vs Item) and entirely different semantics.

Nonmember registration fee refers to the fee for non-members, while Registration Student refers to the fee for students. They are sibling concepts under Registration fee in their respective ontologies, not equivalent.

In confOf, 'Member' is a subclass of Participant (with siblings Regular and Student), representing a full/regular conference member as opposed to a student. In ekaw, 'PC Member' represents a program committee member. In the OAEI Conference track reference alignment, confOf:Member is mapped to ekaw:PC_Member because both denote the standard professional member role in the conference organization context, despite differing parent hierarchies.

An 'Extended abstract' is a specific type of short conference contribution (a regular contribution), whereas an 'Initial manuscript' in iasted refers to the first/initial version of a submitted document (contrasted with 'Final manuscript'). They describe different aspects: one is a document format/type, the other is a submission stage/version. They are not equivalent.

Single Level Conference is a type of conference (event/organization), while Main office is a type of place (physical location). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Paper in Ontology A is a general class for regular conference papers (a subclass of Regular contribution), while Industrial Paper in ekaw is a specific subtype of Paper denoting papers from industry. They are not equivalent; they overlap as both represent kinds of conference papers, but Industrial Paper is more specific and belongs to a different categorization axis.

Tutorial and Workshop are distinct types of working/scientific events in the conference domain. They are siblings under a common parent category (Working event / Scientific Event) but denote different concepts: a tutorial is typically an instructional session, while a workshop is a collaborative research meeting. They are related as co-hyponyms but not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
writeReview links a Reviewer to a Review (authorship), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (association). Different domains and different semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person who chairs the conference (subclass of Chairman), while Technical commitee in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (attendee) and represents a committee or its member. These are conceptually distinct entities with different roles in the conference domain.
The property 'title' gives the title of a Paper (string), while 'has Cost Amount' gives the monetary amount of a Sponsorship (int). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Powerline Transmission Topic is a specific subject area (a subclass of Topic), while Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Call For Reviews is a type of Call (an announcement requesting reviews), while Abstract is a type of Document (a summary of a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf's Working_event is a broad category encompassing Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop (the main academic/working parts of a conference). edas's TalkEvent is a narrower concept under Academic Event with children Closing Talk and Welcome Talk, while Workshop is a sibling of TalkEvent in edas. Thus TalkEvent does not cover the same instances as Working_event; they overlap (both relate to academic activities) but are not equivalent, nor is one strictly subsuming the other given the differing hierarchies.

Both classes represent members of a conference and are subclasses of Person (or Participant which is a subclass of Person). In cmt, Conference Member includes authors, reviewers, chairs, etc. In confOf, Member (with comment 'confTool') under Participant represents registered conference members, with subtypes Regular and Student. Despite different granularities in their children, both denote the same concept: a person who is a member/participant of the conference.
'has tracks' relates a conference volume to its tracks, while 'has Country' relates a conference to its country. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Paid applicant is a class of persons (applicants who have paid), while Registration fee is a class of monetary fees. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain—one is a person role, the other is a financial amount.

Entity A is 'Rejected Paper' while Entity B is 'Accepted Paper'. These are sibling concepts representing opposite outcomes of the paper review process; they are related as disjoint subclasses of evaluated papers but not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference Proceedings is a document/publication. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the same concept: a conference event in the academic domain. They share similar properties such as dates (date vs end Date), members (has Conference Member vs has Member), and paper-related deadlines/assignments. Despite minor differences in modeling details, their intended instances coincide.

In ekaw, Tutorial Chair is a subclass of PC Member (Program Committee member), while in sigkdd, Program Committee member is a distinct class under Organizator. A Tutorial Chair is a specific role that may overlap with or be a kind of PC member, but the two classes are not equivalent; they are related through the broader program committee concept.

Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging (subclass of Place), while Registration form is a document used for registering (subclass of Form). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Camera Ready event is an administrative event (a type of activity/deadline), while Program Committee is a committee (a group of people). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Talk Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event representing scheduled talks. These are entirely different concepts (person vs event) and are unrelated.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for a person (likely a student) with a 'study At' property pointing to University. In edas, Reviewer is a role that reviews papers. These are conceptually distinct: one denotes an academic status/registration type, the other a reviewing function.

Property A (assignedTo) links a Paper directly to a Reviewer, representing the assignment of a paper to a reviewer. Property B (has_been_assigned_a_review_reference) links a Submitted contribution or Topic to a Review preference, which is a different kind of relationship involving preferences rather than direct reviewer assignments. The domains and ranges differ significantly, so they are unrelated.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (reviewer assignment context), while Property B links a Speaker to a Document (presentation context). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference in cmt denotes the event/organization itself, while Conference Paper in ekaw denotes a paper submitted to or presented at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a broad class encompassing all people involved in the conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.), while Author in sigkdd is specifically someone who submits a paper. Conference Participant subsumes Author since authors are a type of conference participant, but they are not equivalent.
Conference Banquet is a social event (a type of activity/gathering), while Fee for extra trip is a monetary fee. They belong to entirely different categories and are not semantically related.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Nonauthor registration fee is a type of monetary fee for non-authors. They are completely unrelated concepts.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Conference Member (which maps to Committee member in the Conference ontology). In the Conference ontology, Committee member is a general class for people serving on committees, with children Chair and Co-chair. An Author (someone who writes/submits papers) is not equivalent to a Committee member; rather, cmt's Conference Member (and thus its subclass Author) would be subsumed by or related to the broader Person/Committee member concept, but Author specifically is strictly narrower than and different from Committee member. Since cmt's Author inherits from Conference Member, and Conference's Committee member is the analogous general role, Author is subsumed_by Committee member.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Call is an announcement soliciting submissions or reviews. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Conference part' is a component of a conference (with children Track, Tutorial, Workshop) and is part of Conference volumes. In Ontology B, 'Conference' is itself a type of Working event (sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). While both involve tutorials and workshops, in A they are parts of a conference, whereas in B Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop are sibling types of events. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.
In Ontology A, 'Program committee' is a Committee (a group of people), whereas in Ontology B, 'Programme' is a Document (a schedule or program booklet). These are entirely different concepts.

In ekaw, Presenter is a superclass of Invited Speaker (Invited Speaker is listed as a child of Presenter). In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a specific subclass of Speaker. Therefore, the ekaw Presenter class subsumes the sigkdd Invited Speaker class, as Presenter is more general and includes Invited Speakers among its instances.
Registration in iasted is a conference activity (event), while Organizator in sigkdd is a person who organizes the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers, while Conference_part in the Conference ontology refers to structural components of a conference such as tracks, tutorials, and workshops. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Organising Agency is a type of organisation (an entity that organises the conference). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Associated Chair in cmt is a type of Chairman (a leadership role), while Listener in iasted is a type of Delegate who attends but does not present. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (a part-whole relationship), while Property B relates a Person to a Place and Time (an attendance/presence relationship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Mailing list is a distribution list for communications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person that groups system roles (Administrator, Author, Reviewer) — essentially anyone who interacts with the conference management system. In edas, Attendee is a subclass of Person representing someone who attends the conference event. These are different concepts: a User need not attend (e.g., an external reviewer or admin), and an Attendee need not be a system User. They overlap (authors/reviewers often attend) but are not equivalent.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (people participating in the conference), while Property B links a Conference volume to its Conference parts (structural components of proceedings). These relate fundamentally different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.
Author (a person who writes/submits papers) and Organizer (a person who organizes the conference) are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Both classes represent the registration activity/event at a conference. In confOf it is modeled as an Administrative event (Registration of participants event), and in iasted as a Conference activity (Registration). Despite different parent hierarchies, their intended instances coincide: the act or event of registering participants/delegates for the conference.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution.

'is held in' relates an Activity (event) to a Place and Time, indicating where/when the event occurs. 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place, indicating accommodation. Different domains, different ranges, and different semantics.

Both classes represent a banquet event within the social program of a conference. 'Banquet' in confOf and 'Dinner banquet' in iasted share the same parent concept (Social event / Social program) and denote the same type of conference activity.
Regular in confOf is a type of Participant (a regular attendee), while Two Level Conference in edas is a type of Conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while is_designed_for is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Company is an organization type (business entity), while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

Published Paper is a paper that has been accepted and published (a subclass of Paper in edas), while Abstract in sigkdd is a sibling of Paper under Document, representing a summary or short description. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Departure tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both are types of abstracts in the conference domain, but they differ significantly: A's Abstract is a sub-class of Extended abstract (a regular contribution) and serves as the abstract part of papers/posters/presentations, while B's Invited Talk Abstract is specifically the abstract of an invited talk. They overlap conceptually as abstracts but are not equivalent nor in a direct subsumption relationship.

In Ontology A, 'Extended abstract' is a sibling of 'Paper' under 'Regular contribution', meaning it is explicitly distinguished from a full paper (an extended abstract is a shorter submission). In Ontology B, 'Conference Paper' represents a full paper submitted to a conference. These are different types of contributions in the conference domain, though they are related as both being regular conference submissions.

Property A links a Program Committee Member to the Program Committee they belong to (domain: member, range: committee). Property B links a Conference volume to its Program Committee (domain: conference, range: committee). They have different domains and express different relationships.

A Steering committee is a type of Committee responsible for guiding a conference, while a Sponsor is a Person who provides support/funding. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event (activity), while Author book proceedings included is a role/status of an author whose paper appears in the proceedings. They are completely different concepts.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person (people attending the conference), while Conference activity is a subclass of Activity (events like lectures, coffee breaks). They are entirely different concepts.

submitPaper (Author -> Paper) and isWrittenBy (Paper -> Author) have inverse directions. While both relate Authors to Papers, submission and authorship are distinct concepts, and the properties point in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.

Both properties express the act of creating/preparing a scholarly work: 'write Paper' links an Author to a Paper, while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item (which in iasted typically represents a paper/submission). The semantics overlap significantly, but the domain and range classes are not identical across ontologies, so they are related rather than strictly equivalent.
Social event is a type of conference event (banquet, reception, trip), while Evaluated Paper is a paper that has undergone review. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Committee to its Co-chair (organizational role), while Property B links an Author to a Contribution (writing activity). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Multimedia Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Paid applicant is a person who has paid to attend the conference, while Fee is a monetary charge (e.g., registration fee). They are fundamentally different concepts (person vs. financial amount) and thus unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document representing a submitted paper. In Conference, Conference document is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, announcements, reviews, and contributions. Paper (cmt) corresponds more closely to 'Conference contribution' (a child of Conference document), so Paper is subsumed by the more general Conference document.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to an integer cost, while heldIn is an object property linking Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the complete/final version of a paper submitted to a conference. In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is contrasted with 'Paper Abstract', while in iasted, 'Final manuscript' is contrasted with 'Initial manuscipt'. Despite slightly different parent hierarchies (Paper vs Submission), their intended instances coincide as the final full document of a submission.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for students (with property 'study At' pointing to University), not an author role. In edas, Author is the person who writes papers. These are conceptually distinct roles in the conference domain.
hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They have different ranges, types, and semantics.

Extended abstract is a type of short contribution (a document format), while Withdrawn Paper is a status-based subclass of Paper indicating it was withdrawn from the process. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Fee for extra trip and Sponzor fee are both subclasses of Fee but refer to entirely different kinds of charges (travel-related vs sponsorship-related). They share no semantic overlap beyond being fees.

In ontology A (cmt), Author is a person who writes and submits papers. In ontology B (Conference), Conference contribution is a document/artefact (e.g., poster, presentation, written contribution) submitted to the conference. One denotes a person role, the other denotes a submitted artefact; they are unrelated.
hasDecision links a Paper to its Decision (accept/reject), while hasCall links an Academic Event to its Call for Papers. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
hasAuthor links a Paper to an Author, while hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.

'Short paper' in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster). 'Assigned Paper' in ekaw is a submitted paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a workflow state). These are orthogonal classifications with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Accommodation Place is a general class for places providing lodging, while Double hotel room is a very specific type of hotel room. Accommodation Place subsumes Double hotel room since a double hotel room is a kind of accommodation place.

In confOf, 'Social event' is a type of Event (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip) representing social gatherings at a conference. In edas, 'Programme' is a subclass of Document (a schedule or programme document) that belongs to a Conference Event. They are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event/activity, the other is a document.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Meeting Room Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In iasted, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee who presents), with children Author and Reviewer. In sigkdd, Organizator is a subclass of Person responsible for organizing the conference (General Chair, Program Chair, etc.), and Speaker is actually a sibling of Organizator, not a child. These are distinct roles: one presents, the other organizes.
hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members, while initiates links chairs/TPC members to a Call. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Talk Event is a type of academic conference event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk), while Gold Supporter is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education), while 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (paper submission). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference contributor (A) is a person who contributes content (authors, speakers, active participants), while Participant (B) in confOf refers to conference attendees/registrants (Regular, Student). In B's ontology, Author is a sibling of Participant, not a child, confirming they are distinct roles. They overlap conceptually as both are subclasses of Person involved in the conference, but their intended instances differ significantly.

Conference Chair and Session Chair are distinct roles in conference organization. In edas they are siblings under Person; in iasted only Session chair exists. They are related as both are chairing roles but not equivalent.

Entity A is a Review (an evaluation of a paper), while Entity B is a Paper (a submitted contribution). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain. Note that Ontology B even has its own sibling class 'Review', confirming Paper and Review are different.

'Two Level Conference' in edas is a subclass of Conference (and oddly Person/TPC Member) representing a type of conference organization structure. 'Conference state' in iasted is a subclass of State representing the status or phase of a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (an administrative action to enable virtual meetings), while heldIn relates an Event to a Location (specifying where an event takes place). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasTitle in confOf is a datatype property on Contribution (paper) giving its title, while hasName in edas is a datatype property on Conference giving the conference's full name. Different domains and different semantics.

Performance Topic in edas is a subject area (a subclass of Topic) for paper submissions, while Simulating in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (topic vs. activity) and are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties representing temporal information about conference-related entities (Conference vs Conference Event) with date/dateTime ranges. However, 'date' is a generic date property for a Conference, while 'hasStartDateTime' specifically denotes the start time of a Conference Event. They overlap in purpose but differ in domain specificity and semantics, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker). Presenter state is a subclass of State representing the status/state of a presenter. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (a person role vs. a state) and are unrelated.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a specific governance body), while Property B links an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. The domains, ranges, and semantics differ significantly; they are not equivalent.

Camera Ready event in confOf is an administrative event (a process/activity), while Deadline hotel reservation in iasted is a temporal deadline for booking accommodation. They belong to different conceptual categories and refer to entirely different aspects of conference organization.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

endDate is a datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime value representing the end date, while eventOnList is an object property linking Event to Programme Brochure or Web Site. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (document structure), while Property B relates an Event to another Event (event hierarchy). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Workshop in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is modeled as a Conference part (alongside Track and Tutorial), while in edas it is modeled as an Academic Event. Despite different modeling hierarchies, they denote the same real-world concept: a workshop held as part of a conference.
hasHomePage links a Person to their homepage URL string, while hasFirstName links a Person to their first name string. These are entirely different attributes of a person and thus unrelated.

In ekaw, Invited Speaker is a specific subclass of Presenter (a person invited to speak). In iasted, Speaker is a general class for anyone who speaks at the conference, with children like Author and Reviewer. Thus, every Invited Speaker is a Speaker, but not every Speaker is an Invited Speaker, making ekaw:Invited_Speaker subsumed by iasted:Speaker.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or general information to attendees, while 'Computer Networks Security Topic' is a specific research topic within the computer networks domain. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

hasAttendee relates a conference event to its attendees (participants), while organisedBy relates an event to its organizers. Attending and organizing are distinct roles; these properties relate different kinds of things in different directions.

eventOnList relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (indicating the event is listed there), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item (indicating the person gives/presents something). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsor), while writtenBy links a Document to a Person (author). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (abstract) is a datatype property on Contribution with range string, representing the abstract text of a paper. Property B (manuscriptDueOn) is a datatype property on Conference with range dateTime, representing a deadline. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:writes relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while iasted:send relates a Person to an Item. In the conference domain, 'send' likely refers to submitting a paper, making these properties semantically related but not strictly equivalent due to differing labels, domains (Author vs Person), and ranges (Contribution vs Item).
Conference in cmt denotes the event/organization itself, while Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Conference' is the top-level event entity (the conference itself). In Ontology B (iasted), 'Conference activity' is a subclass of 'Activity' representing individual events within or around a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture, registration). The iasted ontology likely has a separate class for the conference as a whole. Thus, 'Conference activity' denotes sub-events of a conference rather than the conference itself, making them related but not equivalent.
Property A links a Steering committee to a Conference volume, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself (with properties like dates, members, paper assignments). In iasted, 'Conference hall' is a physical place/venue (subclass of Place, sibling to Building, Hotel room). These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a location.

isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while is_visited_by relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (visitation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

defaultChoice is a datatype property mapping events to a positiveInteger (a confTool setting), while is_given_by is an object property linking an Activity/Item to a Person. They differ in type, domain semantics, and range entirely.

acceptedBy links a Paper to an Administrator (who accepted it), while relatedToEvent links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event. These relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a general class under Document. In ekaw, Demo Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a type of paper for demonstrations). Therefore, the general Paper in cmt subsumes the more specific Demo Paper in ekaw.
isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while obtain relates an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A is a document/artifact class (a camera-ready version of an accepted paper), while Entity B is an event class (the administrative act of submitting contributions). They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent or related in a subsumption sense.

Meta Review is a type of review document evaluating a paper, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

In cmt, Acceptance is a type of Decision (accepting a paper), whereas in edas, Reception is a Social Event (a gathering/party at the conference). These are entirely different concepts that happen to share a loose English association but denote unrelated things in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt represents a summary/short version of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version), while Withdrawn Paper in edas represents a paper that has been withdrawn from the submission process (sibling of Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). These are entirely different concepts.
Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Transport vehicle is a class for vehicles (cars, buses, etc.) under Item, while Organizator is a class for organizing personnel under Person. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference Participant is a subclass of Person representing people attending the conference, while Building is a subclass of Place representing physical structures. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Modelling is a research activity before the conference. They are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

A 'Review Form' is the template or form used to collect review information, whereas a 'Review' (in iasted, a subclass of Document) is the actual completed review document. They are closely related but not equivalent; the form is the structure and the review is the filled-in content.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to scholarly works submitted to a conference (papers, posters, presentations, talks), whereas Form in Ontology B refers to administrative documents (registration forms, author information forms). These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

Conference (A) represents the conference event/organization itself, while Conference city (B) represents a city where a conference takes place. These are fundamentally different concepts (an event vs. a location).

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), representing academic activities. Conference days in iasted is a subclass of Time, representing temporal periods. They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. time) and are unrelated.

Conference in confOf is the overall conference event (a Working event with siblings Tutorial and Workshop), while Closing Talk in edas is a specific talk given at the end of a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In the conference domain, 'Conference Chair' (edas) and 'OC Chair' (Organizing Committee Chair, ekaw) refer to the same role: the person who chairs the organizing committee of a conference. Despite different parent hierarchies, their intended instances coincide.

The property 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (where the event takes place), while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). Different domains and different semantic meanings.

Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Hotel is a place (a venue/accommodation). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Best Student Paper Award is an award given to a student's paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'is submitted at' links a conference contribution to a conference volume (submission relation), while 'awarded by' links an award to its granting entity. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties express an organizational relationship between a conference event and the entity responsible for it. However, 'scientificallyOrganisedBy' in ekaw specifically denotes scientific organization and has range Academic Institution, while 'holded_by' in sigkdd denotes the general organizer/holder with domain Conference and range ACM SIGKDD. They overlap in meaning (organizing a conference) but differ in specificity and intended ranges, so they are related rather than equivalent.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and meanings: 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is held after' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering).

'organised By' relates an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'is designed for' relates an Activity/Money/Time to a target Activity or Person. These properties have different semantics, domains, and ranges, and are unrelated.

In edas, Attendee is a general class for anyone attending the conference (with siblings like Author, Reviewer, etc., suggesting it covers non-role-specific attendees or all participants). In sigkdd, Listener is specifically someone who listens to talks, contrasted with Speaker. A Listener is a type of attendee, but Attendee is broader since it can include speakers and other roles. They are related but not equivalent; Attendee subsumes Listener.
'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'has Menu' links a meal event to its menu. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to the conference), while Social event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering like a banquet). They are entirely different concepts.

Accepted contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted, while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting the final version of a paper. They are entirely different concepts (an artefact vs. a point in time).

Both classes are named Review, share the same parent class Document, and appear among similar sibling classes (Paper, Programme). In the conference domain, both represent a review document of a paper, making them equivalent.

Conference Chair is a leadership role responsible for chairing the conference, while Student lecturer is a student who gives a lecture/presentation. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Reviewed contribution is a conference paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Personal History in edas refers to a person's historical record (e.g., publication or review history). These are entirely different concepts.
One is a datatype property for a person's last name, the other is an object property relating Money to Item. They are completely unrelated.

A Workshop (edas) and a Poster Session (ekaw) are both types of academic/scientific events at a conference, but they denote different kinds of sessions. In ekaw, Workshop Session is a sibling of Poster Session, confirming they are distinct concepts. They are related as co-hyponyms under the broader concept of conference events.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Registration of participants event is an administrative event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and model unrelated concepts: one links a Topic to a Review preference, while the other links a Scholar to a University.
Trip is a social event (a type of activity/excursion), while IASTED non member is a type of delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.
Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event (an activity), while Organizing Committee member is a type of person/role. They are fundamentally different concepts in the domain.
Conference Banquet is a social event (a type of activity), while Conference airport is a building/place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Both properties link a Person to a document-like entity (Document in ekaw, Item in iasted). 'authorOf' denotes authorship while 'sign' denotes signing; in the conference domain these are closely related activities on papers/items but not strictly equivalent relations.

confOf:Person is a general class for all people involved in the conference (authors, participants, administrators, etc.), while sigkdd:Speaker is a subclass of sigkdd:Person representing only those who give presentations. Thus confOf:Person subsumes sigkdd:Speaker.

Associated Chair in cmt is a subclass of Chairman (a general conference leadership role), while Session Chair in edas is a person who chairs a specific session. They are both chair roles but at different levels of the conference organization; they overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.
hasMember relates a Conference to its member Persons, while is_needed_for relates an Item to a Person who needs it. The domains (Conference vs Item) and semantics are entirely different.

Conference applicant in Ontology A refers to a person applying/registering for the conference (with child Registeered applicant), while PC Chair in ekaw is a specific committee role (Program Committee Chair). These are entirely different concepts.

Review Rating in edas is a rating assigned to an Active Paper (with children like Accept/Reject Rating), representing the evaluation outcome. Positive Review in ekaw is a subclass of Review (a document) that expresses a positive sentiment. One is a rating value/outcome, the other is a type of review document. They are related in that they both pertain to the positive evaluation of papers, but they are not equivalent concepts.

'run Paper Assignment Tools' is a specific administrative action linking an Administrator to a Conference, while 'give' is a generic property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Co-chair (A) is a committee co-chair, while Chair PC (B) is the Program Committee chair. These are distinct leadership roles within a conference: a co-chair typically shares or assists with chairing duties, whereas the PC Chair is the primary head of the program committee. They are related as both are senior committee roles but not equivalent.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'enableVirtualMeeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference for enabling virtual meetings, while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution for authorship. They are unrelated.
A Poster Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while an Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'written By' relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Topic to a Conference part (subject-matter relation), while Property B links an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal/scheduling parallelism). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Abstract is a summary of an academic paper, while Cheque is a payment document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'hasMenu' relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu. These are entirely different relations in different parts of the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event where review outcomes are made available to authors, while Submissions deadline is a time/deadline by which papers must be submitted. They refer to entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'acceptedBy' relates a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (indicating temporal parallelism). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they provide. These properties have entirely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference fees refers to the monetary charges for attending a conference, while Conference in sigkdd refers to the conference event itself (with properties like city, start/end dates). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value for acceptance announcement, while Property B is a datatype property linking Participant to a boolean indicating early registration. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
In ekaw, Conference is a Scientific Event (an edition of a conference), while in iasted, Conference airport is a Building/Place (a physical location). They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a conference volume to its program committee, while property B links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a conference it holds. These relate entirely different domain and range concepts and express different relationships.

Both properties express a relationship between a paper/contribution and a topic, but they are inverses of each other: 'dealsWith' goes from Contribution to Topic, while 'topicCoveredBy' goes from Research Topic to Paper/Event. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'isInitiatedBy' relates a Call to conference roles (Chair, TPC Member). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Program Committee is a group of people who review papers, while Sponsorship is a financial support arrangement. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Track workshop chair (A) is a person responsible for tracks/workshops/tutorials in a conference, while Demo Chair (B) is specifically the chair of demo sessions. They are both types of conference chairs/organizers but have distinct responsibilities; they overlap as related roles rather than being equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted manuscript (child of Document, sibling of Review). In ekaw, Review is an evaluation document (child of Document, sibling of Paper). They are distinct concepts in the conference domain; cmt:Paper aligns with ekaw:Paper, not ekaw:Review.

The 'name' property in cmt captures the name of a Conference or Person, while 'hasBiography' in edas captures biographical information about a Person. These are semantically distinct properties with different meanings and partially different domains.

confOf:Person is a general class for all people involved in the conference (with children like Author, Participant, etc.), while ekaw:Student is a specific subclass of ekaw:Person. Therefore, confOf:Person subsumes ekaw:Student.

Both ontologies define Abstract as a direct subclass of Document with the same siblings (Paper, Review). They represent the same concept: an abstract document associated with a conference paper or presentation.

Item in iasted is a very general class for physical objects (equipment, cards, documents, vehicles), while Award in sigkdd specifically denotes prizes/honors given to authors. These are conceptually distinct and unrelated.
Property A links a conference volume to its important dates, while property B links administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, 'Welcome Talk' is a specific type of talk event for welcoming attendees. In iasted, 'Introduction' is a broader conference activity that has 'Welcome address' as a sibling and 'Introduction of speaker' as a child, indicating it refers to general introductions rather than specifically a welcome talk. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Conference in edas represents the event itself (with dates, members, topics), while Proceedings in ekaw is a document/volume (subclass of Multi author Volume) that may be produced as a result of a conference. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Both classes represent an Author in the conference domain—someone who writes/authors a paper or contribution. Although iasted's Author is more deeply nested (Delegate > Speaker > Author) and has specific children, the core intended instances (people who author conference contributions) coincide with confOf's Author.

providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (the sponsor), while organisedBy links an Event to an Organisation or Person (the organizer). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Acceptance is a type of decision (accepting a paper), while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event at a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while Price is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to an integer value. They are entirely unrelated.

Conference Chair in edas is an organizational role responsible for initiating calls and overseeing the conference, while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives presentations (with children Author and Invited Speaker). These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and no hierarchical overlap.

Conference Member is a Person role (individual participating in a conference), while Academic Institution is an Organisation (e.g., university or research institute). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain model and share no semantic overlap.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, while 'is held before' links an Activity to a Time. They are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (indicating who started the bidding process), while 'isReviewing' links people (e.g., Reviewer) to a Paper (indicating what they are reviewing). They are unrelated.
writeReview links a Reviewer to a Review (the act of writing), while isReviewHistoryOf links a PersonalReviewHistory to a Reviewer. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('location') specifies where an event is held (domain: events, range: string), while property B ('hasName') specifies the full name of a conference (domain: Conference, range: string). They have different domains and completely different semantics.

Review in cmt is a document that evaluates a submitted paper (child of Document, written by a Reviewer). Personal Publication History in edas is a record of an individual's past publications (child of Personal History). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties on Conference relating to dates, but 'date' in cmt is a generic date property while 'startDate' in edas specifically denotes the conference start date and time. They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent; 'date' could refer to any date associated with the conference.

Property A 'name' is a string-valued datatype property for naming conferences or persons, while property B 'Start of conference' is a dateTime-valued datatype property indicating when a conference begins. They represent entirely different concepts.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while is_paid_with relates Money to an Item (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Power Point presentation in iasted is a specific type of presentation activity within a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'isWrittenBy' links a Paper to an Author.

External Reviewer in cmt is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another reviewer, while Scholar in confOf is a price category for conference attendees (a student/scholar registration type). These are conceptually distinct roles with different intended instances.
Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B (hasReviewer) relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Security Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

A Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop under Conference part), while a Plenary lecture is a specific type of lecture/presentation event. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

The 'name' property in cmt assigns a string name to a Conference or Person, while 'has Cost Amount' in edas assigns an integer cost to a Sponsorship. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing specifically the full version of a paper (as opposed to 'Paper Abstract'). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for papers. Therefore, cmt's Paper Full Version is subsumed by sigkdd's Paper.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while pay relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
A is a datatype property linking events to a short title string, while B is an object property linking items to activities. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

A Multi-author Volume (e.g., Proceedings) is a collection of published papers, while an Author information form is an administrative form for collecting author details. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

has_short_title is a datatype property mapping events to strings (short titles), while listsEvent is an object property linking programme brochures/websites to Event instances. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Both are chair roles in a conference context, but 'Associated Chair' (cmt) is a subclass of Chairman and Conference Member, typically referring to an Associate/Co-Chair of the overall conference or program committee. 'Session chair' (iasted) is a role assigned to a delegate who chairs a specific session. They overlap as chairing roles but denote different levels/scope within a conference, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Paper is a document/submission artifact, while Deadline is a temporal constraint for submissions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (Author < Speaker < Delegate), while in sigkdd, Speaker is the parent class and Author is its child (Author < Speaker). Thus iasted:Author is more specific than sigkdd:Speaker. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent; they are related.

Both classes represent the same conference-domain concept: a call for papers (CFP). Despite different parent classes (Conference document vs Call), their intended instances coincide as the announcement soliciting paper submissions.
Academia Organization is a type of organization (institution), while Organizing Committee member is a role played by a person. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a member), while Property B relates a PC Member to a Contribution (reviewing a paper). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In the iasted ontology, Transparency is a sibling of Submission and Review under Document, representing overhead transparencies/slides used for presentations. In sigkdd, Paper represents a submitted academic paper. These are distinct types of documents in the conference domain and do not denote the same concept.

Student in ekaw is a general class for students (a type of Person), while Author_of_paper in sigkdd is specifically an author who has written a paper. These are conceptually distinct roles; the fact that sigkdd has a sibling 'Author of paper student' further confirms that 'Author of paper' itself does not imply student status.

Call For Manuscripts (edas) is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Accepting manuscript (iasted) is an Activity before conference (the act of accepting a submitted manuscript). They are related as part of the same submission workflow but denote different concepts: one is a call/announcement, the other is an acceptance activity.

'isReviewing' in edas specifically links reviewing roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper they are reviewing. 'give' in iasted is a very general property linking a Person to an Activity or Item they give. The domain, range, and intended semantics differ significantly; 'give' is far more general and not specific to the reviewing context.
Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area under Topic in edas, while Organizing Committee member is a person role under Organizator in sigkdd. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to a currency string, while locationOf is an object property linking Location to Event. They are entirely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

'parallel with' relates administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'covers Topic' relates papers or events to research topics. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's stated preference or willingness to review papers on specific topics (with a degree), while Personal Review History in edas represents a record of past reviews a reviewer has completed. These are conceptually distinct: one is prospective/preference-based, the other is retrospective/history-based.

Personal History in edas refers to an individual's record (with children like Personal Publication History and Personal Review History), whereas Proceedings in ekaw refers to a published multi-author volume of conference papers. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for anyone contributing to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants), directly under Person. SC Member in ekaw is a Steering Committee member, a specific committee role nested under PC Member. These are conceptually distinct: one covers content contributors, the other a governance/organizational role.
Paper Author is a person who writes papers, while Platinum Supporter is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Poster is a type of academic contribution (a presentation format), while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

An 'Extended abstract' is a short regular contribution (a sibling of Paper in ontology A), while a 'Poster Paper' is a specific type of paper intended for poster presentation in ekaw. They represent different kinds of conference contributions with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers), while Departure is an activity after the conference (leaving the venue). They are entirely different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person representing an individual participating in a conference, while Organization in edas represents institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGO). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Call for paper is a type of conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Paper Author is a type of Person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference applicant in Ontology A is a subclass of Person representing someone who applies to attend the conference (with child Registeered applicant). Speaker in Ontology B is a subclass of Delegate representing someone who presents at the conference. These are conceptually distinct roles: one is about registration/application, the other about presenting.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'has Program Committee Member' links a Program Committee to its members, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document. They are unrelated.

Person in cmt represents a human individual involved in the conference (e.g., reviewer, chairman), while State in iasted represents a geographical or administrative region (a place). These are entirely different concepts.

User in cmt is a general class for any person interacting with the system (parent of Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while Student lecturer in iasted is a very specific role (a student who is also a lecturer). These concepts are entirely different in scope and meaning.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document indicating a conflict of interest, while 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person indicating usage. These are semantically completely different properties with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

'has workshops' relates a conference volume to its workshops (part-of), while 'is situated in' relates physical locations (building/city/place) to broader locations. They describe entirely different relationships.

In cmt, Document is a general class for conference artefacts (Paper, Review). In edas, PersonalHistory is about an individual's background records (publication history, review history). These represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is a subclass of Author representing authors who are not reviewers. Member PC in confOf represents program committee members (reviewers). These are conceptually distinct and even somewhat opposite roles; one is an author without review duties, the other is explicitly a reviewer.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific leadership role (a type of Chairman), while Regular in confOf is a type of conference participant/attendee (non-student, non-member). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Free Time Break is a type of conference event (a temporal break), while Conference hall is a type of place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while design links ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. Completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Both are datatype properties linking a Person (or Contact Information/Person) to a string representing an email address. They serve the same purpose in the conference domain.

paper ID is a datatype property identifying a Paper (domain: Paper, range: unsignedLong), while has an ISBN identifies Conference proceedings (domain: Conference proceedings, range: string). They apply to different entities and serve different identification purposes.

Entity A is a Reviewer (a person who reviews papers) while Entity B is an Author (a person who writes papers). In ontology B, Reviewer is actually a sibling of Author, confirming they are distinct roles. These classes are unrelated.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Extended abstract in Ontology A is a type of regular contribution (a sibling of Paper), representing a short paper submission. Tutorial Abstract in Ontology B is an abstract specifically for a tutorial. These are distinct concepts serving different purposes in a conference.
'writtenBy' relates a Document to its author (Person), while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to the payer (Person). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

A Workshop (edas) is a type of Academic Event typically involving interactive sessions on a specific topic, while a Session (iasted) is a subtype of Lecture within a conference activity hierarchy. They are both conference-related events but represent different concepts; they overlap in the broader sense of being parts of a conference program but are not equivalent.
Meal Menu is a document listing food options for a meal event, while Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

The properties have completely different domains (Conference vs Academic Institution), ranges (Administrator vs unspecified), and semantics (finalizing paper assignments vs scientifically organizing). They are unrelated.
Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person (someone who can review papers), while Person in iasted is the general class for people. Thus Possible_Reviewer is subsumed by iasted's Person.

Student in confOf is a class representing a person (a type of Participant), while Student registration fee in iasted is a class representing a monetary fee. They are fundamentally different concepts (person vs. fee) and thus unrelated.

In edas, 'Conference' is the top-level event (the whole conference), with children like Single Level Conference and Two Level Conference. In ekaw, 'Conference Session' is a sub-event within a conference (a specific session such as an Industrial Session or Regular Session), child of Session. These denote different granularities: the entire conference vs. a session within it.

Property A 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution (Author -> Contribution), while property B 'writtenBy' has domain Document and range Person (Document -> Person). They are inverse properties of each other, not equivalent. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are related.
Security Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is a group of people who review papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution (Author -> Contribution), while property B 'is prepared by' has domain Item and range Person (Item -> Person). They connect the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions: A is the inverse of B. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Author of paper student is a person (a student who authored a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Industrial Paper is a type of academic paper submitted to a conference, while Mailing list is a communication document/list. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
