Property A (writtenBy) goes from Document to Person, while property B (prepare) goes from Person to Item. They express inverse directions of a similar authorship/preparation relationship, so they are related but not equivalent (a property and its inverse are not equivalent).
The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Negative Review is a type of review document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'hasPart' is a general mereological (part-whole) property with unspecified domain/range, while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item. They express entirely different relations.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (signing). These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.

The property 'title' in cmt relates a Paper to its title string, while 'has Cost Currency' in edas relates a Sponsorship to a currency string. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

'technicallyOrganisedBy' denotes the technical organization of an event (a sub-property of 'organised By'), while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give/present. These properties have different semantics, domains, and ranges, and are unrelated.

'employed By' is a specific employment relation from Person to Organization, while 'is connected with' is a very general association property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They differ in semantics, domain, and range.

'has the last name' is a datatype property linking Person to a string (surname), while 'can stay in' is an object property linking Person to a Place (accommodation). They describe entirely different relations.
Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Excursion is a social event/activity at a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Property A links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic classification), while property B links a Conference volume to its Tracks (organizational subdivisions). They have different domains, ranges, and semantic meanings.

A 'Conference announcement' is a document used to announce conference details (e.g., calls for papers), while a 'Book proceeding' is a published collection of accepted conference papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Banquet is a social dining event during the conference, while Departure refers to leaving after the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
In cmt, 'Meta Review' is a subclass of 'Review'. In ekaw, 'Review' is the general class for reviews. A meta review is a specific kind of review, so cmt:Meta Review is subsumed by ekaw:Review.

'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while 'is_needed_for' links an Item to a Person (resource requirement). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

The property 'accepted By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to something it organizes. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Document is an informational item/paper. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Review Rating in edas represents the evaluation outcome of a paper (e.g., accept/reject ratings), while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts such as conference days and deadlines. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
registrationDueOn refers to the deadline for conference registration, while Start_of_conference refers to when the conference begins. These are distinct temporal milestones of a conference.
reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper, while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains (Conference vs Paper), ranges (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer), and semantics (indicating who started reviewer bidding vs assigning a reviewer to a paper).

'has parts' is a whole-to-part relation from Conference volume to Conference part, while 'belongs To Event' links a Programme to a Conference Event. They have different domains, ranges, and directions (composition vs. event association), so they are unrelated.
Paper Abstract is a summary of a research paper, while Hotel registration form is a form for booking hotel accommodation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee (membership/leadership role), while Property B relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizing/holding). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference participant is a Person who attends a conference, while Social event is an Event (e.g., banquet, reception). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
hasEmail and hasFirstName are distinct datatype properties capturing different attributes (email address vs. first name) of a Person. They are not equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a specific type of Working event (sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). In ekaw, Scientific_Event is a broader class whose children include Conference, Workshop, Session, Track, etc. Thus confOf:Conference is subsumed by ekaw:Scientific_Event.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a type of regular contribution (a document format), while in ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a specific lifecycle state of a paper (one that has been submitted). Ekaw's general 'Paper' class would be the closer match to Conference's 'Paper'. 'Submitted Paper' overlaps with but is not equivalent to 'Paper', as not all papers are necessarily submitted and submission is a status rather than a document type.
A Programme Brochure is a document listing conference events/sessions, while an Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are distinct sibling types under Document with different intended instances.
Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, while Early Registered Participant (B) is a specific subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw. Thus A subsumes B.

Meeting Room Place is a venue for holding meetings/sessions, while Hotel room is an accommodation place for lodging. They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain and are not equivalent or hierarchically related.

Conference in edas represents the academic event/organization itself (with dates, topics, members), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place/venue (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Attendee in edas is a general conference participant (child of Person), while Reviewer in iasted is a specific role (child of Speaker) responsible for reviewing papers. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

Paper in edas is a scholarly submission (with reviews, authors, topics), while Flyer in ekaw is a promotional document published by an organisation. They are distinct concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while has_amount_of is a datatype property on Money indicating a monetary amount. They have completely different domains and semantics.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or expertise level for reviewing certain topics or submissions, while Contribution in Ontology B represents an actual submitted work (paper, poster, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Workshop is a type of working event (like a conference or tutorial) focused on collaborative discussion, while a Speaker lecture is a specific session within a conference where a speaker presents. These are fundamentally different kinds of events/activities in the conference domain.

In edas, Excursion is a subclass of Social Event, while in ekaw, Social Event is a class with children like Conference Trip (which corresponds to Excursion). Thus, edas:Excursion is subsumed by ekaw:Social_Event.

City and State are distinct geographic/administrative concepts. In iasted, City is a sibling of State (both appear in the domain/range of 'is situated in'), confirming they are different classes. A city is not equivalent to a state.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information), while a 'Power Point presentation' is a specific format of presentation activity at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of 'Conference applicant', which is a sibling of other Person subclasses, suggesting it refers to someone who applied/registered for the conference (likely an attendee). In Ontology B, 'Conference Participant' is a broad class directly under Person that includes not only registered participants (Early/Late Registered Participant) but also organizers and chairs (PC Chair, Session Chair, etc.). The two classes overlap in intent (people attending/participating in the conference) but differ significantly in scope: ekaw's Conference Participant subsumes roles that are not applicants/registrants, while Conference's Registeered applicant excludes non-registered participants like chairs. Therefore they are related but not equivalent.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person representing someone applying to attend the conference, while Committee is an organizational group (with subtypes like Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Tutorial within the conference domain. Despite different hierarchical placements (ekaw under Individual Presentation, iasted under Lecture), they denote the same concept: a tutorial session at a conference.
employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country (location). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (a direct subclass of Person), while SC Member in ekaw is a specific role within the Steering Committee (subclass of PC Member). These are conceptually distinct: one is a broad participation category, the other a specific organizational role.

Rejected contribution is a class of papers/contributions that were rejected after review, while Week Reject Rating is a type of review rating (a score/evaluation). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent different concepts.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while has_a_volume is a datatype property on Conference proceedings indicating the volume number. They have different domains, different semantics, and are unrelated.
hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while isWrittenBy links a Paper to its Author. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Program committee is a type of committee responsible for reviewing papers in a conference, while University is an educational organization. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

assignedTo (cmt) has domain Paper and range Reviewer, while reviewerOfPaper (ekaw) has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper. They are inverse properties relating the same kinds of entities in opposite directions. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are related.

In edas, AcademicEvent is a broad class encompassing workshops, paper presentations, talks, and organizational meetings. In iasted, Session is a specific type of Lecture (which itself is a Conference activity). An AcademicEvent subsumes a Session since a session is one kind of academic event, but they are not equivalent because AcademicEvent also includes workshops and other broader event types.

hasRating links a paper to its review rating, while is_used_for links an item to an activity or money. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

The 'title' property in cmt gives the title of a Paper (a string), while 'has Last Name' in edas gives the last name of a Person (a string). They have different domains and completely different semantics.

Early Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered early, while Tutorial speaker is a person who gives a tutorial. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.
Poster Paper is a type of document/paper, while Registration deadline is a type of time/deadline. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The 'email' property captures a person's email address, while 'hasBiography' captures biographical information. Although both are datatype properties from Person to string, they represent entirely different attributes and are not semantically equivalent or related.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is connected with' is a much broader property relating Activity or Person to Item or Place. Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly.
Passive conference participant is a type of person attending a conference, while Conference city is a type of city where a conference takes place. They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes are named Document and share some overlap (e.g., both have Review as a child), but their intended instances differ significantly. In ekaw, Document is a broad class covering papers, abstracts, flyers, programme brochures, and websites. In iasted, Document is a subclass of Item (alongside physical items like Audiovisual equipment) and covers administrative/operational documents such as forms, invitation letters, payment documents, visa documents, and transparencies. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

EKAW's Social Event (with children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip) overlaps with IASTED's Activity after conference (with children Full day tour and Departure), as both capture social/recreational activities around a conference. However, they are not strictly equivalent: Social Event is defined by its social nature regardless of timing, while Activity after conference is defined by occurring after the conference and could include non-social activities like Departure.

Company is an organization type (business entity), while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a research topic classification. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and share no semantic overlap.

Company in confOf is a type of Organization (business entity), while Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State representing the status/state of something related to a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class encompassing authors, reviewers, chairs, and PC members (anyone participating in the conference). Track workshop chair in the Conference ontology is a very specific role responsible for chairing a track or workshop. The former is far more general than the latter, and they do not share the same intended instances, so they are unrelated.
Property A links a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while property B links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'lists Event' relates programme brochures or web sites to events they list, while 'is given by' relates activities or items to the person who gives/presents them. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'enter Review Criteria' relates an Administrator to a Conference for entering review criteria, while 'need' relates a Person to an Item they require. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Demo Session is a type of event/session where demonstrations are presented, while Program Committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the technical program. They are entirely different concepts.

Reviewer and Conference Chair are distinct roles in conference organization. A reviewer evaluates papers, while a conference chair oversees the entire conference. They are siblings under Person in edas, confirming they are separate concepts.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-whole within proceedings), while Property B relates a Conference to a Person (membership). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the conference system (authors, reviewers, administrators). Introduction in iasted is a subclass of Conference activity representing an event at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In edas, Conference represents the academic event itself (with dates, topics, papers). In iasted, Conference building is a physical structure (subclass of Building) where conference activities may take place. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Topic in Ontology A refers to a subject area or theme of a conference paper/track, while Time in Ontology B refers to temporal concepts (days, deadlines). These are entirely different domain concepts.

Conference contributor (A) is a person who contributes to the conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Student (B) is a type of participant defined by their student status. These are conceptually distinct roles in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'Author' is a general class for anyone who authored something (with children like 'Author book proceedings included', 'Lecturer', etc.). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a specific subclass of 'Author' restricted to those who authored a paper. Thus, the iasted 'Author' subsumes the sigkdd 'Author of paper'.

writeReview (domain: Reviewer, range: Review) and reviewWrittenBy (domain: Review, range: Possible Reviewer) are inverse properties of each other, not equivalent. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Session is a type of Scientific Event that groups presentations (with children like Conference Session, Workshop Session). In iasted, Plenary lecture is a specific type of Lecture (a single presentation), and Session is actually a sibling of Plenary lecture under Lecture. A session (container of talks) and a plenary lecture (a single talk) are distinct concepts.

setMaxPapers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while expertOn relates a PC Member to a Topic (indicating expertise). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class under Person encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors who contribute to the conference. Hotel presenter in Ontology B is a very specific subclass of Delegate (under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate) likely referring to someone presenting at a hotel venue. These are not equivalent; Hotel presenter might be a kind of contributor but the concepts differ significantly in scope and modeling context.
The 'title' property gives the title of a Paper (string), while 'Currency' gives the currency of a Registration fee (string). They have completely different domains and semantic meanings.
Paper is a document/submission in the conference domain, while Wireless Communications Topic is a specific subject area or topic. They represent entirely different concepts.

locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while Currency is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to a string. They are entirely unrelated in meaning, domain, and range.

In iasted, Document is a broad class with many children including Review, Submission, Form, etc. In sigkdd, Document is the parent of Review, Abstract, and Paper. The iasted Document class is strictly more general than the sigkdd Document class (which would roughly correspond to iasted's Submission/Review subset), so iasted:Document subsumes sigkdd:Document. However, the pair given is iasted:Document vs sigkdd:Review. Since sigkdd:Review is a child of sigkdd:Document, and iasted:Document has Review as one of its children, iasted:Document is much broader and subsumes sigkdd:Review.

Demo Session in ekaw is a specific type of Session (a sibling of Conference Session, Poster Session, etc.), while Session in iasted is a more general class under Lecture/Conference activity. Therefore, the iasted Session subsumes the ekaw Demo Session.

Conference Banquet is a social dining event, while Welcome address is an opening speech or greeting at a conference. They are distinct types of conference activities with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Review Question in edas refers to individual questions on a review form (with numerical/textual subtypes), whereas Review in sigkdd is the complete review document itself (a sibling of Paper and Abstract under Document). These are distinct concepts.

hasRating links a paper to its review rating (a score/evaluation value), while hasReview links a paper to the review document itself. These are distinct concepts: one points to a rating, the other to a review artefact.

Conference contributor (A) is a Person who contributes to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Delegate (B) in iasted is also a Person attending/participating in the conference (speakers, listeners, session chairs, etc.). They overlap significantly as both represent conference participants/contributors, but 'contributor' implies an active contribution role while 'delegate' can include passive attendees (listeners), so they are related rather than strictly equivalent.

Both properties relate a person/author to a conference document/paper they contributed or are related to. In the conference domain, 'Person' aligns with 'Author', and 'Conference document' aligns with 'Paper'. The semantics of contributing to a paper and having a related paper are effectively equivalent in this context.

Property A (isReviewedBy) links a Paper to the person who reviewed it (domain: Paper, range: Reviewer/Chair/etc.). Property B (give) links a Person to an Activity or Item they give (domain: Person, range: Activity/Item). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while paperPresentedAs relates a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation describing how it is presented. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Withdrawn Paper is a subclass of Paper representing a paper that has been withdrawn, while Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline representing the deadline for submitting papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'writtenBy' relates a Document to its author (Person), while 'is designed for' relates an Activity/Money/Time to an intended target (Activity/Person). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
hasTopic links a Working event to a Topic, while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'has Review History' relates a Reviewer to a Personal Review History. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In edas, Active Paper is a Paper that has a rating (i.e., under review), with children including Rated Papers and siblings like Pending/Accepted/Rejected. In ekaw, Assigned Paper is a Submitted Paper that has been assigned for review, with child Evaluated Paper. Both represent the same stage in the paper lifecycle: a submitted paper that is actively being reviewed or has been assigned reviewers. The structural context (between submission and final decision) aligns closely.

locationOf is a specific property linking a Location to an Event (inverse direction: Location -> Event). is_connected_with is a very general property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They differ in specificity, domain/range semantics, and directionality; they are not equivalent.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (event/organization), while Late Registered Participant in ekaw is a type of person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

confOf:dealsWith relates Contribution to Topic, while edas:hasTopic relates Paper (and Conference) to Topic. Since Contribution and Paper are equivalent in this domain, the properties overlap significantly for papers, but edas:hasTopic also applies to Conference, making them not strictly equivalent. They are related.

In cmt, User is a broad class under Person encompassing Administrator, Author, and Reviewer (anyone who uses the system). In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant with siblings Regular and Student, referring specifically to conference members/attendees. These are overlapping but not equivalent concepts: cmt's User includes roles like Administrator that are not conference members, while confOf's Member refers to participant membership types.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place (accommodation). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (participant of a conference), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a Place (physical venue). They are entirely different concepts.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's stated preference or willingness to review a particular topic or submission (with a degree), whereas Review in Ontology B represents the actual written review document of a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both classes represent the program committee of a conference. Despite slight differences in modeling (Ontology B places it under Committee), their intended instances are identical: the group responsible for reviewing and selecting papers.

Both are datatype properties mapping to a string representing a place, but 'location' in confOf applies to events (Social event, Working event) and denotes where the event is held, while 'City of conference' in sigkdd applies specifically to the Conference class and denotes only the city. They overlap semantically but differ in domain and granularity, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while a 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event for reviewing submitted contributions. They are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. event) with different purposes.

hasTitle is a datatype property giving the title of a Contribution (paper), while Name_of_conference gives the name of a Conference. They have different domains and denote entirely different concepts.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Organization is an institution (academia, government, industry, NGO). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while property B 'updatedVersionOf' relates a Document to another Document indicating versioning. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Tutorial Abstract is a specific type of abstract summarizing a tutorial, while Review is an evaluation document for a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the abstract of a paper/contribution in the conference domain. In cmt, PaperAbstract is a subclass of Paper (sibling to PaperFullVersion), representing the abstract portion. In Conference, Abstract is linked via 'is the 1th part of' and 'has an abstract' to Paper, Poster, Presentation, serving the same role. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide.

The two properties have different domains (Conference vs Call), different ranges (boolean vs string), and different semantics: one indicates whether hardcopy submissions are accepted, the other provides submission instructions as text.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts: 'has Program Committee Member' links a Program Committee to its members, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They share no semantic overlap.

Property A links an organizing committee to a conference volume (committee-of relation), while property B links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizer/holder relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes serve as the top-level document class in their respective conference ontologies. They share similar children (Review, web-related documents, papers/contributions) and analogous properties linking them to persons as authors (has authors / written By). Despite slightly different scopes of children, they represent the same concept of a conference-related document.
Property A links programme brochures/websites to events they list, while property B links documents to speakers who present them. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while is_paid_in relates Money to a Building (payment location). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered for a conference, while a 'Credit card' is a payment instrument (a type of card). These are entirely different concepts in the domain.
'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while 'prepare' links a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
One is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), the other is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They are entirely different relations.

Property A relates a Person to an Item they need, while property B relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD (the organization searching for sponsors). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area topic (subclass of Topic). They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Research in iasted is an activity (a type of work done before the conference), while Author in sigkdd is a person who writes and submits papers. These are entirely different concepts.
User is a person role in the conference system (parent: Person), while Session room is a physical place (parent: Place). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Reception is a social event (an activity/gathering), while Conference Venue Place is a physical location (a place). They belong to fundamentally different categories in the ontology and are not equivalent or related.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money (usage). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

hasPhone is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a phone number string, while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They describe entirely different concepts and relations.

Paper Full Version is a type of academic paper document, while Platinum Supporter is a top-tier sponsor category. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in a conference (subclass of Person), while Workshop in Conference ontology is an event/sub-part of a conference (subclass of Conference part). These are entirely different concepts.

In confOf, 'Science Worker' is a direct subclass of Person representing academic/research personnel (scientists, researchers). In iasted, 'Worker non speaker' is deeply nested under Place > Building > Conference building > Delegate > Non speaker, representing a non-speaking worker attending the conference venue. These denote fundamentally different concepts: one is an academic role, the other is a non-speaking delegate category tied to a physical location hierarchy.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (with sibling Review). In ekaw, Document is the top-level class whose children include both Paper and Review. Therefore, cmt:Paper is subsumed by ekaw:Document, as ekaw:Document is more general and encompasses papers, reviews, flyers, etc.

A Steering committee is a type of committee responsible for guiding a conference, while a University is an academic organization/institution. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Poster as a type of conference contribution/paper. In Ontology A it is under Conference contribution, and in Ontology B it is under Contribution. They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Document in ekaw represents written artefacts (papers, reviews, flyers, etc.), while Deadline in sigkdd represents temporal submission/notification deadlines. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while 'Brief introduction for Session chair' in iasted is a type of document. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful relationship.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Review preference in Ontology A is a class representing a reviewer's preference or degree of interest for reviewing a topic/paper (with properties like 'has a degree'). Member PC in Ontology B represents a person who is a program committee member/reviewer. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an abstract preference object, the other is a role played by a person.

Property A 'name' is a datatype property for naming Conferences and Persons, while property B 'remark' is a datatype property for adding remarks to Contributions. They have different semantics, domains, and purposes.

Workshop is an academic event type (a session at a conference), while Renting is a logistical activity performed before a conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (the chair of a conference), while Conference in confOf is an event type (a working event). They are entirely different concepts.
rejectPaper is an action by an Administrator to reject a Paper, while relatedToPaper links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Contribution 1th author is a specific role (first/primary author of a contribution), while Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any author of a paper. They overlap but are not equivalent; the former is more specific than the latter, though their hierarchical placement differs across ontologies.

In Ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific type of conference contributor who gives an invited talk. In Ontology B, 'Regular' (with comment 'confTool') refers to a regular registration type for participants, as evidenced by its siblings 'Member' and 'Student'. These denote entirely different concepts: one is a speaking role, the other is a registration category.
Review is a document representing an evaluation of a paper, while Call For Manuscripts is a type of call soliciting submissions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer who reads it, while property B links a Person to an Item they write. The directions (reading vs writing), domains, and ranges are entirely different, making them unrelated.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Conference proceedings is a publication/document containing the collected papers of a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance action), while parallel_with relates two Administrative events to each other (temporal/scheduling relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while occupy links a Person to a Building/City/State (location). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Research Topic is a subject area covered by papers and events, while ACM SIGKDD represents the organizing body/conference entity that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A (hasProgramCommitteeMember) has domain Program Committee and range Program Committee Member, while property B (was_a_member_of) has domain Committee member and range Committee. Property B is the inverse of a 'has member' property, not equivalent to A. Additionally, A is specific to program committees while B is general to any committee. They are related as they connect similar concepts but in opposite directions and with different specificity.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while search links ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while initiates links a chair or TPC member to a Call. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

endDate is a datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime value, while listsEvent is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Travel Grant is a type of Sponsorship (a funding mechanism), while Invited Speaker is a type of Person/role. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while 'Modelling' is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Administrator in cmt is a conference management role (assigns reviewers, accepts papers), while Author in sigkdd is a person who submits papers. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Registration of participants event is an administrative event. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
Property A links a PC member to a Topic (expertise area), while property B links a Person to a Conference (membership). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Session chair (iasted) is a specific role for chairing a session, which falls under the broader category of Organizator (sigkdd). In sigkdd, Organizator has children like General Chair and Program Chair, indicating it covers various organizing roles. Session chair is more specific than Organizator, so it is subsumed by it.

Property A links a conference part to a conference volume (publication structure), while Property B links a conference event to a place (location). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Review (an evaluation of a paper) and Abstract (a summary of a paper) are distinct document types in the conference domain. They share the same parent class Document but have completely different intended instances.

Reception is a social event (like a welcome gathering), while Full day tour is an excursion/tour activity after the conference. Both are non-academic social activities at a conference, but they denote different specific types of events. They share a common ancestor concept (social/non-academic activity) but are not equivalent.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to sub-events or subdivisions of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), whereas Conference in edas refers to the entire conference event itself. These are distinct concepts at different levels of granularity.
Workshop Chair is a person who chairs a workshop session, while Tutorial speaker is a person who gives a tutorial presentation. These are entirely different roles in a conference.

In edas, 'Dining Place' is a subclass of 'Place', while in sigkdd, 'Place' is the general class with children like Conference hall, Hotel, and Main office. The edas 'Dining Place' is strictly more specific than the sigkdd 'Place', so it is subsumed by it.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. Plenary lecture speaker (B) is a very specific type of speaker/author. Thus A subsumes B, as every plenary lecture speaker is a conference contributor but not vice versa.

AuthorNotReviewer in cmt is a subclass of Author representing authors who are not reviewers. Reviewer in iasted is a subclass of Speaker representing people who review. These are distinct and essentially opposite roles; one explicitly excludes reviewing while the other is defined by it.

Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while Nonauthor registration fee is a type of monetary fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of conference event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A (Conference in cmt) represents the conference event/organization itself, with properties like members, logo URL, and acceptance of submissions. Entity B (Important dates in Conference ontology) represents a collection of deadline dates associated with a conference volume. These are fundamentally different concepts.

'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (who adjusted the bid), while 'has Updated Version' links a Document to another Document (a newer version). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a conference part to a topic (track/workshop/tutorial topic), while property B links a document to a speaker (who presents it). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Presenter university is a type of Building (an academic institution where a presenter is affiliated), while Hotel is an accommodation venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Single Level Conference in edas refers to a type of conference (e.g., single-track vs two-level), while One conference day in iasted refers to a duration/time concept under Conference days. They are entirely different concepts.
writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while invites_co-reviewers links a Reviewer to another Reviewer they invite. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a Review to the person who wrote it (Reviewer in cmt, Possible Reviewer in ekaw). Despite the slight difference in range class naming, they express the same relation in the conference domain.

Working event is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Security Topic is a specific subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

The property 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document. These relate entirely different domain and range concepts and describe different relations in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (who delivers it), while 'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who funds/provides it). They describe different relationships in the conference domain.
heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location, while Date is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who paid late), while Student registration fee is a subclass of Money/Fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Workshop is a type of scientific event (a meeting/session), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to submitted scholarly works (papers, posters, presentations), while Administrative event in Ontology B refers to organizational activities or deadlines (submission event, reviewing event). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Contribution in confOf refers specifically to academic submissions (papers, posters, short papers) written by authors and reviewed by PC members. Item in iasted is a very broad physical/logistical concept (equipment, cards, vehicles, documents) used in conference logistics. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Administrator in cmt is a conference management role (assigns reviewers, accepts papers, enters details), while Reviewer in Conference ontology is the person who reviews papers. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and properties.
The property 'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document, while 'is paid in' relates Money to a Building. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (who adjusted the bid), while 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). They are unrelated.

Submitted Paper in ekaw is a specific type of paper that has been submitted to a conference. Document in iasted is a broad class whose children include Submission, Review, Form, Payment document, etc. Submitted Paper would correspond more closely to the 'Submission' child class in iasted, so it is subsumed by the broader Document class.

In ontology A (iasted), 'Registation deadline' is a subclass of 'Deadline'. In ontology B (sigkdd), 'Deadline' is the general class with specific deadline subclasses. Therefore, the iasted 'Registation deadline' is subsumed by the sigkdd 'Deadline' class.

'has a review' links a paper to its Review (the textual evaluation), while 'has Rating' links a paper to a Review Rating (a score/grade). These are related concepts in the review process but not equivalent: one points to a review document, the other to a rating value.
Van is a transport vehicle (subclass of Item), while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Written contribution is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/artefact such as a paper), while Talk Event is a subclass of Academic Event (a scheduled event like a closing or welcome talk). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event) and are unrelated.
Reviewer in edas is a Person who reviews papers, while Review in sigkdd is a Document (the review artefact itself). They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. document) and thus unrelated.

Tutorial Chair (ekaw) and Program Chair (sigkdd) are distinct roles in conference organization. A Tutorial Chair oversees tutorials, while a Program Chair oversees the overall program. They are related as both are chair/organizer roles but not equivalent.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference, while property B ('references') in ekaw is a generic citation/reference relation between documents or entities. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (assignedByReviewer) links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer, indicating assignment by a reviewer. Property B (invites_co-reviewers) links a Reviewer to another Reviewer, indicating invitation of co-reviewers. The domains differ (ExternalReviewer vs Reviewer), the semantics differ (assignment vs invitation), and they are not inverses of each other.

Both are top-level Person classes in their respective conference ontologies. Despite having different children and properties reflecting each ontology's modeling choices, they denote the same general concept of a person involved in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a member of the conference's technical program committee (TPC). In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a Person who belongs to a Committee and has children Chair/Co-chair. In Ontology B (edas), 'TPC Member' is a Person who reviews papers and initiates calls, with siblings like Conference Chair and Reviewer. TPC stands for Technical Program Committee, so these denote the same concept in the conference domain.

In edas, Free Time Break and Coffee Break are sibling subclasses of Break Event, meaning they are distinct concepts. In iasted, Coffee break is a specific type of conference activity. Therefore, edas:FreeTimeBreak does not match iasted:Coffee_break; rather, iasted:Coffee_break would correspond to edas:CoffeeBreak. The two classes are related as both represent types of breaks during a conference but are not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property linking Review preference to an integer (degree level), while Property B is an object property linking Person to Item (obtaining something). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

An Invited Speaker is a person invited to present at a conference, while a Reviewer is a person who evaluates submitted papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair, while property B links a Person to an Item they need. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in cmt represents the conference event/organization itself, while Conference city in iasted is a subclass of City representing the location where a conference takes place. These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. geographic location).

Submission event refers to the act of authors submitting their contributions/papers, while Accepting manuscript refers to the committee's decision to accept a manuscript. These are distinct phases in the conference workflow (submission vs. acceptance decision) and do not denote the same concept.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while Refusing manuscript is an administrative activity before the conference involving rejecting a paper submission. These are entirely different concepts.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite the unusual parentage including Person and TPC Member), while Session Chair in ekaw is a person role responsible for chairing a session. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property describing the expertise level of a 'Review expertise' entity, while Property B is an object property linking a PC member to a contribution they review. They have different types, domains, ranges, and semantics.

In EKAW, 'Industrial Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper', whereas in SIGKDD, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (a direct child of Document). Therefore, EKAW's Industrial Paper is subsumed by SIGKDD's Paper.

A Government Organization is a type of organization (e.g., a government agency) classified by sector, while an Organizing Committee is a specific committee responsible for organizing a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants), while Webmaster in Ontology B is a specific organizational role responsible for the conference website. They represent fundamentally different concepts.

Registration in iasted is a conference activity (an event/action of registering), while Registration fee in sigkdd is a monetary fee associated with registration. They are related concepts but not equivalent: one is an activity, the other is a financial amount.

An Organizational Meeting is a type of academic event focused on organizational matters (e.g., committee meetings), while a Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference program. They represent fundamentally different concepts within the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Conference volume' is a direct child of 'Conference' and holds all the typical conference properties (location, committees, contributions, tracks, important dates). In Ontology B, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Working event' with siblings Tutorial and Workshop. Both classes represent the same concept: a specific instance/edition of a conference event in the conference-organisation domain.

A Trip is a specific type of social event (an excursion), while a Break Event is a pause in the conference schedule (coffee break, meal break, free time). They are distinct kinds of non-academic events with different intended instances.

Multimedia Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (maximum number of choices), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A is a boolean flag on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted. Property B is a date property on Important dates indicating when acceptance announcements are made. They have different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Country in confOf represents a geopolitical entity (used as range of 'has Country' for Organization/Person), while Person in sigkdd represents a human participant (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are entirely different concepts.

Talk Event in edas is a broader category encompassing any talk at a conference (including Closing Talk, Welcome Talk), while Plenary lecture in iasted is a specific type of lecture given to all attendees. They overlap conceptually as both involve presentations/talks at conferences, but neither subsumes the other cleanly across ontologies, making them related rather than equivalent.

Entity A is a 'Steering committee' (a committee/group), while Entity B is an 'Organizing Committee member' (a person who is a member of the organizing committee). They differ both in kind (group vs. person) and in which committee they refer to (steering vs. organizing).

Property A ('done till') is a datatype property on Deadline indicating when a deadline occurs, while Property B ('End of conference') is a datatype property on Conference indicating the conference end date. They have different domains (Deadline vs Conference) and different semantic meanings (a generic deadline date vs specifically the end of a conference), so they are unrelated.

writeReview is an object property linking a Reviewer to a Review they author, while has_an_expertise is a datatype property describing the expertise level of a Review expertise entity. They relate entirely different concepts and have different types (object vs datatype), so they are unrelated.
readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (reading action), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A links a steering committee to a conference volume, while property B links a person to an item they sign. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference (for setting up review criteria), while 'is Reviewing' links reviewing roles (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.) to a Paper they are reviewing. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Entity A is a research topic related to computer networks management, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Dining Place is a specific type of place for eating/dining, while Building is a general physical structure that includes many subtypes (hotels, universities, restaurants, etc.). They are not equivalent; at best they overlap slightly since a dining place could be in a building, but their intended instances differ significantly.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the event it organizes), while property B links an Organisation to something it technically organises. Both concern organizing relationships in the conference domain, but they differ in directionality focus (A is 'was committee of', B is 'organises'), domain specificity (committee vs organisation), and range (conference volume vs unspecified). They are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Conference' denotes the overall conference event/organization (with properties like accepts submissions, has members, logo URL). In confOf, 'Event' is a broader class with children Administrative_event, Social_event, and Working_event, representing individual scheduled occurrences within a conference rather than the conference itself. They overlap in that a conference involves events, but they are not equivalent; 'Conference' is more specific to the whole gathering while 'Event' covers any sub-activity.

hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They are entirely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

endReview is an object property linking a Program Committee Chair to a Review (an action to end the review process), while endDate is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing when the conference ends. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while relatedToPaper relates a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the same concept: a person who writes/authors a paper or contribution for a conference. They share the same parent (Person), similar siblings (other conference roles), and analogous properties linking them to papers/contributions (writes/writtenBy vs hasRelatedPaper/isWrittenBy).

Although both are datatype properties with range int representing an amount, their domains differ significantly: hasCostAmount applies to Sponsorship (the cost of a sponsorship package), while has_amount_of applies to Money (a monetary value). They model different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

Organization in confOf represents institutions like companies and universities that employ people, while Place in edas represents physical locations such as venues, accommodations, and dining places. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Program committee (A) is a committee/group entity under Committee, while Program Chair (B) is a person role under Person > Organizator. A committee and its chair are fundamentally different kinds of entities (group vs. individual role), so they are unrelated.
Property A links a Co-author to a Paper (co-writing relation), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). They involve different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging, while Worker non speaker is a type of conference delegate (person). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
The properties are inverses of each other: 'writePaper' goes from Author to Paper, while 'is_prepared_by' goes from Item (paper) to Person (author). A property and its inverse are not equivalent.

Both properties capture the nationality or country of a person, but they differ significantly: hasCountry is an object property with domain Organization/Person and range Country (a class), while Nation is a datatype property with domain Person only and range string. They are semantically related but not equivalent due to different domains, ranges, and property types.

'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to its start date string, while 'has Name' links a Conference to its full name string. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes; they are completely unrelated.
dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while submit links an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper, while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations in the conference domain.

The properties have opposite directions and different semantics. 'has Co author' goes from Paper to Co-author (paper has co-author), while 'write' goes from Person to Item (person writes item). They are inverses in spirit but not equivalent, and their domains/ranges differ significantly.
Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person, while Person in iasted is the general class for people. Student is more specific than Person, so Student is subsumed by Person.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting submissions, while Main office is a physical place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Memeber registration fee is a specific type of registration fee for members, while Sponzor fee is a fee paid by sponsors. These are distinct types of fees with different intended instances.
Pending Paper is a status of a paper (Document > Paper), while Registation deadline is a type of deadline (Time > Deadline). They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The 'follows' property in confOf relates administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while the 'obtain' property in sigkdd relates authors to awards they receive. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A represents an accepted contribution/paper, while Entity B represents a rejected paper. These are disjoint sibling concepts (opposite outcomes of the review process) and therefore unrelated in terms of equivalence or subsumption.
Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, while Late Registered Participant (B) is a specific subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw. Thus A subsumes B.

Company in confOf is an Organization (a type of institution/business), while Main office in sigkdd is a Place (a physical location, sibling of Conference hall and Hotel). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while hasLocation relates a Conference Event to a Place. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing the email address of a person. They are semantically identical.

Property A is an inverse of a partOf relation with range Event in ekaw, while property B relates Document to Speaker (presentationed by) in sigkdd. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who paid late), while Hotel fee is a subclass of Money/Fee (a monetary charge for accommodation). They are entirely different concepts.
Bid represents a reviewer's bid on a paper in the conference review process, while City represents a geographical location. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Property A links a conference volume to its organizing committee (a structural/organizational relation), while property B links a conference to the organization that holds it (e.g., ACM SIGKDD). These relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while submit_until relates a Document to a Deadline (submission deadline). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Conference Chair in edas is a Person role (someone who chairs a conference), while Brief introduction for Session chair in iasted is a Document (an informational item). They are completely different concepts.

Conference in cmt represents the overall conference event/organization, while Conference Dinner in edas is a specific meal event that takes place during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

TestOnlyTopic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited_Talk_Abstract is a type of document (abstract) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
'adjusted By' relates a Bid to a Reviewer in the cmt ontology, while 'pay' relates a Person to Money in the iasted ontology. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' contrasts with 'Paper Abstract', denoting the complete manuscript of a paper. In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' contrasts with other paper types (Demo, Poster, Industrial, Workshop), denoting a standard research track submission. While a regular paper is typically submitted as a full version, the two classes partition papers along different axes (completeness vs. track type) and are not equivalent. They overlap but neither strictly subsumes the other.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the overall conference event/organization (with properties like accepts submissions, has members, dates). In iasted, 'Conference activity' is a sub-event or scheduled item within a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture, registration), as shown by its children and parent 'Activity'. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the whole conference, the other is an activity taking place during it.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Person (via Conference Member), representing specifically those who author papers. In ekaw, Person is the top-level class for all people, with Paper Author as a child. Thus cmt:Author is subsumed by ekaw:Person; the true equivalent in ekaw would be Paper Author.

Late Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered late (child of Conference Participant), while Program Committee member is an organizer responsible for reviewing papers (child of Organizator). They represent entirely different roles in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while 'Workshop' is a type of academic event. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while 'reviewes' links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they review. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a specific deadline date. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
In ekaw, 'Demo Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper', while in sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers. Therefore, ekaw's Demo Paper is subsumed by sigkdd's Paper.

Both properties express where an event/conference takes place, but they differ in domain (Conference vs Event) and range (Country vs Location). 'heldIn' is more general in both domain and range, so the two are related rather than equivalent.

'follows' in confOf expresses a temporal or sequential ordering between administrative events (one event follows another), while 'hasEvent' in ekaw is a mereological/containment relation linking an event to its sub-events. They have completely different semantics.
Paper is a document/artefact class in ekaw, while Author of paper is a person/role class in sigkdd. They represent fundamentally different concepts (a thing vs. the person who creates it).
A Workshop Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while a Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent the concept of a Conference in the conference-organisation domain. Although Ontology B places it under Working event and Ontology A has different children (Conference volume), their intended instances coincide as the main conference entity.
Paper is a document/submission in the conference domain, while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a broad class that includes not only written contributions but also Invited talk, Poster, Presentation, and Regular author. Conference Paper in ekaw (Ontology B) specifically refers to paper documents (with children like Camera Ready Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). Therefore, Conference contribution subsumes Conference Paper, as papers are one type of conference contribution, but the former also covers non-paper contributions like talks and posters.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (activity) for submitting contributions, while 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a document item. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while has_workshops relates a Conference volume to its workshops (events). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Presenter is a person role (subclass of Conference Participant), while Lecture is an event/activity (subclass of Conference activity). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
Talk Event is a type of conference event (an activity), while Author is a person role. They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic classification), while is_made_from links an Item to another Item (composition/derivation). These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Student registration fee is a monetary fee for student registration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Receiving manuscript' is an activity (the process of receiving papers), while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a point in time by which papers must be submitted). They are related concepts in the paper submission workflow but are not equivalent, as one is an event/activity and the other is a temporal constraint.

Property A (isReviewedBy) links a Paper to the people who review it, while property B (reviewWrittenBy) links a Review document to the person who wrote it. They have different domains (Paper vs Review) and relate different entities, though they are conceptually related in the reviewing process.
isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while is_present relates a Person to a Time (temporal presence). Different ranges and different semantics.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'eventOnList' relates an event to a publication medium (programme brochure or website) where it is listed. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Hotel presenter is a type of person (Delegate) who presents from a hotel, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.

Reject Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a rating/score value), while Neutral Review in ekaw is a subclass of Review (the review document itself). They represent different concepts: one is a rating category, the other is a type of review. Additionally, 'reject' and 'neutral' convey different sentiments.

Conference's 'Committee member' is a general class for members of any committee (with children Chair and Co-chair), while ekaw's 'OC Member' specifically denotes an Organizing Committee member. Thus, OC Member is a more specific concept subsumed by the broader Committee member class.
Dining Place is a location for eating, while Van is a type of transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Sponzorship in iasted is a general class for sponsorship (a type of Money), while Platinum Supporter in sigkdd is a specific tier/level of sponsor. The general Sponzorship subsumes Platinum Supporter, but since the task asks about these two specific classes, they are related (one is a specific kind of the other) rather than equivalent.
City is a geographical location class, while Conference is an event/organization class. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to the conference (e.g., authors, speakers). Conference Hiker in Ontology B is a subclass of Delegate under Place > Building > Conference building, likely referring to an attendee or participant type. They have different hierarchies, different parent classes (Person vs Delegate/Place), and different intended meanings.
Topic in edas represents a subject area of a paper or conference, while Person in sigkdd represents a human participant. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (the act of authoring a review), while hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating (a score assigned to a paper). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper in cmt is a document/artefact (subclass of Document), while Individual Presentation in ekaw is an event where a paper is presented (subclass of Scientific Event). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place in edas is a specific type of place for meetings, while Building in iasted is a broader physical structure that contains various sub-types (conference building, hotel, etc.) and has siblings like Session room and Conference hall. They overlap conceptually as physical locations but are not equivalent; Building is more general and includes non-meeting structures.

In cmt, Administrator is a system manager who assigns reviewers and accepts papers, while Reviewer is a separate sibling class. In confOf, Member PC (commented as 'Reviewer') reviews contributions. The confOf ontology has its own separate Administrator class as a sibling of Member PC. Thus cmt:Administrator and confOf:Member_PC are distinct roles.
'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members, while 'organised By' relates an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URL (anyURI), while Name_of_conference links a Conference to its name (string). These represent different attributes of a conference and are not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Presenter university is a physical place/building. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Member PC in confOf is a program committee member (reviewer), while Session Chair in edas is a person who chairs a session. These are distinct roles in conference organization. The proper alignment for Member PC would be TPC Member or Reviewer in edas.
hasKeyword links a Contribution to a keyword string, while has_amount_of links Money to an integer amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Rejection is a decision outcome regarding a paper submission, while Excursion is a social event at a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment relation), while 'partOf' is a generic mereological part-whole relation. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.

Both properties express a location/situated-in relationship, but they differ in domain and range. 'has City' links Organization or Person to a City, while 'is situated in' links Building, City, or Place to Building, City, Place, or State. They overlap conceptually (both relate entities to locations) but are not equivalent due to different domains and ranges.

Rejection in cmt is a decision outcome (subclass of Decision), while Renting in iasted is an activity before the conference (subclass of Activity before conference). They are entirely different concepts.

Item in iasted represents physical objects (equipment, documents, vehicles), while Person in sigkdd represents human participants (listeners, speakers, organizers). These are entirely different concepts.

A 'Short paper' in confOf is a type of Contribution (a full but shorter research paper), while an 'Abstract' in sigkdd is a brief summary document. They represent different kinds of scholarly artefacts with different intended instances.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Conference www in Conference ontology is a document/web resource with a URL. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while Property B is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (e.g., instructions, announcements), while 'Bronze Supporter' is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Invited speaker is a person role (a type of conference contributor), while Reception is a social event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members (committee -> member), while Property B links a Chair to the committee they chair (person -> committee). They have different domains, ranges, and directions, so they are unrelated.

readByReviewer links a Paper directly to a Reviewer (the person who reads it), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the review document/artefact). They model related but distinct aspects of the reviewing process: one targets the agent, the other the output. Hence they are related, not equivalent.
hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g., sub-events), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks, while 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place and Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
