Accepted contribution in Ontology A is a specific state of a submitted paper (one that has been reviewed and accepted), whereas Paper in sigkdd is a general class for any paper document. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent; Accepted contribution is more specific than Paper.

'is a starting date' denotes the beginning of an important date period, while 'done till' denotes a deadline (end date). These are semantically opposite temporal properties and do not represent the same relation.
Tutorial in ekaw is a type of Event (a presentation session), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a type of Person (a role). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Document in cmt is a general class for written artefacts (with children Paper and Review), while Review expertise in Conference refers to the level of expertise a reviewer has regarding a submitted contribution. These are entirely different concepts.

hasStreet captures a street address (domain: Contact Information), while E-mail captures an email address (domain: Person). These are entirely different contact attributes with different domains and semantics.

Tutorial and Workshop are distinct types of conference events. In both ontologies they appear as siblings (e.g., confOf lists Tutorial and Workshop as siblings under Working event), confirming they represent different concepts rather than equivalent ones.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to an integer cost amount, while Name_of_sponsor links Sponzor to a string name. They describe entirely different attributes (cost vs. name) with different ranges, so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (someone participating in the conference), while Conference Banquet in ekaw is a Social Event (a banquet held during the conference). They are entirely different concepts.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting people to participate, while a 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event where reviewing results are made available to authors. They represent entirely different concepts (a document vs. an event) with different purposes in the conference domain.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a specific subtype of 'Contribution', alongside 'Paper' and 'Poster'. In edas, 'Paper' is the general class for all submitted papers (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). Therefore, confOf's Short paper is a more specific concept subsumed by edas's general Paper class.

Property A (date) has domain Conference and range date, representing the date of a conference. Property B (starts on) has domain Event and range string, representing the start date of an event. While Conference is likely a subclass of Event in confOf, 'date' is a general temporal property whereas 'starts on' specifically denotes a start time. They overlap semantically but differ in specificity, domain scope, and range type, making them related rather than equivalent.

'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'has an abstract' links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (indicating content). These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express completely different semantics.

hasCostCurrency records the currency of a sponsorship cost, while Name_of_sponsor records the name of the sponsor. These are entirely different attributes despite both having string ranges and sponsorship-related domains.

Both properties link an artefact/event to the person responsible for it (giving a presentation vs preparing an item). However, 'is given by' specifically denotes delivering a presentation by an active conference participant, while 'is prepared by' denotes authoring/preparing any item by a person. They overlap in intent but differ in domain and range specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Conference Session is a type of event (a time-bounded scientific session), while Session room is a type of place (a physical location where sessions occur). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Both properties express the same relation: a paper/item is written by an author/person. In the conference domain, 'Item' in iasted corresponds to 'Paper' in edas, and 'Person' corresponds to 'Author'. The direction (written work -> writer) is identical.

Both classes represent a person who participates in a conference. They share the same parent (Person) and have analogous children representing various participant roles (e.g., chairs, registered participants). 'Participant' in confOf and 'Conference Participant' in ekaw denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Multi author Volume is a document class (a collection of papers/proceedings), while Author is a person class (someone who writes papers). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country, while obtain links a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property mapping Conference or Person to a string name, while property B is an object property mapping Person to Item (obtain). They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics entirely.
University is an organization where scholars study, while Textual Review Question is a type of review question. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value (representing a deadline), while Entity B is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (representing the act of submission). They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Workshop Paper in ekaw is a specific type of academic paper (subclass of Paper). Document in iasted is a broad category including forms, invitation letters, payment documents, etc. They are not equivalent; Workshop Paper would at best be related to Submission or Publication in iasted, but not to the general Document class.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper (subclass of Decision), while University is an organization type where scholars study. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (date) has domain Conference and represents the date of a conference, while property B (Date) has domain Deadline and represents the date of a deadline. Different domains and different intended meanings make them unrelated.

Both classes represent the chair of the organizing committee for a conference. In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a type of Chairman and Conference Member; in ekaw, 'OC Chair' (Organizing Committee Chair) is a type of OC Member. These denote the same role in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person representing someone who serves on a conference committee. In Ontology B, 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a subclass of Registration fee (under Fee), representing a type of registration cost for SIGKDD members. These are entirely different concepts (a person role vs. a fee category) and are unrelated.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Powerline Transmission Topic in edas is a specific subject Topic. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while hasEvent links an Event to another Event. These properties relate fundamentally different kinds of entities and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

Decision represents the outcome of a paper review (acceptance/rejection), while Fee represents monetary charges (registration/sponsor fees). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

The property 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (indicating who entered conference details), while 'has important dates' links a Conference volume to Important dates. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a conference contribution (a document), while Best Student Paper Award is an award given to a paper. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class under Person that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Author in Ontology B is specifically someone who authors papers (a kind of Speaker/Delegate). Thus Conference contributor subsumes Author, as Author corresponds more closely to Regular author (a child of Conference contributor) rather than the broader contributor class itself.

Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Single Level Conference is a type of Conference event. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.

Banquet (confOf) is a specific type of social event involving a meal, while Meal Event (edas) is a broader class of non-academic events that includes meals (with Conference Dinner as a child). They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent since Meal Event is more general than Banquet.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a version/format of a paper (the abstract portion), while Industrial Paper in ekaw is a category/type of paper (submitted to an industrial track). They represent orthogonal classifications and are unrelated.

Information for participants is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Both properties relate an abstract/paper to its presentation form, but A links Abstract to Paper/Poster/Presentation (structural part-of), while B links Abstract/Paper specifically to Individual Presentation (presentation mode). They overlap in the paper-to-presentation aspect but differ in domain/range scope and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Microelectronics Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Transport vehicle is a physical item used for transportation. They are completely unrelated concepts.

confOf's 'Submission event' is a specific type of administrative event for submitting contributions, while ekaw's 'Event' is a broad top-level class covering scientific and social events. Submission event is strictly more specific than Event, so it is subsumed by it.
confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while ekaw:Industrial_Paper is a specific subtype of Paper. Therefore confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Industrial_Paper.
External Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, while Paper is a document submitted to a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class of persons contributing to a conference (including authors, speakers, active participants). Listener (B) is a specific type of delegate who only listens (does not present or contribute). Thus A subsumes B in the general sense that a listener could be considered a contributor/participant, but more precisely A is much broader than B. Since Listener is strictly narrower than Conference contributor, A subsumes B.
Property A gives the first name of a Person, while property B gives a keyword of a Contribution (paper). They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes; they are completely unrelated.

Reviewed contribution (A) is a paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Review (B) is the review document itself. They are distinct but related concepts; A's instances are papers and B's instances are reviews of those papers.

Both classes represent the final camera-ready version of an accepted paper/contribution for a conference. Despite different hierarchical paths (Conference A models the lifecycle stages explicitly while ekaw models document types), their intended instances coincide.

In confOf, 'Regular' is a subtype of Participant (a regular/non-student attendee), while in ekaw, 'Student' represents student participants. These are distinct, disjoint categories of conference attendees, not equivalent concepts.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution, alongside Poster and Short paper), while ekaw:Submitted_Paper specifically denotes a paper that has been submitted (a subclass of Paper in ekaw). They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent because Submitted_Paper carries the additional 'submitted' status constraint, whereas confOf:Paper does not.

Property A is a datatype property linking a review preference to an integer degree value, while Property B is an object property linking a Review to a Possible Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

startDate is specifically the start date of a Conference, while is_dated_on is a more general date property for an Activity. They overlap in relating event-like entities to dateTime values but differ in specificity and domain scope.

In Ontology A, 'Extended abstract' is a type of regular conference contribution (a sibling of Paper), and it has 'Abstract' as a child class. In Ontology B, 'Abstract' is a direct subclass of Document and a sibling of Paper and Review. The concept 'Abstract' in sigkdd likely corresponds to the child class 'Abstract' under 'Extended abstract' in Conference, not to 'Extended abstract' itself. An extended abstract is a specific kind of submission distinct from a plain abstract, so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A refers specifically to an abstract submission date (domain: Important dates), while property B refers to a general submission deadline (domain: Call). An abstract submission date is a specific type of submission deadline, so they are related but not equivalent.

Conference Paper in ekaw is a type of document/paper submitted to a conference, while Conference in sigkdd is the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates. These are entirely different concepts.
Reception is a social event (like a welcome gathering), while Registration is the administrative act of registering for a conference. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property relating physical locations (Building/City/Place) to other locations or states. Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string representing the city name. They differ in domain, range type, and semantic meaning.

Property A links a Topic to a Conference part (indicating what topics a conference part covers), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents a document). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Property A relates a Chair to a Committee (committee chair role), while Property B relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a document/artefact submitted to a conference (e.g., paper, poster, presentation), while Conference in Ontology B is an event type (a kind of working event). These are entirely different concepts.

The properties have completely different domains (Conference vs Paper), ranges (Administrator vs Possible Reviewer), and semantics (entering review criteria vs assigning a reviewer to a paper). They are unrelated.

logoURL refers to the URL of a conference's logo (anyURI), while startDate refers to the start date and time of a conference (dateTime). These are entirely different properties with different meanings and ranges.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer, while search links ACM SIGKDD to a Sponsor. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract (a document part), while property B links an accepted paper to a presentation event. These relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution (a document/artefact), with siblings Poster and Short paper. In edas, Paper Presentation is a subclass of Academic Event (an event/activity), linked to an Accepted Paper via the 'related To Paper' property. One denotes the written artefact, the other denotes the presentation event of that artefact; they are related but not equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), representing the overall conference gathering. In iasted, Lecture is a specific Conference activity (a talk/presentation) occurring within a conference, with children like Plenary lecture and Session. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the event itself, the other is an activity within it.
Property A captures a person's first name (string), while property B indicates whether a participant registered early (boolean). They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Invited speaker (Ontology A) is a Person who gives a talk, while Invited Talk (Ontology B) is an Event (a presentation). They are related (the speaker delivers the talk) but not equivalent since one is a person and the other is an event.
Working event is a type of conference-related activity (e.g., tutorial, workshop), while Hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links 'Important dates' to a 'Conference volume', while property B links an 'Event' to a 'Location'. They have entirely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relationships in the conference domain.

'writes' is a specific authoring relation from Author to Contribution (paper), while 'hasRelatedDocument' is a broad association from various entities (events, persons, etc.) to Document. They differ in domain, range specificity, and semantic intent.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Proceedings in ekaw is a subclass of Document representing a published collection of papers. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an academic gathering), while Trip city in iasted is a type of City (a geographical location). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Presenter university is a building affiliated with a presenter (an academic institution), while Conference hall is a venue where conference sessions take place. These are conceptually distinct types of places in the conference domain.

Both properties link a Paper to a reviewer-like entity, but they differ in semantics and range. 'readByReviewer' (cmt) indicates that a specific Reviewer has read the paper, while 'hasReviewer' (ekaw) links a paper to a Possible_Reviewer who may be assigned or eligible to review it. The ranges (Reviewer vs Possible_Reviewer) and the intended meaning (actual reading vs potential assignment) are not identical, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Conference Member is a Person role (someone participating in the conference), while Conference Session is an Event (a scheduled part of the conference program). They are entirely different concepts.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Management) while B is a state related to a sponsor. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (parent of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference. In edas, Organizational Meeting is a specific type of Academic Event within a conference (sibling of Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop). These denote fundamentally different concepts: the whole conference vs. a single organizational meeting session.

'has authors' links a conference document to its author(s), while 'is signed by' links an item to a person who signs it. Authorship and signing are distinct relations with different semantics in the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where meetings occur, while Conference Trip is a social event (subclass of Social Event). They belong to entirely different categories (place vs. event) and are unrelated.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks, while 'has Member' relates a Conference to Persons. The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts (Track vs Person), so these properties are unrelated.

Regular contribution in Ontology A is a type of conference document/contribution (with children like Paper and Extended abstract), whereas Talk Event in Ontology B is a type of conference event (with children like Closing Talk and Welcome Talk). They belong to different conceptual categories (document vs. event) and are unrelated.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (an action of ending/closing a review), while isReviewedBy relates a Paper to a person who reviewed it (e.g., Reviewer, TPC Member). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties describe an action by a person/author involving a document/item, but 'obtain' (to get/receive) and 'submit' (to hand in) have different semantics and directions of transfer. They are related as both involve Person-Document interactions in the conference domain, but are not equivalent.

hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and types.

Workshop is a type of working event (a session or meeting), while Author cd proceedings included is a role for a person (an author whose work appears on a CD proceedings). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties capture a paper submission deadline as a date/dateTime value, but they differ in domain (Important dates vs Conference) and specificity ('full paper' vs generic 'paper'). They are related but not equivalent.

Committee in Ontology A is an organizational body (with subtypes like Organizing committee, Program committee), while Participant in Ontology B is a person attending the conference (subclass of Person). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both Presenter (ekaw) and Speaker (iasted) represent a conference participant who presents or speaks at the event. In ekaw, Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant with Invited Speaker as a child; in iasted, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate. Despite different modeling choices for children, their intended instances—people who present/speak at the conference—coincide.
Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Session Chair is a role played by a person. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (acceptedBy) links a Paper to an Administrator who accepted it, while property B (relatedToPaper) links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

earlyRegistration is a datatype property indicating whether a participant registered early (domain Participant, range boolean), while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, and range.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while is_paid_for relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (reviewer assignment/bidding), while Property B links an Author to a Paper (paper submission). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Important dates' is a class representing a collection of deadline dates that belongs to a Conference volume. In Ontology B (edas), 'Conference' represents the conference event itself, with date properties like paperDueOn and endDate attached directly to it. They are not equivalent: one models deadlines as a separate entity, the other models the conference as an event. They are related because both deal with conference scheduling information.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while is_present_in links a Person to a Place/Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has Been Assigned' in cmt links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while 'has Part' in ekaw is a generic mereological part-whole relation. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.

Meta Review in cmt is a type of review document (a review written about other reviews), whereas Reviewed contribution in Conference is a submitted paper/contribution that has received at least one review. They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a review artefact, the other is the reviewed paper.

Conference Session in ekaw is a type of event (a scheduled session within a conference), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a type of place (a physical venue). They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.
Paper is a submitted document (child of Document) in the conference review process, while Award is a prize given to authors (e.g., Best Paper Award). They are entirely different concepts.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the complete manuscript of a submitted paper (a document artefact), whereas Cd proceening in iasted refers to a CD-based publication medium containing proceedings. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers), while Property B relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (being the reviewer of a paper). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (direct child of Person), while Invited Speaker in ekaw is a specific role under Presenter, which is under Conference Participant. An invited speaker is a kind of attendee/participant, but Attendee is much broader and not equivalent to Invited Speaker. They are related as overlapping concepts in the participation hierarchy.

Property A relates a Co-chair to a Committee (committee membership/leadership), while Property B relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasAuthor (Paper -> Author) and write (Person -> Item) are inverse properties: hasAuthor links a paper to its author, while write links an author (Person) to their work (Item). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

In confOf, 'Assistant' is a sibling of 'Member PC' under Person, indicating it is a distinct role (likely an administrative or support assistant). In sigkdd, 'Program Committee member' is a specific organizing role. These are different concepts within the conference domain.

Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's past publications (a type of personal history), while Abstract is a summary document of a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (child of Person), while Tutorial Chair in ekaw is a specific organizational role responsible for tutorials (child of Conference Participant and PC Member). They are not equivalent; Attendee is much more general and does not specifically denote a tutorial chair.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the complete manuscript of a paper (as opposed to an abstract), typically submitted during the review process. Published Paper in edas refers to a paper that has been formally published (e.g., in proceedings). These represent different stages/aspects of a paper's lifecycle and are not equivalent, though they are related as both are subtypes of Paper.

In ekaw, 'Proceedings Publisher' is an Organisation (an agent that publishes proceedings), whereas in iasted, 'Cd proceening' is a Publication (a physical/digital item, specifically a CD containing proceedings). One is an organization/agent and the other is an artifact/publication, so they are unrelated.
Property A relates a Committee to its Chair (membership/leadership), while Property B relates a Call to the person who initiated it. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf (Ontology B), 'Short paper' and 'Poster' are distinct sibling subclasses of Contribution, indicating they represent different types of submissions. In Ontology A, 'Poster' is a subclass of Conference contribution representing a poster presentation. Since the two ontologies distinguish posters from short papers as separate concepts, these classes are not equivalent but are related as different specific types of conference contributions.

Both classes represent a submitted paper in the conference domain. They share the same parent (Document), have analogous children (versions/states of papers), and similar properties linking them to authors, reviewers, and topics. Despite minor differences in sibling classes across ontologies, their intended instances coincide.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the overall conference gathering), while Video presentation in iasted is a specific type of presentation activity within a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A ('has a volume') is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer (volume number), while Property B ('abstract') links a Contribution to a string (the abstract text). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Topic is a subject area of a conference or paper. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the complete version of a paper (as opposed to an abstract), while Poster Paper in ekaw refers to a paper intended for poster presentation. These are orthogonal classifications: one distinguishes document completeness, the other distinguishes presentation format. They do not denote the same concept.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of 'Conference applicant' (someone who applied and registered), while confOf's 'Participant' is a broader class for anyone participating in the conference (with children Member, Regular, Student). They overlap conceptually as people attending/participating, but are not strictly equivalent since Participant includes roles beyond just registered applicants.
Invited Speaker is a subclass of Person (a role), while Presenter city is a subclass of City (a location). They are entirely different concepts.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Tip is a monetary gratuity (subclass of Money). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
The two properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'has members' links a Committee to its Committee members, while 'held In' links an Event to a Location. They are unrelated.

Both properties represent a starting date (datatype properties with date/dateTime ranges), but they have different domains: 'Important dates' in ontology A vs 'Conference' in ontology B. They are related as they both capture start-date semantics, but are not equivalent due to differing domain classes.

Both properties express a whole-to-part (hasPart) relationship in the conference domain. However, 'has parts' in Ontology A has domain Conference volume and range Conference part, while 'inverse of part Of 7' in ekaw has range Event. Since Conference volume is not equivalent to Event and Conference part is not equivalent to Event, they are related but not equivalent.

reviewOfPaper relates a Review to a Paper (the subject of the review), while write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
An 'Invited speaker' is a person who gives a talk at the conference, while a 'Non speaker' is explicitly a delegate who does not speak. These are disjoint concepts.

A is a research topic related to computer networks switching, while B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer). They share the word 'Computer' but denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a complete paper document (subclass of Paper), while Slide Set is a set of presentation slides (subclass of Document). They are distinct types of documents with different intended instances.

Organization in confOf represents an institution (company, university) that employs people, while Sponsorship in edas represents a financial support arrangement (e.g., travel grant). They are fundamentally different concepts; an Organization may provide a Sponsorship, but they are not equivalent or hierarchically related.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a registrant who paid late), while Published Paper is a subclass of Document/Paper. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes are named 'Conference' and represent the same core concept in the conference-organisation domain: a scholarly conference event. They share similar properties (hasName/has Name, hasTopic/has Topic) and serve as the central organizing entity in their respective ontologies. Differences in children reflect modeling granularity rather than conceptual divergence.

Ontology A's Person is the top-level class for all people in the conference domain. Ontology B's Possible Reviewer is a subclass of Person (as shown by its path 'Person > Possible Reviewer') representing specifically those persons who may serve as reviewers. Therefore, A's Person subsumes B's Possible Reviewer.

'isWrittenBy' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'is_given_by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (presentation/delivery). These are semantically different relations in the conference domain.

In ontology A, 'Registeered applicant' is a subclass of 'Conference applicant' (under Person), representing someone who has registered for the conference. In ontology B, 'Delegate' represents a registered conference participant (with children like Speaker, Listener, Session chair). While both denote people who have registered/are attending the conference, 'Delegate' in iasted covers all attendees broadly, whereas 'Registeered applicant' in Conference is specifically an applicant who has registered (and has a child 'Paid applicant'). They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; 'Delegate' is broader and more aligned with a general attendee/participant concept.

Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event (an activity), while Conference Proceedings is a type of document (a publication). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.
Workshop is a type of working event (a session at a conference), while Presenter state is a status/state of a presenter. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In EKAW, OC Chair (Organizing Committee Chair) is a subclass of OC Member, distinct from the Program Committee. In SIGKDD, Program Chair is a sibling of Organizing Committee member, indicating it leads the Program Committee rather than the Organizing Committee. These are related leadership roles but not equivalent, as organizing and program committees have different responsibilities in conference organization.
Paper in cmt is a submitted document/artefact, while Computer Networks Topic in edas is a subject area or topic classification. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country (spatial/geographic relation), while is_present links a Person to a Time (temporal relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties are inverses of each other: 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution (Paper), while 'isWrittenBy' has domain Paper and range Author. Per the alignment guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

Review (cmt) is a document evaluating a paper, while Payment document (iasted) is a financial instrument for payment. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

Meeting Room Place is a venue for meetings/conference sessions, while Double hotel room is an accommodation type. They are siblings under different sub-hierarchies of Place (meeting vs accommodation) and denote entirely different concepts.
In cmt, Conference Member is a superclass of Author (Author is listed as a child). In iasted, Author is a specific role under Speaker/Delegate. Therefore, Conference Member subsumes Author.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event (a phase in the conference process), while a 'Program Committee' is a group of people (a committee). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities and are unrelated.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Contribution co author is a class representing a co-author of a conference contribution (a person role), while Conference in confOf is a type of working event. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a conference-related entity to people associated with it, but they differ in domain (Conference vs Conference Event) and range (Conference Member, typically committee/organizing members, vs Attendee/Person). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.
Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.), while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts (days, deadlines). These are entirely different domain concepts.

confOf 'Member PC' is a general program committee member (comment: Reviewer), while ekaw 'SC Member' is a specific subclass of 'PC Member' (Steering Committee Member). Thus the confOf class subsumes the ekaw class.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Presenter university is a physical place/building. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent the same core concept in the conference-organisation domain: a Conference event. Despite confOf placing it under Working event and cmt listing many administrative properties, their intended instances (the conferences themselves) coincide.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a structural part-of relationship), while property B links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise (an agentive action). The domains, ranges, and semantic directions differ fundamentally; they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relation.

Trip is a social event (excursion) during a conference, while Receiving manuscript is an administrative activity before the conference involving paper submission handling. They are entirely different concepts.
Review Rating represents an evaluation score for a paper, while Place represents a physical location. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document indicating a conflict of interest, while has_authors relates a Conference document to a Person indicating authorship. These are entirely different relations with different semantics and directions.

Property A ('issues') links a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while property B ('holded by') links a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Country in confOf represents a nation (used for organizational/person affiliation), while Place in iasted represents a physical venue or location (building, room, hall) where activities occur. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Entity A is a specific type of registration fee (for author attendees booking) in iasted, while Entity B is the general Registration fee class in sigkdd. A is subsumed by B.

manuscriptDueOn is a specific deadline property for paper submissions (domain: Conference), while is_dated_on is a general date property for activities (domain: Activity). They differ in both domain and semantic specificity.

endDate is a datatype property on Conference indicating when the conference ends, while done_till is a datatype property on Deadline indicating when a deadline passes. They have different domains (Conference vs Deadline) and different semantic meanings (event end date vs submission/action deadline), so they are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties with range int representing a monetary amount, but they apply to entirely different domains: hasCostAmount is for Sponsorship (cost of sponsoring), while Price is for Registration fee (cost of registering). They describe different concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.
hasStreet refers to a street address while hasCity refers to a city; they are distinct address components with different domains and meanings.

Associated Chair is a leadership role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Early paid applicant is a registration/payment status of a conference attendee. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Coffee break is a conference activity/event. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to structural subdivisions of a conference such as tracks, tutorials, and workshops. Conference Session in edas typically refers to a time-bounded presentation session within the program. While both are sub-events or components of a conference, they represent different granularities and concepts (a track contains multiple sessions), so they are related but not equivalent.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they wrote, while topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper that covers it. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop is a type of working event (a meeting/session), while Conference Proceedings is a type of document (a published volume). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Co author is a subclass of Author representing someone who co-writes a paper, while Reviewer represents someone who reviews papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

'has a degree' is a datatype property linking a review preference to an integer (likely a degree level), while 'study At' is an object property linking a scholar to a university. They have different domains, ranges, property types, and meanings.

In ekaw, Person is a top-level class with children including Conference Participant, Paper Author, etc. In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker, which is a subclass of Person. Thus ekaw:Person is strictly more general than sigkdd:Author (ekaw:Person subsumes sigkdd:Author).

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person/ContactInformation to a string (email address), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

'speak in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place and Time, while 'Name of conference' is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Academia Organization is a type of organization. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

adjustedBy links a Bid to the Reviewer who adjusted it, while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer assigned to review it. Different domains (Bid vs Paper), different ranges (Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer), and different semantics (bid adjustment vs paper-reviewer assignment).
Event in ekaw represents a conference-related occurrence (scientific or social), while City in iasted represents a geographical location. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A ('is the 1th part of') is a specific part-of relation restricted to Abstract as domain and Paper/Poster/Presentation as range. Property B ('partOf') in ekaw is a general part-of property with unspecified domain and range. Thus A is a specialization (subsumed by) the more general B.

Organization in confOf refers to institutions like companies and universities that employ people, while Committee in sigkdd refers to conference-specific groups (program committee, organizing committee). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference with range int indicating the number of reviews per paper, while remark is a datatype property on Contribution (paper) with range string for textual notes. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Travel Grant is a type of sponsorship/funding. They are entirely different concepts.
Topic represents a subject area of a paper or conference, while Money represents financial amounts such as fees and sponsorships. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
heldIn relates an Event to a Location (where it takes place), while write relates a Person to an Item (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (reviewer assignment), while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (who presents the document). They are unrelated.

'studyAt' relates a Scholar to a University (academic affiliation), while 'is_given_to' relates an Item to a Person (transfer/assignment). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Workshop is a type of Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), representing a full workshop event. In ekaw, Demo Session is a type of Session (sibling of Workshop Session, Poster Session, etc.), representing a session for demonstrations. These are distinct concepts; notably, ekaw has its own 'Workshop Session' which would be closer to confOf's Workshop. A Demo Session is not equivalent or hierarchically related to a Workshop.

Workshop Session is a type of event/session in a conference, while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the program. They are entirely different concepts.

'has a committee chair' relates a Committee to its Chair, while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
Presentation is a conference activity (event) in iasted, while Organizator is a person role in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

adjustBid is a specific property linking a Reviewer to a Bid (preference for reviewing a paper), while give is a general property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. These represent fundamentally different relations in the conference domain.

'has a name' is a datatype property for naming entities (conferences, publishers, topics, etc.), while 'location' specifies where an event is held. They have different semantics, domains, and purposes.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members, while property B links a Committee to its Committee members. The domains (Conference vs Committee) and ranges (Conference Member vs Committee member) differ significantly, so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.
forEvent links a Call to an Academic Event, while scientificallyOrganisedBy links something to an Academic Institution. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (isLocationOf) relates a Place to a Conference Event, indicating where an event takes place. Property B (hold) relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference, indicating who organizes/holds the conference. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paid_applicant in Conference is a person who has registered and paid for the conference (a specific kind of participant). Participant in confOf is a general class for anyone attending/participating in the conference, with children like Regular, Student, Member. Every Paid applicant is a Participant, but not every Participant is necessarily a Paid applicant (e.g., invited members or those who haven't paid yet), so Paid_applicant is subsumed by Participant.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee for member registration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Banquet is a social dining event during the conference, while Full day tour is an excursion activity after the conference. Both are social/recreational activities associated with a conference but they denote different specific events, so they are related but not equivalent.

'has Conflict Of Interest' denotes a conflict-of-interest relationship between a person and a document (e.g., for review assignment), while 'contributes' denotes authorship or contribution of a document by a person. These are semantically distinct relations.

A Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, while an Invited Speaker is a person invited to give a talk at the conference. Although both are subclasses of Speaker in their respective ontologies, they represent entirely different roles with no semantic overlap.
Closing Talk is a type of conference event (a talk), while Listener is a type of person who attends. They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B (reviewWrittenBy) relates a Review to a Possible Reviewer. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics: one is about authoring a paper, the other about writing a review. They are unrelated.
Both are datatype properties with identical domain (Person) and range (string), representing the email address of a person. They are semantically equivalent.
hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (for papers), while search links ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (sponsor). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

confOf's 'Working event' is a subclass of Event with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop. ekaw's 'Event' is the top-level class encompassing both Scientific Event and Social Event. Thus confOf:Working_event is strictly more specific than ekaw:Event (which also includes social events), so Working_event is subsumed by Event.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Cryptography Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the top-level chair of a conference, while OC Member (ekaw) is a general member of the Organizing Committee. In ekaw, the equivalent of Conference Chair would be OC Chair, which is a child of OC Member. Thus Conference Chair and OC Member are distinct concepts: one is a specific leadership role, the other is a broader committee membership class.

Tutorial is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference hall is a type of place (a venue). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
'One conference day' is a temporal concept (a single day of the conference), while 'Organizing Committee member' is a person role involved in organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated.

Both 'Associated Chair' in cmt and 'Co chair' in Conference refer to the same role: a co-chair or associate chair who assists the main chair in organizing a conference or committee. Property A relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (invited by), while Property B relates a Paper to a Review (hasReview). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A relates a committee member to a committee (membership), while property B relates an author to a contribution (authorship). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Sponsorship is a class representing financial support (with children like Travel Grant), while Currency represents a monetary unit. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Call for paper is a type of conference document (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Microelectronics Topic is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to a camera-ready submission date, while Property B is an object property linking a paper to its presentation format. They are entirely unrelated in domain, range, and semantics.

hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject matter), while volumeContainsPaper links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
'writtenBy' denotes authorship (Contribution -> Author), while 'is sent by' denotes a submission/sending action (Item -> Person). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.

Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (indicating committee membership/assignment), while Property B links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference (indicating who holds/organizes it). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A (locationOf) relates a Location to an Event (i.e., an event takes place at a location), while Property B (is_present_in) relates a Person to a Place or Time (i.e., a person is present at a place/time). The domains differ fundamentally (Location vs Person), so they are unrelated.
Early paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a type of conference attendee), while Fee for extra trip is a subclass of Money/Fee (a monetary charge). They are entirely different concepts.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while ekaw:Workshop_Paper is a specific subtype of Paper intended for workshops. Therefore, confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Workshop_Paper.
hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasMember relates a Conference to its member Persons, while is_prepared_by relates an Item (e.g., a paper) to the Person who prepared it. Different domains and different semantics.

minChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (minimum number of choices), while End_of_conference links a Conference to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasCo-author relates a Paper to a Co-author (authorship relation), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Accept Rating is a type of review rating (a value/outcome), while Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Industrial Session is a type of event/session at a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a website/URL resource), while Main office is a physical place. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasRating links a paper to its review rating (a quality score), while hasReviewer links a paper to a possible reviewer (a person). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), representing the overall conference gathering. Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, announcements, reviews, contributions, etc. Abstract in ekaw is a specific type of document (a summary of a paper or presentation). Call for paper is a type of conference document used to solicit submissions, while Antennas Topic is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Rejected contribution is a class of papers/contributions that were rejected after review, while Accept Rating is a type of review rating indicating acceptance. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (contribution vs. rating) and are unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of working event at a conference, while an Author information form is a document/form used for registration purposes. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Review in cmt is a document (an evaluation of a paper), while Call For Papers in edas is a type of call soliciting submissions. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Assistant in confOf is a role under Person (likely an administrative or support assistant), while Two Level Conference in edas is a type of Conference. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while publisherOf relates an Organisation to publication artefacts (Flyer, Web Site, etc.). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'authorOf' relates a Person to a Document (authored paper), while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (e.g., giving a presentation). These are semantically different relations in the conference domain.

Entity A is a class representing a type of conference contributor/author (a person role), while Entity B is a class representing a specific registration fee amount for author attendees who want a CD. Author is a person who writes papers, while Workshop is a conference event/part. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational committee/group. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review (domain: Reviewed contribution, range: Review), while property B links an author to a contribution they wrote (domain: Author, range: Contribution). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Time is a temporal concept (with children like Deadline, Conference days). They are completely unrelated.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, members). Camera ready contribution is a type of accepted paper/contribution (a document), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'is Initiated By' relates a Call to the person who initiated it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (maximum number of choices), while endDate links a Conference to a dateTime representing the end date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A describes the volume number of conference proceedings (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int), while Property B describes the city where a conference is held (domain: Conference, range: string). They refer to entirely different concepts and have different domains and ranges.
Property A links papers/posters/presentations to their abstracts, while property B links the ACM SIGKDD organization to deadlines. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Chairman is a broad class with children including Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair. In Conference, Co chair is a specific role (co-chair) that is a sibling of Chair under Committee member. The cmt 'Associated Chair' likely corresponds to 'Co chair', making the general 'Chairman' class broader than and overlapping with 'Co chair'. They are related but not equivalent.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property linking Conference to an integer count of reviews per paper, while write is an object property linking Person to Item (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A (cmt:date) is a general datatype property giving the date of a Conference, while Property B (Conference:is_a_date_of_camera_ready_paper_submission) is a highly specific datatype property indicating the camera-ready submission deadline within Important dates. They differ in domain, specificity, and intended meaning.
Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review, while property B links a speaker to a document they present. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In Ontology A, 'Conference' is the main academic event (the conference itself). In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Conference Trip' is a specific social sub-event (a trip organized during the conference), sibling to 'Conference Banquet'. They denote entirely different concepts.

Worker_lecturer (iasted) is a Lecturer who is also a worker, while Author_of_paper (sigkdd) is an Author who wrote a paper. Both are subclasses of Author/Speaker in their respective hierarchies and represent people contributing to the conference, but they emphasize different roles (lecturing vs. authoring). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Both classes represent social events within a conference context. They share the same label and have analogous children (Excursion/Conference Trip, Reception/Conference Banquet), confirming they denote the same concept despite slightly different hierarchical placements.

Property A is an action by an Administrator to add a Program Committee Member (domain: Administrator, range: Program Committee Member). Property B relates a Program committee to a Conference volume (domain: Program committee, range: Conference volume). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

NumericalReviewQuestion in edas is a specific type of question on a review form (e.g., a rating scale), whereas Review in iasted is the entire review document itself. These are fundamentally different concepts.
acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance action), while issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publication action). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite odd parentage), while Registration SIGKDD Member in sigkdd is a type of registration fee. These are entirely different concepts.

A Volunteer is a person who offers unpaid help to organize or run the conference, while an Attendee is a person who participates in or attends the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances; confOf even has a separate 'Participant' class that would be closer to 'Attendee'.

Conference Chair in cmt is the overall chair of the conference (a type of Chairman), while SC Member in ekaw is a Steering Committee member (a type of PC Member). These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and hierarchical positions.

Property A (forEvent) links a Call to an AcademicEvent, representing which event a call is for. Property B (inverse_of_partOf_7) is an inverse of a partOf relation with range Event, representing mereological composition. These relate different kinds of entities and express fundamentally different relationships.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). Different ranges and different semantics; they are unrelated.
Multimedia Topic in edas is a subject area for papers (a subclass of Topic), while Computer in iasted is a piece of audiovisual equipment (hardware). They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a conference volume to its steering committee, while property B links an item to a person who signed it. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Microelectronics Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A ('has a date of issue') refers to the issuance date of a conference document, while Property B ('End of conference') refers to the end date of the conference event itself. They have different domains (Conference document vs Conference) and denote entirely different temporal concepts.

'Conference fees' in Ontology A refers to the monetary cost or registration fee for attending a conference, whereas 'Conference' in ekaw refers to the scientific event itself (one edition of a conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Short paper in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), while Accepted Paper in ekaw is a paper classified by its review outcome status (accepted vs rejected). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.
A Web Site is an online document listing events, while a Registration form is a paper or digital form used for registering attendees. They serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain.

Both classes represent people who participate in a conference. 'Conference participant' (A) is a subclass of Person with children Active/Passive participants. 'Delegate' (B) in iasted is also a subclass of Person (despite unusual multiple parents like Conference building) and has children such as Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc., which are types of conference participants. In the conference domain, 'Delegate' is a standard synonym for 'Conference participant', so they are equivalent.

The property 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'for Event' links a Call to an Academic Event. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

'hasPart' is a general mereological (part-whole) property with unspecified domain/range, while 'awarded by' specifically links an Award to the entity that grants it. They describe entirely different relations.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while partOfEvent relates an Event to a parent Event (sub-events). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Accommodation Place in edas refers to lodging (its siblings include Dining Place and Conference Venue Place), while Conference hall in sigkdd refers to the venue where the conference sessions take place (its siblings include Hotel). These are distinct concepts within the Place hierarchy.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Wireless Communications Topic in edas is a specific Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Invited Speaker is a type of person (a presenter). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are unrelated.

minChoice is a datatype property with range positiveInteger indicating a minimum choice count for events, while hasStartDateTime is a datatype property with range dateTime indicating the start time of a conference event. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Both classes represent the same concept: a cocktail reception as a social event during a conference. 'Reception' in edas is under Social Event, and 'Coctail reception' in iasted is a Conference activity alongside other social elements like Coffee break and Social program. They denote the same type of event.

Invited talk is a type of conference contribution/presentation (a document or talk given by an invited speaker), while Poster Session is a type of event/session where posters are displayed. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links an active conference participant to a presentation they give, while property B links a contribution (paper) to its author. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators). Registration SIGMOD Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee, representing a type of fee. These are entirely different concepts (a person vs. a fee) and are unrelated.

assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (assigning a reviewer role), while reviewes relates a Member PC to a Contribution (reviewing a paper). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignReviewer relates an Administrator to a Reviewer (reviewer assignment), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (presentation delivery). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Workshop is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference hall is a type of Place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Conference in ekaw is an event (one edition of a conference), while Conference hall in iasted is a physical place/venue. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Although both are datatype properties with range string and similar names, their domains differ fundamentally: cmt:email applies to Person (an individual's email address), while confOf:contactEmail applies to Contribution (a paper's contact/corresponding email). They relate different kinds of entities and thus are not equivalent.

'is Initiated By' links a Call to conference chairs/TPC members who initiated it, while 'is paid by' links Money to a Person who pays it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role for people contributing to the conference), while Introduction is a subclass of Conference activity (an event/activity). They are entirely different concepts.

Published Paper in edas denotes a paper that has reached the publication stage (a lifecycle status), while Workshop Paper in ekaw denotes a paper submitted to or presented at a workshop (a venue/track type). These are orthogonal classifications; a workshop paper may or may not be published, and a published paper may belong to a conference rather than a workshop. They do not share intended instances.

confOf:writes specifically relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while iasted:give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. In the conference domain, 'give' likely refers to giving a presentation/talk (Activity) rather than authoring a paper. The domains and ranges differ in specificity and intent, so they are related but not equivalent.
Reception in confOf is a social event (a gathering/party), while Programme in edas is a Document (a schedule or program booklet). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Property A links a Co-chair to a Committee (organizational role), while Property B links a PC Member to a Contribution (reviewing activity). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Accepted contribution (A) is a paper that has been reviewed and accepted. Submission (B) in iasted is a general class for submitted documents with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. An Accepted contribution corresponds roughly to a Final manuscript or the accepted state of a Submission, so it is strictly more specific than the general Submission class. Thus A is subsumed by B.

readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper they have read, while reviewerOfPaper relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. The domains differ (actual reviewer vs possible reviewer) and the semantics differ (reading vs being assigned as reviewer). They are related but not equivalent.

Property A links a Topic to a Conference part (indicating the topic of a conference session), while Property B links a Person to an Item (indicating something a person needs). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, IndustryOrganization is a subclass of Organization (with siblings Academia Organization, Government Organization, NGO). Ontology A's Organization is the general class, so it subsumes the more specific Industry Organization in ontology B.

Both properties link a conference event entity (Conference part / Working event) to a Topic. In the conference domain, 'Conference part' in Ontology A and 'Working event' in Ontology B serve analogous roles as tracks, workshops, or tutorials that have associated topics. The domains and ranges align semantically, making these properties equivalent.
Presenter is a Person (a conference participant who presents), while Introduction is an Activity (a type of conference event). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Textual Review Question in edas is a type of question/criterion used during the review process (a subclass of Review Question), whereas Review in ekaw is the actual review document written by a reviewer about a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts.

A Travel Grant is a type of sponsorship (funding provided to cover travel costs), while a Sponzor fee is a type of fee (a payment made by a sponsor). They represent different concepts in the conference domain: one is financial support given, the other is a charge collected.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'belongs to a review reference' links a Topic to a Review preference, while 'is held after' links an Activity to a Time. They are unrelated.

In the Conference ontology, 'Organizer' typically refers to a person or role responsible for organizing the conference. In confOf, 'Organization' (with children Company, University and properties like employedBy) clearly denotes an institution/organization entity. These are conceptually different: one is an agent/role, the other is an institutional body. They are related in that organizations can act as organizers, but they are not equivalent.

In edas, Paper is a direct subclass of Document and includes all lifecycle states (Accepted, Rejected, Pending, etc.). In ekaw, Submitted Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is itself a subclass of Document) and specifically denotes papers that have been submitted. The edas Paper class is broader than ekaw Submitted Paper, as it also encompasses published or withdrawn papers that may not be in a 'submitted' state. They are closely related but not strictly equivalent; edas Paper subsumes ekaw Submitted Paper.
Organizer is a person or organization that organizes a conference, while Conference in confOf is the event itself (a working event). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Scholar in confOf is a subclass of Person (a type of attendee/role), while Nonmember registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent fundamentally different concepts.

Invited talk is a type of conference contribution/presentation (a specific talk given by an invited speaker), while Workshop Session is a type of event/session that groups multiple presentations within a workshop. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Paid applicant in Ontology A is a person who has registered and paid to attend the conference, which is a specific type of Conference Participant in ekaw (Ontology B). Conference Participant is more general as it includes chairs, presenters, and other roles beyond just paid registrants.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (the final outcome for a paper), while Accept Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (an individual reviewer's score). They are related concepts in the review process but not equivalent: one is a final decision, the other is a reviewer's rating.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant, while 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties describe entirely different relations: 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'isReviewedBy' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the person delivering it, while 'is visited by' links a physical location (Building, City, State) to a Person who visits it. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity/event (a kind of Lecture), while Invited Speaker is a type of Person (a kind of Speaker). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). They are unrelated.

addProgramCommitteeMember relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a person to a committee), while occupy relates a Person to a location (Building, City, State). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Call For Reviews is a type of Call (an announcement/request for reviews), while Reviewer is a person who performs reviews. They are entirely different concepts.

Extended abstract is a type of short contribution (a document format), while Assigned Paper is a full paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a workflow state). They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

Week Reject Rating is a subclass of Review Rating (a score/assessment value) in edas, while Negative Review is a subclass of Review (the actual review document) in ekaw. They are related conceptually as both pertain to negative evaluations of papers, but they represent different kinds of entities (a rating vs. a document), so they are not equivalent.
