Conference Chair in edas is a person who chairs the conference, while Reviewer in iasted is a person who reviews papers. These are distinct roles with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

The property 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (indicating necessity), while 'search' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (indicating a search action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper (sibling of 'Paper Full Version'). In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a subclass of Paper representing a paper that has been submitted to the conference. These are conceptually different: one denotes a part/type of document content (abstract), while the other denotes a lifecycle status (submitted). They are not equivalent.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country, while is_equipped_by links a Place to an Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Speaker lecture is a type of session/activity event. They are completely different concepts.

hasConferenceMember is an object property linking a Conference to its members, while City_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string representing the city. They describe entirely different aspects of a conference.

Pending Paper refers to a paper awaiting a decision, while Rejected Paper refers to a paper that has been evaluated and declined. These are distinct states in the paper lifecycle with disjoint intended instances.
The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'design' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Full Version is a specific type of paper (the complete manuscript), while Information for participants is a document providing logistical or general information to conference attendees. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

markConflictOfInterest links people (Author, Chairman, Reviewer) to a Paper to flag a conflict of interest, while has_a_topic_or_a_submission_contribution links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A (Conference), 'Organizer' typically refers to a person or role that organizes the conference. In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Organisation' refers to an institutional entity (with children like Academic Institution, Organising Agency, Proceedings Publisher) that can organise events. While they are related in the organizing domain, one denotes a role/person and the other an institution/agency, so they are not equivalent.
Banquet is a social event (an activity), while Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Place) and denote unrelated concepts.

Property A is an inverse of a partOf relation with range Event (a mereological/structural property), while Property B relates Activities or Items to Persons who give them (an agentive property). Their domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

A 'Textual Review Question' is a specific type of question/criterion used within a review form (e.g., an open-ended text field), whereas B 'Review' is the completed review document itself. They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place is a venue for meetings/conference sessions, while Single hotel room is an accommodation type. They are siblings under different sub-hierarchies of Place (venue vs accommodation) and denote entirely different concepts.
Reviewer in ontology A is a Person who writes reviews, while Review in ontology B (ekaw) is a Document representing the review itself. They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. artefact).
hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its members, while has_a_publisher links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasCity links Organization/Person to a City, while hasCountry links Conference to a Country. They differ in domain, range, and the geographic granularity (city vs country), so they are not equivalent.

Property A links a review expertise/preference to a Reviewer (domain: expertise/preference, range: Reviewer), while Property B links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (domain: Reviewer, range: history). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses.
In cmt, PaperAbstract is a subclass of Paper (a specific version/representation of a paper), whereas in edas, Paper is the general class for papers. Thus, cmt:PaperAbstract is subsumed by edas:Paper.

Contribution_co-author in Conference is a specific role (co-author of a contribution), which is a subclass of Regular author. Author in confOf is the general class for all authors who write contributions. The co-author class is strictly more specific than the general Author class, so it is subsumed by it.
Published Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document), while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Session in ekaw is a scientific event (a session within a conference), while One conference day in iasted is a temporal unit (a single day of the conference). They belong to different conceptual hierarchies and do not denote the same concept.

Property A 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authored work), while property B 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document (presented work). Writing and presenting are distinct activities in the conference domain; however, they overlap since authors often present their papers. They are related but not equivalent.

SC Member in ekaw is a person role (Steering Committee member, subclass of PC Member), while Registration SIGKDD Member in sigkdd is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (subclass of Chairman), while Brief introduction for Session chair in iasted is a document type (subclass of Document). They are entirely different concepts.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding on papers), while isReviewHistoryOf relates a PersonalReviewHistory to a Reviewer. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Presenter house (a building where presenters stay) and Hotel are distinct types of accommodation/place in the conference domain. The iasted ontology even has a separate 'Conference hotel' sibling, confirming that 'Presenter house' is not equivalent to 'Hotel'.
Conference Member is a Person role in a conference, while Conference hall is a Place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Credit card is a payment instrument. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

relatesTo is a very general property linking any Document to events, conferences, sessions, or persons. paperPresentedAs is a specific property linking a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation event. Their domains and ranges differ significantly in scope and specificity, so they are not equivalent.

confOf:Contribution represents scholarly submissions (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like abstract, title, keywords, and authors. edas:Document is a much broader class encompassing not only Paper but also Meal Menu, Programme, Review, and Slide Set. They overlap on the concept of a conference paper, but Document is far more general and includes non-scholarly artefacts, so they are related rather than equivalent or in a strict subsumption relationship.

Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (document structure), while Property B is an inverse of partOf with range Event (event structure). They operate in completely different domains within the conference ontology and are unrelated.
Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (someone applying to a conference), while Conference Venue Place is a subclass of Place (a physical location). They are entirely different concepts.

'references' is a general citation/reference relation with unspecified domain and range, while 'presentation' specifically links a Speaker to a Document they present. These are semantically unrelated properties.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is given by' relates an Activity/Item to a Person (who presents or gives it). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking Person to a string (email address), while hasReview is an object property linking Paper to Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person or Contact Information to a string (email address), while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
'has gender' is a datatype property describing a person's gender, while 'author Of' is an object property linking a person to a document they authored. They are completely unrelated.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a person to a committee), while 'initiates' relates chairs/TPC members to a Call (starting a call for papers). They are unrelated.

Conference Session in ekaw is a type of scientific event (a scheduled session at a conference), while Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State (likely representing the status or phase of a conference). These are fundamentally different concepts.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously (a sibling/temporal relation), while 'part Of Event' is a mereological part-whole relation between events. These are semantically distinct relations.

In EKAW, SC Member is a subclass of PC Member (Steering Committee members are a specialized type of Program Committee member). In SIGKDD, Program Committee member is the general class. Therefore, EKAW's SC Member is strictly more specific than SIGKDD's Program Committee member, making it subsumed_by.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering), while 'eventOnList' in ekaw relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (listing). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

startReviewerBidding is an action property from Administrator to Conference for initiating reviewer bidding, while hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted scholarly document (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions). In Conference, Call for paper is an announcement/invitation document soliciting submissions (sibling of Conference announcement). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (date) is a generic date property on Conference, while Property B (hasSubmissionDeadline) is a specific deadline property on Call. They have different domains (Conference vs Call) and different semantics (generic date vs submission deadline), so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Conference contribution in the Conference ontology is a type of document/artefact submitted to the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

In ekaw, Presenter is a Conference Participant who presents (with Invited Speaker as a child), while in iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (someone who authored a paper). Both represent the role of someone presenting/authoring at a conference, but they are not strictly equivalent: Presenter focuses on the act of presenting, while Author focuses on authorship. They overlap significantly in the conference domain (authors often present their papers), so 'related' is most appropriate.

Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Tutorial is a type of working event. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.

'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.

AcceptRating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (a rating/score assigned to a paper), while Negative_Review in ekaw is a subclass of Review (the review document itself). They belong to different ontological categories (rating vs. document) but are semantically related since an accept rating would typically not correspond to a negative review.

confOf's Member is a subclass of Participant (with siblings Regular and Student), indicating a general conference attendee/participant role. sigkdd's Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator (with siblings General Chair, Program Chair, etc.), indicating an organizing/program committee role. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; they overlap conceptually as people involved in a conference but are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the general concept of a Person in the conference domain. They share similar children (participants, authors, reviewers) and properties relating persons to documents (authorship). The intended instances coincide.

writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship), while Nation is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (nationality). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Regular Session is a type of event/session in a conference program, while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the program. They are entirely different concepts.
Early paid applicant is a subclass of Person representing a registrant who paid early, while Conference is a type of Event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has short title' is a datatype property for events (social/working) to provide an abbreviated title, while 'Name of conference' is a datatype property for the Conference class to provide its name. They have different domains and different semantic purposes.

A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Optical Topic) while B is a type of document (Invited Talk Abstract). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

'hasBeenAssigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while 'referencedIn' indicates that something is cited or referenced in another document. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Social event in confOf represents social gatherings like banquets and receptions (a type of Event), while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts like conference days and deadlines. These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers (sibling of Reviewer and Program Committee Member). In confOf, Member PC is explicitly described as a 'Reviewer' in its comment and reviews contributions; it is a sibling of Author. These are distinct roles in the conference domain.

hasCountry specifically links an Organization or Person to a Country, while is_connected_with is a much more general property linking Activity or Person to Item or Place. They differ in domain, range, and semantic specificity.

Both classes represent a Reviewer in the conference domain: a Person who reviews papers. In cmt, Reviewer is assigned to papers and reads them; in edas, Reviewer is linked via isReviewedBy/isReviewing to Paper. Despite different parent paths (Conference Member vs Person), their intended instances coincide as people performing paper reviews.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a research area, while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (URL), while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Tutorials (a part-whole relation), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (an agent/authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Country represents a nation (used for affiliation of persons/organizations). In iasted, State is a spatial/geographic entity with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state and properties about being situated in or visited by people, functioning more like a region or physical location. These are conceptually different.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (i.e., the paper being reviewed). Property B 'referencedIn' denotes a citation or reference relationship between documents. These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.
City and Country are distinct geographic concepts. A city is a specific urban settlement, while a country is a nation/state. They do not denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Property A provides a URL for a conference website (domain: Conference www), while property B provides the full name of a conference (domain: Conference). They represent entirely different attributes (URL vs. Name) on different domains.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, while Property B links a Person to a Conference they are a member of. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Ontology A's 'Presentation' is a general class for conference presentations (with children like Invited talk, and siblings like Poster). Ontology B's 'Video presentation' is a specific subtype of Presentation (sibling to Power Point presentation). Therefore, the general Presentation class in A subsumes the more specific Video presentation class in B.

Call For Papers is a type of call/announcement soliciting paper submissions, while Rejected Paper is a paper that has been evaluated and not accepted. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Steering committee and Program Committee are distinct types of committees within a conference organization. They are siblings under the Committee class in their respective ontologies, not equivalent concepts.
'has a review' links a reviewed contribution to its review, while 'write' links a person to an item they authored. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference www in Ontology A represents a conference website (a URL/web page), as indicated by its 'has a URL' property and sibling classes like 'Call for paper'. Conference Proceedings in ekaw represents the published proceedings volume of a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

defaultChoice is a datatype property mapping events to a positiveInteger (likely a default selection index in confTool), while hasStartDateTime maps conference events to a dateTime. They have different ranges and entirely different semantics.

Workshop Chair (ekaw) is a person who chairs a workshop and is modeled as both a Conference Participant and PC Member. Organizing Committee member (sigkdd) is a member of the organizing committee under Organizator. These are distinct roles in conference organization: one chairs workshops, the other serves on the organizing committee. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

Property A (assignExternalReviewer) has domain Reviewer and range External Reviewer, representing an assignment action between reviewers. Property B (hasReviewer) has domain Paper and range Possible Reviewer, linking a paper to its reviewer. Different domains, ranges, and semantics make them unrelated.
coversTopic relates a Paper/Event to a Research Topic, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

confOf 'Member PC' is explicitly commented as 'Reviewer' and has properties for reviewing contributions, making it equivalent to edas 'TPC Member' or 'Reviewer'. edas 'Conference Chair' is a distinct leadership role that initiates calls. They are different roles within the conference organization.
Tutorial is a type of conference part (an educational session), while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the completeness/submission stage of a paper (as opposed to Paper Abstract), while Industrial Paper in ekaw refers to a category/track of paper (as opposed to Regular Paper, Demo Paper, etc.). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.

hasAdministrativeEvent links a working event to an administrative event (a sub-event relationship), while organisedBy links an event to its organizing entity (an agent). These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation, while Presenter university is a type of building/place. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Property A (writePaper) relates an Author to a Paper, while Property B is an inverse of partOf relating something to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a contribution to the conference volume it was submitted at, while property B links a contribution to its author. They have different ranges and express entirely different relationships.

Both classes represent the role of a Reviewer in the conference domain. Although iasted places Reviewer under Speaker (a modeling choice where reviewers are also speakers/delegates), the intended instances—people who review papers—are the same. The edas ontology confirms this via properties like isReviewing and isReviewedBy linking Reviewer to Paper.
'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'read By Meta Reviewer' relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a reading/reviewing action), while 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (an acquisition action). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics, making them unrelated.
'written By' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship), while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person (signing). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.

Author (iasted) is a subclass of Speaker/Delegate representing someone who writes and presents papers. Organizator (sigkdd) represents conference organizers such as chairs and committee members. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

memberOfProgramCommittee links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, while organisedBy links an Event to an Organisation or Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an object property linking an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details), while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (start date). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A 'follows' relates Administrative events to other Administrative events (temporal ordering of events), while property B 'is sent after' relates Items to Time points (when something was sent). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Although both are datatype properties relating an entity to a date/dateTime, their domains differ significantly: 'has a date of issue' applies to a Conference document (the date it was issued), while 'is dated on' applies to an Activity (the date the activity occurs). These represent different semantic relations in the conference domain.
Poster Session is a type of scientific event/session, while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties mapping to a string representing a location, but they have different domains: 'Conference volume' (the overall conference) in ontology A versus 'Social event' and 'Working event' (specific events) in ontology B. They express the same kind of relation (a location string) but apply to different concepts, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A (isWrittenBy) relates Paper to Author, while property B (write) relates Person to Item. They express the same authorship relation but in opposite directions (A is the inverse of B). Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent. They are related as they capture the same conceptual link reversed.

The 'remark' property in confOf is a general note attached to a Contribution (paper), while 'hasCostCurrency' in edas specifies the currency of a Sponsorship cost. They have different domains, ranges semantics, and purposes, making them completely unrelated.

The 'location' property in confOf specifies where an event is held (domain: events, range: string), while 'registrationDueOn' in edas specifies a registration deadline (domain: Conference, range: dateTime). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

'related To Event' links an accepted paper to a presentation event, while 'awarded by' links an award to its granting entity. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair (an organizational role assignment), while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item they give/present. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
has_an_email and hasPhone are both datatype properties on Person with string range, but they represent different contact attributes (email vs phone number), so they are not equivalent.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a specific Review they authored, while hasReviewHistory relates a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (an aggregate record). The ranges differ (Review vs Personal Review History) and the semantics are distinct: one is an action of writing a single review, the other is possessing a history of reviews.

Both properties share the same name 'written By' and serve the same semantic role: linking a scholarly work (Contribution/Document) to its creator (Author/Person). In the conference domain, Contribution maps to Document and Author maps to Person, making these properties equivalent.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (the act of adjusting a bidding preference), while hasReviewer relates a Paper to a Possible_Reviewer (assigning a reviewer to a paper). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
confOf:Topic is the general class for conference topics, while edas:CryptographyTopic is a specific subclass of Topic in edas. Therefore confOf:Topic subsumes CryptographyTopic.

A 'Track workshop chair' is responsible for a specific track or workshop within a conference, while a 'Conference Chair' oversees the entire conference. They are both chair roles (subclasses of Person) but at different scopes, so they are related but not equivalent.
writtenBy relates a Contribution (paper) to its Author, while designed_by relates a Deadline to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Sponsor state refers to a status/state of a sponsor, while Program Committee is an organizational committee. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Talk Event is a type of conference event (an activity where talks are given), while Proceedings is a document/publication containing conference papers. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level, while property B links an activity or item to a person who gives it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Review is a document evaluating a paper, while Money represents financial entities (fees, sponsorship, etc.). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

'prepare' (Person -> Item) and 'presentation' (Speaker -> Document) denote different actions/relations in the conference domain. Preparing an item is not the same as giving a presentation of a document; they have different semantics despite loosely related domains and ranges.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Sponsor city is a geographical location (a city). They are completely unrelated concepts.
Coctail reception is a conference activity/event, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to a Conference Event, while 'technicallyOrganisedBy' (a subproperty of 'organisedBy') links something to its technical organizer. These properties have different semantics, domains, and ranges, and are not equivalent.

cmt:name is a general name property with domain Conference and Person, while confOf:hasFirstName specifically denotes the first name of a Person. A first name is a kind of name, so hasFirstName is more specific (subsumed by) the general name property.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while property B is an object property linking a Document to a Person (author). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Time zone is a geographical/temporal concept, while Deadline Author notification is a specific conference deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely unrelated.
Conference in ekaw is an event (one edition of a conference), while Conference city in iasted is a location (a city where a conference takes place). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee in their respective ontologies, but they represent different categories: 'Nonmember registration fee' is for non-members, while 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is for SIGMOD members. They are related as sibling-like concepts under the same parent class but are not equivalent.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while is_held_in links an Activity to a Place/Time. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Optical Topic) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A refers to someone who contributes content (authors, speakers, active participants), while Sponsor in Ontology B refers to a person providing financial support. These are distinct roles despite both being subclasses of Person.

Contact Information in edas is a class representing a person's contact details (email, phone, street, city, postal code), while City in iasted represents a geographical/administrative location. They are fundamentally different concepts; one is an information record and the other is a place.

Both 'Programme' in edas and 'Programme Brochure' in ekaw are subclasses of Document that represent the schedule/programme of conference events. In edas, Programme belongsToEvent (Conference Event), while in ekaw, Programme Brochure listsEvent (Event). Despite the slight naming difference (Programme vs Programme Brochure), they serve the same role as the document describing the conference programme, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

Paper is a document/submission class in cmt, while Computer Networks Switching Topic is a specific subject area/topic class in edas. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, accepts submissions, has members). In sigkdd, 'Conference hall' is a physical place (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel and Main office) where the conference takes place. These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a venue.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the solicitation of papers (a call), while B 'Paper' is an actual submitted contribution/artefact. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Conference volume' is a direct child of the root 'Conference' and carries all the properties one would expect of a conference event (location, committees, tracks, contributions, important dates). In Ontology B, 'Conference' is the main class representing the conference event itself (with dates, country, members, topics). Despite the naming difference ('Conference volume' vs 'Conference'), both classes represent the same concept: a specific instance/edition of a conference. The structural role and properties align closely.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (a large-scale gathering, sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). In edas, Paper Presentation is a specific academic event where a paper is presented (sibling to Talk Event, Workshop). A conference as a whole is not the same concept as an individual paper presentation session within a conference.
Member PC in confOf is a person (reviewer) who reviews contributions, while Review Question in edas is a type of question used in the review process. They are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person with children Administrator, Author, Reviewer, while siblings like Chairman and Conference Member are not Users. In confOf, Person is the top-level class for all people including Administrator, Author, Chair PC, Participant, etc. Thus confOf:Person corresponds to cmt:Person (the root), not cmt:User. cmt:User is a narrower concept covering only some roles, so the two classes overlap but are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while One conference day is a temporal unit representing a single day of the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Computer Networks Security Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In edas, 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a research topic (a subclass of Topic) for paper classification. In iasted, 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (hardware). They share the word 'computer' but denote entirely different concepts.

Both properties express the location where a conference or event takes place, but they differ significantly: A is a datatype property (range string) with domain Conference volume, while B is an object property (range Location class) with domain Event. They are semantically related but not equivalent due to different modeling choices (datatype vs object property) and slightly different domains.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Place is a physical location. They are completely unrelated concepts.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person specifically invited to speak at the conference, while 'Author cd proceedings included' is an author whose paper appears in the CD proceedings. These are distinct roles with different intended instances; one does not subsume the other.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (part of reviewer bidding/assignment), while Property B links a PC Member to a Topic (indicating expertise). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while is_occupied_by links physical locations (Building, City, State) to a Person (physical occupation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The property 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (indicating who added the member), while 'has a committee co chair' relates a Committee to a Co-chair (indicating committee membership/leadership). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasAttendee relates a Conference Event to a Person (attendee), while hold relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (organizer holding an event). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who delivers it (presenter), while 'is Written By' links a Paper to its Author. These are distinct relations in the conference domain: presenting is not the same as authoring, and the domains/ranges differ accordingly.

Property A links a Conference volume to its contributions (papers), while property B links a Call to an Academic Event. The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts; these properties describe unrelated relationships.

Associated Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational committee (subclass of Committee). They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string (street address), while organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to its organizing Organisation/Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and property types.

Both properties share the same name and express authorship, but their domains and ranges differ significantly. In cmt, writtenBy links a Review to a Reviewer (a specific kind of document and role), while in ekaw it links any Document to any Person. Since Review is a subclass of Document and Reviewer is a subclass of Person, the cmt property is more specific. They are related but not equivalent.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Invitation letter is a document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Assistant in confOf refers to a support/administrative role (as indicated by its siblings like Administrator, Volunteer). These are conceptually distinct roles within the Person hierarchy.

Bid in cmt represents a reviewer's bid on a paper, while Person in iasted represents a human being (with subclasses Delegate and Sponsor). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing relation), while 'topicCoveredBy' relates a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (subject coverage relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Person in cmt is a general class for people involved in the conference, while Student in ekaw is a specific subclass of Person. Therefore, cmt:Person subsumes ekaw:Student.

University is an academic institution (sibling of Company under Organization), while NGO is a non-governmental organization (sibling of Academia Organization, Government Organization, Industry Organization). They are distinct types of organizations with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper). In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (a person who authored something and speaks/presents). Both represent the role of someone who authors and/or presents at a conference, but their hierarchical positions differ: edas Presenter is more specific (must be an author who presents), while iasted Author is under Speaker. They overlap significantly in intended instances but are not strictly equivalent due to differing parent hierarchies and scope.
'has the last name' and 'has Fax' are both datatype properties on Person with string range, but they capture entirely different attributes (surname vs fax number) and are therefore unrelated.
'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer for the review process, while 'award' links something to an Award. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Conference Dinner and Conference Trip are both social/non-academic conference events, but they denote different activities (a meal vs. a trip). They are related as sibling-like concepts under the broader category of social events, but not equivalent.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Enterprise Topic) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'is Reviewed By' specifically links a Paper to reviewing roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'is used by' is a generic property linking an Item to a Person. They have different semantics and scopes.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants), with children like Regular author and Invited speaker. Program Committee member in Ontology B is an organizer role responsible for reviewing and selecting papers. These are distinct roles: one contributes content, the other organizes/reviews. They do not share intended instances.

In iasted, 'Author book proceedings included' is a specific subclass of 'Author' (an author whose work is included in book proceedings). In sigkdd, 'Author' is the general class with subclasses like 'Author of paper'. Therefore, the iasted class is strictly more specific and is subsumed by the sigkdd Author class.
Presenter (ekaw) is a conference participant who presents, while Listener (iasted) is a delegate who listens. These are distinct, non-overlapping roles in the conference domain.

hasStartDateTime is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a dateTime value, while hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Record of attendance is a document recording someone's attendance. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Decision is the outcome (Acceptance/Rejection) linked to a Paper via hasDecision. In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is the paper itself after evaluation, with children Accepted_Paper and Rejected_Paper. They model the same review-outcome concept from different perspectives (decision object vs. evaluated paper state), so they are related but not equivalent.

In edas, 'Meeting Room Place' is a specific subclass of 'Place', while in iasted, 'Place' is the general top-level class for locations (with children like Building, Conference hall, Session room). Therefore, the more specific Meeting Room Place is subsumed by the general Place class in iasted.
Social program is a type of conference activity (event), while Program Committee member is a type of person/organizer. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and semantics (running paper assignment tools vs issuing conference proceedings). They are unrelated.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address), while hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation responsible for publishing conference proceedings, while Renting is an Activity before the conference. They are entirely different concepts in both kind and purpose.

PC Chair (Program Committee Chair) and General Chair are distinct conference roles. The General Chair oversees the entire conference organization, while the PC Chair specifically leads the program committee responsible for paper selection and review. In sigkdd, Program Chair is a sibling of General Chair, confirming they are different concepts. They are related as both are senior organizing roles but not equivalent.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B (paperPresentedAs) relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ekaw, Conference is a Scientific Event representing an entire edition of a conference. In iasted, One conference day is a subclass of Time/Conference days representing a single day within a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts (whole event vs. temporal unit).
Proceedings is a document/volume class, while Lecturer is a person/role class. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (with acceptance tracked via the hasDecision property). In ekaw, Accepted_Paper is a specific subclass deep in the Paper hierarchy (Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper > Accepted Paper). Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Accepted_Paper.
Registration is a conference activity (event) in iasted, while Committee is an organizational body in sigkdd. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict), while 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (indicating receiving an award). They are unrelated.

A Meta Review is a higher-level review that summarizes or evaluates other reviews (typically by a meta-reviewer or area chair), while a Positive Review is simply a review with a positive recommendation. They are both subclasses of Review but represent entirely different dimensions (role vs. sentiment) and their intended instances do not coincide.

Session Chair and Reviewer are distinct roles in conference organization. A Session Chair moderates a session, while a Reviewer evaluates papers. Although in edas the Session Chair class is also listed as a possible reviewer of papers, the primary intended concept of 'Session Chair' is not equivalent to 'Reviewer'. They are separate sibling-like roles.
Workshop is a type of working event (a session format), while One day presenter is a type of delegate/person who presents for one day. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee, while property B links persons (chairs, TPC members) to a Call. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to a Time indicating presence. They describe entirely different concepts and have different ranges and types.

Both properties relate an Author to a paper-like entity (Contribution in confOf, Paper in sigkdd). However, 'writes' denotes the act of authoring/creating the document, while 'submit' denotes the act of submitting it to the conference. An author writes a paper before submitting it, and submission may be done by a corresponding author on behalf of others. They are semantically related but not equivalent.

In iasted, Submission is a Document with children 'Initial manuscipt' and 'Final manuscript', clearly representing submitted papers. In sigkdd, Paper is a Document that authors submit (via the 'submit' property). Both denote the same concept: a paper/manuscript submitted to a conference.

Conference Chair is the overall chair of a conference, while Late Registered Participant is a participant who registered after the deadline. These are entirely different roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers to staff working for an agency (e.g., publishing or organizing), while Author of paper in sigkdd refers to someone who authored a paper. These are entirely different roles within the conference domain.

In edas, Author is a direct subclass of Person representing any paper author. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is a subclass of Author (which is itself a subclass of Speaker > Person), making it more specific. Thus edas:Author subsumes sigkdd:Author_of_paper.

Review (an evaluation of a paper) and Abstract (a summary of a paper) are distinct document types in the conference domain. Ontology B even lists Review as a sibling of Abstract, confirming they are different concepts.

Entity A is a Reviewer (a person who reviews papers) while Entity B is an Author (a person who writes papers). These are distinct roles in the conference domain; notably, each ontology lists the other role as a sibling, confirming they are different concepts.
Property A links a Person to a Conference (membership), while Property B links an Item to a Person (preparation/authorship). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links an Administrator to a Conference (entering conference details), while Property B links a Conference part to a Topic (assigning a track/workshop/tutorial topic). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Proceedings Publisher is an organisation that publishes proceedings. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Cryptography Topic is a subject area/topic class in edas, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (abstract for a tutorial) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Property A links a conference volume to its contributions (papers), while property B links a conference to its members (people). The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts, so they are unrelated.
hasTopic relates a Working event to a Topic, while obtain relates a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A links a Review preference to either a Submitted contribution or a Topic (indicating what a reviewer prefers to review), while Property B links a Contribution to a Topic (indicating the subject matter of a paper). They have different domains, different ranges, and different semantic meanings in the conference domain.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Tutorial Chair is a person role (a type of conference participant). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Paper and Review are distinct concepts in the conference domain. A Paper is a scholarly contribution submitted by authors, while a Review is an evaluation of that paper written by reviewers. Both ontologies list them as separate sibling classes under Document.

Submitted contribution in Ontology A refers specifically to a written contribution that has been submitted (with Reviewed contribution as a child), whereas Paper in ekaw is a broader class encompassing all papers including Camera Ready Paper, Submitted Paper, etc. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; Paper subsumes Submitted contribution in scope.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (a direct subclass of Person), while OC Member in ekaw specifically denotes a member of the Organising Committee (a subclass of Conference Participant with child OC Chair). These are distinct roles; an attendee is not necessarily an OC member and vice versa.

Associated Chair in cmt is a subclass of Chairman (typically an Associate/Co-Chair of the main conference), while Workshop Chair in ekaw specifically chairs a workshop. Both are chair roles within a conference organization, but they denote different specific positions; neither subsumes the other.
Author is a person who writes or submits papers, while Abstract is a document (a short summary of a contribution). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Published Paper' is a sibling of 'Accepted Paper', indicating it represents a paper that has progressed beyond acceptance to publication (e.g., in proceedings). In ekaw, 'Accepted Paper' is explicitly defined as an accepted paper that will become part of the proceedings but is not yet the camera-ready/published version. Thus they represent different stages in the paper lifecycle and are related but not equivalent.

Topic in Ontology A represents a subject area or theme of a conference part/paper, while Document in Ontology B represents a physical/digital artefact such as an abstract, paper, or review. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Social event is a type of conference event (e.g., banquet, reception), while Fee is a monetary charge (e.g., registration fee). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while need relates a Person to an Item they require. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a document/artefact (Conference document / Item) to the Person who authored or prepared it. In the conference domain, 'has authors' and 'is prepared by' express the same authorship relation between a paper-like item and its creator.

Person in ontology A represents human individuals (authors, reviewers, participants), while Activity in ontology B represents events or actions (conference activities). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A (contributes) goes from Person to Conference document, while property B (presentationed by) goes from Document to Speaker. They have opposite directions and different semantics: 'contributes' is a general contribution relation, whereas 'presentationed by' specifically links a document to its presenter. They are not equivalent nor inverses of each other in a strict sense.

Call for paper is a type of conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while writtenBy links a Contribution to an Author (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (informational material), while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle, while Listener is a person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Both are datatype properties mapping a Person to a string representing the person's first name. The comment in B mentioning 'involved middle name' is a minor note but does not change the core semantics; they denote the same relation.
Property A links a Co-chair to a Committee (organizational role), while Property B links a Contribution to an Author (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Credit card is a payment instrument. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A assigns an ISBN to conference proceedings, while property B assigns an abstract text to a contribution. They have different domains, different semantic meanings, and are entirely unrelated.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (signing/registration). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

In edas, TPC Member is a direct subclass of Person representing a program committee member who reviews papers. In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a superclass of PC Member (the equivalent concept). Since every TPC Member is a possible reviewer but not every possible reviewer is necessarily a TPC/PC member, edas:TPC Member is subsumed by ekaw:Possible_Reviewer.
Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B (hasReview) relates a Paper to a Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship), while Currency is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to a string. They describe entirely different concepts and relations.

'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (mereological), while 'hold' relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference it organizes. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Entity A is a subclass of Regular author (a person role), while Entity B is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary concept). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating how many reviews each paper should receive (an integer configuration parameter). hasRating is an object property on Active Paper linking a paper to its Review Rating. They differ in domain, range, property type, and semantics.

Short paper is a type of contribution (a document), while Deadline Paper Submission is a type of deadline (a temporal constraint). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Property A links Important dates to a Conference volume, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Security Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a subclass of Committee representing a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
'has gender' and 'has Last Name' are both datatype properties on Person but capture entirely different attributes (gender vs. surname). They are unrelated.

'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer (review bidding context), while 'payed by' links a Registration fee to a Person (payment context). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Author is a Person who writes papers, while Multi-author Volume is a Document (a collection of works such as proceedings). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Registation deadline refers to the deadline for registering for the conference, while Deadline Abstract Submission refers to the deadline for submitting abstracts. These are distinct types of deadlines in the conference domain.

Early Registered Participant refers to a conference attendee who registered early, while Session chair refers to a person who chairs a session. These are distinct roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

maxPapers is a datatype property linking a Program Committee Member to an integer (maximum number of papers they can review), while paperPresentedAs is an object property linking a Paper to an Individual Presentation. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a conference-related entity to a thematic subdivision (Track vs Topic). In the conference domain, tracks are often organized around topics, so they overlap conceptually, but a Track is typically an organizational/programmatic unit while a Topic is a subject area. The domains also differ (Conference volume vs Working event), making them related rather than equivalent.

The property 'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (indicating who added the member), while 'has a program committee' relates a Conference volume to a Program committee. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, University is a direct subclass of Organization with sibling Company. In ekaw, Academic Institution is a subclass of Organisation and has University as one of its children (alongside Research Institute). Therefore, confOf:University is more specific than ekaw:Academic_Institution, making it subsumed_by.

Both classes are named 'Conference Session' and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a session within a conference. The ekaw ontology places it under Session > Scientific Event > Event, which is consistent with how edas uses it as a type of academic/conference event.

In cmt, User is a superclass of active roles (Author, Reviewer, Administrator) who interact with the system. In sigkdd, Listener is a passive conference attendee role, sibling to Speaker and Organizator. Their intended instances do not coincide; they represent different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A gives the issue date of a conference document, while property B gives the start date-time of a conference event. They have different domains (document vs event), different ranges (date vs dateTime), and describe entirely different temporal concepts.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its Reviewer, while property B (writes) links an Author to a Contribution. They have completely different domains and ranges and describe different relationships in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference Member to a Conference (individual membership), while Property B links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (organizational structure). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Conference' denotes the overall conference entity (with children like 'Conference volume'), while in confOf, 'Event' is a broader concept encompassing administrative, social, and working events that occur during a conference. They overlap in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent; 'Event' in confOf is more general than 'Conference' in Ontology A.

Conference Dinner in edas is a Meal Event (an activity/occurrence), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a Building (a physical place). They are related because the dinner may take place at the restaurant, but they are not equivalent as one is an event and the other is a location.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while holded_by links a Conference to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Attendee in edas is a subclass of Person representing a person attending the conference, while Author attendee book registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Money/Fee representing a specific type of registration fee. They are entirely different concepts (person vs. monetary amount).

hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment relation), while is_given_by links an Activity/Item to a Person (provenance/presenter relation). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Conference Session in ekaw is a type of event (a scheduled session within a conference), while Conference hall in iasted is a type of place (a physical venue). They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts (event vs. location).

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'adjusted By' links a Bid to a Reviewer, while 'updated Version Of' links a Document to another Document (versioning). They are unrelated.

A Steering committee is a specific committee that guides a conference, while an Academic Institution is an organization such as a university or research institute. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Call for paper is a type of conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while Signal Processing Topic is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while property B links an Author to a notification Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

endReview links a Program Committee Chair to a Review (an action of ending/concluding a review), while reviews links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (associating a review with the paper it evaluates). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A Time zone represents a geographic time offset region, while a Deadline represents a temporal cutoff for submissions or notifications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasSubmissionInstructions is a datatype property linking a Call to a string (submission instructions), while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., workshop, talk), while Author is a person who writes/submits papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
IASTED non member is a type of delegate (person) attending the conference, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used for announcements, while Computer Networks Aapplications Topic is a specific research topic within computer networks. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a version/format of a paper (the abstract text), sibling to Paper Full Version. Accepted Paper in edas is a paper that has passed the review process (a status). These are orthogonal classifications: one describes document granularity, the other describes acceptance status. They are unrelated.

Sponsorship in edas represents a sponsorship arrangement or grant provided by an organization (with cost amount/currency), while Money in iasted is a general financial concept encompassing fees, tips, taxes, and sponsorships as subtypes. Sponsorship in edas corresponds more closely to 'Sponzorship' (a child of Money) in iasted, not to the broader Money class itself.
hasName is a datatype property linking Conference to its name string, while has_amount_of links Money to an integer amount. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In ekaw, Session Chair is a subclass of PC Member (Program Committee member), while in sigkdd, Program Committee member is a distinct class under Organizator. A session chair is a specific role that may be filled by a PC member, but the two classes are not equivalent; they overlap/are related.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person invited to give a talk (e.g., keynote) without necessarily authoring a submitted paper, while 'Author of paper' is someone who has written a paper for the conference. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different intended instances.

A Tutorial is an instructional working event, while a Plenary lecture is a keynote-style lecture given to all attendees. They are distinct types of conference activities. Notably, iasted has its own Tutorial class as a sibling of Plenary lecture, confirming they are different concepts.

In edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing papers that have been accepted. In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (including submitted, camera-ready, etc.). Therefore, edas:AcceptedPaper is strictly more specific than ekaw:Paper, making it subsumed_by ekaw:Paper.

The property 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator who runs paper assignment tools, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item they author. These describe entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both classes represent a paper or contribution that has been submitted to a conference. In Ontology A, 'Submitted contribution' is a written contribution submitted for review (with children like 'Reviewed contribution'). In Ontology B, 'Submission' is a document representing a submitted paper (with children 'Initial manuscipt' and 'Final manuscript'). Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances in the conference domain coincide.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Review' is the review document itself (a child of Document, written by a Reviewer). In ontology B (Conference), 'Reviewed contribution' is the paper/submission that has been reviewed (a child of Submitted contribution, with property 'has a review' pointing to a Review). These are distinct concepts: one is the review artefact, the other is the reviewed paper. They are related via the review process but not equivalent.

'initiates' in edas relates specific conference roles (Chair, TPC Member) to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while 'sign' in iasted relates a Person to an Item (likely signing a document or form). These properties describe fundamentally different actions with different domains and ranges in the conference context.

Tutorial in confOf is a type of working event (an educational session), while One conference day in iasted is a temporal unit representing a single day of the conference. They are completely different concepts.
'is occupied by' relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person, while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific type of Chairman (under Person > Chairman), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a general member of the organizing committee (under Person > Organizator). They are related as both are organizational roles within a conference, but they are not equivalent since one is a chair-level role and the other is a general committee member role.

A Sponsor (under Person in iasted) is someone who provides financial or material support to the conference, while a General Chair (in sigkdd) is the lead organizer responsible for overall conference management. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

Conference document is a broad class for documents related to a conference (calls for papers, reviews, announcements, etc.), while Award refers to prizes given at the conference (e.g., Best Paper Award). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Entity A is the general class 'Topic', while Entity B is 'Multimedia Topic', a specific subclass of Topic in edas. Therefore A subsumes B.

Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, announcements, reviews, contributions, etc. Conference Proceedings in Ontology B (ekaw) is a specific type of multi-author volume containing accepted papers. Thus, Conference document subsumes Conference Proceedings.
Property 'name' captures the name of a Conference or Person, while 'E mail' captures the email address of a Person. These are distinct attributes with different semantics and are not equivalent.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

'remark' is a datatype property on Contribution (a paper) for storing remarks/comments, while 'Nation' is a datatype property on Person for storing nationality. They have different domains and entirely different semantics.

Property A links conference proceedings to an ISBN string, while property B links a conference to its city string. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and describe entirely different attributes.
Contact Information represents address/phone/email details of a person or entity, while Time represents temporal concepts such as deadlines and conference days. These are entirely different concepts.

A is a topic classification (Computer Networks Enterprise Topic) while B is a type of presentation event (Contributed Talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories in the conference domain.

Property A 'name' denotes a textual name for a Conference or Person, while property B 'has a URL' denotes a web address (URL) for a Conference www entity. These are semantically distinct properties relating different kinds of information.
Medicine Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Committee member' is a person serving on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair), while B 'Speaker' is a delegate who presents at the conference (with children Author, Reviewer). These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different intended instances.

hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their biography), while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (its author). They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.

writePaper (Author -> Paper) and writtenBy (Document -> Person) are inverse properties of each other. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as they describe the same authorship relationship in opposite directions.

Negative_Review is a type of document (a review with negative sentiment), while Reviewer is a person who reviews. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are unrelated.

Paper Presentation in edas refers to presenting an accepted paper at a conference, while Video presentation in iasted refers to a specific medium/format of presentation (video). They are both types of conference presentations but denote different concepts; they overlap as related rather than being equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Chairman in cmt is a leadership/organizing role (with subclasses like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Registeered applicant in Conference is a person who has applied and registered to attend the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Submission event is an administrative event for submitting contributions, while Program Committee is a committee of people. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Student in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person role), while Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

EKAW's Individual Presentation is a scientific event specifically for presenting papers (with children Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, Tutorial and properties linking to Paper/Abstract). IASTED's Presentation is a conference activity categorized by medium (PowerPoint, Video) alongside social events like cocktail receptions. They overlap in the concept of presenting at a conference but differ significantly in scope, context, and intended instances.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Sponsor company house is a building/place. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Rejected Paper is a paper that was evaluated and not accepted, while Final manuscript is the final version of an accepted submission (contrasted with Initial manuscript). These are conceptually distinct stages/outcomes in the conference process.
readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reading action), while writtenBy relates a Contribution to an Author (authorship). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, Paper is a subclass of Regular contribution (sibling to Extended abstract), indicating it refers specifically to full/regular papers. In Ontology B, Conference Paper is a broad superclass encompassing many paper types including Demo Paper, Poster Paper, Workshop Paper, etc. Thus, A's Paper is more specific than B's Conference Paper; they overlap but are not strictly equivalent. 'related' best captures this partial overlap without clear subsumption direction across the two ontologies.

Both properties describe a person/author providing a document/paper to the conference system. However, 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) is broader than 'submit' (Author -> Paper), as contributing can include roles beyond submission (e.g., reviewing, organizing). They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent.

confOf's 'Member PC' has the comment 'Reviewer', is a subclass of Person, and has a 'reviewes' property pointing to Contribution (paper). edas's 'Reviewer' is also a subclass of Person that reviews papers ('is Reviewing' -> Paper). Both denote the same concept: a person who reviews conference submissions.

maxChoice is a datatype property with range positiveInteger indicating the maximum number of choices for events, while hasEndDateTime is a datatype property with range dateTime indicating when an event ends. They describe completely different aspects and have incompatible ranges.
Regular Paper is a specific type of full paper (subclass of Paper), while Abstract is a summary document (sibling of Paper in sigkdd). They represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Programme is a document representing the schedule/programme of a conference event (linked via belongsToEvent). In ekaw, Flyer is a promotional document published by an organisation. These are distinct types of documents with different purposes; note that ekaw has its own 'Programme Brochure' sibling which would be closer to edas's Programme.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference for running assignment tools, while 'has a publisher' relates Conference proceedings to a Publisher.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'is Topic Of' relates a topic to a conference or paper. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reception is a social event (a type of gathering), while Listener is a person who attends the conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

In iasted, Document is a broad class encompassing many types of documents (forms, invitation letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). In sigkdd, Paper is a specific subclass of Document representing submitted papers. Therefore, iasted:Document subsumes sigkdd:Paper.

registrationDueOn is a specific property linking Conference to a dateTime for registration deadlines, while Date is a general property linking Deadline to a dateTime. They are related as both deal with deadline dates but differ in domain specificity and scope.

Late Registered Participant is a conference attendee who registered late, while Organizing Committee member is a person involved in organizing the conference. These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the overall conference organization entity (with administrators, members, paper submissions, review criteria, etc.). In edas, 'Conference Event' represents a scheduled event/session within a conference (with start/end times, location, programme, attendees), and is a superclass of AcademicEvent and NonAcademicEvent. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

The 'name' property in cmt applies to Conference and Person entities as a general name, while 'has short title' in confOf applies to Social event and Working event entities as a shortened title.
