They have different domains and different semantics (general name vs. abbreviated title), making them unrelated.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Computer Networks Enterprise Topic is a subject/topic classification for papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Administrator in cmt is a conference management role (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering details), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a person who may review papers. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and no hierarchical overlap.

Conference Banquet (a social event) and Coctail reception (a conference activity alongside Social program as a sibling) are both social gatherings at a conference but denote different specific types of events. They are related but not equivalent.

Property A (date) is a general datatype property on Conference giving its date, while Property B (is_an_abstract_submission_date) is a specific property on Important dates indicating the abstract submission deadline. They have different domains and different semantics.

Government Organization in edas refers to a government entity (a type of organization by sector), while Proceedings Publisher in ekaw refers to an organization that publishes conference proceedings. These are conceptually distinct roles/types of organizations with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.
Property A links a Paper to its Co-author, while Property B links a Committee to its Co-chair. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Both properties link a Paper (and Conference/Event) to a Topic/Research Topic, expressing the same semantic relation: the subject covers or is about the given topic. The domains and ranges align closely in the conference domain.

'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while 'referencedIn' denotes a citation/reference relationship. These are semantically distinct properties with different domains, ranges, and meanings.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while hasTopic relates a Paper or Conference to a Topic (subject area). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

hasAuthor is an object property linking a Paper to an Author, while has_an_ISBN is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to a string. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, type, and semantics.

Conference proceedings is a published volume of papers (with ISBN, publisher, volume), while Conference Session is a time-slot or thematic session within a conference event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A is 'Conference proceedings', a publication/document (the proceedings volume itself), while Entity B is 'Proceedings Publisher', an organisation that publishes proceedings. They represent fundamentally different concepts (a document vs. an organisation) and are therefore unrelated.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Sensor Topic) while B is an organizational committee (Organizing Committee). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Country in edas represents a geographical nation (used as the location of a conference), while Conference in sigkdd represents the academic event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

Contact Information in edas represents address/contact details (city, email, phone, street, postal code), while Person in sigkdd represents a human individual (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Conference announcement' is an administrative document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while a 'Conference Paper' is a scholarly contribution submitted to the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Abstract is a type of document (summary of a paper), while Award is a prize given to authors/papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Submission event is an administrative event for submitting contributions (papers), while Organizational Meeting is an academic meeting for organizing the conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for participation' is a document inviting people to participate in a conference, while a 'Record of attendance' is a document recording who actually attended. These are entirely different concepts with no subsumption or meaningful overlap.

has First Name is a datatype property for a person's first name (domain: Person, range: string), while Price is a datatype property for a registration fee amount (domain: Registration fee, range: int). They are completely unrelated.
Scholar is a subclass of Person representing an academic individual, while Meal Menu is a subclass of Document representing food options for a meal event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Bid represents a reviewer's bid on a paper, while Country represents a geographical nation. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Venue Place is a physical location (a place), while Hotel presenter is a type of person/delegate. They are completely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Camera ready contribution' is a specific subclass of 'Accepted contribution', representing the final camera-ready version of a paper. In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Conference Paper' is a general class with 'Camera Ready Paper' as a sibling. Thus, Camera ready contribution in A corresponds to Camera Ready Paper in B, not to the more general Conference Paper. The two classes overlap but are not equivalent; Conference Paper subsumes Camera ready contribution.

logoURL refers to the URL of a conference's logo image (range anyURI), while hasName refers to the full textual name of the conference (range string). These are entirely different properties with different meanings and ranges.

In cmt, Document is a superclass of both Paper and Review. In edas, Paper is a subclass of Document (with siblings like Review, Meal Menu, etc.). Therefore, cmt:Document subsumes edas:Paper, as it is the more general class encompassing papers and reviews.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts: 'memberOfProgramCommittee' links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They share no semantic overlap.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of chairman), while Introduction of speaker is a conference activity/event. They are completely different concepts in the domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Tax is a type of money/financial charge. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Conference building is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and describe unrelated relations: 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item.

The property 'enable Virtual Meeting' in cmt relates an Administrator to a Conference for enabling virtual meetings, while 'prepare' in iasted relates a Person to an Item for preparation. These have different semantics, domains, and ranges, and are unrelated.
'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item, while 'Name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string. They describe entirely different relations.

Reviewing event in confOf is an administrative event for the reviewing procedure of submitted contributions, while Call For Papers in edas is a type of call soliciting paper submissions. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Negative_Review in ekaw is a specific subclass of Review (a review with a negative recommendation), while Review in iasted is the general class of reviews. Thus Negative_Review is subsumed by the more general Review class.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while Registration deadline is a temporal deadline for registering. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Class A 'Conference' represents the conference event itself, while class B 'Conference airport' is a specific type of building (an airport used for a conference). These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Organization in confOf represents institutions like companies and universities that employ people, while Document in sigkdd represents artefacts like papers, abstracts, and reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ontology A (cmt), Author is a subclass of Conference Member which is a subclass of Person. In ontology B (Conference), Person is the top-level class for people, with children like Committee member, Conference contributor, etc. Thus, cmt:Author is a specific role subsumed by Conference:Person, not equivalent to it.

The two properties have completely different domains and semantics: 'has a degree' relates a Review preference to an integer (likely an academic degree level), while 'has amount of' relates Money to an integer (a monetary amount). They are unrelated.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Registration fee is a monetary fee. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasCountry links an Organization or Person to a Country, while organisedBy links an Event to an Organisation or Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (a structural/organizational role assignment), while Property B links a Call to the person who initiated it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Student registration fee (A) is a fee for students, while Registration SIGKDD Member (B) is a fee for SIGKDD members. They are both subclasses of Registration fee but target different attendee categories. B's sibling 'Registration Student' would be the equivalent of A.

Industrial Paper is a specific type of full paper (e.g., for an industry track), while Abstract is a brief summary document. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference for initiating reviewer bidding, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document for giving a presentation. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Conference www is a web document/URL resource for a conference, while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a research topic in computer networks. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking various entities to a string name, while Property B is an object property linking a Working event to a Topic. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and purposes.

'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing activity), while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (organizing/hosting activity). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

forEvent in edas links a Call to an AcademicEvent (associating a call for papers with the event it is for), while hasEvent in ekaw links an Event to another Event (a part-whole or sub-event relationship). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Conference Dinner in edas is a specific type of meal event at a conference. In iasted, Social program is a broader category that includes Dinner banquet as a child class. Thus, Conference Dinner is subsumed by Social program (they are not equivalent since Social program also includes cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, etc.).

Early Registered Participant is a subclass of Person (a role/type of attendee), while Registration is a subclass of Activity (an event or process). They belong to fundamentally different categories and are not equivalent.

Conference applicant refers to someone applying to attend or participate in the conference (with child Registeered applicant), while Organizator refers to someone organizing the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Committee member). These are distinct roles with no overlap.

Property A relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers), while Property B relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Rejection is a decision outcome (rejecting a paper), while Sponzorship is a type of money/funding. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee-of relation), while Property B relates an event to an Academic Institution that scientifically organized it. They differ in both domain and range types and express different organizational roles.

Written contribution (Conference) is a broad class of conference contributions that are written, including both submitted and regular (accepted) papers as well as posters. Submission (iasted) specifically denotes documents that have been submitted (initial/final manuscript). They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent: Written contribution includes non-submitted items like invited posters, while Submission is narrowly about the act of submitting manuscripts.

topicCoveredBy relates a Research Topic to Events or Papers that cover it, while need relates a Person to an Item they require. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Participant in confOf is a person attending the conference (subclass of Person), while Memeber registration fee in iasted is a monetary fee (subclass of Money > Fee > Registration fee). They are entirely different concepts.
Workshop is a conference event/session type, while Car is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and Program Committee Members. In edas, TPC Member specifically denotes a Technical Program Committee member (a narrower role). Thus, cmt:Conference Member subsumes edas:TPC Member.
Conference is an event (one edition of a conference), while Program Committee is a committee responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who paid late), while Nonauthor registration fee is a subclass of Money/Fee (a type of registration fee). They belong to entirely different categories (person vs. monetary amount) and are unrelated.

enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference for enabling virtual meetings, while hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference for organizing/holding it. Different domains and different semantics.

Property A denotes the start date/time of a conference event, while property B denotes the end date/time of a conference. They represent opposite temporal boundaries (start vs. end) and have different domains (Conference Event vs. Conference), so they are unrelated.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while B 'Conference' is a type of working event. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference registrant who paid late), while Bank transfer is a subclass of Payment document (a method of payment). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Computer Architecture Topic is a research topic classification under Topic, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
A Programme Brochure lists conference events/sessions, while a Registration form is used for attendee registration. They are entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.
Paper is a type of Contribution (a submitted document), while Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Regular Session is a type of scientific event/session within a conference, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a paper/contribution that has been accepted for the conference. 'Accepted contribution' in Ontology A and 'Accepted Paper' in Ontology B share the same intended instances: contributions/papers that passed review and were accepted. Both have 'Rejected' siblings, confirming they occupy the same position in their respective acceptance-status hierarchies.

Property A denotes the end date/time of a conference event, while property B denotes the start date/time of a conference. They refer to opposite temporal boundaries (end vs. start) and have different domains (Conference Event vs. Conference), so they are unrelated.

'One conference day' in iasted represents a single day within a conference (a temporal unit), while 'Conference' in sigkdd represents the entire conference event. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Silver Supporter is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (memberOfProgramCommittee) has domain Program Committee Member and range Program Committee, while property B (has_members) has domain Committee and range Committee member. They are inverses of each other (B is the inverse of A), not equivalent. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related.

Student in confOf is a type of Participant (person attending the conference), while Best Student Paper Supporter in sigkdd is a type of Sponzor (sponsor). These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution (a document), while Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic (a subject area). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Student is a subclass of Person representing an academic role, while Gold Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor representing a funding tier. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'acceptedBy' links a Paper to an Administrator indicating acceptance, while 'award' links something to an Award. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

A Workshop is a type of academic event/session at a conference, while a PowerPoint presentation is a specific format of presentation activity. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a person-like entity to a Conference, but their domains differ: cmt's 'memberOfConference' has domain 'Conference Member' (a role), while edas's 'isMemberOf' has domain 'Person'. They are semantically related but not strictly equivalent due to the domain mismatch.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster). In edas, 'Published Paper' is a status-based subclass of Paper indicating the paper has been published (sibling of Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). These represent orthogonal dimensions (format vs. publication status) and do not denote the same concept.

Entity A (Paper) is a document/artefact class representing the submitted paper itself, while Entity B (Author of paper) is a person/role class representing someone who authored a paper. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Paper is a scholarly contribution (a research paper submitted to a conference), while Form is an administrative document (registration form, author information form, etc.). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee for non-members/non-authors, but 'Nonauthor registration fee' (iasted) specifically targets people who are not authors, while 'Registration Non Member' (sigkdd) targets people who are not members of the organizing societies. These overlap in practice but have different defining criteria, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In confOf, 'Assistant' is a support/administrative role (sibling of Administrator, Volunteer), whereas in edas, 'Attendee' is someone who attends the conference (confOf has a separate 'Participant' class for that). These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

hasAuthor (Paper -> Author) and authorOf (Person -> Document) are inverse properties: hasAuthor links a paper to its author, while authorOf links an author to their document. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as inverses in the same domain.

In edas, Active Paper is a Paper that has a rating (i.e., has been reviewed), with children including Rated Papers and siblings like Accepted/Rejected Paper. In ekaw, Evaluated Paper is a paper that has been assigned and evaluated, with children Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper. Both classes represent papers that have undergone the review/evaluation process, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

An 'Extended abstract' is a short preliminary contribution (a type of regular contribution), while a 'Workshop Paper' is a full paper submitted to or presented at a workshop. These are distinct types of conference documents with different intended instances.

Organizing committee is a committee (a group/organizational entity) under Committee, while Session Chair is a person role under Person. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
hasFax and hasFirstName are distinct datatype properties capturing different information (fax number vs. first name) about a Person.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Poster Session is a type of event (a subclass of Session). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent fundamentally different concepts.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference organization structure), while Delegate in iasted is a subclass of Person/Registration (an attendee or participant). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

'Conference contributor' in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants), while 'Chair PC' in Ontology B specifically denotes the Program Committee Chair. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

hasPhone captures a phone number (domain: Contact Information) while E-mail captures an email address (domain: Person). Both are contact-related datatype properties with string range, but they represent different kinds of contact information and have different domains, so they are related but not equivalent.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it (inverse of 'gives'), while 'attendeeAt' links a Person to a Conference Event they attend. These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics: one denotes presenting/delivering, the other denotes attending.

Both are datatype properties for email addresses with range string, but they have different domains: contactEmail applies to Contribution (a paper/submission) while E-mail applies to Person. They relate different kinds of entities and thus are not equivalent.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion). They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

hasLocation (domain: Conference Event, range: Place) and locationOf (domain: Location, range: Event) are inverse properties of each other. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related.

'follows' in confOf denotes a temporal or sequential ordering between administrative events (one event follows another), whereas 'partOfEvent' in ekaw denotes a mereological part-whole relationship between events. These are semantically distinct relations.

rejectedBy links a Paper to an Administrator (the person who rejected it), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (the review document). Different ranges and different semantics; they are unrelated.

Paper in edas represents a scholarly paper/contribution submitted to a conference, while Form in iasted represents administrative forms (registration, hotel, author info). These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
Conference www is a type of conference document (a web resource with a URL), while Main office is a physical place. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A represents the date of a conference, while property B represents the city where the conference is held. They capture entirely different aspects (temporal vs. spatial) and are unrelated.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision in cmt, while is_made_from links an Item to another Item in iasted. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('was a committee chair of') relates a Chair to a Committee, indicating a leadership role in a committee. Property B ('give') relates a Person to an Activity or Item, indicating giving/presenting something. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Transport vehicle is a physical conveyance (car, bus, etc.). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Tutorial and Workshop are distinct types of conference events. In Ontology A they are siblings under 'Conference part', and in Ontology B Workshop is a Scientific Event with no Tutorial class present. They are related as similar sub-events of a conference but not equivalent.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item they acquire. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (spatial relation), while hasEvent links an Event to another Event (partonomic/temporal relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to submitted works (papers, posters, talks), while Conference in Ontology B refers to the conference event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

Publisher in Ontology A represents an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Topic in Ontology B represents a subject area (e.g., Antennas, CAD). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

locationOf relates a Location to an Event (indicating where an event takes place), while hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (indicating who organizes it). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring or submitting), while 'need' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., requiring equipment). These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and ranges.
Tutorial is a type of lecture/conference activity, while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a date string, while 'has Last Name' links a Person to their surname string. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

'has a name' is a general naming property applicable to conferences, proceedings, publishers, and topics, while 'has short title' is specifically for abbreviated titles of events. They overlap in purpose (naming) but differ significantly in scope and semantics, so they are related rather than equivalent.

startReviewerBidding is an action property from Administrator to Conference initiating the bidding phase, while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'expert On' relates a PC member to a topic (area of expertise), while 'is present in' relates a person to a place and time (physical/temporal presence). These are semantically unrelated properties.

Week Reject Rating is a type of review rating (a classification/score assigned to a paper), while Refusing manuscript is an activity/event (the act of rejecting a paper). They belong to fundamentally different categories in the conference domain.

Conference proceedings (A) refers to the published volume/book containing accepted papers, with properties like ISBN, volume, and publisher. Conference (B) in edas refers to the event itself, with properties like dates, country, members, and deadlines. These are distinct concepts: one is a publication artefact, the other is an event.

AccommodationPlace is a physical location (subclass of Place) where attendees can stay, while Deadline_hotel_reservation is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline) by which hotel reservations must be made. They belong to entirely different categories (place vs. time) and are not equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role for people contributing to the conference), while Banquet is a subclass of Social event (a type of event). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Property A (heldIn) relates an Event to a Location, while property B (is_present_in) relates a Person to a Place/Time. The domains are fundamentally different (Event vs Person), so they do not denote the same relation.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a subclass of 'Regular contribution' (distinguished from 'Extended abstract'), indicating it refers to a full/regular paper. In Ontology B, 'Regular Paper' is a specific type of 'Paper'. Both denote the same concept: a standard full-length conference paper, as opposed to short papers, posters, or abstracts.

Property A links a Conference to any Conference Member (a broad set of participants), while property B links a Conference volume specifically to an Organizing committee (a specific group responsible for organization). An organizing committee is a kind of conference member group, so the properties overlap in intent but differ in scope; B is more specific than A, making them related rather than equivalent.
Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer), while Positive Review in ekaw is a document (a type of review). They are entirely different concepts.

The 'name' property in cmt provides a name for a Conference or Person, while 'starts on' in confOf provides a start date string for an Event. These are semantically completely different properties with different domains and meanings.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'invited by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer (indicating invitation). They are unrelated.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a type of regular contribution (a document kind), while in Ontology B, 'Active Paper' is a status-based subclass of 'Paper' (indicating the paper is actively under review/consideration). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent: one classifies by document type, the other by lifecycle status. The closest match for edas's 'Paper' would be Conference A's 'Paper', making 'Active Paper' a more specific state-related concept.
writtenBy relates a contribution to its author, while hasReviewer relates a paper to a possible reviewer. These are entirely different relations with different semantics and ranges.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Communications Topic in edas is a subject area/topic for papers. These are entirely different concepts.

reviewsPerPaper captures the number of reviews per paper (int) for a conference, while City_of_conference captures the city name (string) where the conference is held. They describe entirely different attributes.

'has workshops' is a specific part-whole property linking a Conference volume to its Workshops, while 'partOfEvent' is a general part-whole property linking any Event to another Event. They are related as both express mereological relations in the conference domain, but they differ in direction (has-part vs part-of), specificity, and domain/range constraints, so they are not equivalent.

Committee in Ontology A refers to conference-specific committees (organizing, program, steering) with chairs and members, while Organization in edas refers to external entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorship. These are conceptually distinct in the conference domain.

providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides the sponsorship), while is_paid_in links Money to a Building (where payment occurs). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where meetings occur, while Conference Banquet is a social event (subclass of Social Event). They belong to fundamentally different categories (place vs. event) and are unrelated.

Member PC in confOf is a person (reviewer) who reviews contributions, while Numerical Review Question in edas is a type of review question expecting a numerical answer. These are entirely different concepts.

Reviewing event is an administrative event (a process/activity for reviewing submissions), while Organizing Committee is a committee (a group of people). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Conference_part in Ontology A groups Track, Tutorial, and Workshop as structural parts of a conference. Individual_Presentation in ekaw is a Scientific Event whose children include Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, and Tutorial, while Track, Workshop, and Session are siblings (not children). They overlap on Tutorial but differ significantly: Conference_part includes Track and Workshop as sub-classes, whereas ekaw treats them as sibling events. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers, while Sponzor (Sponsor) is an entity that provides financial support to the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'enter Conference Details' is a property for an Administrator to input conference metadata into the system (domain: Administrator, range: Conference), while 'organises' denotes that an Organisation or Person organises an Event (domain: Organisation/Person, range: Event). These describe fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Operating Topicsystems is a specific topic area in the edas ontology. They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area, while publisherOf links an Organisation to published documents (Flyer, etc.). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A links a Review to the contribution it reviews, while property B links a Document to an earlier version of itself. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Reviewer in edas is a Person who performs reviews, while Review in ekaw is a Document (the review artefact itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (agent vs. document) and thus unrelated.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'has Related Document' links various entities (events, persons) to documents. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'acceptedBy' relates a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (indicating giving/presenting). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A 'send' relates a Person to an Item (a sending/submission action), while property B 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents the document). These describe fundamentally different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Contribution is a superclass with children Paper, Poster, and Short paper. In sigkdd, Paper is a specific type of Document. Therefore, confOf:Contribution subsumes sigkdd:Paper, as it includes papers along with other contribution types like posters and short papers.

hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (a reviewer's bidding preference), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (an evaluation). Bids and Reviews are distinct concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Award is a prize given for papers. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Person is the top-level class for all people involved in a conference (Chairman, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc.). In iasted, Speaker is a subclass of Delegate and specifically denotes someone who presents; it has children Author and Reviewer but excludes non-presenting roles like Listener or Non speaker. Thus cmt:Person is strictly more general than iasted:Speaker.

Accepted contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted after review, while Week Reject Rating is a specific rating value used in the review process. They are entirely different concepts.
volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to the papers it contains, while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Pending Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a subclass of Deadline (a time concept). They are entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

'organised By' links an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. The domains (Event vs Document), ranges (Organisation/Person vs Speaker), and semantics (organizing vs presenting) are entirely different.

Workshop is a type of working event (an academic session), while Conference hotel is a type of building (a physical venue/accommodation). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (its title), while hasReview is an object property linking a Paper to a Review object. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and property types.

Regular in confOf is a type of Participant (alongside Member and Student), representing a standard/regular attendee. Student non speaker in iasted is specifically a student who does not present. These are different categories: one denotes registration type, the other denotes student status combined with speaking role. They do not share the same intended instances.

Student is a subclass of Person representing a role, while Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Registration fee (Money) representing a cost. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), representing the textual abstract of a paper. Paper Presentation in edas is a type of conference event (subclass of Academic Event), representing the act of presenting a paper at a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. event) and are unrelated.

Regular author in Ontology A is a type of conference contribution/contributor (a person who submits a regular paper), while Tutorial speaker in Ontology B is a specific role of a speaker who gives tutorials. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.
Short paper is a type of contribution/submission, while Cryptography Topic is a subject area topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Sponsor in iasted is a general class for sponsors (under Person), while Bronze Supporter in sigkdd is a specific tier of sponsor/supporter. The general Sponsor class subsumes the more specific Bronze Supporter class.

acceptedBy links a Paper to an Administrator (acceptance decision), while scientificallyOrganisedBy links an entity to an Academic Institution (organizational role). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Paper is a general class for all papers (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). In ekaw, Poster Paper is a specific subtype of Paper. Therefore, edas:Paper subsumes ekaw:Poster_Paper.

Paper Full Version is a complete academic paper submission, while Cheque is a payment document. They belong to entirely different subdomains (paper submission vs. financial payment) and share no meaningful relationship.
isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship, while locationOf relates a Location to an Event. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (a reviewer's bidding preference), while dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Hotel fee is a monetary charge for accommodation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Submission is a document (manuscript) submitted to a conference, while Committee is a group of people organizing or reviewing for the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

'has tracks' relates a conference volume to its tracks (a part-whole relationship), while 'holded by' relates a conference to its organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Conference Session is a type of event (a session within a conference), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference giving an integer count of reviews per paper, while reviewOfPaper is an object property linking a Review to the Paper it reviews. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range, and semantics.

Invited talk is a type of conference contribution/presentation (a specific talk given by an invited speaker), while Demo Session is a type of session event where demonstrations are presented. They represent different concepts in the conference domain: one is a contribution/presentation artefact, the other is a scheduled session event.
Workshop is a type of working event (a session or meeting format), while Session chair is a role played by a delegate (a person). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'references' is a general citation/reference relation between documents or entities, while 'awarded by' links an Award to the entity that grants it. These are semantically unrelated properties.
isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event, while need relates a Person to an Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

paperID is a datatype property assigning an unsigned long identifier to a Paper, while presentationOfPaper is an object property linking an Individual Presentation to a Paper or Abstract. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Event in ekaw represents conference occurrences (scientific events, social events) with locations and organizers, while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts (conference days, deadlines, trip days). These are fundamentally different concepts.
Conference in edas denotes the event/organisation itself, while Conference Participant in ekaw denotes a person attending or involved in the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.
'is used by' is an object property linking Item to Person, while 'E mail' is a datatype property linking Person to a string. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

'parallel with' in confOf relates two Administrative events that occur simultaneously (e.g., parallel sessions). 'inverse of part Of 7' in ekaw is an inverse-of-partOf property relating something to an Event, expressing a mereological (part-whole) relationship rather than temporal parallelism. These are semantically distinct relations.
PC Chair is a program committee leadership role, while Tutorial speaker is a person who presents a tutorial. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'Author book proceedings included' is a subclass of Author (under Speaker), representing an author whose work appears in the book proceedings. In sigkdd, 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Speaker and a sibling of Author, representing someone invited to speak. These are distinct roles: one is about publication inclusion, the other about being invited to present. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.
Administrator is a person role responsible for managing the conference system, while Mailing list is a type of document. They are completely unrelated concepts.
The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'awarded by' relates an Award to some entity. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership/organizational role (chairman of the conference), while Worker lecturer in iasted is a type of lecturer/speaker who presents at the conference. These are entirely different roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author (a person who authored a paper but is not a reviewer), while Attendee is a general class for anyone attending the conference. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances; an author-not-reviewer may or may not be an attendee, and an attendee need not be an author.

In cmt, 'Program Committee Chair' is a specific kind of Chairman (sibling to Conference Chair and Associated Chair). In Conference, 'Chair' is a general class with 'Co chair' as a sibling, representing any committee chair. Thus, the more specific Program Committee Chair in cmt is subsumed by the more general Chair in Conference.

confOf:Organization is a general class with children Company and University, while edas:AcademiaOrganization is a specific subclass of edas:Organization representing only academic institutions. Thus confOf:Organization subsumes edas:AcademiaOrganization.

Sponsorship in edas is a financial support arrangement (with cost amount/currency, provided by an Organization), while Person in iasted is a human individual class (parent of Delegate and Sponsor). These are entirely different concepts.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Registration SIGMOD Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

'Information for participants' refers to pre-conference informational documents (like calls, announcements), while 'Record of attendance' is a post-event document recording who attended. They are distinct types of conference documents with no overlap in intended instances.
Administrator is a person role responsible for managing the conference system, while Review is a document representing an evaluation of a submission. They are entirely different concepts.

Co author in cmt is a subclass of Author (a person who co-writes papers), while Author attendee book registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and are unrelated.

In edas, Industry Organization is a subclass of Organization (an organizational entity), while in iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (an individual). They differ both in ontological category (organization vs person) and in role (industry affiliation vs sponsorship), making them unrelated.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper submission, while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Chair in Ontology A is a committee chair (head of a committee), while Session chair in Ontology B chairs a specific session at the conference. Both are leadership/chairing roles but operate at different levels (committee vs. session), so they are related but not equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while a 'Tutorial' is a type of lecture/conference activity (an event). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

A 'Short paper' is a type of academic contribution/submission, while an 'Invitation letter' is an administrative document used for visa or attendance purposes. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Administrator in cmt is a system/conference management role (assigns reviewers, accepts papers, enters conference details), while Paper Author in ekaw is someone who authored a paper. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.
User is a person role in the conference system (parent of Author, Reviewer, etc.), while Hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are completely unrelated concepts.

'Information for participants' in Conference ontology refers to logistical or administrative information provided to attendees (e.g., calls, announcements), whereas 'Conference Proceedings' in ekaw is a multi-author volume containing the published papers of the conference. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

In edas, Social Event is a general class with children Excursion and Reception. In ekaw, Conference Trip is a specific type of Social Event (sibling to Conference Banquet). A conference trip/excursion is a kind of social event, so edas:SocialEvent subsumes ekaw:Conference_Trip, but they are not equivalent since edas:SocialEvent also includes receptions and meals. The closest relation is 'related' as one is broader than the other but 'subsumes' would require the pair to be in that direction; however, since edas:SocialEvent strictly contains ekaw:Conference_Trip instances, 'subsumes' is more precise.

Conference Member in cmt is a Person who participates in a conference (e.g., author, reviewer), while Conference in confOf is an Event (a type of working event). They denote entirely different concepts.

In edas, 'Two Level Conference' has TPC Member as a parent class (likely a modeling artifact), making it overlap with the concept of a program committee member. In sigkdd, 'Program Committee member' is a role under Organizator. While both relate to program committee membership, 'Two Level Conference' primarily denotes a type of conference rather than purely a person/role, so they are related but not equivalent.

Both are datatype properties mapping to string for naming purposes. However, A (has a name) has a broader domain including Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, and Topic, while B (has Name) is restricted to Conference only. Thus B is subsumed by A.

Abstract in ekaw is a summary of a paper or presentation, while Form in iasted refers to administrative documents like registration forms. They are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' solicits paper submissions from authors, while B 'Call For Reviews' solicits reviews from reviewers. They are both types of calls in the conference domain but target different activities and participants, so they are related (siblings under a common Call concept) rather than equivalent.
One property captures a person's last name while the other captures a phone number; they represent entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range types.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person, representing only those persons who serve on a committee. In Ontology B, 'Person' is the top-level class for all people (including authors, participants, volunteers, etc.), with 'Member PC' as a child. Thus, Committee member in A is subsumed by Person in B.

Passive conference participant is a type of person attending a conference without an active role, while Single Level Conference is a type of conference event structure. They are entirely different concepts.
Published Paper is a paper that has been published, while Mailing list is a document used for mailing purposes. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' is a specific administrative action linking an Administrator to a Conference, while 'write' is a general authoring action linking a Person to an Item. They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference airport is a physical place/building. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Antennas Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Card is a physical item (e.g., credit card). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Both properties link an event-like entity to another event/activity (Working event -> Administrative event vs Item -> Activity). In the conference domain, 'go through' likely means an item undergoes an activity, which overlaps with a working event having an administrative event, but the domains and ranges differ in specificity and naming, making them related rather than equivalent.
hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members, while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A specifies a 'starting date' for Important dates, while Property B is a generic 'Date' for a Deadline. They are both date-related datatype properties in the conference domain but differ in specificity (start date vs. general/deadline date) and domain (Important dates vs. Deadline), so they are related rather than equivalent.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), representing the overall conference gathering. In iasted, Welcome address is a specific activity that occurs during a conference (a sub-event). These are entirely different concepts: one is the overarching event, the other is a minor scheduled activity within it.

presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract, while give links a Person to an Activity/Item. They have different domains (event vs person) and different ranges (paper vs activity/item), so they are unrelated.

Conference Venue Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where the conference is held, while Conference Trip is a social event/activity (subclass of Social Event). They are fundamentally different concepts.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (bidding on papers), while invited_by relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (invitation chain). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a very broad class encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and PC Members—essentially any person affiliated with the conference. In Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is narrower, specifically a member of a committee (with children Chair and Co-chair), and is a sibling to 'Conference contributor' (which likely covers authors). Thus, Committee member is more specific than Conference Member; they overlap but are not equivalent.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a broad class encompassing any committee role (Chair, Co-chair, Reviewer, etc.), while in Ontology B, 'Member PC' specifically denotes a Program Committee member who reviews contributions (comment: 'Reviewer'). They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent because A's Committee member includes non-PC roles and B's Member PC is narrower.

Conference in Ontology A represents the overall academic conference event/organization, while Social event in confOf is a specific type of social gathering (banquet, reception, trip) that occurs during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
External Reviewer is a person who reviews papers on behalf of another reviewer, while Paper Author is a person who authored a paper. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'forEvent' links a Call to an Academic Event, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Meta Reviewer in cmt is a specialized reviewer who oversees other reviews for a paper, while Member PC in confOf is a general program committee member/reviewer. They overlap in function (both review papers) but Meta Reviewer is a more specific role than the general PC member, so they are related rather than equivalent.

'has a name' is a datatype property linking entities to their string names, while 'manuscript Due On' links a Conference to a dateTime deadline. They represent entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

The 'email' property relates a Person to their email address (string), while the 'Price' property relates a Registration fee to its cost (int). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Regular contribution in Conference refers to a specific type of conference contribution (with children Extended abstract and Paper), while Submission in iasted refers to any submitted document (with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript). They overlap conceptually since regular contributions are typically submitted, but they are not equivalent: Regular contribution is a content/presentation type, whereas Submission is a process/status type encompassing broader documents.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a general class for regular conference contributions (a sibling of Extended abstract). In Ontology B, 'Workshop Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper, restricted to workshop submissions. The general 'Paper' in A is broader and not equivalent to the specialized 'Workshop Paper' in B; they overlap as both are types of papers but differ in scope.

In cmt, Review is a subclass of Document (with Paper as a sibling). In ekaw, Document is a top-level class that has Review and Paper as children. Thus, cmt:Review corresponds to ekaw:Review, not ekaw:Document. ekaw:Document is strictly more general than cmt:Review.

Both classes represent an individual presentation at a conference. Ontology A's Presentation has children like 'Invited talk' and is linked to abstracts and participants; Ontology B's Individual_Presentation has children like 'Contributed Talk', 'Invited Talk', 'Tutorial' and is linked to papers/abstracts via paperPresentedAs/presentationOfPaper. Despite different modeling choices (A treats it as a Conference contribution/document, B as a Scientific Event), their intended instances coincide: individual oral presentations given at a conference.

Both properties link a paper (Accepted Paper in edas, Paper/Abstract in ekaw) to its presentation event (Paper Presentation in edas, Individual Presentation in ekaw). The domain and range classes are closely aligned across the two ontologies, making these properties equivalent in the conference domain.

Property A ('is part of conference volumes') is a specific meronymic property restricted to domain 'Conference part' and range 'Conference volume'. Property B ('partOf') in ekaw is a general part-of relation with unspecified domain and range. Thus A is a specialization (subproperty) of B, meaning A is subsumed by B.
A is a topic classification (Parallel And Distributed Computing) while B is an award type (Best Research Paper Award). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

An 'Invited speaker' is specifically someone invited to give a talk (e.g., keynote), while a 'Presenter' in edas is any author who presents their paper. They overlap (both present at a conference) but are not equivalent: an invited speaker need not be a paper author, and most presenters are not invited speakers.

confOf:Participant is a general class for all conference participants (with children Member, Regular, Student), while ekaw:OC_Member is a specific role (Organizing Committee Member) under Conference Participant. Thus Participant subsumes OC_Member.
Conference hotel is a physical building/place where attendees stay, while Conference in sigkdd represents the conference event itself (with dates, name, city). These are entirely different concepts.
Conference Paper is a type of document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Main office is a type of place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while property B links a paper to its author. These relate entirely different concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Hotel fee is a monetary charge for accommodation. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference proceedings is a published document/volume containing papers, while Activity in iasted refers to events or actions (e.g., conference activities). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Scholar in confOf is a subclass of Person (a role for an academic), while Author attendee book registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (likely a financial backer or sponsor representative), while in sigkdd, Organizator is a person who organizes the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). These are distinct roles in the conference domain and do not denote the same concept.

In confOf, 'Member PC' is a reviewer (comment: 'Reviewer') with properties like 'reviewes' and 'expert On', and is a sibling of 'Chair PC'. In sigkdd, 'Program Chair' is an organizer role, distinct from 'Program Committee member' which appears as a sibling. Thus, Member PC in confOf corresponds to Program Committee member in sigkdd, not to Program Chair.

Person in Ontology A is a top-level class covering all people involved in a conference (participants, reviewers, contributors, etc.). Speaker in Ontology B is a subclass of Person, specifically those who give presentations. Therefore, Person subsumes Speaker.
Workshop is a type of academic event, while Lecturer is a type of person (author/speaker). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Property A is a datatype property for the title of a Paper (string), while Property B is a datatype property for the ending date of Important dates (date). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Regular author in Ontology A denotes a person (an author/contributor), while Regular Paper in Ontology B denotes a document (a paper). Despite sharing the word 'Regular', they refer to fundamentally different concepts (person vs. artefact) and are unrelated.

Session Chair in ekaw is a role responsible for chairing a session (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). Listener in iasted is a delegate who listens to presentations (subclass of Delegate). These are distinct roles; notably, iasted has its own 'Session chair' class as a sibling of Listener, confirming they are different concepts.
isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker. These are entirely different concepts and relations in the conference domain.

In cmt, Review is a document (subclass of Document) written by a reviewer about a paper. In Conference, Review expertise represents the level of expertise or knowledge a reviewer has regarding a topic or contribution. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an artefact (a review document), the other is a qualification or attribute (expertise).

hasPhone relates a Person to their phone number string, while hasStreet relates Contact Information to a street address string. They represent entirely different contact attributes (phone vs. street) with different domains.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting paper submissions, while Operating Topicsystems is a specific topic classification within the edas ontology. They are entirely different concepts.

'Conference contributor' in Ontology A is a broad class under Person encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. 'Session chair' in Ontology B is a specific role under Delegate for someone who chairs a session. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances; a session chair is not necessarily a contributor (e.g., author/speaker), and a contributor is not necessarily a session chair.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee, but A is specifically for nonmembers while B is for SIGKDD members. They represent different member categories and thus overlap only in being registration fees, not equivalent.
An Invited speaker is a person who presents at the conference, while a Listener is an attendee who listens to presentations. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

The property 'title' in cmt relates a Paper to its title string, while 'has Street' in edas relates Contact Information to a street address string. These are completely different concepts with different domains and semantics.

A Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing during the conference), while a Travel Grant is a form of sponsorship (financial support for travel). They are conceptually distinct: one is an activity/event, the other is funding.

In edas, ConferenceVenuePlace is a subclass of Place (alongside AccommodationPlace, DiningPlace, etc.), meaning it denotes specifically the venue where the conference takes place. In sigkdd, Place is the top-level class for all locations (including Hotel and Main office). Thus, edas:ConferenceVenuePlace is more specific than sigkdd:Place, making it subsumed_by sigkdd:Place.

An Organizational Meeting is an administrative/organizational event within a conference, while a Poster Session is a scientific session where posters are presented. They represent entirely different types of conference events with no hierarchical or semantic overlap.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Aapplications Topic is a subject topic for papers. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person representing a conference attendee, while Student registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Money/Fee representing a monetary amount. They are entirely different concepts.

Co chair is a specific committee leadership role (child of Committee member), while Possible Reviewer is a broad class of people who may review papers (parent of PC Member). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Organisation is an institution or agency. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a version/format of a paper (the abstract portion), while Workshop Paper in ekaw is a type of paper based on the venue it is submitted to (a workshop). These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.

Company in confOf is a type of Organization (sibling of University), typically representing commercial entities. Organising Agency in ekaw is a type of Organisation responsible for organizing the conference (sibling of Academic Institution, Proceedings Publisher). While a company could potentially act as an organising agency, they are conceptually different: one classifies by entity type (commercial organization) and the other by role (organizer). They overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A (isLocationOf) has domain Place and range Conference Event, while property B (is_held_in) has domain Activity and range Place,Time. They express inverse directions of the same conceptual relationship (a place hosting an event vs. an event being held in a place). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent per the guidelines, they are related.

Property A relates a Committee to its Chair (membership/leadership), while property B relates a person (Chair or TPC Member) to a Call they initiate. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'occupy' relates a Person to a physical location (Building, City, State), while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Paid applicant in Ontology A is a person who has registered and paid for the conference (a registration/payment status concept), while Author in sigkdd is a speaker who submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different intended instances.

'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'designed by' relates a Deadline to an organization (ACM SIGKDD). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Conference is a Working event (the main academic conference itself), whereas in ekaw, Conference Trip is a Social Event (an excursion or trip organized during the conference). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Social Event in edas is a non-academic event (e.g., excursions, receptions), while Scientific Event in ekaw covers academic activities (conferences, sessions, workshops). They are disjoint sibling concepts under the broader Event hierarchy, not equivalent.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a specific type of Paper (a Document), while Document in iasted is a broad class encompassing many types of documents (forms, letters, reviews, submissions, etc.). Thus, Paper Full Version is subsumed by the more general Document class in iasted.
Property A links a reviewed contribution (paper) to its review, while property B links a personal review history to a reviewer. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both are datatype properties mapping a conference entity to a string representing its location. However, 'has a location' is more general (could be any location string) while 'City of conference' specifically denotes the city. Their domains also differ slightly ('Conference volume' vs 'Conference'). They are related but not strictly equivalent.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers), while Coffee Break is a non-academic break event during a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

In edas, 'Pending Paper' is a sibling of 'Accepted Paper', 'Rejected Paper', and 'Withdrawn Paper', indicating it represents a paper that has been submitted but not yet decided upon. In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is the general class for papers that have been submitted (with 'Assigned Paper' as a child). While both refer to papers in the submission pipeline before acceptance/rejection, 'Pending Paper' specifically denotes the awaiting-decision state, whereas 'Submitted Paper' is broader (any paper that has been submitted). They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent.
hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area, while obtain links a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In cmt, Rejection is a subclass of Decision (an act/outcome), while in edas, Rejected Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been rejected). They are closely related conceptually but belong to different class hierarchies (decision vs. paper state), so they are not equivalent.

An Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event (an activity), while an Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Registration SIGKDD Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.

Organization in confOf represents institutions (Company, University) that employ people, while Person in sigkdd represents individual human participants (Listener, Speaker, Organizator). These are fundamentally different concepts.
Reception is a social event (a type of gathering), while Speaker is a person/role (a delegate who speaks). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference fees is a general concept covering all fees associated with a conference (including registration fees), while Sponzor fee is specifically the fee paid by sponsors. In ontology B, Registration fee is a sibling of Sponzor fee under Fee, indicating Conference fees would be closer to the parent class Fee rather than equivalent to Sponzor fee alone.

listsEvent is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event, while End_of_conference is a datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime value. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

State in iasted is a geographical/administrative location (with children like Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state and properties like is_situated_in), while Conference in sigkdd is an event (the conference itself with start/end dates, name, city). These are entirely different concepts.

confOf:Person is a top-level class for all people in the conference domain (including authors, administrators, etc.), while ekaw:Conference_Participant is a subclass of ekaw:Person specifically for those participating in the conference. Thus confOf:Person subsumes ekaw:Conference_Participant.

Property A (date) is a general datatype property giving the date of a Conference, while Property B (is_a_date_of_acceptance_announcement) is a specific datatype property for the acceptance announcement date within Important dates. They have different domains and different levels of specificity, making them unrelated.

Property A 'contributes' specifically links a Person to a Conference document they authored/contributed to. Property B 'has Related Document' is much broader: its domain includes Academic Event, Conference, Conference Session, and Person, and it denotes any related document, not necessarily a contribution. They overlap when the domain is Person and the document is a contribution, but are not equivalent.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where attendees stay, while Hotel fee is a monetary charge (subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent.

Both classes represent papers that have undergone the review/evaluation process. 'Rated Papers' in edas (child of Active Paper) and 'Evaluated Paper' in ekaw (parent of Accepted/Rejected Paper) denote the same concept: a paper for which reviews/ratings have been submitted. The different labels ('Rated' vs 'Evaluated') are synonymous in this context.

Sponsorship in edas refers to financial support (with cost amount, currency, and provider organization), while Sponsor city in iasted is a subclass of City representing a location. These are entirely different concepts.
Review Question is a type of question used in a review form (with numerical/textual subtypes), while Possible Reviewer is a person who may review papers. These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties express the same relation: an author/person writes a contribution/item (paper). In the conference domain, Author corresponds to Person and Contribution corresponds to Item, making these properties equivalent.

Both Trip (confOf) and Excursion (edas) represent the same concept: an organized outing or tour as a social event during a conference. They share the same parent class (Social event/Social Event) and similar sibling context (Reception), making them equivalent in the conference domain.

The property 'detailsEnteredBy' relates a Conference to an Administrator (entering conference details), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authoring). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties describe entirely different relations: 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Industry Organization in edas refers to a commercial/corporate entity (a type of organization by sector), while Organising Agency in ekaw refers to the body responsible for organizing the conference (a functional role). An industry organization could potentially serve as an organising agency, but the concepts are not equivalent; they overlap only tangentially.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Publication is a published document or proceedings. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

NGO (Non-Governmental Organization) and Proceedings Publisher are both subclasses of Organization/Organisation but represent entirely different concepts. An NGO is a type of non-profit organization, while a Proceedings Publisher is an entity responsible for publishing conference proceedings. They do not share the same intended instances.
Welcome Talk is a type of conference event (a talk), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while has_an_abstract links a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (content relation). They relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.

A Workshop is a working event (typically interactive, hands-on sessions), while a Plenary lecture is a type of lecture delivered to all attendees. They are distinct kinds of conference activities with different intended instances.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Conference building is a physical place/building. They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a city string. They describe entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and purposes.
'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while 'partOf' is a generic mereological/parthood relation. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.

hasRelatedDocument is a general property linking various entities (events, persons) to documents, while presentation specifically links a Speaker to a Document they present.
