They overlap in the Person/Speaker-to-Document case but differ significantly in scope and domain, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A relates an Abstract to the document it is part of (Paper, Poster, Presentation), while Property B relates an Author to a Contribution they write. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasLocation relates a Conference Event to a Place, while is_present_in relates a Person to a Place/Time. The domains are fundamentally different (event vs person), so these properties are not equivalent.

Presenter in ekaw is a subclass of Person (a conference participant who presents), while Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State (an abstract status/state). These are entirely different concepts.

Contribution represents a submitted academic work (paper, poster, etc.), while Sponzor represents a financial sponsor of the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'has gender' and 'has Surname' are both datatype properties on Person but capture entirely different attributes (gender vs. family name). They are unrelated.

Both classes represent a paper in the conference domain. Although Ontology A's Paper is a subclass of Regular contribution (excluding extended abstracts) and Ontology B's Paper is a broader Document subclass with many children (including Conference Paper, Submitted Paper, etc.), both denote the same core concept of a conference paper. The OAEI reference alignment treats these as equivalent.

Reviewer (cmt) is a specific role responsible for reviewing papers, while Conference Participant (ekaw) is a broad class encompassing all attendees and organizers (chairs, presenters, registered participants). They are not equivalent; Reviewer does not even appear as a subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw (which has Possible Reviewer as a sibling instead).

In edas, TalkEvent is a general class for talk-type events with children ClosingTalk and WelcomeTalk, and PaperPresentation as a sibling. In ekaw, Contributed_Talk is a specific kind of Individual Presentation (contrasted with Invited_Talk and Tutorial). Thus edas:TalkEvent is more general and subsumes ekaw:Contributed_Talk.

Paper in edas refers to a submitted academic paper, while Transparency in iasted refers to presentation slides/overheads. They are distinct types of documents with different purposes in the conference domain.

In confOf, Poster is a type of Contribution (a document/artefact), sibling to Paper and Short paper. In ekaw, Poster Session is a type of Session (an event), sibling to Conference Session and Demo Session. A poster (document) and a poster session (event where posters are presented) are distinct concepts in the conference domain, though they are related.
hasHomePage links a Person to their homepage URL string, while hasLastName links a Person to their last name string. These are entirely different attributes of a person and thus unrelated.
'authorOf' relates a Person to a Document they authored, while 'need' relates a Person to an Item they require. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and ranges.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision in the cmt ontology, while is_used_for links an Item to an Activity or Money in the iasted ontology. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Event in confOf is a general conference event (administrative, social, working), while Award in sigkdd is a prize given to authors/papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while holded_by links a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (an assignment relation), while has_a_review_expertise links a Submitted contribution to a Review expertise (a topic/expertise classification). They relate different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Free Time Break is a type of conference event. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Review is a document containing an evaluation of a paper, while SlideSet is a collection of presentation slides. They are distinct types of documents with different purposes in the conference domain.

Both properties link a Paper to a reviewer role, but they target different specific roles: 'read By Meta Reviewer' has range Meta Reviewer (a person who reads/evaluates reviews), while 'has Reviewer' has range Possible Reviewer (a candidate to review the paper). They are related as both connect papers to reviewer-type entities, but are not equivalent due to the distinct roles involved.

Workshop in ontology A and Track in ontology B are distinct types of conference sub-events. In ontology B (ekaw), Workshop and Track are siblings under Scientific Event, confirming they are separate concepts. They do not denote the same thing.
Submitted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been submitted), while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for reserving a hotel. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference in ekaw is an event (one edition of a conference), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place/venue where events are held. They belong to different categories (Event vs Place) and are not equivalent.

'is prepared by' links an Item to the Person who prepared it (authoring/creation), while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains, ranges, and directions differ: one is about preparation/authorship, the other about delivering a presentation. They are not equivalent nor inverses.

locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while Name_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string. They describe entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In confOf, 'Assistant' (commented as confTool) typically refers to a student assistant or helper role in conference organization. In ekaw, 'Student' is a person who is a student. While they overlap (student assistants are students), they are not strictly equivalent: 'Assistant' emphasizes an organizational role while 'Student' emphasizes academic status. They are related but not equivalent.

Delegate in iasted represents any person attending/registered for the conference (including speakers, listeners, session chairs, etc.), while Organizator in sigkdd specifically represents people who organize the conference (chairs, committee members, webmaster). They overlap (e.g., Session chair / Technical commitee in Delegate vs Program Committee member in Organizator) but are not equivalent; Delegate is broader and includes non-organizing attendees.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all submitted papers (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version). In edas, Rated Papers is a specific subclass of Active Paper (which is a subclass of Paper), representing only those papers that have been rated. Thus, cmt:Paper subsumes edas:RatedPapers.
Student is a person role in the conference domain, while Single hotel room is an accommodation type. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants in a conference, while PC Chair (B) is a specific role within the program committee. A subsumes B since every PC Chair is a conference participant, but not vice versa.

Both properties link a written/presented artefact to the person responsible (Item->Person vs Document->Speaker). In the conference domain, 'is written by' refers to authorship while 'presentationed by' refers to presenting. Authors and speakers often overlap but are not identical roles, so these properties are related but not equivalent.

'locationOf' relates a Location to an Event (spatial containment), while 'is_used for' relates an Item to an Activity or Money (instrumental usage). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

'has Country' links an Organization or Person to a Country (a geopolitical entity), while 'is present in' links a Person to a Place or Time (physical/temporal presence). These have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference participant (A) is a subclass of Person representing an attendee, while Conference (B) represents the event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts in the domain.

Workshop in edas is a type of conference event (an activity/session), while Workshop Paper in ekaw is a type of document/paper submitted to or presented at a workshop. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. document) and are not equivalent.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference hall in iasted is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered to apply/attend the conference (with child 'Paid applicant'), while a 'Presenter' in ekaw is a conference participant who presents work (with child 'Invited Speaker'). These are distinct roles: one concerns registration status, the other concerns presenting at the event. They are not equivalent and do not subsume each other.
Conference proceedings is a publication/document class, while Time is a temporal concept class. They are entirely unrelated.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of Working event), while Non speaker in iasted is a type of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.
Member PC in confOf is a program committee member/reviewer (reviews contributions), while Webmaster in sigkdd is an organizer responsible for the website. These are distinct roles with no overlap.

Student lecturer (iasted) is a Lecturer who is a student, while Author of paper student (sigkdd) is an Author who is a student. Both represent students participating in the conference as presenters/authors, but 'lecturer' and 'author of paper' are not strictly equivalent roles. They overlap conceptually (student presenters) but differ in their specific modeling focus.
Invited speaker is a person role (subclass of Conference contributor), while Conference city is a location (subclass of City). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'reject Paper' is a specific action by an Administrator to reject a Paper, while 'give' is a general property for a Person giving an Activity or Item. They differ in domain, range, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'isInitiatedBy' links a Call to chairs/TPC members who initiated it, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document they present.

In edas, 'Slide Set' is a specific subclass of Document (a set of presentation slides). In iasted, 'Document' is the general class for all documents, and it includes 'Transparency' as a child, which is the equivalent concept to Slide Set. Therefore, edas:SlideSet is subsumed by iasted:Document.

Property A (writeReview) links a Reviewer to a Review they authored. Property B (belongs_to_a_review_reference) links a Topic to a Review preference. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Review is a document evaluating a paper in the conference domain, while Value added tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A ('has a volume') describes the number of volumes in conference proceedings (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int). Property B ('max Choice') describes a maximum choice limit for social/working events (domain: Social event, Working event, range: positiveInteger). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in edas represents the academic event itself, while Conference hotel in iasted is a physical building (subclass of Building) used as accommodation for the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Active Paper in edas is a paper that has received a rating (parent of Rated Papers, sibling of Accepted/Rejected), whereas Rejected Paper in ekaw is specifically a paper that was evaluated and rejected. These denote different stages/outcomes in the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent.

markConflictOfInterest flags a conflict between a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) and a Paper, preventing assignment or review. 'reviewes' links a PC Member to a Contribution they are reviewing. These properties express entirely different relations with different semantics and directions.

Security Topic in edas is a specific kind of topic (a sibling among many specialized topics like CAD Topic, Antennas Topic), whereas Research Topic in ekaw is the general class for all research topics. Thus, Security Topic is subsumed by Research Topic.

A Meta Review is a specific type of review document (a senior reviewer's summary/evaluation), while a Review Form is a template or form used to collect review information. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Published Paper' is a scholarly paper that has been published, while a 'Record of attendance' is a document recording someone's attendance at the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version (cmt) represents the complete version of a paper, contrasted with Paper Abstract. Initial manuscript (iasted) represents the first submission of a paper, contrasted with Final manuscript. These are different dimensions of paper versions: completeness vs. revision stage. They overlap in that both can refer to a full submitted paper, but they are not equivalent concepts.

Submitted contribution is a document/artefact (a paper that has been submitted), while Reviewing event is an administrative event (the process of reviewing contributions). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level (domain: Submitted contribution, range: Review expertise), while property B links a PC member to a contribution they review (domain: Member PC, range: Contribution). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Aapplications Topic in edas is a specific sub-topic under Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Both are top-level classes named 'Person' representing human individuals in the conference domain. Their children (authors, participants, speakers, organizers, listeners) are all specific roles of people at a conference, confirming they denote the same concept.

assignReviewer is a specific property linking an Administrator to a Reviewer for the purpose of review assignment. 'give' is a very general property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.
University is an academic organization/institution, while Review is a document evaluating a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a specific research topic (subclass of Topic), while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event (subclass of Individual Presentation). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while is_designed_for links Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Organizer is a class representing a person or role responsible for organizing the conference, while Organizational Meeting is an event (a type of Academic Event) that takes place during the conference. They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. event) and share only a lexical root.

Talk Event in edas is a type of academic event (e.g., welcome talk, closing talk), while Conference days in iasted is a temporal concept representing the days of the conference. They belong to different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

University is an academic organization where scholars study, while Tip is a form of money/gratuity. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.
Radio Communications Topic is a subject area for papers, while Transport vehicle is a physical conveyance (car, taxi, etc.). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Computer Networks Topic is a research subject area in the conference domain, while Transport vehicle is a physical means of transportation. They are completely unrelated concepts.

The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and semantics (printing mailing manifests vs issuing proceedings). They are unrelated.
Workshop is a conference program element (a session or sub-event), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of working event (a session or track within a conference), while a Contributed Talk is an individual presentation given by an author. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference announcement' is an administrative document used to announce information about a conference (e.g., calls, participant info), while 'Conference Proceedings' is a multi-author volume containing the accepted papers presented at the conference. These are distinct types of documents with different purposes and contents.

writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (authorship), while Name is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their name). They are completely different in domain, range, type, and semantics.
Session is a conference activity (a type of lecture/event), while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. They are completely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Session is an event (a type of Scientific Event). They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.
Tutorial Abstract is a specific type of abstract for a tutorial, while Viza (visa) is a travel document. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewed contribution is a submitted paper/contribution that has been reviewed, while Review Form is the document or form used by reviewers to submit their reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Review Rating in edas represents the rating/score assigned to a paper (with children like Accept Rating, Reject Rating), while Review in sigkdd is a document subclass representing the full review text. They are related concepts in the review process but not equivalent.

In Ontology A, Reviewer and Committee member are siblings under Person, indicating they are distinct roles. In ekaw, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer and includes chair roles. While both can review papers, they represent different concepts in their respective ontologies: one is specifically a reviewer, the other is a program committee member who may also review. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Registration Non Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.
Rejection is a decision outcome for a paper, while Car is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Written contribution in Conference is a broad class encompassing all written conference contributions (with children Regular contribution and Submitted contribution). Short paper in confOf is a specific type of contribution. Thus Written contribution subsumes Short paper.
The properties have completely different domains and ranges (Organization->Sponsorship vs Item->Person) and express unrelated relations (providing sponsorship vs being needed for a person).

In edas, Paper is a full submission document (with reviews, authors, topics, and states like accepted/rejected). In sigkdd, Abstract and Paper are distinct siblings under Document, where Abstract typically refers to a summary or short description rather than the full paper. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

Property A ('parallel with') relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur in parallel. Property B ('relates To') links a Document to various entities (events, persons, etc.). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links 'Review expertise' to 'Submitted contribution', while property B links 'Author' to 'Contribution'. The domains are entirely different concepts (review expertise vs. author), so these properties relate different kinds of entities and are not equivalent.

Participant is a class representing a person attending the conference (subclass of Person), while Registration fee is a class representing a monetary fee (subclass of Fee). They are entirely different concepts.

Contribution co author in Ontology A is a specific type of author (a co-author of a contribution), while Author in Ontology B (edas) is the general class for all authors. Thus, Contribution co author is subsumed by Author.

In Ontology A, Paper is a Regular contribution (a full paper), while in Ontology B, Short paper and Paper are siblings under Contribution. Thus, A's Paper corresponds to B's Paper (full paper), not B's Short paper. They are related as both are types of conference contributions but are not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property giving the name (string) of a Conference or Person, while property B is an object property linking a Conference to a Country. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the solicitation of papers (a call), while 'Poster Paper' in ekaw is a specific type of submitted paper formatted as a poster. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Signal Processing Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (a large-scale gathering), while in ekaw, Conference is a sibling of Individual Presentation under Scientific Event. The ekaw 'Individual Presentation' represents a single talk/presentation slot, which is conceptually distinct from the overall conference event in confOf.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while submit relates an Author to a Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an action/event property (an Administrator adding a Program Committee Member), while Property B is a static membership relation (a Committee having members). They differ in domain (Administrator vs Committee), semantics (action vs state), and directionality of intent. They are not equivalent.

assignExternalReviewer relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment action), while write relates a Person to an Item (an authoring action). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'name' is a datatype property for the name of a Conference or Person, while 'has gender' is a datatype property for the gender of a Person. They represent entirely different attributes and are unrelated.

In ontology B (iasted), 'Registration fee' is a specific type of 'Fee', with siblings like 'Hotel fee' and 'Fee for extra trip'. In ontology A (Conference), 'Conference fees' is a general class likely encompassing all fees associated with the conference. Therefore, 'Registration fee' in iasted is a more specific concept subsumed by the broader 'Conference fees' in the Conference ontology.

Conference contributor (A) is a Person who contributes to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Member (B) in confOf is a subclass of Participant, with siblings Regular and Student, indicating it refers to a registered conference attendee/member. Contributors are not necessarily attendees/members, and members/attendees are not necessarily contributors. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Academic Institution in ekaw is an Organisation (e.g., University, Research Institute), while Research in iasted is an Activity performed before a conference. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (organisation vs. activity) and are unrelated.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (a type of conference attendee), with Student as a sibling. In ekaw, Student is a direct subclass of Person representing a student role. These are distinct concepts: one denotes a committee/organizing member, the other denotes a student. They are unrelated.

In edas, Author is a subclass of Person (with siblings like Attendee, Reviewer), while in ekaw, Person is the top-level class whose children include Paper Author. Thus edas:Author corresponds to ekaw:Paper Author and is strictly subsumed by ekaw:Person.

Poster is a type of academic contribution (a presentation format), while Silver Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while designed_by links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (creator/organizer relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of chairman), while Invited talk is a type of conference contribution/presentation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent social activities at a conference. EKAW's Social Event has children Conference Banquet and Conference Trip, while IASTED's Social program has child Dinner banquet and sibling Coctail reception. Their intended instances coincide as the social/non-scientific part of a conference program.

Conference Event represents an event occurring at a conference (with attendees, location, programme, dates), while Time zone represents a geographical time zone. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (subclass of Chairman) responsible for chairing the conference. Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (attendee) under a building hierarchy, likely referring to someone hiking/touring during the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

setMaxPapers is an administrative action to configure the maximum number of papers a PC member can review (domain Administrator, range Program Committee Member), while has_members simply links a Committee to its members. They have different semantics, domains, and purposes.

Property A ('was an organizing committee of') links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume and is the inverse of 'organizes'. Property B ('organises') links an Organisation or Person to an Event in the forward direction. They are related (roughly inverses) but not equivalent: they differ in direction, domain, and range specificity.

Topic in Ontology A refers to a subject area or theme of conference parts and submissions, while Place in Ontology B refers to a physical location (e.g., hotel, conference hall). These are entirely different concepts.

Program Committee in cmt is a group of reviewers for a conference, while Organization in edas refers to external entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorship. These are conceptually distinct and unrelated.

'Two Level Conference' in edas is a type of conference (despite oddly having Person and TPC Member as parents), while 'One day presenter' in iasted is a type of delegate/person who presents for one day. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Individual Presentation in ekaw is a scientific event (e.g., talk, tutorial) where a paper is presented. Item in iasted is a physical or abstract object (equipment, document, vehicle). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (a schedule/document), while partOfEvent links an Event to a parent Event (mereological part-whole). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding a person to a committee), while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference (an organization holding an event). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In cmt, Person is the top-level class for all people (with children like Chairman, Conference Member, External Reviewer, Program Committee Member). In ekaw, PC Member is a subclass of Person (via Possible Reviewer). Thus, cmt:Person is strictly more general than ekaw:PC_Member and subsumes it.
hasTopic relates a working event to a topic, while submit relates an author to a paper. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference in cmt represents the academic event itself (with members, paper assignments, dates), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a physical building/place where meals are served during the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A 'Conference' represents the conference event itself (with children like Conference volume), while Entity B 'Conference Paper' represents a paper submitted to or presented at a conference (a subclass of Document > Paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both 'Working event' (confOf) and 'Scientific Event' (ekaw) are subclasses of Event with siblings 'Social Event/ Social event'. They share key children such as Conference and Workshop, and both represent the scientific/working portion of a conference as opposed to social activities. Despite slightly different child sets (Tutorial vs Session/Track), their intended instances coincide in the conference domain.
A is a topic classification (Computer Networks Applications) while B is a type of scientific event/presentation (Contributed Talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme, while is_given_by links an Activity/Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Trip is a Social event (an excursion/activity), while in iasted, Trip day is a Time concept (a temporal unit like a deadline or conference day). They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the same concept: a conference event in the academic domain. Despite having different properties (cmt focuses on submission management and administration, sigkdd focuses on location and dates), they denote the same real-world entity type within the conference-organisation domain.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while Tutorial is a working event (a type of session at the conference). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (isReviewedBy) links a Paper to the person/role who reviews it (Reviewer, TPC Member, etc.), while Property B (hasReview) links a Paper to the Review document/artefact itself. They have different ranges (person vs. document) and represent distinct relations.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Signal Processing Topic in edas is a specific subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Student registration fee (A) is a fee for students, while Registration SIGMOD Member (B) is a fee for SIGMOD members. They are sibling concepts under Registration fee in their respective ontologies but refer to different categories of registrants.

Pending Paper is a status of a paper (Document > Paper), while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline (Time > Deadline). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewed contribution is a class of documents (papers that have been reviewed), while Possible Reviewer is a class of persons who may review papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference proceedings is a published volume of papers from a conference, while Web Site is an online document/page. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range classes: 'assignedByAdministrator' links a Reviewer to an Administrator (assignment action), while 'presentationed_by' links a Document to a Speaker (presentation action). They share no semantic overlap.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while is_paid_by relates Money to the payer (Person). These are entirely different relations with different domains and semantics.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Activity before conference in iasted refers to preparatory activities that occur prior to the conference (e.g., accepting/receiving manuscripts). These are conceptually distinct.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering/meeting), while Student non speaker in iasted is a type of delegate (a person attending who is a student and not speaking). These are entirely different concepts.
OC Chair is a person role (Organizing Committee Chair), while Introduction of speaker is a conference activity/event. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Proceedings in ekaw is a document/volume (a publication), while Author book proceedings included in iasted is a subclass of Author (a person who has authored content included in book proceedings). They represent entirely different concepts (an artefact vs. a role/person) and are unrelated.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (e.g., instructions, announcements), while 'Multimedia Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

A Workshop is a type of working event (like a conference or tutorial) where participants collaborate on research topics, while 'Introduction of speaker' is a specific ceremonial activity within a conference where a speaker is introduced to the audience. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCostCurrency specifies the currency code (string) for a Sponsorship, while Price specifies the numeric amount (int) of a Registration fee. They describe different aspects (currency vs. amount) of different concepts (sponsorship vs. registration), so they are unrelated.

writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while send relates a Person to an Item they send. These are different relations with different directions and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person or Contact Information to a string (email address), while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person (author). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Rejected Paper is a type of paper (document) that was not accepted, while Registration deadline is a temporal deadline for conference registration. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Property A 'reviews' has domain Review and range Reviewed contribution (Review -> Paper), while property B 'hasReview' has domain Paper and range Review (Paper -> Review). They are inverse properties relating the same kinds of things in opposite directions, so they are not equivalent.

Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (someone participating in the conference), while Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a Document (a published volume of papers). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a conference part to a topic, while property B links an administrative event to another administrative event that runs in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while 'parallel_with' links two Administrative events that occur simultaneously. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Ontology A's Review is the general class of reviews, while Ontology B's Positive_Review is a specific subclass of Review (with siblings Negative_Review and Neutral_Review). Therefore, A's Review subsumes B's Positive_Review.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference returning an integer count of reviews per paper, while hasReview is an object property on Paper linking to individual Review instances. They differ in domain, range, property type, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes contributions, while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Document' and serve as a general category for conference-related documents. In edas, children include Paper, Review, Programme, etc. In iasted, children include Submission (paper), Review, Form, Payment document, etc. Despite different sibling hierarchies, the intended instances (conference-related documents) largely coincide, making them equivalent in the conference domain.
The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'is Initiated By' links a Call to people (chairs/TPC members), while 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item.

Both properties link a reviewing role to a Paper, but their domains differ: edas 'isReviewing' has domain Conference Chair, Reviewer, Session Chair, TPC Member (actual assigned roles), while ekaw 'reviewerOfPaper' has domain Possible_Reviewer (potential reviewers). They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent due to the domain mismatch.
A Session room is a specific room where sessions take place, while a Hotel is an accommodation building. Both are subclasses of Place but denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Member is a person participating in a conference, while Conference fees refers to monetary charges for attending. These are entirely different concepts.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

Deadline hotel reservation refers to the deadline for reserving a hotel, while Deadline Author notification refers to the deadline for notifying authors of acceptance/rejection. These are entirely different types of deadlines in the conference domain.
Review in cmt is a review document written by a reviewer, while Active Paper in edas is a paper that is currently under consideration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Social Event is a type of event (e.g., banquet or trip). They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a leadership/role relation), while property B links a PC Member to a Contribution they review (a reviewing relation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Industry Organization represents commercial/industry entities, while University represents academic institutions. They are disjoint sibling concepts under the broader Organization/Organisation hierarchy in their respective ontologies.

Written contribution in Ontology A refers to academic papers/contributions submitted to a conference (with children like Regular contribution, Submitted contribution). Form in Ontology B refers to administrative documents such as registration forms, hotel forms, and author information forms. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

Entity A is a 'Conference announcement', which is a type of conference document (e.g., a call for papers or information notice). Entity B is the 'Conference' itself, an event with dates, members, and topics. A document about a conference is not the same as the conference event.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Measurements) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, Paper is a specific type of conference contribution (a regular contribution). In Ontology B (iasted), Document is a broad class with many children including Submission, Review, Form, Payment document, etc. Paper corresponds more closely to 'Submission' in iasted, so Paper is subsumed by the much more general Document class.

Conference Chair is a leadership/organizational role responsible for chairing the conference, while Tutorial speaker is a person who presents a tutorial. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Property A (isLocationOf) relates a Place to a Conference Event (inverse of 'has location'), while Property B (is present in) relates a Person to a Place or Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and directions, making them unrelated.

Registation deadline refers to the deadline for attendees to register for the conference, while Deadline Author notification refers to the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection. These are distinct types of deadlines in the conference domain, though they share a common parent class (Deadline).

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (maximum number of choices), while done_till links a Deadline to a date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A (adjustedBy) links a Bid to a Reviewer, while property B (reviews) links a Review to a Reviewed contribution. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Accepting manuscript is an activity (the process of accepting a paper) in the iasted ontology, while Author is a person role in the sigkdd ontology. They are completely different concepts.

'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (a part-whole relationship), while 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (a temporal/sequential relationship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Venue Place refers to the location where the conference sessions are held, while Conference airport is a transportation facility for arriving/departing attendees. Both are places associated with a conference but denote different concepts; they share a common ancestor (Place) and are thus related but not equivalent.
An 'Author information form' is a document/form used to collect author details, while a 'Hotel' is a physical place for accommodation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person), while Main office is a physical place (subclass of Place). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Talk Event in edas is a conference event where talks are given (e.g., welcome talk, closing talk), while Research in iasted is an activity performed before the conference involving modelling and simulating. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Call for paper' is a conference document used to solicit submissions, while 'Test Only Topic' is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization, while pay links a Person to Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring/submitting), while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee (financial transaction). Different semantics, different ranges.

A Review Form is used for the peer-review process of papers, while a Registration form is used for conference attendance registration. They are both subclasses of Form but serve entirely different purposes in the conference domain, so they are only related as sibling-like forms.

Property A (has authors) relates a Conference document to a Person (document -> author), while property B (send) relates a Person to an Item (person -> item). They have different domains, ranges, and directions, representing entirely different relations.

'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (date), while 'has Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have different types, domains/ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference volume to its contributions, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a keyword string. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Research Topic refers to academic subject areas covered by papers and events, while Money refers to financial concepts like fees and payments. They are entirely unrelated.

Property A is an object property linking any Event to a Location class instance, while Property B is a datatype property linking specifically a Conference to a string representing the city name. They differ in domain specificity, range type (object vs datatype), and modeling approach, making them unrelated.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to structural subdivisions of a conference (tracks, tutorials, workshops) that are parts of conference volumes. Activity in Ontology B is a much broader concept encompassing any event or action (before, during, or after the conference), including non-structural activities. They do not denote the same concept.

Both are datatype properties that specify the end date/time of an event. 'ends on' has domain Event and range string, while 'has End Date Time' has domain Conference Event and range dateTime. Despite minor differences in range type (string vs dateTime) and domain specificity (Event vs Conference Event), they express the same relation in the conference domain.

An organizing committee is a group of people responsible for organizing a conference, while an industry organization is a type of institution or company in the industrial sector. These are conceptually distinct entities.

Working event in confOf is a type of conference event (e.g., tutorial, workshop), while Computer Networks Management Topic in edas is a specific subject area/topic within computer networks. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Session room is a physical place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while go_through relates an Item to an Activity. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (expressing how a topic relates to review preferences), while Property B links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has the first name' is a datatype property for a person's given name (domain: Person), while 'has City' is a datatype property for a city in contact information (domain: Contact Information). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who printed hardcopy mailing manifests, while Property B links a Person to an Item they send. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (membership/affiliation), while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (giving/presenting). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a conference paper/document to its author(s). 'Paper' in cmt corresponds to 'Conference document' in Conference, and 'Author' corresponds to 'Person'. Despite the singular/plural naming difference, they express the same relation in the conference domain.
isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while designed_by relates a Deadline to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A captures a person's first name (domain: Person), while property B captures a remark about a contribution (domain: Contribution). They have entirely different semantics and domains.

In Ontology A, 'Conference part' represents a sub-component of a conference (e.g., Track, Tutorial, Workshop), whereas in Ontology B, 'Conference' represents the entire conference event itself (with properties like city, start/end dates). These are distinct concepts: one is a part, the other is the whole.

'Call for paper' is a type of conference document used to solicit submissions, while 'Computer Networks Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

External Reviewer in cmt is a person who reviews on behalf of another reviewer but is not themselves a PC member or regular reviewer. PC Member in ekaw is a program committee member. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and positions in the conference hierarchy.

Property A links an active conference participant to a presentation they give (presenting), while property B links an author to a contribution they write (authoring). These are distinct roles and activities in the conference domain; presenting is not the same as writing/authoring.
Presentation is a type of conference contribution (e.g., a talk), while Audiovisual equipment refers to physical hardware items like projectors and computers. These are entirely different concepts.
'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they provide. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'has title' is a datatype property linking events to their string titles, while 'Start of conference' links a Conference to a dateTime indicating when it starts. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Conference Participant is a class of persons attending the conference, while Registration fee is a monetary amount charged for registration. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference contribution refers to submitted works (papers, posters, talks) while Award refers to prizes given for best papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who runs paper assignment tools, while 'parallel_with' links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.
Person in edas is a general class for all people involved in a conference, while Student in ekaw is a specific subclass of Person. Therefore, edas:Person subsumes ekaw:Student.
'has workshops' links a conference volume to its workshops, while 'has City' links an organization or person to a city. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (has a track/workshop/tutorial topic), while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item (give). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A ('date') relates a Conference to a date value, while property B ('hasName') relates a Conference to its name string. They capture entirely different attributes and are unrelated.

Property A 'name' gives the name of a Conference or Person, while property B 'location' gives the physical location of an event. They have different semantics, different domains, and represent entirely different attributes.

hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string, while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference www is a type of conference document (a web resource with a URL), while Conference airport is a physical building/place where the conference takes place. They are entirely different concepts.

Cryptography Topic is a subject area classification for papers/conferences, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract (cmt) is an abstract of a paper and is modeled as a subclass of Paper, while Tutorial Abstract (ekaw) is an abstract of a tutorial and is modeled as a subclass of Abstract. They describe different kinds of conference artefacts with disjoint intended instances.

Submission in iasted is a type of Document (an artefact submitted), while Deadline Paper Submission in sigkdd is a type of Deadline (a temporal constraint). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

The 'remark' property in confOf is a string-valued datatype property on Contribution (e.g., a paper), while 'has amount of' in iasted is an integer-valued datatype property on Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Full Version in cmt refers to the completeness/version of a paper (as opposed to Paper Abstract), while Workshop Paper in ekaw refers to the venue/track where the paper is presented. These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.
Decision represents an acceptance/rejection outcome for a paper, while Country represents a geographical nation. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Security Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A 'location' specifies where an event is held (a venue/place), while property B 'Name of conference' specifies the name of the conference. These are entirely different concepts with different domains and semantics.

Organization in edas refers to institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorships. Item in iasted refers to physical objects or documents (equipment, cards, publications, vehicles). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent the research topic or subject area of a conference. In confOf, Topic is associated with Contributions (papers), Working events, and PC members. In ekaw, Research_Topic is covered by Papers and Events. The intended instances coincide as both denote the thematic subjects of papers and conference sessions.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while an 'Organizational Meeting' is a conference event. They are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. event) with no semantic overlap.

Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while Slide Set is a type of document (presentation slides). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
'Important dates' represents deadline/date information for a conference, while 'Contribution' represents a submitted paper or poster. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Reviewer is a Person who writes reviews, while Positive Review is a type of Review document. They are entirely different concepts (agent vs. artefact).

writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while isProviderOf links an Organization to a Sponsorship. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic, while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference A's 'Paper' is a general class for regular paper contributions (sibling of Extended abstract), while ekaw B's 'Evaluated Paper' is a very specific subclass of Paper that has already been submitted, assigned, and evaluated. Thus A's Paper subsumes B's Evaluated Paper.

'has an abstract' links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while 'paperInVolume' links a paper to the proceedings volume it appears in. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

A Regular Session in EKAW is a standard session for presenting papers, while a Plenary Lecture in IASTED is a specific type of lecture (typically a keynote) given to all attendees. They are both conference activities/events but denote different concepts; they are related as sibling-like event types rather than equivalent.

The property 'hardcopy Mailing Manifests Printed By' relates a Conference to an Administrator (who prints manifests), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). These describe entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

A Reception is a social event (party/gathering), while a Welcome address is a formal speech or opening remark at a conference. They are distinct types of activities. Note that iasted has 'Coctail reception' as a sibling of 'Welcome address', which would be the true match for confOf's Reception.

Property A links an active conference participant to a presentation they give (person-to-event), while property B links a paper presentation event to the accepted paper it is about (event-to-document). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Negative Review in ekaw is a specific type of Review (a review with a negative recommendation), while Review in sigkdd is the general class for all reviews. Therefore, Negative Review is subsumed by Review.

has_title is a datatype property linking events to their string titles, while listsEvent is an object property linking documents (brochures/websites) to Event instances. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.
hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its keyword string, while Nation links a Person to their nationality string. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.
Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Departure tax is a type of financial tax. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and are unrelated.

Trip (a type of social event involving travel/excursion) and Dinner banquet (a formal meal event) are both subclasses of social activities at a conference, but they denote different kinds of events. They are related as sibling-like concepts under the social program umbrella, not equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or general information to attendees, while 'Computer Networks Switching Topic' is a specific research topic within computer networks. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person representing a student role, while Lecturer in iasted is a subclass of Author/Speaker representing someone who gives lectures. These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

logoURL is a datatype property on Conference with range anyURI (a URL for the conference logo), while earlyRegistration is a datatype property on Participant with range boolean (indicating early registration status). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Committee in Ontology A refers to an organizational group (e.g., program committee, organizing committee) with chairs and members. State in Ontology B refers to a geographical or administrative location (with children like Conference state, Presenter state) used for spatial relations such as 'is situated in'. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of a conference), while University is an organization (an academic institution). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Working event is a type of Event (conference, tutorial, workshop), while Main office is a type of Place. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers specifically to scholarly contributions (papers, posters, talks) submitted to a conference volume. Document in iasted is a much broader class encompassing forms, invitation letters, payment documents, visa documents, etc., with Submission as only one child. They overlap in the area of submissions/papers but are not equivalent; they are related.

Both classes represent a Tutorial within the conference domain. In Ontology A it is a Conference part alongside Track and Workshop; in Ontology B (iasted) it is a type of Lecture/Conference activity. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances (tutorial sessions at a conference) coincide.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Talk Event' is a sibling of 'Paper Presentation', suggesting it refers to specific talks (e.g., welcome/closing talks) rather than full sessions. In ekaw, 'Session' groups multiple presentations (Conference Session, Poster Session, etc.). They overlap as scheduled scientific event blocks but are not equivalent; 'Session' is broader and structurally different from 'Talk Event'.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while has_a_degree is a datatype property on Review preference indicating an academic degree level. They have different domains, different semantics, and are unrelated.

Author in confOf is a Person who writes contributions, while Author information form in iasted is a Document/Form used for registration purposes. They are entirely different concepts (a person vs. a document).
Student is a subclass of Person representing a role, while Renting is a subclass of Activity before conference representing an action. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In edas, Rejected Paper is a direct subclass of Paper representing papers that were rejected. In ekaw, Evaluated Paper is a superclass of both Accepted Paper and Rejected Paper, meaning it covers all papers that have been evaluated (both accepted and rejected). Therefore, edas:RejectedPaper is strictly more specific than ekaw:Evaluated_Paper, making it subsumed_by the latter.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while ekaw:Demo_Paper is a specific subtype of Paper representing demonstration papers. Therefore confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Demo_Paper.

Workshop in edas is a type of academic conference event (a session at the conference), while Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic classification), while is_connected_with is a generic relation linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties represent a street address as a string, but they differ in domain: confOf applies it directly to Organization and Person, while edas applies it to a Contact Information class. They capture the same real-world attribute but with different modeling patterns, so they are related rather than strictly equivalent.

Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (Document > Paper), while Gold Supporter is a type of sponsor (Sponzor). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

Property A (memberOfConference) links a Conference Member to a Conference, while Property B (has_members) links a Committee to a Committee member. They have different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

In ekaw, Social Event is a general class with Conference Banquet as a child. In iasted, Dinner banquet is a specific type of social program (activity). Thus, ekaw's Social Event subsumes iasted's Dinner banquet, as the latter corresponds more closely to ekaw's Conference Banquet.

Property A links a conference volume to its steering committee, while property B links an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to the conference it holds. These relate entirely different domain and range concepts and express different relationships.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (reviewer bidding), while is_paid_for relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Venue Place in edas is a general class for any place where conference activities occur (with siblings like Accommodation Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place). Conference hall in sigkdd is more specific, referring to the main hall/room of the conference venue (with siblings Hotel, Main office). They overlap but are not strictly equivalent; Conference Venue Place subsumes Conference hall.

Reviewer in cmt is a person who reviews papers (a role), while Reviewed contribution in Conference is a document/paper that has been reviewed. They are entirely different concepts (agent vs. artefact).

'references' is a property indicating that one entity cites or refers to another, while 'award' is a property linking something to an Award. These are semantically unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both Excursion and Conference Banquet are subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but they denote different specific types of social events (a trip/outgoing activity vs. a formal meal). They are siblings under the same parent concept, hence related but not equivalent.

hasCountry links a Conference to a Country (domain: Conference, range: Country), while locationOf links a Location to an Event (domain: Location, range: Event). They have different domains, ranges, and directions; they are not equivalent or subsumption-related.

Conference days represents the duration/days of the conference event (a subclass of Time), while Deadline Paper Submission is a specific deadline for submitting papers (a subclass of Deadline). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a type of social event (an activity/excursion), while Trip city in iasted is a type of city (a location). They represent fundamentally different concepts (event vs. place) and are unrelated.

Both are datatype properties mapping a deadline-related class to an xsd:dateTime, but hasSubmissionDeadline is specific to submission deadlines (domain: Call) while Date is a generic date property for any Deadline. They overlap in purpose but are not strictly equivalent.

Camera Ready event in confOf is an administrative deadline/event for submitting final paper versions, while Organizational Meeting in edas is an academic meeting event (e.g., committee or organizational gathering). They belong to different branches of the event hierarchy and serve entirely different purposes.

earlyRegistration is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating whether they registered early, while Price is an integer datatype property on Registration fee indicating the monetary cost. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes are named 'Conference hall', share the same parent class 'Place', and represent the same concept of a venue space where conference sessions are held. The slight difference in siblings does not affect their equivalence.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person and is a sibling of TPC Member (which corresponds to Program Committee member). In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a subclass of Organizator (a role-based class). An attendee is anyone who attends the conference, while a PC member has a specific organizational/reviewing role. They overlap (a PC member typically attends) but are not equivalent; they are related concepts.
Co chair is a person role (committee member), while Building is a physical place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference for mailing purposes, while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur simultaneously. They are unrelated.

Contact Information in edas represents personal contact details (email, phone, street, etc.) of a person, while Conference in sigkdd represents the conference event itself (with name, dates, city). These are entirely different concepts.

External Reviewer is a person who reviews papers on behalf of another reviewer, while Review preference is an attribute or object representing a reviewer's topic preferences. They are entirely different concepts.
hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper, while designed_by links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasLastName captures only the family/surname part of a person's name, while Name likely represents the full name. They are related but not equivalent; Name subsumes hasLastName in scope.

Assistant in confOf is a support role (sibling of Administrator, Volunteer) under Person, while Author in iasted is someone who writes papers/presentations (child of Speaker). These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.
Workshop is an event or part of a conference, while Workshop Chair is a person role (a type of conference participant). They are entirely different concepts.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subclass of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper, while Web Site in ekaw is a subclass of Document representing a website. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both Presenter (ekaw) and Speaker (sigkdd) represent a person who presents at a conference. Both have 'Invited Speaker' as a subclass, strongly suggesting they denote the same concept. Although their parent classes differ slightly (Conference Participant vs Person), their intended instances in the conference domain coincide.
'attendeeAt' links a Person to a Conference Event (attendance), while 'is_prepared_by' links an Item to a Person (authorship/preparation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'Information for participants' is a type of conference document, while 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
'has authors' links a conference document to its author(s), while 'is sent by' links an item to the person who sent it. Authorship and sending are distinct relations in the conference domain.
Conference volume is a subclass of Conference representing the proceedings or event instance, while Conference Chair is a subclass of Person representing a role. They are entirely different concepts.

writtenBy links Contribution to Author (Contribution -> Author), while submit links Author to Paper (Author -> Paper). They involve the same domain concepts but have reversed directions and different semantics: authorship vs. submission action. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Property A links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (paper being reviewed), while property B links a Document to a Speaker (person presenting). These relate entirely different domain concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'One day presenter' is a specific type of Delegate who presents for one day, and it is a sibling of 'Speaker'. In sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a general class (parent of Author, Invited Speaker) representing anyone who gives a presentation. A one-day presenter is a kind of speaker, so the iasted class is subsumed by the more general sigkdd Speaker class.

Both classes represent a session within a conference. 'Conference Session' in edas and 'Session' (a subclass of Lecture under Conference activity) in iasted denote the same concept: a scheduled block of presentations or talks at a conference.

'writtenBy' relates a Contribution to its Author (document -> creator), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (agent -> object). The domains, ranges, and directions are different; they do not express the same relation.

Invited speaker (A) is a conference contributor who is specifically invited to speak, while Author (B) in iasted is a subclass of Speaker representing someone who authored a paper. An invited speaker may or may not be an author, and an author may or may not be invited. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.
Pending Paper is a paper awaiting a decision, while Bank transfer is a payment method. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class whose children include Author, Reviewer, Program Committee Member, etc. In sigkdd, Program Committee member is a specific role under Organizator. Thus cmt:ConferenceMember subsumes sigkdd:Program_Committee_member.

Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person representing a student participant, while Best Student Paper Supporter in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor (Sponsor) representing an entity that sponsors/supports the best student paper award. They belong to entirely different hierarchies and denote different concepts.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Break Event in edas is a subclass of Non Academic Event representing scheduled breaks during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
The properties have completely different domains and ranges (Conference->Administrator vs Document->Speaker) and describe unrelated relations (entering details vs presenting a document).

Test Only Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area for papers, while Card is a subclass of Item representing a physical card (e.g., credit card). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Invited Talk is a type of event/presentation. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have different domains and ranges (Item->Person vs Sponzor->ACM SIGKDD) and express different relationships in the conference domain. 'is needed for' indicates a requirement relationship while 'searched by' indicates a sponsorship-seeking relationship.

'organises' relates an Organisation or Person to an Event (organizing a conference event), while 'occupy' relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (occupying a physical location). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of running assignment tools, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item for authoring. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In the conference domain, 'is Written By' (Paper -> Author) in edas and 'is prepared by' (Item -> Person) in iasted both express the authorship/preparation relation between a scholarly work and its creator. Item corresponds to Paper and Person corresponds to Author in this context, making them equivalent properties.

Both properties express the location of a conference-related event, but they differ significantly in modeling: confOf's 'location' is a datatype property with range string (domain: Social event, Working event), while edas's 'hasLocation' is an object property with range Place (domain: Conference Event). They capture the same real-world relation but are not strictly equivalent due to different ranges and property types.
'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (signing), while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee (payment). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Microelectronics Topic is a subject area (subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (reviewer assignment context), while Property B links a Programme to a Conference Event (scheduling context). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a conference volume to its program committee (an organizational body), while property B links a programme brochure or web site to an event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A relates an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (committee-of-conference), while Property B relates a Person to a Conference (person-member-of-conference). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasTitle is a datatype property on Contribution (a paper/submission) giving its title, while Name is a datatype property on Person giving their name. Different domains and different semantics; they are unrelated.
Communications Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'is Initiated By' links a Call to the chairs/TPC members who initiated it, while 'is sent by' links an Item to a Person who sent it. These describe different relations between different kinds of entities (initiating a call vs. sending an item), so they are unrelated.

Conference Chair is the head of a conference (a specific leadership role), while Volunteer is a person offering unpaid help. These are distinct roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for any paper (child of Document). In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is a very specific subclass deep in the hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper), representing only papers that have already been evaluated/reviewed. Thus cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Evaluated_Paper.

'Call for paper' is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while 'Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Call' represents a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts (an administrative solicitation with deadlines and instructions). In ekaw, 'Event' represents an actual happening such as a scientific or social event (with locations, programmes, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (child of Person). IASTED non member in iasted is a specific type of Delegate (which corresponds to Attendee), restricted to those who are not IASTED members. Therefore, Attendee subsumes IASTED non member.

hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person who attends it, while is_prepared_by links an Item (e.g., a paper or document) to a Person who prepared/authored it. The domains and intended semantics are entirely different.

Reviewer in cmt is a person/role who reviews papers, while Review preference in Conference is an attribute or object representing a reviewer's topic preferences (with properties like 'has a degree'). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Published Paper (edas) and Submitted Paper (ekaw) represent different lifecycle stages of a paper. A published paper has gone through review, acceptance, and publication, while a submitted paper has merely been submitted. They are related as both are subclasses of Paper but are not equivalent.
NGO is a type of organization in edas, while Modelling is a research activity in iasted. They are completely unrelated concepts.
