Property A (expertOn) links a PC Member to a Topic they are expert in, while property B (topicCoveredBy) links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper that covers it. The domains, ranges, and directions are entirely different; these properties describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

Presenter in ekaw is a Conference Participant who presents (with child Invited Speaker). Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate with siblings including Speaker, Listener, Non speaker, etc. A Conference Hiker appears to be an attendee who 'hikes' between sessions rather than specifically a presenter. They overlap as conference participants but are not equivalent; Presenter is more specific to presenting, while Conference Hiker seems to denote a general attendee behavior.

Both properties link a paper to its presentation event, but in opposite directions: edas:relatedToEvent goes from Paper to Presentation, while ekaw:presentationOfPaper goes from Presentation to Paper. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are merely related (inverses).

The two properties describe entirely different relations: 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'reviewerOfPaper' links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper they review. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties relate an Author to the paper/contribution they write. In cmt, 'write Paper' has domain Author and range Paper; in confOf, 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution. Since Paper and Contribution are equivalent concepts in this domain (as noted in the instructions), these two object properties are equivalent.

Entity A (Paper) is a class representing a document/artefact submitted to a conference, while Entity B (Author of paper) is a class representing a person who authored a paper. They belong to entirely different categories (document vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.
Property A links important dates to a conference volume, while property B links administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a trip organized as part of a conference's social events. They share the same parent (Social event/Social Event) and analogous sibling structures (Banquet/Conference Banquet). The slight naming difference ('Trip' vs 'Conference Trip') does not change the intended instances in this domain.

Short paper in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), while Accepted Paper in edas is a paper classified by its review status (accepted vs rejected, pending, etc.). These are orthogonal classifications; a short paper may or may not be accepted, and an accepted paper may or may not be short. They do not denote the same concept.

Accepted contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted (a document type), while Accpet If Room Rating is a subclass of Review Rating representing a reviewer's rating category. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and are unrelated.

A 'Web Site' is a digital document listing conference events, while an 'Author information form' is a specific administrative form for collecting author details. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

Late paid applicant is a very specific subclass of a registered/paid conference applicant (Person > Conference applicant > Registered applicant > Paid applicant > Late paid applicant). Participant in confOf is a general class for all conference participants (Person > Participant) with children like Member, Regular, Student. A late paid applicant is a kind of participant, so the more specific class A is subsumed by the more general class B.
hasHomePage links a Person to their homepage URL string, while hasBiography links a Person to their biography text string. These are entirely different properties with different intended values.

Presenter in ekaw is a general class for anyone presenting at the conference (with Invited Speaker as a child), while Tutorial speaker in iasted is specifically someone who presents a tutorial. Thus Presenter subsumes Tutorial speaker.

In ontology A (iasted), 'Registration fee' is a class under Fee with children including various member/non-member/student registration fees. In ontology B (sigkdd), 'Registration SIGMOD Member' is a specific subclass of 'Registration fee'. Thus, the iasted 'Registration fee' is more general and subsumes the sigkdd 'Registration SIGMOD Member'.

In confOf, Conference is the main academic event (a type of Working event, sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). In edas, Conference Dinner is a specific social meal event occurring during a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (e.g., an author contributing a paper), while 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'study At' relates a Scholar to a University (an affiliation/education relation), while 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (an acquisition relation). These are semantically distinct properties with different domains and ranges.

Contribution co author is a specific role for a co-author (non-first author) of a conference contribution, while Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any author of a paper. They overlap but are not equivalent; Contribution co author is more specific than Paper Author.

Conference contributor (A) is a person who contributes content to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants), while Conference Participant (B) in ekaw covers attendees and organizational roles (chairs, registered participants). They overlap (e.g., a presenter/author may be both) but have different intended instance sets: A focuses on contribution, B on participation/attendance. Hence they are related but not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (parent: Person), while Session chair in iasted is a specific role of a delegate who chairs a session. A session chair is a kind of attendee, but Attendee is much broader, so they are related but not equivalent; Attendee subsumes Session chair.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (the act of authoring a review), while has_a_review_reference_or_expertise relates a Reviewer to their expertise or preferences. These are fundamentally different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Conference participant (A) is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference (active or passive). General Chair (B) is a specific organizing role. A General Chair is necessarily a conference participant, so Conference participant subsumes General Chair, but they are not equivalent.

Property A (addedBy) links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them, while Property B (was_a_committe_co_chair_of) links a Co-chair to a Committee they co-chaired. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Submission event in confOf is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), while Conference Paper in ekaw is a document (the paper itself). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. document) and are unrelated.
hasCountry links organizations or persons to a country, while hasReview links papers to reviews. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

defaultChoice is a datatype property on events mapping to positiveInteger (likely a default selection count), while End_of_conference is a datatype property on Conference mapping to dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Banquet is a subclass of Social event, while in edas, Social Event is the parent class (with children like Excursion and Reception). Thus, confOf:Banquet is subsumed by edas:SocialEvent, as a banquet is one specific type of social event.

Rejected contribution is a specific state of a submitted and reviewed paper/contribution that was not accepted. Paper in sigkdd is the general class for all papers (siblings include Abstract, Review). Thus Rejected contribution is strictly more specific than Paper, i.e., subsumed_by.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (a full workshop event), while in ekaw, Workshop Session is a type of Session (a session within a conference dedicated to workshops). They are related concepts but not equivalent: one denotes an entire workshop event, the other a session slot.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a subclass of Conference document representing submitted works (papers, posters, talks), while Participant in Ontology B is a subclass of Person representing people attending the conference. These are entirely different concepts (artefact vs. person).

In ekaw, Conference Session is a type of Session (event) that groups presentations. In iasted, Lecture is a broader conference activity whose children include Plenary lecture, Session, and Tutorial. A session typically contains lectures/presentations, so they are related but not equivalent; iasted's Lecture is more general and even has Session as a subclass, indicating different modeling choices.

In Ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific type of conference contributor who gives an invited talk. In Ontology B (confOf), 'Member' is a subclass of Participant with siblings 'Regular' and 'Student', indicating it refers to a membership category (e.g., regular member vs student member) rather than a speaker role. These denote different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCity links an Organization or Person to a City (indicating location), while is_occupied_by links a Building, City, or State to a Person (indicating occupancy). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Both properties link a paper-like entity to a person involved in its creation. However, 'has Co author' specifically relates a Paper to a Co-author (a secondary contributor), while 'is writen by' relates an Item to a Person (the general author/writer). They overlap semantically but differ in specificity: co-author is a narrower role than writer/author, and the domain/range classes are not identical. Thus they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), indicating authorship. Property B 'is Reviewed By' relates a Paper to reviewers/chairs, indicating the reviewing relationship. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference website to its URL string, while Property B is an object property linking a physical location to an event. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Science Worker in confOf is a broad category for anyone working in science (parent of Author, Scholar, etc.), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a specific organizational role under Organizator. They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a professional background, the other is a conference organizing role.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Main office is a physical place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Submission in iasted is a type of Document (an artefact submitted), while Deadline Abstract Submission in sigkdd is a type of Deadline (a temporal constraint). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.

Entity A is a committee (a group/organizational body) that is a subclass of Committee, while Entity B is a person role (Conference Chair) that is a subclass of Person. They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the same concept: an invited speaker at a conference. Despite slightly different parent classes (Conference contributor vs Presenter), their intended instances coincide as people specifically invited to give talks.
Both are datatype properties with identical semantics: they map a Person to their first name as a string. Same domain (Person) and range (string).

Property A represents a date for camera-ready paper submission (domain: Important dates, range: date), while Property B represents the location of an event (domain: Social/Working event, range: string). They describe completely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (for papers), while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, 'Published Paper' is a status-based subclass of Paper (alongside Accepted, Rejected, etc.), indicating the paper has been published. In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a venue/format-based subclass of Paper (alongside Workshop Paper, Demo Paper, etc.), indicating the paper is intended for or presented at a conference. A Conference Paper may or may not be published yet, and a Published Paper could theoretically be from any venue. They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not equivalent; they classify papers along different dimensions.

submitPaper (Author -> Paper) and writtenBy (Contribution -> Author) have opposite directions: submitPaper goes from author to paper, while writtenBy goes from contribution (paper) to author. They are not equivalent nor inverses of each other (the inverse of writtenBy would be 'writes' or 'hasAuthor'). They are related as they both connect authors and papers but in different directions and with slightly different semantics (submission vs authorship).
Proceedings is a document/volume class, while Author is a person class. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Cheque is a payment document (financial instrument) while Abstract is a scholarly document summarizing a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper in ontology A is a regular conference contribution (a scholarly paper), while Web Site in ontology B is a document type representing a website that lists events. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Co author is a person role (a type of Author), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are completely unrelated concepts.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person applying to attend or register for the conference (with child 'Registeered applicant'), whereas a 'Session Chair' in ekaw is a specific role responsible for chairing a session during the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have different domains (Sponsorship vs Registration fee) and different ranges (Organization vs Person). 'provided By' links a sponsorship to the sponsoring organization, while 'payed by' links a registration fee to the person paying it. They describe distinct relationships in the conference domain.
Conference fees refers to monetary charges for attending a conference, while Workshop is a type of working event within a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Activity after conference is an event/activity occurring after the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links an Abstract to the Paper/Poster/Presentation it is part of (part-whole relation between document components). Property B links a Speaker to a Document they present (agent-artefact relation). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop). In ekaw, Track is a Scientific Event that occurs within a Conference (Conference is a sibling of Track). A conference as a whole and a track within a conference are distinct concepts.

Rejected Paper is a paper that has been evaluated and not accepted, while Initial manuscript refers to the first version of a submission before final revision. These represent different stages/outcomes in the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent.

paperID is a datatype property assigning an unsigned long identifier to a Paper, while submit is an object property linking an Author to a Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper they are associated with (e.g., authored), while referencedIn typically indicates that one document is cited/referenced in another. These properties have different semantics, domains, and ranges.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Security) while B is an organizational committee responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Speaker (Lecturer < Author < Speaker), making it a more specific role than the general Speaker class in sigkdd. In sigkdd, Speaker is a direct child of Person and includes subtypes like Invited Speaker. Since iasted's Lecturer is narrower than sigkdd's Speaker, they are related but not equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a general conference document providing information to attendees, while 'Viza' (visa) is a specific travel document required for international travel. They are conceptually distinct and not equivalent.

SC Member (Steering Committee Member) in ekaw is a specific type of PC Member involved in conference governance/steering, while Reviewer in iasted is a role focused on reviewing papers. Both may participate in reviewing, but an SC Member is not equivalent to a generic Reviewer; they overlap in function but differ in scope and definition.
hasAuthor is an object property linking a Paper to an Author, while hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Viza (visa) is a travel document for attending a conference, while Paper is an academic submission. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.
publisherOf relates an Organisation to published documents (Flyer, etc.), while obtain relates a Person to an Item they acquire. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the participant who delivers it, while 'is paid by' links Money to the Person who pays it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Single Level Conference is a type of conference (an event/organization), while Conference Trip is a social event (excursion) associated with a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

In the conference domain, 'Attendee' (edas) and 'Delegate' (iasted) both denote a person who attends or participates in a conference. Despite Delegate having an unusual path through Building in iasted, it is also a subclass of Person and its children (Speaker, Listener, Session chair, etc.) confirm it represents conference attendees. These are standard synonyms in this domain.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking a Person/ContactInformation to a string (email address), while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, type, and semantics.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (attendance). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

In Ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' representing the conference website (it has a URL property). In Ontology B, 'Conference' is a subclass of 'Scientific Event' representing the actual conference event. These are entirely different concepts.

Subject Area in cmt refers to a topic or field of study that a paper can be classified under, while Conference in sigkdd refers to the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference applicant in Ontology A is a person applying/registering to attend the conference (child: Registeered applicant), whereas Author in Ontology B is a speaker who has authored a paper/proceedings contribution. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of working event), while Listener in iasted is a person (a type of delegate who attends). They are entirely different concepts.

Both properties relate a person/author to an item/contribution they create. 'writes' (Author -> Contribution) and 'prepare' (Person -> Item) are semantically similar in the conference domain, but their domains and ranges differ in specificity (Author vs Person, Contribution vs Item), making them related rather than strictly equivalent.

Organization in confOf represents an institution (with children Company and University) that employs people, while Contact Information in edas represents address/contact details (email, phone, street). They share some address-related properties but denote fundamentally different concepts.

submitPaper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime (a deadline). They describe entirely different concepts and relations.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document they authored, while is_used_by relates an Item to a Person who uses it. These are entirely different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Research Topic refers to a subject area of research in the conference domain, while Currency refers to monetary units. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution for reviewing, while property B (submit) links an Author to a Paper for submission. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author in cmt is a person who writes papers, while Multi-author Volume in ekaw is a document (e.g., proceedings) containing works by multiple authors. They are entirely different concepts.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member (a person/role) to a Conference, while belongsToEvent links a Programme (a schedule/document) to a Conference Event. The domains and ranges are fundamentally different kinds of entities, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference participant is a Person who attends a conference, while Social Event is an Event (e.g., banquet or trip). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote fundamentally different concepts.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it, while 'awarded by' links an Award to its granting entity. The domains (Presentation vs Award) and semantics (delivering a talk vs granting an award) are entirely different.
Property A links a 'Review expertise' to a 'Submitted contribution', while Property B links a 'Paper' to a 'Review'. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

finalizePaperAssignment links an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Reception is a social event (a type of gathering), while Speaker is a person who presents at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Non_speaker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate representing attendees who do not present (e.g., students, workers). Organizator in sigkdd represents people who organize the conference (chairs, committee members, webmaster). These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person representing system users (Administrator, Author, Reviewer) who interact with the conference management system. In confOf, Regular is a subclass of Participant representing regular (non-student) conference attendees. These are conceptually distinct: one models roles in paper submission/review, the other models attendee registration categories.

Deadline hotel reservation and Deadline Abstract Submission are both subclasses of Deadline but refer to entirely different types of deadlines (accommodation vs. abstract submission). They are sibling-level concepts under Deadline with no semantic overlap.

confOf:reviewes links a PC Member (domain) to a Contribution (range), i.e., reviewer -> paper. edas:isReviewedBy links a Paper (domain) to a Reviewer/TPC Member (range), i.e., paper -> reviewer. They express the same reviewing relationship but in opposite directions (they are inverses of each other). Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are related.

In Ontology A, Chair is a generic committee chair (with Co-chair as sibling), while in ekaw, Session Chair specifically chairs a session and is distinct from PC Chair, Tutorial Chair, etc. The generic Chair in A does not exactly match the specific Session Chair in B; they overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A denotes the date when paper acceptance is announced (domain: Important dates), while Property B denotes the start date of the conference itself (domain: Conference). These are entirely different events in the conference domain.

Both properties link a topic to the things that cover it (papers, conferences/events). However, edas:isTopicOf has range Conference and Paper, while ekaw:topicCoveredBy has range Event and Paper. Since Conference and Event are not strictly equivalent in these ontologies, the properties overlap but are not fully equivalent.

Property A links a Conference volume to its contributions (has contributions), while Property B links an Author to the contributions they write (writes). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'name' is a general name property applicable to both Conference and Person (likely full name or title), while property B 'has the last name' applies only to Person and specifically denotes the surname/last name. They overlap in that both can provide naming information for a Person, but they are not equivalent since one is general and the other is specific to last names.
Dining Place is a location for eating, while Car is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Property A 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while property B 'relatedToEvent' relates an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

reviewsPerPaper is a datatype property on Conference indicating the number of reviews per paper, while minChoice is a datatype property on events indicating minimum choices. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Session Chair in edas is a Person role (someone who chairs a session), while Session room in iasted is a Place (a physical room where a session takes place). They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference Member (person) to a Conference, while Property B links a Conference part (document/proceedings component) to a Conference volume. The domains and ranges are entirely different kinds of entities, so these properties are unrelated.

'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Company in confOf is a subclass of Organization representing a business entity, while Sponsor state in iasted is a subclass of State representing the geographical or political state of a sponsor. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of document (subclass of Conference document), while Academic Event is a type of event (subclass of Conference Event) such as a workshop or paper presentation. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

In EKAW, 'Conference Session' is a sub-event within a conference (e.g., a specific session like a demo or poster session), whereas in SIGKDD, 'Conference' represents the entire conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are distinct concepts at different levels of granularity.

In edas, Conference Event is a top-level class encompassing all events at a conference (academic and non-academic). In ekaw, Conference Session is a specific type of Scientific Event/Session (with siblings like Poster Session, Workshop Session, etc.). A Conference Session is a kind of Conference Event, so edas:ConferenceEvent subsumes ekaw:Conference_Session.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Transport vehicle is a physical item used for transportation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision (i.e., acceptance of a paper). In confOf, Reception is a subclass of Social event (i.e., a welcome reception party at the conference). These are entirely different concepts that happen to share an English word root.

hasProgramme links a conference event to its programme/schedule, while organisedBy links an event to the organisation or person that organises it. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity (event) in iasted, while 'Speaker' is a person role in sigkdd. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while writes relates an Author to a Contribution. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('has a URL') links a conference website to its URL string, while property B ('Name of conference') links a conference to its name string. They have different domains (website vs conference) and represent entirely different attributes (URL vs name), so they are unrelated.

Paper in cmt is a submitted document (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Working_event in confOf is an event such as a conference, tutorial, or workshop. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person applying to attend or register for the conference (child: Registered applicant), whereas a 'PC Member' in ekaw is a member of the Programme Committee responsible for reviewing papers. These are entirely different roles with no overlap.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subtype of Paper representing the abstract portion/format of a paper, while Poster Paper in ekaw is a subtype of Paper representing a paper presented as a poster. These are conceptually distinct: one refers to a document component/format, the other to a presentation/venue type. They share only the common ancestor Paper.

In cmt, Paper is a direct subclass of Document representing any paper. In edas, Active Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is itself a subclass of Document), representing papers that are actively under review. Thus cmt:Paper is more general and subsumes edas:ActivePaper.

Both are subclasses of Event in their respective ontologies, but they cover different aspects: confOf's Administrative event refers to organizational processes (submission, reviewing, registration), while ekaw's Scientific Event refers to the scientific programme itself (conference, session, workshop, presentation). They are siblings under Event in a merged view, hence related but not equivalent.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a specific role (member of the program committee who reviews papers). In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant with siblings Regular and Student, indicating it refers to a membership type/registration category for conference attendees rather than a program committee role. They overlap in that both are persons involved in a conference, but they denote different concepts.

Demo Chair and Session Chair are distinct conference roles. A Demo Chair oversees demonstration sessions, while a Session Chair presides over regular paper sessions. They are siblings in ekaw (both under Conference Participant) but represent different responsibilities.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Co author (a subclass of Author who co-writes papers) and Reviewer (a subclass of Speaker who reviews) are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.
logoURL refers to the URL of a conference's logo image, while Name_of_conference refers to the textual name of the conference. These are distinct properties with different meanings and ranges.
Property A links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while Property B links Money to a Building. These are entirely different concepts and relations in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the role of a Reviewer in the conference domain. Despite differing modeling choices in their respective hierarchies (cmt places it under Conference Member/User, iasted under Delegate/Speaker), their intended instances—people who review papers—are the same.

External Reviewer in cmt is a specific person assigned by a reviewer to review on their behalf and is explicitly not a regular reviewer. Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a broad superclass of anyone who could potentially review (including PC Members). These are conceptually very different: one is a narrow, specific role; the other is a general category. They do not share intended instances.

In edas, 'Pending Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper' representing papers awaiting a decision. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for submitted papers. Therefore, edas:Pending Paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Paper.

Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution (the paper being reviewed), while property B 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution (the paper being authored). They have different domains, different ranges, and represent entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

A Steering committee is a group/committee (subclass of Committee) that guides a conference, while Conference Chair is an individual person role (subclass of Person). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the concept of an author of a paper in the conference domain. In ekaw, Paper Author is a direct subclass of Person. In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker (which is a subclass of Person) and has children like 'Author of paper'. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide: people who author papers submitted to the conference.

Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper (child of Decision), while Trip is a social event during a conference (child of Social event). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.

In confOf, Poster is a sibling of Paper under Contribution, meaning it is a distinct type of contribution (a poster presentation). In sigkdd, Paper is a type of Document representing a written paper submission. These are different concepts in the conference domain: one is a poster, the other is a paper. They are related as both are types of scholarly contributions/documents but not equivalent.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'is needed for' links an Item to a Person (indicating necessity), while 'designed by' links a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (indicating authorship/creation). Their domains and ranges are also unrelated.

Rejection in cmt is a Decision (the outcome of rejecting a paper), while Week Reject Rating in edas is a Review Rating (a score/rating given by a reviewer). They belong to different parent classes and represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference announcement is a type of document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Paper is a scholarly document (with reviews, topics, presentations). In iasted, Card is a physical item (child of Item, sibling of Audiovisual equipment) with Credit card as a subclass, clearly referring to a payment/ID card, not a research paper.
Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role for people contributing to a conference), while Session is a subclass of Lecture/Activity (an event). They are entirely different concepts.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator regarding the bidding process, while 'need' links a Person to an Item they require. They are unrelated.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Web Site is a type of document (a website). They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (an action of accepting), while has_an_abstract relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to its Abstract (a compositional relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Published Paper in edas is a paper that has been accepted and published (a specific lifecycle stage), while Submission in iasted is a general document submitted to the conference (with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript). They overlap conceptually as both relate to papers/submissions in a conference, but they are not equivalent: Published Paper is more specific than Submission, and Submission encompasses pre-publication stages.

hasTopic (domain: Conference/Paper, range: Topic) and topicCoveredBy (domain: Research Topic, range: Event/Paper) are inverse properties of each other. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as they express the same conceptual link in opposite directions.

A Conference restaurant is a dining facility (subclass of Building) for conference attendees, while a Conference hall is a venue/room where conference sessions take place. These are distinct types of places with different purposes.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documents/artefacts (papers, reviews, calls for papers, announcements), while Conference Event in Ontology B refers to scheduled events with locations, start/end times, and programmes. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Company is an organization (business entity), while Student non speaker is a type of conference delegate who is a student and not presenting. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Although both properties share the label 'written By', they relate entirely different domain and range classes. In cmt, it links a Review to a Reviewer (who wrote the review), while in confOf, it links a Contribution (paper) to an Author (who wrote the paper). These are distinct relations in the conference domain.

Regular contribution in Ontology A is a specific type of conference contribution (with children Paper and Extended abstract), while Document in iasted is a very broad class encompassing forms, letters, payment documents, reviews, submissions, etc. They are not equivalent; Document is far more general and includes many non-contribution items. Even 'subsumes' is questionable since Regular contribution is specifically about authored scholarly works, whereas Document includes administrative items like payment documents and visa forms.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Reviewing results event is an administrative event in the conference schedule. They are entirely different concepts.

Poster Paper in ekaw is a specific type of academic paper (subclass of Paper), while Document in iasted is a broad category including forms, letters, payment documents, etc. They are at very different levels of specificity and cover different concepts; Poster Paper does not subsume Document nor vice versa.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code), while is_sent_after is an object property linking an Item to a Time. They describe entirely different concepts and relations.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while 'reviewes' links a Member PC to a Contribution (papers they review). They are unrelated.

The 'name' property in cmt provides a string name for a Conference or Person, while 'endDate' in edas provides a dateTime for when a Conference ends. These are entirely different properties with different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Organization represents an institution such as a company or university, while Award represents a prize given to authors/papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference activity is a type of event/activity (e.g., lecture, coffee break), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
'Receiving manuscript' is an activity/event (receiving a paper submission), while 'Author' is a person role. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Proceedings is a multi-author volume collecting papers from a conference, while Abstract is a short summary document of a single paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A Conference announcement is a type of conference document, while an LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. These are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Submission event is an administrative event for submitting contributions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite having unusual parents like Person and TPC Member), while Demo Chair in ekaw is a person role responsible for demo sessions. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a type of conference contribution (an oral talk), and Abstract is a separate class linked to it via 'has an abstract'. In Ontology B, Abstract is a type of Document that represents the abstract of a paper or invited talk. These are fundamentally different concepts: one denotes the act/artefact of presenting, the other denotes a summary document.

Conference document refers to documents/artefacts related to a conference (papers, reviews, announcements), while Organisation refers to organisational entities (institutions, agencies, publishers). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
has Last Name refers to a person's surname, while Nation refers to a person's country/nationality. These are entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization (alongside University), representing an organizational entity. In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (alongside Delegate), representing an individual person who sponsors. They differ both in kind (organization vs. person) and in role (company vs. sponsor), making them unrelated.

Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject area/topic in a conference, while Power Point presentation is a type of presentation activity. They share only the word 'Power' but are completely different concepts.

Single Level Conference is a type of conference (subclass of Conference), while Sponsor state is a state/role related to sponsorship (subclass of State). They belong to entirely different branches and denote unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent a Presentation in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is modeled as a Conference contribution (with children like Invited talk), while in Ontology B it is modeled as a Conference activity (with children like PowerPoint presentation). Despite different modeling choices (contribution vs. activity), they denote the same real-world concept of presenting at a conference.

EKAW's 'Scientific Event' covers only scientific activities (Conference, Session, Workshop, Individual Presentation) and explicitly excludes social events (sibling 'Social Event'). IASTED's 'Conference activity' includes both scientific items (Lecture, Presentation) and social/administrative items (Coctail reception, Coffee break, Registration, Social program). They overlap on presentations/lectures but neither subsumes the other due to differing scopes.

Conference represents the event/organization itself, while Deadline represents a temporal constraint (submission or notification deadline). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a subclass of Chairman (a leadership role), whereas Member PC in confOf represents a program committee member/reviewer. These are distinct roles within the conference organization hierarchy.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts submissions). In ontology B, 'Conference document' represents a document related to a conference (with children like Call for paper, Review, Conference announcement, and properties like has authors). These are fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a document.

rejectPaper denotes an administrator rejecting a paper, while submit denotes an author submitting a paper. They have different domains (Administrator vs Author), different semantics (rejection vs submission), and represent entirely different actions in the conference workflow.

'has the last name' is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while 'is present in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place and Time. They describe entirely different relations.

TalkEvent in edas represents an event where a talk is given (with children like Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, and sibling Paper Presentation), while Regular_Session in ekaw is a specific type of session within the conference programme. A session typically contains multiple talks/presentations, so they are related but not equivalent; neither strictly subsumes the other.
Author is a person who writes/submits papers, while Deadline is a temporal constraint for submissions. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Withdrawn Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been withdrawn), while Paper in sigkdd is the general class of papers. Therefore, Withdrawn Paper is subsumed by Paper.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a dateTime literal. They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain, and range, and represent different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an ending date value, while Property B is an object property linking a location to an event. They describe entirely different concepts and relations in the conference domain.

'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while 'references' is a generic property with unspecified domain/range likely denoting bibliographic citation. They are semantically unrelated.

Conference Trip (a social event involving a trip/excursion) and Dinner banquet (a social program involving a dinner/banquet) are both social events at a conference but denote different activities. In ekaw, Conference Banquet is a sibling of Conference Trip, so Dinner banquet would align with Conference Banquet rather than Conference Trip. They are related as co-hyponyms under social events.

Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk) in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

A Track workshop chair is responsible for a specific track or workshop within a conference, while a Program Chair oversees the entire conference program. They are both organizing roles (subclasses of Person/Organizator) but have different scopes and responsibilities, so they are related but not equivalent.
acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance action), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains and different semantics.

An 'Invited Speaker' (ekaw) is a presenter invited to speak at the conference, while a 'Plenary lecture speaker' (iasted) specifically gives a plenary lecture. Plenary speakers are typically invited, but not all invited speakers give plenary lectures (they may give keynote or other invited talks). Thus they overlap but are not strictly equivalent.

logoURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI for its logo, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

In edas, AcademiaOrganization is a subclass of Organization (with siblings Government Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). The Conference ontology's Organization class is general, so it subsumes the more specific AcademiaOrganization.
University is an academic organization/institution, while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Video presentation is a type of presentation activity (an event/artefact), while Speaker is a type of Person who gives presentations. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Non speaker in iasted is a type of Delegate (a person attending the conference who does not present), while Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a type of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different categories (person vs. fee) and are unrelated.
dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while is_sent_after links an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Paper is a type of document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Conference city is a geographic location (the city where the conference takes place). They are entirely different concepts.

Paper in cmt is a scholarly document submitted for review, while Event in confOf is a scheduled occurrence (e.g., social or working event). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Member PC in confOf is a Program Committee member (reviewer), as indicated by its comment 'Reviewer' and properties like 'reviewes' and 'expert On'. OC Member in ekaw is an Organizing Committee member, which is a distinct role responsible for organizing the conference rather than reviewing papers. These are different concepts.

Submission event is an administrative event for submitting contributions, while Workshop is an academic event (a type of session at a conference). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasLastName captures a person's last name (surname), while E-mail captures their email address. These are distinct attributes of a Person and do not denote the same relation.

markConflictOfInterest links a person (Author/Chairman/Reviewer) to a Paper to indicate a conflict of interest, whereas hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer to indicate an assigned or potential reviewer. These properties have different semantics, different domains/ranges, and different directions; they are unrelated.

Sponzorship in iasted is a subclass of Money (a financial contribution/payment), while Best Student Paper Supporter in sigkdd is a subclass of Sponzor (an agent/role that provides sponsorship). One denotes a monetary concept, the other an entity acting as a sponsor; they are not equivalent and do not subsume each other.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members (committee -> person), while Property B links a Co-chair to a Committee (person -> committee). They have different domains, ranges, and directions, representing entirely different relationships.

Property A (relatedToEvent) links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event, while property B (give) links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Submission event is an administrative event for submitting contributions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject area/topic classification, while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while searched_by links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Both properties represent an ending date/time, but they differ in domain: 'is an ending date' applies to 'Important dates' (a generic deadline/date entity), while 'End of conference' applies specifically to 'Conference'. They are related as both capture end-date semantics, but are not equivalent due to different domains and specificity.

User in cmt is a general class for people interacting with the conference system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Non speaker in iasted is a specific type of delegate who attends but does not present. These are conceptually distinct and do not share the same intended instances.

The properties have different domains and ranges and point in opposite directions. 'hasConferenceMember' goes from Conference to Conference Member, while 'attendeeAt' goes from Person to Conference Event. They are not equivalent, nor is one a subproperty of the other; they are unrelated.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Sponsor city is a geographic location (a type of City). They are completely unrelated concepts.
Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members, while property B links an Active conference participant to Presentations. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Scientific Event in ekaw is a broad class encompassing Conference, Workshop, Session, Track, and Individual Presentation. Presentation in iasted is a specific type of conference activity (with children like PowerPoint and Video presentation). Scientific Event subsumes Presentation since a presentation is a kind of scientific event, but they are not equivalent due to the much broader scope of Scientific Event.

'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an action of inputting conference details), while 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (indicating who organises the event). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.
Property A relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering), while Property B relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Conference Session is a temporal event/slot within a conference program. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

isTopicOf links a Topic to a Conference or Paper, while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker. These properties relate entirely different domain concepts and serve different semantic purposes.

In Ontology A, Paper is a regular conference contribution (a submitted research paper). In Ontology B, Programme Brochure is a document that lists events in the conference programme. These are entirely different concepts; note that ekaw also has its own Paper class as a sibling of Programme Brochure.

Both classes represent a Workshop as a type of academic/scientific event within the conference domain. Their paths (Academic Event vs Scientific Event) and sibling classes confirm they denote the same concept.

Presenter in ekaw is a conference participant who presents (with Invited Speaker as a subclass), while Author_book_proceedings_included in iasted is specifically an author whose work appears in the book proceedings. They overlap in that both can present at a conference, but they are not equivalent: one focuses on the presenting role and the other on a specific publication outcome.

In cmt, Chairman is a general class with children including Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair. In ekaw, OC Member refers specifically to Organizing Committee members, with OC Chair as a child, while PC Chair is a sibling. Thus cmt:Chairman is broader than ekaw:OC Member (which only covers the organizing committee aspect), making them related but not equivalent.

submitPaper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while is_an_abstract_submission_date is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value. They represent entirely different concepts and have different types, domains, and ranges.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while a 'Presentation' in iasted is a conference activity/event (e.g., giving a talk). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while Property B links a Conference part to a Track workshop chair. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference applicant is a Person who applies to attend a conference, while Conference is an Event (a type of working event). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

In Ontology A, 'Accepted contribution' is a document/artifact (a subclass of Conference contribution) representing a paper that has been accepted. In Ontology B, 'Accepting manuscript' is an activity/event (subclass of Activity before conference) representing the process of accepting a manuscript. They are related in the conference domain but differ fundamentally in kind (artifact vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.
Conference airport (a building/airport for conference attendees) and Hotel (an accommodation place) are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf:Banquet is a specific type of social event (a banquet), while ekaw:Social_Event is the general class for all social events at a conference. ekaw:Social_Event has Conference Banquet as a child, confirming that Banquet is subsumed by Social Event.

assignReviewer is an object property from Administrator to Reviewer (an action of assigning a reviewer), while hasReviewHistory is an object property from Reviewer to Personal Review History (linking a reviewer to their review history). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has tracks' relates a conference volume to its tracks, while 'has Country' relates an organization or person to a country. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an object property linking a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Call to a string of submission instructions. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Presenter house in iasted is a type of building (a place/accommodation). They represent entirely different concepts.
Communications Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference contribution to a Conference volume (where it was submitted), while Property B links an Author to a Paper (the act of submitting). They have completely different domains and ranges and express different relationships.
Property A links review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while property B links a Paper to a Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Departure tax is a type of tax (under Money > Tax) related to travel, while Sponzor fee is a type of sponsorship fee (under Fee). They represent different financial concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.
Workshop is an academic event type, while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

TalkEvent in edas is a broad category of academic events that includes PaperPresentation, Workshop, and specific talks (ClosingTalk, WelcomeTalk). Tutorial in ekaw is a specific type of individual presentation within scientific events. They overlap as both are types of conference presentations/events, but neither subsumes the other nor are they equivalent.

In cmt, Review is a document (the actual written review of a paper), whereas in edas, TextualReviewQuestion is a type of review question (a prompt or criterion used to structure a review). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links review expertise/preference to a reviewer, while Property B links a programme to a conference event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties express a 'writing' action in the conference domain. However, cmt:writeReview is specifically restricted to Reviewer -> Review, while iasted:write is more general (Person -> Item). Since Item likely includes papers and other documents beyond just reviews, these are not equivalent; they overlap semantically but differ in scope.

isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to a newer version of that Document. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the chair of the Program Committee (PC Chair). In cmt, Program Committee Chair is a subclass of both Chairman and Program Committee Member. In ekaw, PC Chair is a subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member. Despite different parent hierarchies, they denote the same role in conference organization.
Conference Chair is a person role in the conference organization, while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for booking accommodation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a Conference volume specifically to its Tutorials (a part-of relationship for tutorial sessions), while Property B is a general relation linking various entities (events, persons) to Documents. Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Author information form is a document/form used for registration purposes. They are entirely different concepts.
Renting is an activity before a conference (e.g., renting equipment or venue), while Author is a person who writes and submits papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The 'abstract' property describes the abstract text of a Contribution (paper), while 'Name of sponsor' describes the name of a Sponsor. They have completely different domains and semantics.
Conference Session in edas is an event (a session within a conference), while Session Chair in ekaw is a person role (someone who chairs a session). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Time in iasted represents temporal concepts (conference days, deadlines, trip days), while Document in sigkdd represents written artefacts (abstracts, papers, reviews). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Company in confOf is an Organization (a type of institution/business entity), while Presenter university in iasted is a Building (a physical place). They are fundamentally different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Property A links 'Important dates' to a 'Conference volume' (a publication/proceedings artefact), while Property B links a 'Programme' to a 'Conference Event' (a scheduled activity). The domains and ranges represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.

Contribution co-author (A) is a specific type of author who is a co-author (not the first author) of a conference contribution. Author of paper (B) is a general class for any author of a paper. Every contribution co-author is an author of a paper, but not every author of a paper is a co-author (e.g., first/sole authors). Thus A is subsumed by B.

Property A is a datatype property assigning a string name to various entities, while Property B is an object property linking events or papers to research topics they cover. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Committee member is a general class for any member of a conference committee (with children Chair and Co-chair), while Session Chair is a specific role chairing a session. A Session Chair would typically be a kind of Committee member, so Committee member subsumes Session Chair.

Paid applicant is a conference registrant who has paid their fee, while TPC Member is a member of the Technical Program Committee responsible for reviewing papers. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Reception in confOf is a social event (like a welcome reception/party), while Introduction in iasted refers to an introductory activity (with child 'Introduction of speaker'). They are distinct concepts; notably, iasted has its own 'Coctail reception' sibling class that would align with confOf's Reception.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Computer Networks Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version). In edas, Rejected Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing only rejected papers. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes edas:RejectedPaper.

Medicine Topic is a subject area classification (a topic), while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event at a conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Paid applicant is a subclass of Person representing someone who has paid to attend the conference, while Activity before conference is a subclass of Activity representing events or tasks occurring before the conference. These are entirely different concepts in different branches of their respective ontologies.
Property A gives the title of a Paper, while property B gives the name of a Sponsor. They have different domains (Paper vs Sponzor) and describe entirely different concepts.

Location in ekaw is a place where events are held (domain of locationOf, range of heldIn), while Conference in sigkdd is the conference event itself with properties like name, city, start/end dates. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a venue/place, the other is an event.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Person (specifically Author), representing a person who co-writes a paper. In Conference ontology, 'Regular author' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact), not a person, despite its name suggesting otherwise. They belong to fundamentally different categories (person vs. document) and are therefore unrelated.

Both properties link a programme/program committee entity to the conference event it belongs to. 'Program committee' in Conference corresponds to 'Programme' in edas, and 'Conference volume' corresponds to 'Conference Event'. The relation 'was a program committee of' and 'belongs To Event' express the same association between these aligned domain and range classes.

In confOf, Participant is a broad class under Person that includes Members, Regular attendees, and Students, as well as having Author as a sibling. In sigkdd, Author is a specific subclass of Speaker (which is a subclass of Person). Since every Author is a Participant but not every Participant is an Author, confOf:Participant subsumes sigkdd:Author.
The properties have completely different semantics: 'has a date of issue' relates a conference document to a date, while 'has title' relates events to a string title. They are unrelated.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Security Topic is a subject area/topic (subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Conference applicant is a Person who applies to attend a conference, while Research is an Activity (a type of work done before the conference). They are entirely different concepts in different branches of their respective ontologies.

Entity A is a class representing a person who participates in a conference (subclass of Person), while Entity B is a class representing a specific type of registration fee (subclass of Money > Fee > Registration fee). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Social Event' is a specific type of non-academic conference event (with children Excursion, Reception). In ekaw, 'Event' is the top-level class for all events, including both Scientific Event and Social Event as children. Therefore, edas:SocialEvent is strictly more specific than ekaw:Event, making it subsumed_by ekaw:Event.

Paper in cmt refers to an academic submission (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Payment document in iasted refers to a financial instrument (bank transfer, cheque). They are completely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

In edas, 'Conference Session' is a general session class. In ekaw, 'Demo Session' is a specific subtype of 'Session', and ekaw also has its own sibling class called 'Conference Session'. Therefore, edas:ConferenceSession is more general than (subsumes) ekaw:Demo_Session, making them related but not equivalent.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting paper submissions, while Silver Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Tutorial is a type of conference activity (a lecture), while Organizator is a type of Person who organizes the conference. They are completely different concepts in the domain.
Invited Speaker is a Person (a role), while Introduction of speaker is an Activity (an event). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.
Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Conference Event in edas is a top-level class for all events at a conference (with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event). Conference Banquet in ekaw is a specific type of Social Event (which itself is under Event). Thus, Conference Event subsumes Conference Banquet.

Both classes represent a person who participates in a conference. They share the same label (modulo spacing), the same parent class (Person), and their children are various specific roles of conference participants (chairs, reviewers, presenters, registered attendees). Despite differences in how each ontology subdivides participants, the intended extension of both classes coincides.

Property A is a specific datatype property for the abstract submission date (domain: Important dates, range: date), while Property B is a general 'Date' property for any deadline (domain: Deadline, range: dateTime). They are related as both capture date information for deadlines/important dates, but A is more specific than B, so they are not equivalent.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties share the same label 'is given by' and serve a similar role of linking an event-like entity to its presenter/agent. However, their domains differ (Presentation vs Activity/Item) and their ranges differ (Active conference participant vs Person). In the conference domain, Presentation is a specific kind of Activity, and Active conference participant is a specific kind of Person, so the properties overlap but are not strictly equivalent.

hasKeyword links a Contribution to its keyword strings, while hasSubmissionInstructions links a Call to submission instruction text. Different domains, ranges in meaning, and entirely different semantics.
'has authors' links a Conference document to a Person (authorship), while 'is present' links a Person to a Time (temporal presence). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee for registration. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Entity A is a class representing a person who actively participates in a conference (e.g., gives presentations), while Entity B is a class representing an event or activity that takes place during a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture). They belong to entirely different categories (Person vs. Activity) and are unrelated.

'is submitted at' links a contribution to the conference volume (proceedings) it is submitted to, while 'paperPresentedAs' links a paper to its individual presentation format at the event. These relate different domain/range concepts and capture different relationships (submission venue vs. presentation mode).

confOf:Conference is a general conference class (child of Working event), while edas:SingleLevelConference is a specific subtype of Conference (distinguished from TwoLevelConference). Thus the confOf class subsumes the edas class.

Accepted Paper is a paper that has been accepted for presentation at a conference, while Invitation letter is an administrative document used to invite someone (e.g., for visa purposes). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties describe a reviewer/PC member evaluating a paper, but they differ in range: cmt's writeReview points to a Review (the review document), while confOf's reviewes points directly to the Contribution (the paper being reviewed). They are semantically related but not equivalent.

Conference participant is a subclass of Person representing an attendee, while Working event is a subclass of Event representing activities like conferences, tutorials, and workshops. They belong to entirely different branches of the domain.

The property 'enter Conference Details' relates an Administrator to a Conference (an action of entering details), while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (a temporal/structural relationship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while 'is connected with' is a general association property relating Activity/Person to Item/Place. They have different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in conference organization, while Industry Organization is a type of organization. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper Full Version in cmt denotes a version/format of a paper (the complete manuscript as opposed to an abstract), while Accepted Paper in edas denotes a paper that has passed the review process and been accepted. These are orthogonal classifications: a full version can be rejected, and an accepted paper is typically a full version but the concepts describe different dimensions (format vs. status).

An 'Invited speaker' is a person specifically invited to speak at a conference, while a 'Student lecturer' is a lecturer who is also a student. These are distinct roles with different defining characteristics; one does not subsume the other, and they are not equivalent.

OC Member in ekaw is a member of the Organizing Committee, while Speaker in iasted is a person who presents at the conference (a subclass of Delegate). These are distinct roles with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Decision in cmt represents the final accept/reject outcome for a paper, while Review Rating in edas represents an individual reviewer's rating (which may include borderline options like 'Accept If Room'). They are related as both concern paper evaluation outcomes and share similar sub-structures (acceptance/rejection children), but they are not equivalent: a decision is typically the aggregate or final result, whereas a review rating is one reviewer's assessment.

Property A links an active conference participant (a person) to a presentation they give, while property B links an accepted paper (a document) to a paper presentation event it is related to. The domains differ fundamentally (person vs. document), so these properties are not equivalent.

hasPhone is a datatype property linking a Person to a phone number string, while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Information for participants is a type of conference document, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasRelatedPaper links Author to Paper (author -> paper direction), while writtenBy links Document to Person (paper -> author direction). They are inverse properties relating the same domain concepts but in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.
hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person (attendee), while hasEvent links an Event to another Event (sub-event). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Tutorial is a conference activity/event (a type of Lecture). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Meal Break is a specific type of break event during a conference (e.g., lunch), while Trip day is a day designated for travel/excursions. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string, while is_used_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Entity A is a research topic (Computer Networks Sensor Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Computer) under Item in iasted. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Rated Papers is a subclass of Paper representing papers that have been rated/reviewed, while Abstract is a sibling of Paper representing a summary document. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while is_held_before relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

Property A links a 'Review expertise' to a 'Submitted contribution', while property B links a 'Person' to an 'Activity' or 'Item'. The domains and ranges are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.
