Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while CAD Topic is a subject area/topic related to Computer-Aided Design. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, directly under Person. OC Member (B) is a specific subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw, representing only Organising Committee members. Thus A subsumes B.

has_the_first_name is a datatype property for a person's first name (domain: Person, range: string), while Price is a datatype property for a registration fee amount (domain: Registration fee, range: int). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

A's 'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (a whole-to-part relation), while B's 'partOfEvent' is a part-to-whole relation between Events. They are conceptually related as inverse meronymic relations in the conference domain, but they differ in direction and specificity, so they are not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of chairman), while Plenary lecture is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Bid represents a reviewer's bid on a paper in the cmt ontology, while Conference represents the conference event itself in sigkdd. These are entirely different concepts.
Break Event is a type of non-academic conference event (e.g., coffee break), while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

hasConflictOfInterest is an object property linking a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an integer amount. They are entirely unrelated in meaning, domain, and range.

In ekaw, University is an Organisation (Academic Institution), representing the institution itself. In iasted, Presenter university is a Place > Building, representing a physical building/location where a presenter is based. They differ in both ontological category (organisation vs. building) and intended instances.
hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper, while obtain relates an Author to an Award. The ranges (Paper vs Award) are entirely different concepts, so these properties are unrelated.

detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., call for papers). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference participant (A) is a subclass of Person representing people attending the conference, while Conference days (B) is a subclass of Time representing temporal periods. They are entirely different concepts in different domains.

In Ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a type of Conference contributor (sibling to Regular author), typically someone invited to give a keynote or talk without necessarily submitting a paper. In Ontology B, 'Author' is a subclass of Speaker with children like 'Author of paper', representing someone who submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain; they overlap as both are speakers/people involved in the conference, but are not equivalent.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'hardcopy Mailing Manifests Printed By' relates a Conference to an Administrator, while 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper. They are unrelated.

In iasted, 'Conference activity' is a subclass of Activity representing individual events within a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture, presentation). In sigkdd, 'Conference' represents the overall conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are fundamentally different concepts: one denotes sub-events/activities, the other denotes the overarching conference.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to an integer cost, while locationOf is an object property linking Location to Event. They are entirely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (Person) with siblings Regular and Student, representing a committee member role. In edas, TPC Member is a Person subclass that reviews papers and initiates calls, i.e., a technical program committee member. Both denote the same conference-domain concept: a person serving as a program/organizing committee member. The OAEI reference alignment maps these as equivalent.
The properties have completely different domains (Person vs Money), ranges (string vs int), and semantics (last name vs monetary amount). They are unrelated.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country, while is_made_from links an Item to another Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Email' captures an email address. These are entirely different attributes of a person and do not denote the same relation.

Contribution co author is a class representing a type of author (person) who co-authored a contribution, while Proceedings is a class representing a published document/volume. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level, while property B links a personal review history record to a reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Bid represents a reviewer's expression of interest in reviewing a paper, while a Conference Session is an event/slot during a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Review is a document (an actual review of a paper), while in edas, Personal Review History is a record of a reviewer's past reviewing activities (a type of personal history). These are fundamentally different concepts.
Organization represents an organizational entity (e.g., a company or institution), while Currency represents a monetary unit. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members, while isProviderOf links an Organization to a Sponsorship. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent events within a conference context. confOf:Event has children Administrative event, Social event, and Working event, while edas:ConferenceEvent has children Academic Event and Non Academic Event, covering the same conceptual space. Both share temporal properties (start/end dates). They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Poster is a specific type of conference contribution (a poster presentation), while Final manuscript is the final version of a submitted document/paper. They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Tutorial in the conference domain. Although they are placed under different parent hierarchies (Conference part vs Individual Presentation), their intended instances coincide: tutorial sessions held as part of a conference.

Property A links a conference volume to its organizing committee, while property B links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a conference it holds. These relate entirely different domain/range concepts and express different relationships.

Both are subclasses of Social Event in their respective ontologies, but a Reception (a social gathering/party) and a Conference Trip (an excursion/trip) are distinct types of social events. They are siblings in the same conceptual hierarchy rather than equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.
Conference applicant refers to a person applying/registering for a conference, while Student refers to an academic status. They are distinct concepts under Person with no semantic overlap.

Worker_lecturer (iasted) is a subtype of Lecturer/Speaker/Author representing a working professional who lectures, while Author_of_paper_student (sigkdd) is a subtype of Author representing a student author. They are both authors/speakers but represent different roles (worker vs student), so they are related but not equivalent.

'One conference day' is a temporal concept representing a single day of the conference, while 'Organizing Committee' is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated.

'is Initiated By' links a Call to the chairs/TPC members who initiated it, while 'is used by' links an Item to a Person who uses it. These describe fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Student registration fee is a monetary fee for student attendees. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while property B links Important dates to a Conference volume (a publication artefact). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Invited speaker is a person invited to give a talk at the conference, while Chair PC is the chair of the program committee. These are distinct roles with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (assignment of review preferences), while Property B links a personal review history to a reviewer. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Rejected contribution refers to a paper that has been reviewed and rejected, while Pending Paper refers to a paper whose review/decision is still pending. These are distinct states in the paper lifecycle. The edas ontology has its own 'Rejected Paper' class as a sibling of 'Pending Paper', confirming they are different concepts.
Contribution represents academic submissions (papers, posters) while Money represents financial entities (fees, sponsorships). They are completely unrelated concepts.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to its organizing Organisation/Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'part Of' is a general mereological relation, while 'awarded by' links an Award to its awarding entity. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.

Property A (authorOf) links a Person to a Document they authored, while property B (is_given_by) links an Activity/Item to the Person who gives/presents it. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.
'has a publisher' links conference proceedings to a publisher, while 'follows' links administrative events in a temporal sequence. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking Person to a string (email address), while writtenBy is an object property linking Document to Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while PC Chair is a person role (Program Committee Chair). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In the conference domain, 'Submitted contribution' in Ontology A (a written contribution that has been submitted) corresponds to 'Paper' in Ontology B (a document that authors submit). Both represent the primary scholarly artefact submitted by authors for review. While Ontology A's hierarchy is more granular (distinguishing regular/submitted/reviewed contributions), the intended instances of Submitted contribution and Paper largely coincide in this context.
Microelectronics Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while 'Simulating' is a research activity performed before a conference. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Review expertise in Ontology A is a class representing the level or domain of expertise a reviewer has (an attribute/quality), whereas Reviewer in Ontology B is a Person who performs reviews. These are fundamentally different concepts.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to a newer version of that Document. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Programme Brochure is a type of document that lists events. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.
Medicine Topic is a subject area for conference papers, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference proceedings (A) is a published document/volume containing the papers of a conference, whereas Conference (B) is an event (a type of Working event). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
'has authors' relates a conference document to a person (authorship), while 'employed By' relates a person to an organization (employment). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Member is a type of Participant (a person attending the conference), with siblings Regular and Student. In iasted, Sponsor is a Person who sponsors the conference, sibling to Delegate. A conference member/participant and a sponsor are distinct roles in the conference domain.

Conference_part in Ontology A refers to organizational subdivisions of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while Place in Ontology B refers to physical locations (Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Conference volume to a string (location name), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to Place/Time entities. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Student registration fee is a monetary fee for student registration. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Security Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

'relatesTo' in edas is a generic property linking a Document to events or persons, while 'organisedBy' in ekaw links an Event to its organising entity (Organisation or Person). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has gender' refers to a person's gender, while 'Nation' refers to a person's nationality or country. These are distinct attributes and not equivalent.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Platinum Supporter is a top-tier sponsor category. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a presentable artefact/event to the person who presents it. However, 'is given by' in iasted has a broader domain (Activity, Item) and range (Person), while 'presentationed by' in sigkdd is narrower (Document -> Speaker). They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent due to differing scope.
locationOf relates a Location to an Event, while search relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, 'Working event' is a superclass whose children include Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop. In edas, 'Workshop' is a specific type of Academic Event (a subclass of Conference Event). Therefore, confOf's Working_event subsumes edas's Workshop, as Workshop is one kind of Working event.

Sponzorship (sponsorship) is a form of financial support/funding under Money in iasted, while Registration fee is the cost paid by attendees to register for the conference under Fee in sigkdd. These are distinct financial concepts. Note that sigkdd even has a separate sibling 'Sponzor fee' under Fee, further confirming they are not equivalent.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review a particular topic or submission (with degree, assigned reviewers, etc.), while Review Question in edas represents a question on a review form (numerical or textual) that reviewers answer when evaluating a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Passive conference participant is a subclass of Person (a type of attendee), while Conference Trip is a subclass of Event (a social activity). They belong to entirely different categories in the domain.

Review preference in Ontology A is a class representing a reviewer's preference or degree of interest regarding topics or submissions (with properties like 'has a degree'). Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person representing someone who can potentially review papers. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an abstract preference/assignment entity, the other is a person role.

Main office and Hotel are both subclasses of Place in their respective ontologies, but they denote different kinds of locations. A main office is an administrative/organizational venue, while a hotel is an accommodation venue. They are siblings under Place (as seen in sigkdd's hierarchy) but not equivalent.

A Call (e.g., Call for Papers) is an announcement inviting submissions, while a Deadline is the date by which something must be submitted. They are related (a Call has a submission deadline), but they are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

Property A links a review expertise to a submitted contribution (paper), while property B links a personal review history to a reviewer. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics, making them unrelated.
A 'Call for paper' is an announcement document inviting submissions (a call), whereas B 'Paper' is the actual submitted contribution/artefact. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Published Paper is a scholarly paper that has been published, while Bank transfer is a payment method document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Track is a type of scientific event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'initiates' in edas relates committee members (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call they initiate, while 'organised By' in ekaw relates an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. The domains, ranges, directions, and semantics are entirely different.

In cmt, Paper is a direct subclass of Document and represents any paper in the conference system (including submitted, reviewed, accepted papers). In ekaw, Conference Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is itself a subclass of Document) and specifically denotes papers that are part of the conference proceedings. Since ekaw's Conference Paper is more specific than cmt's Paper, cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Conference_Paper.

Meal Event in edas is a specific type of Non Academic Event focused on meals (with child Conference Dinner). Social program in iasted is broader, encompassing not only dinner banquets but also cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, introductions, etc. They overlap (both can include dinners) but are not equivalent; they are related concepts with partial overlap.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is oddly placed under 'Conference contribution' (likely a modeling quirk) but also inherits from 'Conference contributor', and its children are 'Contribution 1th author' and 'Contribution co author', indicating it represents any standard author of a paper. In Ontology B (edas), 'Presenter' is a subclass of 'Author' representing specifically the person who presents the work. Not all regular authors are presenters (co-authors often do not present), so Presenter is more specific. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

'invites co reviewers' is a specific property relating a Reviewer to another Reviewer for the purpose of co-reviewing. 'send' is a very general property relating a Person to an Item. They differ in domain, range, and semantic intent.

In confOf, 'Assistant' is a sibling of Administrator, Volunteer, etc., and likely refers to an administrative or clerical assistant role. In sigkdd, 'Organizing Committee member' is a specific organizing role under 'Organizator', with siblings like General Chair and Webmaster. These denote different roles in conference organization and are not equivalent.

A Session chair manages an individual session within a conference, while a Program Chair oversees the entire conference program. They are distinct roles with different scopes of responsibility, though both are organizational/leadership roles at a conference.

Conference part (A) represents structural components of a conference such as tracks, tutorials, and workshops, while Person (B) represents human individuals such as attendees, authors, and chairs. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (which also has Review as a sibling). In edas, Document is the top-level class whose children include Paper, Review, Meal Menu, etc. Therefore, cmt:Paper corresponds to edas:Paper and is strictly subsumed by edas:Document.
hasRating links a paper to its review rating, while write links a person to an item they authored. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

'has a date of issue' refers to the publication/issuance date of a conference document, while 'done till' refers to the deadline date by which something must be completed. These are semantically distinct temporal properties with different domains and meanings.
'has a program committee' links a Conference volume to its Program committee, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Tutorial is a Working event (a type of conference activity/session), whereas in ekaw, Invited Talk Abstract is a Document (specifically an Abstract). They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. document) and describe different concepts (tutorial vs. invited talk).
hasLocation links a Conference Event to a Place (spatial relation), while hold links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizational relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, 'Conference Session' is a general class for sessions at a conference. In ekaw, 'Regular Session' is a specific subtype of 'Session', with siblings including 'Conference Session', 'Demo Session', etc. Since ekaw distinguishes 'Regular Session' from its own 'Conference Session' as sibling subtypes, the edas 'Conference Session' (a general session concept) does not strictly equate to the more specific 'Regular Session'. They are related but not equivalent.

Conference in cmt represents the conference event/organization itself, while Call in edas represents a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts associated with an academic event. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Sponsor company house is a building/place. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Decision in cmt represents the outcome of a paper review (Acceptance/Rejection), while Speaker in sigkdd represents a person who gives a presentation. These are entirely different concepts.
Paper in cmt is a document/artefact (child of Document), while Author in sigkdd is a person who writes/submits papers (child of Person > Speaker). They are entirely different concepts.

startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference for initiating reviewer bidding, while writes relates an Author to a Contribution for authoring a paper. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Chair (cmt) is the overall chair of the conference, while Session Chair (edas) chairs an individual session. Notably, edas itself distinguishes Conference Chair and Session Chair as siblings. They are related as both are chair roles but not equivalent.

Property A ('has title') assigns a title to social or working events (e.g., sessions, banquets), while Property B ('Name of conference') assigns a name to the conference itself. They have different domains and refer to different concepts in the conference domain.

Powerline Transmission Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a research subject area, while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Conference Hiker is a type of delegate (a person). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Presenter house in iasted is a building/place (subclass of Building). They are entirely different concepts.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while is_held_after links an Activity to a Time. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasMember relates a Conference to its Person members (e.g., committee members), while organisedBy relates an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.
Submitted Paper is a document/paper class, while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline class. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Call for participation' is a sibling of 'Call for paper', indicating it refers to a general invitation to participate (e.g., attend) rather than submit papers. In Ontology B, 'Call For Manuscripts' is a sibling of 'Call For Papers' and specifically invites manuscript submissions. These are related concepts within the broader 'Call' category but do not denote the same thing.

TalkEvent in edas represents a specific presentation or talk (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk), while Conference_Session in ekaw represents a session that groups multiple presentations together (with children like Industrial Session). A session typically contains one or more talks, so they are related but not equivalent.

confOf's 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the process/activity of submitting contributions), while sigkdd's 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a deadline (a point in time by which papers must be submitted). They are related to the same phase of conference organization but represent fundamentally different concepts (event vs. deadline), so they are not equivalent.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members (Program Committee Member), while property B links a Committee to its chair (Chair). Both relate committees to people, but they target different roles (member vs. chair) and have different domain/range specificity, so they are related but not equivalent.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an academic gathering), while Technical commitee in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person/role). These are entirely different concepts.

Reception in edas is a social event (under Non Academic Event > Social Event), while Welcome address in iasted is a conference activity with siblings like Lecture and Presentation. The iasted ontology has a separate 'Coctail reception' sibling that better matches edas's Reception. A welcome address may occur at a reception but they are distinct concepts, so they are related but not equivalent.

Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
CAD Topic is a subject area (Computer-Aided Design) under Topic in edas, while Transport vehicle is a physical item (car, bus, etc.) under Item in iasted. They are completely unrelated concepts.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review, while writes relates an Author to a Contribution (paper). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges in the conference domain.

Both properties link a Topic to something it is a topic of, but their ranges differ: A's range is 'Conference part' while B's range includes 'Conference' and 'Paper'. They overlap in intent (associating topics with conference-related entities) but are not strictly equivalent due to different range classes.
Property A links a conference volume to its important dates, while property B links a conference to its organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (has members) relates a Committee to its Committee members, while Property B (is Member Of) relates a Person to a Conference. They differ in domain, range, direction, and semantic scope; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing posters, presentations, invited talks, and written contributions submitted to a conference volume. Abstract in ekaw is specifically the abstract/summary document of a paper that gets presented. While an abstract could be considered part of a contribution, the two classes have very different scopes: Conference contribution covers all types of contributed works (including talks and posters), whereas Abstract is narrowly the textual summary associated with a paper presentation. They are not equivalent, nor does one clearly subsume the other in a meaningful alignment sense.

attendeeAt links a Person to a Conference Event they attend, while organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. These are semantically distinct relations (attending vs organising) with different domains and ranges.

Paper Abstract in cmt refers to a version/format of a paper (the abstract document), while Rejected Paper in edas refers to a paper's status in the review process (rejected). These are orthogonal concepts and not equivalent.

Both properties link a document-like entity (Document in ekaw, Item in iasted) to a Person who created it. 'writtenBy' and 'is prepared by' express the same authorship/creation relation in the conference domain, but since the domain classes (Document vs Item) may not be strictly equivalent across ontologies, they are closely related rather than fully equivalent.

Both are top-level Person classes in the conference domain. Although their children differ (Delegate/Sponsor vs Listener/Organizator/Speaker), they represent the same general concept of a person involved in a conference, and their intended instances coincide.

Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing papers, reviews, calls for participation, etc., while Payment document in Ontology B specifically refers to financial payment instruments (bank transfer, cheque). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A is 'Program Committee' (the committee/group itself), while Entity B is 'Program Committee member' (a person who is a member of the committee). They are related but not equivalent; one is a group and the other is an individual member of that group.

Entity A is a Person role (a chair of a track or workshop), while Entity B is an Event type (a workshop itself). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are unrelated.

The property 'start Reviewer Bidding' relates an Administrator to a Conference for initiating reviewer bidding, while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'added By' relates a Program Committee Member to the Administrator who added them (an administrative action), while 'was a member of' relates a Committee member to the Committee they belong to (a membership relation). These are semantically distinct properties with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Author in cmt is a person who writes/submits papers (subclass of Person/Conference Member), while Written contribution in Conference ontology is a document/artefact (subclass of Conference document > Conference contribution). They represent fundamentally different concepts: an agent vs. a produced work.

In cmt, User is a broad class under Person with children Administrator, Author, and Reviewer. In ekaw, SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a specific role under PC Member. Since an SC Member is a type of conference participant/user, the general cmt:User subsumes the specific ekaw:SC_Member, but they are not equivalent.

Property A (locationOf) relates a Location to an Event (i.e., an event takes place at a location). Property B (is_situated_in) relates spatial entities like Building/City/Place to other spatial entities like State (i.e., a place is geographically situated in another place). The domains and ranges differ fundamentally: one connects places to events, the other connects places to places. They are not equivalent nor subsumption-related.

Organising Agency in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation (an institutional entity), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (an individual role). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.

confOf:Student is a general student participant (subclass of Participant), while iasted:Student_lecturer is specifically a student who is also a lecturer/speaker/author (deep subclass of Lecturer). They overlap in that both involve students at a conference, but Student_lecturer has the additional constraint of being a lecturer, so they are related but not equivalent.

hasTopic (domain: Working event, range: Topic) and isTopicOf (domain: Topic, range: Conference/Paper) are inverse properties relating topics to events/papers. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as inverses in the same domain.

contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to an email string, while hasPostalCode links Contact Information to a postal code string. They represent entirely different pieces of information (email vs postal code) on different domains.
Property A is the title of a Paper (string), while property B is the starting date of Important dates (date). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reception is a social event in the conference schedule, while Neutral Review is a type of document (a review with neutral sentiment). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

memberOfConference is an object property linking a Conference Member to a Conference, while Start_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime. They describe entirely different relations.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (indicating assignment or delivery). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while 'listsEvent' links a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event that it lists. They are unrelated.

Both classes represent the presentation of a paper at a conference event. However, in ekaw, Individual_Presentation is a broader class that includes Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, and Tutorial as children, whereas edas Paper Presentation is specifically tied to an Accepted Paper via relatedToPaper. Thus they overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; they are related.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Hotel fee is a monetary cost for accommodation. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Meal Menu is a document describing food options for a meal event, while Tip is a monetary gratuity. They belong to entirely different hierarchies (Document vs Money) and represent unrelated concepts.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (presentation responsibility). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A is a datatype property linking Person to a string (first name), while B is an object property linking Item to Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Co-chair and General Chair are distinct conference organizing roles. A Co-chair typically shares leadership of a committee (often the program committee), while a General Chair is the overall head of the conference organization. They are related as both are chair-level organizer roles but not equivalent.

'has authors' links a conference document to its authoring persons, while 'is occupied by' links a physical location (Building, City, State) to persons occupying it. The domains and intended semantics are entirely different.

In Ontology A, 'Call for participation' is a specific sibling of 'Call for paper' under 'Conference document', meaning it refers to a call inviting attendees/participants rather than papers. In Ontology B, 'Call' is a general class whose children include 'Call For Papers', 'Call For Manuscripts', and 'Call For Reviews'. Since A's concept is specifically about participation (distinct from papers) and B's concept is a broad superclass covering various types of calls, they are not equivalent. They overlap in the general notion of conference calls but differ in scope and specificity, making them related.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person specifically invited to give a talk at the conference, whereas a 'Listener' is a delegate who attends but does not present. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.
AccommodationPlace is a general class for any place providing lodging, while Hotel is a specific type of accommodation. Thus AccommodationPlace subsumes Hotel.

'assignedByAdministrator' specifically links a Reviewer to an Administrator who assigned them, while 'give' is a general property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Conference contribution (A) is a broad class encompassing papers, posters, invited talks, and presentations as submitted artefacts or roles. Paper Presentation (B) in edas is specifically an event (subclass of Academic Event) where an accepted paper is presented. While A includes 'Presentation' as a child, B is strictly an event tied to an accepted paper, making them related but not equivalent.
Review is a conference document representing an evaluation of a paper, while Value added tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.
'rejected By' relates a Paper to an Administrator (rejection action), while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Computer Architecture Topic is a subject area for papers in edas, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass) in iasted. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
A Tutorial is a type of working event (like a conference or workshop), while an Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Accept Rating in edas is a specific rating value (a subclass of Review Rating) assigned during the review process, whereas Review in sigkdd is a document (subclass of Document) that contains the written evaluation. A rating and a review document are distinct concepts.
Banquet is a social event (a type of gathering/meal), while Speaker is a person who presents at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference in edas is an event/organization entity, while Conference Hiker in iasted is a type of delegate (person) attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Student is a subclass of Person representing a type of individual, while Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference_part represents a structural component of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while Speaker represents a person who gives a presentation. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Invited speaker is a type of person (conference contributor), while Sponsor state is a type of state. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted scholarly work (paper, poster, short paper) written by authors and reviewed by PC members. Conference Session in edas represents a scheduled session at the conference that relates to documents. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is a research topic (Satellite And Space Communications) while B is an award category (Best Research Paper Award). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Industry Organization in edas is a type of organization from the commercial/industry sector (sibling to Academia Organization), while Research Institute in ekaw is an academic institution (child of Academic Institution). They represent fundamentally different types of organizations and are not equivalent.

Entity A is a class representing a type of author/contributor to a conference paper, while Entity B is a class representing a specific type of registration fee (money). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

'references' in ekaw denotes a citation or reference relationship (e.g., a paper referencing another), while 'sign' in iasted denotes a person signing an item. These are semantically unrelated properties.
Contribution co author is a role for paper authors, while Double hotel room is an accommodation type. They are completely unrelated concepts.
'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a date string, while 'Name' links a Person to a name string. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an organized gathering), while Session chair in iasted is a type of delegate (a person who chairs a session). These are entirely different concepts.

In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (a sibling of Talk Event, Paper Presentation, etc.), while in ekaw, Track is a sibling of Workshop under Scientific Event. A workshop and a track are distinct concepts in conference organization; notably, ekaw itself lists Workshop as a sibling of Track, confirming they are not equivalent.
Review is a document evaluating a paper, while Value added tax is a type of tax under Money. They are completely unrelated concepts.

confOf:Author is a subclass of confOf:Person representing someone who writes contributions. ekaw:Person is the top-level class for all people, with Paper Author as a child. Thus confOf:Author corresponds to ekaw:Paper Author and is subsumed by ekaw:Person.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (organizational membership), while 'is present in' relates a Person to a Place and Time (physical/temporal presence). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a subclass of Person representing people attending the conference, while Conference in sigkdd represents the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role for people contributing to the conference), while Activity before conference is a subclass of Activity (events or tasks occurring before the conference). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote fundamentally different concepts.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while is_visited_by relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (visitation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad subclass of Person that includes Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and PC Members—essentially anyone involved in the conference. In confOf, Participant (with children Member, Regular, Student) specifically denotes attendees/registrants, while roles like Author, Chair PC, and Member PC are siblings of Participant rather than subclasses. Thus, Conference Member subsumes Participant but also covers many other roles, making them related (overlapping) rather than equivalent.

Author in cmt refers to a paper author (person who writes/submits papers), while Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers to staff of an agency (e.g., funding or organizing agency). These are entirely different roles in the conference domain. The equivalent of Author in ekaw would be Paper Author.

A 'Call for paper' is a document soliciting paper submissions, while a 'Mailing list' is a distribution list or document used for mass communication. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

Pending Paper is a paper awaiting a decision in the review process, while Cheque is a payment document. They belong to entirely different subdomains (paper management vs. financial/payment) and share no semantic overlap.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Computer Networks Switching Topic is a subject area/topic within computer networks. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Optical Topic) while B is an organizational committee (Organizing Committee). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Fee is a monetary charge (e.g., registration fee). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both properties relate a person (Person/Speaker) to something they present (Activity,Item / Document). In the conference domain, 'give' likely includes giving presentations, and 'presentation' specifically links a Speaker to a Document they present. They overlap in intent but differ in range (Activity/Item vs Document) and specificity, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Conference restaurant is a physical place/building. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Workshop in ontology A is a conference event/part (a session or sub-conference), while Workshop Paper in ontology B is a type of document/paper submitted to or presented at a workshop. They are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. document) and thus unrelated.

One is a datatype property (remark) mapping a Contribution to a string, the other is an object property (writtenBy) mapping a Document to a Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and types.
Week Reject Rating is a type of review rating in edas, while Abstract is a type of document in sigkdd. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a leadership role within a committee), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). These involve entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'scientifically Organises' relates an Academic Institution to something it organizes. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop chair (a person role), while property B links an event to a programme brochure or web site (a document). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A gives the first name of a Person, while property B gives the title of a Contribution (paper). They have different domains, different ranges semantically, and represent entirely different concepts.

TalkEvent in edas is a subclass of AcademicEvent (with children like Closing Talk, Welcome Talk), while Social_Event in ekaw represents non-academic social gatherings (Conference Banquet, Conference Trip). They are disjoint sibling-like concepts under the broader Event hierarchy and do not share intended instances.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme, while technicallyOrganises links an Organisation to something it organises. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and Program Committee Members. Co chair in the Conference ontology is a specific role (co-chair of a committee). Thus, Conference Member subsumes Co chair, as every co-chair is a conference member but not vice versa.

The property 'title' in cmt gives the title of a Paper (domain: Paper, range: string), while 'location' in confOf gives where an event is held (domain: Social event/Working event, range: string). They describe entirely different attributes of different kinds of entities and are unrelated.

Both properties link an event-like entity to a person/participant, but 'is given by' specifically relates a Presentation to its presenter (Active conference participant), while 'has Attendee' relates a Conference Event to any attending Person. The domains and ranges differ in specificity and semantics (presenter vs. attendee), so they are related but not equivalent.
One property captures a person's first name while the other captures their email address; they represent entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range.

In ontology A (cmt), Meta Review is a subclass of Review. In ontology B (Conference), Review is the general class for reviews. A meta review is a specific kind of review (typically summarizing other reviews), so Meta Review in cmt is subsumed by the more general Review class in Conference.

A 'Call for participation' invites people to attend or participate in a conference, while B 'Call For Reviews' specifically solicits reviewers to review papers. Both are types of calls/announcements in the conference domain but target different audiences and purposes, so they are related but not equivalent.
hasBid is an object property linking a Paper to a Bid, while has_amount_of is a datatype property linking Money to an integer amount. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (e.g., guidelines, instructions), while 'Technic activity' is a type of conference activity/event (e.g., lecture, presentation). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event) and are unrelated.

hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime for the submission deadline, while notification_until is an object property linking an Author to a Deadline Author notification entity. They differ in domain, range, property type, and semantic meaning (submission vs. notification).
Conference document is a class of documents (papers, reviews, announcements), while Participant is a class of people attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Mobile Computing Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Bronze Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Accepted contribution in Ontology A is a specific state of a contribution (one that has been reviewed and accepted), while Paper in Ontology B is the general class for all papers regardless of status (its children include Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc.). Therefore, Accepted contribution is subsumed by Paper.

hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to a currency string, while heldIn is an object property linking Event to Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Poster is a type of Contribution (a submitted document/artefact), sibling to Paper and Short paper. In edas, Paper Presentation is a type of Conference Event (an activity where a paper is presented). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs event) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Both classes represent a physical place/room where conference sessions or meetings are held. 'Meeting Room Place' in edas and 'Conference hall' in iasted both sit under 'Place' and serve the same purpose of hosting conference activities. While 'hall' might suggest a larger space than 'meeting room', in the conference domain they are used interchangeably to denote the venue rooms for sessions.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while send relates a Person to an Item (transmission). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference participant is a Person who attends or contributes to a conference, while Session is an Activity (a type of Lecture) within the conference program. They are entirely different concepts.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'technically Organised By' relates an entity to its technical organizer. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and directions.

Presenter in ekaw is a general class for anyone who presents at the conference (with Invited Speaker as a subclass). One day presenter in iasted is a more specific type of presenter (someone presenting for only one day), and iasted also has a separate 'Speaker' sibling class. Therefore, ekaw:Presenter subsumes iasted:One_day_presenter.

In iasted, Activity is a broad class with children including 'Conference activity', 'Activity before conference', and 'Activity after conference'. In sigkdd, Conference refers specifically to the conference event itself. Since Conference activity is a subclass of Activity in iasted, Activity is more general than (subsumes) Conference.
Committee member is a person role in a conference committee, while Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Microelectronics Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Paper is a subclass of Document and specifically represents a submitted paper (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper). In iasted, Document is a broad class covering many administrative items (forms, invitation letters, payment documents, etc.), with 'Submission' as a child that would correspond to edas:Paper. Thus edas:Paper is related to iasted:Document but not equivalent; it roughly corresponds to iasted:Submission.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing the email address of a person. 'has Email' and 'E mail' are synonymous in this context.

In edas, 'Academic Event' is a broad class encompassing Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop, and Organizational Meeting as children. In ekaw, 'Conference' is specifically one edition of a conference (a sibling of Workshop, Session, Track, Individual Presentation). While both are academic/scientific events, edas AcademicEvent is much broader than ekaw Conference, which denotes only the main conference event itself. They overlap but are not equivalent.

AccommodationPlace in edas is a general class for places where attendees can stay (hotels, houses, etc.), while Conference hotel in iasted is specifically a hotel used for the conference. A conference hotel is a type of accommodation place, so AccommodationPlace subsumes Conference hotel.

hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their biography), while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document they authored. They have different ranges, different property types, and entirely different semantics.

The two properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges. 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (requirement). They are unrelated.

hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (someone who reviews the paper), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (someone who presents it). These are entirely different roles and relations in the conference domain.

Conference participant (A) is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference (active or passive). Program Chair (B) is a specific organizing role. A Program Chair is a kind of conference participant, so A subsumes B, but they are not equivalent.

The 'name' property in cmt applies to Conference and Person entities to capture their names, while 'contact Email' in confOf applies to Contribution entities to capture an email address. They have different domains, ranges (semantically), and purposes, making them unrelated.
Session is a type of conference activity (a time slot or event), while Speaker is a type of Person who presents. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Radio Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Industrial Session is a type of event/session (temporal), while Session room is a physical place/location. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Chairman in cmt is a specific leadership role (with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Conference Participant in ekaw is a much broader class encompassing all participants including chairs, registered attendees, and presenters. Thus Chairman is subsumed by Conference Participant.

Property A is a datatype property giving the starting date of important dates, while Property B is an object property indicating that one activity is held before another (or before a time). They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing papers that have been submitted. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for papers (with a 'submit' property linking authors to papers). Thus, ekaw's Submitted Paper is more specific than sigkdd's Paper, making it subsumed_by.
Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area for papers in edas, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as subclass) in iasted. They are completely unrelated concepts.

An 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk), while 'Author attendee book registration fee' is a type of monetary fee. These are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'parallel with' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Chair in edas is the overall chair of a conference (a Person who initiates calls and reviews papers). Speaker in iasted is a delegate who presents at the conference, with Author and Reviewer as subclasses. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity (a lecture), while Program Committee is a type of committee responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the program. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
Committee member is a person role in a conference committee, while Money is a financial concept. They are entirely unrelated.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference restaurant is a physical place/building. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while is_present links a Person to a Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review expertise in Ontology A represents a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill regarding a topic/paper (linked to reviewers and submitted contributions), whereas Review in edas is a Document subclass representing the actual written review artefact. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both classes represent a person who registered for the conference late. 'Late paid applicant' in Conference and 'Late Registered Participant' in ekaw both denote participants whose registration occurred after the early/regular deadline. Despite slightly different naming (applicant vs participant, paid vs registered), they refer to the same concept in the conference domain.

In edas, Person is the top-level class for all people (including authors, reviewers, chairs). In ekaw, Conference Participant is a subclass of Person, specifically for those participating in the conference, while other roles like Paper Author and Possible Reviewer are siblings outside Conference Participant. Thus edas:Person is broader than ekaw:Conference_Participant; they overlap but are not equivalent.

Student is a type of conference participant (person attending as a student), while Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

reviewWrittenBy links a Review to its reviewer (Possible Reviewer), while submit links an Author to a Paper. They describe entirely different relationships between different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while paperPresentedAs links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (a presentation event). These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.
Trip is a social event (an organized excursion) in confOf, while Van is a transport vehicle in iasted. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Conference www is a type of conference document (a web page/URL resource), while Tutorial is a type of lecture/conference activity. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The properties have completely different domains and ranges (Person->Organization vs Money->Building) and express unrelated concepts (employment vs payment location).

'is dated on' is a general datatype property linking any Activity to a dateTime, while 'Start of conference' specifically links a Conference to its start dateTime. They overlap in purpose (associating an event with a date) but differ in generality and specificity; the domain of A (Activity) subsumes B's domain (Conference), and A's meaning is broader than just a start date.

Submission event in confOf is an administrative event for submitting contributions, while Conference in ekaw is a scientific event representing one edition of a conference. They are conceptually distinct and unrelated.

In Ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific type of conference contributor. In Ontology B (sigkdd), 'Speaker' is a broader class that has 'Invited Speaker' as a subclass. Therefore, the general 'Speaker' class in sigkdd subsumes the more specific 'Invited speaker' class in Conference.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review certain topics/papers, while Paper in Ontology B represents the actual submitted document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper (child of Decision), while Tip is a form of money/gratuity (child of Money). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both properties relate a document-like entity (Item/Document) to a temporal constraint (Time/Deadline) concerning submission timing. However, 'is sent before' is a general temporal ordering property while 'submit until' specifically denotes a submission deadline. They overlap in the conference domain context but are not strictly equivalent.
Invited speaker is a type of person (a conference contributor), while Conference state is a type of state. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Passive conference participant is a type of person attending a conference, while Trip city is a type of city. They are completely unrelated concepts.

readByReviewer goes from Paper to Reviewer (Paper is read by Reviewer), while isReviewing goes from Reviewer (and other roles) to Paper (Reviewer is reviewing Paper). They express the same underlying relationship but in opposite directions, so they are inverses/related rather than equivalent.
Extended abstract is a type of conference document/contribution, while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are completely unrelated concepts.

hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (schedule), while hasEvent links an Event to sub-Events. A programme is a schedule of events rather than an event itself, so these properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent, though they are loosely related in the conference scheduling domain.

Country in confOf represents a geopolitical nation (used as a location/affiliation for persons and organizations), while Organization in edas represents an institutional entity such as academia, government, industry, or NGO. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume (organizational relationship), while Property B links an Author to a Contribution (authorship relationship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to its contained papers, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In edas, Social Event is a general class with children like Excursion and Reception (and sibling Meal Event). In iasted, Dinner banquet is a specific type of social program activity. A dinner banquet is a kind of social event, so edas:SocialEvent subsumes iasted:Dinner_banquet.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings. They are unrelated.
Meal Break is a type of conference event (a temporal break for eating), while Conference hall is a type of place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

confOf's Administrative event covers process-oriented events like submission, reviewing, and registration, while edas's Academic Event covers scholarly activities like paper presentations, talks, and workshops. They are both subclasses of a general conference event concept but have disjoint children and different intended instances, so they are related (overlapping as event types) but not equivalent.

Meeting Room Place refers to a room where sessions/meetings occur, while Main office refers to an administrative office location. Both are subclasses of Place but denote entirely different types of locations within the conference domain.

Both classes represent a member of the Program Committee in a conference organization context. Despite different parent hierarchies (Conference Member vs Organizator), their intended instances coincide: individuals serving on the program committee.

Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) responsible for chairing, while Lecture is a conference activity/event (subclass of Conference activity). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

maxPapers is a datatype property linking Program Committee Member to an int (maximum number of papers), while done_till links Deadline to a date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in edas represents a conference event/organization, while Document in sigkdd represents written artefacts like papers and reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Reception is a subclass of Social Event, while in ekaw, Social_Event is the broader class with children like Conference Banquet and Conference Trip. Thus, edas:Reception is subsumed by ekaw:Social_Event.

Reception in confOf is a social event (like a party or gathering) at a conference, while Receiving manuscript in iasted is an administrative activity of receiving paper submissions before the conference. They share no semantic overlap despite both containing the word root 'receiv'.
readByMeta-Reviewer relates a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (reading action), while obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

startReviewerBidding relates an Administrator to a Conference to initiate reviewer bidding, while need relates a Person to an Item they require. These properties have entirely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Property A ('has a volume') describes the number of volumes in conference proceedings (domain: Conference proceedings, range: int). Property B ('min Choice') describes a minimum choice constraint for social/working events (domain: Social event, Working event, range: positiveInteger). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
startDate denotes the beginning of a conference while End_of_conference denotes its end. They are distinct temporal properties with opposite meanings, not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Property A ('is sent before') relates an Item to a Time (a temporal constraint), while property B ('submit') relates an Author to a Paper (an action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator regarding paper assignment finalization, while 'submit' links an Author to a Paper regarding submission.

'ends on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (date), while 'part Of Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (mereological relation). They have completely different semantics, domains/ranges, and purposes.

Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document/publication (subclass of Multi author Volume > Proceedings), while Conference days in iasted is a temporal concept (subclass of Time). They share only the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

An Invitation letter is a document used to invite participants (e.g., for visa purposes), while a Paper is a scholarly submission. They are distinct types of documents with no overlap in intended instances.
Dining Place is a location for eating, while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent the scientific/academic portion of a conference event hierarchy. 'Academic Event' in edas (child of Conference Event, sibling of Non Academic Event) and 'Scientific Event' in ekaw (child of Event, sibling of Social Event) share the same intended meaning: events such as paper presentations, workshops, sessions, and talks that are scholarly in nature, as opposed to social or non-academic activities. Their children (Workshop, Paper Presentation/Individual Presentation, etc.) further confirm equivalence.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person invited to give a talk at the conference, while a 'Student' is a participant who is a student. These are entirely different roles/concepts with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship in the conference domain.

Participant in confOf is a general class for all conference attendees (subclasses include Member, Regular, Student), whereas Lecturer in iasted is a very specific role (a type of Speaker/Author who gives lectures). These are not equivalent; Participant is far more general and does not specifically denote someone giving a lecture.

Both properties represent a currency string, but they apply to entirely different domains: hasCostCurrency is for Sponsorship in edas, while Currency is for Registration fee in sigkdd. Since they relate different kinds of things, they are not equivalent.

Conference Banquet is a social event (an activity), while Conference hotel is a building (a place). They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent or related in a subsumption sense.

Conference Venue Place is a spatial location (subclass of Place) where the conference is held, while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline (subclass of Deadline) for reserving a hotel. They are entirely different concepts.

Rejected contribution is a paper/submission that was not accepted, while Negative Review is an evaluation document (a review) expressing a negative opinion. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version in cmt is a complete paper (child of Paper), while Abstract in sigkdd is a summary document (sibling of Paper). They represent different kinds of documents and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Property A (hasLocation) links a Conference Event to a Place, indicating where an event takes place. Property B (is_situated_in) links spatial entities (Building, City, Place) to broader spatial entities (State, etc.), expressing geographic containment. The domains and ranges differ fundamentally (event-to-place vs. place-to-place), so they are unrelated.

Author Not Reviewer is a subclass of Author representing an author who is not a reviewer, while Two Level Conference is a type of conference in edas. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Author is a person who writes or submits papers, while Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., paper presentation, workshop). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Welcome Talk is a conference event (a type of Talk Event). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Meal Break (a specific type of break event for eating) and Social program (a broader category of social conference activities including dinner banquets, cocktail receptions, etc.) overlap in the domain of non-academic/social conference events but are not equivalent. Meal Break is more specific than Social program, yet they belong to different taxonomic structures; 'related' best captures their partial overlap.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered review criteria), while 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution. They are unrelated.

In sigkdd, 'Deadline Abstract Submission' and 'Deadline Paper Submission' are distinct siblings, indicating that the abstract submission deadline is specifically for submitting abstracts (not full papers). In iasted, 'Submissions deadline' likely refers to the full paper submission deadline. Since sigkdd distinguishes between abstract and paper submission deadlines while iasted does not, these are related but not strictly equivalent.

Both classes represent physical locations where conference events take place. In edas, Place is the range of hasLocation for ConferenceEvent; in ekaw, Location is the range of heldIn for Event. Their intended instances coincide.
An organizing committee is a group responsible for organizing a conference, while a university is an educational institution. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee (whole-part relationship), while Property B links a Person to a Conference (membership relationship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee (general membership), while property B links a Chair to a Committee (a leadership role). Both express committee affiliation but differ in the specificity of the role (member vs chair) and the type of committee, so they are related but not equivalent.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Reviewer and Program Committee Member are distinct sibling classes under Conference Member. In ekaw, PC Member is a subclass of Possible Reviewer. These represent overlapping but not equivalent roles: a reviewer in cmt need not be a PC member, and a PC member in ekaw is a specific type of possible reviewer. They are related but not equivalent.
Short paper is a type of academic contribution (a document), while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor (an organization or role). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information), while a 'Full day tour' is an activity after the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The two properties have completely different domains (Person vs Sponsorship), ranges (string vs int), and semantics (first name of a person vs cost amount of a sponsorship). They are unrelated.
Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic in the conference domain, while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Submitted Paper is a document/artefact (a paper that has been submitted), while Committee is a group of people organizing or reviewing for the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A ('has a location') denotes the physical or virtual location of a conference volume, while Property B ('Name of conference') denotes the name/title of a conference. These are semantically distinct properties with different meanings, despite both being datatype properties with string ranges.

Both classes represent the same role: the chair of a conference. Despite slightly different positions in their respective hierarchies (cmt places it under Chairman and Conference Member, edas directly under Person), the intended instances are identical—the person who chairs the conference.

Both classes represent the concept of a paper that has been accepted for a conference. Despite differences in their parent hierarchies (edas uses Paper directly, ekaw uses Evaluated Paper), they denote the same set of instances: papers that have passed the review process and been accepted.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (e.g., instructions, announcements), while 'CAD Topic' is a subject area topic (Computer-Aided Design) for paper submissions. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Review expertise in Ontology A denotes a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill regarding a topic/paper, while Review in Ontology B (iasted) is a Document subclass representing the actual written review artefact. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Property A links a review preference to a submitted contribution or topic, while property B links a person to an item they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Call for paper is a type of conference document (an announcement soliciting papers), while Conference hall is a physical place where conferences are held. They are entirely different concepts.
