Both properties link an Author to a Paper, but 'hasRelatedPaper' is a general association (an author may be related to a paper without submitting it), while 'submit' specifically denotes the act of submission. They overlap in practice but are not semantically equivalent.

Rejected contribution is a class of papers/contributions that were rejected after review, while Reject Rating is a type of review rating (a score or classification given by a reviewer). They belong to different branches of the ontology hierarchy and represent fundamentally different concepts.
Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who entered details, while property B links a Conference volume to its Tutorials. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Paper is a general class (child of Document) encompassing all paper states including Active, Pending, Accepted, Rejected, etc. In ekaw, Assigned Paper is a much more specific subclass of Submitted Paper (which is itself a subclass of Paper). Therefore, edas:Paper subsumes ekaw:Assigned_Paper.

Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in the conference (subclass of Person), while Conference www in the Conference ontology is a web document/URL resource (subclass of Conference document). They are entirely different concepts.
Passive conference participant is a type of person attending a conference, while Conference is an event. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for finalizing paper assignments, while writes relates an Author to a Contribution for authoring. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'has important dates' links a conference volume to its important dates, while 'organised By' links an event to the organisation or person that organises it. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Review is a document evaluating a paper, while Tax is a monetary charge. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejection action), while issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publication action). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

cmt:User is a subclass of Person representing anyone who uses the system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). iasted:Speaker is a subclass of Delegate representing someone who presents at the conference. While both share Author and Reviewer as children, their intended instances differ: User includes administrators and non-presenting roles, while Speaker specifically denotes presenters. They overlap but are not equivalent.
Company is an organization (e.g., employer or sponsor), while Credit card is a payment instrument. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and share no semantic overlap.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper (part-of/content relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Tax (a type of Money with children like Departure tax and Value added tax) is conceptually distinct from Sponzor fee (a type of Fee). They represent different financial concepts in the conference domain.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

maxPapers relates a Program Committee Member to the maximum number of papers they can handle (an int), while has_a_volume relates Conference proceedings to its volume number (an int). They have completely different domains and semantics.

Session Chair in edas is a person who chairs a session and participates in reviewing, while Author in sigkdd is a speaker who submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.
'has authors' links a conference document to its author(s) (Person), while 'has City' links an Organization or Person to a City. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

has_an_ISBN is a datatype property for the ISBN of conference proceedings, while hasTitle is a datatype property for the title of a contribution. They describe entirely different attributes (identifier vs. name) on different domains.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while is_present relates a Person to a Time (temporal presence). Different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document indicating a conflict of interest, while hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country indicating geographic affiliation. These are entirely different relations.

Entity A is a class representing an individual person who is a member of the program committee (Program Committee Member), while Entity B is a class representing the committee as a collective body (Program committee). A member belongs to a committee, but they are not the same concept.

confOf's Social event (children: Banquet, Reception, Trip) overlaps with edas's Non Academic Event but is not strictly equivalent. edas's Non Academic Event also includes Break Event and Meal Event, and has its own child called Social Event. confOf's Social event is broader than edas's Social Event but narrower than edas's Non Academic Event, making them related rather than equivalent or in a clean subsumption.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Reviewing event is an administrative event/procedure. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information), while a 'Video presentation' is a type of presentation activity at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes are named 'Organization' in the conference domain. Ontology B's Organization has children (Academia, Government, Industry, NGO) and properties related to sponsorship, which is consistent with a general organization class in a conference ontology. Ontology A's Organization is also a general class for organizations. They denote the same concept.
Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts.

Both properties associate a date value with a deadline/important-dates entity, but 'is an ending date' specifically denotes the end date of an important date period, whereas 'Date' in sigkdd is a more general date property for a Deadline. They overlap in purpose but are not strictly equivalent.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Presenter university is a physical building/place where a presenter is affiliated. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference in edas represents the actual conference event/organization, while Conference state in iasted represents a status or state of a conference (subclass of State). These are fundamentally different concepts.
Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee, while property B links a Person to an Item (writing). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Organization in Conference is a general class for any organization, while Government Organization in edas is a specific subclass of Organization (with siblings like Academia Organization, Industry Organization, NGO). Therefore, the general Organization subsumes Government Organization.
The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person, while 'design' relates ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. They are unrelated.

In cmt, Meta Reviewer is a subclass of Reviewer (Person > Conference Member > Reviewer > Meta Reviewer). In Conference, Reviewer is a direct subclass of Person. A Meta Reviewer is a specific type of reviewer, so the cmt Meta Reviewer class is subsumed by the more general Conference Reviewer class.

Track is a thematic subdivision of a conference (e.g., research track), while Meal Event is a non-academic social event involving food. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

belongsToEvent links a Programme to the Conference Event it belongs to (domain: Programme, range: Conference Event), while eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed (domain: Event, range: Programme Brochure/Web Site). The domains, ranges, and directions are different; they model distinct relationships.
Conference Proceedings is a document/publication (a collection of papers), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They share the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

endReview is an object property linking a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while End_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (the date the conference ends). They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and meanings.

reviewerOfPaper relates a reviewer to a paper they review, while write relates a person to an item they author. Reviewing and writing/authoring are distinct roles in the conference domain, so these properties are unrelated.

Program Committee in cmt is a committee/group entity, while Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a subclass of Person (an individual role). They represent fundamentally different concepts (a group vs. a person) and are unrelated.

Property A links a Presentation to the participant who delivers it, while property B links a Call (e.g., call for papers) to the person who initiated it. The domains (Presentation vs Call), ranges (Active conference participant vs Chair/TPC Member), and semantics (delivering vs initiating) are entirely different.

ConferenceVenuePlace in edas is a general venue for the conference (with siblings like AccommodationPlace and DiningPlace), while Session_room in iasted specifically denotes a room where sessions take place. In edas, MeetingRoomPlace would be the closer equivalent to Session_room. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for a person (likely a student) who studies at a university. In ekaw, SC Member is a Steering Committee member, which is a specific role within the PC hierarchy. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific kind of conference contributor. In ontology B (ekaw), 'Presenter' is a broader class that has 'Invited Speaker' as a child. Therefore, A's Invited speaker is subsumed by B's Presenter.

Person in confOf represents a human individual (author, participant, etc.), while State in iasted represents a geographical or administrative region (with children like Conference state, Presenter state being locations). These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties represent a postal code as a string, but they differ in domain: confOf applies it directly to Organization or Person, while edas applies it to Contact Information (an intermediary class). They capture the same real-world attribute but relate different kinds of entities, so they are related rather than equivalent.
'has authors' links a conference document to its author (Person), while 'occupy' links a Person to a location (Building, City, State). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A Workshop is a working event (a session for collaborative work or presentations), while a Coffee break is a social/rest activity during a conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Submitted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been submitted), while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'isMenuOf' links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. They are unrelated.
'isWrittenBy' relates a Paper to its Author, while 'pay' relates a Person to Money. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Submission event in confOf is an administrative event (a process/activity for submitting contributions), while Record of attendance in iasted is a document (an artefact recording who attended). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities with no semantic overlap.

Member in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (an event type). They represent entirely different concepts in the domain.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a superclass that includes both Invited talk and other contributed presentations (Regular contribution, Poster, Written contribution are siblings but Invited talk is also listed as a child). In Ontology B, Contributed Talk is a subclass of Individual Presentation, with Invited Talk as a sibling. Thus, A's Presentation is more general than B's Contributed Talk, which specifically excludes invited talks. Therefore A subsumes B.
Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while Presenter house is a building (a physical place/accommodation). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

hasCo-author links a Paper to its Co-author (paper -> person), while contributes links a Person to a Conference document (person -> document). They have opposite directions and different semantics: one denotes co-authorship of a paper, the other denotes contribution to a document.

In Ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a type of conference document/contribution (with children Paper, Extended abstract). In Ontology B, 'Regular' is a type of Participant (person), sibling to Student and Member. They share the word 'Regular' but denote entirely different concepts (a document vs. a person role).

Science Worker in confOf is a broad class for any person involved in scientific work (parent of Author, Scholar, etc.), while Program Chair in sigkdd is a specific organizational role responsible for the conference program. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in a meaningful alignment sense.
A Slide Set is a collection of presentation slides, while an Abstract is a brief summary of a paper. These are entirely different types of documents in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the concept of an Author in a conference domain. In confOf, Author is a Person who writes Contributions (papers). In sigkdd, Author is a Speaker (subclass of Person) who submits Papers. Despite different parent hierarchies (Person vs Speaker), their intended instances—people who author/submit papers to the conference—coincide.

Conference hotel in iasted is a specific type of hotel used for conference purposes (subclass of Building), while Hotel in sigkdd is a general accommodation class (subclass of Place). The conference-specific hotel is subsumed by the more general Hotel class.
Conference activity is a type of event/activity (e.g., lecture, coffee break), while Speaker is a role played by a person. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur simultaneously, while 'for Event' relates a Call to an Academic Event it is associated with. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

locationOf relates a Location to an Event (the event takes place at the location), while can_stay_in relates a Person to a Place (a person stays at a place). The domains and ranges are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.
The properties have completely different domains and ranges (Conference->Administrator vs Person->Item) and different semantics (entering details vs preparing an item). They are unrelated.

Property A gives a URL for a conference website (domain: Conference www), while property B gives a title for a contribution/paper (domain: Contribution). They describe entirely different attributes of different entities.

The properties have different domains and ranges and opposite directions: 'relatesTo' links a Document to events/persons, while 'give' links a Person to activities/items. They do not express the same relation.

manuscriptDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline for manuscript submission, while paperPresentedAs is an object property linking a Paper to an Individual Presentation. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their email address (string), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to an Item they obtain. They have different ranges, different types (datatype vs object), and entirely different semantics.

Both classes represent the general concept of a Person in the conference domain. They share similar properties (email/E-mail, name/Name) and serve as top-level parent classes for various conference roles (Chairman, Reviewer vs Listener, Speaker, Organizator). Their intended instances coincide.

'technicallyOrganisedBy' in ekaw is a sub-property of 'organisedBy', relating an event to its organizing body. 'presentationed_by' in sigkdd relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'hold' relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Accpet If Room Rating is a type of review rating in edas, while Abstract is a type of document in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
writtenBy relates a Document to its authoring Person, while obtain relates an Author to an Award they received. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes are named 'Review' and are subclasses of 'Document' in their respective conference ontologies. In the conference domain, a Review refers to the evaluation document written for a submitted paper. Despite differences in sibling classes due to varying ontology granularity, the intended instances (review documents) coincide.

confOf's 'Science Worker' is a broad class under Person encompassing anyone working in science (authors, scholars, PC members, etc.). iasted's 'Worker lecturer' is a very specific subclass of Lecturer > Speaker > Author > Delegate, denoting a lecturer who is also a worker. The latter is much more specific than the former, so they are related but not equivalent; 'Science Worker' subsumes 'Worker lecturer'.
Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Mailing list is a type of document. They are completely unrelated concepts.

A Sponsor is a person or entity providing financial support for the conference, while a Webmaster is an organizer responsible for the conference website. These are entirely different roles with no semantic overlap.

Property A links a Topic to a Conference part (indicating subject matter), while Property B links an Item to a Person (indicating necessity). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
has_an_email refers to an email address while hasFirstName refers to a person's first name; they are distinct datatype properties with different semantics despite sharing the same domain and range.

hasUpdatedVersion relates a Document to another Document (a newer version), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

A 'Sponsor company house' is a building associated with a sponsor company (a sibling of Conference building, Conference hotel, etc.), while a 'Conference hall' is the venue where conference sessions take place. These are distinct types of places in the conference domain.

Track workshop chair is a specific organizational role responsible for chairing tracks or workshops at a conference. Scholar in confOf is a price category for attendees (e.g., students/academics paying a scholar rate) and has no chairing responsibilities. They are unrelated concepts.

Review in Ontology A is a conference document representing the evaluation of a paper, while Numerical Review Question in edas is a specific type of question (with a numerical answer) used within a review form. They are entirely different concepts.

Tutorial in confOf is a type of Event (a working event), while Tutorial Chair in ekaw is a type of Person (a conference participant role). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities and thus unrelated.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference registrant who paid late), while Accepting manuscript is a subclass of Activity (the process of accepting a manuscript). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Neutral Review is a type of review document (an artefact), while Reviewer is a person who reviews. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are unrelated.
Social event is a type of conference event (e.g., banquet, reception), while Speaker is a type of person who presents at the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

A 'Program committee' is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the technical program of a conference, while a 'Social program' is a type of conference activity (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Meta Reviewer is a subclass of Reviewer (a special type of reviewer who oversees other reviews). In iasted, Reviewer is the general reviewer class. Therefore, cmt:Meta Reviewer is subsumed by iasted:Reviewer, as every meta-reviewer is a reviewer but not every reviewer is a meta-reviewer.
Property A is a string-valued remark on a Contribution (paper), while property B is a dateTime deadline on a Conference. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Antennas Topic is a subject area classification under Topic, while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Submitted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been submitted), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal deadline. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while belongs_to_a_review_reference links a Topic to a Review preference. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Conference Chair is a leadership role (chairman of the conference), while Student non speaker is a student delegate who does not present. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a presentation/document to the person delivering it (Active conference participant / Speaker). In the conference domain, 'is given by' from Presentation and 'presentationed by' from Document express the same relation: who presents the work.

confOf's 'Social event' is a general class with children including Banquet, Reception, and Trip. iasted's 'Dinner banquet' is a specific type of social program (a banquet). Therefore, Social event subsumes Dinner banquet.

Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document/publication (a multi-author volume), while Conference activity in iasted refers to events or activities occurring at a conference (e.g., lectures, coffee breaks). These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties express an assignment/giving relationship from a document-like entity to a person-like entity. In the conference domain, 'assigned To' (Paper -> Reviewer) and 'is given to' (Item -> Person) likely serve similar purposes (assigning a paper/item to a reviewer/person). However, the domain and range classes differ in specificity (Paper/Reviewer vs Item/Person), so they are related rather than strictly equivalent.

In ontology A, 'Conference' represents the overall conference entity (with children like Conference volume and properties like has a name). In edas, 'ConferenceEvent' represents individual events/sessions occurring within a conference (with children Academic Event, Non Academic Event, and properties like start/end date, location, programme). The overall conference in edas would be modeled differently. These are related concepts but not equivalent; Conference is broader than a single event.

Property A links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (governance/oversight role), while Property B links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizing/hosting role). These are conceptually distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

cmt:name is a general name property with domain Conference and Person, while edas:hasFirstName specifically denotes a person's first name (domain Person only). The general 'name' subsumes the more specific 'first name'.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Proceedings in ekaw is a type of multi-author document/volume. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person (with siblings like Chairman and Conference Member also under Person), so it represents only a subset of people involved in the conference. In the Conference ontology, Person is the top-level class for all individuals. Thus cmt:User overlaps with but does not fully coincide with Conference:Person; they are related rather than equivalent.
Administrator is a person role responsible for managing the conference system, while Paper is a document submitted by authors. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Rejected contribution is a submitted paper that was not accepted, while Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's past publications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Event' and serve as the top-level class for conference-related happenings. Both have 'Social event' as a child (Administrative/Working vs Scientific are subtypes of events in a conference). In the OAEI Conference track reference alignment, confOf:Event and ekaw:Event are considered equivalent.

Invited speaker is a specific type of conference contributor who gives an invited talk. IASTED non member refers to a delegate's membership status (not being a member of IASTED). These are conceptually distinct: one describes a speaking role, the other describes organizational membership. They are unrelated.

'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'holded by' links a Conference to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and purposes.

In edas, 'Published Paper' denotes a paper in a specific lifecycle state (having been published), sibling to Accepted, Rejected, etc. In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' denotes a category/type of paper (as opposed to Demo, Poster, Industrial papers). These are orthogonal classifications: one is about publication status, the other about submission track/type. They do not denote the same concept.

In Ontology A, 'Paper' is a general class for all papers (a type of regular contribution). In edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper', restricted to papers that have been accepted. Therefore, the general 'Paper' in A subsumes the more specific 'Accepted Paper' in B.

Property A is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while Property B is an object property linking an Organisation to published documents. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Accpet If Room Rating is a type of review rating. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'hardcopy Mailing Manifests Printed By' relates a Conference to an Administrator who prints manifests, while 'follows' relates one Administrative event to another in a temporal sequence. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event, while obtain links a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Both properties express an end date/time, but 'ends on' applies to any Event (with string range) while 'End of conference' applies specifically to Conference (with dateTime range). They overlap in meaning for conferences but differ in domain generality and range type, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Credit card is a payment instrument (subclass of Card/Item), while Author of paper is a person role (subclass of Author/Speaker). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Contribution co-author is a specific role denoting a non-primary author of a conference contribution, while Lecturer is a type of speaker who delivers a lecture at the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances and no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

In Ontology A, 'Important dates' is a class representing a collection of deadline dates (abstract submission, full paper submission, camera ready, acceptance announcement, start/end dates) associated with a conference volume. In Ontology B, 'Submission event' is specifically an administrative event for the submission of contributions. While both relate to the submission process, 'Important dates' is a broader container of multiple date properties covering the entire conference lifecycle, whereas 'Submission event' is a specific type of event. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other; they model different aspects of conference organization.

Chairman in cmt is a specific leadership role (with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), whereas Participant in confOf is a general conference attendee role (with children like Regular, Student). In confOf, chair roles are modeled as siblings of Participant (e.g., Chair PC), not as subclasses. These classes represent different concepts and do not share the same intended instances.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an organized gathering), while Worker non speaker in iasted is a type of delegate/person attending the conference who is neither a speaker nor a student. These are entirely different concepts (event vs. person role).
Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (track/workshop/tutorial topic), while Property B links a Person to an Item they need. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking a location (Building, City, State) to a Person who visits it. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Conference building (iasted) is a type of Building used for the conference, while Hotel (sigkdd) is an accommodation place. They are both subclasses of Place in their respective ontologies and serve related but distinct roles in conference organization. The iasted ontology has a separate 'Conference hotel' sibling class, confirming that 'Conference building' is not equivalent to 'Hotel'.

Both classes represent the proceedings of a conference. Ontology A's 'Conference proceedings' has properties like publisher, volume, and ISBN typical of proceedings, while Ontology B's 'Conference Proceedings' is explicitly placed under Document > Multi author Volume > Proceedings in its hierarchy. They denote the same concept.
Banquet is a social event (a meal/gathering), while Publication is a published document or proceedings. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version). In ekaw, Workshop Paper is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper submitted to a workshop). Therefore, the general Paper in cmt subsumes the more specific Workshop Paper in ekaw.

In the conference domain, a 'Bid' (cmt) represents a reviewer's preference or bid on a paper to review it. 'Review preference' (Conference) captures the same concept: a reviewer's stated preference for reviewing a submitted contribution or topic. Both link reviewers to papers/topics and express willingness/preference to review, making them equivalent in this context.

Submitted contribution in Ontology A refers to a paper or written work submitted for review at a conference. Form in Ontology B (iasted) is an administrative document with children like registration form and hotel registration form. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, while technicallyOrganises links an Organisation to something it organises. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in Ontology A represents the conference event/organization itself (with children like Conference volume and properties like has a name), while Conference hall in Ontology B is a physical place/venue (subclass of Place, sibling of Hotel). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Accepted Paper (edas) and Submitted Paper (ekaw) represent different stages in the paper lifecycle. A submitted paper is one that has been turned in for review, while an accepted paper is one that has passed review and been accepted. They are related as sequential states of a paper but not equivalent.

An 'Organizing committee' is a group of people (a Committee) responsible for organizing a conference, while an 'Administrative event' is a type of Event (with children like Submission event, Reviewing event). These are fundamentally different concepts (group vs. event) and are unrelated.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while payed_by links a Registration fee to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Paper in edas represents a submitted academic paper (with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper), while Review in sigkdd represents a review document. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; notably, sigkdd also has its own Paper class as a sibling of Review.

Company in confOf represents a commercial/business organization (sibling of University), while Academia Organization in edas represents an academic institution. These are distinct types of organizations; Company would more closely align with Industry Organization in edas, and University with Academia Organization. They overlap only in both being subclasses of Organization.
Property A links a Publisher to Conference proceedings it issues, while property B links an Academic Event to its Call (for papers). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Conference volume' is a direct subclass of 'Conference' and represents the conference event itself (it has committees, location, tracks, important dates, etc.). In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Conference Proceedings' is a document/publication (subclass of Multi author Volume > Proceedings). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event/organizational entity, the other is a published document. They are related in that proceedings are typically produced for a conference, but they are not equivalent.

'is situated in' relates spatial entities (Building, City, Place) to broader locations (State), while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place for accommodation. Different domains and different semantics.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while 'speak in' relates a Person to a Place/Time (indicating where/when someone speaks). These are entirely different relations with different semantics and ranges.

In edas, Paper is a direct subclass of Document and represents all papers in general. In ekaw, Regular Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is itself a subclass of Document), making it a specific type of paper. Therefore, edas:Paper subsumes ekaw:Regular_Paper.

markConflictOfInterest indicates a conflict between a person and a paper (preventing assignment/reviewing), while isReviewing indicates an active reviewing relationship. These are semantically distinct and even somewhat opposite in intent.

Reviewed contribution is a document/paper that has undergone review (a subclass of Submitted contribution), while Reviewing event is an administrative event/procedure for reviewing contributions. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (artefact vs. event) and thus unrelated.
Property A links a Conference volume to Important dates, while property B links a Person to an Item they need. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
Conference Trip is a social event (an excursion), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person representing system users (Administrators, Authors, Reviewers) who interact with the conference management system. In Conference ontology, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person representing people applying to attend or register for the conference (with child 'Registeered applicant'). These are conceptually different roles: one is about system access/management, the other is about attendance application. They share only the common ancestor Person.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person specifically invited to present at the conference, while a 'Hotel presenter' in iasted is a subclass of Delegate under Conference building (likely someone presenting from/at a hotel venue). These are conceptually distinct roles with different intended instances and hierarchical contexts.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while is_given_to relates an Item to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper review assignment), while technicallyOrganisedBy is a sub-property of organisedBy relating an event or session to its technical organizer. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Audiovisual equipment refers to physical items like projectors and computers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the concept of a conference in the conference-organisation domain. In cmt, Conference is a top-level class with properties like date, members, and paper assignments. In ekaw, Conference is a subclass of Scientific Event (under Event) with the comment 'One edition of a conference'. Despite different modeling choices (standalone vs. event hierarchy), they denote the same real-world concept.

Paper Presentation in edas is a specific type of presentation tied to an accepted paper, while Presentation in iasted is a more general conference activity that includes subtypes like PowerPoint and Video presentations. Thus, Paper Presentation is subsumed by the broader Presentation class.

Both classes represent a review document in the conference domain. They share the same label, are subclasses of a document class (Conference document vs Document), and have analogous properties linking them to papers/contributions and reviewers.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (inverse direction of authorship/ownership), while Property B links a Person to an Item they write. The domains, ranges, and directions are fundamentally different, making them unrelated.

Both classes represent the subject area or research topic of a conference paper/event. In Conference ontology, Topic is linked to submitted contributions and conference parts; in ekaw, Research_Topic is covered by Papers and Events. They denote the same concept in the conference domain.
locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while done_till is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor (an organization or entity exhibiting at the conference). These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties describe entirely different concepts: 'print Hardcopy Mailing Manifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference for mailing purposes, while 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. They share no semantic overlap.

'has title' is a datatype property linking events to their string titles, while 'End of conference' links a Conference to a dateTime representing when it ends. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call (call for papers/participation), while hold links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it organizes. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both are subclasses of Committee in the conference domain, but an Organizing committee is responsible for overall conference organization, while a Best Paper Awards Committee specifically selects best paper award winners. They are distinct sibling concepts under Committee, hence related but not equivalent.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event concerning the submission of contributions, while B 'Registation deadline' is a time/deadline for registration. They differ both in domain concept (event vs. deadline) and topic (submission vs. registration).
confOf:City is a general city class, while iasted:Presenter_city is a specific subclass of City (a city associated with a presenter). The general City subsumes the more specific Presenter city.
The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'designed by' relates a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while pay relates a Person to Money (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewCriteriaEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator for entering review criteria, while 'invited_by' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer who invited them.

Camera ready manuscript deadline refers to the deadline for submitting the final version of an accepted paper, while Deadline Paper Submission refers to the initial paper submission deadline. Both are types of deadlines in the conference domain but represent different stages, so they are related but not equivalent.

Reviewing event is an administrative procedure for reviewing submitted contributions, while Conference is a scientific event representing one edition of a conference. They are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Conference is an event/organization. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Multimedia Topic is a subject area for papers/conferences, while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Video presentation is a type of conference activity (a presentation format), while Organizator is a type of Person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

The property 'member Of Program Committee' links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document. These relate entirely different domain concepts and have no semantic overlap.
Money is a financial concept (with children like Fee, Tax, Tip), while ACM SIGKDD represents the organizing body/conference entity. They are entirely unrelated.

Both properties link a paper presentation event to the paper being presented, but they point in opposite directions: 'relatedToPaper' goes from Paper Presentation to Accepted Paper, while 'paperPresentedAs' goes from Paper to Individual Presentation. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related (inverses).

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Operating Topicsystems in edas is a subclass of Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent the entity that publishes conference proceedings. In Ontology A, Publisher issues Conference proceedings and is named; in ekaw, Proceedings_Publisher is a subclass of Organisation serving the same role. They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference document to its authors (Person), while property B links a Conference (event) to its members (Person). The domains are fundamentally different (document vs. event), and the relations express different semantics (authorship vs. membership), so they are unrelated.

Both properties link a conference document/paper to the person(s) who authored it. 'has authors' (Conference document -> Person) and 'written By' (Document -> Person) express the same authorship relation in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Conference Trip is a social event (an activity/outing). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Technic activity is a type of conference activity (event), while Conference hall is a type of place (location). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.
hasSurname captures a person's family name while E-mail captures their email address; these are distinct properties with different semantics despite sharing the same domain and range.

Both represent organized excursions/tours as part of a conference's social programme. However, confOf:Trip is a general 'Social event' (sibling of Banquet, Reception) without duration constraints, while iasted:Full_day_tour specifically denotes a tour lasting a full day and occurring after the conference. They overlap in intent but are not strictly equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial match.

Positive Review is a type of document (a review with positive sentiment), while Reviewer is a person who writes reviews. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (document vs. person) and are unrelated.

Late Registered Participant refers to a conference attendee who registered late, while Session chair refers to a person who chairs a session. These are entirely different roles within the conference domain.
'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'is paid by' relates Money to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

A Session Chair is a specific role responsible for chairing a session, while Possible Reviewer is a broader class of people who could potentially review papers (with PC Member as a subclass). They share the ability to review papers in their respective ontologies but denote different concepts; they overlap but are not equivalent.

'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document, while 'is sent by' has domain Item and range Person. They are inverses of each other (Person contributes Document vs Document is sent by Person), not equivalent properties.

The property 'assign External Reviewer' relates a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment action), while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (a writing/authorship action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has members' is a specific property linking a Committee to its Committee members, while 'has Part' is a generic mereological part-whole relation with unspecified domain and range. They serve different purposes and relate different kinds of entities.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Presenter is a person (a type of author). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing the abstract version/format of a paper submission (sibling of 'Paper Full Version'). In Conference ontology, 'Extended abstract' is a type of 'Regular contribution' (sibling of 'Paper') and has 'Abstract' as a child class. While both relate to short-form academic submissions, they occupy different positions in their respective hierarchies: one is a subtype of Paper, the other is a sibling of Paper. They are related but not equivalent.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Switching Topic is a research topic classification. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Week Reject Rating is a specific type of review rating (a score/decision category) in edas, while Review in sigkdd is a document representing the written evaluation of a paper. They are fundamentally different concepts: one is a rating classification, the other is a document.
providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (the sponsor), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (the presenter). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A is a datatype property giving the name of a Conference or Person (range: string), while B is an object property linking an Event to its organiser (Organisation or Person). They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

A 'Conference city' is a city where the conference takes place (a geographic/administrative entity), while a 'Conference hall' is a specific building or room where sessions are held. These are distinct concepts at different levels of granularity and are not equivalent.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' is the event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts submissions). In ontology B, 'Conference contributor' is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to the conference (e.g., authors, speakers). These are entirely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a person role.

Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject area/topic for conference papers (related to electrical power transmission), while Transport vehicle is a physical item class representing vehicles like cars and buses. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level, while property B links an author to a contribution they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

isReviewing relates reviewers/chairs to papers they review, while presentationed_by relates documents to speakers who present them. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while 'hasMenu' in edas relates a meal event to a meal menu. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Attendee in edas is a subclass of Person representing a person attending the conference, while Author attendee cd registration fee in iasted is a subclass of Money/Registration fee representing a monetary amount. They are entirely different concepts (person vs. fee).

Program Committee Chair is a leadership role within the program committee (subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member), while Reviewer in iasted is a subclass of Speaker/Delegate who reviews papers. A chair may review but the concepts are distinct roles; they are not equivalent.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment for review), while writes links an Author to a Contribution (authorship). These relate entirely different domain entities and express different relationships.
One property represents a person's first name while the other represents a phone number; they capture entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range.
Taxi is a transport vehicle class, while Organizator is a person role involved in organizing a conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Assigned Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document that has been assigned for review), while Committee is an organizational body (e.g., Program Committee). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Operating Topicsystems is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area, while Program Committee is a subclass of Committee representing an organizational body. They are entirely different concepts.

Ontology A's 'Committee' is a general class with children including Organizing committee, Program committee, and Steering committee. Ontology B's 'Organizing Committee' is a specific subclass of Committee. Therefore, A's Committee subsumes B's Organizing Committee.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Presenter state is a status/state of a presenter. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their email string, while Property B is an object property linking an Item to a Time indicating when it was sent before. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A is 'Author' (a person who writes/submits papers) while Entity B is 'Reviewer' (a person who reviews). In ontology B, Author is a sibling of Reviewer, confirming they are distinct roles. These classes are unrelated.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while hasTopic links a Working event to a Topic. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'pay' relates a Person to Money. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

'is given by' links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who delivers it, while 'event On List' links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In EKAW, Individual_Presentation is a Scientific Event (a presentation slot such as a talk or tutorial), while in SIGKDD, Paper is a Document (the written artefact). They are related via properties like paperPresentedAs/presentationOfPaper linking papers to presentations, but they are not the same concept.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (an academic gathering like a workshop or tutorial). In iasted, IASTED member is a type of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts: one is an event, the other is a person.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is oddly placed under 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact class) and mixes roles like first author and co-author. In Ontology B, 'Author' is a subclass of Person > Speaker who submits papers. While both relate to the concept of an author in a conference, their ontological placements differ significantly (A treats it partly as a contribution type, B as a person role). They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent due to these structural differences.

Person in edas is a general class for all people involved in a conference (attendees, authors, reviewers, chairs, etc.). Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person, specifically someone who gives a presentation. Therefore, edas:Person subsumes sigkdd:Speaker.

A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while B is an object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They are entirely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

assignedByReviewer relates an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (a delegation/assignment relationship between people), while reviewes relates a Member PC to a Contribution (a reviewing relationship between a person and a paper). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper they wrote, while volumeContainsPaper relates a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Call in edas represents a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts associated with an academic event, while Time in iasted represents temporal concepts like deadlines and conference days. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Submitted Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while Audiovisual equipment refers to physical AV hardware (projectors, etc.). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Submitted Paper in ekaw is a full paper that has been submitted (child of Paper), while Abstract in sigkdd is a summary document (sibling of Paper under Document). They represent different types of documents in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

Conference Event in edas represents a temporal event (with start/end dates, programmes, attendees), while Building in iasted represents a physical structure/location. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Meta Reviewer is a person/role (a special type of reviewer), while Paper is a document/artefact submitted to the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Subject Area in cmt refers to a topic or field of study that a paper can be classified under, while Building in iasted refers to a physical structure/venue. These are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A links a Review to a Paper (reviewOfPaper), while property B links a Speaker to a Document (presentation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'rejected By' links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In ontology A, 'Fee for extra trip' and 'Registration fee' are sibling subclasses of 'Fee', meaning they are distinct concepts. Ontology B's 'Registration fee' corresponds to A's 'Registration fee', not to 'Fee for extra trip'. They are related as both are types of fees but not equivalent.

isWrittenBy links a Paper to its Author (authorship), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (presentation). Although authors often present their papers, writing and presenting are distinct roles/relations in the conference domain, so these properties are related but not equivalent.

Short paper (confOf) and Regular Paper (ekaw) are both types of conference papers/contributions, but they represent different categories. A short paper is typically a brief contribution, while a regular paper is a full-length standard paper. They are sibling-like concepts under the broader notion of a paper, hence related but not equivalent.
Property A links an Abstract to the document it is part of (Paper, Poster, Presentation), while Property B links a Paper to its Author. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Organization is a general class for organizations (with children Company and University), while edas:Government Organization is a specific subclass of edas:Organization. Thus confOf:Organization subsumes edas:Government Organization.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (paper), while Gold Supporter is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific leadership role within a conference, while Conference participant (Conference) is a general class for anyone participating in the conference. A Conference Chair is necessarily a Conference participant, so Conference participant subsumes Conference Chair.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person applying to attend or participate in the conference (with child 'Registeered applicant'), while a 'Program Committee member' is an organizer who reviews papers and shapes the program. These are distinct roles with no subsumption relationship.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Place is a physical location. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'has a submitted contribution' links a review expertise to a submitted contribution (paper), while 'awarded by' links an award to its granting entity. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.
Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment, while Listener is a person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the subject/topic area of a paper or conference. In cmt, 'Subject Area' is linked to Paper via 'has Subject Area'; in edas, 'Topic' is linked to Paper and Conference via 'has Topic'. They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document (which also has Review as a sibling). In iasted, Document is a broader class whose children include Submission, Review, Form, etc. The cmt Paper corresponds more closely to iasted's Submission, while iasted's Document corresponds to cmt's Document. Therefore, cmt:Paper is subsumed by iasted:Document.
An 'Invited speaker' is a person who speaks at the conference by invitation, while a 'Student non speaker' is explicitly a delegate who does not speak and is a student. These are disjoint concepts.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Management Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Presenter house is a physical building/place where a presenter stays. They are entirely different concepts.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference event), whereas OC Member in ekaw is a subclass of Conference Participant (an organizing committee person). Despite the unusual parentage shown for Two Level Conference in edas (Conference, Person, TPC Member), it represents a conference format, not an organizing committee member role. These are unrelated concepts.

rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper they reject, while paperPresentedAs relates a Paper to the Individual Presentation it is presented as. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Organizer' typically refers to a person or role responsible for organizing the conference. In Ontology B (edas), 'Organization' refers to an institutional entity (e.g., academia, government, industry, NGO) that provides sponsorship. These are conceptually different: one is an agent/role, the other is an institution. They are related in that organizations can act as organizers, but they are not equivalent.

Property A links a Track workshop chair (person/role) to a Conference part they chaired, while Property B links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organised it. They have different domains, ranges, and directions of agency; one is about chairing a track, the other about organising an event.

In edas, 'Published Paper' is a specific subclass of 'Paper' (alongside Accepted, Rejected, etc.), representing a paper that has been published. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for submitted papers under Document. Therefore, edas:PublishedPaper is subsumed by sigkdd:Paper, as every published paper is a paper, but not every paper is published.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Event is a top-level class encompassing Administrative, Social, and Working events. edas:BreakEvent is a specific type of Non Academic Event (children include Coffee Break, Meal Break). Thus confOf:Event is strictly more general than edas:BreakEvent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Industrial Session is a type of event/session. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (domain: PersonalReviewHistory, range: Reviewer), while Property B links a Paper to a Review (domain: Paper, range: Review). They have completely different domains and ranges and represent distinct relationships in the conference domain.
Track is a conference part (like a tutorial or workshop), while Sponzorship is a type of Money (financial contribution). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Member in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while Registration Student in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (person vs. fee) and are unrelated.

A Tutorial is an instructional/educational working event, while an Organizational Meeting is a meeting for organizational purposes. They are distinct types of conference events with different intended instances.

Conference announcement is a type of document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Technic activity is a type of conference activity/event (e.g., lecture, presentation). They belong to fundamentally different categories (documents vs. activities) and are unrelated.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to the conference), while Social Event is a subclass of Event (a social gathering like a banquet or trip). They are entirely different concepts.

Organization in confOf represents an institution (Company, University) that employs people, while State in iasted represents a condition or status (Conference state, Presenter state, Sponsor state). These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the same concept: a person who is the author of a paper. 'Paper Author' in ekaw and 'Author of paper' in sigkdd have identical intended instances despite different hierarchical placements (ekaw places it directly under Person, while sigkdd refines it through Speaker > Author).

In cmt, Document is a top-level class whose children are Paper and Review (academic artefacts). In iasted, Form is a subclass of Document representing administrative forms (registration form, hotel registration form, etc.). These denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person representing a role (e.g., author, reviewer), while Conference Event in edas represents an event or activity at the conference with temporal and location properties. They are entirely different concepts.

dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Medicine Topic is a subject area classification for papers/contributions, while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and share no semantic overlap.

In edas, Programme is a schedule/agenda document for a conference event (sibling of Paper, Meal Menu, etc.), whereas in sigkdd, Paper is a scholarly submission document. They are distinct concepts within the conference domain.
Paper is a conference contribution (a document), while Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational committee. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

writePaper (Author -> Paper) is more specific than contributes (Person -> Conference document). Author subsumes/is equivalent to Person in this context, but Paper is a specific kind of Conference document. Thus writePaper is a specialization of contributes, making them related rather than strictly equivalent.
Reviewed contribution is a paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Review Question is a question used within a review form. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are subclasses of Speaker in the conference domain, but a Tutorial speaker specifically gives tutorials while an Invited Speaker is invited to give a talk (often keynote or special session). They overlap as types of speakers but are not equivalent; they represent distinct roles.

Trip is a type of social event involving travel/excursion, while Coctail reception is a specific social gathering with drinks. They are both social conference activities but denote different kinds of events. In confOf, Reception is a sibling of Trip, and in iasted there is no direct Trip equivalent, so they are merely related as social activities.

Both classes represent a member of the Program Committee (PC Member vs Program Committee member). They share the same intended instances in the conference domain: persons who serve on the program committee to review papers and make acceptance decisions.

Both properties are named 'pay', share the same domain (Person), and relate a person to a monetary/fee concept (Money vs Registration fee). In the conference domain, paying money and paying a registration fee denote the same action. The slight difference in range labels (Money vs Registration fee) reflects modeling granularity rather than a conceptual mismatch.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Conference Session in edas is an event/time slot within a conference, while Session chair in iasted is a person (a role of a delegate) who chairs a session. They are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. person).

Sponsor state in iasted is a subclass of State (likely representing the status or condition of a sponsor), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person/Speaker. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a sibling of 'Conference Chair', suggesting it is an Associate/Co-Chair role distinct from the main Conference Chair. In ekaw, 'OC Chair' (Organizing Committee Chair) corresponds to the main conference chair role. They are related as both are chair-level roles in conference organization, but they are not strictly equivalent given the sibling distinction in cmt.
Property A 'reviews' links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while property B 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Conference state' in iasted is a subclass of 'State' (alongside Presenter state, Sponsor state), representing a status or condition related to a conference. 'Conference' in sigkdd represents the actual conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are fundamentally different concepts.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment relation), while has_a_review links a Reviewed contribution to a Review (review document relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference volume to its contained Conference contributions (papers), while property B links a Paper to the Individual Presentation event at which it is presented. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted academic work (paper, poster, etc.), while PersonalHistory in edas represents a person's historical record (publication or review history). These are entirely different concepts.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a full paper submission), while Computer Networks Optical Topic is a subject area/topic within computer networks. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Academic Event in edas is a type of conference event (e.g., paper presentation, workshop), while Academic Institution in ekaw is an organization (e.g., university, research institute). They share the word 'Academic' but denote entirely different concepts.

Social Event in edas refers to non-academic social gatherings (excursions, receptions), while Registration in iasted refers to the act of registering for a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Workshop as part of a conference. In Ontology A it is a Conference part alongside Track and Tutorial; in Ontology B it is a Working event (subclass of Event) alongside Conference and Tutorial. The intended instances coincide.
A Review Form is a document/template used for reviewing papers, while a Time zone is a geographical time reference. These are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's or user's preference (e.g., topic or paper preference), while Person in sigkdd refers to a human individual involved in the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Published Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document), while Best Student Paper Award is a subclass of Award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Contact Information represents address/communication details (city, email, phone, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair is a leadership role (subclass of Chairman) responsible for organizing the conference program, while Conference Hiker is a subclass of Delegate representing an attendee at the conference venue. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

In edas, 'Personal History' is an abstract class representing a person's history (with children Personal Publication History and Personal Review History). In iasted, 'Publication' is a concrete item/artefact (sibling of Document, Audiovisual equipment, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts.

paperDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime deadline, while presentationOfPaper is an object property linking an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Paper is a scholarly document in the conference domain, while Credit card is a payment instrument. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Performance Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while is_paid_by links Money to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Performance Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk is a type of presentation event in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Meal Menu (a document listing food options for a meal event) and Review (an evaluation of a paper) are entirely different concepts in the conference domain, despite both being subclasses of Document.
Entity A is the general class 'Topic', while Entity B is 'Security Topic', a specific subclass of 'Topic' in edas. Therefore A subsumes B.
providedBy links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides the sponsorship), while pay links a Person to a Registration fee (payment). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code), while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Demo Session is a type of scientific event (a session), while Session room is a physical place where sessions are held. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Place) and are not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in cmt, while Academia Organization is a type of organization in edas. They are completely different concepts.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while obtain relates a Person to an Item. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different.

Session Chair and Tutorial Chair are distinct roles in conference organization. A Session Chair moderates paper sessions, while a Tutorial Chair organizes tutorial events. They are siblings under Person/Conference Participant in their respective ontologies, not equivalent concepts.

The property 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'follows' links one Administrative event to another to indicate temporal ordering. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enter Conference Details' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They are unrelated.

Contribution co-author is a type of author who co-authored a conference contribution, while Invited Speaker is a type of speaker invited to present at the conference. These are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.

An IASTED member is a type of delegate (attendee) in the IASTED ontology, while an Organizing Committee member is a type of organizer in the SIGKDD ontology. These are distinct roles: one is a conference participant/attendee and the other is part of the organizing body.
Conference Chair is a person role (the chair of a conference), while Workshop is a type of academic event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Call to the person who initiated it (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member), while Property B links a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (part-whole), while 'hold' relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference it organizes. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself, with properties like date, logo URL, and members. In ontology B, 'Conference announcement' is a subclass of 'Conference document', representing an informational document or announcement about a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the event entity, the other is a document.

Deadline hotel reservation and Deadline Paper Submission are both subclasses of Deadline but refer to entirely different types of deadlines (accommodation vs. paper submission). They are sibling-level concepts with no equivalence or subsumption.

Both properties map an entity to a dateTime representing a start time, but A's domain is the broader 'Conference Event' (any event in a conference) while B's domain is specifically 'Conference'. They overlap semantically but are not equivalent due to differing domain specificity.
Publisher is an entity that issues conference proceedings, while Money represents financial amounts (fees, taxes, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Reviewed contribution is a conference paper that has been reviewed, while Money is a financial concept with children like Fee and Tax. They are entirely unrelated.
Paper Full Version is a type of academic document (a complete paper), while Full day tour is a post-conference social activity. They share only the word 'Full' and are completely unrelated concepts.
