Both are datatype properties mapping a deadline/important-dates concept to a date value representing when something ends or is due. 'is an ending date' (domain: Important dates) and 'done till' (domain: Deadline) serve the same semantic role in the conference domain.

The property 'expert On' relates a PC member to a topic (indicating expertise), while 'submit' relates an author to a paper (indicating submission). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (email address), while is_sent_by is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a type of conference attendee), while Fee for extra trip is a subclass of Money/Fee (a monetary charge). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and are unrelated.

Activity after conference is a temporal activity/event occurring after the conference, while Main office is a physical place/location. They belong to entirely different categories (Activity vs Place) and are unrelated.
'organised By' links an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'go through' links an Item to an Activity it undergoes. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'Information for participants' in Conference ontology refers to documents providing information to attendees (e.g., calls, announcements), while 'Form' in iasted refers to fillable forms (registration, hotel, author info). They are both document types but serve different purposes; they overlap loosely as conference-related documents but are not equivalent.
Property A links a Conference volume to Important dates, while property B links an Author to a Contribution. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A 'issues' links a Publisher to Conference proceedings (a specific publishing relationship), while property B 'relatesTo' is a generic relation from Document to events or persons. Their domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In Ontology A, 'Invited talk' is a type of conference contribution/document (a presentation artefact), whereas in Ontology B, 'Invited Speaker' is a type of Person/Presenter (the individual giving the talk). They represent fundamentally different concepts (an event/artefact vs. a person) and are therefore unrelated.

set Max Papers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while submit until relates a Document to a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

adjustBid relates a Reviewer to a Bid (reviewer preference for papers), while payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (who paid the fee). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Conference days' in iasted is a subclass of Time representing the temporal duration/days of a conference, whereas 'Conference' in sigkdd represents the conference event itself (with properties like name, city, start/end dates). They are conceptually distinct: one is a time period, the other is an event.

belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event (indicating which event a programme belongs to), while hold links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (indicating who organizes/holds the conference). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has the last name' is a datatype property for a Person's surname, while 'ends on' is a datatype property for an Event's end date. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

Accepted Paper is a class representing a paper that has been accepted for presentation, while Deadline Author notification is a class representing the deadline by which authors are notified of acceptance/rejection. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasPostalCode refers to a postal/zip code for an organization or person, while hasLastName refers to a person's family name. These are entirely different concepts.

Author is a subclass of Person (a human role), while Document is a class for written artefacts (papers, reviews, etc.). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are unrelated.
paper ID is a datatype property assigning an unsignedLong identifier to a Paper, while has amount of assigns an int value to Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In EKAW, SC Member (Steering Committee Member) is a subclass of PC Member, representing a senior role in the scientific/program committee organization. In IASTED, 'IASTED member' is a subclass of Delegate (attendee), indicating membership in the IASTED organization rather than a conference steering or program committee role. These are conceptually distinct.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors—anyone who contributes to the conference. Worker lecturer (B) is a very specific subclass deep in the iasted hierarchy (Delegate > Speaker > Author > Lecturer > Worker lecturer). While a worker lecturer could be considered a type of conference contributor, B is far more specific than A, so they are related but not equivalent; A subsumes B.

'is Initiated By' links a Call to conference chairs or TPC members who initiated it, while 'is writen by' links an Item (e.g., a paper) to its author. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a Person in the conference domain. They share similar children (Author, various chair/committee roles, attendees/participants) and overlapping properties (has Email, has First Name). Despite minor differences in child class naming, their intended instances coincide.

In cmt, 'Paper Abstract' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing only the abstract portion of a paper. In confOf, 'Paper' represents the full paper contribution (with siblings Poster and Short paper). Thus, cmt's Paper Abstract is strictly more specific than confOf's Paper, making it subsumed_by.

The 'name' property in cmt denotes the name of a Conference or Person (a string identifier), while 'City of conference' in sigkdd denotes the city where the conference is held. These are semantically distinct properties with different meanings.

Free Time Break is a type of break event (non-academic) during a conference, while Conference Trip is a social event involving travel/excursion. They are distinct types of non-academic/social events with different intended instances.
Property A links Important dates to a Conference volume, while Property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Registation deadline refers to the deadline for attendee registration, while Deadline Paper Submission refers to the deadline for submitting papers. These are distinct types of deadlines in the conference domain.
hasCity is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a city string, while Name links a Person to their name string. They have different domains and represent entirely different concepts.

Participant in confOf is a subclass of Person representing someone attending the conference, while Research in iasted is a subclass of Activity (specifically an activity before the conference). They are entirely different concepts.

The 'email' property represents a person's email address, while the 'Nation' property represents a person's nationality or country. Although both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, they capture entirely different attributes.

'writes' is a specific authorship relation (Author -> Contribution), while 'hasPart' is a generic mereological part-whole relation with unspecified domain and range. They denote entirely different concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Modelling is a research activity performed before the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract (a document part), while property B links a paper/abstract to the presentation format it was delivered as (e.g., Individual Presentation). These relate entirely different concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (paper submission), while is_paid_in relates Money to a Building (payment location). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains (Document vs Academic Institution) and semantics ('relatesTo' is a general relation from documents to events/persons, while 'scientificallyOrganises' describes an institution organizing something scientifically). They are unrelated.

has the first name is a datatype property for a person's given name (domain: Person), while has Street is a datatype property for a street address (domain: Contact Information). They describe entirely different attributes of different entities.

organisedBy relates an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Computer Networks Topic is a subject area classification for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Chair' is a general class for committee chairs (with 'Co chair' as a sibling), while in Ontology B, 'General Chair' is a specific role listed alongside 'Program Chair'. Thus, the general 'Chair' class in A subsumes the more specific 'General Chair' in B.

Scholar is a subclass of Person representing an academic individual (with a comment about price category), while Sponzor fee is a subclass of Fee representing a monetary charge. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

confOf:Topic is a general class for any conference topic, while edas:Performance Topic is a specific subclass of edas:Topic (a particular subject area). Thus confOf:Topic subsumes edas:Performance Topic.

The property 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who finalizes paper assignments, while 'write' links a Person to an Item they author. These describe entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Person in Conference is a general class for all people involved in the conference. Student in ekaw is a subclass of Person (path: Person > Student), representing specifically students. Therefore, Conference:Person subsumes ekaw:Student.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while speak_in relates a Person to a Place and Time for speaking. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

University is an academic institution (a type of Organization), while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organization in edas represents institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorships, while Person in sigkdd represents individual human participants (listeners, speakers, organizers). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Event in confOf refers to scheduled conference occurrences (administrative, social, working events) with start/end times. Item in iasted refers to physical or informational objects (equipment, documents, vehicles). These are entirely different concepts.
Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (Document), while Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In ekaw, Student is a direct subclass of Person representing a student participant. In iasted, Worker lecturer is a deeply nested subclass (under Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate) representing a working lecturer. These are distinct roles with no intended overlap in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used to announce information, while Computer Networks Switching Topic is a specific research topic within computer networks. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference Chair is a specific leadership role in organizing the conference, while Early Registered Participant refers to an attendee who registered early. These are entirely different concepts with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

Both classes serve as top-level document abstractions in their respective ontologies and share 'Review' as a child. However, cmt:Document is narrowly scoped to Paper and Review (artefacts of the review process), while Conference:Conference_document is much broader, encompassing calls for papers/participation, announcements, web pages, and contributions. Their intended instance sets overlap but do not coincide, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Science Worker in confOf is a broad class for anyone working in science (parent of Author, Scholar, PC members, etc.), whereas Student in ekaw is a specific role for students. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other; they are largely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a Presentation to the Active conference participant who gives it, while Property B links a Conference to its member Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Presentation is a type of conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to a starting date value, while Property B is an object property linking an event to a location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has parts' relates a conference volume to its constituent parts (e.g., papers, proceedings), while 'has Location' relates a conference event to a physical place. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator (who entered details), while has_tracks links a Conference volume to its Tracks. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Trip in confOf is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Sponsor city in iasted is a type of City (a geographical location). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
Social program is a type of conference activity (event), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. They are completely different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a person role (subclass of Person) involved in a conference, while Conference Session in edas is an event or time slot within a conference. They denote entirely different concepts.

A Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity/event (a lecture), while an Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation event, while Property B links a Speaker to a Document. They have completely different domains and ranges and model different relationships in the conference domain.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (review assignment context), while Property B links a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (visit context). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Multimedia Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (individuals), while property B links a Committee (a group) to a Conference volume. They have different domains, ranges, and directions of membership/affiliation, so they are not equivalent.

Review Rating in edas is a rating/score assigned to a paper (with children like Accept Rating, Reject Rating), while Negative Review in ekaw is a type of review document classified by sentiment. They are conceptually different: one is a rating value, the other is a review artifact. They are related because negative reviews typically correspond to reject ratings, but they are not equivalent.

A 'Rejected contribution' is a paper that was reviewed and declined, whereas a 'Withdrawn Paper' is one removed by the author before or during review. These are distinct outcomes in the conference domain. Ontology B (edas) even has a separate sibling 'Rejected Paper' which would be the true equivalent of A.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Cryptography Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while is_connected_with is an object property linking Activities/Persons to Items/Places. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.
City is a geographical location class, while Conference is an event class. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Communication Theory Topic is a subject area for conference papers, while Transport vehicle is a physical conveyance (car, taxi, etc.). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In iasted, 'Memeber registration fee' is a subclass of 'Registration fee', while in sigkdd, 'Registration fee' is the parent class with children like 'Registration SIGKDD Member'. Thus, the iasted class is more specific and is subsumed by the sigkdd class.

In Ontology A, Poster is a specific type of Conference contribution (a sibling of Presentation and Written contribution), typically referring to a poster presentation at a conference. In Ontology B (sigkdd), Paper is a general Document submitted by an Author, representing a full research paper. These are distinct types of conference artefacts; a poster is not equivalent to a paper, though both are contributions/documents in the broader conference domain.

Attendee is a subclass of Person representing someone who attends a conference, while Student registration fee is a subclass of Money/Fee representing a monetary charge. These are entirely different concepts.

In edas, Review is a subclass of Document. In iasted, Document is a superclass that has Review as one of its children. Therefore, edas:Review is subsumed by iasted:Document (iasted:Document is more general).
Trip in confOf is a social event (an excursion), while Trip city in iasted is a type of City (a location). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Both properties represent a submission deadline date, but A is specifically for full paper submissions (domain: Important dates) while B is a general submission deadline (domain: Call). They overlap in meaning but differ in specificity and domain context, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Conference announcement is a type of conference document, while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Document), ranges (Conference vs multiple types including Academic Event, Person), and semantics (entering conference details vs a generic 'relates to' association). They are unrelated.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for anyone participating in a conference, with children Active and Passive participants. Speaker (B) is a specific type of Delegate who presents, which is a narrower concept. Thus Conference participant subsumes Speaker.

In Ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' representing the conference website/URL (it has property 'has a URL'). In Ontology B, 'Conference' is a type of working event (subclass of Event). These are entirely different concepts: one is a web resource/document, the other is an event.

In cmt, 'Conference Member' is a general class for anyone involved in the conference (authors, reviewers, chairs, PC members). In iasted, 'IASTED member' is a specific subclass of 'Delegate' representing someone who holds membership in the IASTED organization, distinct from 'IASTED non member'. These are conceptually different: one is a broad conference role, the other is an organizational membership status.

Property A links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (indicating who read the paper), while Property B links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (indicating who wrote the review). They have different domains (Paper vs Review), different ranges (Meta Reviewer vs Possible Reviewer), and different semantics (reading vs writing).

Conference in confOf is a type of Event (a working event like a tutorial or workshop), whereas Conference Participant in ekaw is a type of Person who attends the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers to a staff member of an agency (e.g., organizing or sponsoring body), while Author of paper student in sigkdd refers to a student who authored a paper. These are entirely different roles with no semantic overlap.

Conference Member in cmt is a Person (participant role such as author, reviewer, chair), while Conference volume in the Conference ontology is a subclass of Conference representing the proceedings or event instance itself. They are entirely different concepts.
Member PC is a person (reviewer) in confOf, while Reject Rating is a type of review rating in edas. They are completely different concepts.
Invited speaker is a type of person (conference contributor), while Conference is a type of event. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, Track is a structural part of a conference (like a thematic track), sibling to Tutorial and Workshop under 'Conference part'. In Ontology B, Paper Presentation is an academic event where a specific accepted paper is presented. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an organizational/thematic subdivision, the other is a presentation activity.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is occupied by' relates a Building/City/State to a Person (physical occupation). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.
Administrator in confOf is a person who manages the conference system (confTool), while Author in iasted is a speaker who authored a paper. These are entirely different roles with no overlap.

Property A links a 'Review expertise' to a 'Submitted contribution', while property B links a 'Paper' to a 'Possible Reviewer'. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantic meanings in the conference domain.
Invited speaker is a type of conference contributor who presents, while Administrator is an organizational/management role. They represent entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

Both properties link a paper-like document to an author-like person, but 'has Co author' specifically targets co-authors (a subclass of authors) while 'has authors' targets all authors. They are related but not equivalent due to the difference in specificity of both domain and range.
Organization represents an institution (company, university) while Money represents financial amounts (fees, sponsorship). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while design relates ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used for announcements, while Computer Networks Enterprise Topic is a specific research topic within computer networks. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Tutorial Chair is a person role (a conference participant), while Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

A passive conference participant is someone who attends without actively presenting (e.g., a listener), while a sponsor is an entity or person providing financial support for the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

In the conference domain, 'Scholar' in confOf (with comment 'price category - scholar' and property 'study At -> University') refers to a student/academic attendee eligible for a reduced registration rate. This aligns with 'Student' in ekaw, which is also a subclass of Person representing students attending the conference. Both denote the same concept of a student participant.

A 'Registeered applicant' is a person who has registered to attend or apply to the conference (child of Conference applicant), while an 'Author' in sigkdd is a Speaker who submits papers and receives notifications. These are distinct roles: one is about registration/application, the other about authoring and presenting papers.

Paper Abstract in cmt denotes a specific version/format of a paper (the abstract text), as evidenced by its sibling Paper Full Version. Pending Paper in edas denotes a status of a paper in the review workflow (not yet decided). These are orthogonal dimensions (format vs. status) and do not share intended instances.
Property A links a conference document to its authors (Person), while property B links an Author to an Award they obtain. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop Chair and Session chair are distinct roles in conference organization. A Workshop Chair oversees an entire workshop event, while a Session Chair manages a specific session within a conference or workshop. They are siblings in ekaw (both under Conference Participant), confirming they are different concepts.
Van is a transport vehicle (a type of item), while Listener is a person who attends and listens at a conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while need relates a Person to an Item (requirement). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to a Paper or Abstract. These properties relate entirely different domain and range classes and express different relationships.

In ekaw, Workshop Session and Conference Session are sibling subclasses of Session, meaning they are distinct types of sessions. The edas Conference Session is a general session class, but it is not equivalent to the more specific Workshop Session in ekaw. They are related as both represent types of conference sessions.

Both classes represent the role of a session chair at a conference. However, in ekaw 'Session Chair' is a subclass of both Conference Participant and PC Member (implying program committee membership), while in iasted 'Session chair' is a subclass of Delegate (attendee) and sibling to 'Technical commitee'. The differing parent constraints (PC member vs general delegate) mean they are not strictly equivalent but overlap in intended instances.

Property A is a datatype property linking 'Review expertise' to an unspecified range (likely a skill level), while Property B is an object property linking a 'Reviewer' to their 'Personal Review History'. They have different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (e.g., instructions or materials given to attendees), while 'Modelling' is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference. In iasted, Session is a sub-type of Lecture within a conference activity, representing a single session/lecture slot. These are at very different granularities and denote distinct concepts.

Company (a for-profit business organization) and NGO (a non-governmental, typically non-profit organization) are distinct sibling types of Organization in their respective ontologies. They do not denote the same concept.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Performance Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

'has a name' is a datatype property for naming entities (range string), while 'start Date' is a datatype property for the start date/time of a conference (range dateTime). They represent entirely different concepts.
Both are datatype properties linking a Person (or Contact Information associated with a Person) to a string representing an email address. They denote the same relation in the conference domain.

Property A captures a person's first name (domain: Person), while property B captures an abstract of a contribution (domain: Contribution). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

In edas, Document is a broad class with children like Paper, Review, Programme, etc. In iasted, Payment document is a specific subclass of Document (with children Bank transfer and Cheque). Therefore, the edas Document class subsumes the iasted Payment document class.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted manuscript (with authors, reviewers, decisions, bids) in the conference review process. In iasted, Publication is a published output (Book proceeding, Cd proceeding) under Item, sibling to equipment and vehicles. These denote fundamentally different concepts: a submission vs. a published proceedings volume.

Decision in cmt represents an outcome (Acceptance/Rejection) for a paper, while Person in iasted represents a human individual (Delegate/Sponsor). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

In ontology A, 'Review' is a subclass of 'Conference document' and represents the actual review content written for a contribution (linked via 'reviews' to 'Reviewed contribution'). In ontology B (edas), 'Review Form' typically denotes the template or form used to structure a review, not the completed review itself (which edas models as a separate 'Review' class). Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Reviewing event is an administrative event for reviewing submitted contributions, while Workshop is an academic event (a type of session at a conference). They belong to different branches of the event hierarchy and denote entirely different concepts.

Property A links a conference volume to its program committee, while property B links a person to a physical location (building, city, state). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Paper is a general class for all papers (a type of Contribution), while edas:RejectedPaper is a specific subclass of Paper representing only those that have been rejected. Therefore, confOf:Paper subsumes edas:RejectedPaper.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where attendees stay, while Conference Trip is a social event/activity (subclass of Social Event). They belong to fundamentally different categories (place vs. event) and are not equivalent.

Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review (domain: Reviewed contribution, range: Review), while property B links a person/role to a paper they are reviewing (domain: Conference Chair/Reviewer/etc., range: Paper). The domains, ranges, and directions are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (someone applying to a conference), while Accommodation Place is a subclass of Place (a location for lodging). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named 'Review', share the same parent class 'Document', and exist in the conference domain. In both ontologies they represent a review document associated with papers, making them equivalent concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of chairman), while Conference hotel is a physical place/building. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasCo-author links a Paper to its Co-author (Paper -> Author), while writes links an Author to a Contribution (Author -> Paper). They connect the same kinds of entities but in opposite directions; since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are merely related.

A Reviewer and a Session Chair are distinct conference roles. In edas, both Reviewer and Session Chair exist as separate sibling classes under Person. While edas shows that Session Chairs can also review papers (isReviewedBy/isReviewing), the primary intended instances of these two classes differ: one is for reviewing submissions, the other for chairing sessions. They overlap but are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Conference Dinner is a social event (a meal). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Chairman in cmt is a leadership role (with children like Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair), while Author in iasted is someone who writes papers/proceedings. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.
'part Of' is a mereological/parthood relation with unspecified domain and range, while 'give' is an action property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. They express entirely different semantics.

Property A (has authors) has domain Conference document and range Person, while property B (authorOf) has domain Person and range Document. They are inverses of each other, not equivalent. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

An 'Invited talk' is a type of conference contribution/presentation given by an invited speaker, whereas 'Introduction of speaker' is the act of introducing a speaker before their talk. These are distinct activities in a conference program.

Both classes are named 'Review' and share the same parent class 'Document' in their respective ontologies. In the conference domain, both represent a review document (e.g., of a paper submission), so their intended instances coincide.

hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.
isTopicOf relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference part to a Conference volume (mereological relation), while Property B links a Person to an Item (signing/authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has contributions' links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions, while 'written By' links a Contribution to an Author. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
The properties have completely different domains (Contribution vs Sponsorship), ranges (string vs int), and semantics (a remark/note vs a cost amount). They are unrelated.
Company in confOf is a type of Organization (business entity), while Main office in iasted is a type of Place (physical location). They belong to fundamentally different categories and are unrelated.

In cmt, Conference is a specific type of academic gathering with properties like accepting submissions and having members. In ekaw, Event is a very general class (parent of Scientific Event and Social Event) representing any happening at or around a conference. A Conference in cmt would more likely correspond to 'Conference' in ekaw (if it exists) or be a kind of event, but the broad 'Event' class in ekaw is not equivalent to the specific 'Conference' class in cmt.

A Registration form is a document used to collect registration information, while a Registration fee is a monetary charge for registering. They are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. fee) and are unrelated.

Multimedia Topic is a subject area for conference papers (a subclass of Topic), while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a subclass of Item). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (preparation/authoring). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.
locationOf relates a Location to an Event, while is_present relates a Person to a Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'was a member of' relates a Committee member to a Committee, while 'hold' relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ontology A, Sponzorship and Fee are siblings under Money, meaning they are distinct concepts. In ontology B, Fee is a broader class that includes 'Sponzor fee' as a child. Sponsorship (A) overlaps with the sponsorship-fee aspect of Fee (B), but they are not equivalent since Fee in B also covers registration fees and Fee in A is a separate sibling concept.
Property A links a Topic to a Conference part, while Property B links a Speaker to a Document. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different.

Review Question in edas refers to a question used during the review process (with numerical/textual subtypes), while Submission in iasted refers to a submitted manuscript/document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains (Administrator vs Publisher), ranges (Conference vs Conference proceedings), and semantics (entering conference details vs issuing proceedings). They are unrelated.

'acceptedBy' relates a Paper to an Administrator (acceptance relation), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'virtualMeetingEnabledBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while 'hold' links the ACM SIGKDD organization to a Conference it organizes. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.
Reviewed contribution (A) is a paper/submission that has been reviewed, while Review (B) is the review document itself. They are related via the review relationship but are distinct concepts.

Multi-author Volume in ekaw is a collection of documents (parent of Proceedings), while Abstract in sigkdd is a summary document. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while Property B links a Presentation to an Active conference participant who gives it. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper in confOf is a type of Contribution (a document/artefact), while Paper Author in ekaw is a type of Person who writes papers. These are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. person) and are unrelated.

In cmt, Document is a superclass of both Paper and Review, making it a general document artefact. In confOf, Contribution is a superclass of Paper, Poster, and Short paper—i.e., submitted scholarly works only (no reviews). Thus cmt:Document is strictly more general than confOf:Contribution, so it subsumes it.

Workshop is a type of scientific event (a gathering/session), while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Industrial Session is a type of conference event/session, while Hotel is a type of place/venue. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an academic gathering), while Conference restaurant in iasted is a type of building/place where meals are served. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A captures a person's last name (domain: Person), while property B captures a keyword of a contribution/paper (domain: Contribution). They describe entirely different concepts and relate different domains.

confOf:Member is a general class for regular conference members (siblings: Regular, Student), while ekaw:Early-Registered_Participant specifically denotes participants who registered early. They overlap in the sense that an early-registered participant could be a member, but they are not equivalent; Early-Registered_Participant is more specific regarding registration timing, and Member is more general.

confOf:Participant is a general class for anyone participating in the conference (with children Member, Regular, Student), while edas:TPC Member specifically denotes a Technical Program Committee member who reviews papers. Participant subsumes TPC Member since a TPC member is a type of participant, but they are not equivalent.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference registrant who paid late), while Cheque is a subclass of Payment document (a financial instrument). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment for review), while hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper (authorship/association). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
In iasted, 'Registration fee' is a subclass of 'Fee', while in sigkdd, 'Fee' is the parent class with 'Registration fee' as a child. Thus, iasted's Registration fee is subsumed by sigkdd's Fee.

paperID is a datatype property linking a Paper to its numeric identifier (unsignedLong), while isWrittenBy is an object property linking a Paper to its Author. They represent entirely different relations.

In edas, 'Accommodation Place' is a subclass of 'Place', specifically denoting lodging. In iasted, 'Place' is a general class whose children include 'Hotel room', 'Building', 'Conference hall', etc. Thus, the edas 'Accommodation Place' is strictly more specific than (subsumed by) the iasted 'Place'.
Property A relates a Person to a Time (attendance/presence), while property B relates an Author to a Paper (submission). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (co-writePaper) has domain Co-author and range Paper, meaning it points from an author to a paper. Property B (isWrittenBy) has domain Paper and range Author, meaning it points from a paper to an author. These are inverse directions of each other, not equivalent properties.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper), representing the act of reviewing a paper. Property B (hasRating) links an Active Paper to a Review Rating, representing the score/rating assigned to a paper. They have different domains, different ranges, and express fundamentally different relationships in the conference domain.
Entity A is a type of conference document (an extended abstract), while Entity B is a deadline for paper submission. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Computer Networks Topic' is a research topic area for papers (subclass of Topic). In iasted, 'Computer' is a piece of audiovisual equipment (subclass of Audiovisual equipment). They are entirely different concepts.
Paper Full Version is a complete version of a submitted paper, while Flyer is a promotional document. They are distinct types of documents with different purposes in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'has workshops' links a Conference volume to a Workshop, while 'expert On' links a Member PC to a Topic. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

In ontology B (confOf), Company is a subclass of Organization (with sibling University), meaning it represents a specific type of organization. In ontology A (Conference), Organization is the general class. Therefore, A's Organization subsumes B's Company.

In cmt, User is a general class for system users (Author, Reviewer, Administrator) under Person. In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is a specific role under Organizator (organizer). These represent different concepts: one is a broad user category including paper submitters and reviewers, the other is specifically an organizing committee role. They are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other in a meaningful way.

Entity A is 'Review' (a review document) while Entity B is 'Paper' (a submitted paper). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; in fact, ekaw's own ontology lists Review as a sibling of Paper and connects them via hasReview/reviewOfPaper properties.

Property A links a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while property B links a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsorship provision). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

scientificallyOrganises relates an Academic Institution to something it organizes scientifically, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasSurname specifically denotes a person's family/last name, while Name is more general and could refer to a full name or given name. They are related but not strictly equivalent.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for a person who studies at a university (a student), with Author as a sibling class. In iasted, Author is someone who has written a paper/presentation (child of Speaker). These are conceptually distinct roles in the conference domain.

The two properties relate entirely different concepts: 'is part of conference volumes' links a Conference part to a Conference volume, while 'is Menu Of' links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event. They share no semantic overlap in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

'heldIn' relates an Event to a Location (spatial/venue), while 'holded_by' relates a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). They express fundamentally different relations (location vs organizer) and are not equivalent.

readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read/review, while write relates a Person to an Item they author. These are fundamentally different actions (reading vs writing) with different domain/range semantics.
Chair PC in confOf is a person role (Program Committee Chair), while Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference event. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Property A links review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
forEvent links a Call to an Academic Event, while need links a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Research is an activity (a type of work done before a conference), while Speaker is a person role. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Computer Networks Sensor Topic is a research topic classification in edas, while Workshop is a type of scientific event in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to the Reviewer who authored it. Property B (belongs_to_reviewers) links Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer. The domains are entirely different (Review vs. Review expertise/preference), so these properties relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a general class for anyone participating in the conference (chairs, authors, reviewers, registered participants). Conference Hiker in iasted is a specific subclass of Delegate, representing a particular type of attendee. Thus, Conference Participant subsumes Conference Hiker.

Activity in iasted refers to events or tasks (e.g., conference activities) with properties like 'is held in' and 'is given by', while Deadline in sigkdd refers to temporal cutoff dates for submissions or notifications. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while property B links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'name' property captures a person's or conference's name (a string), while 'has an email' captures an email address. These are semantically distinct properties relating different kinds of information, even though both have Person in their domain and string as range.

Attendee is a subclass of Person representing someone who attends a conference, while Nonmember registration fee is a subclass of Money/Fee representing a monetary charge. These are entirely different concepts.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation that publishes proceedings, while Receiving manuscript is an Activity before conference involving the receipt of manuscripts. They are entirely different concepts.
Paper is a scholarly contribution (submission), while Mailing list is a document used for communication purposes. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur simultaneously, while 'presentation' relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Member is a general participant role (with siblings Regular and Student), while iasted:Student non speaker is a very specific subclass of delegate who is both a student and not speaking. Member subsumes Student non speaker in scope but they are not equivalent; they overlap as both can represent student participants.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a sibling of 'Paper' and 'Poster' under 'Contribution', denoting a specific short-length submission type. In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a broad category under 'Paper' with siblings like 'Regular Paper', 'Demo Paper', 'Poster Paper', etc. A short paper could be presented at a conference, but the two classes are not equivalent: one denotes length/format (short), the other denotes venue context (conference). They overlap but neither subsumes the other cleanly.

Property A links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (publishing relation), while Property B links an Author to a Contribution (authorship/writing relation). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

hasCity relates organizations or persons to a city (location), while hasMember relates a conference to a person (membership). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'reviewer Of Paper' relates a Possible Reviewer to a Paper. These are entirely different relations with different domains and semantics.

Conference Chair is a leadership role responsible for organizing the conference, while Late paid applicant is a registrant who paid their fees late. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher, while 'write' links a Person to an Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics (publishing vs authoring), so they are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference Proceedings is a document (a multi-author volume). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Bid in cmt represents a reviewer's bid on a paper, while ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd represents the organization/conference entity. These are completely unrelated concepts.
writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while is_paid_in relates Money to a Building (payment location). These are entirely different relations with no semantic overlap.

Entity A is a class representing a person who actively participates in a conference (e.g., gives presentations), while Entity B is a class representing the presentation event itself. They belong to entirely different categories (Person vs Event) and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

earlyRegistration is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating whether they registered early, while done_till is a date datatype property on Deadline indicating when the deadline occurs. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a person who registered and paid for the conference early. 'Early paid applicant' in Conference ontology and 'Early Registered Participant' in ekaw ontology denote the same concept: an attendee who completed early registration/payment. The sibling 'Late paid applicant' vs 'Late Registered Participant' further confirms this alignment.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (likely a registration or form). These denote different relations in the conference domain.

hasCo-author relates a Paper to its Co-author (a person), while hasRelatedPaper relates an Author to a Paper. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Conference Chair is the person who chairs/organizes the conference, while Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (assignment relation), while writes links an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Author in confOf represents a person who writes contributions (papers), while Possible Reviewer in ekaw represents a person who may review papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain. The equivalent of Author in ekaw would be Paper Author, not Possible Reviewer.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country, while speak_in links a Person to a Place and Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

An Organizational Meeting is an administrative/organizational event within a conference, while a Plenary lecture is a specific type of academic presentation given to all attendees. They serve entirely different purposes and have different positions in their respective hierarchies.

Both properties express an end date/time, but confOf's 'ends on' applies to any Event (domain: Event) while edas's 'endDate' applies specifically to Conference (domain: Conference). Since Conference is a kind of Event in most conference ontologies, the edas property is more specific in domain. They are related but not strictly equivalent.

Property A links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part (role/organizational relation), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a person participating in a conference. They share the same parent (Person) and have overlapping children representing various conference roles (chairs, committee members, authors/presenters). In the OAEI Conference track reference alignment, Conference Member (cmt) and Conference Participant (ekaw) are considered equivalent.

Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Invitation letter is an administrative document used to invite someone (e.g., for visa purposes). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

isWrittenBy relates a Paper to its Author, while updatedVersionOf relates a Document to a previous version of that Document. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has a publisher' links conference proceedings to a Publisher entity, while 'relates To' is a generic property linking Documents to events, conferences, sessions, or persons. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Registration of participants event is an administrative event for registering attendees, while Organizational Meeting is an academic/organizational meeting event (e.g., committee meeting). They are distinct types of events with different purposes and contexts.

Property A 'name' is a general name property (domain includes Conference and Person), while property B 'has the first name' specifically denotes a person's first name. A full name subsumes a first name, so A is more general than B.
Volunteer is a person role (someone who volunteers), while Two Level Conference is a type of conference event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Meeting Room Place' is a room where meetings or sessions are held, while a 'Main office' is an administrative office space. Although both are subclasses of Place, they denote entirely different types of locations within the conference domain.

'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details (a data-entry action), while 'organisedBy' links an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. The domains, ranges, and semantics differ significantly.

enableVirtualMeeting links an Administrator to a Conference to enable virtual meetings, while hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person who attends it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers), while Property B relates a PersonalReviewHistory to a Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Coctail reception is a social event/activity at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

has_a_URL is a datatype property on Conference www pointing to a URL string, while hasEmail is a datatype property on Person pointing to an email string. They have different domains and represent different contact information types.
A is a research topic (Computer Networks Management) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of Author representing any co-author of a paper (with properties co-write Paper and has Co-author). In sigkdd, 'Author of paper' is also a subclass of Author but represents the primary author of a paper (distinguished from its sibling 'Author of paper student'). While both are types of authors, they capture different roles: one emphasizes co-authorship, the other emphasizes being the main author of a paper. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while expertOn relates a PC Member to a Topic (indicating expertise). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in edas represents the conference event/organization itself, while Conference city in iasted is a subclass of City representing the location where a conference takes place. These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. geographic location).
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while is_paid_by relates Money to a Person who pays it. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Computer Architecture Topic is a research topic classification in edas, while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment in iasted. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasVAT is a datatype property for value added tax on events, while Name is a datatype property for the name of a person. They have different domains, ranges (both string but semantically different), and meanings.

maxPapers is a datatype property linking a Program Committee Member to an integer (maximum number of papers), while topicCoveredBy is an object property linking a Research Topic to Events or Papers. They are entirely different in domain, range, type, and semantics.

In Ontology A, Paper is a subclass of Regular contribution (a full research paper), while in Ontology B, Demo Paper is a specific type of paper used for demonstrations. These are distinct kinds of conference contributions that overlap only at the general 'contribution/document' level but are not equivalent nor in a direct subsumption relationship.

confOf:Trip is a specific kind of social event (a trip/excursion), while ekaw:Social_Event is the general class for all social events. ekaw even has 'Conference Trip' as a child of Social_Event, confirming that Trip is subsumed by Social Event.

Submitted Paper is a paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Transparency refers to overhead transparencies (presentation slides). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasCity in edas is a datatype property on Contact Information (giving the city of a contact address), while City_of_conference in sigkdd is a datatype property on Conference (giving the city where the conference is held). Different domains and different intended meanings.

confOf's 'Administrative event' is a broad class that includes 'Registration of participants event' as one of its children (alongside Camera Ready event, Reviewing event, Submission event, etc.). iasted's 'Registration' corresponds specifically to the registration aspect. Therefore, Administrative event subsumes Registration.

In confOf, 'Conference' is a type of Event (a working event alongside Tutorial and Workshop). In iasted, 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time (alongside Deadline and Trip day), representing temporal duration rather than the event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Both properties express an agentive 'created/organized by' relationship (A: Call initiated by chairs/TPC members; B: Item prepared by a Person). However, their domains differ significantly (Call vs. Item) and the specific semantics of 'initiating a call for papers' versus 'preparing an item' are not identical. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

'has the first name' is a datatype property for a person's given name (domain: Person), while 'has VAT' refers to value added tax for events (domain: Social event, Working event). They are completely unrelated concepts.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while coversTopic relates a Paper or Event to a Research Topic (subject matter). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'is Menu Of' links a meal menu to a meal event. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Dinner banquet is a social event/activity at a conference, while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) responsible for chairing activities, while Administrative event is a type of event (subclass of Event) such as submission or reviewing. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote fundamentally different concepts.

Property A ('is the 1th part of') relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation as a structural part-of relation. Property B ('is Topic Of') relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper as a subject-matter relation. These are semantically distinct relations with different domains and meanings.

The property 'follows' relates administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while 'obtain' relates a person to an item (acquisition). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.) with properties like abstract, title, and author. ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd represents the organizing body/society that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'One day presenter' is a specific type of delegate who presents for one day, while an 'Organizator' is a person involved in organizing the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). These are distinct roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Signal Processing Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Both classes are named Document and serve as the parent class for conference-related written artefacts such as Paper, Review, and Programme/Programme Brochure. Their children overlap significantly in the conference domain, indicating they represent the same concept.

writePaper denotes authorship (an Author writes a Paper), while hasRelatedPaper is a broader association that may include co-authorship or other relationships. They share domain and range but differ in semantics; hasRelatedPaper subsumes writePaper.

Property A (memberOfProgramCommittee) links a Program Committee Member to a Program Committee, while property B (hasMember) links a Conference to a Person. They have different domains, different ranges, and opposite directions (A is 'member of', B is 'has member'). They are not equivalent nor inverses of each other in this context.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while hasCountry relates a Conference to a Country. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference is an event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Author of paper is a type of person (a subclass of Author). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent fundamentally different concepts.
Property A gives the last name of a Person, while property B gives the name of a Sponsor (Sponzor). They have different domains and different semantic meanings.

Student in confOf is a subtype of Participant (a person attending the conference who is a student). Attendee in edas is the general class for anyone attending the conference. Every Student participant is an Attendee, but not every Attendee is a Student, so Student is subsumed by Attendee.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an organized gathering), while Author in iasted is a person who writes papers (a subclass of Speaker/Delegate). These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties describe entirely different concepts: 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of paper assignment, while 'presentation Of Paper' relates an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. They share no semantic overlap.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string, representing the surname/last name of a person. 'has the last name' and 'has Surname' are synonymous in this context.

has_short_title is a datatype property linking events to a string (short title), while hasEvent is an object property linking an Event to another Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a document/submission class, while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They are entirely unrelated.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants), while Organizing Committee member in Ontology B refers to people involved in organizing the conference. These are distinct roles with different intended instances.

Author in edas represents a person who writes papers, while Possible Reviewer in ekaw represents a person who may review papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain. The equivalent of Author in ekaw would be Paper Author, and the equivalent of Possible Reviewer in edas would be Reviewer or TPC Member.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing relation), while 'is Topic Of' relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper (subject-matter relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is specifically the deadline for full paper submissions, while property B is a generic 'done till' date for any kind of deadline. They share the same datatype structure (domain is a dates/deadline class, range is date) but differ in specificity; A is more specific than B, so they are related rather than equivalent.
Publisher is an entity that issues conference proceedings, while Time represents temporal concepts like deadlines and conference days. They are completely unrelated.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class under Person that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author. Presenter (B) in ekaw is a subclass of Conference Participant with only Invited Speaker as a child. A regular author who contributes a paper but does not present would be a Conference contributor but not a Presenter. Thus Conference contributor subsumes Presenter.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a specific role that is a subclass of Program Committee Member and Chairman. In confOf, 'Member PC' represents a general program committee member/reviewer, while 'Chair PC' is listed as a sibling representing the chair role. Therefore, Program Committee Chair is more specific than Member PC and is subsumed by it.

Coffee Break and Conference Trip are distinct types of non-academic/social events at a conference. A coffee break is a short rest period, while a conference trip is an excursion or outing. They do not denote the same concept.
Property A links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (who reads the paper), while Property B links a Topic to a Review preference. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Workshop Session is a type of event (a session within a workshop). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Entity A is a committee (a group/organizational body) that is a subclass of Committee, while Entity B is a person role (Conference Chair) that is a subclass of Person. They represent fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Conference is an event with properties like city, start/end dates. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both properties link an event to a call-for-papers-like administrative entity (confOf's Administrative event and edas's Call). However, their domains differ (Working event vs Academic Event) and their ranges are not strictly equivalent (Administrative event is broader than Call). They overlap in intent but are not fully equivalent.

A 'Call for paper' is a public announcement soliciting paper submissions, while an 'Invitation letter' is typically a personal document (e.g., for visa purposes) inviting someone to attend. They are distinct types of conference documents with different intended instances.

Entity A is a subclass of Person (an applicant who paid early), while Entity B is a subclass of Money (a registration fee for students). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.
studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education), while relatesTo links a Document to events or persons. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (e.g., guidelines, schedules), while 'Coffee break' is a social/conference activity. They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while Property B links a Conference contribution (paper) to a Conference volume (event). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In ekaw, 'Conference' denotes the entire conference event (one edition), with siblings like Workshop and Session. In iasted, 'Conference activity' denotes individual activities that take place during a conference (e.g., coffee break, registration, lecture), as evidenced by its children. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the overarching event, the other is a sub-event/activity within it.

In edas, Session Chair is a direct subclass of Person and a sibling to TPC Member, making it a distinct role. In ekaw, PC Member is a broader class whose children include Session Chair. Thus, edas:SessionChair corresponds to ekaw:Session_Chair (a child of PC_Member), not to ekaw:PC_Member itself. The two classes are related but not equivalent; ekaw:PC_Member subsumes the concept of edas:SessionChair.

Property A is an object property linking an Item to a Person (is given to), while Property B is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (Name). They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Property A is a datatype property linking Conference to a date value, while property B is an object property linking Location to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Withdrawn Paper is a specific status of a paper (a submission that has been withdrawn), while Mailing list is a communication document/list. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'is submitted at' links a conference contribution to a conference volume, while 'provided By' links a sponsorship to an organization.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Sponzorship (iasted) is a subclass of Money representing the financial contribution or sponsorship amount, while Sponzor (sigkdd) represents the sponsor entity/person/organization providing support. They are related concepts (sponsor provides sponsorship) but not equivalent.
Short paper is a type of contribution/submission, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Activity before conference is a class of activities/events occurring before the conference, while Organizator is a class of persons who organize the conference. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (activity vs. person) and are unrelated.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history record (metadata about an individual's past publications), whereas Publication in iasted is a physical or digital published item (e.g., book proceedings). These are fundamentally different concepts.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring or submitting), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (e.g., signing a registration form). These denote different actions with different intended semantics and ranges.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event (an excursion), while One conference day in iasted is a temporal unit representing a single day of the conference. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event in the conference timeline, while an 'Organizing Committee' is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A denotes the end date of a conference, while property B denotes the start date. These are distinct temporal properties and not equivalent.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to organizational subdivisions of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while Building in Ontology B refers to a physical structure/venue. These are entirely different concepts.

'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Biography' captures biographical text. Despite sharing domain (Person) and range (string), they represent entirely different attributes.

set Max Papers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit), while submit relates an Author to a Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Company is an Organization (a business entity), while Meeting Room Place is a physical location (Place). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class encompassing anyone who contributes to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants). Program Chair (B) is a specific organizational role. While a Program Chair could be considered a contributor in a loose sense, the two classes are not equivalent; A is strictly more general than B.

Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (a session or activity at a conference), while Technical commitee in iasted is modeled as a subclass of Delegate (a person/role). These are entirely different concepts.
Reception is a social event (a gathering), while Single hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
confOf:Company is a subclass of Organization (a specific type of organization), while ekaw:Organisation is the general class for organizations. Therefore, Company is subsumed by Organisation.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (street name), while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Short paper is a type of contribution (a document), while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Associated Chair is a type of Chairman (organizational role), while Tutorial speaker is a type of Speaker/Author who presents a tutorial. These are entirely different roles in a conference.

In cmt, Paper is the general class for submitted papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In confOf, Short paper is a specific subtype of Contribution, with sibling classes Paper and Poster. Thus cmt:Paper is a general concept that overlaps with but is not equivalent to confOf:Short_paper; they are related.

'has a publisher' links conference proceedings to a Publisher, while 'has Topic' links a Conference or Paper to a Topic. These properties relate entirely different domain and range concepts and serve unrelated purposes.

hasPhone is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a phone number string, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain.
'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'E mail' captures their email address. These are distinct attributes of a Person and not semantically equivalent.
Speaker is a person (a type of Delegate) who presents at a conference, while Conference hall is a physical place/venue where events are held. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Invitation letter is a type of Document, while Author is a type of Person (Speaker). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Committee member to a Committee (membership relation), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
