A is a datatype property giving the title of a Paper (range: string), while B is an object property linking an Author to a Paper they submit. They differ in kind, domain, range, and semantics.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Invitation letter is a document. They are entirely different concepts.

has First Name refers to a person's given name, while Nation refers to a person's country/nationality. These are entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

Both are datatype properties mapping to string and both serve as 'name' properties, but their domains are disjoint: A applies to Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc., while B applies exclusively to Person. They relate different kinds of entities and thus are not equivalent in a reference alignment.

Both classes represent a Review document in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is a subclass of Conference document with properties linking it to reviewed contributions; in Ontology B it is a subclass of Document alongside Submission and other conference artefacts. Their intended instances coincide.

Accepted contribution is a class representing a paper/contribution that has been accepted, while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline class. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference Trip is a social event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ontology A (cmt), Reviewer is a subclass of Conference Member responsible for reviewing papers. In ontology B (Conference), 'Conference contributor' is a superclass that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author, while 'Reviewer' is listed as a sibling of Conference contributor. These are entirely different concepts: one is a specific role (reviewer), the other is a broad category of people who contribute content to a conference.

hasEndDateTime is a datatype property on Conference Event specifying an end date/time, while Date is a datatype property on Deadline specifying a deadline date. They have different domains (Conference Event vs Deadline) and different semantics (end time of an event vs date of a deadline), so they are unrelated.

'has parts' is a mereological relation linking a conference volume to its constituent parts, while 'is Location Of' links a place to an event occurring there. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different semantics.
Government Organization is a type of organization (institutional entity), while Main office is a type of place (physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (informational artefact), while 'Coctail reception' is a social event/activity at a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Property A (has authors) has domain Conference document and range Person, linking a document to its authors. Property B (sign) has domain Person and range Item, linking a person to an item they sign. They have opposite directions (document->person vs person->item) and different semantics, so they are not equivalent.
Country is a geographical/political entity, while Research Topic is an academic subject area. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A ('is submitted at') links a conference contribution to a conference volume (event/proceedings), while property B ('writes') links an author to a contribution. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while One day presenter in iasted is a type of delegate (a person who presents for one day). These are entirely different concepts.

'isWrittenBy' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'referencedIn' relates an entity to something that cites or references it (citation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Person in confOf represents human individuals (authors, participants, etc.), while Document in edas represents artefacts such as papers, reviews, and menus. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of Person representing an individual who serves on a committee. In Ontology B, 'Committee' represents the organizational body itself (with children like Program Committee). A member and the committee they belong to are distinct concepts, though related via the 'has members' / 'was a member of' properties in Ontology A.

A Tutorial Chair is an organizational role responsible for managing the tutorial track (a type of PC Member/Conference Participant), whereas a Tutorial speaker is the person who actually presents/delivers the tutorial content. These are distinct roles in conference organization.
hasFax and hasLastName are both datatype properties on Person with string range, but they capture entirely different attributes (fax number vs. last name). They are unrelated.
Social program is a type of conference activity/event (e.g., dinner banquet), while Speaker is a person role. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference www is a web document/URL resource for a conference, while Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a subject area topic. They are entirely different concepts.

In edas, Paper is a general class covering all paper states (Active, Pending, Accepted, Rejected, etc.). In ekaw, Evaluated_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing only papers that have already been evaluated (with children Accepted and Rejected). Thus edas:Paper subsumes ekaw:Evaluated_Paper.

In edas, TalkEvent is a type of AcademicEvent with children like ClosingTalk and WelcomeTalk, and PaperPresentation as a sibling, suggesting it covers broader talk-style events. In iasted, Session is a subclass of Lecture (under Conference activity) with Speaker lecture as a child and Plenary lecture/Tutorial as siblings, representing a scheduled session block. While both relate to conference speaking/presentation time slots, their hierarchical placements differ significantly (TalkEvent vs. Session-as-Lecture), so they overlap but are not strictly equivalent.
University is an organization where scholars study, while Departure tax is a type of monetary tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.

hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid in the conference review bidding process, while is_paid_with relates Money to an Item in a payment context. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

University in confOf is an educational institution where scholars study, while Proceedings Publisher in ekaw is an organization that publishes conference proceedings. Although both are subclasses of Organisation/Organization, they represent distinct roles and their intended instances do not coincide.

Activity in iasted is a broad class covering conference events (before, during, after), while Award in sigkdd refers specifically to prizes given for papers. These are conceptually distinct and unrelated.
Poster is a type of conference contribution (a document/artefact), while Speaker is a type of Person who presents. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while notification_until relates an Author to a Deadline Author notification (a temporal deadline). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (assignment of review), while Property B links an author to a contribution they write. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasKeyword is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string keyword, while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They are entirely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is a specific kind of author (as opposed to invited speakers or other contributors), while in Ontology B, 'Author' is the general class for all authors. Thus, Regular author is subsumed by Author.

Property A (scientificallyOrganises) has domain Academic Institution and denotes an institution organizing a scientific event. Property B (give) has domain Person and range Activity/Item, denoting a person giving/presenting something. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Computer Networks Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Academic Institution is an Organisation (e.g., university or research institute), while Speaker is a Person who gives presentations. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Chairman is a role/person in the conference organization hierarchy, while Event is an occurrence or activity (e.g., social event, working event). They are entirely different concepts.
Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and are unrelated.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Conference in Ontology B is a subclass of Scientific Event (the conference event itself). These are entirely different concepts.

'is the 1th part of' relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (a structural part-of relation), while 'paperInVolume' relates a paper to a proceedings volume. These are conceptually distinct relations in the conference domain.

Conference document in Ontology A refers to documents/artefacts associated with a conference (papers, reviews, calls, announcements), while Conference in Ontology B refers to the conference event itself (with properties like city, start/end dates, name). These are entirely different concepts.
Reviewing event is an administrative event (a process/activity), while Conference Participant is a person attending the conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

In cmt, Paper is a submitted document (with authors, decisions, etc.) and Review is a sibling class representing the evaluation of a paper. In iasted, Review is a type of Document but Submission is a separate sibling. Thus cmt:Paper corresponds to iasted:Submission, not iasted:Review. They are unrelated concepts.

In cmt, PaperAbstract is a subclass of Paper (a specific version/part of a paper), while in sigkdd, Abstract is a direct subclass of Document and a sibling of Paper (a standalone document type). They both represent abstracts but have different hierarchical placements and modeling intentions, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In cmt, Person is the top-level class for all people (including reviewers, committee members, etc.). In sigkdd, Organizator is a subclass of Person, specifically covering organizing roles (chairs, committee members, webmaster), excluding Listener and Speaker. Thus cmt:Person subsumes sigkdd:Organizator.

A Session chair presides over a specific session within a conference, while a General Chair is the overall leader/organizer of the entire conference. They are both organizational roles but at different levels of responsibility, so they are related but not equivalent.

Associated Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person) involved in conference organization, while Organising Agency is an organization (subclass of Organisation) that organizes the event. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. organization).

Conference www in Ontology A is a web page/URL resource for the conference (child of Conference document, with property 'has a URL'), whereas Conference Paper in ekaw is a scholarly paper submitted to the conference (child of Paper). These are entirely different concepts.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the chair of the program committee, while Tutorial Chair (ekaw) is the chair responsible for tutorials. These are distinct roles within a conference organization. The equivalent of Program Committee Chair in ekaw would be PC_Chair, which appears as a sibling of Tutorial Chair.

'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance decision), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (indicating who presents). These are entirely different relations with different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Operating Topicsystems is a specific research topic (subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Measurements Topic is a specific research topic area. They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasCall links an Academic Event to a Call, while searched_by links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Individual Presentation is an event where a paper is presented. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Medicine Topic in edas is a specific sub-topic (sibling to Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.) under the general class Topic. Research_Topic in ekaw is the general class representing any research topic that can be covered by events or papers. Therefore, Medicine Topic is a more specific concept subsumed by the more general Research_Topic.
Meta Reviewer is a specialized type of reviewer who oversees reviews for a paper, while Author is the person who writes a paper. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

In confOf, Workshop is a type of Working event (sibling of Conference and Tutorial), representing an interactive session format. In edas, Paper Presentation is a specific academic event where accepted papers are presented (sibling of Workshop). These denote different concepts within the conference domain.

Property A links a Program Committee to a Conference Volume (indicating committee membership/assignment), while Property B links an Event to an Organisation or Person (indicating who organized the event). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'has parts' is a general mereological property linking a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts, while 'has Programme' specifically links a Conference Event to its Programme. They differ in domain, range, and semantic intent.
Paper is a type of scholarly contribution (a document), while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award/honor. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Scientific Event in ekaw covers academic activities (conferences, sessions, workshops, presentations), while Social program in iasted covers non-academic social activities (dinner banquets, cocktail receptions). These are disjoint concepts; ekaw's sibling 'Social Event' would be the counterpart to iasted's 'Social program'.

email is a datatype property mapping Person to a string (an email address), while send is an object property mapping Person to Item (an action of sending). They have different types, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'has a review expertise' links a submitted contribution to a review expertise level, while 'presentation' links a speaker to a document. They are unrelated.

Property A links Topic to Conference part (topic is a topic of a conference part), while Property B links Conference or Paper to Topic (conference/paper has topic). They connect the same domain concepts but in opposite directions and with different domains/ranges, so they are related (roughly inverses) rather than equivalent.
Property A links conference proceedings to a publisher, while property B links a contribution (paper) to an author. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Initial manuscipt is a type of document/submission (the paper itself), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Camera Ready Paper is a type of document/paper, while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They are entirely different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

Entity A is an Event (a registration event), while Entity B is a Person (a participant who registered early). They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and are not equivalent or related by subsumption.

Industry Organization in edas refers to a commercial/corporate entity (sibling of Academia, Government, NGO), while Proceedings Publisher in ekaw refers specifically to an organization that publishes conference proceedings. A proceedings publisher could be an industry organization (e.g., Springer, IEEE) but could also be an academic institution. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent concepts.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject outcome), while submit_until links a Document to a Deadline (temporal constraint). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award given to a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Call For Papers is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting paper submissions), while Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Location in ekaw refers to a physical place where events are held (domain/range of heldIn/locationOf), while Time zone in iasted refers to a temporal/geographic time zone concept. These are entirely different concepts.
Acceptance is a decision outcome for a paper submission, while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Topic in Ontology A is a general class for conference topics, while Antennas Topic in edas is a specific subclass of Topic. Therefore, the general Topic subsumes Antennas Topic.

Property A relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (inviting co-reviewers), while Property B relates a PC Member to a Contribution (reviewing a paper). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating, while is_given_to links an Item to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
The two properties have completely different domains (Conference vs Deadline), ranges (boolean vs date), and semantics (accepting hardcopy submissions vs a deadline date). They are unrelated.

startReviewerBidding is an action by an Administrator to initiate the reviewer bidding phase for a Conference, while invites_co-reviewers is a relation where a Reviewer invites other Reviewers as co-reviewers. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a specific type of Social Event (sibling of Conference Banquet). Social program in iasted is a broader category of social/conference activities that includes Dinner banquet, Coctail reception, etc. A conference trip is a kind of social program, so Conference Trip is subsumed by Social program.

In edas, 'Programme' is a subclass of Document representing the schedule/programme of a conference event (linked via belongsToEvent). In ekaw, 'Web Site' is a subclass of Document representing a website that lists events. These are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of finalizing paper assignments, while submit relates an Author to a Paper for submission. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Event is a broad class with children including Administrative event, Social event, and Working event. In sigkdd, Conference is a specific type of event (the conference itself). Therefore, confOf:Event subsumes sigkdd:Conference, as a conference is one kind of event but Event also covers social and administrative events.

Program Committee Member (A) is a specific committee role responsible for reviewing and managing papers. Conference contributor (B) is a broader class whose children include Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author—people who contribute content to the conference but are not necessarily on the program committee. The sibling 'Committee member' in B would be closer to A. These classes have different intended instances.

Document in cmt represents written artefacts (Paper, Review), while Organization in confOf represents institutions (Company, University). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Venue Place (edas) refers to the specific physical location/building where the conference is held, while Conference city (iasted) refers to the city hosting the conference. A venue is located in a city but they are not the same concept; they are related.

Both classes represent a member of the program committee (a reviewer). confOf's 'Member PC' has comment 'Reviewer' and reviews contributions; sigkdd's 'Program Committee member' is under Organizator alongside Program Chair. They denote the same concept.

Both classes represent the concept of a Topic in the conference domain. In Ontology A, Topic is associated with submitted contributions and conference parts (tracks/workshops). In Ontology B, Topic is dealt with by Contributions, has expertise from PC Members, and is associated with Working events. The intended instances coincide: both denote subject areas or themes relevant to papers/contributions and conference sessions.

Associated Chair in cmt is a subclass of Chairman (and Conference Member), typically referring to a co-chair or associate chair role. OC Member in ekaw is an Organizing Committee member, which is a broader category that includes OC Chair as a child. While both are organizational roles within a conference, they are not equivalent: Associated Chair is a specific leadership role, whereas OC Member is a general committee membership. They overlap conceptually but are not the same.

has First Name is a datatype property for a person's first name (domain: Person), while Currency is a datatype property for the currency of a registration fee (domain: Registration fee). They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

Contribution 1th author is a specific role denoting the first/primary author of a conference contribution, nested under Regular author. Participant in confOf is a broad class for any person participating in the conference (with children Member, Regular, Student). These are not equivalent; at best they are loosely related as both involve people in a conference context, but their intended instances differ significantly.

'has an abstract' is a specific property linking papers/posters/presentations to their abstract, while 'hasPart' is a generic mereological part-of relation with unspecified domain and range. They are not equivalent.

Both are types of abstracts in the conference domain, but they refer to different kinds: 'Extended abstract' in Ontology A is a regular contribution (a sibling of Paper), while 'Invited Talk Abstract' in ekaw is specifically an abstract for an invited talk. They overlap as abstracts but are not equivalent.

Property A relates a Committee to its Chair (a membership/leadership relation), while Property B relates an Author to a Contribution they write (an authorship relation). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A gives the volume number of conference proceedings, while property B gives a monetary amount. Different domains (Conference proceedings vs Money) and different semantics; they are unrelated.

In ekaw, Paper and Abstract are sibling classes under Document, with Paper being a full paper (having reviews, reviewers, topics) and Abstract being a short summary. In sigkdd, Abstract is also a sibling of Paper under Document. Thus, ekaw:Paper corresponds to sigkdd:Paper, not sigkdd:Abstract. They denote different concepts.

City (confOf) is a specific type of place, while Location (ekaw) is a more general concept for where events are held. Every city can serve as a location, but not every location is necessarily a city (it could be a venue, building, etc.). Thus City is subsumed by Location.

Session is a type of scientific event (e.g., conference session, poster session), while Fee is a monetary charge (e.g., registration fee). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper in cmt is a document/artefact (a submitted manuscript), while Activity before conference in iasted is a type of activity or event occurring prior to the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while a 'Coctail reception' is a social event/activity at a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while is_held_after relates an Activity to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Administrative event is a type of Event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Agency Staff Member is a type of Person. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.

readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer (domain: Paper, range: Reviewer), while reviewOfPaper links a Review to a Paper (domain: Review, range: Paper). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.
hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while property B (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'accepted By' links a Paper to an Administrator (indicating who accepted the paper), while 'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (indicating who delivers the presentation). These relate different domain concepts and express entirely different relationships.

Conference volume in Ontology A represents a specific instance/edition of a conference (with committees, location, contributions, tracks, etc.), while Conference days in Ontology B is a temporal concept under Time representing the days during which a conference occurs. These are fundamentally different concepts.
RatedPapers is a subclass of Paper (a paper that has been rated), while Review is the review document itself. They are related through the reviewing process but denote different concepts.
Paper is a type of Contribution (a submitted document), while Antennas Topic is a specific subject area under Topic. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

authorOf relates a Person to a Document (person authored document), while is_given_to relates an Item to a Person (item given to person). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other in a meaningful alignment sense.

readPaper (domain: Reviewer, range: Paper) and hasReviewer (domain: Paper, range: Possible Reviewer) have opposite directions and different semantics. readPaper describes a reviewer reading a paper, while hasReviewer links a paper to its assigned reviewer. They are not inverses of each other either (the inverse of hasReviewer would be 'is reviewer of'), so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Meta Reviewer is a specialized subclass of Reviewer with a distinct role (overseeing other reviews). In edas, Reviewer is the general class for anyone who reviews papers. Therefore, cmt:Meta Reviewer is subsumed by edas:Reviewer, as every meta-reviewer is a reviewer but not every reviewer is a meta-reviewer.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'presentation' links a Speaker to a Document.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document representing a submitted paper. In iasted, Item is a very general class whose children include Document, Publication, Audiovisual equipment, etc. Paper (a document) would be subsumed by the much broader Item class, but they are not equivalent.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (reviewer bidding), while issues relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to the papers it contains, while presentationed_by relates a document to its speaker/presenter. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Submission event in confOf is an administrative event (a process/deadline for submitting contributions), while Final manuscript in iasted is a document (an artefact). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. document) and are unrelated.

logoURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI for its logo, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They describe entirely different concepts and have different domains, ranges, and property types.
Written contribution is a type of conference document/artefact (a paper or submission), while Author is a person who writes papers. They belong to entirely different categories in the domain.

Property A ('has short title') applies to events (Social event, Working event) and captures a short/abbreviated title, while Property B ('has Name') applies to Conference and captures the full name. They differ in both domain and semantic intent (short title vs. full name), so they are unrelated.
hasMember relates a Conference to its member Persons, while is_given_by relates an Activity or Item to the Person who gives/presents it. Different domains and different semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Book proceeding is a type of publication. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

A 'Reviewing results event' is an administrative event where review results are made accessible to authors, while a 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a time/deadline for submitting the final camera-ready version of a paper. They refer to different concepts (event vs. deadline) and different stages of the conference process.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for submitted papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In Conference ontology, Camera ready contribution is a very specific subclass deep in the hierarchy representing only the final accepted camera-ready version of a paper. These are not equivalent; Camera ready contribution is much more specific than Paper.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of 'Person', while in Ontology B, 'Person' is the top-level class for people. Thus, Committee member is strictly more specific than (subsumed by) Person.
Abstract is a type of Document (a summary of a paper), while Deadline is a temporal constraint for submissions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who started the bidding process, while 'invites_co-reviewers' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer they invite as a co-reviewer.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Computer Networks Aapplications Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.
'written By' relates a Contribution to its Author, while 'searched by' relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Communication Theory Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasSubjectArea relates a Paper to a Subject Area, while obtain relates an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Regular contribution' is a broader class that has 'Paper' as one of its children (along with 'Extended abstract'). In Ontology B, 'Paper' is a specific document type. Therefore, Regular contribution subsumes Paper.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic paper (Document), while Computer is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
writtenBy links a Document to its author (Person), while give links a Person to an Activity or Item they present. They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value for acceptance announcements, while Property B is an object property linking Administrative events in a sequential order. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Place in edas represents a physical location (with children like Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place), while Conference in sigkdd represents the conference event itself (with properties like Name, Start/End dates). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A links a Conference to an Administrator who prints hardcopy mailing manifests, while Property B links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

minChoice is a datatype property (domain: events, range: positiveInteger) indicating minimum choices, while listsEvent is an object property (domain: Programme Brochure/Web Site, range: Event) linking publications to events. They are completely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'go through' relates an Item to an Activity (process). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Student is a type of conference participant (person attending as a student), while Gold Supporter is a type of sponsor (organization or entity providing financial support). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.

Property A links an organizing committee to a conference volume (part-of/organizer relation), while Property B links two administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Payment document in iasted is a specific type of Document (with children Bank transfer, Cheque), while Document in sigkdd is a general class (with children Abstract, Paper, Review). The iasted Payment document is subsumed by the more general sigkdd Document class.

Person in cmt is a general class for all people involved in the conference. Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (as shown by its path 'Person > Speaker') representing specifically those who give presentations. Therefore, cmt:Person subsumes sigkdd:Speaker.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a subclass of Conference document (an artefact like a paper, poster, or presentation), while Event in ekaw represents an occurrence such as a scientific or social event. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, Presentation is a sibling of Written contribution and Poster, indicating it refers to an oral/talk-style presentation (with child Invited talk). In Ontology B, Short paper is a sibling of Paper and Poster under Contribution, referring to a short written submission. These are distinct types of conference contributions.
logo URL refers to the web address of a conference's logo image, while City of conference refers to the city where the conference is held. These are entirely different attributes of a Conference.
Track is a part of a conference (like a tutorial or workshop), while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper, while design links ACM SIGKDD to a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'abstract' relates a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while 'Nation' relates a Person to their nationality (string). They have completely different domains and semantic meanings.

Contributed Talk is a type of event/presentation (a talk given at a conference), while Speaker is a type of person who gives presentations. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Person) and are not equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing information to attendees, while 'Platinum Supporter' is a top-tier sponsor category. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Member in cmt refers to a person participating in the conference (author, reviewer, chair, etc.), while Sponzor in sigkdd refers to an organization or entity sponsoring the event. These are entirely different concepts.

Extended abstract is a specific type of conference contribution (a short paper), while Submission in iasted is a general class for any submitted document (with children Final manuscript and Initial manuscript). Extended abstract is a kind of submission, so the iasted Submission subsumes the Conference Extended_abstract.
In edas, Programme is a Document (like a schedule/agenda) associated with a Conference Event. In sigkdd, Program Committee is a Committee (a group of people). These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document/publication (a volume of papers), while Conference in sigkdd is the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates. These are fundamentally different concepts.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person (authorship/signature). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Paper is a scholarly contribution (sibling of Poster and Short paper). In ekaw, Flyer is a promotional document (sibling of Programme Brochure, Web Site) published by an Organisation. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Call For Manuscripts' and 'Call For Papers' are distinct sibling classes under 'Call', suggesting they represent different concepts (e.g., manuscripts for journals vs papers for conferences). In ontology A, 'Call for paper' is a type of Conference document. While both relate to soliciting submissions, the presence of a separate 'Call For Papers' sibling in edas indicates 'Call For Manuscripts' is not equivalent to 'Call for paper'. They are related but not equivalent.

Passive conference participant is a subclass of Person (a role for attendees), while Conference Dinner is a subclass of Meal Event (an event). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Event in ekaw represents conference occurrences (scientific events, social events) with properties like heldIn and organisedBy, while Document in sigkdd represents written artefacts (Abstract, Paper, Review) with properties like submit until. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

reviewsPerPaper is an integer count of reviews per paper for a conference, while manuscriptDueOn is a dateTime deadline for manuscript submission. They represent entirely different concepts with different ranges and semantics.
Coffee Break is a type of event (a break during a conference), while Conference hall is a type of place/venue. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties express authorship ('written by'), but they differ significantly in domain and range specificity. In cmt, 'writtenBy' specifically links a Review to a Reviewer, while in iasted, 'is_writen_by' links a generic Item to a Person. Since Review is a kind of Item and Reviewer is a kind of Person, the cmt property is more specific. They are related (both denote authorship) but not equivalent due to different domain/range constraints.

Personal Review History in edas is a record/history of reviews associated with a reviewer (a kind of Personal History), whereas Possible Reviewer in ekaw is a person who may review papers. One is an informational artefact/history, the other is a role played by a person; they are conceptually unrelated.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while writes links an Author to a Contribution (authorship relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A links an active conference participant to a presentation they give, while property B links a conference to a person who is a member of it. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

The two properties describe entirely different concepts: 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (e.g., a paper they have a conflict with), while 'is paid with' relates Money to an Item. They share no semantic overlap.

Property A (writtenBy) links Document -> Person (authorship), while property B (submit) links Author -> Paper (submission). They differ in both direction and semantics: one denotes authorship, the other denotes the act of submitting. They are not equivalent nor inverses (inverse of writtenBy would be writes/hasWritten, not submit).
'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'hold' relates an organization (ACM SIGKDD) to a Conference (organizing/holding). Different domains and different semantics.

In cmt, Administrator is a system role (subclass of User) responsible for managing the conference platform (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, etc.). In confOf, Scholar is a type of participant/attendee (a price category for students/scholars) who studies at a university. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement in Ontology A is a type of conference document (an artefact/notice), while Conference in Ontology B is a type of working event (the event itself). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Rejected contribution is a type of conference document (a paper that was rejected), while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (locationOf) relates a Location to an Event (i.e., an event takes place at a location), while Property B (is_visited_by) relates a Building/City/State to a Person (i.e., a person visits a place). The domains and ranges are fundamentally different (Event vs. Person), so these properties are unrelated.

Main office and Conference hall are distinct sibling classes under Place in both ontologies. A main office is an administrative location while a conference hall is a venue for sessions; they are related as types of places but not equivalent.

Property A links a conference contribution (paper) to a conference volume (proceedings), expressing where a paper is submitted/published. Property B links an Event to another Event, expressing mereological part-whole relationships between events. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.
Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.), while Person in iasted represents a human individual. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Radio Communications Topic is a subject area/topic within a conference. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.

Property A specifies an abstract submission date (a temporal value on Important dates), while Property B provides submission instructions (textual guidance on a Call). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
OC Member is a person role (Organizing Committee member), while Registration fee is a monetary amount. They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a 'Review expertise' entity to a 'Submitted contribution' (a paper), while Property B links a 'Reviewer' to their 'Personal Review History'. These relate different domain and range concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.

User in cmt is a general class for any person interacting with the conference system (including administrators, authors, reviewers). Worker lecturer in iasted is a very specific subclass of Lecturer > Speaker > Author > Delegate, representing a lecturer who is also a worker. These concepts have entirely different scopes and intended instances.

Both Administrator (confOf) and Organizator (sigkdd) are subclasses of Person representing the organizing/administrative staff of a conference. The children of Organizator (General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc.) correspond to administrative/organizational roles, matching the intent of Administrator in confOf. Despite different labels, they denote the same concept in the conference domain.
Property A links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract, while property B links an author to a related paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event where review outcomes are made available to authors, while Call For Reviews is a call soliciting reviewers. They belong to different class hierarchies (Event vs Call) and represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any person who authors a paper (child of Person). Author of paper student in sigkdd is specifically a student author (child of Author). The general Paper Author subsumes the more specific student author.

In cmt, Paper is the main submitted document (child of Document). In confOf, Contribution is a broader class encompassing Paper, Poster, and Short paper. Thus cmt:Paper corresponds to the general concept of a submission but is strictly subsumed by confOf:Contribution, which also includes posters and short papers.

Entity A is a 'Registration of participants event' (an administrative event for registering attendees), while Entity B is a 'Submissions deadline' (a deadline for paper submissions). They refer to entirely different concepts in the conference domain—different activities and different types (event vs. deadline).

'has the last name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their surname), while 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

Both properties relate an author-type entity to a paper/contribution (Co author->Paper vs Author->writes->Contribution). However, 'co write Paper' specifically denotes co-authorship while 'writes' is a general writing relation. They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent due to the co-author nuance.

Entity A is a research topic related to computer networks in enterprises, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Conference announcement in Ontology A is a type of document (subclass of Conference document), while Conference Event in Ontology B is an event/activity with temporal and spatial properties (start/end dates, location, attendees). They represent entirely different concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Tutorial is a type of event/presentation. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Conference fees is a general concept covering all fees associated with a conference, while Hotel fee is a specific type of fee for hotel accommodation. In ontology B, Registration fee is a sibling of Hotel fee under Fee, suggesting Conference fees would be closer to the parent Fee class or specifically to Registration fee. They overlap in domain but are not equivalent; Conference fees is more general and could subsume Hotel fee if it were in the same hierarchy, but as they stand they are merely related.

Property A ('is a full paper submission date') is a specific kind of deadline date (for full paper submissions), while Property B ('Date') is a general date property for any Deadline. Thus A is subsumed by B, as every full paper submission date is a deadline date, but not vice versa.

confOf:Student is a general participant role (any student attending the conference), while sigkdd:Author_of_paper_student is specifically a student who has authored a paper. The latter implies both authorship and student status, whereas the former only implies student status as a participant. They overlap but are not equivalent; they are related concepts.
reviewsPerPaper is an integer count of reviews per paper for a conference, while paperDueOn is a dateTime deadline for paper submission. They have different ranges and entirely different semantics.

In edas, Conference is the main conference event entity with properties like dates, country, members, and topics. In iasted, 'Conference days' is a subclass of Time representing temporal duration/days of the conference, not the conference itself. They are conceptually distinct.

Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (like a conference or tutorial), whereas Simulating in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Registration of participants event is an administrative sub-event (e.g., the registration phase) within a conference system, while Conference in ekaw represents the entire scientific event itself. They are at completely different levels of granularity and serve different purposes.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Welcome address is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members (committee -> person), while property B links a PC member to the contributions they review (person -> paper). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event for submitting contributions, while a 'Best Paper Awards Committee' is a committee responsible for selecting best papers. They are entirely different concepts (event vs. committee) with no meaningful overlap.

Member PC in confOf represents a program committee member/reviewer (comment: 'Reviewer', properties: reviewes Contribution), while Paper Author in ekaw represents an author of a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain.

Entity A is a research topic (Computer Networks Security) under the Topic hierarchy, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a physical computer) under the Item hierarchy. They are completely unrelated concepts.
hasVAT represents a value-added tax identifier for events, while hasEmail represents an email address for persons or contact information. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

isLocationOf has domain Place and range ConferenceEvent, while heldIn has domain Event and range Location. They are inverse properties of each other (Place isLocationOf Event vs Event heldIn Location), not equivalent. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

'initiates' in edas specifically relates conference chairs/TPC members to a Call (e.g., call for papers), while 'give' in iasted is a very general property relating a Person to an Activity or Item. Their domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly, making them unrelated.
A is a datatype property assigning a numeric ID to a Paper, while B is an object property linking a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Property A is a specific datatype property for the camera-ready paper submission date (domain: Important dates, range: date), while Property B is a general 'Date' property for any deadline (domain: Deadline, range: dateTime). Since camera-ready submission is one type of deadline, A is more specific than B, making A subsumed by B.
has Country links an Organization or Person to a Country, while is equipped by links a Place to an Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Chair is the head of a conference (a type of Chairman), while Assistant is a support role. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (someone who presents their own paper). In ekaw, Invited_Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (which is under Conference Participant), typically an invited keynote speaker who may not be an author. These are different roles in the conference domain; they overlap conceptually as 'people who present' but have different intended instances and hierarchical contexts.

Property A 'writes' has domain Author and range Contribution, while property B 'is writen by' has domain Item and range Person. They are inverse properties of each other (Author writes Contribution vs Item is written by Person). Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, but they are clearly related as inverses in the same domain.

'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'has Fax' captures a fax number. Despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string), they represent entirely different attributes and are unrelated.

An Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing a conference, while an Academic Institution is an organization such as a university or research institute. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties mapping to string for naming purposes, but A's 'name' has domain Conference and Person while B's 'hasName' is restricted to Conference with comment 'Conference Full Name'. They overlap on Conference naming but differ in domain scope, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A links Topic to Conference part (Topic is domain), while Property B links Working event to Topic (Topic is range). They are roughly inverse relations over overlapping but not identical domains/ranges (Conference part vs Working event), so they are related but not equivalent.
Property A 'name' gives the name of a Conference or Person, while property B 'ends on' gives the end date/time of an Event. They have different semantics, domains, and purposes.
Accepted contribution is a type of conference paper that has been accepted, while Deadline hotel reservation is a temporal deadline for reserving a hotel. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Author Not Reviewer is an author who does not serve as a reviewer, while Student non speaker is a student delegate who does not give a talk. These are conceptually distinct roles in the conference domain with no meaningful overlap.

Program Committee in cmt is a specific committee of reviewers for evaluating papers, while Organisation in ekaw refers to institutional entities like academic institutions or organising agencies. These are conceptually distinct.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (an assignment/reference), while property B links a PC member to a contribution they review. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Organization in Ontology A refers to an organizational entity (e.g., institution, company), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a Person role (subclass of Person > Organizator). These are fundamentally different concepts.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of Chairman (a leadership role in the conference/program committee). In confOf, 'Assistant' is a direct subclass of Person with comment 'confTool', likely referring to an administrative or support assistant role. These are distinct roles in the conference domain and do not denote the same concept.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite also inheriting from Person/TPC Member, likely an ontology modeling artifact), while Tutorial Chair in ekaw is a person role responsible for tutorials. These are entirely different concepts.

readByMeta-Reviewer links a Paper to a Meta Reviewer (a person/role), while hasRating links an Active Paper to a Review Rating (an evaluation object). The domains are similar but the ranges and semantic meanings are entirely different.

The property 'enable Virtual Meeting' relates an Administrator to a Conference, while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring), while 'pay' relates a Person to Money (financial transaction). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Meeting Room Place is a venue for holding meetings/sessions, while Hotel is an accommodation place. They are distinct sibling concepts under Place in their respective ontologies and do not denote the same concept.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Activity after conference is a post-conference event/activity (e.g., departure, full day tour). They belong to entirely different categories (documents vs. activities) and are unrelated.
Tutorial in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Tutorial speaker in iasted is a person/role who speaks at a tutorial. An event and a person are fundamentally different concepts.
siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'is sent by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person (sender), while 'E mail' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (email address). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Government Organization in edas refers to a government-affiliated organization (a type of organization by sector), while Organising Agency in ekaw refers to an entity that organizes the conference (a functional role). They overlap conceptually since a government body could act as an organising agency, but they are not equivalent: one classifies by sector, the other by function.

Conference proceedings in Ontology A is a published document/volume (has ISBN, publisher, volume), whereas Conference activity in Ontology B refers to events or scheduled activities during a conference (e.g., lectures, coffee breaks, registration). These are entirely different concepts.

Workshop is a type of working event (a session or meeting), while Worker non speaker is a type of delegate (a person attending the conference who is not speaking). They are entirely different concepts.

A TPC Member is a program committee member responsible for reviewing papers and initiating calls, while a Speaker is someone who gives a presentation at the conference. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and properties.

Rejected Paper is a specific status of a full paper (a Paper that was not accepted), while Abstract is a summary document type distinct from Paper in sigkdd. They represent different concepts at different levels of the document hierarchy and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.
hasSurname refers to a person's family/last name, while hasFirstName refers to a person's given/first name. These are distinct properties capturing different parts of a person's name.

isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while occupy relates a Person to a Building, City, or State (location). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

Web Site and Abstract are entirely different concepts within the conference domain. A Web Site is an online resource listing events, while an Abstract is a summary document of a paper. They share only the common superclass Document but have no semantic overlap.

Entity A is a 'Registration of participants event' (an administrative event for registering attendees), while Entity B is a 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' (a time/deadline for submitting camera-ready papers). They refer to entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Sponsor state in iasted is a state/status related to sponsorship (subclass of State). These are entirely different concepts.

The two properties relate entirely different domain and range concepts: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator (who runs paper assignment tools), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (who presents it). They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

In iasted, Lecturer is a subclass of Author (path: ... > Speaker > Author > Lecturer), meaning it represents a specific kind of author who lectures. In sigkdd, Author is a direct subclass of Speaker and represents anyone who authors/submits papers. The iasted Lecturer is more specific than the sigkdd Author, so Lecturer is subsumed_by Author.

Property A (has_parts) relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts and is the inverse direction of Property B (partOfEvent), which relates an Event to another Event it is part of. They differ in domain/range semantics and directionality; they are not equivalent.
Paper Full Version is a complete paper submission (child of Paper), while Review is an evaluation document written by a reviewer. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while B is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and types.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Currency refers to monetary units. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Presenter city is a subclass of City (a location). They are entirely different concepts.

A Committee member is a person serving on an organizing or program committee, while a Speaker is a person giving a presentation. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different properties and contexts.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while property B (has_a_review) links a Reviewed contribution (paper) to its Review. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'virtual Meeting Enabled By' links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while 'gives presentations' links an Active conference participant to a Presentation they deliver.
publisherOf relates an Organisation to published documents (Flyer, etc.), while obtain relates an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review expertise in Ontology A represents a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill regarding a topic, while Document in Ontology B is a general class for artefacts like papers, abstracts, and reviews. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Workshops (part-of relation), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation/authorship relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Meal Event is a type of conference event (a meal), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.
'writePaper' relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while 'need' relates a Person to an Item (a requirement). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-event in the conference domain, while is_made_from relates an Item to another Item indicating composition/derivation. These properties have different semantics and purposes.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'technically Organises' relates an Organisation to something it organises. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Volunteer is a person who offers unpaid help at the conference, while a Workshop Chair is a specific academic role responsible for chairing a workshop session. These are entirely different concepts with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

Property A (date) is a generic date property with domain Conference, while property B (is an ending date) specifically denotes an ending date with domain Important dates. They differ in both semantics and domain, making them unrelated.

Student is a class representing a person (a type of attendee/author), while Best Student Paper Award is a class representing an award given to a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Country is a geopolitical entity (used as the location of organizations or persons), while Currency is a monetary unit. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, Workshop is a specific type of Conference part (sibling to Track and Tutorial). In Ontology B, Working_event is a broader category that has Workshop as one of its children (along with Conference and Tutorial). Therefore, Workshop in A is subsumed by Working_event in B.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC member to a contribution they review (domain: Member PC, range: Contribution). Property B (is given to) links an item to a person it is given to (domain: Item, range: Person). The domains and ranges are reversed in semantic role, and the relations describe fundamentally different interactions (reviewing vs. being given something), so they are unrelated.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of Working event), while Conference hall in sigkdd is a physical place/venue. They are fundamentally different concepts.

In ekaw, 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of Document/Paper representing the paper artifact itself after acceptance. In iasted, 'Accepting manuscript' is a subclass of Activity (specifically 'Activity before conference'), representing the process/event of accepting a manuscript, not the document. An artifact and an activity are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item, while 'Nation' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string representing their nationality. They describe entirely different relations.

hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (assigning a reviewer), while write links a Person to an Item (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Author is a person who writes a paper, while Registration form is a document used for conference registration. They are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Abstract' is a child of 'Extended abstract', meaning Extended abstract is a broader concept that subsumes Abstract. In Ontology B, 'Abstract' is a direct subclass of Document and represents paper abstracts (with children like Invited Talk Abstract). Thus, A's Extended abstract is more general than B's Abstract; they overlap but are not equivalent.

Reviewing event is an administrative event/procedure for reviewing submitted contributions, while Submissions deadline is a time/deadline by which submissions must be made. They are conceptually distinct (event vs. deadline) and pertain to different phases of the conference process (reviewing vs. submission).

Workshop and Tutorial are both types of academic/conference activities but represent distinct concepts: a workshop is typically an interactive session focused on a specific topic, while a tutorial is an instructional lecture. They are related as sibling-like subtypes of conference events but not equivalent.
Document in cmt represents written artefacts like papers and reviews, while Organisation in ekaw represents institutions and agencies. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

confOf 'Social event' is a general class with children Banquet, Reception, and Trip. ekaw 'Conference Banquet' is a specific subclass of 'Social Event'. Therefore, confOf's Social event subsumes ekaw's Conference Banquet.
Conference Session is a type of scientific event (a time-bounded session), while Main office is a type of place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Cd proceening is a type of Publication (a CD containing proceedings), while Invited Speaker is a type of Person/Role. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference part (A) has children Track, Tutorial, Workshop and represents sub-events or components of a conference volume. Working event (B) has children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop and is itself a subclass of Event. They overlap on Tutorial and Workshop but differ: A includes Track while B includes Conference as a child. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Administrative event (confOf) represents conference processes/activities like submission, reviewing, and registration, while Deadline (iasted) represents specific time points by which those activities must be completed. They share similar sub-concepts (e.g., submission event vs submissions deadline, camera ready event vs camera ready manuscript deadline), but an event is not the same as a deadline. They are related but not equivalent.

Registration of participants event is an administrative event for registering attendees, while Workshop is a scientific event where research is presented. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Coctail reception is a conference activity/event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A links a Program committee to a Conference volume, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Early paid applicant is a registration/payment status class under Conference applicant, while Author in sigkdd is a role under Speaker who submits papers. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing individuals who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Research Institute in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation/Academic Institution. These are entirely different concepts (person vs organization) and are unrelated.
locationOf relates a Location to an Event (spatial relation), while is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (temporal relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a street name string, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

In edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a paper that has been accepted (a final positive decision). In ekaw, 'Evaluated Paper' is a paper that has been reviewed/evaluated but not yet decided upon; it is the parent of both 'Accepted Paper' and 'Rejected Paper'. Thus, edas:AcceptedPaper corresponds to ekaw:AcceptedPaper, not ekaw:Evaluated_Paper. They are related as both represent post-review states, but they are not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Invited Talk is a type of event/presentation. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties express where an event/activity takes place, but they differ significantly in modeling: A is a datatype property (range string) while B is an object property (range Place, Time). They capture the same conceptual relationship but are not strictly equivalent due to different ranges and property types.

Accepted contribution is a class of documents (papers that have been accepted), while Reviewing event is a class of administrative events (the process of reviewing). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

In cmt, Document is a general class with children Paper and Review. In ekaw, Web Site is a specific subclass of Document. Thus, cmt:Document subsumes ekaw:Web_Site (or equivalently, ekaw:Web_Site is subsumed_by cmt:Document). They are not equivalent since Document in cmt covers papers and reviews broadly, while Web Site in ekaw is a very specific type of document.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'enter Conference Details' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'for Event' links a Call to an Academic Event. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while writtenBy is an object property linking a Document to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Research Topic refers to a subject area of research, while Time refers to temporal concepts (days, deadlines). They are completely unrelated.
The 'title' property in cmt gives the title of a Paper (a string), while 'has First Name' in confOf gives the first name of a Person. They have different domains and completely different semantics.
The 'email' property captures a person's email address, while 'has First Name' captures a person's given name. These are entirely different attributes of a Person and do not denote the same relation.

Property A links a Conference part to a Conference volume (part-whole relationship within conference proceedings), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation/authorship relationship). These are entirely different relations in both domain and range.

Property A 'name' is a general datatype property for naming Conferences and Persons (range: string), while property B 'registrationDueOn' is a specific deadline property for Conference registration dates (range: dateTime). They represent entirely different concepts.
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while updatedVersionOf relates a Document to a previous version of that Document. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

hasName is a datatype property linking Conference to a string (its full name), while heldIn is an object property linking Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A is 'Workshop', a part of a conference, while Entity B is 'Conference', the overall event. In confOf, Workshop is actually a sibling of Conference under Working event. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties relate an author-type entity to a Paper, but they denote different actions: 'co write Paper' refers to co-authoring/writing a paper (domain Co author), while 'submit' refers to the act of submitting a paper (domain Author). They overlap in connecting authors to papers but are not equivalent.

In iasted, Form is a specific subclass of Document (with children like Registration form, Hotel registration form). In sigkdd, Document is a general class whose children are Abstract, Paper, and Review. The iasted Form does not correspond to the sigkdd Document; they represent different levels of specificity and different concepts within their respective ontologies.

A is a topic classification for papers (Parallel And Distributed Computing), while B is an award category (Best Applications Paper Award). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a conference paper/document to its author(s). 'Conference document' aligns with 'Paper' and 'Person' aligns with 'Author' in the conference domain, making has_authors and isWrittenBy semantically equivalent.

Abstract in Ontology A is a type of conference contribution (a short document), while Topic in Ontology B represents a subject area or theme of a paper/conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties express the same relation: a paper/document is written by an author/person. In edas, domain is Paper and range is Author; in ekaw, domain is Document (which includes papers) and range is Person (which includes authors). The intended instances coincide, making them equivalent.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (the head of the PC), while Tutorial Chair in ekaw is specifically the chair responsible for tutorials. These are distinct roles within a conference organization, though both are types of chairs. They are related but not equivalent.

Paper Full Version is a complete paper document (subclass of Paper), while Tutorial Abstract is an abstract for a tutorial (subclass of Abstract). They represent entirely different types of documents in the conference domain.

manuscriptDueOn is a datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime deadline, while topicCoveredBy is an object property linking Research Topic to Event or Paper. They are completely unrelated in domain, range, type, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Speaker lecture is an event/activity (a type of session). They are completely different concepts.
The two properties have completely different semantics: 'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to people who review it, while 'is equipped by' links a Place to an Item that equips it. They are unrelated.

Workshop Chair and General Chair are distinct roles in conference organization. A Workshop Chair manages a specific workshop, while a General Chair oversees the entire conference. They are related as both are chair/organizer roles but not equivalent.

'invites co reviewers' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer for the purpose of inviting co-reviewers, while 'write' relates a Person to an Item for authorship. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Both classes represent a Tutorial in the conference domain. In confOf it is a Working event (sibling of Conference and Workshop), while in iasted it is a type of Lecture under Conference activity. Despite different taxonomic placements, their intended instances—tutorial sessions at a conference—are the same.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (general PC chair), while Demo Chair in ekaw is specifically the chair responsible for demo sessions. These are distinct roles; the equivalent of Chair PC in ekaw would be PC Chair. They are related as both are chair roles within a conference.
