Submitted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been submitted), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Review is a document (the actual written review of a paper). In Conference, Review preference is a metadata concept expressing a reviewer's preference or expertise level for a topic or submission. These are entirely different concepts.

hasProgramCommitteeMember links a Program Committee to its members, while organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'is used for' relates Item to Activity/Money, while 'obtain' relates Author to Award. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while obtain relates a Person to an Item they acquire. These properties have different semantics, different directions, and different domain/range types; they are unrelated.

Meal Break is a type of non-academic conference event (a break for eating), while Program Committee is an organizational committee responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Submission event is an administrative event (a process/activity for submitting contributions), while Committee is a group of people (organizing or program committee). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Student is a subclass of Person representing a role, while Best Applications Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasMenu links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu, while hasEvent links an Event to a sub-Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its members (people), while has_tracks links a Conference volume to its tracks (organizational subdivisions). These relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.

'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name string, while 'speak in' is an object property linking a Person to a Place and Time. They represent entirely different relations.

Entity A is a 'Conference announcement', which is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants). Entity B is the 'Conference' event itself, with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. A document about a conference is not the same as the conference event.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (expressing reviewer topic preferences), while Property B links a PC Member to a Contribution (expressing that a PC member reviews a paper). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subject area/topic classification, while Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for a tutorial). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.
Session in ekaw is a type of scientific event (a time-bounded program element), while Main office in iasted is a type of place (a physical location). They are entirely different concepts.

University is an organization (an institution where scholars study), while Student lecturer is a person role (a lecturer who is also a student). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasStreet is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string (street address), while is_connected_with is an object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place. They have completely different semantics, types, domains, and ranges.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (a person role), while property B links a Speaker to a Document (presentation). These relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve completely different purposes in the conference domain.
Conference www in Ontology A is a type of conference document (a website/webpage), while Conference Session in ekaw is a type of event/session at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.

startReviewerBidding is an administrative action linking an Administrator to a Conference to initiate the bidding phase, while isReviewing links reviewing roles (e.g., Reviewer) to a Paper they are currently reviewing. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Conference volume' is a direct child of 'Conference' and represents a specific edition/instance of a conference (with committees, location, tracks, contributions, etc.). In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Conference' is explicitly commented as 'One edition of a conference'. Both denote the same concept: a single occurrence/edition of a conference event.

confOf:Contribution is a general class for any submitted work (Paper, Poster, Short paper), while ekaw:Evaluated_Paper is a very specific subclass of Paper that has already been assigned and evaluated. Contribution subsumes Evaluated Paper since every evaluated paper is a contribution, but not vice versa.

In cmt, Administrator is a specific system role (a User who manages papers, reviewers, and conference details). In the Conference ontology, Organizer is a broader concept encompassing anyone involved in organizing the event. An Administrator is a type of organizer, but Organizer may also include chairs, committee members, etc., so they are related but not strictly equivalent.

In confOf, Tutorial is a type of Event (a working event like a conference or workshop). In ekaw, Tutorial Abstract is a type of Document (an abstract describing a tutorial). An event and a document about that event are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A (hasBeenAssigned) links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review, while property B (reviewOfPaper) links a Review document to the Paper it reviews. The domains differ (Reviewer vs Review) and the semantics differ (assignment vs authorship of a review), so they are unrelated.
Session is a type of scientific event (a time slot or meeting), while Author is a type of person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Review Question' in edas is a question used within a review form (with numerical/textual subtypes), whereas a 'Review' in ekaw is the actual review document written about a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Assigned Paper is a paper that has been assigned to reviewers (a stage in the review process), while Abstract is a summary document type. They are distinct concepts at different levels of the document hierarchy with different intended instances.

Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a registrant who paid late), while Deadline Paper Submission is a subclass of Deadline (a temporal deadline for submitting papers). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'accepted By' in cmt relates a Paper to an Administrator (indicating acceptance), while 'issues' in Conference relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (indicating publication). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
The properties have completely different semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered details, while 'hasEvent' links an Event to a sub-Event. They are unrelated.

Both properties link entities to events in the conference domain, but they differ in scope: edas:relatedToEvent specifically links an Accepted Paper to a Paper Presentation, while ekaw:hasEvent is a general property linking any Event to another Event. They are related but not equivalent.
Reception is a social event in confOf, while Invited Speaker is a type of person/role in sigkdd. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Government Organization is a type of organization. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants in a conference, with children Active and Passive participants. Demo Chair (B) is a specific role under Conference Participant in ekaw. Thus A subsumes B.

Tutorial in ekaw is a type of individual presentation/event at a conference, while Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

Both are datatype properties mapping entities to their string name. Despite slightly different domain unions (A covers Conference and Person; B covers Conference, Conference part, Conference proceedings, Publisher, Topic), they serve the same semantic role of providing a name for conference-domain entities. In ontology alignment, these naming properties are considered equivalent.

In edas, 'Accepted Paper' denotes a paper that has passed the review process (a status-based classification), with siblings like Rejected Paper and Pending Paper. In ekaw, 'Regular Paper' denotes a type/category of paper (e.g., full research paper vs. Demo Paper or Poster Paper), not its acceptance status. These are orthogonal dimensions of classification and do not denote the same concept.

Conference Participant in ekaw refers to people attending or organizing the conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants), while Sponsor in iasted refers to a person who sponsors/funds the conference. These are distinct roles with no subsumption relationship.
Conference Proceedings is a document/publication (subclass of Multi author Volume > Proceedings), while Conference building is a physical place/building. They are entirely different concepts.
Working event is a type of Event (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Organizator is a type of Person involved in organizing. These are entirely different concepts.
A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Best Research Paper Award' is an award given to a top paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

writtenBy links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their PersonalReviewHistory. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses.

A 'Track workshop chair' is a person who chairs a specific track or workshop within a conference, while B 'Chair PC' (Program Committee Chair) is the head of the entire program committee. Both are chair roles under Person, but they refer to different scopes and responsibilities, so they are related but not equivalent.

Entity A is a datatype property linking various entities to a string name, while Entity B is an object property linking an Organisation to published documents. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.
Wireless Communications Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee (a structural/organizational relation), while property B links an Organisation to something it technically organises (an event or activity). They involve different domains and ranges and express different directions of the organizing relationship, but are loosely related through the concept of organization.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference in ekaw is an event (one edition of a conference). They are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is a class representing a co-author of a contribution (a person role), while Entity B represents the contribution itself (a document/artefact such as a paper or poster). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an object property linking a Person to an Item (obtain), while property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a string (name). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference Banquet is a social event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
adjustedBy links a Bid to a Reviewer (who adjusted the bid), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Published Paper is a document (a paper that has been published), while Receiving manuscript is an activity/event (the act of receiving a manuscript). They belong to entirely different categories (Document vs Activity) and are unrelated.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while is_present relates a Person to a Time (indicating attendance). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Short paper is a type of contribution defined by its length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), while Initial manuscript is a submission stage (sibling of Final manuscript). They represent orthogonal dimensions: one is about document type/length, the other about the submission lifecycle stage.

Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They belong to entirely different categories and are not semantically equivalent or related in a hierarchical way.
Invited speaker is a subclass of Person (a conference contributor), while Presenter city is a subclass of City (a location). They represent entirely different concepts in the domain.

In edas, 'Coffee Break' is a specific type of break event. In iasted, 'Conference activity' is a general class whose children include 'Coffee break'. Therefore, edas:CoffeeBreak is subsumed by iasted:Conference_activity.

Chair PC in confOf is the chair/head of the program committee (a leadership role), while Program Committee member in sigkdd is a general member of the program committee. These are distinct roles; notably, sigkdd has 'Program Chair' as a sibling of 'Program Committee member', which would be the true equivalent of confOf's 'Chair PC'.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for anyone who contributes to a conference (authors, speakers, active participants), while Conference Chair in Ontology B is a specific leadership role responsible for chairing the conference and initiating calls. These are distinct concepts with different intended instances.

One property represents an abstract submission date (domain: Important dates, range: date) while the other represents a contact email (domain: Contribution, range: string). They describe entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Week Reject Rating is a type of review rating (a score/evaluation metric), while Rejected Paper is a paper that has been rejected. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories in the conference domain.

Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Important dates represents scheduling deadlines (submission dates, acceptance announcements, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasTitle is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its title string, while hasSubmissionInstructions links a Call to submission instruction text. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.
Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer), while Neutral Review in ekaw is a document (a type of review). They are entirely different concepts.

'parallel with' relates two Administrative events indicating they occur simultaneously, while 'has Call' links an Academic Event to a Call (e.g., call for papers). These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('gives presentations') has domain Active conference participant and range Presentation (participant -> presentation). Property B ('is given by') has domain Activity/Item and range Person (activity -> person), making it the inverse direction of A. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, and their domains/ranges differ in specificity, they are unrelated for alignment purposes.

In Ontology A, Poster is a subclass of Conference contribution with siblings including Presentation and Written contribution. In Ontology B, Paper is a subclass of Contribution with siblings including Poster and Short paper. Thus, Poster in A and Paper in B are distinct types of contributions; they are related as sibling concepts under the broader notion of conference contributions but are not equivalent.

hasConferenceMember relates Conference -> Conference Member, while isMemberOf relates Person -> Conference. They express the same membership relationship but in opposite directions (inverse properties), so they are related but not equivalent.
hasMember relates a Conference to its Person members, while writtenBy relates a Document to its Person author(s). Different domains and different semantic roles; they are unrelated.

An Invited speaker is a specific type of conference contributor who gives an invited talk, while an Attendee is a general participant at the conference. An invited speaker is typically also an attendee, but not all attendees are invited speakers. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

A Workshop is a scientific event consisting of interactive sessions on a specific topic, while a Plenary lecture is a single lecture delivered to all conference attendees. They are distinct types of conference activities with different intended instances.
Author is a Person who writes papers, while Form is a Document (e.g., registration form). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'has gender' captures a person's gender, while 'has First Name' captures a person's first name. These are entirely different attributes of a Person and do not denote the same relation.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (agent writes review), while is_writen_by relates an Item to a Person (passive authorship). They differ in direction, domain, range, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Pending Paper is a status of a paper (a Document), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Credit card is a payment item (subclass of Card), while Speaker is a person who presents at a conference. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

In EKAW, OC Member is specifically an Organizing Committee member (child of Conference Participant). In SIGKDD, Organizator is a broader class that includes General Chair, Organizing Committee member, Program Chair, Program Committee member, and Webmaster. Thus EKAW's OC Member corresponds to one specific child of SIGKDD's Organizator, making OC Member subsumed by Organizator.
Conference www is a web-related conference document (with a URL property), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasSurname is a datatype property linking a Person to their surname string, while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They are entirely different relations.
'has Home Page' refers to a person's web page URL, while 'Nation' refers to a person's country. They capture entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range types.

Sponzorship in iasted is a type of Money (a financial contribution/payment), while Gold Supporter in sigkdd is a specific tier/role of a Sponzor (an entity that sponsors). They are related through the sponsorship concept but differ in nature: one is a monetary amount, the other is a supporter role. Thus they are not equivalent.
Author is a Person who writes papers, while Deadline Author notification is a temporal Deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Contribution 1th author is a subclass of Regular author (a person who authored a contribution), while Presenter is a subclass of Conference Participant representing someone who presents at the conference. Although an author may also present, these classes model distinct roles and their intended instances do not coincide.

Both are subclasses of Speaker in their respective ontologies, but 'Author cd proceedings included' refers to an author whose paper is included in the CD proceedings (a publication-related role), while 'Invited Speaker' refers to a speaker invited to present (an event-related role). They overlap as speakers but denote different concepts.
Both are datatype properties with identical semantics: they link a Person to their last name as a string. Same domain (Person) and range (string).

The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'is Review History Of' relates a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'location' property in confOf specifies where an event is held (domain: events, range: string), while 'paperDueOn' in edas specifies a deadline date/time for paper submission (domain: Conference, range: dateTime). They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

In ekaw, Paper is a subclass of Document, while in sigkdd, Document is the superclass of Paper (along with Abstract and Review). Thus, ekaw:Paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Document; they are not equivalent since sigkdd:Document is more general.

Property A 'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document, while property B 'is writen by' has domain Item and range Person. They express inverse directions of a similar authorship/writing relationship (Person writes/contributes to Document vs Document is written by Person). Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related but not equivalent.
Review expertise refers to a reviewer's area of knowledge for evaluating papers, while Money is a financial concept with children like Fee and Tax. They are entirely unrelated.

Property A (isTopicOf) has domain Topic and range Conference/Paper, while property B (coversTopic) has domain Event/Paper and range Research Topic. They are inverses of each other: A links Topic -> Paper/Conference, B links Paper/Event -> Topic. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a document/artefact submitted to a conference (e.g., paper, poster, talk), while Conference in ekaw is an event (one edition of a conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Member in cmt is a person participating in the conference (subclass of Person), while Conference Dinner in edas is a meal event (subclass of Meal Event). They are entirely different concepts.
hasRelatedPaper links an Author to a Paper (authorship/association), while updatedVersionOf links a Document to a prior version of itself (versioning). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair in cmt is a role (a type of Chairman/Person), while Two Level Conference in edas is a type of Conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Committee member is a person role in conference organization, while Building is a physical place/structure. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference hall in iasted is a type of Place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Student is a subclass of Person representing an academic role, while Platinum Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor representing a funding tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Reviewer in cmt is a person who reviews papers (child of Conference Member), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person who gives presentations (parent of Author). These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.
Chair is a person role (committee chair) while Building is a physical place. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Written contribution is a type of conference document/artefact (subclass of Conference contribution), while Speaker is a type of Person who presents at the conference. They are fundamentally different concepts in the domain.

A Workshop is a type of academic event (typically a focused session or mini-conference), while a Speaker lecture is a specific type of session/lecture within a conference. These are distinct kinds of conference activities with different intended instances.

Both properties express the authorship/preparation relationship: 'writtenBy' links a Contribution to an Author in confOf, while 'is_prepared_by' links an Item (paper/submission) to a Person in iasted. In the conference domain these denote the same relation between a paper and its author.

Decision in cmt represents the outcome of a review (Acceptance/Rejection), while Submitted contribution in Conference represents a paper or document that has been submitted. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
University is an academic organization where scholars study, while Sponzorship is a type of financial contribution (Money). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties on Conference relating to dates, but 'date' in cmt is a generic date property while 'Start of conference' in sigkdd specifically denotes the start date. They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent.

In ontology A (cmt), Author is a subclass of Person (via Conference Member). In ontology B (iasted), Person is the top-level class for people. Therefore, cmt:Author is strictly more specific than iasted:Person, making it subsumed_by iasted:Person.
Written contribution is a type of conference document/paper, while Registration fee is a monetary fee for attending the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Associated Chair is a type of Chairman (organizational role), while Author is a person who writes papers/presentations. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Workshop is a type of working event in the conference domain, while Author book proceedings included is a role/type of author whose work appears in book proceedings. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Coffee break is a conference activity (event), while Main office is a place (location). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Reject Rating is a type of review rating (a score or assessment value), while Rejected Paper is a paper that has been rejected after evaluation. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (rating vs. document status) and are not equivalent.
Communications Topic is a subject area for papers in the edas ontology, while Transport vehicle is a physical item (car, bus, etc.) in the iasted ontology. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both represent shorter forms of conference contributions (siblings of Paper in their respective ontologies). However, an 'Extended abstract' and a 'Short paper' are distinct submission types in most conference management systems (e.g., confTool distinguishes them). They overlap conceptually as brief contributions but are not strictly equivalent.
hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic, while hasReview links a Paper to a Review. These are entirely different relations with different ranges and semantics.

In Ontology A, Abstract is a very specific leaf class (a subtype of Extended abstract). In Ontology B, Document is a broad superclass that includes Abstract as one of its children along with Paper, Review, etc. Therefore, the A:Abstract class is subsumed by the B:Document class.

Dining Place is a location for eating meals, while Conference hall is a venue for conference sessions. They are distinct types of places with different purposes; in edas the equivalent would be Meeting Room Place or Conference Venue Place.

Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Presenter city in iasted is a geographic location (subclass of City) associated with a presenter. They are entirely different concepts.
Talk Event is a type of conference event (activity), while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Invited speaker is a Person (a role played by an individual), while Tutorial is an Event (a type of presentation). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are unrelated.

In edas, 'Accepted Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing only papers that have been accepted. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (submitted by authors). Therefore, edas:AcceptedPaper is subsumed by sigkdd:Paper, as every accepted paper is a paper but not every paper is an accepted paper.

Property A ('added By') links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them, while property B ('has members') links a Committee to its Committee members. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion during a conference), while Car is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Break Event is a non-academic event for breaks (coffee, meals, free time), while Presentation is an academic activity for presenting work. They are conceptually distinct and unrelated.
Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee, while Property B links a Document to a Speaker. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasTopic relates a working event to its topic/subject matter, while go_through relates an item to an activity it undergoes. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

hasBid links a Paper to a Bid (a bidding action/record), while hasReviewer links a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (a person). These are fundamentally different relations with different ranges and semantics.

Topic in ontology A represents a subject area or theme of the conference, while Contribution in ontology B represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts; confOf even has its own separate Topic class that Contribution 'deals With'.
Workshop is a conference event/session type, while Van is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person (individuals who use the system such as authors, reviewers, administrators), while Organising Agency in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation (an entity that organises the conference). They represent fundamentally different concepts (person vs organisation) and are unrelated.

In cmt, 'Conference Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and is distinct from its sibling 'Program Committee Chair'. In confOf, 'Chair PC' (with comment 'confTool') refers to the Program Committee Chair. These are different roles in conference organization: the Conference Chair oversees the entire conference while the PC Chair leads the program committee. They are related as both are chair roles but not equivalent.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members, while Property B links a Track workshop chair to a Conference part. They involve entirely different domains, ranges, and roles within the conference organization.
'assignedTo' in cmt links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while 'hasPart' in ekaw is a generic mereological part-whole relation. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.

Property A 'name' has domain Conference and Person, while property B 'Name of conference' has domain only Conference. Both map to string. Therefore B is strictly more specific than A; A subsumes B (B is subsumed_by A).

Administrator is a person role (subclass of User) who manages the conference system, while Review is a document (subclass of Conference document) that evaluates a contribution. They are entirely different concepts.

An 'Invited Talk Abstract' is a summary of an invited talk (a type of abstract), while an 'Invitation letter' is a formal letter inviting someone to attend or participate in the conference. These are entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.

A Closing Talk is a specific type of talk event that concludes a conference, while Introduction of speaker is an activity where a speaker is introduced. These are distinct conference activities with different purposes and instances.

In cmt, Paper is a general class (child of Document) representing any paper. In ekaw, Assigned_Paper is a much more specific subclass of Paper (Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper), representing only papers that have been assigned for review. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Assigned_Paper.
isMenuOf relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no semantic overlap.

hasCity is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (city name), while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for submitted papers (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version). In edas, Published Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing papers that have been published. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes edas:PublishedPaper.

Both properties link a paper/contribution that has been reviewed to its review. 'Reviewed contribution' in Conference and 'Paper' in ekaw serve the same role as the domain (a paper that has received a review), and both have 'Review' as range. They express the same relation in the conference domain.

Location in ekaw is a generic spatial/place class where events are held. ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd represents the specific organizing body/conference series that holds conferences, designs deadlines, and searches for sponsors. These are entirely different concepts.

A 'Full day tour' is an activity/event occurring after a conference, while a 'Conference hall' is a physical place/venue. They belong to entirely different categories (Activity vs Place) and are unrelated.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who performed the assignment), while reviewerOfPaper links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (the paper they review). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Social Event is a type of event (e.g., banquet, trip) while Organizator is a type of person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

OperatingTopicsystems is a subclass of Topic representing a subject area in the conference, while Invited Talk Abstract is a subclass of Abstract (Document) representing a written summary for an invited talk. These are entirely different concepts.
Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging, while Worker lecturer is a person role (a type of lecturer). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
has an email and has Surname are both datatype properties on Person with string range, but they capture entirely different attributes (email address vs. family name). They are unrelated.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country (spatial/geographic), while is_held_after links an Activity to a Time (temporal). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Entity A is an event (a type of administrative activity for participant registration), while Entity B is a fee (a monetary amount to be paid). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories in the conference domain.
assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (paper assignment), while searched_by relates a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD (sponsor search). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing the start date. They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain, range, and semantic meaning.

Both properties relate a person role (Person/Speaker) to a document artefact (Conference document/Document). However, 'contributes' is broader (a person can contribute by authoring without presenting), while 'presentation' specifically denotes delivering a presentation. Speaker subsumes/is a kind of Person in this context, and presenting is a specific form of contributing, so they are related but not equivalent.

'has a degree' is a datatype property on Review preference with range int, while 'has Surname' is a datatype property on Person with range string. They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.
Accepted contribution is a type of conference paper/contribution that has been accepted, while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are entirely different concepts.

In confOf, 'Conference' is a type of working event (an activity), whereas in iasted, 'Conference building' is a physical place/building where the conference takes place. They represent fundamentally different concepts (event vs. venue).

Both classes represent the same general concept of an organization/organisation in the conference domain. Despite slightly different children (Academia Organization vs Academic Institution, etc.) and different associated properties (sponsorship vs publishing/organising), they both serve as the top-level class for organizational entities involved in conferences. The spelling difference (Organization vs Organisation) is merely a regional variant.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer (reviewing context), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (presentation context). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

setMaxPapers is an administrative action linking an Administrator to a Program Committee Member to set a paper limit, while is_given_to links an Item to a Person indicating something is given to them. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (individual participants), while Property B links an Organizing Committee to the Conference volume it organizes. They have different domains, ranges, and directions of relationship, making them unrelated.

The properties have completely different domains (Paper vs Award) and semantics: 'accepted By' links a paper to an administrator who accepts it, while 'awarded by' links an award to its granter. They are unrelated.

Working event in confOf (parent of Conference, Tutorial, Workshop) represents scientific/working activities, while Social Event in ekaw (parent of Conference Banquet, Conference Trip) represents social activities. They are disjoint sibling categories under Event in their respective ontologies.

Both properties link a conference paper/contribution to its author(s). 'Conference document' aligns with 'Contribution', and 'Person' (in the context of has authors) aligns with 'Author'. They express the same relation in the same direction.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'is sent by' relates an Item to a Person (the sender). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Short paper is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), while Final manuscript is a submission classified by its stage in the review process (sibling of Initial manuscript). They represent orthogonal dimensions and are not equivalent.

'has the first name' is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their first name), while 'obtain' is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have completely different semantics, ranges, and purposes.

hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime representing a deadline, while is_sent_after is an object property linking an Item to a Time indicating when something was sent. They have different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'holded by' relates a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

'is given by' links a Presentation to an Active conference participant (the presenter), while 'is used by' links an Item to a Person (a user). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an organized gathering), while Tutorial speaker in iasted is a person/role who speaks at a tutorial. These are entirely different concepts.
Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite unusual parentage), while OC Chair in ekaw is a person role (Organizing Committee Chair). They denote entirely different concepts.

Conference Banquet in ekaw is a specific type of social event (a banquet), while Social program in iasted is a broader category that includes Dinner banquet as a child class. Thus Conference Banquet is subsumed by Social program.

Working event in confOf refers to academic activities like conferences, tutorials, and workshops, while Deadline in sigkdd refers to temporal submission/notification deadlines. These are entirely different concepts.

In the conference domain, 'hasAuthor' (Paper -> Author) and 'is prepared by' (Item -> Person) express the same relationship: linking a scholarly work to its creator. Item corresponds to Paper and Person corresponds to Author in this context.
Meal Event is a type of conference event (a meal), while Speaker is a type of person who presents. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Review in cmt is a document (subclass of Document) representing the written evaluation of a paper. Member PC in confOf is a person (subclass of Person) who acts as a reviewer/committee member. One is an artefact, the other is a role held by a person; they are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while Property B links a Conference volume to a Committee (organizational structure). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Track is a conference organizational unit (part of a conference), while Car is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.
'remark' is a string-valued datatype property on Contribution for textual notes, while 'Date' is a dateTime-valued datatype property on Deadline. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Workshop and a Tutorial are distinct types of academic events. In edas, Workshop is a sibling of Talk Event under Academic Event, while in ekaw, Tutorial is a type of Individual Presentation. They represent different concepts in the conference domain.

Industry Organization is a type of organization (a company or business entity), while Sponsor state is a type of state (geopolitical entity) associated with a sponsor. They belong to entirely different class hierarchies and represent fundamentally different concepts.

submitPaper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while is_a_date_of_camera_ready_paper_submission is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Property A (acceptedBy) links a Paper to an Administrator indicating acceptance, while property B (writes) links an Author to a Contribution indicating authorship. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Extended abstract in Ontology A is a type of regular contribution (a short paper format), while Pending Paper in Ontology B is a status-based subclass of Paper indicating a paper awaiting a decision. They differ both in document type and classification axis (format vs. submission status), so they are unrelated.

In cmt, Chairman is a general class with children including Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair, and Associated Chair. In edas, Session Chair is a specific role (a sibling of Conference Chair). Therefore, the cmt Chairman class subsumes the edas Session Chair concept, as a session chair is one type of chairman.
Paper is a conference contribution (a document), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'isInitiatedBy' links a Call to the person who initiated it (Conference Chair, etc.), while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. The domains, ranges, and directions are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.
hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic, while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Presenter in edas is a general class for anyone who presents (a subclass of Author). Plenary lecture speaker in iasted is a very specific type of speaker/author who gives a plenary lecture. Every plenary lecture speaker is a presenter, but not every presenter is a plenary lecture speaker, so Presenter subsumes Plenary lecture speaker.

Conference Paper is a type of document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Best Paper Awards Committee is an organizational body (a committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'held In' relates an Event to a Location. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In edas, 'Conference Event' is a broad class encompassing both Academic and Non-Academic events (sessions, social events, etc.) within a conference. In ekaw, 'Conference' specifically denotes one edition of the overall conference itself (a Scientific Event), with siblings like Session, Track, and Workshop representing sub-events. Thus, edas Conference Event is broader and overlaps with ekaw Conference but also includes non-academic events; they are related but not equivalent.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Tip is a monetary gratuity (subclass of Money). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume (structural containment), while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing its end date. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

NGO is a type of organization (Non-Governmental Organization), while Organizing Committee is a specific committee responsible for organizing a conference. They belong to different branches of the domain hierarchy and denote entirely different concepts.

In cmt, ExternalReviewer is explicitly defined as someone who reviews a paper on behalf of another Reviewer but is NOT themselves a Reviewer (cmt has a separate Reviewer class). In edas, Reviewer is the general class for anyone who reviews papers. Thus they are not equivalent; they overlap in that both perform reviewing activities, but ExternalReviewer is a more specific role distinct from the primary reviewer.

hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu, while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
hasEvent relates an Event to a sub-Event in ekaw, while awarded_by relates an Award to its awarding entity in sigkdd. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, User is a general class (child of Person) with subclasses Administrator, Author, and Reviewer. In confOf, Member PC specifically represents a program committee member/reviewer (as indicated by its comment 'Reviewer' and properties like 'reviewes'). Thus, cmt:User subsumes confOf:Member_PC because Member_PC corresponds to one specific role (Reviewer) under the broader User class.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a membership/leadership relation), while Property B links a Speaker to a Document they present. These relate entirely different domain concepts and serve different purposes.

Property A is a specific datatype property linking 'Important dates' to a full paper submission date, while Property B is a general datatype property linking an 'Activity' to a dateTime. They have different domains, different levels of specificity, and different intended meanings in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property linking Activity/Person to Item/Place, while Property B is a datatype property linking Person to a string name. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Chairman is a person role (a type of Person who chairs something), while Registration is a conference activity/event. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Contribution in confOf represents a scholarly submission (paper, poster, short paper) with properties like abstract, title, and author. Sponsorship in edas represents financial support (e.g., travel grants) with cost and provider properties. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review. These are distinct relations with different ranges and semantics in the conference domain.

publisherOf relates an Organisation to published materials (Flyer, Programme Brochure, etc.), while submit relates an Author to a Paper. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Switching), while B is an organizational committee. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent events occurring at a conference. edas 'Conference Event' has children 'Academic Event' and 'Non Academic Event', while ekaw 'Event' has children 'Scientific Event' and 'Social Event'. Both share similar properties such as location (hasLocation/heldIn), programme association, and part-of relations. They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference part to a Conference volume, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime value representing its start date. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, and range.

Workshop in edas is a type of conference event (an activity/session), while Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (an abstract for a tutorial). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document indicating a conflict of interest, while hasCity relates an Organization or Person to a City indicating location. These are entirely different relations.
'is Written By' denotes authorship (Paper -> Author), while 'is sent by' denotes a submission/sending action (Item -> Person). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.
The 'email' property maps a Person to a string (email address), while 'has amount of' maps Money to an int (monetary amount). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person who participates in a conference, while Conference in ekaw is an Event (a scientific event). These are entirely different concepts.

confOf:Person is a general class for all people involved in the conference (with children including Author, Participant, Administrator, etc.), while sigkdd:Author is a specific subclass of Speaker (which is itself a subclass of Person). Therefore, confOf:Person strictly subsumes sigkdd:Author.

'has a name' is a datatype property mapping entities to their string names, while 'Start of conference' maps a Conference to a dateTime indicating when it starts. They represent entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered its details, while 'isTopicOf' links a Topic to a Conference or Paper that the topic pertains to. They are unrelated.
isMenuOf links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (menu-to-event), while partOfEvent links an Event to another Event (event-to-event). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
SC Member is a person role (Steering Committee member) in the conference organization, while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Conference applicant' is a sibling of 'Conference participant', meaning it specifically denotes someone who has applied/registered but is distinct from a general participant. In Ontology B, 'Conference Participant' is a broad class encompassing all attendees including chairs and presenters. Thus they overlap (an applicant may become a participant) but are not equivalent; 'Conference applicant' is more specific in intent than the broad 'Conference Participant'.

Camera Ready Paper is a type of document (a final version of a paper), while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference in cmt denotes the conference event/organization itself, while Participant in confOf denotes a person attending or involved in the conference (subclass of Person). These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent sponsorship in the conference domain. 'Sponzorship' in iasted is a clear typographical variant of 'Sponsorship' in edas. Although iasted places it under Money (reflecting its financial aspect) and edas links it to organizations and costs, their intended instances (sponsorships provided for a conference) coincide.

Passive conference participant (A) refers to attendees who do not actively present or chair, while Late Registered Participant (B) refers to participants who registered after a deadline. A late-registered participant could be active or passive. They overlap conceptually as types of conference participants but are not equivalent; they capture different dimensions (role vs. registration timing).

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while University in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation representing an academic institution. These are entirely different concepts.

Sponsorship in edas represents financial support provided by an organization (with children like Travel Grant), while Fee in sigkdd represents a cost to be paid (with children like Registration fee and Sponsor fee). They are related through the concept of conference finances but denote different things: one is a provision of funds, the other is a charge.

Property A is the inverse of 'has organizing committee' linking an Organizing Committee to a Conference volume. Property B ('technicallyOrganisedBy') is a sub-property of 'organisedBy' in ekaw, likely linking an event to its technical organizer (e.g., a Technical Program Committee). Both concern organizational roles for conference events, but they differ in directionality (A goes from committee to event, B goes from event to organizer) and specificity (A is about organizing committees generally, B is specifically about technical organization). They are related but not equivalent.

In iasted, Listener is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee who listens to presentations). In sigkdd, Organizator is a person who organizes the conference (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). These are distinct roles: one is an audience member, the other is an organizer. They are unrelated.

In confOf, Contribution is a general class for submitted works (Paper, Poster, Short paper) with properties like title, abstract text, keywords, and authors. In ekaw, Abstract is a specific Document subclass representing the abstract of an invited talk or tutorial, not the submitted contribution itself. These are conceptually distinct: one is a full submission artefact, the other is a summary document type.
hasSubjectArea links a Paper to a Subject Area (topic classification), while can_stay_in links a Person to a Place (accommodation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Rejection is a type of Decision about a paper, while Listener is a type of Person attending a conference. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Nonauthor registration fee is a type of monetary fee for non-authors. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Attendee in edas is a Person who attends the conference, while Record of attendance in iasted is a Document (an artefact recording that someone attended). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and thus unrelated.

'organised By' relates an Event to its organizing Organisation or Person, while 'is occupied by' relates a physical location (Building, City, State) to a Person occupying it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and semantics.

acceptsHardcopySubmissions is a boolean property indicating whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions, while hasName is a string property for the conference's full name. They describe entirely different attributes.

An 'Extended abstract' is a short regular contribution (a type of abstract), while a 'Demo Paper' is a paper accompanying a demonstration. They are distinct types of conference submissions with different intended instances.
Both classes are named 'Review' and are subclasses of 'Document' in their respective conference ontologies. They represent the same concept: a review document of a paper/submission.

relatesTo has domain Document and range including Person/Event, while presentation has domain Speaker (a Person) and range Document. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses (inverse of relatesTo would have domain Person/Event and range Document).
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Regular Session is a type of event/session. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the call for submissions (a solicitation), whereas in Ontology B, 'Paper' is an actual submitted contribution/document. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

'has the first name' is a datatype property for a person's first name, while 'Currency' is a datatype property for the currency of a registration fee. They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.

earlyRegistration is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating whether they registered early, while Currency is a string datatype property on Registration fee indicating the currency of the fee. They describe entirely different concepts and have different domains and ranges.
Conference participant is a person attending the conference, while Conference Dinner is a meal event at the conference. They are entirely different concepts (person vs. event).
Chairman is a person role in conference organization, while Fee for extra trip is a monetary charge. They are completely unrelated concepts.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (informational material), while 'Tutorial' is a working event (a session at the conference). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Review in ontology A is a document (subclass of Conference document) representing the written evaluation of a paper, while Reviewer in ontology B is a person (subclass of Person) who performs the reviewing. They are fundamentally different concepts (artefact vs. agent).
Tutorial is a type of conference event/part, while Speaker is a role played by a person. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In iasted, 'Building' is a superclass of various venue buildings and has 'Main office' as a sibling. In sigkdd, 'Main office' is a direct subclass of Place (sibling to Conference hall and Hotel). Since Building in iasted subsumes Main office rather than being equivalent to it, and the sigkdd Main office corresponds to the iasted sibling Main office, these two classes are unrelated.

In Ontology A, 'Passive conference participant' is a subclass of 'Conference participant'. In Ontology B (ekaw), 'Conference Participant' is the general class for all participants (including chairs, presenters, etc.). Therefore, the more specific 'Passive conference participant' from A is subsumed by the broader 'Conference Participant' in B.
Property A gives the last name of a Person, while property B provides submission instructions for a Call. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Computer Networks Sensor Topic is a subject area/topic within the computer networks domain. They are entirely different concepts.

endDate in edas has domain Conference and represents the conference end date/time, while Date in sigkdd has domain Deadline and represents a deadline date. Different domains and different semantics make them unrelated.

The 'email' property represents an email address of a Person, while 'has the last name' represents the surname/last name of a Person. These are entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range.
Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging, while Student non speaker is a type of conference delegate (person). They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place), while Hotel fee is a monetary charge (subclass of Fee). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Regular contribution in Ontology A is a type of conference document/artefact (with children like Paper and Extended abstract), while Author in Ontology B is a person who submits papers. These are fundamentally different concepts (document vs. person) and are unrelated.

Property A (memberOfProgramCommittee) links a Program Committee Member to the Program Committee they belong to, while property B (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they review. Different domains/ranges and entirely different semantics.

confOf 'Member PC' is a regular program committee member (comment: Reviewer), while ekaw 'PC Chair' is the chair of the program committee. In ekaw, PC Chair is a subclass of PC Member, so they are not equivalent. confOf has a separate 'Chair PC' class for the chair role. Thus 'Member PC' and 'PC Chair' are related but distinct roles.

'has the last name' captures a person's surname (domain: Person), while 'has Phone' captures a phone number (domain: Contact Information). They represent entirely different attributes with different domains and semantics.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its Conference Members, while isTopicOf relates a Topic to a Conference or Paper. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference www represents a conference website/web document with a URL, while Hotel registration form is a specific form for hotel registration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific type of Chairman (a role within the conference committee hierarchy), while Administrator in confOf is a general administrative role directly under Person. They overlap in that both are organizational/administrative roles, but they are not equivalent: Associated Chair is more specific and tied to chairing duties, whereas Administrator is a broader or different administrative function.

confOf:Participant is a general class for all conference participants (with children Member, Regular, Student and a property 'early Registration'). ekaw:Early-Registered_Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant denoting only those who registered early. Therefore, Participant subsumes Early Registered Participant.

Written contribution refers to a scholarly paper or document submitted to a conference, while Card in the iasted ontology refers to a physical card (e.g., credit card) as an item. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference Chair is a leadership role in organizing a conference, while Author book proceedings included is a specific type of author whose work appears in the conference proceedings. These are entirely different concepts.

Workshop and Tutorial are distinct types of conference activities. In Ontology A they are siblings under Conference part, and in Ontology B Tutorial is a subclass of Lecture. They do not denote the same concept.
Conference Venue Place is a physical location for the conference, while Student non speaker is a type of delegate (person) who is a student and not presenting. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment of review duties), while search relates ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (searching for sponsors). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

An 'Invited speaker' is a person invited to give a talk at a conference, while a 'Reviewer' is a person who reviews submitted papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Property A 'send' relates a Person to an Item (sending documents/materials), while property B 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person (payment). They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Program committee, while Property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

finalizePaperAssignment is a specific administrative action linking an Administrator to a Conference for finalizing paper assignments, while prepare is a generic property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in domain, range, and intended semantics.

isReviewedBy (edas) has domain Paper and range Reviewer/Chair/etc., while reviewerOfPaper (ekaw) has domain Possible Reviewer and range Paper. They are inverse properties of each other, not equivalent. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are related.

Presenter in edas is a Person (specifically an Author who presents), while Presenter university in iasted is a Place/Building (the university affiliated with a presenter). They are entirely different kinds of entities.
Conference Member is a person role in a conference, while Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Student is a person role in the conference domain, while Van is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Submitted contribution in Ontology A is a specific type of written conference contribution that has been submitted (and may be reviewed). Document in sigkdd is a very broad class encompassing Abstract, Paper, and Review. While a Submitted contribution is a kind of document/paper, the sigkdd Document class also includes Reviews and Abstracts, making it much more general. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

Tutorial in Ontology A is a conference event/part (a session), while Tutorial speaker in Ontology B is a person (role) who presents at a tutorial. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (event vs. person).

In cmt, Document is a general class for conference artefacts (with children Paper and Review). In edas, ReviewQuestion refers to specific questions used in the review form (with children NumericalReviewQuestion and TextualReviewQuestion). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'give' has domain Person and range Activity/Item (a person gives an activity or item), while property B 'presentationed by' has domain Document and range Speaker (a document is presented by a speaker). The domains, ranges, and directions are fundamentally different; they do not express the same relation.
Conference participant is a Person who attends the conference, while Conference Venue Place is a Place where the conference is held. They are entirely different concepts.

Co author (cmt) refers to any co-author of a paper, while Contribution 1th author (Conference) specifically denotes the first/primary author of a contribution. They are related as both are author roles but not equivalent; the Conference ontology even has a separate sibling class 'Contribution co author' that would be closer to cmt's Co author.

Acceptance in cmt is a subclass of Decision (the final outcome), while Accpet If Room Rating in edas is a subclass of Review Rating (an individual reviewer's score). They are related in that both concern accepting a paper, but they represent different concepts: a final decision vs. a reviewer rating.
A Programme Brochure lists conference events/sessions, while a Hotel registration form is used for accommodation registration. They are entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.

Both classes represent papers submitted to or presented at a conference. In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution (alongside Poster and Short paper). In ekaw, Conference Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is under Document) with siblings like Regular Paper, Poster Paper, etc. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances—papers for the conference—are the same.

Assistant in confOf is a support/administrative role under Person (sibling to Administrator, Volunteer, etc.), while Reviewer in iasted is an academic reviewing role under Speaker/Delegate. These are distinct roles with different intended instances and no hierarchical overlap.
partOfEvent relates an Event to a containing Event (mereological), while need relates a Person to an Item they require. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A 'pay' has domain Person and range Money (Person pays Money), while property B 'payed by' has domain Registration fee and range Person (Registration fee is paid by Person). They describe the same payment concept but with different domains/ranges and are near-inverses of each other, not equivalent.

cmt:Person is a general class for all people in the conference domain, while confOf:Member_PC is specifically a Program Committee member (a subclass of confOf:Person). Thus cmt:Person subsumes confOf:Member_PC.

In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person representing anyone attending the conference. In iasted, Conference Hiker is a specific type of Delegate (which itself corresponds to Attendee), implying someone who hikes or tours during the conference. Thus, Conference Hiker is a more specific concept subsumed by the general Attendee class.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a banquet held during a conference), while Sponsor city is a type of city (the city of a sponsor). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (domain: Conference part, range: Topic), while Property B links a Research Topic to an Event or Paper (domain: Topic, range: Event/Paper). They are roughly inverse in direction and differ in domain/range specificity, so they are related but not equivalent.
Conference contributor is a subclass of Person (a role played by people), while Lecture is a subclass of Conference activity (an event). They are entirely different concepts.

Conference volume in Ontology A represents a specific edition/instance of a conference (with committees, tracks, contributions, etc.), while Conference hall in Ontology B is a physical place/venue where the conference is held. These are entirely different concepts.

'contributes' has domain Person and range Conference document (Person -> Document), while 'isWrittenBy' has domain Paper and range Author (Document -> Person). They express inverse directions of a similar authorship/writing relationship, so they are related but not equivalent.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (event/organization), while Reviewer in iasted is a person role (subclass of Speaker/Delegate). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while pay relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

scientificallyOrganises relates an Academic Institution to something it organizes scientifically, while occupy relates a Person to a physical location (Building, City, State). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Property A links a Committee to a Conference volume, while property B links a Contribution to an Author. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Company is an organization type (business entity), while Van is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
University is an academic organization/institution, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain with no meaningful overlap.

confOf:Event is a general class for all events (with children Administrative event, Social event, Working event), while edas:MealEvent is a specific type of non-academic conference event. Thus Event subsumes MealEvent.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution), while ekaw:Accepted_Paper is a specific subclass of Paper that has gone through submission, assignment, evaluation, and acceptance. Thus confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Accepted_Paper.

Administrative event in confOf is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Active Paper in edas is a document/paper that is currently under review. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has workshops' is a mereological part-whole relation linking a conference volume to its workshop components, whereas 'organised By' links an event to the organisation or person that organises it. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

SC Member is a person role (Steering Committee member) in the conference organization hierarchy, while Registration Student is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

endReview links a Program Committee Chair to a Review (likely to mark the end of a review process), while reviewWrittenBy links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (indicating authorship). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Review expertise in Ontology A is a class representing the level or area of expertise of a reviewer (a skill/attribute concept), while Member PC in Ontology B is a person who serves on the program committee (a role/person concept). Despite both being related to reviewing, they denote fundamentally different kinds of entities.

In sigkdd, Registration fee is a subclass of Fee (with sibling Sponzor fee), meaning it specifically covers registration costs. Conference fees in the Conference ontology is a broader term encompassing all conference-related fees, including but not limited to registration. Thus Conference fees subsumes Registration fee.
Submitted Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while Transport vehicle refers to physical vehicles (cars, buses, etc.). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Country in edas represents a geopolitical entity (used as the location of a conference), while Person in sigkdd represents a human being (listener, organizer, speaker). These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a reviewer's preference regarding topics or submissions for review purposes. In the cmt ontology, Preference captures reviewer preferences, and in the Conference ontology, Review preference serves the same role (linked to reviewers, topics, and submitted contributions with a degree). They denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Company (a commercial organization) and University (an academic institution) are distinct types of organizations in the conference domain. They do not share instances and are not in a subsumption relationship with each other.

Published Paper (edas) and Rejected Paper (ekaw) represent disjoint states in the paper lifecycle. A published paper has been accepted and made public, while a rejected paper was not accepted. They are siblings under different hierarchies but denote mutually exclusive concepts.

In confOf, Administrator is a broad role under Person (with comment 'confTool') covering system/tool administration, with siblings like Assistant and Volunteer. In sigkdd, General Chair is a specific leadership role under Organizator, responsible for overall conference organization. They are not equivalent; they overlap loosely as organizational roles but differ significantly in scope and specificity.

External Reviewer is a person assigned to review a paper on behalf of another reviewer, while Conference Chair is the person who chairs/organizes the conference. These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

confOf:location is a datatype property mapping an event to a string (the place name), while ekaw:locationOf is an object property mapping a Location individual to an Event. They capture the same domain concept (where an event takes place) but differ in type (datatype vs object), direction (event→string vs location→event), and modeling approach, so they are related rather than equivalent.
hasCountry links Organizations and Persons to a Country, while is_held_in links Activities (events) to a Place/Time. Different domains, ranges, and intended semantics.

In iasted, Speaker is a general class (child of Delegate) with many subtypes including Author and Reviewer. In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a specific subtype of Speaker. The general Speaker class in iasted subsumes the more specific Invited Speaker class in sigkdd.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations: 'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator (who added them), while 'organised By' links an Event to an Organisation or Person (who organised it). They are unrelated.

Program Committee Member in cmt is a person who reviews papers and serves on the program committee, while Author in iasted is a speaker who authored a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain.

A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Measurements) while B is a research activity (Simulating). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.
'hasPart' is a generic mereological property indicating parthood, while 'award' is a specific property linking something to an Award. They have completely different semantics and are unrelated.
Accepted Paper is a document/artefact (a paper that has been accepted), while Author is a person who writes papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a subclass of Chairman (a leadership role), while Program Committee member in sigkdd is a general committee member role under Organizator.
