hasName refers to the full name of a conference, while City_of_conference refers to the city where the conference is held. These are distinct properties with different meanings.
An 'Invited speaker' is a person who speaks at the conference, while 'Worker non speaker' explicitly denotes a non-speaking worker. These are disjoint concepts.
Camera Ready Paper is a type of document (a paper), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a type of deadline (a point in time). They are fundamentally different concepts and thus unrelated.
hasBeenAssigned links a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment relation), while hasReview links a Paper to a Review (document relation). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Reviewer in Ontology A is a Person who reviews papers, while Review in Ontology B is a Document (the review artefact itself). They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. document) and thus unrelated.
belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, while give links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'add Program Committee Member' in cmt specifically relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (adding them to the committee). The property 'give' in iasted is a general relation from a Person to an Activity or Item. These have different domains, ranges, and semantics, making them unrelated.

Two Level Conference is a type of conference (subclass of Conference), while Sponsor state is a type of state (subclass of State) representing the status or location of a sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference to its individual Conference Members (people), while Property B links a Conference volume to a Steering committee (a group/committee). The domains and ranges differ significantly: one targets individual members, the other targets an organizational committee. They are not equivalent.

Property A (readPaper) relates a Reviewer to a Paper they read, while Property B (belongs_to_reviewers) relates a Review expertise or preference to a Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference www is a web document/URL resource (subclass of Conference document), while Conference restaurant is a physical place/building where meals are served. They share only the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

TPC Member (Technical Program Committee Member) in edas and SC Member (Steering/Program Committee Member) in ekaw both represent members of the conference program committee responsible for reviewing papers. Despite slightly different naming conventions across the two ontologies, they denote the same role in the conference domain.

maxChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positive integer (maximum number of choices), while Start_of_conference links a Conference to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

email is a datatype property for an email address (domain: Person), while hasPostalCode is a datatype property for a postal code (domain: Contact Information). They represent entirely different pieces of contact information.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) corresponds to PC Chair in ekaw, which is listed as a sibling of Session Chair. A Program Committee Chair oversees the review process and program committee, while a Session Chair chairs a specific session at the conference. They are related as both are chair roles within a conference but are not equivalent.
A 'Call for paper' is a conference document soliciting submissions, while a 'Short paper' is a type of contribution/submission. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'scientifically Organised By' relates an entity to an academic institution that organises it scientifically. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

In ekaw, 'Submitted Paper' is a general paper that has been submitted (with child 'Assigned Paper'), representing any stage after submission. In iasted, 'Final manuscript' is explicitly contrasted with 'Initial manuscipt' as a sibling under 'Submission', indicating it is the final/camera-ready version of a manuscript. These represent different stages in the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent, though they are related as both are types of submitted documents.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., a written notice), while Welcome Talk is a specific type of talk event at a conference. They belong to entirely different categories (document vs. event) and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subtype of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper, while Poster in confOf is a type of Contribution (a presentation format). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Regular Paper in ekaw is a specific type of academic paper (subclass of Paper). Document in iasted is a broad category including forms, invitation letters, payment documents, etc. They are not equivalent; Regular Paper does not subsume Document nor vice versa. While Submission in iasted might relate to papers, the Document class itself is far too general and different in scope to be related to Regular Paper.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to the conference (e.g., author, speaker), while Non Academic Event is a subclass of Conference Event representing social or break events. They are entirely different concepts (person vs event) with no semantic overlap.
'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while 'send' links a Person to an Item (communication/transmission relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference for setting review criteria, while 'invites co reviewers' links a Reviewer to another Reviewer for inviting co-reviewers. They are unrelated.
hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while hasUpdatedVersion links a Document to a newer version of that Document. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In iasted, 'Final manuscript' is a specific type of Submission (contrasted with 'Initial manuscipt'), representing the camera-ready version of a paper. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a general document class that authors submit. A Final manuscript is a kind of Paper, but not all Papers are final manuscripts (some may be initial submissions). Therefore, Final manuscript is subsumed by Paper.
hasBid relates a Paper to a Bid (bidding process), while obtain relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic, while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.

In the Conference ontology, 'Reviewed contribution' is a specific subclass of 'Submitted contribution' (which itself descends from 'Conference contribution'), representing papers that have undergone review. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a sibling of 'Abstract' and 'Review' under 'Document', serving as the general class for submitted papers. While both represent the paper artefact in a conference context, 'Reviewed contribution' is more specific (post-review) than the general 'Paper' class. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial alignment.

A 'Submission event' is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), while B 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal deadline (the date by which submissions must be made). They are closely related in the conference domain but denote different kinds of entities (event vs. time point), so they are not equivalent.
Conference Chair in cmt is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Conference in sigkdd is the event itself. They are entirely different concepts.

Co-chair in Ontology A is a committee member who co-chairs a committee (with Chair as sibling), while Program Chair in Ontology B specifically chairs the program committee/program. They are related leadership roles but not equivalent: Co-chair is more generic and could apply to any committee, whereas Program Chair is specific to the program. Neither strictly subsumes the other.

'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (a membership/affiliation relation), while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item (an action of providing/presenting). These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics, making them unrelated.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Meal Event is a type of conference event involving food. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both properties relate a person/author to a conference document/contribution they authored. 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) and 'writes' (Author -> Contribution) express the same authorship relation in the conference domain, with Author being a subclass of Person and Contribution equivalent to Conference document.

Property A gives the volume number (int) of conference proceedings, while property B gives the name (string) of a conference. They describe entirely different attributes with different domains and ranges.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Sponsor company house in iasted is a type of building (a physical place). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Both classes share the identical label 'Main office', the same parent class 'Place', and represent the same concept of a main administrative office within the conference venue context.
Paper is a scholarly contribution (document), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Medicine Topic is a subject area (a subclass of Topic). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Program Committee Chair in cmt is a person role (subclass of Chairman and Program Committee Member), whereas Program committee in Conference is an organizational body (subclass of Committee). A chair is a member/leader of a committee, not the committee itself.
Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while CAD Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

One is a datatype property linking a review preference to an integer degree, the other is an object property linking a paper to its review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, University is an Organization where scholars study. In iasted, Presenter university is a Building (a physical place/venue) grouped with hotels, airports, and restaurants. They model fundamentally different concepts (organization vs. physical building) in different hierarchies.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an abstract submission date, while Property B is an object property linking a location to an event. They describe entirely different concepts and relations in the conference domain.

Property A ('invited by') relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while property B ('review Written By') relates a Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

writtenBy links a Review to its Reviewer (authorship of a review), while presentation links a Speaker to a Document (delivering a presentation). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Departure is a post-conference activity/event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

memberOfConference relates a Conference Member to a Conference (membership), while isLocationOf relates a Place to a Conference Event (location). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (track/workshop/tutorial topic), while Property B links a Speaker to a Document (presentation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A relates a Steering committee to a Conference volume (committee-of-conference relation), while Property B relates a Person to a Conference (membership relation). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Review is a document type (subclass of Document). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.

'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its Conference parts (a mereological relation), while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (an authorship relation). These are entirely different properties with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'name' is a datatype property for the name of a Conference or Person, while 'Nation' is a datatype property for the nationality/country of a Person. They represent entirely different attributes and are unrelated.

Property A is a datatype property linking Deadline to a date value, while Property B is an object property linking Author to a Deadline entity. They have different domains, ranges, and property types, making them unrelated.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is used by' relates an Item to a Person (usage). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Chair PC (Program Committee Chair) in confOf is a senior academic role responsible for the scientific program, whereas Webmaster in sigkdd is a technical/organizational role responsible for the conference website. These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

'has authors' links a conference document to its authoring persons, while 'payed by' links a registration fee to the person who paid it. The domains (document vs. fee) and semantics are entirely different.
Review is a document representing an evaluation of a paper, while Tax is a type of money/financial charge. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
hasVAT is a datatype property for value added tax (string) on events, while is_dated_on is a datatype property for the date/time of an activity. They represent completely different concepts.

In iasted, 'Technical commitee' is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference), listed alongside roles like Session chair and Speaker. In sigkdd, 'Organizator' is a subclass of Person representing organizing roles (General Chair, Program Committee member, etc.). While both represent people involved in conference organization/committee work, they come from different modeling hierarchies (Delegate vs Person) and have different scopes: Technical committee is one specific role, whereas Organizator is a broader category encompassing multiple organizing roles. They are related but not equivalent.

markConflictOfInterest links people (Author, Chairman, Reviewer) to a Paper to flag a conflict of interest, whereas has_been_assigned_a_review_reference links a Submitted contribution or Topic to a Review preference for assignment purposes. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Submitted contribution is a paper or document submitted to a conference, while Review Question is a question used in the review process. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to its author. Contribution in confOf and Paper in edas are equivalent classes in this domain, and both properties share the same direction (document -> Author) and semantics.

Regular author in Ontology A is a subclass of Conference contribution (a document/artefact role), while Invited Speaker in Ontology B is a subclass of Person/Speaker. They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is an author of a regular contribution, the other is a person invited to speak.

Regular author in Ontology A is a person/contributor role (subclass of Conference contributor), while Regular Session in Ontology B is a type of event/session. They share the word 'Regular' but denote entirely different concepts.

Property A ('was a member of') links a Committee member to a Committee, while Property B ('has Member') links a Conference to a Person. They have different domains, different ranges, and different directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

Property A links an Administrator to a Conference for entering review criteria, while Property B links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Published Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been published), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Country in confOf represents a nation (used for affiliation of persons/organizations), while Place in sigkdd represents physical venues such as conference halls, hotels, and offices where people stay. These are conceptually distinct: one is a geopolitical entity, the other is a physical location/building.

Conference in cmt represents the entire conference event/organization, while One conference day in iasted represents a single day within a conference (a temporal sub-unit). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Acceptance in cmt is a type of Decision (an act/outcome of accepting), whereas Rejected Paper in ekaw is a subclass of Paper (a document that was rejected). They differ both in kind (decision vs. paper) and in polarity (acceptance vs. rejection), making them unrelated.

earlyRegistration is a boolean datatype property on Participant indicating early registration status, while hasFirstName is a string datatype property on Person for the person's first name. They describe entirely different concepts.

In the conference domain, 'write' (Person -> Item) and 'submit' (Author -> Paper) are closely related but not equivalent. Writing/authoring a paper is conceptually distinct from submitting it to a conference; one can write without submitting, and submission typically implies authorship but denotes a different action. The domains (Person vs Author) and ranges (Item vs Paper) also differ in generality.

Single Level Conference is a type of conference (subclass of Conference), while Conference state is a status/state related to a conference (subclass of State). They represent entirely different concepts in the domain.

The two properties describe entirely different relations: one links a Conference to an Administrator who printed hardcopy mailing manifests, while the other links two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They share no semantic overlap.
acceptedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (acceptance action), while providedBy relates Sponsorship to an Organization (provision/sponsorship). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
listsEvent relates Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event (listing events), while give relates Person to Activity/Item (giving/presenting). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reception is a social event (a gathering/party), while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation (a place). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Both properties link an event (Conference Event / Event) to a place or location (Place / Location). They express the same relation: where an event is held.

Both properties express a part-whole relationship within the conference domain (tracks/events as parts of a larger conference structure). However, 'has tracks' specifically links a Conference volume to its Tracks, while 'has Event' links an Event to sub-Events. They are related in purpose but differ in domain, range, and specificity, so they are not equivalent.

'is present in' relates a Person to a Place and Time (attendance), while 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper (paper submission). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Subject Area represents a research topic or field of study that papers are categorized under, while Country represents a geographical nation associated with organizations and persons. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (informational material), while 'Welcome address' is a conference activity/event (a speech or ceremony). They belong to different categories and do not denote the same concept.

Flyer in ekaw is a promotional document (sibling of Paper, Programme Brochure, etc.), while Paper in sigkdd is a scholarly submission. They are distinct types of documents with different purposes and are not equivalent.
'isWrittenBy' relates a Paper to its Author (authorship), while 'references' denotes a citation or reference relation between documents. These are semantically distinct properties.
'has Been Assigned' links a Reviewer to a Paper (review assignment), while 'awarded by' links an Award to its granter. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

acceptPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance action), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Camera ready contribution is a type of accepted paper/contribution, while Deadline Abstract Submission is a deadline for submitting abstracts. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Antennas Topic is a subject area classification under Topic, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Property A assigns an external reviewer (domain Reviewer, range External Reviewer), while property B links a reviewer to their expertise or preferences (domain Reviewer, range Review expertise/Review preference). They relate entirely different concepts despite sharing the same domain.

Evaluated Paper in ekaw is a paper that has been submitted, assigned, and evaluated (reviewed). Submission in iasted is a general submitted document with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript, corresponding more closely to Submitted Paper in ekaw. Since Evaluated Paper is a more specific stage (post-review) than the general Submission concept, Evaluated Paper is subsumed by Submission.

Both classes are named 'Presenter' and represent a person who presents at a conference. In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (one who presents their paper), while in ekaw it is a subclass of Conference Participant with Invited Speaker as a child. Despite different parent hierarchies, the intended instances—people presenting at a conference—coincide sufficiently for equivalence in the conference domain.

hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime, while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They describe entirely different concepts and relations.
writtenBy relates a Document to a Person (authorship), while designed_by relates a Deadline to ACM SIGKDD (organizational responsibility). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Plenary lecture is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference applicant in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone applying to a conference), while Conference in Ontology B is the event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

Power Point presentation is a type of conference activity (a presentation format), while Organizator is a type of Person who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

The 'name' property in cmt assigns a name to a Conference or Person, while 'has an ISBN' in the Conference ontology assigns an ISBN identifier to Conference proceedings. These are entirely different properties with different domains and semantics.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while ekaw:Regular_Paper is a specific subtype of Paper (distinguished from Demo Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). Thus confOf:Paper subsumes ekaw:Regular_Paper.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted for review, while Registration fee is a monetary charge for attending the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both classes are named 'Place' and represent physical locations in the conference domain. Their children confirm this: edas has Accommodation Place, Conference Venue Place, Dining Place, Meeting Room Place; sigkdd has Hotel, Conference hall, Main office. These correspond closely (Hotel~Accommodation, Conference hall~Conference Venue/Meeting Room). Both serve as location-related classes for conference entities.

'provided By' links a Sponsorship to an Organization (who provides the sponsorship), while 'is paid for' links Money to an Activity or Item (what the money pays for). They have different domains, ranges, and directions of meaning, so they are unrelated.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking an Item to another Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

'assignedTo' links a Paper to a Reviewer (review assignment), while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker (presentation delivery). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

The properties have different directions and meanings: 'is given by' links a Presentation to the person who delivers it (agent), while 'is given to' links an Item to a Person who receives it (recipient). They are not equivalent nor inverses of each other.

A 'Short paper' in confOf is a type of academic contribution (a short research paper), while a 'Flyer' in ekaw is a promotional document published by an organisation. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Best Applications Paper Award' is an award given to a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Tutorial in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is a Conference part alongside Workshop and Track; in Ontology B it is a Working event (a type of Event) alongside Workshop and Conference. Despite different parent class names, they denote the same concept: a tutorial session at a conference.

University (confOf) is a subclass of Organization representing academic institutions, while Industry Organization (edas) is a subclass of Organization representing commercial/industry entities. They are sibling-like concepts under Organization in their respective ontologies but denote different kinds of organizations. In edas, the closer match to University would be Academia Organization. Thus they are related (both are types of organizations) but not equivalent.

registrationDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime (a deadline), while eventOnList is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.) by an author, while ReviewForm in edas is a form used for reviewing. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A (Conference), 'Regular author' is oddly placed under 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact class) rather than under a Person hierarchy, and its siblings include talks and posters. In Ontology B (confOf), 'Author' is clearly a subclass of Person who writes Contributions. Although both relate to the concept of an author in a conference domain, their ontological modeling differs significantly: one treats it as a contribution role/artefact, the other as a person. They overlap semantically but are not strictly equivalent.

Break Event in edas is a specific type of non-academic event (coffee break, meal break, free time), while Conference activity in iasted is a much broader class that includes lectures, presentations, registration, welcome addresses, and social programs in addition to coffee breaks and cocktail receptions. Therefore, Break Event is subsumed by Conference activity.

In edas, Call represents a call for papers/reviews/manuscripts (an invitation to submit), with children like CallForPapers. In sigkdd, Document represents actual submitted artefacts such as Abstract, Paper, and Review. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain: one is a solicitation, the other is a scholarly work. They are unrelated.

A Program Committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the technical program, whereas a Social program is a type of conference activity (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Submitted Paper is an academic paper submitted to a conference, while Bank transfer is a payment document. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Plenary lecture speaker is a person/role (a type of author/speaker). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
paperInVolume relates a paper to a proceedings volume in ekaw, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document in sigkdd. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Computer Architecture Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

EKAW's Social Event is specifically for social activities (banquet, trip), while IASTED's Conference activity is broader, including both social events (cocktail reception, social program) and scientific/formal activities (lecture, presentation, welcome address). They overlap but are not equivalent; Conference activity subsumes Social Event in scope.

In edas, Workshop is a specific type of Academic Event. In ekaw, Scientific_Event is a broader class that has Workshop as one of its children (along with Conference, Session, Track, etc.). Therefore, edas:Workshop is subsumed by ekaw:Scientific_Event.
Both classes represent the organizing committee of a conference, share the same parent class (Committee), and have analogous sibling classes (e.g., Program Committee). They denote the same concept.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (including authors, reviewers, chairs), while Invited Speaker in sigkdd is a specific role under Speaker. An invited speaker is typically an attendee, but Attendee is much broader. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.
Property A gives the title of a Paper, while property B gives the name of a Conference. They have different domains (Paper vs Conference) and describe entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the same role in a conference: a person who chairs a session. Despite slight differences in their parent hierarchies (edas places it directly under Person, ekaw under Conference Participant and PC Member), the intended instances coincide.
hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, while reviewOfPaper links a Review to the Paper it reviews. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties express a membership relation, but they differ in domain and range: 'was a member of' links a Committee member to a Committee, while 'is Member Of' links a Person to a Conference. They are related (both denote membership) but not equivalent.

Review expertise in Ontology A represents a reviewer's level of expertise or knowledge area relevant to reviewing a specific paper (linked to Submitted contribution). Personal Review History in edas represents a record of past reviews performed by a reviewer (a subclass of Personal History, sibling to Personal Publication History). These are conceptually distinct: one is about competence/skill level for a submission, the other is a historical record of past reviewing activity.
hasBeenAssigned relates a Reviewer to a Paper (assignment for review), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission). Different domains and different semantics.

Property A is an object property linking Money to Item (payment relationship), while Property B is a datatype property linking Registration fee to a string representing currency. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantic meaning.

Accepted contribution (A) is a specific state of a contribution that has been reviewed and accepted, while Contribution (B) in confOf is the general class for all contributions (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper). Thus A is strictly more specific than B, i.e., A is subsumed by B.

Workshop and Tutorial are both types of conference activities/events, but they are distinct concepts. A workshop is typically a collaborative session with multiple presentations, while a tutorial is an instructional lecture. They are siblings or related subtypes under the broader category of conference events, not equivalent.

'is Reviewed By' links a Paper to its reviewers (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.), while 'is prepared by' links an Item to the Person who prepared/authored it. These denote fundamentally different roles (reviewing vs. authoring/preparing) and are unrelated.
isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (providing sponsorship), while is_paid_by relates Money to a Person (who pays). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Organization represents an institution such as a company or university. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Meal Event in edas is a specific type of non-academic conference event (path: Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Meal Event), while Event in ekaw is the top-level class for all events (including Scientific Event and Social Event). Therefore, Meal Event is strictly subsumed by the more general Event class.
Shuttle bus is a type of transport vehicle, while Registration Student is a type of registration fee. They belong to completely different domains and are unrelated.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering), while 'is Menu Of' in edas relates a Meal Menu to a Meal Event (menu assignment). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both are datatype properties with domain Conference and range dateTime, representing the start date/time of a conference. The edas comment explicitly states 'Conference Start Date and Time', matching sigkdd's 'Start of conference'.

Entity A is an administrative event for participant registration, while Entity B is a deadline for notifying acceptance decisions. They represent different concepts (event vs. deadline) with different purposes (registration vs. acceptance notification).
memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference, while isInitiatedBy links a Call to a chair or TPC member. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
University is an academic organization/institution, while Student lecturer is a person role (a student who lectures). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class for anyone who contributes to the conference (including active participants, invited speakers, regular authors). One day presenter (B) is a very specific type of person who presents for one day. A subsumes B because a one-day presenter is a kind of conference contributor, but they are not equivalent since A is much more general.

Pending Paper in edas is a specific status of a Paper (a submitted paper awaiting decision). Submission in iasted is the general class for submitted documents, with children Initial manuscript and Final manuscript. Pending Paper is more specific than Submission, so edas:PendingPaper is subsumed by iasted:Submission.
Talk Event is a type of academic conference event (e.g., closing talk, welcome talk), while Silver Supporter is a sponsorship tier. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
'has authors' links a conference document to its author(s) (Person), while 'has Country' links an Organization or Person to a Country. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Trip in confOf is a social event (an excursion), while Fee for extra trip in iasted is a monetary fee charged for such an excursion. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. money) and are not equivalent.

hasTopic relates a Conference or Paper to a Topic, while write relates a Person to an Item (something they authored). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link a reviewer (or similar role) to a paper, but 'hasBeenAssigned' denotes the assignment action while 'isReviewing' denotes the active reviewing state. Additionally, edas's isReviewing has a broader domain (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) than cmt's hasBeenAssigned (Reviewer only). They are closely related but not strictly equivalent.

Both classes are named 'Review', share the same parent class 'Document', and appear as siblings to 'Paper' in their respective ontologies. In the conference domain, both clearly represent a review document written for a paper submission.

Both classes represent people who participate in or attend a conference. EKAW's 'Conference Participant' (child of Person, with children like Presenter, Session Chair, PC Chair) and IASTED's 'Delegate' (also child of Person, with children like Speaker, Session chair, Technical commitee) cover the same intended instances in the conference domain. The task instructions explicitly note that Attendee/Delegate are synonyms when context agrees.

Property A links a reviewed contribution to its review (domain: Reviewed contribution, range: Review). Property B links a PC member to a contribution they review (domain: Member PC, range: Contribution). The domains, ranges, and directions are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Person in Ontology A is a top-level class encompassing all people involved in the conference (committee members, participants, reviewers, contributors, etc.). Author in Ontology B is a subclass of Person in confOf, specifically denoting someone who writes contributions. Therefore, Person (A) subsumes Author (B).

Sponsor state in iasted is a subclass of State (likely representing the status or condition of a sponsor), whereas Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person representing someone who organizes the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Although both properties share a similar name ('has members' vs 'has Member'), they relate entirely different domain and range classes. In Ontology A, the property links a Committee to its Committee members, while in Ontology B, it links a Conference to Persons. These are structurally and semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.

A passive conference participant is an attendee who does not actively contribute (e.g., a listener), while an organizing committee member is someone who helps organize the conference. These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.
Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, directly under Person. Presenter (B) is a specific subclass of Conference Participant in ekaw. Therefore A subsumes B.

Both classes represent the general concept of a Person in the conference domain. Their children (Chairman, Reviewer, Author, Participant, etc.) are all specific roles that people play at conferences, confirming they cover the same intended set of instances.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (child of Person). Late Registered Participant in ekaw is a specific kind of Conference Participant who registered late. Thus, Attendee subsumes Late Registered Participant.
Conference document refers to documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, announcements), while Sponzor refers to sponsors/supporters of the conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Accommodation Place is a type of location for lodging, while Taxi is a type of transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

Attendee is a subclass of Person representing a person who attends the conference, while Memeber registration fee is a subclass of Money/Registration fee representing a monetary amount. They are entirely different concepts.

Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (a scholarly contribution), while Bank transfer is a payment method document. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories within the conference domain.

maxPapers is a datatype property linking a Program Committee Member to an integer (maximum number of papers they can handle), while paperDueOn links a Conference to a dateTime representing the paper submission deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Venue Place refers to the location where the conference sessions are held (a type of meeting place), while Presenter university refers to the academic institution affiliated with a presenter. These are conceptually distinct types of places in the conference domain.

Conference Chair (cmt) is a specific role (chairman of the conference), while Conference Participant (ekaw) is a broad class encompassing all participants including chairs (e.g., Demo Chair, Session Chair, PC Chair are its children). Thus Conference Chair is subsumed by Conference Participant.

Entity A is an object property linking a Conference volume to Important dates, while Entity B is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value. They differ in property type (object vs datatype), domain, and range, making them unrelated.
Trip is a social event (a type of activity), while Speaker is a person role. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A is a topic classification (Computer Networks Sensor Topic) while B is a type of presentation event (Contributed Talk). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Both properties link a Paper to its subject/topic area (Subject Area in cmt, Topic in edas). In the conference domain, 'subject area' and 'topic' are synonymous concepts used to classify papers. Although edas also allows Conference as a domain, the core relation for papers is equivalent.

Author is a person role (subclass of Person/Conference Member) who writes or submits papers, while Administrative event is a type of event (subclass of Event) such as submission or reviewing events. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote completely different concepts.

Property A refers to the camera-ready paper submission date (domain: Important dates), while Property B refers to the initial paper submission deadline (domain: Call). These are distinct deadlines in the conference lifecycle with different domains and meanings.

Both are datatype properties linking to dateTime, but they have different domains: 'is dated on' applies to Activity while 'Date' applies to Deadline. They serve similar purposes (assigning a date) but are not equivalent due to differing domain classes.

In edas, 'Conference Chair' is a direct subclass of Person and appears to serve as the top-level chair role (no separate General Chair exists). In sigkdd, 'Program Chair' is a subclass of Organizator, distinct from 'General Chair'. The edas Conference Chair likely corresponds more closely to sigkdd's General Chair, while sigkdd's Program Chair has no direct equivalent in edas (TPC Member is the closest program-related role). Thus they are related but not equivalent.

Poster Paper is a type of academic paper (Document > Paper), while Bronze Supporter is a sponsorship tier (Sponzor). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
Property A links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while property B links something to an Award. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Regular contribution is a type of conference document/submission (e.g., a paper), while Conference Session is a type of event (a time slot in the program). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
Short paper is a type of contribution/document, while Author of paper is a type of person/role. They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.
Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee, while Property B links a Contribution (paper) to an Author. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Paper is a submitted manuscript (with states like Accepted, Rejected, Pending) that is written by authors and reviewed. In iasted, Publication has children Book proceeding and Cd proceeding, indicating it refers to published proceedings or volumes, not individual submitted papers. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

setMaxPapers is an object property from Administrator to Program Committee Member used to set a maximum paper limit, while hasMember is an object property from Conference to Person indicating conference membership. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has the last name' captures a person's surname while 'has Email' captures an email address; these are distinct datatype properties with different semantics.

Conference in confOf is a top-level working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference gathering. Invited Talk in ekaw is a specific type of individual scientific presentation given at a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a specific type of committee chair, while Committee member (Conference) is a general class for any committee member. In the Conference ontology, Chair and Co-chair are children of Committee member, indicating that a Program Committee Chair would be a subclass of Committee member. Thus, cmt's Program Committee Chair is subsumed by Conference's Committee member.
Presentation in iasted is a conference activity (event), while Speaker in sigkdd is a person role. They are fundamentally different concepts (an event vs. a participant).

In cmt, 'Co author' is a subclass of 'Author', representing specifically a co-author of a paper. In confOf, 'Author' is the general class for anyone who writes a contribution. Thus, cmt's Co author is subsumed by confOf's Author, as every co-author is an author but not every author is necessarily designated as a 'co-author' in the same sense.
NumericalReviewQuestion is a type of review question expecting a numerical answer, while Abstract is a summary document of a paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Registration fee is a monetary fee for attending a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Property A links 'Important dates' to a 'Conference volume', while property B links 'ACM SIGKDD' (an organization) to a 'Conference'. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference in Ontology A represents an academic conference event, while Organization in Ontology B represents an organizational entity such as a company or university. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Worker non speaker is a type of conference delegate (a person who attends but does not speak), while Conference hall is a physical venue/place where the conference is held. They are entirely different concepts.

Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's topic or paper preference, while Review in ekaw is a document containing an evaluation of a paper. These are conceptually distinct entities in the conference domain.

Class A 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself, while class B 'Conference state' represents a status or state related to a conference (a subclass of 'State', sibling to 'Presenter state' and 'Sponsor state'). These are entirely different concepts.

'is submitted at' specifically links a conference contribution to the conference volume it was submitted to, while 'relates To' is a very general property linking a Document to various entities (events, conferences, sessions, persons). They differ significantly in specificity, domain semantics, and range; they are not equivalent.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Credit card is a payment instrument. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

The two properties are completely different: 'expert On' links a PC member to a topic of expertise, while 'notification until' links an author to a notification deadline. They share no semantic overlap.

Chair PC in confOf is a specific role (Program Committee Chair), while Organizator in sigkdd is a general organizer class whose children include Program Chair, General Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc. Thus Chair PC is subsumed by the broader Organizator class.

Both properties link a Person to a City, but hasCity also applies to Organization and occupy also applies to Building and State. They overlap in the Person-to-City relation but differ in domain and range scope, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In edas, Meal Event and Social Event are siblings under Non Academic Event, meaning they are distinct concepts. In ekaw, Social Event is a direct subclass of Event with children like Conference Banquet (a meal) and Conference Trip. While there is overlap (banquets/dinners appear in both hierarchies), the two classes are not strictly equivalent because edas separates meals from social events, whereas ekaw groups them together under Social Event. They are related but not equivalent.

Person is a class representing human individuals involved in the conference, while State represents a geographical or administrative region (with children like Conference state, Presenter state being states of places). They are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a part-of/has-committee relation), while Property B links a Person to a Conference (a membership relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking Conference volume to a string (location name), while Property B is an object property linking Place to Conference Event. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range, and directionality, so they are not equivalent.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Important dates (deadlines/schedule info), while Property B links a Programme to a Conference Event. These relate different domain concepts and serve different purposes in the conference ontology.

A Textual Review Question is a type of question/criterion used in the review process (a form field), whereas a Negative Review is an actual review document with a negative assessment. They are fundamentally different concepts.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (with children Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In edas, Pending Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing papers awaiting a decision. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes edas:PendingPaper.

hasCountry links Organizations and Persons to a Country (nationality/origin), while is_situated_in links physical locations (Building, City, Place) to broader geographic entities (State, etc.). The domains, ranges, and intended semantics are entirely different.

Paper Presentation in edas is an academic event where an accepted paper is presented at a conference. Power Point presentation in iasted is a specific format/medium of a presentation (using PowerPoint slides). They overlap in the conference domain as both relate to presenting, but they are not equivalent: one denotes the event type tied to a paper, the other denotes the technological medium of delivery.

Workshop and Tutorial are distinct types of conference events. In both ontologies they appear as siblings (e.g., confOf lists Workshop and Tutorial as siblings under Working event), confirming they are separate concepts, not equivalent.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Programme Brochure in ekaw is a type of document that lists events. They are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A links a Call to an Academic Event, while property B links a Sponsor to ACM SIGKDD. They relate entirely different domain and range concepts and serve different purposes in the conference domain.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting paper submissions, while Platinum Supporter is a top-tier sponsor category. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Welcome address is a type of conference activity/event (e.g., lecture, presentation). They belong to different categories (document vs. activity) and are unrelated.

Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for an invited talk), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent unrelated concepts.

Contribution co author is a class representing a type of person (a co-author of a contribution), while Multi author Volume is a class representing a type of document (a volume with multiple authors, such as proceedings). They are entirely different concepts.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while hasRelatedDocument relates various entities to Documents. They have completely different domains and ranges and represent unrelated concepts.

Published Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been published), while Camera ready manuscript deadline is a temporal deadline for submitting the final version of a paper. They are entirely different concepts.

In edas, 'Session Chair' is a direct subclass of Person and serves as a chair role. In ekaw, 'PC Chair' (Program Committee Chair) is a distinct role from 'Session Chair' (which appears as a sibling in ekaw). A Session Chair manages a session, while a PC Chair manages the program committee. They are related as both being chair roles but are not equivalent.
Personal Review History in edas represents a reviewer's history of reviews, while Paper in sigkdd represents a submitted document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer (indicating who read the paper), while reviewWrittenBy links a Review to a Possible Reviewer (indicating who authored the review). They have different domains (Paper vs Review) and different semantics (reading a paper vs writing a review), so they are unrelated.

isReviewing relates reviewing roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to a Paper they review, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document they present. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In confOf, Company is a subclass of Organization (an entity type like a business). In iasted, Sponsor company house is a subclass of Building under Place (a physical location/building). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an organization, the other is a building/place.

'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership/participation), while 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event (organizing role). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.
readByReviewer relates a Paper to a Reviewer (who read it), while invited_by relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignedByReviewer links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (a delegation/assignment relation between reviewer roles), while write links a Person to an Item (an authorship/writing relation). These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Personal Review History in edas is a record/history associated with a reviewer (child of Personal History), whereas Review in ekaw is an individual review document (child of Document) written about a paper. They represent fundamentally different concepts: one is a history log tied to a person, the other is a single review artefact tied to a paper.

A is a conference topic (subject area) related to parallel and distributed computing, while B is an activity (simulating) performed as part of research before a conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the domain.

'Important dates' in Ontology A represents a collection of deadlines and key dates for a conference, while 'Abstract' in Ontology B represents a type of document (a summary of a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

An Associated Chair (cmt) is a type of Chairman who assists the main conference chair, while a Session Chair (ekaw) chairs an individual session during the conference. These are distinct roles in conference organization, though both involve chairing responsibilities, so they are related but not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Trip city is a geographical location (a type of City). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A is a datatype property assigning an unsigned long identifier to a Paper, while Property B assigns a date for full paper submission to Important dates. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' in Conference ontology refers to informational documents like calls for papers or announcements provided to attendees, whereas 'Publication' in iasted refers to published works such as book proceedings. These are conceptually distinct types of items.

Committee member in Ontology A refers to a person serving on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair), while Author in Ontology B refers to a person who writes papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.
Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Location is a place where events are held. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both are datatype properties mapping a paper/contribution to its title string. In the conference domain, Paper (cmt) and Contribution (confOf) are equivalent classes, so their title properties are equivalent.
Conference in ekaw is a scientific event (one edition of a conference), while Conference state in iasted is a status/state related to a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.

hasConferenceMember relates a Conference to its members (people), while parallel_with relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Accommodation Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where attendees stay, while Hotel registration form is a document/form used to register for a hotel. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (place vs. document).
Author is a person who writes or submits papers, while Sponsorship is a financial arrangement (e.g., travel grant) provided by an organization. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

paperAssignmentFinalizedBy is an object property linking a Conference to an Administrator who finalized paper assignments, while paperDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime representing the paper submission deadline. They have different ranges (Administrator vs dateTime) and completely different semantics.
readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer (reading action), while write links a Person to an Item (writing action). They differ in direction, semantics (read vs write), and domain/range types.

In Ontology A, Tutorial is a conference part/event (sibling of Track and Workshop), whereas in Ontology B, Tutorial Abstract is a document (a subclass of Abstract). An event and its abstract are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

hasPhone is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (phone number), while obtain is an object property linking Person to Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Conference Chair (edas) is the overall chair of a conference, while Demo Chair (ekaw) is specifically responsible for the demo track/session. They are both chair roles under Person/Conference Participant but denote different responsibilities, so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A 'date' has domain Conference and represents the date of a conference, while property B 'done till' has domain Deadline and represents the deadline date. They apply to different classes and capture different temporal concepts, so they are unrelated.

Welcome Talk in edas is a type of conference event (a talk), while Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (an abstract). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. document) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Associated Chair is a leadership role (a type of Chairman) in conference organization, while Late paid applicant is a registration/payment status of a conference attendee. They represent entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Contact Information holds address/phone/email details for a person or entity. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Test Only Topic in edas is a subclass of Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In iasted, 'Tutorial speaker' is a specific subclass of 'Author' (a speaker who gives tutorials). In sigkdd, 'Author' is the general class for anyone who authors/submits a paper. The iasted Tutorial speaker is a more specific kind of author, so it is subsumed by the sigkdd Author class.
Workshop is a type of working event (an activity), while Session room is a physical place where sessions occur. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. location) and are unrelated.

contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to an email string, while listsEvent is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI string, while listsEvent is an object property linking a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

hasEmail is a datatype property linking Person to a string (email address), while is_used_by is an object property linking Item to Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to submitted scholarly works (papers, posters, invited talks) that are part of a conference volume. Conference activity in Ontology B refers to scheduled events during the conference (cocktail receptions, coffee breaks, registration, social programs). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Review to the Reviewed contribution (paper) it evaluates. Property B links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. The domains and ranges are entirely different concepts, so these properties are unrelated.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an academic gathering), while Presenter university in iasted is a type of building/place where a presenter is affiliated. These are entirely different concepts.

Trip is a social event (an excursion), while Fee is a monetary charge. Although iasted has a 'Fee for extra trip' as a child of Fee, the Trip class itself and the Fee class are entirely different concepts.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme (schedule), while eventOnList links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site where it is listed. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while 'is designed for' relates Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Meeting Room Place is a physical location (subclass of Place), while Worker non speaker is a person/role (subclass of Delegate/Non speaker). They are completely unrelated concepts.
Dinner banquet is a social event/activity at a conference, while Program Committee member is a person role involved in organizing the conference program. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

assignedTo relates a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment of review), while locationOf relates a Location to an Event (spatial containment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while 'notification until' relates an Author to a Deadline (temporal notification deadline). These properties have entirely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer on the program committee), while Personal Review History in edas is a record/history object associated with a reviewer. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. information artifact) and thus unrelated.

Social program is a type of conference activity (e.g., dinner banquet, cocktail reception), while Program Committee is an organizational committee responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Presenter in edas is a Person (specifically an Author who presents), while Presenter house in iasted is a Building/Place. They are completely different concepts.
authorOf relates a Person to a Document (authorship), while is_paid_by relates Money to a Person (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

hasBiography is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (their biography), while is_designed_for is an object property linking Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and types.

Property A links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (event-to-artefact), while property B links a Speaker to a Document (person-to-artefact). The domains and ranges are fundamentally different, so these properties are not equivalent.

Session in ekaw is a type of scientific event (a time-block or meeting), while Session chair in iasted is a person/role (a delegate who chairs a session). These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. person) and are unrelated.
Conference in cmt represents the conference event/organization itself, while Abstract in ekaw is a subclass of Document representing a paper abstract. These are entirely different concepts.
Multi-author Volume in ekaw is a collection of papers (parent of Proceedings), whereas Paper in sigkdd is an individual submitted paper. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Dinner in edas is a specific social meal event occurring during a conference, while Conference in ekaw represents the entire scientific conference event itself (one edition). These are fundamentally different concepts at different levels of granularity and type.
Event in ekaw represents a conference occurrence (scientific or social event), while Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person who gives presentations. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a conference volume to its organizing committee, while property B links a physical location (building/city/state) to a person who occupies it. These are entirely different relations in both domain and range.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator, while 'hasMenu' links a MealEvent to a MealMenu. They are unrelated.

In confOf, 'Conference' is a specific type of working event (sibling to Tutorial and Workshop), representing the conference itself. In iasted, 'Conference activity' represents individual activities that take place during a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture, registration). These are conceptually different: one denotes the overarching event, the other denotes constituent activities within it. They overlap in domain but are not equivalent.

Research Institute is an organization (a type of academic institution), while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. They share the word 'Research' but denote entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Extended abstract is a type of conference contribution/document (a written artefact), while Conference in confOf is a type of working event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

paperDueOn is a specific datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime for the paper deadline, while Date is a general datatype property linking Deadline to a dateTime. They are related (both capture date/time information) but not equivalent due to different domains and specificity.

Industrial Paper is a type of academic paper (Document), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Item). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
TPC Member is a person role (Technical Program Committee member), while Registration fee is a monetary concept. They are entirely unrelated.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a general class under Person with children including Chair and Co-chair, covering all committee types. In Ontology B, 'Program Committee member' is specifically a member of the program committee, distinguished from siblings like 'Organizing Committee member'. Thus, the general 'Committee member' in A subsumes the more specific 'Program Committee member' in B.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted manuscript (child of Document, with authors, reviews, decisions), while Topic in edas represents a subject area or theme (e.g., Antennas, Cryptography). These are entirely different concepts; Paper has a property 'has Subject Area' that would relate to Topic, but the classes themselves are unrelated.

Active conference participant in Ontology A includes Regular author and Invited speaker as siblings, meaning it covers anyone who actively contributes (e.g., gives presentations). Speaker in Ontology B is specifically someone who gives a presentation, with children Author and Invited Speaker. While they overlap significantly (both give presentations), Active conference participant may also include regular authors who contribute papers without necessarily presenting, making them related but not strictly equivalent.

confOf:Participant is a general class for all conference participants (with children Member, Regular, Student), while ekaw:Presenter is a specific role of someone who presents at the conference. Participant subsumes Presenter since every presenter is a participant, but not every participant is a presenter.

Presenter is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Sponsor company house is a building/place associated with a sponsor company. They are entirely different concepts.

assignedByReviewer links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (assignment relationship), while belongs_to_reviewers links Review expertise or Review preference to a Reviewer (association of metadata to a reviewer). Different domains and different semantics.

Invited Talk is an Event (a presentation), while Invited Speaker is a Person who delivers such a talk. They are closely related in the conference domain but belong to different categories (event vs. person), so they are not equivalent.

Contribution in confOf represents a submitted work (paper, poster, short paper) with properties like title, abstract, and author. Topic in edas represents a subject area or theme of the conference/paper. These are entirely different concepts; Contribution 'deals With' Topic, but they are not equivalent.
Property A captures the first name (given name) of a Person, while property B captures the surname (family name). These are distinct attributes and not equivalent.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI string, while is_present_in is an object property linking a Person to a Place/Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

A Conference restaurant is a dining facility (subclass of Building), while a Hotel is an accommodation facility (subclass of Place). They serve different purposes in the conference domain and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

A is a specific research topic (Satellite And Space Communications Topic) under Topic, while B is a type of document (Invited Talk Abstract) under Abstract. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In ekaw, Student is a general subclass of Person with no restriction on speaking status. In iasted, Student non speaker is specifically a student who is not a speaker (subclass of Non speaker). Therefore, the ekaw Student class subsumes the iasted Student non speaker class, as it includes both speakers and non-speakers.

OC Chair in ekaw is a subclass of OC Member (Organizing Committee member). In sigkdd, Organizing Committee member is the general class with General Chair as a sibling. Thus, OC Chair is more specific than and subsumed by Organizing Committee member.

Person is a class representing human individuals (with children Delegate, Sponsor), while Deadline is a class representing temporal submission/notification deadlines. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion during the conference), while Conference city is a geographical location (the city where the conference takes place). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Working event in confOf is a type of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Enterprise Topic in edas is a specific subject area/topic within computer networks. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Paper in cmt represents a submitted academic paper (with authors, reviews, decisions), while Meal Menu in edas represents a menu for a meal event. They are entirely different concepts that merely share the same parent class 'Document'.

locationOf relates a Location to an Event (i.e., an event takes place at a location), while is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (i.e., a place is equipped with some item). These are semantically different relations with different ranges and purposes.
'is Menu Of' links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a submitted contribution (a document), while Call For Papers is an announcement inviting submissions. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact), despite its confusing name and parentage. In Ontology B, 'Regular' is a subclass of 'Participant' (a person/attendee type). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain (artefact vs. person) and are unrelated.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (administrative material), while 'Performance Topic' is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

hasPostalCode captures a postal/zip code from Contact Information, while E-mail captures an email address from Person. These are entirely different contact attributes with different domains and semantics.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of 'Author', representing authors who are not reviewers. In confOf, 'Author' is the general class for all authors. Since every AuthorNotReviewer is an Author but not every Author is necessarily an AuthorNotReviewer (confOf's Author has no such restriction), the cmt class is subsumed by the confOf class.

The 'name' property in cmt is a general naming property for Conference and Person entities, while 'has VAT' in confOf specifically denotes a value-added tax identifier for events. They have completely different semantics, domains, and purposes.

A Steering committee is a type of Committee (an organizational body), while Possible Reviewer is a type of Person who may review papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a subclass of Person (people attending the conference), while Conference activity in iasted is a subclass of Activity (events happening at the conference). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Both classes represent a paper that has been rejected in the conference review process. Despite differing intermediate hierarchy paths (edas uses Paper directly, ekaw goes through Submitted/Assigned/Evaluated Paper), their intended instances coincide: papers that were not accepted.

In edas, Presenter is a subclass of Author (a person who presents a paper). In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker (a person who writes/submits a paper). Both represent people involved in authoring and presenting papers at a conference, but their hierarchical positions differ: edas Presenter is more specific (must present), while sigkdd Author is the one who submits. They overlap significantly in the conference domain but are not strictly equivalent due to differing parent-child structures.

In iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (path: Delegate > Speaker > Author), meaning all authors are speakers. In sigkdd, Invited Speaker is a specific type of Speaker, while Author is a sibling class. An Author in iasted is not necessarily an invited speaker; they may be regular paper presenters. The concepts overlap (both can speak at the conference) but are not equivalent, and neither strictly subsumes the other across ontologies.

In edas, Paper is a full conference paper (with reviews, authors, acceptance states). In ekaw, Abstract and Paper are distinct sibling classes under Document; Abstract represents a short summary (e.g., for invited talks or tutorials), not the full paper. They overlap in the conference domain but are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (the chairperson of a conference), while Conference activity is an event or scheduled activity at a conference. They are entirely different concepts.
