A Double hotel room is a type of accommodation for sleeping, while a Conference hall is a venue for holding conference sessions. They are entirely different concepts within the Place hierarchy.

hasEndDateTime specifies the end date/time of a Conference Event, while is_dated_on provides a general date for an Activity. They share similar domains (Conference Event ~ Activity) and range (dateTime), but differ in specificity: one denotes an end time, the other a generic date. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal succession), while 'lists Event' in ekaw relates a Programme Brochure or Web Site to an Event (content listing). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A ('has an abstract') links a paper/poster/presentation to its abstract document. Property B ('presentation Of Paper') links an individual presentation event to the paper or abstract being presented. They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and serve different semantic purposes.

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

IASTED non member is a subclass of Delegate (a person/role), while Registration Non Member is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote different kinds of entities.

Conference contribution in Ontology A refers to submitted scholarly works (papers, posters, presentations) that are part of a conference volume. Activity in Ontology B refers to events or happenings (before, during, or after the conference) such as sessions or social events. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference for enabling virtual meetings, while organisedBy relates an Event to an Organisation or Person that organises it. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In edas, Attendee is a general class for anyone attending the conference (with siblings like Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair). In sigkdd, Organizator specifically denotes people who organize the conference (children include General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member), and is disjoint from Listener and Speaker. These are conceptually distinct roles: one is about attendance, the other about organization.

Session Chair in ekaw is a specific role (chairing a session), while IASTED member in iasted denotes membership in the IASTED organization. They are distinct concepts; notably, iasted has its own 'Session chair' class as a sibling of 'IASTED member', confirming they are not equivalent.

A Slide Set is a collection of presentation slides (a type of Document), while a Review is an evaluation document for a paper. They are distinct sibling concepts under Document with no semantic overlap.

Computer Networks Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference to any Conference Member (a general membership relation), while Property B links a Conference part to a specific Track workshop chair role. The domains differ (Conference vs Conference part) and the ranges differ significantly (general member vs specific chair role), making them unrelated.
Conference is a type of working event (a gathering), while Mobile Computing Topic is a specific subject area/topic. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The property 'has a review' links a reviewed contribution to its review, while 'is paid for' links money to an activity or item. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Entity A is the general class 'Topic' in the Conference ontology, while Entity B is 'Performance Topic', a specific subclass of 'Topic' in edas. Therefore, A subsumes B.

'belongsToEvent' links a Programme to the Conference Event it is part of, while 'organises' links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Break Event in edas refers to pauses/breaks during a conference (coffee break, meal break, free time), while Introduction in iasted refers to an introductory activity (with child 'Introduction of speaker'). These are conceptually distinct types of conference activities.
Paper is a document/submission class, while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing), while Hotel fee is a monetary charge for accommodation. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and represent fundamentally different concepts.
Reception is a social event (an activity), while Accommodation Place is a physical location for lodging. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Place) and have no semantic overlap.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In iasted, Sponsor is a subclass of Person (an individual who sponsors), while in sigkdd, Platinum Supporter is a subclass of Sponzor (an organization/entity providing sponsorship). They are related through the sponsorship concept but differ in nature (person vs. supporter tier) and hierarchy, so they are not equivalent.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (paper), while Silver Supporter is a type of sponsor. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Conference city is a geographic location (city where the conference takes place). They are entirely different concepts.

Paper in edas refers to a scholarly submission (with reviews, authors, topics), while Payment document in iasted refers to a financial instrument (bank transfer, cheque). They are completely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Simulating in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.

A is a topic classification (Computer Networks Enterprise Topic) while B is a type of presentation event (Invited Talk). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.
TPC Member in edas is a program committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls, while Author in sigkdd is a person who submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain.
Paper is a scholarly document submitted to a conference, while Transport vehicle refers to physical vehicles (cars, buses, etc.) used for transportation. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A links a Co-chair to a Committee (a specific committee membership role), while Property B links a Conference to a Person (general conference membership). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Contribution 1th author is a class representing the first author of a contribution (a person role), while Multi author Volume is a class representing a document type (e.g., proceedings). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasPhone denotes a telephone number while Name denotes a person's name; they are different attributes of Person and not equivalent.

Conference Participant is a subclass of Person representing people attending the conference, while Activity before conference is a subclass of Activity representing tasks performed prior to the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Travel Grant is a type of Sponsorship (a funding mechanism), while Sponsor is a Person who provides sponsorship. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
'has an expertise' relates a Review expertise to some value, while 'Nation' relates a Person to a string representing their nationality. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Working_event is a broad class covering Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop (children). ekaw:Individual_Presentation covers Contributed Talk, Invited Talk, and Tutorial—essentially individual presentation slots within scientific events. Working_event is strictly more general, encompassing entire conferences and workshops as well as tutorials, while Individual_Presentation only covers specific presentation-level events. Social Event in edas is a non-academic event during the conference (with children like Excursion and Reception). Activity after conference in iasted is defined by its temporal placement (after the conference) and includes Departure and Full day tour. While they overlap (e.g., excursions/tours can be social events occurring after the main program), they are classified along different axes (type vs. timing) and neither subsumes the other.

Entity A is a general 'Paper' class (a regular contribution to a conference), while Entity B is a 'Withdrawn Paper', which is a specific status subclass of Paper in the edas ontology. They are not equivalent; B is more specific than A. Since they come from different ontologies with different hierarchies and B represents only withdrawn papers rather than all papers, 'related' best captures their overlap without strict subsumption across ontologies.

Both classes represent a Person in the conference domain. Their children (Chairman/Chair PC, Program Committee Member/Member PC, etc.) and properties (email) align well, indicating they denote the same concept.

Conference document represents documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, announcements), while Time represents temporal concepts (days, deadlines). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Computer Networks Enterprise Topic is a research topic classification under Topic, while Trip day is a temporal concept under Time. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

'has Author' links a Paper to its Author (intellectual creator), while 'is signed by' links an Item to a Person who signed it. These are semantically different relations with different intended meanings and domains/ranges.

Conference in confOf is a working event (a gathering of people), while Cd proceening in iasted is a publication item (a CD containing proceedings). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a conference volume to its program committee (a group of people), while property B links a conference event to its programme (a schedule of sessions). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Computer Networks Aapplications Topic is a subject area/topic for conference papers. They are entirely different concepts.

hasTopic links a Conference or Paper to a Topic (subject area), while paperInVolume links a paper to a volume/proceedings it appears in. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Entity A is a Conference (an event), while Entity B is a specific type of Author whose proceedings are included on a CD. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Invited_Speaker is a subclass of Presenter (a specific kind of speaker). In sigkdd, Speaker is a broader class that has both Author and Invited Speaker as children. Therefore, ekaw's Invited_Speaker is subsumed by sigkdd's Speaker, but they are not equivalent since sigkdd's Speaker also includes regular authors who present.

In edas, 'Two Level Conference' is a subclass of Conference (despite odd multiple parents including Person and TPC Member), representing a type of conference organization. In iasted, 'IASTED member' is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These denote fundamentally different concepts: one is a conference type, the other is a participant role.

Important dates is a class representing deadline information for a conference, while Individual Presentation is a class representing a scientific event (talk/tutorial). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A 'contributes' links a Person to a Conference document (person contributes a document), while property B 'relatesTo' links a Document to various entities including Person, Event, etc. They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

Conference Paper is a scholarly paper submitted to a conference, while Transparency refers to overhead transparencies/slides used for presentations. These are entirely different types of documents in the conference domain.

Submission event in confOf is an administrative event (the act/process of submitting contributions), while Transparency in iasted is a type of document (a physical or digital item). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Trip is a social event (an excursion or outing) in the conference schedule, while Transport vehicle is a physical item (car, bus, taxi) used for transportation. They are fundamentally different concepts.

In edas, Reception is a specific type of Social Event (sibling of Excursion). In iasted, Social program is the general category for social activities, with Coctail reception as one of its children. Thus, edas:Reception is subsumed by iasted:Social_program.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Dinner banquet is a social event/activity. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Plenary lecture speaker (iasted) is a specific type of Author who gives a plenary lecture, while Author (sigkdd) is the general class of all authors. The iasted class is strictly more specific, so it is subsumed by the sigkdd Author class.

In cmt, Bid refers to a reviewer's bid on a paper (part of the review assignment process). In iasted, Money is a financial concept with children like Fee, Tax, Tip. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' in Ontology A is a class of documents providing information to attendees, while 'Review' in Ontology B is a document representing an evaluation of a submission. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.

A Workshop is a working event (like a conference or tutorial) involving interactive sessions, while a Welcome Talk is a specific type of talk event at the opening of a conference. They are distinct concepts in the conference domain.

Excursion in edas is a specific type of Social Event (with sibling Reception), while Activity after conference in iasted is a broader category that includes Full day tour and Departure as children. Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Parallel And Distributed Computing Topic is a subject/topic area for papers. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Rejection is a type of decision about a paper, while Speaker is a role played by a person at a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both represent organized leisure trips/excursions associated with a conference. However, 'Excursion' in edas is a type of Social Event (which could be half-day or full-day), while 'Full day tour' in iasted specifically denotes a full-day activity after the conference. They overlap significantly but are not strictly equivalent due to the duration specificity of the iasted class.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while employedBy relates a Person to an Organization. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.
hasFax is a datatype property linking a Person to a fax number string, while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They represent entirely different relations.

Industry Organization in edas is a type of organization (commercial/industry entity), while Organizing Committee in sigkdd is a committee responsible for organizing the conference. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Welcome Talk and Invited Talk are both types of talks/presentations at a conference, but they serve different purposes. 'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (membership). They have different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.
A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while 'Government Organization' is a type of organization. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewing event in confOf is an administrative event (a process/activity for reviewing contributions), while Review Form in edas is a document/artifact used during the review process. An event and a form are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

confOf's Administrator is a broad role under Person (with comment 'confTool', likely covering system/tool administrators), while sigkdd's Organizing Committee member is specifically a member of the organizing committee under Organizator. They overlap in that both are organizational roles but are not equivalent; they are related.

Decision in cmt represents the outcome of a paper review (Acceptance or Rejection), while Document in sigkdd represents written artefacts such as Abstracts, Papers, and Reviews. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'Record of attendance' in iasted is a document tracking who attended (e.g., for registration purposes), while 'Paper' in sigkdd is a scholarly contribution submitted by an author. These are entirely different concepts within the conference domain.
hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (URL), while obtain is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They have different ranges, types, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'enter Conference Details' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'has Menu' links a Meal Event to a Meal Menu. They are unrelated.
Working event in confOf is a type of conference event (e.g., tutorial, workshop), while Web Site in ekaw is a type of document. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Conference in Ontology A represents the conference event itself (with children like Conference volume and properties like has a name), while Conference hotel in Ontology B is a specific type of building/place where a conference might be held. These are fundamentally different concepts.

confOf's Social event (with children Banquet, Reception, Trip) is a specific type of conference event. In edas, Conference Event is the top-level class for all events at a conference, with children Academic Event and Non Academic Event. Social event would correspond to Non Academic Event in edas, making it strictly more specific than (subsumed by) Conference Event.
'updatedVersionOf' relates a Document to another Document (versioning), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and a sibling of 'Conference Chair', indicating it is a distinct, more specific role (associate/vice chair). In edas, 'Conference Chair' is the top-level chair role. They are related as both are chair roles but not equivalent; if anything, Conference Chair in edas would subsume Associated Chair in cmt, but since they are explicitly distinguished as siblings in cmt, 'related' is most appropriate.

User is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the conference system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Conference Session is a subclass of Event representing a scheduled session at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Negative Review is a specific type of review expressing a negative assessment, while Abstract is a summary document of a paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Organization/Person to a string postal code, while writtenBy is an object property linking Document to Person. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

Working event is a type of conference event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Delegate is a type of person/attendee. They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both properties link a programme-related entity to an event, but they differ in semantics and domain: 'belongsToEvent' (domain Programme) indicates that a programme is part of a conference event, while 'listsEvent' (domain Programme Brochure, Web Site) indicates that a brochure or website enumerates/lists events. They are related but not equivalent.
Paper is a document/artefact submitted to a conference, while Deadline is a temporal constraint for submissions or notifications. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Personal Review History is about a reviewer's history of reviews, while Departure tax is a type of financial tax. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Invited speaker is a Person (a conference contributor), while Invited Talk Abstract is a Document (an abstract). They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent.
'writtenBy' denotes authorship (Document -> Person), while 'is sent by' denotes the act of sending/submission (Item -> Person). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite odd parentage including Person/TPC Member), while Speaker in iasted is a person who presents at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.
Program Committee is a group of people reviewing papers, while State is a geographical or administrative region. They are completely unrelated concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Conference volume' is a subclass of Conference representing a specific edition/instance of a conference (with committees, contributions, tracks, etc.). In Ontology B, 'Working event' is a superclass of Conference, Tutorial, and Workshop, representing any academic working event. They overlap in that both can represent a conference, but Working event is more general (includes tutorials/workshops) while Conference volume is specifically a conference instance. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Meta Review' is a subclass of 'Review', making it a more specific type of review. In iasted, 'Review' is the general class for reviews. Therefore, cmt's Meta Review is subsumed by iasted's Review.
Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation, while Sponsor state is a status/state of a sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The property 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (an administrative action), while 'organised By' relates an Event to an Organisation or Person (indicating who organises the event). These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Contribution 1th author is a role for the first author of a conference contribution, while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Organizing committee is a group of people responsible for organizing a conference, while Building is a physical structure/place. They are entirely different concepts.
dealsWith links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while submit_until links a Document to a Deadline (temporal constraint). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop in confOf is a type of event (a working event), while Workshop Paper in ekaw is a type of document/paper submitted to or presented at a workshop. They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. document) and are not equivalent.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Building is a physical place/structure. They are completely unrelated concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enter Conference Details' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'event On List' links an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site. They are unrelated.

hasLocation relates a Conference Event to a Place (spatial location), while holded_by relates a Conference to an organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.

Property A is specifically the date for camera-ready paper submission, while Property B is a generic deadline date ('done till'). They share the same datatype pattern (domain is a deadline/dates class, range is date) but differ in specificity; A is a specific kind of deadline, so they are related but not equivalent.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event/excursion that is part of a conference (sibling of Conference Banquet), whereas Conference in sigkdd represents the main conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and name. These are distinct concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Tutorial is a type of working event (an activity at the conference). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Trip day is a temporal concept (a day for travel). They are completely unrelated.

'adjusted By' relates a Bid to a Reviewer in the paper bidding process, while 'pay' relates a Person to a Registration fee for payment purposes. These properties operate on entirely different domains and ranges and describe unrelated concepts.
Property A relates a Committee to its Co-chair (membership/role), while Property B relates ACM SIGKDD to a Conference it organizes. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasCity links an Organization or Person to a City (indicating location), while is_visited_by links a City/Building/State to a Person (inverse direction of visiting). They involve similar domain concepts (Person, City) but express different relations in opposite directions; they are not equivalent nor inverses of each other, but loosely related through shared concepts.
Invited speaker is a person role (subclass of Conference contributor), while Sponsor city is a type of city. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property A (siteURL) has domain Conference and represents the URL of a conference event. Property B (has_a_URL) has domain 'Conference www' (a website/web-page entity) and represents the URL of that web resource. Since their domains refer to different concepts (the conference itself vs. its website), they are not equivalent.

Committee in Ontology A refers to conference committees (organizing, program, steering) with chairs and members, while Organization in Ontology B refers to institutions like companies and universities that employ people. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Final manuscript is a type of submission document, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite oddly having Person and TPC Member as parents), while Agency Staff Member in ekaw is a person working for an agency. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organization in confOf represents institutions like companies and universities that employ people, while Item in iasted represents physical objects or documents (equipment, cards, publications). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Committee member is a Person role in a conference committee, while Dining Place is a physical location for eating. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

hasCity is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (city name), while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantic meaning.

Presenter_state in iasted is a subclass of State (a status/condition), whereas Speaker in sigkdd is a subclass of Person (a role). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

hasTopic (domain: Working event, range: Topic) and topicCoveredBy (domain: Research Topic, range: Event, Paper) express the same conceptual link between events/papers and topics, but in opposite directions. hasTopic goes from event to topic, while topicCoveredBy goes from topic to event/paper. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent, they are related.

In cmt, Review is a document (the actual review written by a reviewer), whereas in edas, ReviewQuestion is a question used to structure or guide the review process (with subtypes like Numerical and Textual). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an artefact produced during reviewing, the other is a template element for eliciting review content.

Program Committee and Organizing Committee are distinct types of committees in conference organization. Ontology B explicitly lists 'Program committee' as a sibling of 'Organizing committee', confirming they are separate concepts. They are related as both are kinds of committees but not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person/role in conference organization, while Dinner banquet is a social event/activity. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information for participants), while Introduction is a type of conference activity/event (e.g., welcome address, introduction of speaker). They belong to fundamentally different categories (documents vs. activities) and are unrelated.

Member in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a person attending the conference), while Registration Non Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a monetary fee category). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote completely different concepts.

Conference Chair is a leadership role responsible for organizing the conference, while Early paid applicant is a registrant who paid their fees early. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Conference state is a status/state concept. They are entirely different kinds of entities.
Session Chair is a person role in a conference, while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts.

OC Member (Organizing Committee) in ekaw is distinct from Program Committee member in sigkdd. The sigkdd ontology itself separates 'Program Committee member' and 'Organizing Committee member' as siblings, confirming these are different roles. OC members handle logistics/organization while PC members handle paper reviewing.

TPC Member (Technical Program Committee) in edas is responsible for reviewing papers and initiating calls, while OC Member (Organizing Committee) in ekaw handles organizational logistics. These are distinct roles in conference organization with different responsibilities; the PC Chair is a separate sibling class in ekaw, confirming OC Member does not cover program committee duties.
Property A relates a Chair to a Committee (committee chair role), while Property B relates an Item to a Person (signing/authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes are named 'Place' and represent physical locations in the conference domain. They share key children such as 'Conference hall' and 'Main office', and both are used as locations where persons or activities occur (e.g., 'is held in', 'can stay in'). Despite minor differences in other children (Building vs Hotel), their intended instances coincide.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Camera Ready event is an administrative event/deadline. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Program committee and Organizing Committee are distinct types of committees within a conference. Both ontologies list them as siblings under Committee (Ontology A has Organizing committee as a sibling of Program committee; Ontology B has Program Committee as a sibling of Organizing Committee). They are related as co-hyponyms but not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an acceptance announcement date, while Property B is an object property linking a location to an event. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

confOf:Paper is a general class for all papers (siblings include Poster, Short paper), while edas:AcceptedPaper is specifically a paper that has been accepted (a subclass of edas:Paper with siblings like Rejected Paper, Pending Paper). Therefore confOf:Paper subsumes edas:AcceptedPaper.

TalkEvent in edas is a broad class for talk-type events (with children Closing Talk, Welcome Talk and sibling Paper Presentation), while Invited_Talk in ekaw is a specific kind of individual presentation (sibling to Contributed Talk and Tutorial). They overlap conceptually as both relate to talks at a conference, but neither subsumes the other cleanly across the two ontologies' hierarchies, so they are related rather than equivalent.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is occupied by' relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person (occupancy). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Program Committee Member is a person role involved in reviewing and organizing the conference program, while Social program is a type of conference activity (e.g., dinner banquet). They are entirely different concepts.
Tutorial is a type of scientific event/presentation, while Memeber registration fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Registeered applicant is a subclass of Person (a registered conference applicant), while Conference in edas represents the event itself. These are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a conference volume to its program committee, while property B links administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's topic or paper preference, while Organization in Conference refers to an organizational entity (e.g., institution). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference (domain: Reviewer, range: Review expertise/Review preference). Property B links a Paper to its assigned reviewer (domain: Paper, range: Possible Reviewer). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members, while 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

maxPapers is a datatype property linking a Program Committee Member to an integer (maximum number of papers they can review), while Name_of_conference links a Conference to a string (the conference's name). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Co author in cmt is a person (subclass of Author) who co-writes papers, while Multi author Volume in ekaw is a document (subclass of Document) such as proceedings. They are entirely different concepts sharing only the word 'author'.

In Ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' representing the conference website (it has a URL property). In Ontology B, 'Conference' represents the actual conference event with properties like start/end dates and city. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference volume in Ontology A represents the overall conference proceedings or event edition (with committees, location, tracks, contributions), while Conference Session in ekaw is a specific session within a scientific event (e.g., demo, poster, regular session). These are fundamentally different concepts.

readByReviewer links a Paper to a Reviewer (reading relation), while writtenBy links a Contribution to an Author (authorship relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a person serving on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair). In confOf, 'Scholar' is explicitly described as a price category for scholars (e.g., students/academics attending), with sibling 'Member PC' being the actual committee member class. These are entirely different concepts.

Mobile Computing Topic is a subclass of Topic representing a research area, while Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award representing a prize. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a person participating in or associated with a conference, directly subclassing Person. In cmt, Conference Member includes authors, reviewers, chairs, and PC members; in Conference, Conference participant includes active and passive participants. Despite slightly different child taxonomies, their intended instances (people involved in the conference) coincide, making them equivalent in the conference domain.

Paper Presentation in edas is a Conference Event (an activity where a paper is presented), while Conference Paper in ekaw is a Document (the written artefact itself). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. document) and are not equivalent.

Property A captures a person's last name (domain: Person), while property B captures a contribution's contact email (domain: Contribution). They represent entirely different attributes of different entities.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a social event/excursion during the conference (sibling of Conference Banquet), while Departure in iasted is an activity after the conference involving leaving. These are conceptually distinct activities.

Both classes represent the subject/topic area of a paper or contribution in the conference domain. In cmt, 'Subject Area' is linked to Paper via 'has Subject Area'; in confOf, 'Topic' is linked to Contribution (the equivalent of Paper) via 'deals With'. They denote the same concept.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while paperPresentedAs relates a Paper to an Individual Presentation (presentation format). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In iasted, Deadline is a general class with children including 'Deadline for notification of acceptance'. In sigkdd, 'Deadline Author notification' is a specific subclass of Deadline. Thus the iasted Deadline subsumes the sigkdd Deadline Author notification.

Both classes represent a poster contribution to a conference. In Ontology A, Poster is a Conference contribution (alongside Presentation and Written contribution), while in ekaw, Poster Paper is a subclass of Paper. Despite different parent class names, both denote the same concept: a paper/poster presented at a conference.

In ekaw, Track is a type of Scientific Event (a thematic track/strand within a conference). In iasted, 'One conference day' is a temporal unit under Time > Conference days. These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. time period) and are unrelated.

Working event is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Radio Communications Topic is a specific research Topic. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In Ontology A, Paper is a document/contribution (a written artefact under Conference contribution). In Ontology B, Paper Presentation is an event (under Academic Event) where a paper is presented. They are related via the 'related To Paper' property in edas but denote fundamentally different concepts (document vs. event), so they are not equivalent.
The property 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'isProviderOf' relates an Organization to a Sponsorship. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties link entities to a Topic, but they differ in domain: A's property has domain 'Conference part' (tracks, workshops, tutorials), while B's property has domain 'Conference' and 'Paper'. They are related as they both express topic assignment, but not equivalent due to different intended domains.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Payment document is a financial document used for payment. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

cmt:AuthorNotReviewer is a subclass of Author restricted to those who are not reviewers. iasted:Author is the general Author class (with Reviewer as a sibling under Speaker). Thus cmt:AuthorNotReviewer is strictly more specific than iasted:Author, making it subsumed_by.

'Conference contributor' in Ontology A is a broad class under Person encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. 'Student lecturer' in Ontology B is a very specific subclass of Lecturer (and ultimately Delegate/Place). The student lecturer concept is far more specific than conference contributor, and they do not share the same intended instances; thus they are unrelated for alignment purposes.

Although both are datatype properties mapping to string and serve as 'name/title' properties, their domains are disjoint: has_title applies to Social event and Working event, while hasName applies to Conference. They relate different kinds of entities and thus are not equivalent.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution they wrote, while property B (reviewOfPaper) relates a Review to the Paper it reviews. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Social event is a type of conference event (e.g., banquet, reception), while Hotel room is a type of place/accommodation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' representing the conference website (with a URL property). In Ontology B, 'Conference' represents the actual conference event itself (with dates, members, topics, etc.). These are entirely different concepts.

'organises' in ekaw relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise, while 'give' in iasted relates a Person to an Activity or Item they give (e.g., present). These denote different roles/relations in the conference domain: organising vs. giving/presenting.

Both properties express a publishing relationship but in opposite directions: 'has a publisher' goes from proceedings to publisher, while 'publisher Of' goes from organisation (publisher) to published documents. Since they are inverses rather than equivalent, and their domains/ranges differ slightly (Conference proceedings vs Flyer/Multi-author Volume/etc.), they are related.
Property A links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (paper), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (person). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Abstract is a type of conference document (a summary of a paper), while Time is a temporal concept with children like Deadline and Conference days. They are completely unrelated.

eventOnList is an object property linking an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site, while Start_of_conference is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Computer Networks Security Topic is a subject area for papers, while Sponsor state is a status/state of a sponsor. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee is a general participant in a conference (parent: Person), while Program Chair is a specific organizational role responsible for the program (parent: Organizator). They represent distinct concepts with no subsumption relationship.

Registeered applicant is a subclass of Person representing someone who has registered to apply to a conference, while Working event is a subclass of Event representing academic sessions like conferences, tutorials, and workshops. They are entirely different concepts.

hasPostalCode is a datatype property linking Contact Information to a string (postal code), while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.
hasMenu relates a Meal Event to a Meal Menu, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

A 'Co chair' is a co-chair of a committee (subclass of Committee member), while B 'Conference Chair' is the overall chair of the conference (direct subclass of Person). They are distinct leadership roles in the conference domain; they overlap conceptually as chairs but are not equivalent.

Property A 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing action), while property B 'prepare' relates a Person to an Item (preparation action). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Final manuscript is a type of submission document, while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Contribution co author is a role related to paper authorship, while Single hotel room is an accommodation type. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A is the abstract text of a Contribution (paper), while property B is the name of a Conference. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes; they are completely unrelated.

In Ontology A, Poster is a type of conference contribution (a document/artefact), whereas in Ontology B, Poster Session is a type of event/session during which posters are presented. They are related but not equivalent since one is a document and the other is an event.
Author is a Person who writes contributions, while Web Site is a Document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Both are datatype properties with domain Person and range string. 'has Surname' and 'has Last Name' are synonymous terms referring to the family name of a person.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Conference Member which is a subclass of Person. In sigkdd, Person is the top-level class for people with children Listener, Organizator, and Speaker. Thus cmt:Author is a more specific concept subsumed by sigkdd:Person.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a 'Review preference' (a reviewer's bidding/preference for reviewing), while Property B links a Paper to an actual 'Review' (the completed review document). These represent different stages and concepts in the review process: preference assignment vs. having a review.

Short paper in confOf is a specific type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster). Submitted Paper in ekaw classifies papers by their lifecycle status (submitted vs camera-ready). A short paper may or may not be submitted, and a submitted paper may or may not be short. They overlap but are not equivalent, nor does one strictly subsume the other.

Property A links a Steering committee to a Conference volume (indicating which conference a steering committee belongs to), while Property B links an Event to an Organisation or Person (indicating who organised the event). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

A 'Call For Manuscripts' is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a type of Deadline (a point in time). They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A ('ends on') specifies the end date of an Event (e.g., a conference session), while property B ('done till') specifies the deadline date for a Deadline. Their domains (Event vs. Deadline) and semantics are fundamentally different in the conference domain.

Both properties express the same relation: a program committee member or reviewer reviewing a paper/contribution. confOf's 'reviewes' links Member PC to Contribution, while edas's 'isReviewing' links Reviewer (and related roles) to Paper. Contribution and Paper are equivalent in this domain, as are Member PC and Reviewer/TPC Member, making these properties equivalent.

A 'Conference announcement' is a type of conference document (informational text), while a 'Talk Event' is a scheduled academic event (an activity). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broader class that includes Active conference participant, Invited speaker, and Regular author as children. Paper Author in ekaw corresponds only to the author role (similar to Regular author). Therefore Conference contributor subsumes Paper Author.
confOf:Topic is the general class for conference topics, while edas:Antennas Topic is a specific subclass of edas:Topic. Therefore confOf:Topic subsumes edas:Antennas Topic.

Both classes represent an Author in the conference domain—someone who writes a paper/contribution. In edas, Author is a direct subclass of Person with properties linking to Paper. In iasted, Author is under Delegate > Speaker, but its children (Author book proceedings included, Author cd proceedings included) confirm it denotes the same concept: a person who authored a conference contribution. Despite different hierarchy placements, their intended instances coincide.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (participant in a conference), while Conference city in iasted is a City (location of a conference). They are entirely different concepts.
'has gender' and 'has First Name' are both datatype properties on Person but capture entirely different attributes (gender vs. first name). They are unrelated.

Workshop and Track are distinct types of conference events. In ekaw, Workshop is a sibling of Track under Scientific Event, confirming they represent different concepts. A workshop is a focused interactive session, while a track is a thematic strand within a conference.

Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (an activity/session at a conference), while Tutorial Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (an abstract for a tutorial). They belong to entirely different categories (event vs. document) and are unrelated.
'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a date string, while 'Name' links a Person to a name string. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

'Introduction of speaker' is a conference activity (event) in iasted, while 'Invited Speaker' is a person role in sigkdd. They belong to entirely different categories (Activity vs Person) and are unrelated.
Multi-author Volume is a type of Document (e.g., proceedings), while Author is a Person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper) representing the abstract text of a paper, while Multimedia Topic is a subject area (a subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a specific version/type of a Paper (a document), while Call for paper in Conference is a type of Conference document used to solicit submissions. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasVAT refers to value added tax for events, while hasPostalCode refers to a postal code in contact information. They have different domains, ranges semantics, and meanings.
Conference participant is a Person who attends the conference, while Conference Session is an Event (a scheduled session). They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

acceptedBy links a Paper to an Administrator (acceptance decision), while paperPresentedAs links a Paper/Abstract to an Individual Presentation (presentation format). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while reviewes links a PC Member to a Contribution (reviewing relation). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has authors' links a conference document to its author (Person), while 'has Related Document' links various entities (events, persons, etc.) to a related document. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Acceptance is a subclass of Decision (a classification/outcome), whereas in iasted, Accepting manuscript is a subclass of Activity before conference (a process/action). They represent different ontological perspectives on the same domain event—outcome vs. activity—so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A links an active conference participant (a person) to a presentation they give, while property B links a paper/abstract to the individual presentation it is presented as. The domains are fundamentally different (person vs. document), so these properties are not equivalent.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants, with children Active and Passive conference participant. Workshop Chair (B) is a specific role under Conference Participant in ekaw. Thus A subsumes B.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'for Event' links a Call to an Academic Event, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They describe unrelated relations in the conference domain.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution), while ekaw:Rejected_Paper is a very specific subclass representing only papers that have been evaluated and rejected. The general Paper class subsumes Rejected Paper.
Property A links a conference volume to its steering committee, while property B links a person to an item they sign. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'need' relates a Person to an Item. These are semantically different relations with different domains and ranges.
Session Chair in edas is a Person role (someone who chairs a session), while Workshop Session in ekaw is an Event (a type of session). They are entirely different concepts.

In edas, Social Event is a general class with children Excursion and Reception. In ekaw, Conference Banquet is a specific type of Social Event (sibling to Conference Trip). The edas Social Event class is more general and subsumes the ekaw Conference Banquet concept.

Published Paper in edas denotes a paper that has been published (a lifecycle/status classification), while Poster Paper in ekaw denotes a paper submitted/presented as a poster (a format/type classification). These are orthogonal dimensions of paper categorization and do not denote the same concept.

finalizePaperAssignment relates an Administrator to a Conference for finalizing paper assignments, while parallel_with relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

writeReview relates a Reviewer to a Review (authoring a review), while presentationed_by relates a Document to a Speaker (presenting a document). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while has_an_abstract relates a Paper/Poster/Presentation to an Abstract (content). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Chairman is a superclass with children including 'Conference Chair', 'Program Committee Chair', and 'Associated Chair'. In edas, ConferenceChair is a specific role directly under Person. Therefore, cmt:Chairman subsumes edas:ConferenceChair.

Both classes are named 'Organization' and represent organizations in the conference domain. Although their children differ (Company/University vs Academia/Government/Industry/NGO), they cover the same general concept of an organization involved in conferences. The properties differ but both describe organizational attributes or roles. They are equivalent as top-level organization concepts.
A is a deadline for paper submissions (subclass of Deadline), while B is an award category (subclass of Award). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Nonmember registration fee is a monetary fee for non-members. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to a conference, while Hotel room is a subclass of Place representing accommodation. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In cmt, Decision represents the outcome of a paper review (Acceptance or Rejection). In iasted, Activity represents events or tasks related to the conference (before, during, or after). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, Conference is a Scientific Event (one edition of a conference), while in iasted, Conference days is a subclass of Time representing the duration/days of a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. time period) and are unrelated.
Entity A is a document/form (Author information form) used to collect author details, while Entity B is a person role (Author). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Tutorial Chair is a person role (the chair of a tutorial), while Tutorial is an event/activity type. They are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting participation), while a 'Workshop' is an academic event held during a conference. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Call' refers to a call for papers/manuscripts/reviews (an announcement soliciting submissions), with properties like submission deadlines and instructions. In iasted, 'Activity' refers to events or actions such as conference activities, things held before/after a conference, etc. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Reception is a social event (a gathering/party) during a conference, while Departure is an activity after the conference involving leaving. They are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Non speaker is a type of delegate/person who does not present. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event with siblings Tutorial and Workshop, meaning it represents the main conference itself. In edas, Workshop is a type of Academic Event (a sub-event within a conference) with siblings like Paper Presentation and Talk Event. These are distinct concepts: one is the overarching event, the other is a sub-event.

Both are datatype properties assigning a date to an entity, but their domains differ: 'date' applies to Conference while 'is dated on' applies to Activity (which in iasted typically represents events like sessions or presentations, not the conference itself). They serve analogous roles but relate different kinds of things, so they are related rather than equivalent.
'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference, while 'sign' links a Person to an Item. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Person in ekaw represents human individuals (authors, participants, reviewers), while Sponzor in sigkdd represents organizations or entities that sponsor the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a specific subtype of 'Paper' (sibling to 'Paper Abstract'), representing the complete manuscript. In confOf, 'Paper' is a general type of 'Contribution' (sibling to 'Poster' and 'Short paper'). The confOf 'Paper' is more general and would encompass both full versions and abstracts, so cmt's 'Paper Full Version' is subsumed by confOf's 'Paper'.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself (with properties like accepts submissions, has members, etc.). In iasted, 'Conference airport' is a physical building/place (subclass of Building) used as an airport for the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference in Ontology A denotes the conference event/organisation itself, while Conference Hiker in Ontology B is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A (writtenBy) links a Review to its authoring Reviewer, while Property B (belongs_to_a_review_reference) links a Topic to a Review preference. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference volume in Ontology A represents a specific conference event/edition with committees, contributions, and tracks. State in Ontology B is a geographic or administrative location (with children like Conference state, Presenter state) that can be occupied or visited by persons. These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a Person to a document-like entity (Conference document / Document). However, 'contributes' is broader than 'author Of': contributing can include roles beyond authorship (e.g., editing, reviewing), whereas 'author Of' specifically denotes authorship. Thus they are related but not strictly equivalent.
Invited Talk Abstract is a Document (an abstract for an invited talk), while Invited Speaker is a Person (the speaker giving the talk). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

Property A links a Review expertise to a Submitted contribution (indicating which paper an expertise applies to), while Property B links a Person to an Item (indicating authorship). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

confOf:Scholar is a price category for persons studying at a university (a student attendee), while sigkdd:Author_of_paper_student is specifically a student who has authored a paper. They overlap in the 'student' aspect but differ significantly: Scholar need not be an author, and Author_of_paper_student must be an author/speaker. Hence they are related but not equivalent.

Bid represents a reviewer's bid on a paper in the conference review process, while Country represents a geographical nation associated with organizations or persons. These are entirely different concepts.
Conference in confOf is an event (a working event like a tutorial or workshop), while Conference Proceedings in ekaw is a document (a multi-author volume). They are fundamentally different concepts.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history (a record of an individual's publications), while Cd proceening in iasted is a physical publication item (CD proceedings). These are fundamentally different concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference Venue Place is a physical location for the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Property A relates a Committee member to a Committee (membership), while Property B relates a Document to a Person (authorship). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'hasRelatedDocument' is a general association between entities (events, persons) and documents, while 'prepare' denotes the specific act of preparing/creating an item by a person. These are semantically different relations.

Member PC in confOf is a person (reviewer) who reviews contributions, while Textual Review Question in edas is a type of review question (an artefact/form element). These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, Meta Review is a subclass of Review, making it a more specific kind of review (typically a summary review by a meta-reviewer). In edas, Review is the general class for reviews. Therefore, cmt's Meta Review is subsumed by edas's Review.
City is a geographic location class, while Currency is a monetary unit class. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A Steering committee is an organizational group of people responsible for guiding a conference, while a Building is a physical place/structure. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A represents a date associated with a Conference, while property B represents a URL string associated with a Conference www (website). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference applicant in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone applying to attend a conference), while Conference in Ontology B is the event itself with properties like city, start/end dates. These are entirely different concepts.

Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers to a person working for an agency (e.g., publishing or organizing), while Student lecturer in iasted refers to a student who is also a lecturer/speaker at the conference. These are entirely different roles with no semantic overlap.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to an abstract submission date, while Property B is an object property linking a paper/abstract to its presentation format. They are entirely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

Both classes represent the dinner/banquet social event at a conference. In edas it is modeled under Meal Event (a Non Academic Event), and in iasted under Social program (a Conference activity). Their intended instances coincide.

siteURL is a datatype property linking Conference to a URI string, while earlyRegistration is a datatype property linking Participant to a boolean. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'email' property relates a Person to their email address string, while 'Currency' relates a Registration fee to a currency string. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

'Information for participants' is a general class of documents providing information to conference attendees (e.g., announcements, calls), while 'Slide Set' is a specific type of presentation document. They are distinct concepts with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Workshop and Tutorial are distinct types of conference events. In confOf they are siblings under Working event; in ekaw Tutorial is a sibling of Contributed Talk and Invited Talk under Individual Presentation. They represent different concepts.

'Organizator' in sigkdd is clearly a variant spelling of 'Organizer'. Its children (General Chair, Program Chair, Organizing Committee member, etc.) confirm it represents the same concept as Organizer in the Conference ontology.

In cmt, User is a general subclass of Person covering roles like Administrator, Author, and Reviewer who interact with the conference management system. In ekaw, Agency Staff Member is a specific role under Person, likely referring to staff from a funding or publishing agency. These denote different concepts with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.

'has the last name' refers to a person's surname, while 'Nation' refers to a person's country or nationality. These are distinct attributes despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).

Conference announcement is a type of conference document used for announcements, while Computer Networks Sensor Topic is a specific research topic within the computer networks domain. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
A Tutorial is a type of conference event/session, while an LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) responsible for chairing activities, while Session is an event (subclass of Scientific Event) representing a time slot or meeting. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named Document and share the same core children (Abstract, Paper, Review). In both ontologies they represent written artefacts in the conference domain (papers, reviews, abstracts). Although ekaw's Document has additional children (Flyer, Programme Brochure, etc.), the intended instances of the base concept coincide as the general class for conference documents.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference. In ekaw, Regular Session is a specific type of session within a scientific event. These are conceptually distinct: one is the whole conference, the other is a sub-event/session within it.

In Ontology A, Chair is a subclass of Committee member (with Co-chair as sibling), suggesting a general committee chair role. In Ontology B, Conference Chair is a direct subclass of Person and is specifically the chair of the entire conference (initiating calls, etc.). While both represent leadership roles in a conference, 'Chair' in A appears more general (any committee chair) whereas 'Conference Chair' in B is specifically the overall conference chair. They overlap but are not strictly equivalent.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Antennas Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

An 'Extended abstract' is a type of conference contribution (a submission by authors), whereas a 'Review' is an evaluation document written about a submission. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference volume is a class representing a conference event/edition (subclass of Conference), while Participant is a class representing a person attending the conference (subclass of Person). They are entirely different concepts.

Scholar in confOf is a Person subclass (a price category for scholars/students), while Registration fee in sigkdd is a Fee subclass representing monetary charges. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. fee), even though the scholar concept may relate to a student registration fee.

Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Receiving manuscript is an Activity before conference (the actual process of receiving manuscripts). They are related as part of the same submission workflow but represent different concepts: one is the invitation to submit, the other is the act of receiving.

In edas, 'Rated Papers' is a specific subclass of Paper (via Active Paper), representing papers that have already been rated. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers. Therefore, Rated Papers is subsumed by (is more specific than) Paper.

Meta Review is a type of review document (a summary/evaluation of other reviews), while Numerical Review Question is a type of question used in the review form that expects a numerical answer. They are entirely different concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of scientific event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Welcome Talk is a ceremonial opening talk at a conference, while Contributed Talk is a scientific presentation of an accepted paper. Both are types of talks/presentations but serve different purposes and have different intended instances, so they are related (siblings under a broader 'talk' concept) rather than equivalent.

Paper in cmt is a Document (the written submission itself), while Paper Author in ekaw is a Person who authored a paper. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (artefact vs. person) and thus not equivalent, though they are related via authorship.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Conference proceedings is a publication volume containing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a conference volume specifically to its organizing committee, while property B (technicallyOrganisedBy) is a more general relation indicating technical organization of an event by some entity (e.g., an organization or committee). They overlap in intent but differ in specificity and range constraints, so they are related rather than equivalent.

In edas, TalkEvent is a specific subtype of AcademicEvent, which itself is a subtype of ConferenceEvent. In ekaw, Event is the top-level class for all events (with children ScientificEvent and SocialEvent). Therefore, edas:TalkEvent is strictly more specific than ekaw:Event, making it subsumed_by ekaw:Event.

Conference in Ontology A represents the conference event or entity itself (with properties like name and children like Conference volume), while Conference building in Ontology B is a physical place/building where a conference takes place (subclass of Building, sibling to Conference hotel, etc.). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference Venue Place in edas refers to the location where conference sessions/meetings take place (sibling of AccommodationPlace, DiningPlace). Main office in sigkdd likely refers to the administrative/organizational office of the conference. Both are subclasses of Place but denote different specific types of locations within the conference domain, so they are related but not equivalent.
acceptedBy relates a Paper to an Administrator (acceptance action), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (subclass of Person), while Academic Event in edas is a type of Conference Event (e.g., paper presentation, workshop). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

'added By' links a Program Committee Member to an Administrator who added them, while 'occupy' links a Person to a physical location (Building, City, State). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's topic or paper preference, while Participant in confOf refers to a person attending the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Reviewer (A) is a person who reviews papers, while Conference Participant (B) is a broad class for anyone participating in the conference (with children like OC Member, Presenter, Workshop Chair, etc.). They overlap conceptually since reviewers often participate in conferences, but they are not equivalent; Reviewer is more specific and role-focused on reviewing, whereas Conference Participant is a general attendance/participation class.

Both properties express a part-of/association relationship to an event, but they differ in domain: edas:belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, while ekaw:partOfEvent links an Event to another Event (sub-event). Since Programme and Event are not the same class, these properties relate overlapping but distinct concepts.

In Ontology A, Paper is a full regular contribution (with Abstract as a sibling under Conference contribution), while in Ontology B, Abstract is a separate document type that is a sibling of Paper. They denote different concepts: a full paper vs. an abstract summary.

Meal Break and Coffee break are both types of breaks during a conference, but they denote different specific events (a meal vs. coffee). In edas, Meal Break and Coffee Break are siblings under Break Event, confirming they are distinct concepts. They are related as similar kinds of break activities but not equivalent.

Both classes represent the chair of the program committee. 'Program Committee Chair' in cmt and 'Chair PC' in confOf denote the same role: the person leading the program committee. Despite different hierarchical placements (cmt places it under Chairman and Program Committee Member, confOf directly under Person), their intended instances coincide.

'is used by' is an object property linking Item to Person, while 'Nation' is a datatype property linking Person to a string. They have completely different semantics, domains, ranges, and property types.

Sponsorship in edas denotes the financial support or grant itself (with cost amount/currency), while Sponzor in sigkdd denotes the organization or entity providing sponsorship (with tiers like Gold, Silver). They are related concepts (sponsor provides sponsorship) but not equivalent; one is an act/resource and the other is an agent.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering), while 'hasAttendee' in edas relates a Conference Event to a Person (participation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their email string, while Property B is an object property linking a Document to its author (Person). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'writtenBy' links a Contribution to its Author (authorship), while 'need' links a Person to an Item (requirement). These are semantically completely different relations.

'starts on' is a datatype property linking an Event to a string (a date), while 'part Of Event' is an object property linking an Event to another Event (mereological part-of). They have different domains/ranges and entirely different semantics.

Textual Review Question in edas is a type of question used in a review form (a template element), whereas Neutral Review in ekaw is a classification of an actual review document based on its sentiment. These are fundamentally different concepts.

A Review is an evaluation of a submission, while an Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are distinct document types in the conference domain. Note that sigkdd even has its own separate Review class as a sibling of Abstract, confirming they are different concepts.
The 'title' property in cmt assigns a string title to a Paper, while the 'Date' property in sigkdd assigns a dateTime to a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Conference is a top-level working event (sibling of Tutorial and Workshop), representing the entire conference. In ekaw, Industrial Session is a specific type of session within a conference. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

hasStreet is a datatype property for the street address within Contact Information, while Name is a datatype property for a Person's name. They have different domains and represent entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference for running assignment tools, while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker for presentations. They are unrelated.

Possible Reviewer in ekaw represents a person who may review papers (parent of PC Member), while Author in sigkdd represents a person who writes/submits papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

The two properties describe entirely different relations: 'paperAssignmentToolsRunBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who runs paper assignment tools, while 'presentationOfPaper' links an Individual Presentation to the Paper/Abstract being presented. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'has a degree' is a datatype property on Review preference with range int (likely indicating academic degree level), while 'has Biography' is a datatype property on Person with range string. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
