Property A relates a Conference part to a Conference volume (publication/proceedings structure), while Property B relates an Event to another Event (temporal/organizational hierarchy). These are entirely different domain concepts and relations.
A 'Full day tour' is an activity/event occurring after a conference, while 'Main office' is a physical place. They belong to entirely different categories and share no semantic overlap.

Property A links Money to Item (is paid with), while Property B links Person to Registration fee (pay). They have completely different domains and ranges and express different relations in the conference domain.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (review assignment), while property B links an author to a paper (submission action). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a specific subtype of 'Contribution', with siblings 'Paper' (full paper) and 'Poster'. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is a general class under 'Document' representing submitted papers. A short paper is a kind of paper, so confOf:Short_paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Paper, but they are not equivalent since sigkdd:Paper also includes full/regular papers.
Late paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a conference registrant who paid late), while Renting is a subclass of Activity before conference. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'is needed for' relates an Item to a Person (requirement). They share no conceptual overlap.

Reviewer and Author are distinct roles in the conference domain. A Reviewer evaluates papers while an Author writes them. They share the same parent class (Person) but have different intended instances and properties.

In ekaw, 'Session Chair' is a role for chairing a session (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member). In iasted, 'Hotel presenter' is a subclass of Delegate under the Place > Building > Conference building hierarchy, indicating someone presenting at a hotel venue. These are entirely different concepts; note that iasted has its own separate 'Session chair' sibling class.

Two Level Conference is a type of conference (subclass of Conference), while Registration Student is a type of registration fee (subclass of Fee/Registration fee). They belong to entirely different branches of the domain and share no semantic overlap.
hasFirstName is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while done_till links a Deadline to a date. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the Administrator role in a conference management system, subclassing Person (directly or via User). In cmt, Administrator handles tasks like accepting papers, adding PC members, and entering conference details. In confOf, Administrator is annotated with 'confTool', indicating it serves the same administrative function. Despite different sibling structures, their intended instances coincide as the system administrators of the conference platform.

A Contributed Talk is a regular paper presentation by an author, while a Plenary Lecture is typically a keynote or invited talk for all attendees. In ekaw, Invited Talk is a sibling of Contributed Talk, and Plenary lecture is closer to an invited/keynote talk. They are both types of individual presentations/lectures at a conference, so they are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, Conference Member is a broad class encompassing Authors, Reviewers, Chairs, and PC Members (anyone participating in the conference). In ekaw, OC Member specifically denotes an Organising Committee member, which is only one type of conference participant. Thus, cmt:Conference Member subsumes ekaw:OC Member.

Accommodation Place is a location (subclass of Place) where attendees can stay, while Hotel presenter is a type of person/role (subclass of Delegate). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
Subject Area represents a research topic or field of study for papers, while City represents a geographical location. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while follows links an Administrative event to another Administrative event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

City in confOf is a geographic location class (range of hasCity for Organization/Person), while Contact Information in edas is a broader class representing contact details (email, phone, street, postal code, and city as a string property). They are conceptually different: one is a place, the other is a bundle of contact data.

Property A 'follows' relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering), while property B 'has Programme' relates a Conference Event to a Programme (composition/association). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Hotel fee and Registration fee are distinct types of fees in the conference domain. They share a common parent (Fee) but refer to different concepts: one is for accommodation, the other for conference registration.

Ontology A's 'Committee' is a general class with children including Organizing committee, Program committee, and Steering committee. Ontology B's 'Program Committee' is a specific subclass of Committee. Therefore, A's Committee subsumes B's Program Committee.

Author in cmt is a person role (subclass of Conference Member and User) who writes/submits papers. Conference document in the Conference ontology is a class of documents (with children like Call for paper, Review, etc.). A person role and a document are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a Review to the paper/contribution being reviewed. 'Reviewed contribution' in Conference and 'Paper' in ekaw serve the same role as the range (the artefact under review), and both share the same domain (Review). They express the same relation in the conference domain.
'has the first name' captures a person's given name, while 'Nation' captures their nationality or country. These are distinct attributes of a Person and do not denote the same relation.
Property A links a contribution to the conference volume it was submitted at, while property B links a contribution to a topic it deals with. Different ranges and different semantics.

Associated Chair is a type of chairman/organizer role in the conference committee, while Plenary lecture speaker is a specific type of speaker/presenter. These are entirely different roles with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

Location in ekaw is a general class for places where events are held. Hotel in sigkdd is a specific type of Place (sibling to Conference hall and Main office). A Location subsumes a Hotel since a hotel is one kind of location, but they are not equivalent because Location is more general.

In the conference domain, 'Subject Area' (cmt) and 'Topic' (Conference) both denote the thematic categories or research areas that papers/submissions are classified under and that conference parts (tracks, workshops) are organized around. The properties confirm this: cmt's Paper has SubjectArea maps to Conference's Submitted contribution has a topic, and Conference's Topic is linked to Conference parts just as subject areas would be.
Property A (relatedToPaper) links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper, while property B (write) links a Person to an Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Early paid applicant is a very specific subclass of a registered/paid conference applicant (Person > Conference applicant > Registered applicant > Paid applicant > Early paid applicant). Participant in confOf is a general class for all conference participants (Person > Participant) with children like Member, Regular, Student. Every early paid applicant would be a participant, but not every participant is an early paid applicant, so A is subsumed by B.

Conference Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person) responsible for chairing the conference, while Proceedings Publisher is an organisation that publishes the proceedings. They are entirely different concepts in both kind and function.

In Ontology A, 'Chair' is a generic committee chair with a sibling 'Co chair', while in Ontology B (sigkdd), 'Program Chair' is a specific role alongside 'General Chair'. Since sigkdd distinguishes Program Chair from General Chair, the generic 'Chair' in Conference does not exactly coincide with 'Program Chair'; they overlap but are not strictly equivalent.

Call For Papers is a type of Call (an announcement soliciting submissions), while Review is a type of Document (an evaluation of a paper). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Document in ekaw represents written artefacts (papers, reviews, etc.), while Money in iasted represents financial entities (fees, sponsorships). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Operating Topicsystems is a specific research topic (a subclass of Topic) in the edas ontology, while Modelling is a type of research activity (subclass of Research/Activity) in the iasted ontology. They belong to different conceptual categories (topic vs. activity) and are unrelated.

Active conference participant in Ontology A is a broader class that includes anyone who actively contributes (e.g., gives presentations), with siblings like Invited speaker and Regular author. Speaker in Ontology B specifically denotes someone who speaks/presents. While they overlap significantly (both involve presenting), Active conference participant is more general than Speaker, and the two ontologies structure their hierarchies differently. They are related but not strictly equivalent.
hasCity links an Organization or Person to a City, while hasReview links a Paper to a Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Rejected contribution is a submitted paper/contribution that was rejected after review, while Abstract in sigkdd is a type of document (summary) alongside Paper and Review. These are entirely different concepts.

paperInVolume relates a paper to the volume it appears in, while presentationed_by relates a document to the speaker who presents it. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and are not equivalent or related in the ontology alignment sense.

Paper is a scholarly contribution submitted to a conference, while Mailing list is a communication document/list. They are entirely different concepts despite both being subclasses of Document in their respective ontologies.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a Social Event (an excursion/trip for attendees), while Technic activity in iasted refers to technical conference activities (e.g., lectures, presentations). These are conceptually distinct types of conference events with no overlap.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Contribution to its abstract text (string), while property B links a Deadline to a date indicating when it is done. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'remark' property in confOf is a datatype property on Contribution (a paper/submission) for general remarks, while 'hasSubmissionInstructions' in edas is a datatype property on Call providing submission instructions. They have different domains and entirely different semantics.
Member PC in confOf is a person (a reviewer), while Review in edas is a document (the written review itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.
Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while Multimedia Topic is a subject area/topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

writePaper relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while presentationOfPaper relates an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract (presentation schedule). These are entirely different relations with different domains and semantics.

Conference Event in edas is an event/activity (with location, start/end time, programme), while Conference Participant in ekaw is a person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is 'Program Committee Member' (a person who serves on the program committee), while Entity B is 'Program Committee' (the committee/group itself). A member belongs to a committee, but they are not the same concept. They are related via membership.

Property A ('has amount of') links Money to an integer representing the numeric amount, while Property B ('Currency') links Registration fee to a string representing the currency type. They capture different aspects (amount vs. currency) and have different domains and ranges, so they are unrelated.
has_an_email relates a Person to their email address, while hasLastName relates a Person to their last name. These are entirely different attributes despite sharing the same domain and range types.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC member to a contribution they review, while property B (is paid for) links money to an activity or item it pays for. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Reception as a type of Social Event within the conference domain. Their paths (Event > Social event > Reception vs Conference Event > Non Academic Event > Social Event > Reception) and sibling classes (Banquet/Trip vs Excursion) confirm they denote the same concept.

Program committee in Ontology A is a Committee (a group/organizational entity), while Possible Reviewer in Ontology B is a Person who may review papers. These are fundamentally different kinds of entities (group vs. individual) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'reviewerBiddingStartedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator regarding the bidding process, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution regarding authorship.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Sponsor company house is a building/place. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Both properties link a paper/contribution to a person involved in writing it, and Paper~Contribution are equivalent classes. However, hasCo-author specifically targets a Co-author (a secondary author), while writtenBy targets an Author in general. Thus they overlap but are not strictly equivalent; writtenBy is more general.
Tutorial Abstract is a document (an abstract for a tutorial), while Tutorial speaker is a person who delivers a tutorial. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A (writtenBy) links a Contribution to its Author, while property B (reviewOfPaper) links a Review to the Paper it reviews. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Student is a subclass of Person representing an academic role, while Silver Supporter is a subclass of Sponsor representing a sponsorship tier. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in cmt, while NGO is a type of Organization in edas. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Regular Session is a type of event (a session at a conference). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
hasCountry links a Conference to a Country, while is_visited_by links a location (Building/City/State) to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference contributor in Ontology A is a subclass of Person (someone who contributes to a conference), while Conference in Ontology B is the event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Review' is a conference document that reviews a contribution (the actual review text/artefact). In Ontology B, 'Review Question' represents a question or criterion used within a review form (e.g., numerical or textual questions), not the review itself. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Poster Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Entity A is 'Steering committee', a specific subclass of Committee in ontology Conference. Entity B is 'Committee', the general parent class in ontology sigkdd (with children like Organizing Committee and Program Committee). Therefore, Steering committee is subsumed by Committee.

Both properties link a Person to a document/item in the conference domain (contributes vs send). They share the same domain (Person) and similar ranges (Conference document vs Item), but 'contributes' implies authorship or intellectual contribution while 'send' implies a submission or transmission action. They overlap in context but are not strictly equivalent.

In confOf, Trip is a subclass of Social event (with siblings Banquet and Reception). In iasted, Social program is the broader class encompassing social activities like Dinner banquet and Coctail reception. Thus, Trip (a specific type of social event) is subsumed by Social program (the general category of social activities at a conference).

In Ontology A, Abstract is a very specific subclass deep in the hierarchy (Conference document > Conference contribution > Regular contribution > Extended abstract > Abstract). In Ontology B, Document is a general class whose children include Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus, the concept of Abstract in A is subsumed by the broader concept of Document in B.

NGO (Non-Governmental Organization) is a specific type of organization defined by its non-governmental nature, while Organising Agency is an organization that organises the conference. These are conceptually distinct; an NGO is not necessarily an organising agency and vice versa.

endDate specifically denotes the end date/time of a Conference, while is_dated_on is a more general property linking an Activity to a dateTime. They overlap in purpose (associating an event with a date) but differ in specificity and semantics (end vs. generic date), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Company is an organization type (subclass of Organization), while Satellite And Space Communications Topic is a research topic (subclass of Topic). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Dining Place in edas is a specific subclass of Place (a location for dining), while Place in iasted is a general top-level class encompassing buildings, conference halls, hotel rooms, etc. Therefore, Dining Place is subsumed by the more general Place class.

Student is a subclass of Person representing an academic participant, while Exhibitor is a subclass of Sponsor (Sponzor) representing an organization or entity that exhibits at the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

CAD Topic is a specific subject area (Computer-Aided Design) under Topic, while Program Committee is an organizational body under Committee. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Conference is a specific type of Working event, sibling to Tutorial and Workshop. In edas, AcademicEvent is a broader category that includes Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop, etc. They overlap (both can encompass workshops and presentations) but are not equivalent: confOf's Conference is a top-level event type while edas's AcademicEvent is a category of conference-related activities. They are related but neither strictly subsumes the other.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (membership relation), while organisedBy links an Event to an Organisation or Person (organizing relation). These properties have different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Chairman is a person role (subclass of Person) while Scientific Event is a type of event (subclass of Event). They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Meal Event is a non-academic event involving meals (e.g., conference dinner), while Scientific Event is an academic event (e.g., sessions, workshops, presentations). They are disjoint concepts within the conference domain.

Both classes represent a Review document in the conference domain. In Ontology A it is a subclass of Conference document and is linked to reviewed contributions; in Ontology B it is a subclass of Document alongside Abstract and Paper. The intended instances (review documents for papers) coincide.
The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'is used for' links an Item to an Activity or Money, while 'can stay in' links a Person to a Place.

'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously, while 'organises' relates an organisation or person to an event they organise. These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Company is an Organization (a type of institution), while Sponzorship is a form of Money (financial support). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Reviewer (Ontology A) is a person who reviews papers, while Speaker (Ontology B) is a person who gives presentations. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no equivalence or subsumption relationship.
Refusing manuscript is an activity (the act of rejecting a paper), while Author is a person role. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Demo Chair is a person who chairs/organizes demo sessions at a conference, while Tutorial speaker is a person who presents a tutorial. These are entirely different roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.
belongsToEvent links a Programme to a Conference Event, while organisedBy links an Event to an Organisation or Person. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, while Property B links a Person to an Activity or Item. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Property A links a Program Committee to its Program Committee Members, while Property B links a Conference to Persons in general. The domains (Program Committee vs Conference) and ranges (Program Committee Member vs Person) differ significantly, so they are not equivalent relations.

'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person who signs it, while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to a Person who pays it. These are different actions on different kinds of entities and do not denote the same relation.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (paper), while Registration SIGMOD Member is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

Contribution 1th author refers to the first/primary author of a conference contribution, while Author of paper student refers to a student author. These are distinct specializations of authors based on different criteria (author order vs. student status) and do not denote the same concept.

Presenter in ekaw is a general conference participant who presents (with Invited Speaker as a subclass). Hotel presenter in iasted is a very specific subtype of delegate who presents from a hotel (likely remote/virtual). The iasted ontology also has a separate 'Speaker' class. Thus, Hotel presenter is much more specific than Presenter; they overlap but are not equivalent.
Pending Paper is a status of a paper (Document > Paper), while Submissions deadline is a temporal deadline (Time > Deadline). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Sponsor in iasted is a general class for sponsors (under Person), while Gold Supporter in sigkdd is a specific type of sponsor/supporter. Therefore, Sponsor subsumes Gold Supporter.

'Information for participants' is a broad category of conference documents intended for all participants (including attendees, reviewers, etc.), while 'Author information form' is a specific form targeted at authors. They overlap in purpose but are not equivalent; the former is more general and could subsume the latter, but given different parent hierarchies and scopes, 'related' is most appropriate.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while is_present relates a Person to a Time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Proceedings is a document/publication type. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Entity A is a 'Call for participation', which is a type of conference document (an announcement or invitation). Entity B is a 'Conference', which is a type of working event. A document calling for participation and the conference event itself are fundamentally different concepts in the domain.

'has Conference Member' links a Conference to its members (people participating), while 'holded by' links a Conference to its organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These relate fundamentally different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

Property A ('parallel with') relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur in parallel, while Property B ('has Location') relates a Conference Event to a Place to indicate its location. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor (an entity that exhibits at the conference). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Multi-author Volume is a type of document (e.g., proceedings), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Entity A is 'Review' (a review document) while Entity B is 'Paper' (a submitted/conference paper). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain. In fact, ontology B (ekaw) has its own 'Review' class as a sibling of 'Paper', confirming they are different entities.

Both properties relate to expertise in the conference domain, but they differ significantly: A is a datatype property on 'Review expertise' (likely indicating a level of expertise), while B is an object property linking a PC member to a Topic they are expert on. They capture related concepts but are not equivalent.

Student non speaker is a type of delegate (person attending but not speaking), while Registration Non Member is a type of registration fee (monetary amount). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.
Currency is a monetary unit class, while Person represents human individuals (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
The property 'title' gives the title of a Paper (string), while 'has amount of' gives the numeric amount of Money (int). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

SC Member in ekaw is a Steering Committee member (a type of PC Member involved in conference organization), while Author in iasted is someone who writes papers/presentations. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence.
'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item (acquisition). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

In cmt, Paper is a direct subclass of Document and represents papers in general. In ekaw, Regular Paper is a specific type of Paper (which itself is under Document). Therefore, cmt:Paper is more general and subsumes ekaw:Regular_Paper.

Conference Event in edas represents an event or activity occurring at a conference (with dates, programmes, attendees), whereas City in iasted represents a geographical location. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Social program is a type of conference activity (event), while Program Chair is a role held by a person. They are entirely different concepts.

In ontology A, 'Organization' is a general class for organizations. In ekaw, 'Organising Agency' is a specific subclass of 'Organisation' (with siblings like Academic Institution and Proceedings Publisher), representing only those organisations that organise the conference. Thus, the general 'Organization' subsumes the more specific 'Organising Agency'.

Session Chair in edas is a Person role (someone who chairs a session), while Session in iasted is an Activity/Event (a type of lecture). They are fundamentally different concepts: one is a person, the other is an event.

In cmt, Document is a superclass of both Paper and Review. In ekaw, Review is a subclass of Document. Therefore, cmt:Document subsumes ekaw:Review, as the former includes reviews (and papers) while the latter is specifically reviews.

Property A relates two Administrative events (parallel scheduling), while Property B relates a Person to a Conference Event (attendance). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a broad class encompassing all people involved in the conference (chairs, presenters, registered participants, etc.), while Author in iasted is a specific role (a speaker who authored something). Conference Participant subsumes Author.

Committee member in Ontology A is a general class for any member of a committee (with children Chair and Co-chair), while Conference Chair in Ontology B is a specific leadership role. They overlap conceptually (a conference chair is typically a committee member) but are not equivalent; Committee member is more general.
Workshop Paper is a type of academic document/paper, while Shuttle bus is a type of transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links an Organizing committee to a Conference volume (the event it organizes), while Property B links a Conference to ACM SIGKDD (the organization that holds/sponsors it). They relate different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

confOf:Paper is a general class for all papers (a type of Contribution), while edas:WithdrawnPaper is a specific status subclass of Paper representing only those papers that have been withdrawn. Thus confOf:Paper subsumes edas:WithdrawnPaper.

Both classes are named 'Person' and serve as the top-level class for human participants in the conference domain. They share similar properties (first name, last name, email) and have analogous subclasses (Reviewer, Author/Contributor, Chair roles, Committee/TPC Member, Attendee/Participant). Their intended instances coincide.

Conference participant (A) is a broad class covering all persons participating in a conference (active or passive). Program Committee member (B) is a specific role within the organizing structure. Every Program Committee member is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is a PC member, so A subsumes B.

Pending Paper refers to a paper's review status (awaiting decision), while Industrial Paper refers to a paper's track/category (industry-focused). These are orthogonal classifications with no semantic overlap.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, while property B links a Review to a Possible Reviewer. Both concern the relationship between review artefacts and reviewers, but they operate on different domain classes (Personal Review History vs Review) and thus are not equivalent. They are related as they both capture reviewer-review associations.

Call For Papers is a type of Call (an announcement inviting submissions), while Review is a Document representing the evaluation of a submission. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Associated Chair in cmt is a type of Chairman (a leadership role), while IASTED member in iasted is a type of Delegate (an attendee/participant). These represent different roles in the conference domain and are not equivalent.
A's Topic is a general class for conference topics, while B's CAD Topic is a specific subclass of Topic in edas (with siblings like Antennas Topic, etc.). Therefore A subsumes B.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Medicine Topic' is a subject area classification within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Both properties represent a phone number as a string, but they have different domains: confOf's hasPhone applies directly to Person, while edas's hasPhone applies to Contact Information (which is associated with a person). They are semantically related but not equivalent due to the domain mismatch.

Rejected contribution and Accepted Paper are opposite outcomes in the review process. One denotes a contribution that was rejected, while the other denotes a paper that was accepted. They are disjoint concepts, not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Late Registered Participant is a type of person (a conference participant). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote unrelated concepts.
The properties have different ranges (Time vs Place) and different semantics: 'is present' relates a person to a time, while 'can stay in' relates a person to a place. They are unrelated.

PC Chair (Program Committee Chair) in ekaw and Program Chair in sigkdd both denote the person who chairs the program committee of a conference. Despite different parent classes (Conference Participant vs Organizator), their intended instances coincide.

Working event in confOf refers to academic/program events (Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Break Event in edas refers to non-academic breaks (Coffee Break, Meal Break). These are disjoint concepts within the conference domain.
'write Paper' relates an Author to a Paper (authorship), while 'sign' relates a Person to an Item (signing). These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.

'Information for participants' in Conference ontology refers to logistical/administrative documents for attendees (sibling of Call for paper, Conference announcement), while 'Abstract' in sigkdd is a summary of a paper (sibling of Paper, Review). These are entirely different concepts.
'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'relatesTo' relates a Document to events, conferences, sessions, or persons. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Paper is a subclass of Document and represents papers submitted to the conference (evidenced by properties like hasDecision, assignedTo, hasBid). In ekaw, Submitted_Paper is a subclass of Paper (which is a subclass of Document) representing papers that have been submitted. Despite the slight difference in hierarchy depth, both classes denote the same concept: a paper submitted to a conference for review. The OAEI reference alignment treats these as equivalent.

Both properties link a Paper to a reviewer entity, but 'assignedTo' in cmt denotes an actual assignment to a Reviewer, while 'hasReviewer' in ekaw links to a Possible_Reviewer (a candidate pool). The range semantics differ (assigned vs potential), so they are related but not strictly equivalent.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review certain topics/papers, while Person in Ontology B is a general class representing human individuals. These are entirely different concepts with no meaningful overlap.
Company is an organization type (business entity), while Shuttle bus is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and share no semantic overlap.
Property A gives the first name of a Person (string), while property B gives the amount of Money (int). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a Paper in the conference domain: a scholarly document submitted by authors. In Ontology A it is a Regular contribution under Conference contribution, and in Ontology B it is a Document that can be submitted by an Author. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances (submitted conference papers) coincide.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Measurements) while B is an organizational committee responsible for organizing a conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
'is Written By' relates a Paper to its Author, while 'is visited by' relates a location (Building, City, State) to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both properties relate a person/speaker to their presentation activity in the conference domain, but they differ significantly: 'speak in' has range Place and Time (where/when someone speaks), while 'presentation' has range Document (what is presented). They overlap conceptually around the act of presenting but are not equivalent due to different ranges and semantics.
writtenBy relates a Document to its author (Person), while pay relates a Person to a Registration fee. They describe entirely different relationships in the conference domain.
'initiates' relates conference roles (Chair, TPC Member) to a Call, while 'held In' relates an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In iasted, Building is a subclass of Place, while in sigkdd, Place is the top-level class for locations (with children Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). The iasted Building class covers physical structures like hotels and conference buildings, which aligns with sigkdd's broader Place concept. Thus, iasted:Building is subsumed by sigkdd:Place.
hasRating links a paper to its review rating, while go_through links an item to an activity it undergoes. These are semantically distinct relations with different domains and ranges.

Sponsor company house is a building associated with a sponsoring company (under Building), while Hotel is an accommodation place. They are distinct types of places in the conference domain with no hierarchical or semantic overlap.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Security Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (e.g., authoring a paper), while 'obtain' relates an Author to an Award (receiving an award). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Property A links a submitted contribution to its review expertise level (domain: Submitted contribution, range: Review expertise), while Property B links a reviewer to their personal review history (domain: Reviewer, range: Personal Review History). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, Abstract is a very specific subclass deep in the hierarchy (under Extended abstract > Regular contribution > Conference contribution), representing just the abstract text of a paper/poster/presentation. In Ontology B, Contribution is a top-level class representing any submitted work (with children Paper, Poster, Short paper). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a small component of a submission, the other is the submission itself.

Property A (rejectedBy) links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while property B (relatedToPaper) links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Active_conference_participant in Conference is a broad class covering anyone who actively contributes (gives presentations), including Invited speakers and Regular authors as siblings/children. Author in sigkdd is specifically someone who submits papers, with Speaker as its parent. They overlap significantly (authors are active participants) but are not equivalent: Active_conference_participant is broader (includes invited speakers who may not be authors), while Author is narrower (specifically paper submitters). Hence 'related'.

Submitted contribution is a type of conference document (a paper that has been submitted), while Deadline Author notification is a temporal deadline for notifying authors. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A 'name' is a string-valued datatype property for naming conferences or persons, while property B 'early Registration' is a boolean-valued datatype property indicating whether a participant registered early. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman/Person) responsible for leading a conference, while Government Organization is a type of organization. They are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Session is a type of scientific event (a time slot for presentations), while Program Committee is an organizational body responsible for reviewing papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'locationOf' relates a Location to an Event, while 'is_sent_after' relates an Item to a Time.
Property A links a Conference to an Administrator for entering review criteria, while property B links a Person to an Item for writing. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The 'name' property in cmt assigns a name string to a Conference or Person, while 'hasSubmissionInstructions' in edas provides submission instruction text for a Call. They have completely different domains, ranges (semantically), and purposes.

Entity A is a type of conference document (informational material for participants), while Entity B is a type of administrative event (the registration process). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event) and are not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Invited Talk Abstract is a type of document (abstract for an invited talk) in ekaw. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Entity A (Author in edas) is a general class for all authors of papers. Entity B (Author book proceedings included in iasted) is a specific subclass of Author representing only those whose work is included in the book proceedings. Therefore, A subsumes B.

Both properties represent an end date/time, but they have different domains: 'is an ending date' applies to 'Important dates' (e.g., deadlines), while 'endDate' applies to 'Conference' (the conference event itself). They are semantically related as both denote ending dates, but not equivalent due to differing domains and intended usage.

Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Conference building in iasted is a physical place/building where the conference is held. They are entirely different concepts.

Reviewer in cmt is a person who reviews papers (child of Conference Member), while Scholar in confOf refers to a price category for attendees/students ('price category - scholar') with a 'study At' property pointing to University. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Conference Chair' is a sibling of 'TPC Member', indicating it refers to the overall conference chair (general chair), not the program committee chair. In ekaw, 'PC Chair' is explicitly a subclass of 'PC Member', denoting the head of the program committee. These are distinct roles in conference organization, though they overlap as senior organizers.

Review in ontology A is a document that reviews a contribution, while Review Rating in ontology B is an evaluation score (e.g., accept/reject) assigned to a paper. These are distinct concepts: one is the review text itself, the other is a rating outcome.
A Textual Review Question is a type of question used in the review process, while a Final manuscript is a submitted document/paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

paperDueOn is a specific datatype property on Conference for the paper submission deadline (dateTime), while done_till is a general datatype property on Deadline for any deadline's date. They are related in that both express deadline dates, but they differ in domain specificity and generality.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

A 'Conference applicant' is a person applying to attend or register for the conference (with child 'Registeered applicant'), whereas a 'Conference Chair' is a senior organizer who initiates calls and oversees reviewing. These are entirely different roles.

A 'Dining Place' is a location for meals/eating, while a 'Conference hall' is a venue for conference sessions or events. They serve entirely different purposes within the conference domain and are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.

hasAuthor (Paper -> Author) and submit (Author -> Paper) are inverse properties: they relate the same domain concepts but in opposite directions. Per the guidelines, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

Both classes represent the concept of an Author in a conference domain. In edas, Author is a subclass of Person who writes papers (is Written By). In sigkdd, Author is a subclass of Speaker (which is a subclass of Person) who submits papers. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide: people who author/submit papers to a conference.
The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'covers Topic' relates an Event or Paper to a Research Topic. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'follows' in confOf relates an Administrative event to another Administrative event (temporal ordering), while 'forEvent' in edas relates a Call to an Academic Event (association). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Invited speaker is a Person (a conference contributor), while Introduction of speaker is an Activity (a type of introduction event). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

hasEmail relates a Person to their email address (string), while hasPostalCode relates Contact Information to a postal code (string). These are entirely different properties with different domains and semantics.
paperID is a datatype property on Paper (unsignedLong) identifying a paper, while Name is a datatype property on Person (string) naming a person. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Workshop Session is a type of scientific event/session, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes represent the published proceedings of a conference. 'Conference Proceedings' in ekaw and 'Book proceeding' in iasted denote the same concept: a volume containing the papers presented at a conference.

Conference contributor (A) is a Person who contributes to the conference (e.g., author, speaker). IASTED non member (B) is a Delegate who is not an IASTED member. While both represent people involved in a conference, 'non member' refers to membership status rather than contribution role. They overlap (a contributor could be a non-member) but are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of scientific event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Conference Venue Place in edas is a physical location (a place). They represent fundamentally different concepts: an event vs. a venue.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman) in the conference organization, while Coffee Break is a non-academic event during the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item (delivering/presenting). These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and ranges.

Single Level Conference is a type of conference (subclass of Conference), while Presenter state is a status/state of a presenter (subclass of State). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

reviewsPerPaper denotes the number of reviews assigned per paper in a conference, while Price denotes the monetary cost of a registration fee. They have different domains, different semantics, and are entirely unrelated.
Property A links conference proceedings to a publisher, while property B links a speaker to a document they present. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

isWrittenBy relates Paper to Author (Paper -> Author), while submit relates Author to Paper (Author -> Paper). They are inverse properties connecting the same classes but in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.

In ekaw, 'Web Site' is a subclass of 'Document', while in iasted, 'Document' is the general class encompassing various document types (Submission, Review, Form, etc.). The ekaw 'Web Site' is a specific kind of document, so it is subsumed by the more general iasted 'Document' class.
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while isMemberOf relates a Person to a Conference. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Meta Reviewer in cmt is a person/role (a special type of reviewer), while Review in iasted is a document/artefact. They are entirely different concepts.
Rejected Paper is a type of paper (document), while Submissions deadline is a type of deadline (time). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Both are datatype properties named 'has First Name' with domain Person and range string, serving the same purpose of recording a person's first name in the conference domain.

Conference document in Ontology A is a broad class encompassing calls for papers, announcements, web pages, contributions, and reviews. Document in Ontology B (sigkdd) is narrower, with children limited to Abstract, Paper, and Review. Thus Conference document subsumes Document, as it covers all of Document's intended instances plus additional administrative/organizational documents.
Withdrawn Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been withdrawn), while Paper in ekaw is the general class of all papers. Therefore, Withdrawn Paper is subsumed by Paper.
Renting is an activity performed before a conference (e.g., renting equipment or venue), while Author of paper is a person role. They are completely unrelated concepts.

In Ontology A, 'Regular author' is a subclass of 'Conference contribution' (a document/artefact), despite its confusing name and parentage. In Ontology B, 'Participant' is a subclass of 'Person'. They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.
Tutorial is a type of scientific event/presentation in ekaw, while Speaker is a type of person who presents in sigkdd. They are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. person) and thus unrelated.

minChoice is a datatype property with range positiveInteger indicating a minimum choice count for events, while hasEndDateTime is a datatype property with range dateTime indicating the end time of a conference event. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Company (a commercial organization) and Research Institute (an academic research organization) are distinct types of organizations. They share a similar structural role as siblings of University within their respective Organization hierarchies, but their intended instances differ. They are related as sibling concepts under the broader Organisation class, but not equivalent.

Talk Event in edas is a conference event where talks are given (e.g., welcome talk, closing talk), while Simulating in iasted is a pre-conference research activity. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference document to its date of issue, while Property B is an object property linking a research topic to events or papers that cover it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper is a document/submission class, while Registation deadline is a temporal deadline class. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas is a general person attending the conference (similar to Conference Participant in ekaw), while Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers specifically to staff from an agency (e.g., funding or travel agency). These are distinct roles with no semantic overlap.
'writtenBy' links a Contribution to its Author, while 'awarded_by' links an Award to the entity that grants it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Closing Talk is a conference event (a type of Talk Event). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all submitted papers (children: Paper Abstract, Paper Full Version). In edas, Accepted Paper is a specific subclass of Paper representing only those papers that have been accepted. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes edas:AcceptedPaper.

cmt:hasCo-author links a Paper specifically to a Co-author (a secondary author role), while ekaw:writtenBy links a Document to any Person (author). The domains are equivalent (Paper/Document) but the ranges differ in specificity (Co-author vs Person). They overlap semantically as both express authorship, but hasCo-author is more specific than writtenBy, making them related rather than strictly equivalent.

In cmt, Author is a Conference Member who writes/submits papers. In sigkdd, Speaker is a Person who gives presentations, and Author is actually a subclass of Speaker. The two classes overlap (authors often present their papers as speakers) but are not equivalent: cmt's Author focuses on paper authorship while sigkdd's Speaker focuses on giving presentations. They are related but neither subsumes the other.

'contributes' relates a Person to a Conference document (authorship/contribution), while 'is paid for' relates Money to an Activity or Item (payment). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

A is a datatype property (Conference -> int) representing the number of reviews per paper configured for a conference. B is an object property (Member PC -> Contribution) linking a PC member to the papers they review. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

In cmt, Author is a subclass of Conference Member (which extends Person), representing someone who authors papers. In ekaw, Conference Participant is a broad class directly under Person with children like OC Member, PC Chair, Session Chair, etc., and Paper Author is a sibling of Conference Participant. Thus, cmt:Author corresponds more closely to ekaw:Paper Author, while ekaw:Conference Participant is a much broader concept that subsumes the role of an author/participant.

Property A 'date' is a generic date property for Conference, while property B 'registrationDueOn' is a specific registration deadline property. They share the same domain (Conference) and similar range types (date/dateTime), but differ in specificity and intended meaning. B is more specific than A, so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A (title) gives the title of a Paper as a string, while property B (Price) gives the monetary price of a Registration fee as an integer. They describe entirely different concepts with different domains and ranges.

Conference participant (A) is a general class for all participants in a conference, while OC Chair (B) is a specific role within the Organising Committee. Every OC Chair is a conference participant, but not every conference participant is an OC Chair. Thus A subsumes B.

In cmt, Review is a document (the actual review written by a reviewer), whereas in edas, NumericalReviewQuestion is a type of question on a review form that expects a numerical answer. These are entirely different concepts.

The property 'expertOn' relates a PC member to a topic they have expertise in, while 'writtenBy' relates a document to its author. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Non Academic Event in edas covers social/meal/break events, while Scientific Event in ekaw covers academic/scientific activities like conferences, sessions, and workshops. These are essentially complementary (opposite) concepts within the conference domain, not equivalent or in a subsumption relationship.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators). Registration SIGKDD Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee, representing a type of fee. These are entirely different concepts (person vs. fee) and are unrelated.

Entity A is a conference document providing information to participants, while Entity B is an administrative event representing the release of reviewing results. They differ in kind (document vs. event) and purpose.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (an academic gathering like a workshop or tutorial). In iasted, One conference day is a subclass of Time/Conference days, representing a single day within the conference schedule. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event type, the other is a temporal unit.

contactEmail is a datatype property linking a Contribution to a string (email address), while send is an object property linking a Person to an Item. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Accepted contribution is a type of conference paper that has been accepted after review, while Deadline is a temporal concept representing a due date. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

'writtenBy' links a Review to its author (Reviewer), expressing authorship. 'send' links a Person to an Item, expressing a sending/transmission action. These are semantically different relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Test Only Topic is a subject area/topic classification. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

In edas, 'Paper Presentation' is a Conference Event (an activity where a paper is presented), linked to an Accepted Paper via relatedToPaper. In ekaw, 'Paper' is a Document (the written artefact itself), which is presented as an Individual Presentation. Thus one is an event/activity and the other is a document; they are related but not equivalent.

Personal History in edas refers to a person's background information (publication and review history), while Submission in iasted refers to a submitted document/manuscript. These are entirely different concepts.

Submitted Paper is a type of document (a paper that has been submitted), while Program Committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the program. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'has a name' is a datatype property linking entities to a string name, while 'topic Covered By' is an object property linking a research topic to events or papers. They are entirely different in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Conference days represents the duration/days of a conference (a subclass of Time), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a specific deadline for submitting abstracts (a subclass of Deadline). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while property B 'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution. These have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Associated Chair in cmt is a specific chair role (subclass of Chairman) responsible for conference organization, whereas Scholar in confOf is a price category for attendees who study at a university. They represent entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the concept of an author of a paper in the conference domain. In ekaw, Paper Author is a subclass of Person; in iasted, Author is a subclass of Speaker (which is under Delegate). Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide: persons who have authored a paper/contribution for the conference.

Both entities represent the organizational body responsible for organizing a conference. However, 'Organizing committee' in Ontology A is modeled as a type of Committee (a group of people), while 'Organising Agency' in Ontology B is modeled as a type of Organisation (an institutional entity). They serve the same functional role in the conference domain but differ in ontological modeling (committee vs. organization), making them related rather than strictly equivalent.
'has a publisher' links conference proceedings to a publisher, while 'covers Topic' links events or papers to research topics. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both are datatype properties mapping an entity to its title string, but their domains differ significantly: cmt:title applies to Paper, while confOf:has_title applies to Social event and Working event. Since they relate different kinds of things, they are not equivalent but semantically related as analogous title properties.

Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a specific leadership role within a committee), while Property B links a Person to a Conference (general membership). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. Author cd proceedings included (B) is a very specific subclass of Author. Since B's instances (authors whose work appears in CD proceedings) are a subset of A's instances (anyone who contributes to the conference), A subsumes B.

Reviewer in cmt is a person (role) who reviews papers, while Review in Conference is a document (the review itself). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities (person vs. document) and thus unrelated.
has First Name is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while is dated on links an Activity to a dateTime. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a conference document (informational artefact), while 'Reviewing event' is an administrative event (a process/activity). They belong to fundamentally different categories and are unrelated.

assignedByReviewer relates an External Reviewer to a Reviewer in the review process, while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document for presenting. These properties involve entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator regarding paper assignment finalization, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker regarding who presents it.

Both classes represent the student registration fee in a conference context. They share the same parent (Registration fee) and analogous sibling structures (non-member, member fees). Despite slightly different naming conventions ('Student registration fee' vs 'Registration Student'), they denote the same concept.

Author Not Reviewer in cmt is a specific subclass of Author denoting an author who does not serve as a reviewer. Scholar in confOf is a sibling of Author under Person, with a comment indicating it relates to a 'price category - scholar' and has a property 'study At -> University', suggesting it represents a student/academic attendee rather than an author role. These are distinct concepts.

'employed By' relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while 'is designed for' relates Activity/Money/Time to Activity/Person (purpose/design). These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

memberOfConference links a Conference Member to a Conference (member -> conference), while hasMember links a Conference to a Person (conference -> member). They are inverses of each other in direction, not equivalent properties.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Overhead projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Banquet is a social event (a type of activity/gathering), while Trip city is a geographical location (a type of City). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

A Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the head of the program committee responsible for managing reviews and paper selection, while a Session chair (iasted) presides over a specific session during the conference. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities, though both are types of chairs in a conference context.
Poster Paper is a specific type of academic paper submitted to a conference, while Mailing list is a communication document/list. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Contact Information in edas represents address/phone/email details of a person, while Document in ekaw represents written artefacts like papers, reviews, and abstracts. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the main conference itself), while Coffee Break in edas is a non-academic break event occurring during a conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a submitted contribution to its review expertise, while property B links a person to an activity or item they give. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Both properties connect a person/author to a document/paper, but 'authorOf' denotes authorship while 'submit' denotes the act of submission. An author does not necessarily submit their own paper (e.g., a corresponding author or another co-author may submit), so they are related but not equivalent.

Property A (abstract) is a datatype property on Contribution (a paper/submission) representing its abstract text, while Property B (Name) is a datatype property on Person representing a person's name. They have completely different domains and semantics.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while is_the_1th_part_of links an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (mereological part-of relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Chairman (cmt) is a specific leadership role with children like Conference Chair and Program Committee Chair, while Committee member (Conference) is a broader class that includes chairs but also regular members (has members property linking to Committee). A Chairman is a kind of committee member, but not all committee members are chairmen, so they overlap without being equivalent.

Both classes represent the concept of a Conference in the conference-organisation domain. They share similar properties such as name, end date, and location (country vs city). Despite differences in modeling detail, their intended instances coincide.

Property A relates a conference document to its date of issue (range: date), while property B relates a contribution to its title (range: string). They describe entirely different attributes and are unrelated.

Property A 'title' has domain Paper and represents a paper's title, while property B 'Name' has domain Person and represents a person's name. They relate different kinds of entities and denote different concepts.

'relates To' in edas is a very general property linking a Document to various entities (events, conferences, sessions, persons). 'presentationed by' in sigkdd specifically links a Document to a Speaker who presents it. While both connect documents to people/events, the sigkdd property is much more specific in semantics and range. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'relates To' subsumes 'presentationed by' in scope.

Review expertise refers to a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill in a topic area, while Review Question refers to a specific question on a review form (e.g., numerical or textual). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

enableVirtualMeeting relates an Administrator to a Conference (enabling virtual meetings), while hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'hasBeenAssigned' in cmt specifically links a Reviewer to a Paper they are assigned to review. 'give' in iasted is a generic property linking a Person to an Activity or Item. The domains, ranges, and intended semantics differ significantly; they do not represent the same relation.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper), while Main office is a type of place. They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, Paper is a general class for all papers (children include Paper Abstract and Paper Full Version). In ekaw, Rejected Paper is a very specific subclass deep in the hierarchy (Document > Paper > Submitted Paper > Assigned Paper > Evaluated Paper > Rejected Paper) representing only papers that have been rejected. Therefore, cmt:Paper subsumes ekaw:Rejected_Paper.

'Call for paper' in Ontology A is a type of conference document representing the call/announcement soliciting paper submissions (sibling of 'Call for participation', 'Conference announcement'). 'Conference Paper' in Ontology B is an actual submitted/accepted paper (subclass of Paper). These are entirely different concepts: one is an invitation to submit, the other is the submission itself.
Conference Paper is a type of document (a scholarly paper), while Conference hall is a type of place (a physical venue). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Science Worker in confOf denotes a person involved in scientific work (researcher/scholar), with Participant as a separate sibling class for attendees. Attendee in edas denotes someone who attends the conference. These are conceptually distinct roles; confOf's Participant would be the closer match to edas's Attendee.

In edas, Organizational Meeting is a specific type of Academic Event (alongside Paper Presentation, Talk Event, Workshop). In ekaw, Scientific Event is a broad category encompassing Conference, Individual Presentation, Session, Track, and Workshop. An organizational meeting is typically administrative rather than scientific, so it does not fall under Scientific Event. They are related as both represent types of conference events but are neither equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.

Property A is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an ISBN string, while Property B is an object property linking a Person to an Item they obtain. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A links a track workshop chair to a conference part (organizational role), while property B links a speaker to a document (presentation activity). They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is a datatype property indicating whether a conference accepts hardcopy submissions (Conference -> boolean), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to an Item they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Conference Member is a person role in a conference (subclass of Person), while Social event is a type of event (subclass of Event) such as a banquet or reception. They are entirely different concepts.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is a specific role that is a kind of Program Committee Member. In sigkdd, 'Program Committee member' is the general class and 'Program Chair' is listed as a sibling, indicating it is a distinct but related role. The cmt Program Committee Chair is subsumed by the more general sigkdd Program Committee member class.
Workshop is a type of working event (an academic session), while Conference airport is a type of building/place (a venue). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Conference part in Ontology A refers to organizational sub-events of a conference (Track, Tutorial, Workshop), while Conference Paper in ekaw refers to a scholarly document submitted to the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a conference event/activity to its location (Place). 'Conference Event' in edas corresponds to 'Activity' in iasted, and both have Place in their range. Despite iasted also including Time in the range, the core semantic relation of specifying where an event is held is the same.

Property A 'date' is a generic date property for a Conference, while property B 'manuscriptDueOn' is a specific deadline (manuscript due date) for a Conference. They share the same domain but differ in specificity and semantics; B is a particular kind of conference date, making them related but not equivalent.

Property A links a Topic to a Review preference (indicating reviewer topic preferences), while Property B links a Paper to a Review (indicating an actual review written for a paper). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In confOf, Participant is a subclass of Person (which is not shown but implied by siblings like Administrator, Author being at the same level or above). In edas, Person is the top-level class for people with children like Attendee, Author, Reviewer. confOf's Participant (with children Member, Regular, Student) roughly corresponds to edas's Attendee rather than edas's Person. Since confOf also has a separate Person root and sibling classes like Author that are not under Participant, confOf:Participant is narrower than edas:Person. They overlap significantly but are not equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a broad category of conference documents intended for attendees, while 'Registration form' is a specific type of form used during registration. A registration form could be considered one piece of information for participants, but the two classes are not equivalent; they overlap in purpose.
Call for paper is a conference document inviting submissions, while Communication Theory Topic is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They are entirely different concepts.

submitPaper is an object property linking an Author to a Paper (the act of submission), while is_a_full_paper_submission_date is a datatype property linking Important dates to a date value. They represent entirely different concepts and have incompatible domains, ranges, and types.
Topic in Ontology A represents a subject area or theme of a conference part, while Paper in Ontology B represents a submitted document. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (an administrative action), while 'presentationed by' relates a Document to a Speaker (a presentation relationship). They are unrelated.

'has a name' is a general name property for conferences, proceedings, publishers, and topics, while 'has Last Name' is specifically the surname of a Person. They differ in both domain and semantic specificity.

Conference Chair and Workshop Chair are distinct roles in conference organization. A Conference Chair oversees the entire conference, while a Workshop Chair is responsible for a specific workshop within the conference. They are related as both are chair roles but not equivalent.

Computer Networks Optical Topic is a specific research topic in computer networks, while Sponsor state represents the status/state of a sponsor. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Contribution represents a submitted work (paper, poster, etc.) while Deadline represents a time constraint for submissions or notifications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference website to a URL string, while Property B is an object property linking an event to a physical location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
writtenBy relates a Contribution to its Author, while pay relates a Person to Money. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Viza (Visa) is a travel document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation responsible for publishing proceedings, while Organizing Committee member is a Person who serves on the organizing committee. They are fundamentally different concepts (organisation vs person) with different roles.

Abstract in ekaw refers to a summary of a paper or presentation, while Payment document in iasted refers to financial instruments like bank transfers or cheques. They are completely different concepts that merely share 'Document' as an ancestor.
A is a datatype property assigning an unsigned long ID to a Paper, while B is an object property linking a Person to an Item they write. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics entirely.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (subsumed by Person), while Demo Chair in ekaw is a specific organizational role responsible for demo sessions. They are not equivalent; Attendee is more general but does not subsume Demo Chair since Demo Chair is an organizer role rather than merely an attendee.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Nonmember registration fee is a monetary fee for conference registration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Mobile Computing Topic in edas is a specific subject area under Topic. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Both classes represent the subject/topic area of a paper in the conference domain. In cmt, 'Subject Area' is linked to Paper via 'has Subject Area'; in ekaw, 'Research Topic' is linked to Paper via 'covers Topic'. They denote the same concept.

Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any person who authored a paper. Worker lecturer in iasted is a very specific subclass of Lecturer > Author > Speaker > Delegate, implying someone who both lectures and works (e.g., staff). While both involve authorship, Worker lecturer is much more specific (requires lecturing/working role) than the general Paper Author concept, so they are related but not equivalent.
Scientific Event is a type of event (conference, workshop, session, etc.), while Speaker is a type of person who presents. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

virtualMeetingEnabledBy links a Conference to an Administrator who enables virtual meetings, while hasMember links a Conference to a Person who is a member. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings and ranges.
