Property A (reviewes) links a PC member to a contribution they review, while property B (is used by) links an item to a person who uses it. These have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges in the conference domain.

'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to indicate they occur simultaneously, while 'has Attendee' relates a Conference Event to a Person who attends it. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
In confOf, University is a subclass of Organization (path: Organization > University), while in Conference, Organization is the general class. Therefore, Organization subsumes University.

A Volunteer is a person who helps with conference logistics without decision-making authority, while a Program Committee member is responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the scientific program. These are distinct roles with no overlap in intended instances.
Entity A is a Person role (a track/workshop chair), while Entity B is a Document (a brief introduction document for a session chair). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Single Level Conference in edas is a specific subtype of Conference (contrasted with Two Level Conference), whereas Conference in ekaw is the general concept of a conference event. Therefore, the ekaw Conference subsumes the edas Single Level Conference.

In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is a subclass of 'Paper', representing specifically the full version of a paper (as opposed to an abstract). In edas, 'Paper' is the general class for papers. Therefore, cmt's Paper Full Version is subsumed by edas's Paper.

Property A links a Paper to an Individual Presentation (a presentation format/event), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (the person presenting). The ranges are fundamentally different concepts (presentation event vs. person), so these properties are not equivalent.

Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference (subclass of Conference Participant), while Presenter university in iasted is a building/place (subclass of Building). They are completely different concepts.
hasProgramme links a Conference Event to its Programme, while hold links ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Co author is a person who co-writes a paper, while Nonauthor registration fee is a type of monetary fee for non-authors. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

cmt:name is a general name property applicable to both Conference and Person, while edas:hasLastName specifically denotes the last name of a Person. The general 'name' subsumes 'last name' since a full name includes the last name, but they are not equivalent due to differing specificity and domain.

rejectPaper relates an Administrator to a Paper (rejection action), while writes relates an Author to a Contribution (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

detailsEnteredBy links a Conference to an Administrator who entered details, while has_workshops links a Conference volume to its Workshop parts. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Trip is a social event (an excursion during a conference), while Card is a physical item (with Credit card as a subclass). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties describe entirely different relations: one links a Conference to an Administrator for printing mailing manifests, while the other links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract. They share no semantic overlap.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (subclass of Person), while Conference in sigkdd is an event entity with properties like city, start/end dates. They are entirely different concepts.

Person represents individual human beings involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, participants), while Organization represents institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGOs) that provide sponsorship. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (despite odd parentage including TPC Member), while Technical commitee in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person). They represent fundamentally different concepts.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Student lecturer' is a student who gives a lecture/presentation at the conference (subclass of Lecturer/Speaker), while a 'Best Student Paper Supporter' is a sponsor that funds or supports the best student paper award (subclass of Sponzor). These are entirely different roles in the conference domain.

Paper Full Version is a complete academic paper submission, while Hotel registration form is an administrative form for booking accommodation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links an Abstract to the document it is part of (Paper, Poster, Presentation), while Property B links a Contribution to its Author. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relationships.

Administrator in confOf refers to a system/organizational administrator (e.g., confTool admin), while Attendee in edas refers to a person attending the conference. These are distinct roles with no subsumption or equivalence.

Performance Topic is a subject area (a subclass of Topic) for papers/presentations, while Plenary lecture is a type of conference activity/event (a subclass of Lecture). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while an 'Industry Organization' is a type of organization in the industry sector. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
hasHomePage is a datatype property linking a Person to a string (URL), while authorOf is an object property linking a Person to a Document. They represent entirely different relations.
A Poster is a type of academic contribution (presentation format), while a Mailing list is a document used for communication purposes. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking Conference proceedings to an integer volume number, while Property B is an object property linking a Working event to an Administrative event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.
Track is a conference organizational unit (part of a conference), while Van is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (informational artefact), while Workshop is a type of academic event (a scheduled session). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while heldIn links an Event to a Location (venue relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent the act of rejecting/refusing a submitted paper (manuscript). In cmt, Rejection is a Decision (sibling of Acceptance); in iasted, Refusing manuscript is an Activity before conference (sibling of Accepting manuscript). Despite different modeling choices (Decision vs Activity), they denote the same concept in the conference domain.

Personal Publication History in edas is a type of personal history document/record (sibling of Personal Review History), whereas Paper Author in ekaw is a role played by a Person who authored a paper. These are fundamentally different concepts.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions (papers), while property B links a Speaker to a Document they present. The domains and ranges are entirely different, so these properties are unrelated.

Reviewing event is an administrative event/procedure for reviewing contributions, while Transparency is a type of document (e.g., overhead transparency). They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

isReviewing in edas goes from reviewer roles (Conference Chair, Reviewer, etc.) to Paper, while hasReviewer in ekaw goes from Paper to Possible Reviewer. They are inverse properties relating the same domain concepts but in opposite directions, so they are related but not equivalent.

'Call for participation' is a document inviting people to participate in a conference, while 'Viza' (visa) is a travel document required for entry into a country. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Cryptography Topic is a subject area under Topic in edas, while Best Research Paper Award is a type of Award in sigkdd. They are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

An 'Invited speaker' is a specific type of conference contributor who has been invited to give a talk, while a 'Conference Hiker' in the iasted ontology is a subclass of Delegate (attendee) with no indication of being an invited speaker. These are distinct roles and not equivalent.

Property A is a datatype property on Conference indicating whether hardcopy submissions are accepted, while Property B is an object property on Paper linking it to a presentation type. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Member in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people involved in a conference, while Conference days in iasted is a subclass of Time representing temporal periods. They are entirely different concepts.

Both properties link a Person to a document/item they produce for the conference. 'contributes' (Person -> Conference document) and 'prepare' (Person -> Item) have similar domains and ranges, but 'contributes' is broader (could include reviewing, etc.) while 'prepare' implies authoring/creating. They overlap in meaning but are not strictly equivalent.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman', representing a co-chair or associate chair role (a leadership position). In ekaw, 'SC Member' is a subclass of 'PC Member' (Steering Committee Member), which is a committee membership role, not a chair role. The sibling classes in ekaw show that chair roles (PC Chair, Session Chair) are distinct from SC Member. Therefore, these two classes represent different concepts and are unrelated.

Topic in edas represents a subject area of a paper or conference (e.g., Antennas, Cryptography), while ACM SIGKDD in sigkdd represents the organizing body/society that holds conferences and sets deadlines. These are entirely different concepts.

In iasted, 'Nonmember registration fee' is a subclass of 'Registration fee'. In sigkdd, 'Registration fee' is the parent class with children including 'Registration Non Member'. Thus, the iasted class is more specific and is subsumed by the sigkdd class.
Conference Chair is the person who chairs/organizes the conference, while Presenter is someone who presents a paper or talk at the conference. These are distinct roles with no hierarchical overlap.
Conference Paper is a type of document (a paper submitted to a conference), while Conference hall is a type of place (a venue). They are entirely different concepts.

Science Worker in confOf is a subclass of Person representing someone working in science (e.g., researcher, scholar). Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference representing a conference with two organizational levels. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Microelectronics Topic is a subject area for conference papers, while Transport vehicle is a physical conveyance item. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Excursion is a specific type of social event (an outing/trip), while Coctail reception is a specific type of conference activity (a drinks/social gathering). In edas, Excursion and Reception are siblings under Social Event, meaning they are distinct concepts. The iasted Coctail reception corresponds more closely to edas's Reception than to Excursion. They are related as both are non-academic social activities at a conference, but not equivalent.

Property A ('has a location') maps a Conference volume to its location string, while Property B ('has Title') maps a Contribution to its title string. They have different domains, different semantic meanings (location vs. title), and are entirely unrelated.

Conference applicant is a subclass of Person (someone applying to attend), while Registration Student is a subclass of Fee/Registration fee (a type of monetary charge). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent fundamentally different concepts.
Organization represents an institution (company, university) while Review Rating represents a score given to a paper review. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

City in confOf is a general class for cities, while Sponsor city in iasted is a specific subclass of City (as shown by its path 'City > Sponsor city' and siblings like Conference city). Therefore, the general City subsumes the more specific Sponsor city.
has_the_last_name refers to a person's surname, while hasPostalCode refers to a postal/zip code. These are entirely different concepts despite both being datatype properties with string range.
Banquet is a social event at a conference, while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item (e.g., projectors, computers). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasTopic links a working event to its topic/subject area, while hasEvent links an event to a sub-event. These properties relate entirely different kinds of entities and express different relations.

Publication is a class representing published items (e.g., book proceedings), while Author is a class representing people who write papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Topic in confOf represents a subject area or theme of a contribution/event, while Person in iasted represents a human being (with children Delegate, Sponsor). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Travel Grant in edas is a type of Sponsorship (financial support for travel), while Conference Trip in ekaw is a Social Event (the actual trip/activity). They are related concepts in the conference domain but not equivalent: one is funding, the other is an event.

earlyRegistration is a datatype property linking a Participant to a boolean indicating early registration status, while heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Person is the top-level class for all people involved in a conference (authors, reviewers, committee members, etc.). In confOf, Participant is a subclass of Person that specifically denotes someone who participates/attends the conference, while other roles like Author, Chair PC, and Member PC are siblings of Participant under Person. Thus cmt:Person corresponds to confOf:Person, not confOf:Participant. The two classes overlap but are not equivalent.

Reviewed contribution in Ontology A is a specific type of submitted conference paper that has been reviewed. Document in Ontology B (sigkdd) is a much broader class that includes Abstract, Paper, and Review as children. While a Reviewed contribution is a kind of document/paper, the sigkdd Document class also encompasses reviews and abstracts, making it strictly more general. They overlap but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap given the options.

Program Committee Member (cmt) is a specific role within the conference organization, while Conference Participant (ekaw) is a broader class encompassing all participants including chairs, presenters, and registered attendees. PC Chair is a child of Conference Participant in ekaw, confirming that Program Committee Member would be subsumed by Conference Participant.

hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (e.g., registration, social events), while forEvent links a Call (for papers/reviews) to an Academic Event. The domains and ranges are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Non Academic Event in edas is strictly a subset of conference events (Break, Meal, Social), whereas Conference activity in iasted includes both academic activities (Lecture, Presentation) and non-academic ones (Coffee break, Cocktail reception, Social program). Thus Conference activity subsumes Non Academic Event but also covers Academic Event, making them related/overlapping rather than equivalent.
hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while volumeContainsPaper links a proceedings volume to the papers it contains. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

Hotel fee and Sponzor fee are both subclasses of Fee in their respective ontologies, but they refer to different specific types of fees (accommodation vs sponsorship). They are related as sibling concepts under the same parent class but are not equivalent.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to an integer cost amount, while is_paid_in is an object property linking Money to a Building. They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.
Property A is a datatype property giving the title (string) of a Paper, while Property B gives the completion date (date) of a Deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Transport vehicle is a class for vehicles (Car, Shuttle bus, etc.) under Item, while Speaker is a class for people who present at a conference under Person. These are entirely unrelated concepts.

'One conference day' is a temporal concept (subclass of Time/Conference days), while 'Conference hall' is a spatial/location concept (subclass of Place). They represent entirely different dimensions and are unrelated.

isInitiatedBy relates a Call to the person who initiated it (e.g., Conference Chair), while is_visited_by relates a physical location (Building, City, State) to a Person visiting it. These are entirely different relations in both semantics and domain/range.

Computer Networks Switching Topic is a subject area/topic classification in edas, while Contributed Talk is a type of presentation event in ekaw. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for students/academics (with property studyAt -> University), while in ekaw, Paper Author specifically denotes a person who authored a paper. These are different roles: a scholar may or may not be an author, and an author may or may not be a scholar. They overlap but are not equivalent.

Property A relates an organizing committee to a conference volume, while property B relates a person to a physical location (building, city, state). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Review preference in Ontology A represents a reviewer's preference or willingness to review certain topics/papers (with degree, topic, etc.), while Document in Ontology B is a general class for artefacts like Abstract, Paper, and Review. These are entirely different concepts.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing individuals who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Proceedings Publisher in ekaw is a subclass of Organisation that publishes conference proceedings. They are entirely different concepts.

cmt:date is a generic date property for Conference, while edas:endDate specifically denotes the conference end date/time. They overlap in domain and purpose but endDate is more specific, so they are related rather than equivalent.

A Demo Session is a session where software or system demonstrations are presented, while a Plenary lecture is a keynote-style lecture attended by all conference participants. They are distinct types of conference events with different purposes and formats.

Numerical Review Question is a type of review question (a criterion for evaluating papers), while Final manuscript is a type of submission document. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

The two properties describe entirely different concepts: 'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document regarding conflicts, while 'is paid for' relates Money to an Activity or Item regarding payment. They share no semantic overlap.
readPaper relates a Reviewer to a Paper (reading action), while submit relates an Author to a Paper (submission action). Different domains and different semantics.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (paper review assignment), while scientificallyOrganisedBy links an entity to an Academic Institution (organizational role). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Rejection is a type of Decision (rejecting a paper). In edas, Reception is a Social Event (a welcome reception/party at the conference). These are entirely different concepts that happen to share a similar word root.
Accpet If Room Rating is a type of review rating in edas, while Speaker is a type of conference delegate in iasted. They are completely unrelated concepts.

'referenced In' relates a document to another that cites it, while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item they present/provide. These are semantically unrelated properties with different domains, ranges, and meanings.
Communication Theory Topic is a subject area for papers, while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Presenter city is a type of City (a geographic location), while Conference hall is a type of Place representing a specific building or room where events are held. A city and a conference hall are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

cmt:Paper is a general class for all papers, while edas:WithdrawnPaper is a specific subclass of Paper representing only those that have been withdrawn. Therefore cmt:Paper subsumes edas:WithdrawnPaper.

Conference www in Ontology A is a type of conference document (specifically a web page/URL resource), while Academic Event in Ontology B is a type of conference event (e.g., paper presentation, workshop). These are entirely different concepts.
Introduction is a conference activity (event) in iasted, while Organizator is a person role in sigkdd. They are completely different concepts.

Both classes represent a cocktail reception at a conference. In confOf, Reception is a Social event (with siblings Banquet, Trip), while in iasted, Coctail reception is a Conference activity (with siblings like Coffee break, Social program). Despite different parent labels, they denote the same concept: a social reception/cocktail event during a conference.

Non Academic Event is a type of conference event (e.g., social or meal events), while Registration Student is a type of registration fee for students. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Active Paper in edas is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been rated), while Document in iasted is a broad class encompassing many types of documents including submissions, reviews, forms, etc. Active Paper is strictly more specific than the general Document class, so it is subsumed by it.
Invited speaker is a type of person who speaks at a conference, while Two Level Conference is a type of conference event. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.

Both are datatype properties from Person to string representing contact information, but 'has Home Page' refers to a web page URL while 'E mail' refers to an email address. They are related as contact details but not equivalent.

locationOf relates a Location to an Event (spatial containment), while holded_by relates a Conference to its organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Call for participation' is a sibling of 'Call for paper', indicating it is a distinct concept (e.g., inviting attendees rather than paper submissions). In Ontology B, 'Call For Papers' specifically solicits paper submissions. They are related as both are types of calls in the conference domain, but not equivalent.
Regular Paper is a type of academic paper submitted to a conference, while Mailing list is a document used for communication purposes. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Place is a general location class with children including Conference Venue Place, Accommodation Place, Dining Place, and Meeting Room Place. In iasted, City is specifically an urban settlement (a type of place). Since every city is a place but not every place is a city, edas:Place subsumes iasted:City.

confOf's 'Administrative event' is a specific subclass of confOf's 'Event', covering only administrative activities (camera ready, registration, reviewing, submission). ekaw's 'Event' is the top-level event class encompassing both Scientific and Social events. Therefore, confOf:Administrative_event is strictly subsumed by ekaw:Event.

Multi-author Volume in ekaw is a specific type of document (parent of Proceedings), while Publication in iasted is a broader class encompassing Book proceeding and Cd proceeding. A multi-author volume is a kind of publication, so ekaw's Multi-author Volume is subsumed by iasted's Publication.

Extended abstract is a short summary contribution (child of Regular contribution, sibling of Paper), while Industrial Paper is a full paper submitted for an industrial track (child of Paper). They represent different types of conference submissions with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.

Property A links a Conference part to a Topic (domain: Conference part, range: Topic), while Property B links a Topic to a Conference or Paper (domain: Topic, range: Conference/Paper). They are roughly inverse in direction and differ in domain/range scope, so they are related but not equivalent.
hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g., sub-events), while give relates a Person to an Activity or Item. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The property 'need' (Person -> Item) expresses a requirement relationship, while 'presentation' (Speaker -> Document) expresses that a speaker gives a presentation of a document. These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

Both properties have Reviewer as their range, but their domains differ: 'writtenBy' links a Review to its author (Reviewer), while 'isReviewHistoryOf' links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer. A review and a personal review history are related but not the same concept, so the properties are related rather than equivalent.
Publisher is an organization that issues conference proceedings, while Research Topic is a subject area covered by papers and events. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Coffee break is a conference activity/event. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

The 'email' property represents an email address of a Person, while 'has Street' represents a street address as part of Contact Information. These are entirely different contact details with different domains and meanings.

Proceedings Publisher is an Organisation that publishes proceedings, while Author book proceedings included is a person (Author) whose work appears in book proceedings. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a Review preference to a Submitted contribution or Topic, while Property B links a Paper to a Review. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Tutorial Chair is a person role (a type of conference participant), while Author attendee cd registration fee is a monetary fee. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and share no semantic overlap.

Invited talk (A) is a type of conference contribution/presentation, while Tutorial Abstract (B) is an abstract document for a tutorial. They represent different concepts: one is a presentation format, the other is a document type for a different session format. Even 'Invited Talk Abstract' in ekaw would only be related to Invited talk as its abstract, not equivalent.

Paper in confOf is a scholarly contribution (a document submitted to a conference), while Call For Papers in edas is an announcement inviting submissions. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Call for paper is a conference document (an announcement inviting submissions), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.
OC Member is a person role (Organizing Committee member), while Session is a conference activity/event. They are entirely different concepts.

Contribution co author is a specific type of author (a co-author of a conference contribution), while Author in iasted is a general class for all authors. The former is strictly more specific than the latter, so it is subsumed by Author.

Accpet If Room Rating is a type of Review Rating (a score/assessment given by a reviewer), while Rejected Paper is a subclass of Paper representing a paper that was not accepted. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (rating vs. paper status) and are unrelated.
confOf:Topic is a general class for any conference topic, while edas:CAD Topic is a specific subclass of Topic (Computer-Aided Design). Therefore, the general Topic subsumes CAD Topic.

Both properties link an event/activity to its location (Event->Location vs Activity->Place). In the conference domain, 'Event' and 'Activity' are synonymous, as are 'Location' and 'Place'. The iasted range also includes Time, but the core spatial relation is the same.

Both are subclasses of Person in their respective ontologies, but they cover different roles. User (cmt) includes Administrator, Author, and Reviewer, while Organizator (sigkdd) includes chairs, committee members, and webmaster. They overlap on administrative/committee roles but neither subsumes the other since User includes Authors/Reviewers and Organizator does not.

has_an_email relates a Person to their email address (string), while hasPhone relates Contact Information to a phone number (string). They represent different contact attributes (email vs phone) and have different domains, so they are unrelated.

Personal Publication History is a type of personal history related to an author's publications, while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee for sponsors. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Multimedia Topic is a subject area for papers (a subclass of Topic), while LCD projector is a piece of audiovisual equipment (a subclass of Item). They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and are unrelated.
Program committee is a group of people responsible for reviewing papers, while Building is a physical structure/place. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (a chairman of the conference), while Program Committee is a committee/group. They are fundamentally different kinds of entities in the conference domain.

In cmt, Administrator is a sibling of Reviewer under User and has management duties (accepting papers, assigning reviewers, entering conference details). In edas, Reviewer is a person who reviews papers. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities; they are not equivalent, nor does one subsume the other.
hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision, while is_visited_by relates a location (Building/City/State) to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Conference Paper (ekaw) is a full paper submitted to a conference, while Abstract (sigkdd) is a summary document. In sigkdd, Abstract and Paper are siblings under Document, indicating they are distinct concepts. A Conference Paper may contain or be associated with an Abstract, but they are not equivalent.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Applications) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for paper' is a conference document announcing the solicitation of papers, while an 'Industrial Paper' is a specific type of submitted paper. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
'writtenBy' links a contribution to its author (authorship), while 'references' denotes a citation or reference relation between documents. These are semantically distinct properties.

Conference Banquet is a social event (a type of activity), while Conference hall is a place (a physical location). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain and are unrelated.

Rejection in cmt is a type of Decision (an act/outcome), while Accepted contribution in Conference is a type of submitted paper that was accepted. They are fundamentally different concepts: one is a decision event, the other is a document/contribution. Moreover, Rejection corresponds to rejecting, whereas Accepted contribution corresponds to acceptance, so they are not even aligned in polarity.

The property 'member Of Program Committee' relates a person to a committee, while 'parallel with' relates two administrative events that occur simultaneously. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

ReviewQuestion in edas refers to a specific question used during the review process (with numerical/textual subtypes), while Document in sigkdd is a broad class encompassing Abstract, Paper, and Review. These are conceptually distinct entities in the conference domain.

Personal History in edas refers to a person's background records (publication history, review history), while Document in sigkdd refers to conference artefacts such as papers, abstracts, and reviews. These are conceptually distinct classes with no meaningful overlap.

hasDecision relates a Paper to a Decision in the conference review process, while is_equipped_by relates a Place to an Item (equipment). These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

assignReviewer links an Administrator to a Reviewer (assignment action), while presentationed_by links a Document to a Speaker (presentation relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document (administrative material), while 'Communications Topic' is a subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

'authorOf' relates a Person to a Document they authored, while 'obtain' relates a Person to an Item they obtained. These are semantically different relations (authorship vs. acquisition) despite sharing the same domain type.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) heads the Program Committee responsible for paper reviewing, while OC Chair (ekaw) heads the Organising Committee responsible for logistics. These are distinct roles in conference organisation, though both are chair-level positions.

Property A 'name' denotes the name of a Conference or Person, while property B 'hasPostalCode' denotes the postal code of an Organization or Person. These are entirely different attributes with different semantics and ranges of meaning, despite both having string as their range.

Both properties link a Person to something they provide in a conference context (contributes links Person to Conference document; give links Person to Activity/Item). They share the same domain and similar intent, but their ranges differ (Conference document vs Activity/Item), so they are related rather than equivalent.
Poster Paper in ekaw is a specific subtype of Paper (a paper presented as a poster), while Paper in sigkdd is the general class for all papers. Therefore, Poster Paper is subsumed by Paper.

Both classes represent the same concept: a person who writes or submits a paper to a conference. In cmt, Author is under Person > Conference Member and has properties like write Paper and submit Paper. In edas, Author is under Person and has properties like is Written By (inverse) and has Related Paper. Despite slight differences in hierarchy depth, their intended instances coincide.

Conference announcement is a type of conference document (e.g., call for papers, information), while Deadline Paper Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Property A is a datatype property linking a conference document to a date of issue, while Property B is an object property linking a programme brochure or web site to an event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Rejected Paper is a type of document (a paper that was not accepted), while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline. They are completely unrelated concepts.

confOf's Topic is a general class for any conference topic, while edas's Communications Topic is a specific subclass of Topic (one of many sibling topics like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Therefore, the general Topic subsumes the specific Communications Topic.

Both are subclasses of Registration fee, but they refer to different categories: A is a registration fee for author attendees who book (likely a printed proceedings book), while B is a registration fee specifically for students. They do not denote the same concept.

Chair is a committee leadership role (subclass of Committee member), while Possible Reviewer is a broad class of people who may review papers (superclass of PC Member). They represent different roles in the conference domain with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Conference Trip in ekaw is a specific type of Social Event (alongside Conference Banquet). Conference activity in iasted is a broad class encompassing many types of activities including lectures, presentations, registration, and social programs. A Conference Trip is one kind of conference activity, so the ekaw class is subsumed by the iasted class.

In edas, Country is a geopolitical entity (a nation) used as the location of a conference. In iasted, State is a physical/geographic region or condition with children like 'Conference state', 'Presenter state', and 'Sponsor state', and properties about being occupied/visited by persons and situated in places. These are fundamentally different concepts.

A 'Call for paper' is an announcement document inviting submissions (a sibling of Conference announcement), while a 'Demo Paper' is a specific type of submitted paper. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Form is a type of Document (e.g., registration form, author information form), while Author is a type of Person who submits papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Entity A is 'Review' (a document reviewing a paper), while Entity B is 'Viza' (a visa/travel document). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC member to a contribution they review, while property B (submit until) links a document to its submission deadline. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'writtenBy' denotes authorship of a document, while 'is signed by' denotes signing an item. These are semantically distinct relations despite both having Person as range.

Reject Rating is a specific type of review rating (a score/outcome indicating rejection), while Review in iasted is the document/artefact itself. They are related through the reviewing process but are not equivalent.

Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee (an organizational body), while Property B links a Call to individual roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) who initiated it. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

'has the first name' is a datatype property for a Person's first name, while 'starts on' is a datatype property for an Event's start date/time. They have different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

In cmt, Author is a general class with Co-author as a child. In Conference, 'Contribution co author' is a specific subclass of Regular author (which itself is under Conference contribution). Thus, the general Author class in cmt subsumes the more specific co-author class in Conference.

Program committee is a type of committee responsible for reviewing papers and organizing the technical program, while Sponsor is a person or entity providing financial support. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Student is a type of person/participant in a conference, while Best Student Paper Award is a type of award given to a paper. They are entirely different concepts.
coversTopic relates papers/events to research topics, while need relates persons to items. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Person in iasted is a general class with children Delegate and Sponsor. Sponzor (Sponsor) in sigkdd is a specific type of sponsor. Since iasted:Person has Sponsor as a child, Person subsumes Sponzor.
A is a datatype property mapping Conference or Person to a string name, while B is an object property relating an Item to a Person. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics entirely.

Both properties have Review as their range, but they differ in domain and semantics: 'writeReview' links a Reviewer (agent) to the Review they authored, while 'has_a_review' links a Reviewed contribution (paper/artefact) to its associated Review. They relate different kinds of things and are not equivalent or inverses.

Author Not Reviewer (cmt) is a subclass of Author restricted to those who are not reviewers, while Paper Author (ekaw) is any person who authored a paper with no such restriction. They overlap significantly but are not equivalent; Author Not Reviewer is more specific.

confOf's Topic is the general class for all conference topics, while edas's MultimediaTopic is a specific subclass of Topic (as shown by its path 'Topic > Multimedia Topic' and siblings like Antennas Topic, CAD Topic, etc.). Therefore, confOf:Topic subsumes edas:MultimediaTopic.
The 'title' property gives the title of a Paper, while 'has VAT' records the value-added tax for events. They have completely different domains, ranges in meaning, and purposes.

'has tracks' relates a Conference volume to its Tracks (a part-whole relationship), while 'held In' relates an Event to a Location (a spatial relationship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

In iasted, 'Speaker lecture' is a subclass of Session (a type of conference activity/event), whereas in sigkdd, 'Speaker' is a subclass of Person (a role played by an individual). They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.

Conference:Chair is a generic committee chair (with Co-chair as sibling), while ekaw:PC_Chair is specifically the Program Committee Chair. In ekaw, other chairs like Session Chair and Workshop Chair are siblings of PC Chair, indicating that PC Chair is a narrower concept than a generic Chair. Thus they are related but not equivalent.
heldIn is an object property linking an Event to a Location, while Price is a datatype property linking a Registration fee to an integer. They describe entirely different concepts and relations.

Person in ekaw represents a human being (with children like Author, Participant), while State in iasted represents a geographical or administrative region (with properties like is_situated_in). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings (publishing relation), while 'write' relates a Person to an Item (authoring relation). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name (string), while can_stay_in is an object property linking a Person to a Place. They describe entirely different relations.

Topic in ontology A represents a subject area or theme of a conference/paper, while Individual Presentation in ontology B represents a specific event where a paper is presented (e.g., a talk or tutorial). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Author in cmt represents a person who writes/submits papers (a conference member role), while Student in ekaw represents a student person. These are distinct concepts; the equivalent of Author in ekaw would be Paper Author, not Student.
The properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'expertOn' links a PC member to a topic of expertise, while 'obtain' links an author to an award they received.

Person in cmt is a top-level class for all people involved (Chairman, Reviewer, User, etc.), while Committee member in Conference is a subclass of Person specifically denoting members of a committee. Thus, cmt:Person subsumes Conference:Committee_member.

Review and Abstract are distinct types of documents in the conference domain. A Review is an evaluation of a paper, while an Abstract is a summary of a paper. They are siblings under Document in their respective ontologies but denote different concepts.

Committee member in Ontology A is a Person who serves on a conference committee (with children Chair, Co-chair). Registration SIGMOD Member in Ontology B is a subclass of Registration fee, representing a type of fee for SIGMOD members. They are entirely different concepts (a role vs. a fee category) and share no meaningful semantic overlap.

Single Level Conference is a type of conference event (subclass of Conference), while Conference hall is a physical location/venue (subclass of Place). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A 'Call for paper' is a document inviting paper submissions, while a 'Registration form' is a form used to register for the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'belongs to reviewers' links review expertise/preference to a Reviewer, while 'write' links a Person to an Item they authored. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

siteURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to its website URL (anyURI), while hasName links a Conference to its full name (string). These represent entirely different attributes of a conference and are not equivalent or subsumption-related.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Reject Rating is a type of review rating for papers. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Entity A is a class representing a person who authors papers (a role under Conference Member), while Entity B is a specific type of registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Rejected Paper in ekaw is a specific subclass of Paper (a paper that has been evaluated and rejected), while Paper in sigkdd is the general class of papers. Therefore, Rejected Paper is subsumed by Paper.

'is submitted at' links a conference contribution (paper) to a conference volume (proceedings), while 'held In' links an event to a physical location. These relate entirely different domain and range concepts and express different semantics.

hasCostCurrency is a datatype property linking Sponsorship to a currency string, while is_paid_for is an object property linking Money to Activity or Item. They differ in type, domain, range, and semantics.

Both classes represent a conference paper (a scholarly submission). In Ontology A it is a subclass of Regular contribution under Conference document; in edas it is a subclass of Document with children like Accepted Paper, Rejected Paper, etc., and properties such as isWrittenBy and isReviewedBy. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances coincide: they both denote the same concept of a paper submitted to a conference.

Property A relates a Chair to a Committee (committee membership/leadership), while Property B relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while is_sent_before relates an Item to a Time (temporal ordering). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Trip in confOf is a social event (an organized excursion), while Taxi in iasted is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

Neutral_Review in ekaw is a specific subclass of Review (a review with neutral sentiment), while Review in iasted is the general class for all reviews. Therefore, Neutral_Review is subsumed by Review.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Week Reject Rating is a type of review rating. These are entirely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

In ekaw, 'Workshop Paper' is a specific subtype of 'Paper', whereas in sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers (directly under Document). Therefore, ekaw's Workshop Paper is subsumed by sigkdd's Paper.
Conference in confOf is an event (a type of Working event), while Author book proceedings included in iasted is a role/person (a type of Author). They are completely different concepts.

'is submitted at' links a conference contribution to a conference volume (proceedings), while 'location Of' links a physical location to an event. These properties have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Conference Chair in edas is a person role (the chair of a conference), while Conference hall in iasted is a physical place/venue. They are entirely different concepts.

Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (an attendee/participant), while Organizator in sigkdd represents an organizer (with children like General Chair, Program Chair, etc.). These are distinct roles in the conference domain: one attends, the other organizes.

Both properties express the same authorship relation: hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author in cmt, while writtenBy links a Document (which includes papers) to a Person (the author) in ekaw. Despite slightly different domain/range class names, they denote the same relation in the conference domain.
Steering committee is a type of committee responsible for guiding a conference, while Author is a person who writes contributions. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while publisherOf relates an Organisation to publication artefacts like Flyers or Web Sites. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In edas, 'Active Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper' representing papers currently under review (having ratings). In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for submitted papers. Thus, edas:Active Paper is subsumed by sigkdd:Paper.

Both classes represent the core submitted scholarly work in a conference domain. In Ontology A, 'Submitted contribution' is a written contribution that gets reviewed and has topics; in Ontology B (edas), 'Paper' is a document that is written by authors, has topics, and is reviewed. Despite different hierarchical placements (A nests it under Conference contribution > Written contribution, B directly under Document), their intended instances coincide: papers/contributions submitted to a conference for review.

Administrative event in confOf covers submission, reviewing, registration, and camera-ready events (organizational/administrative tasks). Break Event in edas covers coffee breaks, meal breaks, and free time (non-academic leisure breaks during the conference). These are entirely different concepts with no overlap.
Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference, while Property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasAttendee links a Conference Event to a Person (attendee), while holded_by links a Conference to an ACM SIGKDD organization. They relate entirely different domain and range concepts and express different relationships.
Property A links Money to an integer amount, while property B links a Sponsor to a string name. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Track workshop chair is responsible for a specific track or workshop within the conference, while a General Chair oversees the entire conference organization. Both are organizing roles (subclasses of Person/Organizator), but they have different scopes and responsibilities, so they are related but not equivalent.

City in iasted is a specific geographic/administrative entity (with children like Conference city, Presenter city), while Place in sigkdd refers to physical venues/buildings (with children like Conference hall, Hotel, Main office). They overlap as location concepts but are not equivalent; City is more of a geographic area whereas Place denotes specific buildings or facilities.

Conference contributor (A) is a broad class under Person encompassing active participants, invited speakers, and regular authors. Lecturer (B) in iasted is a specific subclass of Author/Speaker who gives lectures. A lecturer is a type of conference contributor, but Conference contributor is much broader, so A subsumes B.

'has the last name' refers specifically to a person's surname/family name, while 'Name' in sigkdd likely refers to the full name or general name of a person. They overlap (both are string-valued properties on Person) but are not strictly equivalent since one is more specific than the other.

hasSubmissionDeadline is a datatype property linking a Call to a dateTime representing a deadline, while is_sent_before is an object property linking an Item to a Time entity indicating when something was sent. They differ in type (datatype vs object), domain, range semantics, and intended meaning.

Both classes represent the conference website/web page. 'Conference www' in Ontology A is a subclass of 'Conference document' with a URL property, while 'Web Site' in Ontology B is a subclass of 'Document'. They denote the same concept: the web presence of a conference.

In confOf, Conference is the main academic event (a type of Working event, sibling to Tutorial and Workshop). In edas, Free Time Break is a non-academic break during a conference (sibling to Coffee Break and Meal Break). These are entirely different concepts.

Both properties represent an email address as a string, but they have different domains: confOf's contactEmail applies to Contribution (paper), while edas's hasEmail applies to Contact Information or Person. They relate different kinds of entities to their email strings, so they are related but not equivalent.
The two properties have completely different domains (Activity vs Person), ranges (Time vs Place), and semantics (temporal ordering vs accommodation). They are unrelated.

logoURL is a datatype property linking a Conference to a URI for its logo, while locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A ('date') is a generic date property with domain Conference, while property B ('hasEndDateTime') specifically denotes an end date/time with domain Conference Event. They overlap in the temporal aspect of conference-related entities but differ in specificity (generic date vs. end date) and domain (Conference vs. Conference Event), so they are related but not equivalent.

Important dates in Conference refers specifically to deadline-related dates (submission, acceptance, camera-ready, start/end) for a conference volume. Time in iasted is a much broader temporal concept with children including Conference days, Deadline, and Trip day. They overlap (both can represent deadlines/dates) but Important dates does not subsume or equal the general Time class; they are related.

Value added tax is a specific type of tax (under Money > Tax), while Registration fee is a fee paid to register for a conference (under Fee). These are entirely different financial concepts in the conference domain.

'is designed for' relates activities/money/time to activities/persons (purpose/design), while 'can stay in' relates persons to places (accommodation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

endReview relates a Program Committee Chair to a Review (ending the review process), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document (giving a presentation). These are entirely different relations with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In confOf, Member is a subclass of Participant (which extends Person), with siblings Regular and Student, indicating it represents a type of conference attendee/participant. In edas, Attendee is a direct subclass of Person representing someone who attends the conference. Since confOf's Member is a specific kind of participant (alongside Regular and Student), it is more specific than edas's general Attendee class. Thus Member is subsumed by Attendee.

Attendee is a general participant in a conference (parent: Person), while General Chair is a specific organizing role (parent: Organizator). They represent different concepts: one is a broad attendance role, the other is a leadership/organizer role. No subsumption holds since Attendee does not necessarily organize and General Chair is not merely an attendee.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (who performed the assignment), while isReviewHistoryOf links a PersonalReviewHistory to a Reviewer. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Academic Institution is an organization (e.g., university). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Published Paper is a subclass of Paper (a document), while Best Research Paper Award is a subclass of Award. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking important dates to a full paper submission date, while Property B is an object property linking a paper to its presentation type. They describe entirely different concepts and have different domains, ranges, and property types.

Conference Participant in ekaw is a broad class encompassing all people involved in a conference (chairs, reviewers, presenters, registered participants, etc.). Lecturer in iasted is a specific type of speaker/author who gives lectures. A Lecturer would be a kind of Conference Participant (specifically a Presenter), so Conference Participant subsumes Lecturer.

Workshop in confOf is a type of working event (like a conference or tutorial), whereas Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Organisation in ekaw refers to an organizational entity (e.g., academic institution, publisher), while State in iasted refers to a geographical or administrative location/state. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Tutorial in the conference domain. Although they are placed under different parent hierarchies (Working event vs Individual Presentation), their intended instances coincide: tutorial sessions held at a conference.
Conference Member is a person participating in a conference, while Travel Grant is a type of sponsorship/funding. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Closing Talk is a specific talk event that concludes a conference, while Plenary lecture is a lecture delivered to all attendees. Both are conference-wide presentation events but serve different purposes and occur at different times; they overlap as related concepts but are not equivalent.

In ekaw, Student is a subclass of Person, representing specifically students. In sigkdd, Person is the top-level class for all people (with children Listener, Organizator, Speaker). Therefore, ekaw:Student is strictly more specific than sigkdd:Person, making it subsumed_by sigkdd:Person.

Property A is specifically the abstract submission date (a particular kind of deadline), while property B is a generic 'done till' date for any Deadline. They share the same datatype pattern (domain -> date) and both relate to deadlines, but A is more specific than B, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A ('is a topis of conference parts') links a Topic to a Conference part, expressing a thematic/subject relationship. Property B ('partOf' in ekaw) is a standard mereological (whole-part) relation between entities. These are semantically different relations.

markConflictOfInterest relates people (Author, Chairman, Reviewer) to Papers to indicate a conflict of interest, while parallel_with relates Administrative events to each other to indicate they occur in parallel. These are entirely different concepts with no overlap.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a version/format of a paper (the abstract portion), while Demo Paper in ekaw is a category/type of paper submitted for a demonstration track. They represent orthogonal classifications and are not equivalent.
'is Menu Of' links a Meal Menu to a Meal Event, while 'need' links a Person to an Item. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

A 'Conference Session' in edas is a sub-event or part of a conference (e.g., a specific session within the program), whereas 'Conference' in sigkdd represents the entire conference event itself with properties like city, start/end dates, and organizer. These are distinct concepts at different levels of granularity.

isProviderOf relates an Organization to a Sponsorship (providing sponsorship), while payed_by relates a Registration fee to a Person (who pays the fee). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasConflictOfInterest relates a Person to a Document (indicating a conflict of interest), while hasRating relates an Active Paper to a Review Rating. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

In Ontology A, 'Rejected contribution' is a subclass of document/artefact (a paper that was rejected). In Ontology B, 'Refusing manuscript' is a subclass of Activity (the act/process of refusing a manuscript). They refer to the same conference-domain concept (rejection of a paper) but model it differently—one as an artefact state, the other as an activity—so they are related but not equivalent.
Conference is an event (a type of working event), while Hotel registration form is a document/form used for hotel registration. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of past reviews), while Property B links a specific Review to the Possible Reviewer who wrote it. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics; they are not equivalent nor inverses.

eventOnList relates an Event to a Programme Brochure or Web Site (indicating the event is listed there), while presentation relates a Speaker to a Document. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Workshop is a type of event. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (child of Person). Early Registered Participant in ekaw is a specific kind of Conference Participant who registered early. Thus, Attendee subsumes Early Registered Participant.
Car is a transport vehicle (subclass of Item), while Organizator is a person who organizes the conference. These are completely unrelated concepts.

confOf:Organization is a general organization class (with children Company and University), while ekaw:Academic Institution is specifically an academic organization (a subclass of Organisation with children Research Institute and University). Thus Organization subsumes Academic Institution.

Organisation in ekaw represents an organizational entity (e.g., academic institution, publisher), while Document in sigkdd represents a written artefact (e.g., paper, abstract, review). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Committee (a structural part), while property B links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Company is an Organization (a type of institution/business), while Hotel is a Place (a physical venue for accommodation). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.
hasCountry is an object property linking Conference to Country, while Nation is a datatype property linking Person to a string. They differ in domain, range, property type, and intended meaning.

Student registration fee in iasted is a specific type of Registration fee, which is a subclass of Fee. In sigkdd, Fee is the general class with Registration fee as a child. Therefore, Student registration fee is strictly subsumed by Fee.

Conference www is a type of conference document (a web resource with a URL), while Sponsor company house is a physical building/place where a sponsor company is located. They are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the concept of a topic or subject area within the conference domain. In confOf, Topic is associated with contributions (papers), working events, and PC members. In edas, Topic is associated with conferences and papers. Their intended instances coincide as subject areas for papers/conferences.

Both classes represent the final, complete version of a paper (as opposed to an abstract or draft). In cmt, 'Paper Full Version' is contrasted with 'Paper Abstract', while in ekaw, 'Camera Ready Paper' denotes the final submission-ready version. In the conference domain, these refer to the same concept: the full, finalized paper.

Both classes are named Paper, share the same parent class Document, and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a paper submitted by an author for review. Despite differences in property richness between the two ontologies, their intended instances coincide.
A Workshop is a conference event/session, while a Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

In cmt, Author is a person who writes/submits papers. In Conference, 'Conference contributor' is a broader class whose children include 'Regular author', 'Active conference participant', and 'Invited speaker'. Thus Author (cmt) is subsumed by Conference contributor (Conference), as the latter encompasses more than just authors.

Property A is a datatype property linking a Person to their first name (string), while Property B is an object property linking a Person to a Place and Time of presence. They describe entirely different relations.

registrationDueOn is a datatype property linking a Conference to a dateTime for registration deadlines, while listsEvent is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision, while has_a_publisher links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Chair is a person role (committee chair) while Registration fee is a monetary concept. They are entirely unrelated.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Video cassette player is a piece of audiovisual equipment. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
hasMember relates a Conference to a Person (membership), while hold relates ACM SIGKDD (an organization) to a Conference (organizing/holding an event). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while Final manuscript is a type of Submission (the actual document submitted). They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'writtenBy' relates a Document to its author (Person), while 'notification until' relates an Author to a notification deadline. These properties have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
Acceptance is a type of Decision (outcome of paper review), while Speaker is a type of Person who presents at a conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contribution in Ontology A is a subclass of Conference document (an artefact like a paper, poster, or talk), whereas Speaker in Ontology B is a subclass of Person (a role). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Workshop is a type of working event (a conference session), while Powerline Transmission Topic is a subject area/topic for papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Administrator in confOf is a person who manages the conference system (confTool), while Reviewer in iasted is a speaker who reviews papers. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities and positions in their respective ontologies.

confOf:Paper is a general class for papers (a type of Contribution), while edas:PendingPaper is a specific subclass of Paper representing papers in a pending state. Therefore confOf:Paper subsumes edas:PendingPaper.

In ekaw, 'Possible Reviewer' is a subclass of 'Person', representing people who could review papers. In sigkdd, 'Person' is the top-level class for all people. Thus, ekaw's Possible Reviewer is strictly more specific than (subsumed by) sigkdd's Person.

'has Conflict Of Interest' relates a Person to a Document they have a conflict with, while 'submit' relates an Author to a Paper they are submitting. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
hasMember relates a Conference to its Person members (attendees/committee), while holded_by relates a Conference to the organizing body (ACM SIGKDD). Different ranges and different semantics.
Property A links a review preference to a submitted contribution or topic, while Property B links a personal review history to a reviewer. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links 'Important dates' to a 'Conference volume', while Property B links an 'Event' to its organizing 'Organisation' or 'Person'. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Regular author in Ontology A is a type of conference contribution/contributor (a person who authored a paper), while Two Level Conference in Ontology B is a type of conference event. These are entirely different concepts in the domain.
Government Organization is a type of organization (institution), while Organizing Committee member is a type of person/role. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Committee member is a person role in conference organization, while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They are completely unrelated concepts.

Track is a scientific event (a thematic track within a conference), while Organizing Committee is a committee responsible for organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (with organizational hierarchy), while One conference day in iasted is a temporal concept representing a single day of a conference. They are completely unrelated.

Abstract in Ontology A is a type of conference document (a short summary of a paper/poster/presentation), while Activity in Ontology B represents an event or action (e.g., conference activity) with temporal and spatial properties. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is a research topic (Computer Networks Applications Topic) under the Topic hierarchy in edas, while Entity B is a piece of audiovisual equipment (Computer) under Item in iasted. They represent entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Workshop is a type of event (a working event), while Demo Chair is a role played by a person (a conference participant). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Accommodation Place in edas refers to lodging (its sibling is Conference Venue Place), while Main office in sigkdd refers to an administrative/organizational office. In sigkdd, Hotel is the accommodation equivalent. These are distinct types of places with no subsumption relationship.

In iasted, 'Student non speaker' is a subclass of Delegate > Non speaker, meaning the student does not present. In sigkdd, 'Author of paper student' is a subclass of Speaker > Author, meaning the student is an author who presents. These are conceptually opposite roles (non-speaker vs. speaker/author), so they are unrelated.
forEvent links a Call to an Academic Event, while search links ACM SIGKDD to a Sponzor (Sponsor). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In cmt, Program Committee Member is a specific role (a conference member who can review). In ekaw, Possible Reviewer is a broader class whose child is PC Member. Thus cmt's Program Committee Member corresponds to ekaw's PC Member and is subsumed by ekaw's Possible Reviewer.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Conference contributions, while property B links a Person to an Item they prepare. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Conference announcement is a type of document (informational artefact), while Conference hall is a physical place/venue. They share only the word 'Conference' but denote entirely different concepts.

writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author (paper-to-author direction), while presentation links a Speaker to a Document (person-to-paper direction). The domains, ranges, and directions are different, so these properties are unrelated.
Accommodation Place is a type of location for lodging, while Van is a type of transport vehicle. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

studyAt relates a Scholar to a University (affiliation/education), while isWrittenBy relates a Paper to an Author (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (event), while Presenter in ekaw is a person who presents at a conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A 'date' is a generic date property for a Conference, while property B 'paperDueOn' is a specific deadline (paper submission due date) for a Conference. They share the same domain but differ in specificity and semantics; 'paperDueOn' is a particular kind of conference date, so they are related but not equivalent.
Early paid applicant is a subclass of Person (a type of conference attendee), while Hotel fee is a subclass of Money/Fee (a monetary charge). They are entirely different concepts.

Short paper in confOf is a type of contribution classified by length/format (sibling of Paper and Poster), whereas Rejected Paper in edas is a paper classified by its review outcome status (rejected). These are orthogonal classifications and denote entirely different concepts.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Architecture Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. They are entirely different concepts.

Invited Talk and Tutorial are both types of conference presentations/lectures but are distinct concepts. In ontology A (ekaw), they are siblings under Individual Presentation, confirming they are different kinds of events. They are related as co-hyponyms in the conference domain but not equivalent.

Property A ('name') is a string-valued datatype property for naming conferences or persons, while property B ('has a date of issue') is a date-valued datatype property for conference documents. They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.
The property 'deals With' links a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter), while 'is paid with' links Money to an Item (payment). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Sponsor state in iasted is a status/state of a sponsor. These are entirely different concepts.
Property A is an inverse of a partOf relation with range Event, while property B relates to Award. They have completely different semantics and ranges.

assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while coversTopic links an Event or Paper to a Research Topic (subject-matter relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
'writtenBy' denotes authorship of a document, while 'is used by' denotes usage of an item. These are semantically distinct relations with different meanings.
Property A links a conference volume to its tutorials (events), while property B links a conference to its members (people). The domains and ranges are entirely different, so they are unrelated.

startDate is a datatype property linking Conference to a dateTime value, while listsEvent is an object property linking Programme Brochure/Web Site to Event. They have completely different domains, ranges, property types, and semantics.

Person in ekaw is a general class for all people involved in the conference (authors, participants, reviewers, etc.), while Speaker in sigkdd is a specific subclass of Person (with siblings Listener and Organizator). Therefore, ekaw:Person subsumes sigkdd:Speaker.

'has gender' is a datatype property on Person indicating gender, while 'is used by' is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and type.

Entity A is a Review (a document evaluating a paper), while Entity B is a Paper (the submitted manuscript). These are distinct concepts in the conference domain; notably, edas also has its own Review class as a sibling of Paper.

'is occupied by' relates a physical location (Building, City, State) to a Person who occupies it, while 'payed by' relates a Registration fee to the Person who pays it. The domains and semantics are entirely different.
presentationOfPaper links an Individual Presentation to a Paper/Abstract, while write links a Person to an Item (authorship). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both properties represent an end date/time, but they differ in domain: 'is an ending date' applies to 'Important dates' (deadlines), while 'has End Date Time' applies to 'Conference Event' (scheduled events). They capture the same temporal notion but for different kinds of entities, so they are related rather than equivalent.
assignedTo links a Paper to a Reviewer (assignment relation), while sign links a Person to an Item (signing relation). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a 'Review expertise' entity to a 'Submitted contribution', while property B links a 'Member PC' (person) to a 'Contribution'. The domains are fundamentally different (an expertise/skill vs. a person), so these properties do not denote the same relation.

In Ontology A, 'Invited speaker' is a specific type of conference contributor who speaks. In Ontology B, 'Speaker' is a general class for anyone who speaks at the conference (with children Author, Reviewer, etc.). Every invited speaker is a speaker, but not every speaker is an invited speaker, so Invited speaker is subsumed by Speaker.

Workshop in edas and Conference in ekaw are distinct types of academic events. In ekaw, Workshop is a sibling of Conference under Scientific Event, confirming they are different concepts. They are related as both are types of scientific/academic events but not equivalent.
