Both classes are named 'Fee' in the conference domain and share a common child 'Registration fee'. They represent the same concept of monetary fees associated with a conference, despite slight differences in their other subclasses (e.g., Hotel fee vs Sponzor fee).

The property 'issues' relates a Publisher to Conference proceedings, while 'searched by' relates a Sponzor (Sponsor) to ACM SIGKDD. These describe entirely different relationships between different kinds of entities.

Paper Author in ekaw is a general class for any person who authored a paper. Lecturer in iasted is a much more specific subclass of Author (under Speaker) denoting someone who gives a lecture. A lecturer may be a paper author, but not all paper authors are lecturers. They overlap but are not equivalent.

In cmt, Reviewer and Program Committee Member are distinct sibling classes under Conference Member, while in edas, TPC Member and Reviewer are also siblings under Person. A TPC Member in edas can review papers but is conceptually a program committee member, not strictly equivalent to a generic Reviewer. They overlap in function (both can review papers) but are not equivalent.

In edas, 'TPC Member' is a subclass of Person representing a Technical Program Committee member who reviews papers and initiates calls. In iasted, 'IASTED member' is a subclass of Delegate (under Place > Building > Conference building) representing membership in the IASTED organization, with siblings like 'Conference Hiker' and 'IASTED non member'. These are conceptually distinct: one is a program committee role, the other is an organizational membership status within a specific conference society.

'speak in' relates a Person to a Place and Time for the purpose of giving a talk/presentation, while 'can stay in' relates a Person to a Place for accommodation purposes. These are semantically distinct relations in the conference domain.
The property 'title' refers to the name/title of a paper, while 'abstract' refers to the summary text of a contribution. These are distinct concepts in the conference domain and are not equivalent.

Attendee in edas is a general participant (sibling of Author, Reviewer, etc.), while Organizing Committee member in sigkdd is a specific organizer role under Organizator. They represent different concepts: one is a general attendee, the other is an organizing committee member.

Both properties link an author-type entity to a Paper, but 'co write Paper' (domain: Co author) specifically denotes co-authorship of a paper, while 'has Related Paper' (domain: Author) is a more general association between an author and a related paper. They overlap in intent but are not strictly equivalent.

The property 'has a publisher' links conference proceedings to a publisher, while 'topic Covered By' links a research topic to events or papers. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Reviewer in Conference ontology is a person who reviews papers (has review expertise, invited by other reviewers). Scholar in confOf is a price category for attendees who study at a university. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Conference document refers to documents related to a conference (papers, reviews, announcements), while State in the iasted ontology refers to a geographical or administrative location (with children like Conference state, Presenter state being states of entities, and properties relating to buildings/cities). These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, Document is an abstract class for conference artefacts (Paper, Review). In iasted, Card is a physical item (child of Item, with child Credit card), clearly unrelated to the document concept. Note that iasted also has its own separate Document class as a sibling of Card.
Reviewer is a person who reviews papers, while Numerical Review Question is a type of question used in a review form. They are entirely different concepts.

Submitted Paper is a research paper that has been submitted to a conference, while Payment document is a financial instrument (bank transfer, cheque) used for payment. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Security) while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In Ontology A, 'Review preference' represents a reviewer's topic preference or willingness to review (with properties like degree and topic), whereas in Ontology B, 'Review' is a Document subclass representing the actual written review artefact. These are conceptually distinct entities.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'forEvent' links a Call to an Academic Event, while 'give' links a Person to an Activity or Item. They represent unrelated relations in the conference domain.

The properties have completely different semantics: 'detailsEnteredBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who entered details, while 'has_a_publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. Different domains, ranges, and meanings.

A 'Call for participation' is a document inviting people to participate in a conference, while 'Brief introduction for Session chair' is a specific informational document prepared for a session chair. These are entirely different types of documents with no semantic overlap.
'locationOf' relates a Location to an Event (spatial), while 'is held before' relates an Activity to a Time (temporal). They describe entirely different dimensions and are unrelated.

Person in Ontology A is a top-level class encompassing all people involved in the conference (committee members, reviewers, participants, contributors, etc.). Author in Ontology B is a subclass of Speaker, which is itself a subclass of Person. Therefore, Person strictly subsumes Author.
Written contribution refers to a scholarly paper or document submitted to a conference, while Bank transfer is a payment method/document. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Both classes represent the general concept of a Person in the conference domain. They share similar properties (email, name/nation) and both have subclasses representing various conference roles (e.g., Author/Participant vs Speaker/Listener). Despite different naming conventions for children and properties, their intended instances coincide.

A Tutorial and a Plenary lecture are distinct types of conference activities. In ontology B (iasted), Tutorial is a sibling of Plenary lecture under Lecture/Conference activity, confirming they are different concepts. They are related as both are conference parts/activities but not equivalent.

'has a name' is a general naming property applicable to multiple entities (Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc.), while 'City of conference' specifically denotes the city where a conference is held. They capture entirely different semantics.

A is a research topic (Computer Networks Security) while B is a type of document (Invited Talk Abstract). They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

submitPaper (Author -> Paper) and contributes (Person -> Conference document) are semantically related as both describe a person providing a document to the conference system. However, they are not strictly equivalent: 'contributes' is more general in both domain (Person vs Author) and range (Conference document vs Paper), and 'contributes' could encompass other types of contributions beyond paper submission. Thus they overlap but are not identical.

Preference in cmt refers to a reviewer's or author's topic/track preference, while Time zone in iasted refers to a geographical time zone. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.
Radio Communications Topic is a subject area for papers, while Card is a physical item (e.g., credit card). They are completely unrelated concepts.

The properties have completely different domains (Conference volume vs Person), ranges (Tutorial vs Item), and semantics (part-of relationship for tutorials vs a need relationship for items). They are unrelated.

Student lecturer (iasted) is a subclass of Lecturer representing a student who gives lectures/talks, while Author of paper (sigkdd) is a subclass of Author representing someone who authored a paper. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with different intended instances.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a review preference (assignment of reviews), while Property B links an activity or item to a person who gives it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing individuals who interact with the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Organization in Conference represents an institution or organizational entity. These are fundamentally different concepts.
Rejected contribution and Accepted Paper represent opposite outcomes of the review process. One is a rejected submission while the other is an accepted paper; they are disjoint concepts.

Property A relates an Abstract to a Paper/Poster/Presentation (part-of relation), while Property B relates a Person to an Activity/Item (giving/presenting relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Presenter in ekaw is a general class for anyone who presents at the conference (with Invited Speaker as a subclass). Plenary lecture speaker in iasted is a specific type of speaker/author who gives a plenary lecture. Since a plenary lecture speaker is a kind of presenter, ekaw:Presenter subsumes iasted:Plenary_lecture_speaker.
'has members' relates a Committee to its Committee members, while 'give' relates a Person to an Activity or Item. The domains, ranges, and intended meanings are entirely different.
A is a specific research topic (Computer Networks Switching), while B is an organizational committee (Program Committee). They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Conference volume to a Committee, while property B links an Author to a Contribution. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Workshop is an academic event typically focused on research presentations and discussions, while an Industrial Session is a conference session dedicated to industry-related topics. They are distinct types of events within a conference with different purposes and intended audiences.

Both properties express a person's participation in a conference: 'memberOfConference' links a Conference Member to a Conference, while 'attendeeAt' links a Person to a Conference Event. The domains (Conference Member vs Person) and ranges (Conference vs Conference Event) differ slightly in specificity, so they are related but not strictly equivalent.

Contact Information in edas represents personal contact details (email, phone, street, city, postal code) of a person, while Location in ekaw represents a physical venue/place where an event is held. These are entirely different concepts.

In cmt, User is a subclass of Person and represents people who interact with the system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer). In edas, Person is the top-level class for all people involved (Attendee, Author, Reviewer, etc.). The children of cmt:User largely overlap with the children of edas:Person, indicating that cmt:User corresponds to edas:Person. Therefore, cmt:User is subsumed by edas:Person.

Property A links a conference part to a track/workshop/tutorial chair (a person role), while property B links a PC member to a topic they are expert on. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

TPC Member (Technical Program Committee Member) in edas and Program Committee member in sigkdd refer to the same role: a person who is part of the program committee responsible for reviewing papers and shaping the conference program. Both are subclasses of Person (or an organizer subclass of Person) and serve equivalent functions in the conference domain.
hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author, while has_a_publisher links Conference proceedings to a Publisher. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Program Committee Chair (cmt) is the chair of the main conference program committee, while Workshop Chair (ekaw) chairs a workshop. Both are chair roles within a conference and share PC Member as a parent, but they refer to distinct organizational roles. The ekaw ontology has a separate PC Chair class that would be the true equivalent of cmt's Program Committee Chair.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (document vs. deadline) and are unrelated.

hasLastName is a datatype property linking a Person to their last name string, while is_given_to is an object property linking an Item to a Person. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Conference Dinner in edas is a specific meal event occurring during a conference, while Conference in sigkdd represents the entire conference event itself (with properties like city, start/end dates, name). These are fundamentally different concepts.

Conference Chair in cmt is a leadership role (Chairman) responsible for the conference, while Hotel presenter in iasted is a type of Delegate who presents from a hotel. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

In cmt, Paper Abstract is a specific part/version of a paper (sibling of Paper Full Version). In Conference, Regular contribution is a broad category of submissions that includes Extended abstract, Paper, etc. as children. These are conceptually very different: one is a component of a document, the other is a class of conference contributions.

An 'Extended abstract' is a short preliminary contribution type, while a 'Final manuscript' is the final camera-ready version of a submission. They represent different stages and types of documents in the conference process and are not equivalent.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Conference hotel is a physical place (building). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Workshop in edas is a type of academic event (a session or meeting), while Workshop Chair in ekaw is a person role (a conference participant who chairs a workshop). These are fundamentally different concepts (event vs. person) and are unrelated.

assignedByAdministrator links a Reviewer to an Administrator (assignment relation), while presentation links a Speaker to a Document (presentation relation). They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

assignExternalReviewer links a Reviewer to an External Reviewer (an assignment action), while hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History (a record of past reviews). These are entirely different relations with different ranges and purposes.

Demo Chair and General Chair are distinct conference roles. A Demo Chair oversees the demonstration track, while a General Chair is the overall head of the conference organization. They share a common ancestor as Person/organizer roles but are not equivalent.
Country and Time zone are entirely different concepts in the conference domain; a country is a geopolitical entity while a time zone is a temporal/geographic region for timekeeping.

Hotel fee is a monetary charge (subclass of Fee/Money) for staying at a hotel, while Hotel is a physical place (subclass of Place). They represent entirely different concepts: one is a cost, the other is a location.
Conference Hiker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending the conference), while Conference in sigkdd represents the conference event itself. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (an activity), while Session room in iasted is a type of Place (a physical location). They represent fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Presenter state in iasted is a status/state of a presenter. These are entirely different concepts.

Contribution co-author is a specific type of author (a role in writing a paper), while Presenter is a conference participant who presents work. These are distinct roles with different intended instances and no hierarchical relationship.
One property represents an email address and the other a biography; they are semantically distinct despite sharing the same domain (Person) and range (string).
writePaper (Author -> Paper) and isWrittenBy (Paper -> Author) are inverse properties of each other, not equivalent. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent.

In Ontology A, 'Extended abstract' is a sibling of 'Paper' under 'Regular contribution', meaning it is explicitly not a paper but a shorter contribution type. In Ontology B, 'Regular Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper'. These denote different kinds of conference contributions (an extended abstract vs. a full regular paper), so they are unrelated.

Property A relates a Committee to its Co-chair (a specific leadership role within a committee), while Property B relates a Person to a Conference (general membership). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A Conference Chair is a leadership role responsible for organizing the conference, while a Passive conference participant is an attendee who does not actively contribute (e.g., a listener). These are distinct roles with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.
hasKeyword relates a Contribution to a string keyword, while hasCostAmount relates a Sponsorship to an integer cost. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Exhibitor is a type of sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Member in confOf is a subclass of Participant (a Person), while Registration SIGMOD Member in sigkdd is a subclass of Registration fee (a Fee). They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies (person vs. monetary fee) and are therefore unrelated.

Research Institute is an organization (a type of academic institution), while Simulating is a research activity performed before a conference. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
The two properties have completely different domains (Conference volume vs Money), ranges (string vs int), and semantics (location vs monetary amount). They are unrelated.

Review Rating in edas represents the numerical/categorical rating assigned to a paper (e.g., Accept, Reject), while Review in ekaw represents the actual review document written by a reviewer. They are related concepts in the reviewing process but not equivalent; one is a rating value and the other is a document.

Author (cmt) is a person who writes/submits papers, while Session Chair (edas) is a person who chairs sessions and may review papers. These are distinct roles in the conference domain with no hierarchical or equivalence relationship.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Nonmember registration fee is a type of monetary fee. They are completely unrelated concepts.

hasAuthor links a Paper to its Author (Paper -> Author), while prepare links a Person to an Item they prepare (Person -> Item). The domains and ranges are in opposite directions relative to the person/author role, and the properties describe different relationships (authorship vs preparation). They are not equivalent.
Associated Chair is a person role (subclass of Chairman), while Main office is a physical place (subclass of Place). They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Conference Member is a person role (subclass of Person) involved in a conference, while Review is a document (subclass of Conference document) that evaluates a contribution. They are entirely different concepts.

Both are subclasses of Person in their respective ontologies, but they cover different sets of roles. cmt:User includes Author and Reviewer (with Chairman and Conference Member as siblings), while confOf:Participant includes Regular and Student participants (with Author, Chair PC, etc. as siblings). They overlap conceptually as people involved in a conference but are not equivalent since their intended instances differ significantly.

Both 'Conference Chair' in cmt and 'General Chair' in sigkdd denote the top-level chairperson responsible for organizing the conference. They occupy analogous positions in their respective hierarchies (under Chairman/Person vs. Organizator/Person) and are siblings to Program Chair roles, indicating they refer to the same concept.

In EKAW, 'Rejected Paper' is a subclass of Paper (a Document), representing the paper artefact that was rejected. In IASTED, 'Refusing manuscript' is a subclass of Activity, representing the act/process of refusing. They are related concepts in the conference domain (the activity results in the document state) but belong to fundamentally different categories (artefact vs. activity), so they are not equivalent.

Paper Abstract is a type of document (a subclass of Paper), while Author of paper student is a type of person (a subclass of Author). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and represent fundamentally different concepts.

'Refusing manuscript' is an activity (the act of rejecting a paper) in the iasted ontology, while 'Deadline Paper Submission' is a temporal deadline for submitting papers in the sigkdd ontology. They represent fundamentally different concepts (an action vs. a date/deadline) and are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics: 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference, while 'presentationed by' links a Document to a Speaker. They are unrelated.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who finalizes paper assignments, while 'writes' links an Author to a Contribution they authored.

In Conference ontology, 'Committee member' is a person serving on a committee (with children Chair, Co-chair). In confOf, 'Member' is a subclass of Participant with siblings Regular and Student, indicating it refers to a type of conference attendee/participant rather than a committee member. They share the word 'member' but denote different concepts in the conference domain.

In confOf, Student is a subclass of Participant (which is under Person). In ekaw, Conference Participant is the general class for all people participating in the conference, and it has its own separate Student subclass. Thus confOf:Student corresponds to ekaw:Student, which is a child of ekaw:Conference_Participant, making confOf:Student subsumed by ekaw:Conference_Participant.

Paper Abstract in cmt is a subtype of Paper representing the abstract portion of a paper, while Assigned Paper in ekaw is a subtype of Submitted Paper representing a paper that has been assigned to reviewers. These are entirely different concepts.

Conference contributor is a Person role (someone who contributes to the conference, e.g., author or speaker), while Registration is an Activity (the act of registering for the conference). They are fundamentally different kinds of entities.

The property 'follows' relates administrative events to each other (temporal ordering), while 'is present in' relates a person to a place and time. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
volumeContainsPaper relates a volume to the papers it contains, while write relates a Person to an Item they authored. These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.

'Conference city' in iasted is a subclass of City representing the location where a conference takes place, whereas 'Conference' in sigkdd represents the conference event itself. These are fundamentally different concepts (a place vs. an event).

Reception and Dinner banquet are both social events at a conference, but they denote different specific types of gatherings (a reception is typically a lighter welcome event with drinks, while a dinner banquet is a formal meal). In confOf, Reception and Banquet are siblings under Social event, indicating they are distinct concepts. Thus they are related but not equivalent.

In cmt, 'Program Committee Member' is a general member of the program committee, with 'Program Committee Chair' as a child class. In sigkdd, 'Program Chair' and 'Program Committee member' are siblings under 'Organizator'. Thus, cmt's Program Committee Member is more general than sigkdd's Program Chair; they overlap but are not equivalent.
Conference Trip is a social event (an organized excursion during a conference), while Taxi is a transport vehicle. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

'starts on' specifically denotes the start date of an Event, while 'is dated on' is a more general dating property for an Activity (which corresponds to Event). They overlap in purpose but differ in specificity: one is strictly about the start, the other could refer to any associated date. Hence they are related rather than equivalent.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document inviting participation, while 'NGO' is a type of organization (Non-Governmental Organization). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area, while submit links an Author to a Paper. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Sponzor fee is a type of monetary fee for sponsors. They belong to entirely different branches of the conference domain and share no semantic overlap.

authorOf (Person -> Document) and is_prepared_by (Item -> Person) are inverse properties: authorOf links a person to the document they authored, while is_prepared_by links an item to the person who prepared it. Since a property and its inverse are not equivalent per the guidelines, they are related.

Property A specifically denotes the date of an acceptance announcement, while property B is a generic deadline date ('done till'). They share the same range (date) and similar domain concepts (Important dates vs Deadline), but A is much more specific than B. They are related but not equivalent.

Submitted Paper is an academic paper submitted to a conference, while Cheque is a payment document. They belong to entirely different conceptual hierarchies and serve unrelated purposes in the conference domain.
hasEvent relates an Event to another Event (e.g., sub-events), while award is a property whose range is Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A is an action by an Administrator to add a Program Committee Member (domain: Administrator, range: Program Committee Member). Property B links a Conference volume to its Program committee (domain: Conference volume, range: Program committee). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics—one is an administrative action on individuals, the other is a structural relation between a conference and its committee.

In iasted, 'Author cd proceedings included' is a specific subclass of Author (authors whose work is included in the CD proceedings). In sigkdd, 'Author' is a general class with subclasses like 'Author of paper' and 'Author of paper student'. The iasted class is strictly more specific than the sigkdd Author class, so it is subsumed by it.

Both classes represent the subject area or research topic of a paper or conference/event. In edas, Topic is linked to Paper and Conference via hasTopic/isTopicOf; in ekaw, Research_Topic is linked to Paper and Event via coversTopic/topicCoveredBy. The intended instances coincide.

The properties have completely different domains and ranges: 'is Written By' relates Paper to Author, while 'is equipped by' relates Place to Item. They describe unrelated concepts in the conference domain.
Both are datatype properties linking a Person to a string representing their email address. Identical domain, range, and semantics.
Modelling is a type of research activity before a conference, while Webmaster is an organizer role (a person). They are completely unrelated concepts.

Chairman in cmt is a leadership/organizational role (parent of Conference Chair, Program Committee Chair) under Person, while Speaker in iasted is a presentation role (child of Delegate) with different children (Author, Reviewer). They represent distinct concepts in the conference domain.
Administrative event is a type of conference event (e.g., submission, reviewing), while Computer Networks Sensor Topic is a subject topic for papers. They are completely unrelated concepts.
Invited speaker is a type of person who participates in a conference, while University is an academic organization. They are completely unrelated concepts.
employedBy relates a Person to an Organization (employment), while providedBy relates a Sponsorship to an Organization (sponsorship provision). Different domains and different semantic meanings.

In cmt, Chairman is a superclass that includes Program Committee Chair as a child, while in sigkdd, Program Committee member is a sibling of Program Chair under Organizator. A chairman (especially a program committee chair) may be a kind of program committee member, but the two classes are not equivalent: Chairman in cmt is broader (includes Conference Chair, Associated Chair), and Program Committee member in sigkdd refers to regular members rather than chairs. They overlap but are not the same concept.

confOf's hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event (a specific subtype), while ekaw's hasEvent links any Event to any Event. Since Administrative events are Events and Working events are Events, hasAdministrativeEvent is a more specific (narrower) property than hasEvent, making it subsumed by hasEvent.

hasSubjectArea links a Paper to its Subject Area (topic), while is_held_in links an Activity to a Place and Time (location/scheduling). These are entirely different relations in the conference domain.
hasCountry relates an Organization or Person to a Country, while hasMember relates a Conference to a Person. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
A 'Call for paper' is a conference document inviting submissions, while 'Powerline Transmission Topic' is a specific subject topic in the edas ontology. They are entirely different concepts.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'written By' relates a Contribution to an Author (who wrote it). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

confOf:Participant is a general class for all conference participants (with children Member, Regular, Student), while ekaw:Late-Registered_Participant is a specific subclass of Conference Participant restricted to those who registered late. Therefore, Participant subsumes Late Registered Participant.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Memeber registration fee is a monetary fee for registration. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference Paper is a scholarly paper presented at a conference, while Record of attendance is an administrative document tracking who attended. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference proceedings refers to the published volume of papers from a conference, while Conference in sigkdd refers to the event itself (with city, start/end dates). These are distinct concepts.

set Max Papers relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (setting a limit on papers), while is Member Of relates a Person to a Conference (indicating membership). These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

A 'Track workshop chair' chairs an entire track or workshop within a conference, while a 'Session chair' chairs a specific session (a smaller unit). They are both types of chairs/organizers but operate at different levels of granularity, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Tutorial Abstract is a type of document (an abstract for a tutorial), while Deadline Abstract Submission is a temporal deadline for submitting abstracts. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
rejectedBy links a Paper to an Administrator who rejected it, while submit links an Author to a Paper they submitted. Different domains, ranges, directions, and semantics.

IASTED member is a specific type of delegate (attendee/participant) in the IASTED conference ontology, while Organizator represents an organizer role (e.g., General Chair, Program Committee member) in the SIGKDD ontology. These are distinct roles: one is a participant/member, the other is an organizer.

Working event in confOf is a type of Event (with children Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Optical Topic in edas is a specific research Topic. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, 'Academic Event' is a subclass of 'Conference Event', which also has a sibling 'Non Academic Event'. In ekaw, 'Event' is the top-level class with children 'Scientific Event' and 'Social Event'. Thus edas:AcademicEvent corresponds to ekaw:ScientificEvent, while edas:ConferenceEvent corresponds to ekaw:Event. Therefore Academic Event is subsumed by (more specific than) Event.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (the head of the PC), while Session Chair in ekaw refers to a person chairing an individual session during the conference. These are distinct roles. Note that ekaw has a separate 'PC Chair' class which would be the true equivalent of confOf's 'Chair PC'. Therefore they are related (both are chair roles) but not equivalent.

In confOf, 'Short paper' is a sibling of 'Paper' and 'Poster' under 'Contribution', meaning it is a specific type of contribution. In ekaw, 'Paper' is a general class with many subtypes (Regular Paper, Demo Paper, Poster Paper, etc.). Thus, confOf's 'Short paper' is subsumed by ekaw's more general 'Paper' class.

Reception is a social event (e.g., a welcome reception at a conference), while Research is an activity before the conference involving scientific investigation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In edas, Sponsorship is a class representing financial support (with cost amount, currency, and provider organization). In iasted, Sponsor state is a subclass of State representing the status/state of a sponsor (alongside Conference state and Presenter state). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a financial arrangement, the other is a status indicator.

In confOf, Conference is a type of Working event (alongside Tutorial and Workshop), representing the overall conference gathering. In edas, Talk Event is a specific academic session within a conference (e.g., Closing Talk, Welcome Talk), sibling to Paper Presentation and Workshop. These denote different concepts: the whole conference vs. a talk session within it.

Property A is an object property linking a Conference volume to an Important dates entity, while Property B is a datatype property linking a Conference Event to a dateTime literal. They differ in type (object vs datatype), domain, and range, and represent different concepts.

hasStreet is a datatype property for the street address of an Organization or Person, while City_of_conference is a datatype property for the city where a Conference takes place. They differ in both domain (Organization/Person vs Conference) and semantic meaning (street vs city), making them unrelated.

Paper Full Version is a complete paper (subclass of Paper), while Invited Talk Abstract is an abstract for an invited talk (subclass of Abstract). They represent entirely different document types at different levels of completeness and for different purposes.

In ekaw, 'Tutorial Abstract' is a specific subclass of 'Abstract', while in sigkdd, 'Abstract' is the general class for all abstracts (with siblings Paper and Review). Therefore, the more specific Tutorial Abstract from ekaw is subsumed by the general Abstract class in sigkdd.

In cmt, Rejection is a Decision (an act/outcome), while in ekaw, Rejected Paper is a Paper (a document that received a rejection decision). They are closely related conceptually but belong to different categories (decision vs. paper), so they are not equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or general information to attendees, while 'Computer Networks Aapplications Topic' is a specific research topic within the computer networks domain. These are entirely different concepts with no semantic overlap.

Property A links a Personal Review History to a Reviewer, while property B links a Speaker to a Document (presentation). These relate entirely different concepts and directions in the conference domain.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' denotes the event/organization itself (with properties like date, logo URL, accepts submissions). In ontology B, 'Conference applicant' is a subclass of Person representing someone who applies to attend the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent the Program Chair role in a conference organization. 'Chair PC' (Chair of the Program Committee) in confOf and 'Program Chair' in sigkdd denote the same concept: the person leading the program committee. Both are subclasses of Person (directly or via Organizator), and their sibling classes (Member PC / Program Committee member) further confirm they occupy the same position in the conference hierarchy.

Antennas Topic is a research subject area (subclass of Topic), while Audiovisual equipment is a physical item (subclass of Item). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Conference Chair in cmt is the overall chair of a conference (a leadership role), while One day presenter in iasted is a delegate who presents for only one day. These are entirely different roles with no hierarchical or overlapping relationship.

Property A (logo URL) has domain Conference and range anyURI, specifically pointing to a logo image. Property B (has a URL) has domain 'Conference www' (a website class) and range string, pointing to a general website URL. They differ in both domain (Conference vs Conference www) and intended meaning (logo vs general web address), so they are unrelated.
Property A links a Conference volume to its Tutorial parts, while property B links a Contribution (paper) to a Topic it deals with. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Paid applicant is a subclass of Person representing someone who has paid to attend the conference, while Social event is a subclass of Event representing social activities like banquets or receptions. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A 'Call for participation' is a conference document (an announcement inviting participation), while 'Submissions deadline' is a temporal deadline for submitting papers. They belong to entirely different categories (document vs. time/deadline) and are unrelated.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'enter Review Criteria' links an Administrator to a Conference for setting review criteria, while 'hasReview' links a Paper to its Review. They are unrelated.

Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Delegate in iasted is a person attending the conference (with parents including Person and Registration). These are entirely different concepts.

A 'Published Paper' is a paper that has been accepted and published (a final state), while an 'Initial manuscript' is the first version of a submission before revisions. These represent opposite ends of the paper lifecycle and are not equivalent.
Property A links a Committee to its Chair (a membership/leadership role), while Property B links an Event to its organising Organisation or Person. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Both classes represent a Paper in the conference domain. In confOf, Paper is a subclass of Contribution (with siblings Poster and Short paper), while in sigkdd it is a subclass of Document (submitted by an Author). Despite different parent class names, both denote the same concept: a full paper submitted to a conference.

Workshop is a type of working event (an academic session), while Presenter house is a type of building (a physical accommodation place). They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.

hasReviewHistory links a Reviewer to their Personal Review History, while presentation links a Speaker to a Document. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Rejected contribution (A) refers specifically to papers that have been rejected after review, while Active Paper (B) is a broader class representing papers still in the process (with Rejected Paper as a sibling). They denote different stages/concepts and are not equivalent.

'invited by' relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while 'reviewes' relates a PC Member to a Contribution (paper they review). These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both classes represent a talk or lecture given by a speaker at a conference. In edas, Talk Event is an academic event with children like Welcome Talk and Closing Talk, and sibling Paper Presentation. In iasted, Speaker lecture is a type of session/lecture within conference activities. Despite different hierarchical placements, their intended instances (a speaker delivering a talk/lecture at a conference) coincide.

Multimedia Topic is a subject area/topic for papers (subclass of Topic), while Audiovisual equipment refers to physical hardware items like projectors and computers (subclass of Item). They are entirely different concepts.
Conference in confOf is a type of Working event (an academic gathering), while Trip day in iasted is a subclass of Time (a temporal unit). They represent entirely different concepts.

In ontology A, Organizer is a specific role (likely a subclass of Person or a distinct class for those who organize). In ontology B (ekaw), Person is a general class with children like Paper Author, Conference Participant, etc., and can participate in organizing via the 'organises' property. An Organizer is a kind of Person, but not all Persons are Organizers, so they are related (Organizer subsumed_by Person) rather than equivalent.

In ontology A (iasted), 'Registration fee' is a class under Fee with children including various member/non-member/student registration fees. In ontology B (sigkdd), 'Registration SIGKDD Member' is a specific subclass of 'Registration fee'. Therefore, the iasted 'Registration fee' subsumes the sigkdd 'Registration SIGKDD Member'.

hasPhone relates Contact Information to a phone number string, while has_amount_of relates Money to an integer amount. These are entirely different properties with different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'writtenBy' is a specific authorship property linking a Contribution to an Author, while 'hasPart' is a generic mereological (part-whole) property with unspecified domain and range. They express fundamentally different relations.

has_tracks relates a conference volume to its tracks (programmatic subdivisions), while hasLocation relates a conference event to a physical place. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both classes are named Paper, share the same parent Document, and represent the same concept in the conference domain: a paper submitted by an author for review. The edas ontology provides more detail (children, additional properties), but the intended instances coincide.

Camera Ready event is an administrative event for submitting final camera-ready papers, while Conference is a scientific event representing the conference itself. They are entirely different concepts under different branches of the Event hierarchy.

In ekaw, 'Conference Paper' is a specific subclass of Paper (which is under Document). In iasted, 'Document' is a broad class whose children include Submission, Review, Form, etc. A Conference Paper is a kind of document/submission, so the more specific ekaw class is subsumed by the more general iasted Document class.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Signal Processing Topic' is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.
Trip is a social event (an activity/excursion), while IASTED member is a type of delegate (a person). They are completely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Author Not Reviewer' is a subclass of 'Author', representing authors who are not reviewers. In edas, 'Author' is the general class for all authors. Therefore, cmt's 'Author Not Reviewer' is strictly more specific than (subsumed by) edas's 'Author'.

In ekaw, 'Assigned Paper' is a subclass of 'Submitted Paper', which is a subclass of 'Paper'. In sigkdd, 'Paper' is the general class for papers. Therefore, ekaw's 'Assigned Paper' (a paper that has been assigned to reviewers) is strictly more specific than sigkdd's general 'Paper' class, making it subsumed by sigkdd's Paper.

Academia Organization in edas refers to academic institutions (universities, research centers), while Proceedings Publisher in ekaw refers to an organization that publishes conference proceedings. Although an academic institution could act as a proceedings publisher, the concepts have different intended meanings and roles. They are related but not equivalent.

Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a Document (specifically an Abstract) for an invited talk, while Plenary lecture in iasted is an Activity/Event (a type of Lecture). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event), so they are unrelated.

In edas, 'Conference' represents the overall conference event/organization (with properties like end date, country, paper deadlines). In iasted, 'Conference activity' is a subclass of 'Activity' representing specific scheduled activities within a conference (e.g., coffee break, lecture, registration). These are fundamentally different concepts: one is the conference itself, the other is an activity that takes place during it.

In Ontology A, Poster is a type of conference contribution (a presentation format), while Abstract is a separate class linked to Poster via 'has an abstract'. In Ontology B, Abstract is a type of Document representing the abstract text itself. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is a presentation/contribution type, the other is a document/summary.

Property A (reviewes) links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper), indicating who reviews which paper. Property B (reviewWrittenBy) links a Review document to a Possible Reviewer, indicating authorship of the review text. They have different domains (Member vs Review), different ranges (Contribution vs Possible Reviewer), and model different relationships in the reviewing process.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Meeting Room Place is a physical location. They are entirely unrelated concepts.
hasKeyword relates a Contribution to its keyword string, while hasLastName relates a Person to their last name string. Different domains and entirely different semantics.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of a conference), while Conference days is a temporal concept representing the duration/days of a conference. They are entirely unrelated.

hasConferenceMember links a Conference to its Conference Members (participants/committee members), while organisedBy links an Event to the Organisation or Person that organises it. These relate different kinds of entities in different roles (membership vs. organisation) and are not equivalent.

Registration form is a document/form used for registration, while Registration Student is a type of registration fee. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories (document vs. fee) and are unrelated.
Reception is a social event at a conference, while Credit card is a payment card. They are entirely unrelated concepts.

Property A (writes) relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), expressing authorship. Property B (relatedToPaper) relates a Paper Presentation (an event) to an Accepted Paper, expressing that a presentation is about a paper. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

In confOf, Scholar is a price category for a person (likely a student) who studies at a University. In iasted, Reviewer is a subclass of Speaker (subclass of Delegate) representing someone who reviews papers. These are conceptually distinct roles in the conference domain.

Property A (updatedVersionOf) relates a Document to another Document indicating versioning, while property B (give) relates a Person to an Activity or Item indicating presentation/delivery. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Gold Supporter is a sponsorship tier. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A is a datatype property linking events to a string location, while property B is an object property linking persons to place/time entities. They differ in domain (events vs persons), range type (string vs object), and semantic intent.
Paper is a document/contribution (a written work), while Paper Author is a person who authored a paper. They belong to entirely different categories and are unrelated.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (summary of a paper), while Double hotel room is a type of accommodation place. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Reception is a social event (e.g., welcome reception) occurring as part of the conference, while Departure is an activity after the conference involving attendees leaving. They are conceptually distinct and unrelated.

In ontology A (cmt), 'Conference' represents the conference event/organization itself with properties like dates, members, and administrators. In ontology B (Conference), 'Conference www' is a subclass of 'Conference document' representing a conference website or web page (with siblings like Call for paper, Review, etc.). These are entirely different concepts: one is an event/organization, the other is a document/web resource.

Organization in edas represents institutional entities (academia, government, industry, NGO) that provide sponsorships, while Person in iasted represents human individuals (delegates, sponsors). These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference state in iasted is a subclass of State (likely representing a status or phase), while Organizator in sigkdd is a subclass of Person representing an organizer role. These are entirely different concepts.

The property 'run Paper Assignment Tools' relates an Administrator to a Conference for the purpose of running assignment tools, while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (author writes paper), while 'is signed by' relates an Item to a Person in the inverse direction (item is signed by person). The semantics and directions differ significantly; they are not equivalent or closely related.

'writes' relates an Author to a Contribution (paper), while 'references' denotes a citation or reference relationship between documents. These are semantically distinct properties in the conference domain.

'has a name' is a datatype property for naming entities (domain includes Conference, Publisher, Topic, etc., range string), while 'end Date' is a datatype property specifically for the end date/time of a conference (range dateTime). They represent entirely different concepts.

In the conference domain, 'Paper' in edas and 'Submission' in iasted both refer to the manuscript/paper submitted by authors for review. Both are subclasses of Document, have Review as a sibling, and their children (Accepted/Rejected vs Initial/Final manuscript) represent stages of the same artefact. They denote the same concept.

Property A links a Program Committee to its members (range: Program Committee Member), while Property B links a Program committee to the Conference volume it serves (range: Conference volume). They have different ranges and express fundamentally different relationships.

A 'Conference applicant' is someone who applies to attend (with child 'Registeered applicant'), while an 'Attendee' in edas is someone who actually attends the conference. They are related roles in the participation lifecycle but not equivalent: one denotes a prospective participant and the other a confirmed/actual participant.
submitPaper relates an Author to a Paper (submission action), while dealsWith relates a Contribution to a Topic (subject matter). Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Rejected Paper is a type of paper (document) that was not accepted, while Deadline for notification of acceptance is a temporal deadline. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.
Conference Member in cmt is a Person role (participant in a conference), while Conference state in iasted is a State (status/condition related to a conference). These are entirely different concepts.

Regular contribution in Ontology A is a type of conference document/contribution (a written artefact like a paper or extended abstract), while Paper Presentation in Ontology B is a type of conference event (the act of presenting a paper). They belong to fundamentally different categories (document vs. event) and are not equivalent.
'deals With' links a Contribution (paper) to a Topic (subject area), while 'go through' links an Item to an Activity (process/event). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Early paid applicant and Late Registered Participant are conceptually distinct: one refers to an early-paying registrant, the other to a late-registered participant. They are related as both represent conference attendees differentiated by registration timing, but they are not equivalent nor in a subsumption relationship.
'has a name' is a datatype property linking various entities to a string name, while 'registrationDueOn' links a Conference to a dateTime deadline. They have different semantics, domains, and ranges.
'is Member Of' relates a Person to a Conference (membership), while 'need' relates a Person to an Item (requirement). These are semantically distinct relations with different ranges and meanings.

The properties describe entirely different relations: 'paperAssignmentFinalizedBy' links a Conference to an Administrator who finalizes paper assignments, while 'paperPresentedAs' links a Paper to an Individual Presentation. Different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Fee in iasted represents a monetary charge (with children like Registration fee, Hotel fee), while Silver Supporter in sigkdd represents a sponsorship tier. These are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.
hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event, while submit links an Author to a Paper. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Accepted contribution is a class of documents (a paper that has been accepted), while Submission event is a class of events (the act of submitting contributions). They belong to entirely different categories in the conference domain.

A Workshop Paper is a specific type of full paper presented at a workshop, while an Abstract is a brief summary document. They are distinct types of documents in the conference domain with different intended instances.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a subclass of 'Person', representing specifically those persons who serve on a committee. In Ontology B (edas), 'Person' is the top-level class for all people, with children including Attendee, Author, Reviewer, TPC Member, etc. Thus, edas:Person subsumes Conference:Committee_member.
Presenter in edas is a Person (specifically an Author who presents), while Presenter city in iasted is a City. They are completely different concepts.

Both properties represent a start date as datatype properties with dateTime/date ranges, but they have different domains: 'Important dates' in ontology A versus 'Conference' in ontology B. They are related (both capture the notion of a starting date) but not equivalent because they apply to different classes.
Multimedia Topic is a subject area for papers, while Program Committee is an organizational body that reviews papers. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

A is a registration fee for author attendees who want the conference book, while B is a registration fee for non-members. They are sibling-level subclasses of Registration fee in their respective ontologies but denote different categories (author-attendee-book vs. non-member), so they are unrelated.

Conference Member in cmt is a broad class encompassing all roles (Author, Reviewer, Conference Chair, Program Committee Member, etc.), while Session Chair in edas is a specific role for chairing a session. Conference Member subsumes Session Chair since a session chair is a type of conference member, but they are not equivalent.
Paper Presentation is an academic event where a paper is presented, while Best Student Paper Supporter is a type of sponsor. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Conference contributor in Ontology A is a broad class for people who contribute content (authors, speakers, active participants), while OC Member in ekaw refers specifically to an Organizing Committee member. These are distinct roles: one contributes scholarly content, the other organizes the event. They do not share the same intended instances.
'writtenBy' links a contribution to its author, while 'award' links something to an award. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference, while property B links a Person to an Activity or Item they give. These have different domains, ranges, and semantics in the conference domain.

Pending Paper in edas refers to a paper's review status (awaiting decision), while Workshop Paper in ekaw refers to the venue/track type where the paper is presented. These are orthogonal classifications and do not denote the same concept.

Sponzorship in iasted is a type of Money (financial concept), while Bronze Supporter in sigkdd is a specific tier/role of a Sponzor (sponsor). They are related through the sponsorship domain but are not equivalent: one represents a financial transaction/category and the other represents a sponsor role.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Organizing committee, while property B links an Author to a Contribution they write. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.

Chair in Ontology A is a generic committee chair (with Co-chair as sibling), while OC Chair in ekaw specifically denotes the Organizing Committee Chair. They overlap conceptually but are not strictly equivalent since A's Chair could also refer to a PC Chair or other committee chairs.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Steering committee (a structural/organizational part), while Property B links an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Conference applicant is a person applying to attend or register for the conference (child: Registeered applicant), while SC Member is a Steering Committee member involved in organizing the conference. These are entirely different roles.
writtenBy links a Contribution to its Author, while hasReview links a Paper to its Review. These are entirely different relations with different domains and ranges.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Contributed Talk is a type of event/presentation. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

In cmt, 'Associated Chair' is a subclass of 'Chairman' and sibling to 'Program Committee Chair', suggesting it is a distinct role (e.g., Associate/Co-Chair). In sigkdd, 'Program Chair' corresponds to the head of the program committee. These are related chair-level organizing roles but not equivalent; the cmt ontology explicitly distinguishes Associated Chair from Program Committee Chair.

Chair PC in confOf refers to the Program Committee Chair (head of the entire PC), while Session Chair in edas refers to a person chairing an individual session during the conference. These are distinct roles with different responsibilities, though both are types of chairs within a conference organization.

Conference in confOf is the main conference event itself (a subtype of Working event), while Activity after conference in iasted refers to activities that take place after the conference (e.g., departure, tours). These are distinct concepts with no subsumption or equivalence relationship.

Property A ('invited by') relates a Reviewer to another Reviewer (who invited them), while Property B ('has Reviewer') relates a Paper to a Possible Reviewer (assigned to review it). The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Academic Institution is an organization (e.g., university or research institute), while Author is a person who writes papers. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Attendee in edas is a general class for any person attending the conference (parent: Person), while Presenter in ekaw is a specific role of someone who presents (child of Conference Participant, with child Invited Speaker). A presenter is typically an attendee, but not all attendees are presenters. They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent; 'related' best captures this partial overlap.

User in cmt is a broad class covering anyone interacting with the system (Administrator, Author, Reviewer), while Speaker in sigkdd specifically denotes someone who gives a presentation at the conference. They overlap (both can have Authors as children) but are not equivalent; they are related concepts under Person.

In cmt, 'Conference' represents the overall conference event/organization (with members, dates, logo, etc.). In the Conference ontology, 'Conference volume' is a child of 'Conference' and represents a specific edition/volume of a conference (with committees, location, tracks, contributions). They overlap in meaning but are not strictly equivalent: one is the general concept, the other a specific instantiation or sub-concept. Hence 'related'.

Workshop is a type of event (a working session at a conference), while Plenary lecture speaker is a role/person who delivers a plenary lecture. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

'acceptPaper' is a specific administrative action linking an Administrator to a Paper (acceptance decision), while 'give' is a general action linking a Person to an Activity or Item. They differ in domain, range, and semantic intent.

confOf's Social event is a broad category including Banquet, Reception, and Trip. edas's Meal Event is specifically about meals (with child Conference Dinner) and is a sibling of edas's own Social Event class. They overlap (banquets/dinners are both social and meal events) but neither subsumes the other, so they are related.

In confOf, 'Camera Ready event' is an Administrative event (a process/activity), while in iasted, 'Camera ready manuscript deadline' is a Deadline (a point in time). They are related as they both pertain to the camera-ready phase of a conference, but they model different aspects (event vs. deadline) and are not equivalent.

Both are subclasses of Author in their respective ontologies, but 'Author Not Reviewer' specifically restricts authors who are not reviewers, while 'Author of paper' is a general class for anyone authoring a paper (with a student subclass). They overlap significantly but are not equivalent due to the reviewer constraint in A.
Property A relates two Administrative events that occur in parallel, while property B relates a Document to the Speaker who presents it. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Science Worker in confOf is a broad category for academic/research personnel (with subclasses like Author, Scholar, Member PC), whereas Agency Staff Member in ekaw refers to staff from an external agency (e.g., event management or travel agency). They represent fundamentally different roles in the conference domain.

minChoice is a datatype property (range positiveInteger) indicating a minimum selection count for events, while organisedBy is an object property linking an Event to its organiser (Organisation or Person). They have completely different semantics, domains, and ranges.

Conference document in Ontology A is a specific class for conference-related documents (calls for papers, reviews, contributions, etc.). Item in Ontology B (iasted) is a very broad physical/logistical class encompassing audiovisual equipment, cards, transport vehicles, and also documents/publications. They do not denote the same concept; at best they overlap slightly via Document/Publication children of Item, but overall they are unrelated.

Workshop is a type of academic event (a session at a conference), while Organizing Committee is a group of people responsible for organizing the conference. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Review expertise in Ontology A represents a reviewer's level of knowledge or skill regarding a topic/paper, while Review Form in edas is a document template used to structure the review process. These are entirely different concepts.

'heldIn' relates an Event to a Location (where the event takes place), while 'is_equipped_by' relates a Place to an Item (equipment). These are semantically distinct relations with different domains, ranges, and meanings.

In edas, 'Rated Papers' is a subclass of 'Active Paper', which is itself a subclass of 'Paper'. In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers. Therefore, 'Rated Papers' (a paper that has been rated) is strictly more specific than and subsumed by the general 'Paper' class in ekaw.

In edas, Social Event is a Non Academic Event (excluding lectures/presentations). In iasted, Conference activity includes both academic events (Lecture, Presentation) and social events (Cocktail reception, Social program, Coffee break). Therefore, edas Social Event is strictly narrower than iasted Conference activity, making it subsumed_by.

Conference proceedings in Ontology A refers to a published document/volume (with ISBN, publisher, volume), while Conference Event in Ontology B refers to an event with attendees, location, and dates. These are entirely different concepts.

confOf:Paper is a specific type of academic contribution (alongside Poster and Short paper). iasted:Submission represents the act or document of submitting something, with children like 'Initial manuscipt' and 'Final manuscript', but also includes non-paper items like forms and payment documents as siblings. They overlap in that papers are submitted, but they are not equivalent concepts.

Reviewer is a Person who reviews papers, while Personal Review History is a record/history of reviews associated with a reviewer. They are fundamentally different concepts (agent vs. information artifact).

The two properties have different domains: 'readPaper' has domain Reviewer (a person), while 'reviewOfPaper' has domain Review (a document/artefact). They relate different kinds of entities to Paper and thus are not equivalent.

Conference Venue Place (edas) refers to the physical venue/building where the conference is held, while Presenter city (iasted) refers to the city associated with a presenter. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Company is an organization type (business entity), while Personal Publication History is a record of an individual's publications. These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Property A links a Reviewer to their review expertise or preference, while Property B links a Person to an Item they write. These describe entirely different relationships in the conference domain.

Conference_applicant in Ontology A is a direct subclass of Person representing someone who applies to attend the conference, with Registeered applicant as a child. Early Registered Participant in ekaw is a subclass of Conference Participant representing someone who has already registered early. An applicant is not yet a participant, and 'early registered' adds a temporal qualifier absent from the general applicant concept. They are related through the registration/application process but are not equivalent, nor does one strictly subsume the other.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Conference Banquet is a social event. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
The 'email' property represents an email address of a Person, while 'has Last Name' represents the last name (surname) of a Person. These are entirely different attributes and thus unrelated.
Conference in confOf is a type of Working event (the main academic gathering), while Coffee break in iasted is a specific short activity within a conference. They denote entirely different concepts.

Decision in cmt refers to the outcome of a paper review (Acceptance/Rejection), while Organisation in ekaw refers to an institutional entity (Academic Institution, Organising Agency, etc.). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

Property A links a Conference volume to its Workshops (part-of relation for events), while Property B links a Conference to Persons (membership relation). The domains and ranges are entirely different, making them unrelated.

Dining Place is a spatial location (subclass of Place) where meals are served, while Conference Banquet is a social event (subclass of Social Event). They belong to different ontological categories (place vs. event), though a banquet typically takes place at a dining place, making them related but not equivalent.

Paper Full Version is a document/artefact (subclass of Paper), while Author of paper is a person/role (subclass of Author). They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and denote fundamentally different concepts.

Working event in confOf is a type of conference event (e.g., Conference, Tutorial, Workshop), while Computer Networks Measurements Topic in edas is a specific research topic area. They are entirely different concepts.
Property A links a Review to a Reviewed contribution, while property B links a Person to Money. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different semantics: 'add Program Committee Member' relates an Administrator to a Program Committee Member (an administrative action), while 'parallel with' relates two Administrative events to each other (a temporal/scheduling relation). They are unrelated.

Property A links a track/workshop chair to the conference part they chair, while property B links various roles (Conference Chair, Session Chair, TPC Member) to a Call they initiate. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.
Call For Manuscripts is a type of Call (an invitation to submit), while Review is a Document representing an evaluation of a submission. They are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (a gathering), while Invited Talk Abstract in ekaw is a type of document (an abstract). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain.

locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while Name_of_sponsor is a datatype property linking a Sponsor to a string. They describe entirely different relations in the conference domain.

'has parts' relates a Conference volume to its constituent Conference parts (e.g., proceedings sections), while 'has Member' relates a Conference to a Person (participant). These are fundamentally different relations with different domains and ranges.

Both are datatype properties mapping an entity to a string label, but 'has a name' applies broadly to conferences, publishers, topics, etc., while 'has Title' is specifically for the title of a Contribution (paper). They overlap in purpose (naming) but differ significantly in domain and semantics (name vs. title), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Property A (co-writePaper) specifically relates a Co-author to a Paper they co-wrote, while property B (contributes) is more general, relating any Person to any Conference document. They overlap in the sense that co-writing a paper is a form of contributing to a conference document, but they differ in both domain specificity and range scope, so they are related rather than equivalent.

Reviewing results event is an administrative event concerning the release of review outcomes to authors, while Workshop is a scientific event where research is presented. They belong to different branches (Administrative vs Scientific) and denote entirely different concepts.

Both classes represent a Person in the conference domain. They share similar properties (email, first name) and have children that correspond to typical conference roles (authors, participants, committee/PC members, chairs). Despite slight differences in property sets, their intended instances coincide.
Author is a person who writes papers, while Tutorial is a type of conference event/session. They are completely unrelated concepts in the conference domain.

Contributed Talk and Tutorial are both types of conference presentations/lectures but are distinct concepts. A contributed talk is a regular paper presentation by an author, while a tutorial is an instructional session. They are siblings in ekaw (both under Individual Presentation) and related as subtypes of lecture/presentation activities, but not equivalent.

User in cmt is a subclass of Person representing people who use the system (authors, reviewers, administrators), while Non Academic Event in edas is a subclass of Conference Event representing social/break/meal events. These are entirely different concepts.

Entity A is a class representing a person who authors papers (a role under Conference Member), while Entity B is a class representing a specific type of registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Rated Papers (edas) are papers that have already received ratings/reviews, while Assigned Paper (ekaw) are papers assigned to reviewers but not yet evaluated (Evaluated Paper is a child of Assigned Paper in ekaw). They represent different stages in the review lifecycle and overlap only in that both are papers undergoing the review process, so they are related but not equivalent.

Author Not Reviewer (cmt) denotes an author who is not a reviewer, while Worker non speaker (iasted) denotes a working delegate who is not a speaker. Both capture the idea of a conference participant with a contribution role but without a presentation/review role, yet they differ in domain specifics (author vs worker, reviewer vs speaker). They overlap conceptually but are not equivalent.

Property A (organises) relates an Organisation or Person to an Event they organise, while property B (presentationed by) relates a Document to a Speaker who presents it. The domains, ranges, and semantics are entirely different.

Two Level Conference in edas is a type of conference (event/organization), while Early Registered Participant in ekaw is a type of person attending the conference. They are entirely different concepts.

The two properties have completely different domains (Activity vs Document) and different semantics: 'is held before' relates an activity to a time point indicating temporal ordering, while 'submit until' relates a document to a deadline indicating a submission cutoff. They are unrelated.

Invited Speaker is a subclass of Person (a role played by a human), while Speaker lecture is a subclass of Session/Activity (an event). They belong to entirely different categories in the ontology and are not equivalent.
In cmt, Document is a superclass of Paper and Review. In ekaw, Paper is a subclass of Document (with siblings like Review, Abstract, etc.). Thus cmt:Document subsumes ekaw:Paper.
Contributed Talk is a type of scientific event/presentation at a conference, while Conference state is a status/state related to the conference itself. These are entirely different concepts.
Both classes represent the same concept: an invited speaker at a conference. Despite slightly different parent hierarchies (Presenter vs Speaker), their intended instances coincide.

Call for paper is a type of conference document used to solicit submissions, while Cryptography Topic is a specific subject area/topic within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Property A links a Conference to its Conference Members (people), while property B is an auto-generated inverse of a partOf relation with range Event. They relate entirely different kinds of entities and serve different purposes.

The two properties have completely different domains and ranges and express unrelated relations: 'expertOn' links a PC member to a topic of expertise, while 'publisherOf' links an organisation to published documents.

In Ontology A, 'Extended abstract' and 'Paper' are siblings under 'Regular contribution', meaning they are distinct types of contributions. In ekaw, 'Paper' is a broad class with many subtypes (Conference Paper, Regular Paper, etc.) and 'Abstract' is a sibling, not a subtype. An extended abstract is not equivalent to a full paper; they overlap as submission artefacts but denote different concepts.

Dining Place is a physical location (subclass of Place) where meals are served, while Conference Trip is a social event/activity (subclass of Social Event). They belong to fundamentally different categories (place vs. event) and are not equivalent.

defaultChoice is a datatype property linking events to a positiveInteger (likely a default selection count), while Start_of_conference links a Conference to a dateTime. They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

Tutorial in ekaw and Plenary lecture in iasted are both specific types of conference presentations/events, but they denote different concepts: a tutorial is typically an instructional session, while a plenary lecture is a keynote-style talk for all attendees. Notably, iasted has its own Tutorial class as a sibling of Plenary lecture, confirming they are distinct. They are related as co-hyponyms under the broader concept of presentation/lecture.
Paper Abstract is a type of document (a summary of a paper), while Antennas Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.
