setMaxPapers is an object property from Administrator to Program Committee Member (setting a paper limit for reviewers), while maxChoice is a datatype property from events to positiveInteger. They have completely different domains, ranges, types, and semantics.

Property A links a Presentation to the person who gives it (domain: Presentation, range: Active conference participant), while Property B links an Author to a Contribution they write (domain: Author, range: Contribution). The domains and ranges are reversed in direction relative to the agent/artifact relationship, and the semantics differ (presenting vs. writing).

'has an expertise' is a datatype property on 'Review expertise', while 'Name' is a datatype property on 'Person' representing a person's name. They describe entirely different concepts and are unrelated.
Accommodation Place is a general class for any place providing lodging, while Hotel room is a specific type of accommodation. Accommodation Place subsumes Hotel room.

Session Chair in ekaw is a person role (subclass of Conference Participant and PC Member), while Brief introduction for Session chair in iasted is a document (subclass of Document). They are entirely different kinds of entities.

startReviewerBidding is an administrative action linking an Administrator to a Conference to initiate the bidding phase, while reviewes links a PC Member to a Contribution (paper) they are reviewing. They have entirely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasDecision links a Paper to a Decision (accept/reject), while hasAdministrativeEvent links a Working event to an Administrative event. These relate entirely different domain and range concepts with different semantics.
One property captures the last name (surname) and the other captures the first name (given name). They are distinct attributes of a Person and not equivalent.

In Ontology A, Tutorial is a type of conference part (an event/session), sibling to Track and Workshop. In Ontology B, Programme is a Document (a printed schedule or program booklet), sibling to Paper and Review. These are fundamentally different concepts: one is an event, the other is a document.

In ontology A (iasted), 'Speaker lecture' is a subclass of Session/Activity, representing an event or talk type. In ontology B (sigkdd), 'Invited Speaker' is a subclass of Person/Speaker, representing a role played by a person. They belong to fundamentally different categories (event vs. person) and are therefore unrelated.
Associated Chair is a person role (a type of Chairman), while Conference Trip is a social event. They belong to entirely different branches of the ontology and share no semantic overlap.

Conference contributor in Ontology A refers to people who contribute content to the conference (authors, speakers, active participants), while Agency Staff Member in Ontology B refers to staff from an agency (e.g., funding or travel agency). These are conceptually distinct roles within the conference domain.

Property A (assignedByReviewer) links an External Reviewer to a Reviewer (person-to-person assignment), while Property B (reviewerOfPaper) links a Possible Reviewer to a Paper (person-to-document). They have different domains and ranges and express fundamentally different relationships.
Conference in confOf is a type of working event (the conference itself), while Modelling in iasted is a research activity performed before the conference. These are entirely different concepts.

Property A links a Paper Presentation to an Accepted Paper (presentation-to-paper), while Property B links a Document to a Speaker (document-to-presenter). They relate different kinds of entities in different directions and are not equivalent.
Paper Full Version is a type of document (a complete paper submission), while Mobile Computing Topic is a subject area/topic within the conference domain. They are entirely different concepts.

The property 'title' in cmt relates a Paper to its title string, while 'has First Name' in edas relates a Person to their first name string. They have different domains (Paper vs Person) and represent entirely different concepts.

'has a publisher' links Conference proceedings to a Publisher (an organization that publishes), while 'writtenBy' links a Document to a Person (the author). These are conceptually distinct relations with different domains and ranges.
Regular in confOf is a type of Participant (a person), while Registration Student in sigkdd is a type of Registration fee (a monetary amount). They belong to entirely different conceptual categories.

Talk Event in edas is a broad academic event category (parent of Paper Presentation, Workshop, etc.), while Introduction of speaker in iasted is a very specific sub-activity under Introduction. They differ significantly in scope and intended instances.

startDate is a datatype property on Conference indicating when the conference begins, while done_till is a datatype property on Deadline indicating when a deadline expires. They have different domains and different semantics.

locationOf is an object property linking a Location to an Event, while Date is a datatype property linking a Deadline to a dateTime value. They are completely unrelated in meaning, domain, range, and property type.

Presenter is a role played by a Person (subclass of Conference Participant), while Registration is an Activity (event) in the conference schedule. They belong to entirely different branches of their respective ontologies and denote unrelated concepts.

Two Level Conference in edas is a subclass of Conference (a type of conference organization), while Non speaker in iasted is a subclass of Delegate (a person attending who does not present). These are entirely different concepts.

Property A (has authors) has domain Conference document and range Person, while property B (writes) has domain Author and range Contribution. They are inverse properties relating the same kinds of entities in opposite directions. Per the instructions, a property and its inverse are not equivalent, so they are related.

Entity A is a Review (an evaluation of a paper), while Entity B is a Programme Brochure (a document listing conference events). These are entirely different concepts in the conference domain. Note that ontology B does have its own 'Review' class as a sibling of Programme Brochure, confirming they are distinct.
Paper is a type of scholarly contribution (document), while Best Applications Paper Award is a type of award. They are fundamentally different concepts in the conference domain.

Both classes are named Document and serve as a superclass for Paper and Review in their respective ontologies. Although edas:Document has additional children (Meal Menu, Programme, Slide Set), the core intended concept—a document artefact within the conference domain—is the same. A reference alignment would typically map these as equivalent.

'Information for participants' is a type of conference document providing logistical or procedural information to attendees, while 'Antennas Topic' is a specific research subject area (topic) within the edas ontology. They belong to entirely different conceptual categories and are unrelated.

Attendee in edas is a general class for anyone attending the conference (parent: Person), while Session Chair in ekaw is a specific role responsible for chairing a session (parents: Conference Participant, PC Member). They are distinct concepts; Attendee does not subsume Session Chair in edas since they are siblings under Person, and Session Chair is far more specific than Attendee.

Organizational Meeting is a type of conference event (an activity), while Author cd proceedings included is a type of person/role (an author whose work appears on a CD proceedings). They are completely different concepts.

Property A links a submitted contribution or topic to a 'Review preference' (a reviewer's stated interest/bid), while property B links a paper directly to a 'Possible Reviewer' (a person). Both concern the reviewer-assignment process, but they relate different kinds of entities (a preference vs. a person), so they are related rather than equivalent.

Conference contributor is a subclass of Person representing someone who contributes to a conference (e.g., author, speaker), while One conference day is a subclass of Time representing a single day of the conference. They are entirely different concepts.
Conference Chair is a person role (chairman of the conference), while Session is an event/activity (a lecture session). They are entirely different concepts.

Workshop Session is a type of event (a session within a workshop), while Session room is a physical place where sessions are held. They belong to entirely different categories (Event vs Place) and are not equivalent.

In edas, 'Active Paper' is a subclass of 'Paper' representing papers that are currently under review (having a rating). In ekaw, 'Paper' is the general class for all papers. Therefore, edas:Active Paper is subsumed by ekaw:Paper.

scientificallyOrganisedBy relates an event to an Academic Institution that organizes it, while occupy relates a Person to a Building/City/State they inhabit. These properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

hasCostAmount is a datatype property on Sponsorship returning an integer (the monetary amount), while Currency is a datatype property on Registration fee returning a string (the currency code). They differ in domain, range type, and semantic meaning (amount vs. currency unit), so they are unrelated.

Property A denotes the issue date of a conference document (domain: Conference document), while Property B denotes the registration deadline for a conference (domain: Conference). They have different domains, ranges, and semantics.

In Ontology A, 'Committee member' is a general class under Person with children Chair and Co-chair, covering all committee types. In Ontology B, 'Organizing Committee member' is specifically a member of the organizing committee, distinct from its sibling 'Program Committee member'. Thus, the general 'Committee member' in A subsumes the more specific 'Organizing Committee member' in B.
reviewWrittenBy links a Review to its reviewer (Possible Reviewer), while obtain links an Author to an Award. They have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics.

The two properties have completely different domains, ranges, and semantics. 'printHardcopyMailingManifests' relates an Administrator to a Conference for printing manifests, while 'presentationed_by' relates a Document to a Speaker for presentations. They are unrelated.

Property A ('is writen by') links an Item to its author (Person), expressing authorship. Property B ('presentation') links a Speaker to a Document, expressing that the speaker presents the document. These relate different domain/range types and express different relations (authorship vs. presentation), so they are unrelated.
